1CH 10:1 When the Philistines fought against Israel and the Israelites fled before them, and fell down slain on mount Gelbue,
1CH 10:2 the Philistines pursued close after Saul and after his sons; and when they had slain Jonathan and Aminadab and Melchisue, the sons of Saul, the weight of the battle was directed against Saul.
1CH 10:3 And the archers assailed him with bows, and darts, and wounded him with arrows.
1CH 10:4 Whereupon Saul said to his armour bearer, Draw thy sword and run me through with it, lest the uncircumcised come and insult me. But his armour bearer would not; for he was greatly terrified. Thereupon Saul took the sword and fell on it.
1CH 10:5 And when his armour bearer saw that he was dead, he also fell on his sword.
1CH 10:6 Thus Saul died with his three sons that day. And all his house died together.
1CH 10:7 And when the Israelites who dwelt in the plain, saw that Israel had fled and that Saul and his sons were dead they left their cities and fled, and the Philistines came and dwelt therein.
1CH 10:8 Now on the next day when the Philistines came to strip the dead, they found Saul and his sons fallen, on mount Gelbue.
1CH 10:9 And when they had stripped him, they took his head and his armour, and sent them to the land of the Philistines round about, to proclaim the good news to their idols, and to the people.
1CH 10:10 And having deposited his armour in the house of their god, they fixed up his head, in the house of Dagon.
1CH 10:11 But when all the inhabitants of Galaad heard all that the Philistines had done to Saul and Israel,
1CH 10:12 all the valiant men of Galaad arose and took the body of Saul and the bodies of his sons, and carried them to Jabis and buried their bones under the oak at Jabis, and fasted seven days.
1CH 10:13 Thus died Saul, for his transgressions, which he had committed against God, according to the word of the Lord. Because he did not keep watch; because Saul sought to consult by a belly speaker, therefore Samuel the prophet answered him,
1CH 10:14 though he sought not the Lord, and the Lord slew him, and transferred the kingdom to David, son of Jessai.
1CH 11:1 Then all Israel came to David to Chebron, and said, Behold we are thy bones and thy flesh.
1CH 11:2 Even in time past when Saul was king, it was thou who didst lead us and bring in Israel, and the Lord said to thee, Thou shalt feed my people Israel, and thou shalt be ruler over Israel.
1CH 11:3 So when all the elders were come to the king at Chebron, king David made a covenant with them at Chebron before the Lord, and they anointed him to be king over Israel, according to the word of the Lord by the ministry of Samuel.
1CH 11:4 When the king and his men went to Jerusalem, which is Jebus, the inhabitants of the land,
1CH 11:5 the Jebusites who were there said to David, Thou shalt not come here, yet he took the fortress Sion which is now the city of David.
1CH 11:6 He indeed said, Whoever first smiteth the Jebusites, he shall be made chief and general of the army. Upon which Joab son of Saruia went up first and was made chief.
1CH 11:7 And David made his abode in the fortress, for which cause he called it the city of David,
1CH 11:8 and built the city around it.
1CH 11:9 And David proceeded on advancing in greatness, for the Lord Almighty was with him.
1CH 11:10 Now these are the chiefs of the mighty men who were with David, who with him prevailed with all Israel during his reign, that he should be, according to the word of the Lord, king over Israel.
1CH 11:11 And this is the number of David's worthies. Jesebada son of Achaman, the first of thirty. He drew his sword once against three hundred men who were slain at one time.
1CH 11:12 And after him Eleazar son of Dodai the Achochite, who was one of the three worthies.
1CH 11:13 He was with David at Phasodamin when the Philistines were assembled there for battle. And there was a portion of a field full of barley. And when the people fled before the Philistines,
1CH 11:14 he stood in the midst of the piece of ground and maintained it and smote the Philistines, and the Lord gave a great victory.
1CH 11:15 When three of the thirty chiefs went down to the rock to David, to the cave Odollam, at the time when the Philistines were encamped in the giant's vale,
1CH 11:16 and David was in the fortress and there was a garrison of the Philistines at Bethlehem,
1CH 11:17 David longed and said, O that some one would give me some water to drink out of the well of Bethlehem which is by the gate!
1CH 11:18 Upon this the three broke through the camp of the Philistines, and having drawn some water out of the well of Bethlehem by the gate, they took it and came to David. But David would not drink it, but poured it out as a libation to the Lord,
1CH 11:19 and said, God forbid that I should do such a thing! Shall I drink the blood of these men who have jeoparded their lives? Because they had brought it at the hazard of their lives he would not drink it. These things were done by these three worthies.
1CH 11:20 And Abisa brother of Joab, who was chief of the three; he drew his sword against three hundred  who were slain at one time.
1CH 11:21 He was renowned among the three. Of the three he was higher in rank than two and was their chief, but did not come up to the three.
1CH 11:22 And Banaias son of Jodae, son of a worthy, whose works for Kabasael were many; he smote the two Ariels of Moab. He went down also and smote a lion in the pit in a snowy day.
1CH 11:23 He smote also the Egyptian, a noted man of five cubits high. Though the Egyptian had in his hand a spear like a weaver's beam, Banaias went against him with a staff, and wresting the spear out of the hand of the Egyptian, he slew him with his own spear.
1CH 11:24 These things Banaias son of Jodae did, and had a name among the three worthies.
1CH 11:25 He was higher in rank than the thirty but did not come up to the three, and David set him over his family.

1CH 12:1 Now these were they who came to David to Sekelag, while he kept himself close because of Saul son of Kis; and these among the worthies assisted in battle,
1CH 12:2 and used the bow, slung stones and hurled darts with both hands. Of the brethren of Saul; of Benjamin
1CH 12:3 the chief Achiezer and Joas son of Asma the Gabathite, and Joel and Jophalet sons of Asmoth and Berchia and Jeul the Anathothite,
1CH 12:4 and Samaias the Gabaonite, a commander among the thirty and over the thirty; Jeremia and Jeziel and Joanan and Joazabath the Gadarathiite
1CH 12:5 Azai and Arimuth and Baalia and Samaraia and Saphatias the Charaiphielite,
1CH 12:6 Elkana and Jesuni and Ozriel and Jozara and Sobokam, who were Korites,
1CH 12:7 and Jelia and Zabadia sons of Iroam and who were Gedorites.
1CH 12:8 And from the Gadites there withdrew to David from the wilderness, valiant men fit to command an army in battle array, wielding shields and spears. Their faces were the face of a lion, and they were swift as roes on the mountains;
1CH 12:9 Asa the chief, Abdia the second, Eliab the third,
1CH 12:10 Masmana the fourth, Jeremias the fifth,
1CH 12:11 Jethi the sixth, Eliab the seventh,
1CH 12:12 Joanan the eighth, Eliazer the ninth,
1CH 12:13 Jeremia the tenth, Melchabania the eleventh.
1CH 12:14 These from among the sons of Gad were officers of the army, the least of them commanded a hundred, and the greatest a thousand.
1CH 12:15 These were they who crossed the Jordan in the first month, when it overflowed all its banks, and put to flight all the inhabitants of the plains, from east to west.
1CH 12:16 There came also some from Benjamin and Juda to the assistance of David.
1CH 12:17 And David went out to meet them, and said to them, If you are come to me with good intent, let my heart as it is disposed be knit to you: but if to betray me to my enemies, and not with sincerity, may the God of our fathers see and rebuke.
1CH 12:18 Whereupon Amasai, a chief of the thirty, became inspired, and said, Advance, David son of Jessai! for they are thy people; Peace! peace to thee! and peace to them who assist thee, because thy God hath helped thee. So David received them, and made them officers of the armies.
1CH 12:19 There withdrew also to David some from Manasses, when the Philistines came against Saul to battle. He indeed did not assist them, for in a council of war held by the generals of the Philistines, they said, With the heads of these men he will return to his master Saul.
1CH 12:20 As David was returning to Sekelag there came to him from Manasses, Edna and Josabath and Rodiel and Michael and Josabaith and Elimuth and Semathi. They were the leaders of the thousands of Manasses,
1CH 12:21 and they assisted David in the battle against the roving horde; for they were all men of valour, and for their valour commanders in the army.
1CH 12:22 For there came men daily to David to form a great army like the host of God.
1CH 12:23 Now these were the rolls of the chiefs of the army who came to David to Chebron, to transfer the kingdom of Saul to him, according to the word of the Lord.
1CH 12:24 The children of Juda armed with shields and spears, six thousand eight hundred, fit for the array of battle;
1CH 12:25 of the Symeonites fit for the array of battle, seven thousand one hundred;
1CH 12:26 of the Levites, four thousand six hundred,
1CH 12:27 and Joadas the leader of the house of Aaron, and with him three thousand seven hundred,
1CH 12:28 with Sadok a young man of valour, and of his patriarchal family twenty two chiefs;
1CH 12:29 and of the Benjaminites, Saul's brethren, three thousand; but still the greater part of them kept the watch of Saul's house;
1CH 12:30 of the Ephraimites, twenty thousand eight hundred valiant men, the most renowned in the houses of their respective families;
1CH 12:31 and of the half of the tribe of Manasses, eighteen thousand, who were enrolled for the express purpose of making David king
1CH 12:32 and of the children of Issachar, men who had knowledge suitable for the times, who knew what Israel should do, two hundred chiefs, and all their brethren with them;
1CH 12:33 and from Zabulon there came ready for battle, with all the implements of war with them, fifty thousand, to assist David effectually;
1CH 12:34 and from Nephthaleim, a thousand chiefs, and with them thirty seven thousand, armed with shields and spears;
1CH 12:35 and from the Danites, twenty eight thousand eight hundred, marshalled for battle;
1CH 12:36 and from Aser they who go forth for battle, forty thousand;
1CH 12:37 and from beyond the Jordan; from battle and Gad, and from the half of the tribe of Manasses, with all the implements of war, a hundred and twenty thousand.
1CH 12:38 All these warriors were arrayed for battle, with a peaceable intention. They came to Chebron to make David king over all Israel. And all the rest of Israel were of one mind that David should be king.
1CH 12:39 And they were three days eating and drinking. For their brethren made provision for them.
1CH 12:40 And they who were nearest, as far as Zabulon and Issachar and Nephthaleim brought provisions for them on camels and asses and mules and oxen, namely, flour, fig cakes, dried grapes, wine and oil, with cattle and sheep in abundance; for there was joy in Israel.
1CH 13:1 When David had consulted with the captains of thousands and captains of hundreds, under every leader,
1CH 13:2 he said to the whole congregation of Israel, If it seemeth good and be countenanced by the Lord our God, let us send to the rest of our brethren who are left in all the land of Israel, and with them let the priests, the Levites in the cities of their possession be assembled with us;
1CH 13:3 and let us bring the ark of our God to us. For they had not sought it from the days of Saul.
1CH 13:4 Thereupon the whole congregation gave orders to do so; for the proposal was right in the eyes of all the people.
1CH 13:5 Accordingly, David assembled all Israel from the border of Egypt to the bay of Emath, to bring the ark of God from the city Iarim,
1CH 13:6 and David brought it up. Now when all Israel came to the city Iarim which belonged to Juda, to bring up thence the ark of God the Lord, enthroned on cherubim whose name was invoked,
1CH 13:7 they put the ark of God on a new cart. And from the house of Aminadab, Oza and his brothers guided the cart,
1CH 13:8 while David and all Israel were playing with all their might before God, on psalteries and kinyras and nablas and tympanums and cymbals and trumpets.
1CH 13:9 But when they came to the threshing floor, Oza stretched forth his hand to take hold of the ark, because the bullock caused it to lean:
1CH 13:10 whereupon the anger of the Lord was kindled against Oza, and he smote him there, because he stretched forth his hand upon the ark, and he died there before God.
1CH 13:11 And David was disheartened because the Lord had made a breach on Oza, and called that place, Breach of Oza, which is still its name.
1CH 13:12 And David was that day afraid of God and said, How can I bring the ark of God home to me?
1CH 13:13 So David did not bring the ark of God home to himself, to the city of David, but caused it to turn aside to the house of Abeddara, the Gethite.
1CH 13:14 And the ark of God abode in the house of Abeddara three months, and God blessed Abeddara and all that belonged to him.
1CH 14:1 When Chiram king of Tyre sent messengers to David, with cedar timber, and masons and carpenters to build him a house,
1CH 14:2 and David knew that the Lord had prepared him to be king over Israel; for his kingdom was highly exalted for the sake of his people Israel,
1CH 14:3 David took still more wives in Jerusalem, and more sons and daughters were born to him.
1CH 14:4 Now these are the names of those who were born to him in Jerusalem, Samaa, Sobab, Nathan and Solomon,
1CH 14:5 and Baar and Elisa, and Eliphaleth
1CH 14:6 and Nageth, and Naphath and Japhie,
1CH 14:7 and Elisamae and Eliade, and Eliphala.
1CH 14:8 When the Philistines heard that David was anointed king over all Israel, they all came up to seek David. And when David heard it he went out to meet them.
1CH 14:9 Now the Philistines had come and spread themselves in the giant's vale.
1CH 14:10 And David inquired of God, saying, If I go up against the Philistines, wilt thou deliver them into my hands? And the Lord said to him, Go up and I will deliver them into thy hands.
1CH 14:11 So he went up to Baal Pharasin. And when he had smitten them there David said, God broke through, my enemies by my hand, like the breaking out of water, therefore he called the name of that place, Breach of Pharasin.
1CH 14:12 And the Philistines having left their gods there, David ordered them to be burned.
1CH 14:13 Again the Philistines came up and spread themselves again in the giant's vale.
1CH 14:14 And when David again inquired of God, God said to him, Thou shalt not go up after them. Turn from them and come upon them near the pear trees.
1CH 14:15 And when thou shalt hear a sound of rustling in the tops of the pear trees, then thou shalt come to battle, for God is gone out before thee to smite the camp of the Philistines.
1CH 14:16 Accordingly he did as the Lord commanded him, and he smote the camp of the Philistines from Gabaon to Gazera.
1CH 14:17 And the fame of David spread through all the land, and the Lord brought the dread of him on all the nations.
1CH 15:1 When David had built houses for himself in the city of David, and prepared the place for the ark of God, and made for it a tabernacle:
1CH 15:2 then David said, None but the Levites ought to carry the ark of God; for the Lord hath chosen them to carry the ark of the Lord and to minister to him forever.
1CH 15:3 So when David assembled all Israel at Jerusalem, to bring the ark of the Lord to the place which he had prepared for it,
1CH 15:4 he assembled the sons of Aaron, the Levites;
1CH 15:5 of the Kaathites, Uriel the chief and his brethren, a hundred and twenty;
1CH 15:6 of the Merarites, Asaia the chief and his brethren, two hundred and twenty;
1CH 15:7 of the Gersonites, Joel the chief and his brethren, a hundred and thirty;
1CH 15:8 of the sons of Elisaphat, Semei, the chief and his brethren, two hundred;
1CH 15:9 of the sons of Chebron, Eliel the chief and his brethren, eighty;
1CH 15:10 of the sons of Oziel, Aminadab the chief and his brethren, a hundred and twelve.
1CH 15:11 And David sent for Sadok, and Abiathar the priests, and for the Levites, Uriel, Asaia and Joel, and Semaia and Eliel, and Aminadab,
1CH 15:12 and said to them, You chiefs of the families of the Levites, purify yourselves, both you and your brethren, that you may carry up the ark of the God of Israel to the place which I have prepared for it;
1CH 15:13 for because you did not do this on the former occasion, our God made a breach among us, because we did not seek him with judgment.
1CH 15:14 So when the priests and the Levites had purified themselves to carry the ark of the God of Israel,
1CH 15:15 the Levites took up the ark of God, as Moses had by the word of the Lord ordered in writing, with the staves on their shoulders.
1CH 15:16 Now David had said to the chiefs of the Levites, Appoint your brethren, such as play on musical instruments, on nablas and kinyras, and cymbals, that they may make a loud sound with the voice of joy.
1CH 15:17 And the Levites had appointed Aiman son of Joel and of his brethren, Asaph son of Barachia, and of the sons of Merari his brethren, Aithan the son of Kisias
1CH 15:18 and with them their brethren of the second rank, Zacharias and Oziel, and Semiramoth and Jeiel, and Elioel and Eliab, and Banaia and Maasaia, and Matthathia and Eliphena, and Makellia and Abdedom, and Jeiel and Ozias, the keepers of the gates;
1CH 15:19 and the musicians Aiman, Asaph and Aithan, sung and played on brass cymbals in the highest key;
1CH 15:20 and Zacharias and Oziel, Semiramoth, Jeiel; Oni, Eliab, Maasias, Banias, on nablas in alaimoth;
1CH 15:21 and Mattathias and Eliphalu, and Makenia and Abdedom, and Jeiel and Ozias, on kinyras in Amasenith to give a strong sound.
1CH 15:22 And Chononias, a chief of the Levites, was master of the odes, for he was skilled therein.
1CH 15:23 And Barachia and Elkana were door keepers of the ark.
1CH 15:24 And Somnia and Josaphat, and Nathaniel and Amasai, and Zacharia and Banaia, and Eliezer the priests, sounded the trumpets before the ark of God. And Abdedom and Jeia were door keepers of the ark of God.
1CH 15:25 And David with the elders of Israel and the captains of thousands, marched before when they were bringing up the ark of the covenant from the house of Abdedom with joy.
1CH 15:26 And because God strengthened the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, therefore they sacrificed each seven bulls and seven rams.
1CH 15:27 Now David was girded in a cotton stole, as were all the Levites who carried the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the musicians and Chonenias the chief of the singers. And when David in his cotton stole,
1CH 15:28 and all Israel were bringing up the ark of the covenant of the Lord with shouting and the sound of clarions and trumpets, answered by nablas and kinyras,
1CH 15:29 it happened that when the ark of the covenant of the Lord came to the city of David, Melchol the daughter of Saul looking out at a window saw king David dancing and playing, and she despised him in her heart.
1CH 16:1 And when they had brought in the ark of God and set it in the midst of the tabernacle, which David had erected for it, they offered whole burnt offerings and offerings of thanks giving before God.
1CH 16:2 And when David had finished offering the whole burnt offerings and the offerings of thanksgiving, he blessed the people in the name of the Lord,
1CH 16:3 and distributed to all Israel both men and women, to every one a loaf of baker's bread, and a cake made with honey.
1CH 16:4 Then he appointed some of the Levites to minister before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and in responsive strains to thank and praise the Lord the God of Israel.
1CH 16:5 Asaph was the leader, and to him responded Zacharias, Jeiel, Semiramoth and Jeiel, Matthathias, Eliab and Banaias, Abdedom and Jeiel, with musical instruments, nablas and kinyras; but Asaph used the cymbal;
1CH 16:6 and Banaias and Oziel the priests, with trumpets, were to be continually before the ark of the covenant of God.
1CH 16:7 On that day David gave orders for beginning the praises of the Lord by the ministry of Asaph and his brethren, with this Ode:
1CH 16:8 O give thanks to the Lord, Invoke him by his name; Among peoples make known his designs.
1CH 16:9 Sing to him. Sing praises to him. Proclaim to all the wonders which the Lord hath done.
1CH 16:10 Sing praises to his holy name. Let the heart which seeketh his favour be triad.
1CH 16:11 Seek the Lord and persevere; Seek his face continually.
1CH 16:12 Remember the wonders which he hath done; The miracles and judgments of his mouth.
1CH 16:13 The seed of Israel are his servants; The sons of Jacob, his chosen ones.
1CH 16:14 He is the Lord our God; In all this land are his judgments.
1CH 16:15 Let us ever remember his covenant; His word which he enjoined for a thousand generations.
1CH 16:16 The covenant which he made with Abraham; And the oath which he sware to Isaak,
1CH 16:17 This he confirmed for a law to Jacob; To Israel as an everlasting covenant,
1CH 16:18 Saying, To thee I will give the land of Chanaan, To be the portion of your inheritance.
1CH 16:19 When they were very few in number; Of little account, and sojourned therein;
1CH 16:20 When they were passing from nation to nation; And from one kingdom to another people;
1CH 16:21 He suffered no man to oppress them; He rebuked kings for their sake
1CH 16:22 Touch not these my anointed ones, And to these my prophets do no harm.
1CH 16:23 Sing to the Lord, all ye of this land, From day to day proclaim his salvation.
1CH 16:24 Declare his glory among the nations; Among all peoples his marvellous works;
1CH 16:25 That the Lord is great and greatly to be praised; Above all the gods he is awful
1CH 16:26 That all the gods of the nations are idols; But our God hath made the heavens.
1CH 16:27 Glory and honour are before him; Majesty and gladness in his abode.
1CH 16:28 Ascribe to the Lord, ye families of nations, Ascribe to the Lord glory and majesty
1CH 16:29 Ascribe to the Lord, glory to his name. Take gifts and bring them before him, And worship the Lord in his holy courts.
1CH 16:30 Let all the earth be awed at his presence, Let the earth be renovated and not dismayed.
1CH 16:31 Let heaven rejoice, and the earth exult with joy, Let them say among the nations, The Lord is king.
1CH 16:32 Let the sea roar and the fulness thereof; And the trees of the field and all therein;
1CH 16:33 Let the trees of the forest also rejoice at the presence of the Lord; Because he is come to judge the earth.
1CH 16:34 praise the Lord; for it is good, For to everlasting his mercy endureth.
1CH 16:35 And say, Save us, God of our salvation! Gather us and deliver us from our enemies; That we may praise thy holy name, And in thy praises make our boast.
1CH 16:36 Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, From everlasting to everlasting, And let all the people say, Amen.
1CH 16:37 And when they had praised the Lord, they left there, before the ark of the covenant of the Lord, Asaph and his brethren, that they might minister before the ark continually as each day's service required.
1CH 16:38 And with regard to Abdedom and his brethren who were sixty eight, Abdedom son of Idithun and Osa were to be door keepers.
1CH 16:39 And they left Sadok the priest, and his brethren the priests, before the tabernacle of the Lord at the high place at Gabaon,
1CH 16:40 that they might offer whole burnt offerings to the Lord, on the altar of whole burnt offerings continually every morning and evening, according to all that is written in the law of the Lord, which he enjoined on the children of Israel by the ministry of Moses the servant of God:
1CH 16:41 and with him were Aiman and Idithun, and the rest who were chosen by name to praise the Lord, because his mercy endureth forever.
1CH 16:42 And they had with them trumpets and high sounding cymbals, and musical instruments, for the songs of God. And the sons of Idithun were to be keepers of the gate.
1CH 16:43 Then all the people returned every one to his home, and David returned to bless his household.
1CH 17:1 When David was settled in his house, he said to Nathan the prophet, Behold I dwell in a house of cedar, but the ark of the covenant of the Lord is beneath curtains of skin.
1CH 17:2 Thereupon Nathan said to David, Do whatever is in thy heart; for God is with thee.
1CH 17:3 But that very night there came to Nathan a word of the Lord,
1CH 17:4 Go, and say to David my servant, Thus saith the Lord, Thou shalt not build me a house to dwell in.
1CH 17:5 Because I have not dwelt in a house from the day I brought up Israel even to this day, but have been in a tent and under a curtain
1CH 17:6 in all the places, through which passed among Israel, did I ever speak to any tribe of Israel, whom I commanded to feed my people, and say, Why have you not built for me a house of cedar?
1CH 17:7 But now, Thus shalt thou say to my servant David, Thus saith the Lord Almighty, I took thee from the fold; from following the flocks, to be ruler over my people Israel,
1CH 17:8 and have been with thee wherever thou hast gone, and have cut off all thy enemies from before thee, and made thee a name like the name of the great men on the earth;
1CH 17:9 and I will fix a place for my people Israel, and plant them, and they shall dwell by themselves and no more be in trouble, nor shall a son of iniquity any more humble them as at the first,
1CH 17:10 even from the time I appointed judges over my people Israel. I have indeed subdued all thy enemies, and I will increase thee and the Lord will build thee a house.
1CH 17:11 And when thy days are fulfilled and thou shalt go to rest with thy fathers, I will raise up thy seed after thee who shall proceed from thy loins, and I will prepare his kingdom.
1CH 17:12 He shall build a house for me, and I will establish his throne forever.
1CH 17:13 I will be to him a father and he shall be to me a son; and I will not withdraw my mercy from him as I withdrew it from them who were before him;
1CH 17:14 but will confirm him in my house and in his kingdom, and his throne shall be established forever.
1CH 17:15 According to all these words and according to all this vision, so did Nathan speak to David.
1CH 17:16 Whereupon king David went and sat down before the Lord, and said, Who am I, Lord my God, and what is my house that thou shouldst love me forever!
1CH 17:17 Though these were very small before thee, my God, yet thou hast spoken of thy servant's house for a great while to come, and hast looked upon me as with the eyes of a man, and exalted me. Lord my God,
1CH 17:18 what more can David address to thee to express thy praise? Thou knowest thy servant,
1CH 17:19 and according to thy own heart thou hast made all this greatness.
1CH 17:20 O Lord! there is none like thee, nor is there a god besides thee according to all that we have heard with our ears;
1CH 17:21 nor is there another nation on the earth like thy people Israel. How hath God led them to redeem a people for himself, to make himself a name great and glorious, by driving out nations from before thy people whom thou didst redeem out of Egypt!
1CH 17:22 As thou hast made thy people Israel a people for thyself forever, and thou the Lord art become their God;
1CH 17:23 now therefore, Lord, let the word which thou hast spoken to thy servant, and touching his house be established forever, and do as thou hast spoken;
1CH 17:24 and let thy name be established and magnified forever by men, saying, Lord, Lord Almighty, thou art the God of Israel, and the house of thy servant David is established before thee.
1CH 17:25 Because thou, Lord my God, hast revealed to the ear of thy servant, that thou wilt build him a house; therefore thy servant hath found freedom to make supplication before thee.
1CH 17:26 And now, Lord, thou art God. As thou hast spoken these good things, respecting thy servant;
1CH 17:27 now therefore begin to bless the house of thy servant that it may be before thee forever. Because thou hast blessed, therefore bless it forever.
1CH 18:1 Now after these things, David smote the Philistines and subdued them, and took out of their hands Geth and the villages thereof.
1CH 18:2 He smote Moab also, and they became vassals to David and brought him gifts.
1CH 18:3 David also smote Adraazar king of Suba Emath. As he was going to establish his dominion over the river Euphrates;
1CH 18:4 David intercepted a thousand of his chariots and seven thousand cavalry, and twenty thousand infantry. And David destroyed all the chariots, reserving only a hundred of them.
1CH 18:5 And when the Syrians of Damascus came to assist Adraazar king of Suba, David smote of the Syrians twenty two thousand men.
1CH 18:6 And David garrisoned that part of Syria which belonged to Damascus, and the inhabitants became David's vassals, and brought him gifts. And the Lord preserved David wherever he went.
1CH 18:7 And David took the chains of gold which were on the servants of Adraazar, and brought them to Jerusalem.
1CH 18:8 And from Matabeth and from the chief cities which belonged to Adraazar, David took brass in great abundance, of which Solomon made the brasen sea and the pillars and the vessels of brass.
1CH 18:9 Now when Thoa king of Emath, heard that David had smitten all the army of Adraazar king of Suba,
1CH 18:10 he sent his son Aduram to king David, to sue for peace with him, and to congratulate him because he had fought Adraazar and defeated him; for Thoa was at war with Adraazar.
1CH 18:11 And all the vessels of gold and silver and brass, which he brought, these king David dedicated to the Lord, together with the silver and the gold which he took from all the nations from Idumea and Moab, and from the Ammonites and the Philistines and from Amelek.
1CH 18:12 When Abessa son of Saruia had smitten of the Idumeans in the valley of salt, eighteen thousand,
1CH 18:13 he put garrisons in the vale; and the Idumeans became David's vassals, and the Lord preserved David wherever he went.
1CH 18:14 And David reigned over all Israel, and continued to execute judgment and justice among all the people.
1CH 18:15 And Joab son of Saruia was over the army; and Josaphat son of Achilud was recorder;
1CH 18:16 and Sadok son of Achitob and Achimelech son of Abiathar, were the priests; and Sousa was secretary;
1CH 18:17 and Banaias son of Jodae was over the Cherethites and the Phelethites, and David's sons were next in rank to the king.
1CH 19:1 Now after these things, when Naas king of the Ammonites died and his son Anan reigned in his stead,
1CH 19:2 David said, I will shew kindness to Anan son of Naas as his father shewed kindness to me. So David sent messengers to comfort him for his father.
1CH 19:3 But when David's servants came to the country of the Ammonites to Anan to comfort him, the chiefs of the Ammonites said to Anan, Is it to honour thy father in thy presence that David hath sent comforters to thee? Is it not that they may examine the city and spy the country that his servants are come to thee?
1CH 19:4 Thereupon Anan took David's servants and shaved them, and having cut off the half of their military robe even to the under garment, he dismissed them.
1CH 19:5 And when messengers came to inform David respecting his servants, David sent to meet them, because they had been greatly dishonoured; and the king said to them, Abide at Jericho till your beards grow and then return.
1CH 19:6 Now when the Ammonites saw that David's people were dishonoured, Anan and the children of Ammon sent a thousand talents of silver to hire for themselves chariots and cavalry from Syrian Mesopotamia, and from Syrian Maacha and from Sobal.
1CH 19:7 And they hired thirty two thousand of the chariot army, and the king of Maacha and his people. And when they arrived they encamped over against Medaba, and the Ammonites were drawn together out of their cities, and came to commence war.
1CH 19:8 When David heard this he sent Joab with all the army of the worthies.
1CH 19:9 And the Ammonites came out and drew up in array for battle before the gate of the city; but the kings who had come, encamped by themselves in the plain.
1CH 19:10 When Joab saw that they were arrayed for battle against him both in front and rear, he made a draught out of all the youth of Israel and drew them up in array against the Syrians.
1CH 19:11 And the rest of the people he put under the command of Abesai his brother, and they were drawn up in array against the Ammonites.
1CH 19:12 And Joab said, If the Syrians be too strong for me, thou must come to my assistance; and if the children of Ammon prove too strong for thee I will support thee.
1CH 19:13 Be of good courage and let us act valiantly for our people and for the cities of our God, and the Lord will do what is good in his sight.
1CH 19:14 And when Joab and the people with him drew up in array for battle over against the Syrians they fled from them.
1CH 19:15 And soon as the Ammonites saw that the Syrians fled they also fled before Abesai and before Joab his brother, and entered the city. Upon which Joab returned to Jerusalem.
1CH 19:16 When the Syrian saw that Israel had defeated him, he despatched messengers and drew out the Syrians from beyond the river. And Sophath the general of Adraazar's army was at their head.
1CH 19:17 This being told David, he assembled all Israel and crossed the Jordan and came upon them, and drew up for battle against them. And while David was marshalling his army for battle against the Syrians, they attacked him;
1CH 19:18 but the Syrians fled before Israel, and David slew of the Syrians seven thousand of the chariot army, and forty thousand infantry. He slew also Sophath the general of the army.
1CH 19:19 And when the servants of Adraazar saw that they were defeated before Israel, they made peace with David and served him. And the Syrians would not help the Ammonites any more.
1CH 20:1 And at the return of the year when kings take the field, Joab led out all the strength of the army, and having laid waste all the while David abode at Jerusalem. And when Joab had smitten Rabba and demolished it
1CH 20:2 David took the crown of Molchom their king from his head, and the weight of it was found to be a talent of gold, and in it was a precious stone and it was on the head of David. And having brought out the spoils of the city which were very great,
1CH 20:3 he brought out the people who were in it, and put them to saws and iron mattocks and among quarry men. And when David had done in this manner to all the Ammonites, he and all the people returned to Jerusalem.
1CH 20:4 And after these things there was another battle at Gazer with the Philistines, in which Sobochai-Sosathai smote Saphut a descendant of the giants and subdued him.
1CH 20:5 There was also another battle with the Philistines, when Eleanan son of Jair smote Lachmai a brother of Goliath the Gethite, the staff of whose spear was like a weaver's beam.
1CH 20:6 There was also another battle at Geth, and there was a man of great stature there, who had six fingers on each hand and six toes on each foot, in all twenty four, and he also was a descendant of the giants,
1CH 20:7 and he defied Israel; but Jonathan son of Samaa, a brother of David, smote him.
1CH 20:8 These were the descendants of Rapha at Geth. They were all four giants, and they tell by the hand of David and by the hand of his servants.
1CH 21:1 Now when an adversary stood up in Israel and persuaded David to number Israel,
1CH 21:2 and king David said to Joab and the chiefs of the army, Go, number Israel from Dan to Bersabee, and let me know the number of them,
1CH 21:3 Joab replied, The Lord add to his people a hundred times as many as there are. and may the eyes of my lord the king see it. They are all servants to my lord. Why doth my lord seek this? May it not be a cause of trespass to Israel?
1CH 21:4 But the king's determination prevailed against Joab, so he went forth, and having passed through all Israel, and come to Jerusalem,
1CH 21:5 he gave David an account of the review of the people, and the whole number of the men of Israel who drew a sword, w r as eleven hundred thousand, and the children of Juda were four hundred and seventy thousand men who drew a sword.
1CH 21:6 But he did not number Levi and Benjamin among them. Because the king's word prevailed over Joab,
1CH 21:7 and the thing was evil in the sight of God, therefore he smote Israel.
1CH 21:8 When David said to God, I have sinned greatly in doing this, now therefore take away, I beseech thee, this wickedness of thy servant, for I have acted very foolishly
1CH 21:9 the Lord spoke to Gad, the seer, saying,
1CH 21:10 Go, and speak to David, and say, Thus saith the Lord, I offer thee three things, chuse for thyself one of them that I may do it to thee
1CH 21:11 So Gad went to David and said to him, Thus saith the Lord, Chuse for thyself
1CH 21:12 either three years of famine; or three months to flee before thy enemies while the sword of thy enemies is destroying thee; or the sword of the Lord and pestilence for three days throughout the land, while an angel of the Lord is making havock in all the inheritance of Israel. Now therefore consider What answer shall I make to him who sent me?
1CH 21:13 Thereupon David said to Gad, Very hard indeed to me are all the three. Let me however fall into the hands of the Lord, for his tender mercies are exceeding great. But let me not fall into the hands of men.
1CH 21:14 So the Lord sent a pestilence through Israel, and there fell of the Israelites seventy thousand men.
1CH 21:15 And when God sent an angel to Jerusalem to destroy it, and he was making havock, the Lord looked and relented at the calamity, and said to the destroying angel, Let this suffice thee. Stay thy hand. Now the angel of the Lord was standing at the threshing floor of Orna, the Jebusite.
1CH 21:16 And when David raised his eyes and saw the angel of the Lord standing between the earth and heaven, with a drawn sword in his hand stretched out over Jerusalem, he and all the elders being clad in sackcloth, fell on their faces,
1CH 21:17 and David said to God, Was it not I who ordered the numbering of the people? I indeed am the sinner. It is I who committed the sin. But as for this flock, what have they done? Lord my God, Let thy hand be upon me, and on my father's house, and not on this thy people, O Lord, to destruction.
1CH 21:18 Thereupon the angel of the Lord ordered Gad to tell David to go up and erect an altar to the Lord on the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite.
1CH 21:19 So David went up according to the word which Gad spoke in the name of the Lord.
1CH 21:20 And when Orna turned and saw the king and his four sons with him, with attendants [now Orna was threshing wheat]
1CH 21:21 upon David's approach to Orna, Orna came out of his threshing floor and made obeisance to David with his face to the ground.
1CH 21:22 And David said to Orna, Grant me the place of this threshing floor of thine, that I may build thereon an altar to the Lord; grant it to me for its worth in money, that the plague may be stayed from the people.
1CH 21:23 And Orna said to David, Take it for thyself; and let my Lord the king do what is good in his sight. Behold I have given these young bulls for a whole burnt offering, and that plough for wood, and this corn for a sacrifice. Of all these things I make a gift.
1CH 21:24 And David said to Orna, By no means: for I must buy them for their worth in money. For I cannot take what are thine for the Lord, to offer a whole burnt offering to the Lord at free cost.
1CH 21:25 So David gave Orna for the place six hundred shekels of gold by weight.
1CH 21:26 And having built there an altar to the Lord, he offered up the offerings of homage and thanksgiving, and cried to the Lord, and the Lord hearkened to him by fire from heaven upon the altar of the whole burnt offering, which consumed the whole burnt offering.
1CH 21:27 Then the Lord spoke to the angel and he sheathed his sword.
1CH 21:28 When David saw that the Lord hearkened to him at the threshing floor of Orna the Jebusite, and that he had sacrificed there
1CH 21:29 at that time, though the tabernacle of the Lord which Moses had made in the wilderness, and the altar for whole burnt offerings were at that time at the high place of Gabaon
1CH 21:30 now he could not go before it to inquire of God, for that would not have been answerable to the haste in which he was, on account of the sword of the angel of the Lord
1CH 22:1 David said, This is the house of the Lord God, and this is the altar for whole burnt offerings for Israel.
1CH 22:2 Then David ordered the strangers in the land of Israel to be assembled, and appointed stone cutters to cut hewn stones to build the house for God.
1CH 22:3 He provided also iron in abundance for nails, for the doors and gates, and for hinges; and brass in abundance, without weight,
1CH 22:4 and cedar beams innumerable; for the Sidonians and Tyrians, brought for David, cedar timber in abundance.
1CH 22:5 And David said, My son Solomon is young and tender, and the house to be built for the Lord is for extraordinary grandeur, for renown and glory, through every land, I will make provision for it. So David provided materials in abundance before his death.
1CH 22:6 And he called Solomon his son, and gave him a charge, to build the house for the Lord God of Israel.
1CH 22:7 And David said to Solomon, My son, it was in my mind to build a house for the name of the Lord God,
1CH 22:8 when there came to me a word from the Lord saying, Thou hast shed much blood, and fought many battles, thou shalt not build a house for my name, because thou hast shed much blood on the earth before me.
1CH 22:9 Behold a son shall be born to thee. He shall be a man of rest. I will give him rest from all his enemies round about. For his name shall be Solomon; and I will give Israel peace and rest in his days.
1CH 22:10 He shall build a house for my name. And he shall be to me a son; and I will be to him a father. And I will establish the throne of his kingdom in Israel forever.
1CH 22:11 Now therefore, my son, the Lord will be with thee, and will prosper thee, and thou shalt build a house for the Lord thy God, as he hath spoken concerning thee.
1CH 22:12 Let but the Lord grant thee wisdom and understanding, and strengthen thee over Israel, that thou mayst keep and perform the law of the Lord thy God;
1CH 22:13 then will he prosper thee, if thou be watchful to execute the statutes, and judgments, which the Lord enjoined on Israel by Moses. Quit thyself like a man, and be strong. Fear not nor be dismayed.
1CH 22:14 Now behold according to my poor ability I have provided for the house of the Lord a hundred talents of gold, and ten hundred talents of silver, and brass and iron without weight, because of their abundance. I have also provided timber and stones, but thou must add thereto.
1CH 22:15 And thou must add to the number of Workmen of whom there are with thee artists, and masons and carpenters and men skilled in every kind of work,
1CH 22:16 of gold and silver and brass and iron, an innumerable number. Up therefore; and fall to work. And the Lord be with thee.
1CH 22:17 David also gave a charge to all the chiefs of Israel to assist his son Solomon, saying,
1CH 22:18 Hath not the Lord been with you, and given you rest all around? For he hath delivered into your hands the inhabitants of this land, and the land is subdued before the Lord, and before his people.
1CH 22:19 Now therefore apply your hearts, and your souls to seek the Lord your God and arise and build a sanctuary for your God, that you may carry the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and the holy vessels of God, into the house to be built for the name of the Lord.
1CH 23:1 When David was old and full of days, and had made Solomon his son king over Israel in his stead,
1CH 23:2 then he assembled all the chiefs of Israel, and the priests and the Levites,
1CH 23:3 and the Levites were numbered, from thirty years old and upwards; and the number of them by their poll, amounted to thirty eight thousand men.
1CH 23:4 Of these, twenty four thousand were for the works for the house of the Lord; and six thousand were scribes and judges;
1CH 23:5 and four thousand were guards of the gates, and four thousand were to praise the Lord with musical instruments, which he had made for praising the Lord.
1CH 23:6 And David distributed them into daily classes, under the heads of Gerson, Kaath and Merari, the sons of Levi.
1CH 23:7 Now to Gerson belonged Edan and Semei;
1CH 23:8 the sons of Edan, were chief Jeiel, and Zethan and Joel, three:
1CH 23:9 the sons of Semei, were Salomith, Jeiel and Dan, three. Those were the chiefs of the families of the Edantes;
1CH 23:10 but the Semeites, had also Jeth and Ziza, and Joas and Beria; these four were sons of Semei,
1CH 23:11 and Jeth was the chief and Ziza the second, and Joas and Beria not having many children were comprehended in one muster, for a house of a family.
1CH 23:12 And the sons of Kaath were Ambram, Issaar, Chebron, Oziel; four.
1CH 23:13 The sons of Ambram were Aaron and Moses. Now Aaron was set apart for the sanctification of the most holy things, he and his sons, to burn incense before the Lord, to minister in the priest's office, and to bless in his name forever
1CH 23:14 But as for Moses the man of God, his sons were classed in the tribe of Levi.
1CH 23:15 The sons of Moses, were Gersam and Eliezer.
1CH 23:16 Of the Gersamites, Subael was chief,
1CH 23:17 and of the Eliezerites, Rabia was chief. Now Eliezer had no other sons; but the sons of Rabia were increased to a multitude.
1CH 23:18 The sons of Issaar, were Salomith the chief.
1CH 23:19 The sons of Chebron, were Jeria the chief, Amaria the second, Jeziel the third, Jekemias the fourth
1CH 23:20 The sons of Oziel, were Micha the chief and Isia the second.
1CH 23:21 The sons of Merari were Mooli and Mousi. The sons of Mooli were Eleazar and Kis.
1CH 23:22 Now Eleazar died, and left no sons, but only daughters. So the sons of Kis, their brethren, took them.
1CH 23:23 The sons of Mousi were Mouli and Eder and Jerimoth, three.
1CH 23:24 These are the sons of Levi, according to the houses of their patriarchal families. The chiefs of these families, according to the review of them, according to the number of their names was polled to perform the works of the service of the house of the Lord, from twenty years old and upwards.
1CH 23:25 For David said, The Lord Cod of Israel hath given his people rest and fixed his abode in Jerusalem forever.
1CH 23:26 So the Levites not having to carry the tabernacle and all the utensils thereof for its service;
1CH 23:27 for this cause by these last orders of David, the Levites are numbered from twenty years old and upwards,
1CH 23:28 for he set them under the superintendance of Aaron to serve in the house of the Lord, over the courts and over the store houses and over the purification of all the holy things, and over the work of the service of the house of God,
1CH 23:29 and for the shew bread, and for the fine flour of the sacrifice and for the unleavened cakes, and for the frying pan, and the mixed sacrifice, and for all kinds of measuring,
1CH 23:30 and to stand every morning to sing praises, and give thanks to the Lord, and the same every evening:
1CH 23:31 and to have charge of all the offerings of homage made to the Lord, on the sabbaths and at the new moons, and at the festivals according to the number, and according to the rule prescribed for them, continually for the Lord.
1CH 23:32 And they are to keep the watch of the tabernacle of the testimony, and to guard the sanctuary, and to guard the sons of Aaron, their brethren, that they may minister as priests, in the house of the Lord.
1CH 24:1 Now with regard to the sons of Aaron in the line of Nadab and of Abiud, and of Eleazar and of Ithamar.
1CH 24:2 As Nadab and Abiud died in the presence of their father and had no sons; and . Eleazar and Ithamar had officiated as priests;
1CH 24:3 David classed Sadok at the head of the sons of Eleazar, and Achimelech at the head of the sons of Ithamar, according to the review of them according to their service, according to the houses of their families.
1CH 24:4 And as the Eleazarites were found to be more numerous for chiefs of mighty men than the sons of Ithamar, therefore he distributed them; for the sons of Eleazar sixteen chiefs for houses of families, and for the sons of Ithamar chiefs for eight houses of families.
1CH 24:5 These he distributed by lot, one with the other. Because there were chiefs of the holies, and chiefs of the Lord, among the sons of Eleazar and among the sons of Ithamar,
1CH 24:6 therefore in the presence of the king and the chiefs, Samaias son of Nathaniel, the muster master of the Levites, wrote down Sadok the priest and Achimelech son of Abiathar, and the chiefs of the families of the priests and the Levites, a chief of a house of families alternately, one for Eleazar and one for Ithamar,
1CH 24:7 and the first lot came out for Joarim; the second for Jedia;
1CH 24:8 the third for Charib; the fourth for Seorim;
1CH 24:9 the fifth for Melchias; the sixth for Meiamin;
1CH 24:10 the seventh for Kos; the eighth for Abia;
1CH 24:11 the ninth for Jesus; the tenth for Sechenias;
1CH 24:12 the eleventh for Eliabi; the twelfth for Jakim;
1CH 24:13 the thirteenth for Oppha; the fourteenth for Jesbaal;

1CH 24:15 the seventeenth for Chesin; the eighteenth for Aphese;
1CH 24:16 the nineteenth for Phetaia; the twentieth for Ezekel;
1CH 24:17 the twenty first for Achim; the twenty second for Gamul;
1CH 24:18 the twenty third for Adallai; the twenty fourth for Maasai.
1CH 24:19 This was the review of them according to their service, to go into the house of the Lord according to the rule prescribed for them, under the inspection of Aaron their father, as the Lord God of Israel commanded Moses.
1CH 24:20 And for the rest of the Levites; for the Ambramites, Sobael; for the sons of Sobael, Jedia;
1CH 24:21 for the Rabiates, the chief.
1CH 24:22 For the Isaarites Salomoth, for the sons of Salomoth, Jath;
1CH 24:23 the sons of Ekdiu; Amadia the second; Jaziel the third; Jekmoam the fourth.
1CH 24:24 For the Ozielites, Micha; for the sons of Micha, Samer;
1CH 24:25 the brother of Micha, Isia; the sons of Isia, Sacharia;
1CH 24:26 the Merarites Mooli and Mousi;
1CH 24:27 the sons of Ozia, to whom belonged the title Merarite; his sons Isoam; and Sakckur, and Abai;
1CH 24:28 for Mooli, Eleazar and Ithamar, now Eleazar died and had no sons,
1CH 24:29 for him Kis; the sons of Kis, Jerameel;
1CH 24:30 the sons of Mousi, Mooli and Eder and Jerimoth, these sons of the Levites according to the houses of their families;
1CH 24:31 they also drew lots as their brethren the sons of Aaron did, in the presence of the king and of Sadok and Achimelech, the senior chiefs of the families both of the priests and the Levites submitting to the lot equally with their younger brethren.
1CH 25:1 Then David the king with the chiefs of this host, appointed to their services the sons of Asaph and Aiman and Idithun, who chanted with kinyras and with nablas and with cymbals, and an account was taken by poll of those employed in these services.
1CH 25:2 The sons of Asaph were Zakchur and Joseph, and Nathanias and Erael. The sons of Asaph were near the king.
1CH 25:3 With Idithun were the sons of Idithun, Godolias and Suri, and Iseas and Asabias, and Matthathias, six after their father Idithim, chanting on kinyras thanksgiving and praise to the Lord.
1CH 25:4 When Aiman were the sons of Aiman, Bukias and Matthanias, and Oziel and Subael, and Jerimoth and Ananias, and Anan and Eliatha, and Godollathi and Rometthiezer, and Jesbasaka and Melithi, and Otheri and Meazoth.
1CH 25:5 All these sons Aiman had with him when he commenced a psalm for the king in the words of God. To exalt the horn God indeed had given Aiman fourteen sons and three daughters.
1CH 25:6 All these with their father, sung in the house of God to cymbals and nablas and kinyras, for the service of the house of God near the king, with Asaph and Idithun and Aiman.
1CH 25:7 And the number of them, including younger brethren, who were instructed to sing to the Lord, even all who were skilled, was two hundred and eighty eight.
1CH 25:8 And they cast lots for their daily courses, as well the younger as the senior, both teachers and scholars.
