NEH 13:1 On reading that day in the book of Moses in the audience of the people, it was found written therein, that the Ammonites and the Moabites should not enter into the congregation of God forever;
NEH 13:2 because they did not meet the Israelites with bread and water; but hired Balaam against them to curse them; but our God turned the curse into a blessing.
NEH 13:3 And when they heard the law, they separated from Israel all the mixed multitude.
NEH 13:4 Now before this, Eliasib the priest, made his dwelling in a store house of the house of our God. Having an affinity with Tobias,
NEH 13:5 he had fitted up for himself a large store house in which they formerly stored up the sacrifice and the frankincense, and the vessels, and the tythe of the corn, and the wine and the oil, the allotment of the Levites and the musicians, and the keepers of the gates, and the oblations which belonged to the priest.
NEH 13:6 But during all that time I was not at Jerusalem. For in the thirty second year of Arthasastha king of Babylon, I went to the king. And at the end of the year, having obtained the king's leave,
NEH 13:7 I came to Jerusalem. When I was informed of the wickedness which Eliasib had committed for the sake of Tobias, in fitting up for him a treasure house in the court of the house of God,
NEH 13:8 it grieved me exceedingly; therefore I threw all the furniture of Tobias out of the treasure house.
NEH 13:9 And when by my orders they had purified the rooms, I caused to be brought there again the utensils of the house of God, and the sacrifice and the incense.
NEH 13:10 And when I understood that the portions of the Levites had not been given them; and that the Levites and the musicians who were employed in the service had fled, every man to his field,
NEH 13:11 I quarrelled with the officers and said, Why is the house of God forsaken?
NEH 13:12 Then I brought them together and set them in their station; and all Juda brought in the tythe of the corn, and the wine, and the oil into the treasuries,
NEH 13:13 under the charge of Selemia the priest, and Sadok the scribe, and Phadaia, one of the Levites, who had for assistants Anan, son Zakchur, son Mathanias, because they were accounted faithful. And it was their business to make distribution among their brethren.
NEH 13:14 Remember me, God, for this; and let not the observance I have paid to the house of the Lord God be blotted out.
NEH 13:15 In those days I saw in Juda some treading wine presses on the sabbath day, and some carrying sheaves, and loading their asses with wine and grapes and figs, and all kinds of burdens, and bringing them to Jerusalem on the sabbath day. Whereupon I testified against them, touching the day of their selling.
NEH 13:16 Some also dwelt there who brought fish, and sold all sorts of wares on the sabbath, to the children of Juda, even in Jerusalem.
NEH 13:17 Upon this I chided the freemen of Juda, and said to them, What evil is this which you do in profaning the sabbath?
NEH 13:18 Did not your fathers do so, and did not our God bring upon them and upon us, and upon this city, all these evils? And are you bringing more wrath upon Israel by profaning the sabbath?
NEH 13:19 And when the gates of Jerusalem were set up, I ordered them to be shut before the sabbath, and gave a charge that they should not be opened till after the sabbath; and I stationed some of my servants at the gates that no burdens might be brought in on the sabbath day.
NEH 13:20 Upon this they all lodged and carried on their traffick without Jerusalem once or twice.
NEH 13:21 Then I testified against them and. said to them, Why do you lodge before the walls? If you do so any more I will lay hands on you. From that time they did not come on the sabbath.
NEH 13:22 Then I ordered the Levites who were sanctified and come to guard the gates, to keep holy the sabbath day. For these things remember me, my God, and have compassion on me according to thy abundant mercy.
NEH 13:23 In those days also I saw the Jews who had married wives of Azotus, of Ammon, and of Moab,
NEH 13:24 and their children spoke half in the dialect of Azotus, and did not know how to speak the Jewish language;
NEH 13:25 and I .quarrelled with them, and reproached them, and smote some men among them, and caused some of them to be shaved, and adjured them by God, saying, You shall not give your daughters to their sons, nor take any of their daughters for your sons.
NEH 13:26 Did not Solomon king of Israel sin by doing so? Though among many nations there was not a king like him? Though he was beloved by God, and God had made him king over all Israel, yet strange women led him astray.
NEH 13:27 Let us not therefore hear of your committing all this iniquity, breaking covenant with our God, and marrying strange women.
NEH 13:28 And one of the sons of Joada the son of Elisub the high priest, being the son in law of Sanaballat the Ouranite, I drove him from me.
NEH 13:29 Put them in mind, God, of their near relation to the priesthood, and of the covenant of the priesthood.
NEH 13:30 As for the Levites I purified them from all connexion with strangers, and appointed the courses of the priests and the Levites, every man according to his business, and the offering of the wood carriers at stated periods, and at the festivals. Remember me God, for good.
EST 1:1 After these things, in the days of Artaxerxes the same who reigned from India, over a hundred and twenty seven provinces,
EST 1:2 when Artaxerxes was settled on his throne in the city Susoi,
EST 1:3 in the third year of his reign, he made an entertainment for his friends, both for other nations, and for the nobles of the Persians and Medes, and for the governors.
EST 1:4 And having after this displayed to them the riches of his kingdom, and the transporting glory of his riches, for a hundred and eighty days,
EST 1:5 when the days of his marriage were fulfilled, the king made an entertainment for all the nations who were in the city, for six days, in the court of the royal palace,
EST 1:6 which was adorned with painted hangings of cotton, extended with cords of cotton, and purple yarn, to capitals of gold and silver, on pillars of parian marble and alabaster. The couches were of gold and silver, on a pavement of smaragdine, pinine, and parian stone; and their covers were of gause, painted with a variety of flowers; and roses were scattered all around.
EST 1:7 The goblets of gold and silver, with a small carbuncled cup to each, amounted in value to thirty thousand talents. There was wine in abundance and of a sweet quality, such as the king himself drank.
EST 1:8 Now this entertainment was not according to an established custom; but the king would have it so, and he commanded the stewards to comply with his pleasure, and that of the guests.
EST 1:9 Astin the queen also made an entertainment for the women in the royal palace, where king Artaxerxes was.
EST 1:10 And on the seventh day, the king, in high good humour, ordered Anian and Basan and Tharra and Barazi and Zatholtha and Abataza and Tharaba, the seven chamberlains, who waited on king Artaxerxes,
EST 1:11 to bring the queen to him to proclaim her queen, and crown her with a diadem, and shew her to the chiefs, and her beauty to the nations; for she was beautiful.
EST 1:12 But queen Astin hearkened not to him to come with the chamberlain, at which the king was greatly offended and inflamed with anger
EST 1:13 and he said to his friends, Astin hath spoken so and so; do you therefore execute law and judgment, touching this matter.
EST 1:14 Thereupon there came before him, Arkesaius and Sarsathaius and Malisear the chiefs of the Persians and Medes, who were5 near the king, and had the first seats next him;
EST 1:15 and told him according to the laws what ought to be done to queen Astin, because she had not done what the king had commanded by the chamberlains.
EST 1:16 And Muchaius said to the king and to the chiefs, Queen Astin hath wronged, not the king only, but also all the king's chiefs and leaders;
EST 1:17 for he hath told them the queen's conduct and how she hath contradicted the king. Therefore as she hath contradicted the king Artaxerxes, so will the rest of the ladies now,
EST 1:18 the wives of the Persian and Medean princes, upon hearing what she hath said to the king, presume in like manner to dishonour their husbands.
EST 1:19 If therefore it seemeth good to the king, let him pass a royal decree and let it be written according to the laws of the Medes and Persians, and let him not alter it nor suffer the queen any more to approach him; but let the king give her royalty to another woman, better than her.
EST 1:20 And let this edict of the king be proclaimed, which if he cause to be done throughout his kingdom, then will all the women both rich and poor, pay respect to their husbands.
EST 1:21 And the speech pleased the king and the princes; and the king did as Muchaius had spoken,
EST 1:22 and sent the decree throughout the whole kingdom, into every province in the language and writing thereof, that men might be feared by their own families.
EST 2:1 After this when the king's wrath was appeased and he no more remembered Astin, nor made any mention of what she had spoken, and how he had condemned her;
EST 2:2 the king's servants said, Let there be sought for the king a virgin of unblemished chastity, and beautiful;
EST 2:3 and let the king appoint officers in all the provinces of his kingdom, and let them select and send to the city Susoi to the house of the women, virgins remarkable for beauty; and let them be delivered to the king's chamberlain, the keeper of the women; and let the things necessary for purification be given them.
EST 2:4 And let the woman who shall please the king be made queen in the room of Astin. And the proposal pleased the king, and he did so.
EST 2:5 Now there was at the city of Susoi, a man, a Jew, whose name was Mordecai. He was the son of Jairus, the son of Semeias, the son of Kisaius, of the tribe of Benjamin.
EST 2:6 He had been carried away captive from Jerusalem among them whom Nabuchodonosar king of Babylon had captivated.
EST 2:7 And this man had a foster child, a daughter of Aminadab, his father's brother; and her name was Esther. On the decease of her parents he educated her to be a wife for himself. But as the girl was beautiful,
EST 2:8 when the decree of the king was published, and many young women were brought to the city Susoi and put under the care of Gai, Esther also was brought to Gai the keeper of the women.
EST 2:9 And the young woman pleased him and found favour in his sight, so that he hastened to give her the things for purification and the allotted portion; and seven waiting maids were assigned to her out of the king's house: and he treated her and her maids courteously in the house of the women.
EST 2:10 Now Esther did not disclose her family, nor her country;
EST 2:11 for Mordecai had charged her not to tell. But Mordecai walked every day before the court of the women"s house to see what would happen to Esther.
EST 2:12 Now the time for every young woman to go to the king was when she had compleated twelve months; for thus were the days of their purification fulfilled. Six months they were anointed with oil of myrrh, and six months with aromatics and lotions used by women.
EST 2:13 Then she goeth in to the king. The keeper is to deliver her to whomsoever the king ordereth to go with her from the women"s apartment to the king's house.
EST 2:14 In the evening she goeth in, and in the morning goeth with all speed to the second house of the women, which is under the care of Gai the king's chamberlain, the keeper of the women, and no more cometh to the king unless called for by name.
EST 2:15 So when the time was fulfilled for Esther the daughter of Aminadab, Mordecai's uncle, to go to the king, she neglected nothing which the chamberlain the keeper of the women ordered her; for Esther found favour with all who saw her.
EST 2:16 And Esther went in to Artaxerxes the king, in the twelfth month which is the month Adar in the seventh year of his reign.
EST 2:17 And the king was enamoured of Esther, and she found favour above all the virgins, so that he set the queen's crown on her head
EST 2:18 and made an entertainment for all his friends and potentates for seven days, and to celebrate the marriage of Esther he made a release to those under his government.
EST 2:19 Now Mordecai performed service in the court,
EST 2:20 and Esther had not yet declared her family, for Mordecai having charged her in this manner to fear God and execute his commands as when she was with him, Esther did not alter her conduct.
EST 2:21 And two of the king's chamberlains, who were captains of his life guard, being displeased because Mordecai was promoted, sought to kill king Artaxerxes.
EST 2:22 But the matter being made known to Mordecai, he informed Esther and she disclosed the conspiracy to the king;
EST 2:23 whereupon the king having examined the chamberlains, caused them to be hanged, and ordered a record to be made in the royal library with an encomium on Mordecai's fidelity.
EST 3:1 After these things king Artaxerxes honoured Haman of Amadathus the Bougaian, and promoted him, and seated him first of all his friends,
EST 3:2 so that all the court bowed down to him for so the king had commanded to be done. But Mordecai did not bow down to him;
EST 3:3 whereupon they who were in the king's court said to him, Mordecai, Why trangressest thou the king's commands.
EST 3:4 And when they spoke to him daily and he hearkened not to them, they told Hainan, that Mordecai disobeyed the king's commands. Now Mordecai had told them that he was a Jew.
EST 3:5 So when Haman understood that Mordecai did not bow down to him,
EST 3:6 he was greatly inflamed with wrath, and determined to destroy all the Jews throughout the whole kingdom of Artaxerxes.
EST 3:7 And having drawn up a decree in the twelfth year of the reign of Artaxerxes, he cast lots for one day after another and for one month after another so as to destroy the whole race of Mordecai in one day. And the lot having fallen on the fourteenth day of the month Adar,
EST 3:8 he spoke to king Artaxerxes, saying, There is a nation scattered among the nations throughout thy whole kingdom, whose laws differ from all the nations. And as they disobey the king's laws and it is not expedient for the king to let them alone;
EST 3:9 if it seemeth good to the king, let him pass a decree to destroy them and I will subscribe ten thousand talents of silver to the king's treasury.
EST 3:10 Thereupon the king taking off his ring gave it to Haman to seal the writings against the Jews.
EST 3:11 And the king said to Haman, Keep the money, and do with the nation what thou pleasest.
EST 3:12 So the king's secretaries were convened on the thirteenth day of the first month, and they wrote as Haman directed to the generals and the governors in every province, from India to Ethiopia a hundred and twenty seven provinces, and to the chiefs of the nations according to their dialect in the name of king Artaxerxes,
EST 3:13 and the decree was despatched by posts throughout the whole kingdom of Artaxerxes, to destroy the race of the Jews on a certain day of the twelfth month which is Adar, and to make spoil of their goods.
EST 3:14 And copies of the decree were to be sent through every province and all the nations were ordered to be ready against that day.
EST 3:15 And when the business was despatched at Susoi, the king and Haman sat down to revel, but the city was struck with consternation.
EST 4:1 Now when Mordecai knew what was done, he rent his clothes and put on sackcloth and strewed himself with ashes, and running through the street of the city, he cried with a loud voice, A nation is to be cut off, which hath committed no fault.
EST 4:2 But when he came to the king's gate, he stopped; for it was not lawful for him to enter the court in sackcloth and ashes.
EST 4:3 And in every country where the writings were published there was a cry with lamentation and great grief among the Jews, and they put on sackcloth and ashes.
EST 4:4 When the queen's maids and chamberlains came in and told her, she was troubled at the news, and sent to clothe Mordecai and to take away his sackcloth from him; but he would not be persuaded.
EST 4:5 Then Esther called Achrathaius her chamberlain, who attended her, and sent him to learn from Mordecai an exact state of the matter.
EST 4:6 [Omitted]
EST 4:7 Whereupon Mordecai told him what was done and the promise which Haman had made to the king of ten thousand talents to the royal treasury, that he might destroy the Jews;
EST 4:8 and he gave him a copy of the decree for their destruction, which was published among the Susians to shew it to Esther, and told him that he charged her to go in and supplicate the king and to entreat him for the people, calling to mind the days of thy humiliation when thou wast brought up by my bounty. Seeing Haman who is second to the king, hath spoken against us to destroy us, call thou upon the Lord and speak to the king for us, to deliver us from death.
EST 4:9 Accordingly Achrathaius went in and told her all these words.
EST 4:10 Thereupon Esther said to him, Go to Mordecai and tell him,
EST 4:11 that all the nations of the kingdom know, that no man or woman who shall go to the king into the inner court without being sent for, hath any security for life: he only can be saved to whom the king shall stretch forth the golden sceptre. Now I have not been called to go to the king these thirty days.
EST 4:12 When Achrathaius delivered this message of Esther to Mordecai,
EST 4:13 Mordecai said to him, Go say to her, Esther, do not flatter thyself that thou alone of all the Jews in the kingdom shall escape.
EST 4:14 Be assured, that if thou neglectest the present opportunity, help and protection will come to the Jews from some other quarter; but thou and thy father's house shall be destroyed. Who knoweth but that for this very occasion thou hast been made queen.
EST 4:15 Then Esther sent back the messenger to Mordecai, saying,
EST 4:16 Go and assemble the Jews who are at Susoi and fast for me. You must neither eat nor drink for three days; night nor day; and as for me, I and my maids will fast likewise, and then I will go to the king contrary to law, though perhaps I must die.
EST 4:17 So Mordecai went and did as Esther commanded him.
EST 5:1 And on the third day Esther put on her royal apparel and stood in the inner court of the king's palace over against the king's house, when the king was sitting on his royal throne, in the royal house, over against the gate.
EST 5:2 And when the king saw Esther standing in the court, she obtained favour in his sight, and the king held out to Esther the golden sceptre which was in his hand, and Esther drew near and touched the top of the sceptre.
EST 5:3 And the king said, What would queen Esther? And what is thy petition? To the half of my kingdom it shall be granted thee.
EST 5:4 Thereupon Esther said, To-day is my set day, if therefore it seemeth good to the king, let him come with Hainan to the banquet which I will this day prepare.
EST 5:5 And the king said, Call Haman quickly that we may do as Esther hath said. So they both went to the banquet which Esther had ordered.
EST 5:6 And at the banquet the king said to Esther, What would queen Esther? Whatever thou askest shall be granted.
EST 5:7 To which she replied,
EST 5:8 If I have found favour in the sight of the king, Let the king come again with Haman to-morrow to the banquet which I will prepare for them, and to-morrow I will make my request and my petition.
EST 5:9 Then Haman went out from the king overjoyed and gladdened, but upon seeing Mordecai the Jew in the court, he was inflamed with great indignation.
EST 5:10 So going home, he called his friends and his wife Zosara,
EST 5:11 and having displayed to them his riches and the honour which the king had conferred on him; how he had promoted him to the highest rank and made him ruler of the kingdom,
EST 5:12 the queen, said he, invited none to the banquet with the king, but only me: and to-morrow I am invited:
EST 5:13 but these things give me no pleasure, when I see Mordecai the Jew in the court.
EST 5:14 Thereupon Zosara his wife and his friends said to him, Let a gallows fifty cubits high be made for thee, and early in the morning speak to the king and let Mordecai be hanged thereon, then go to the banquet with the king and take thy fill of joy. And the thing pleased Haman. So the gallows was got ready.
EST 6:1 Now on that night the Lord removed sleep from the king, therefore he ordered his attendant to bring the book of daily records, and read to him;
EST 6:2 and finding what was written concerning Mordecai, how he had informed the king of the king's two chamberlains, when they commanded the guard, and sought to lay hands on Artaxerxes,
EST 6:3 the king said, What honour or favour did we confer on Mordecai? To which the king's servants replied, Thou hast conferred none.
EST 6:4 And while the king was making inquiry concerning Mordecai's fidelity behold Haman was in the court. And the king said, Who is in the court? Now Haman had come to speak to the king, that he might order Mordecai to be hanged on the gallows which he had prepared.
EST 6:5 So the king's servants said, Behold Haman is standing in the court, and the king said, Call him in.
EST 6:6 And the king said to Haman, What shall I do to the man whom I wish to honour? Upon this Haman said to himself, Whom doth the king wish to honour but me?
EST 6:7 So he said to the king, With regard to the man whom the king wisheth to honour,
EST 6:8 Let the king's servants bring out the royal robes with which the king is arrayed, and the horse on which the king rideth, and give them to one of the most honourable of the king's friends,
EST 6:9 and let him array the man whom the king loveth, and mount him on the horse, and make proclamation through the street of the city saying, Thus shall it be done to every man whom the king honoureth.
EST 6:10 Then the king said to Haman, Thou hast spoken well, Do thou so to Mordecai the Jew, who is an attendant in the court. Let nothing be omitted of what thou hast spoken.
EST 6:11 So Haman took the robe and the horse, and having arrayed Mordecai he mounted him on the horse, and went through the street of the city and made proclamation saying, Thus shall it be done to every man whom the king wisheth to honour.
EST 6:12 Then Mordecai returned to the court, and Haman went home in grief with his head covered.
EST 6:13 And when Haman told his wife and his friends all that had happened to him; his friends and his wife said, If Mordecai be of the race of the Jews thy humiliation before him is begun. Thou shalt continue falling and shalt not be able to have thy revenge of him; for with him is the living God.
EST 6:14 And while they were speaking the chamberlains came to hasten Haman to the banquet which Esther had prepared.
EST 7:1 And when the king came with Haman to banquet with the queen,
EST 7:2 the king said to Esther the second day at the banquet, What is it queen Esther? What is thy request, and what thy petition? to the half of my kingdom it shall be granted thee.
EST 7:3 Thereupon she in reply said, If I have found favour in the sight of the king, let my life be granted at my request, and my people at my petition;
EST 7:4 for I and my people are sold to be destroyed. Had it been to be plundered and reduced to slavery; that we and our children should be bondmen and bondwomen, I would have dissembled hearing it, for the accuser is not worthy of the king's court.
EST 7:5 And the king said, Who is he who hath dared to do such a thing?
EST 7:6 To which Esther replied, The adversary is Haman, this bad man. At this Haman was struck with consternation for fear of the king and the queen.
EST 7:7 Then the king rising from the banquet went into the garden, and Haman supplicated the queen, for he saw himself in a desperate situation.
EST 7:8 And on the king's returning out of the garden as Haman had prostrated himself on the sopha to supplicate the queen, the king said, What! would he offer violence to my wife in my house? Upon hearing this Haman was confounded.
EST 7:9 Then Bugathan one of the chamberlains said to the king, Behold Hainan hath prepared a gallows for Mordecai who spoke for the king. There is at Haman's house a gallows actually erected fifty cubits high. Thereupon the king said, Let him be hanged thereon.
EST 7:10 So Haman was hanged on the gallows which he had prepared for Mordecai, and the king's anger was appeased.
EST 8:1 And on that same day the king made a present to Esther of all that belonged to Haman the accuser. And the king sent for Mordecai; [for Esther told him that he was her kinsman;]
EST 8:2 and the king took the ring which he had taken back from Haman and gave it to Mordecai, and Esther set him over all that belonged to Haman.
EST 8:3 Then she spoke to the king again and fell at his feet and besought him to avert the mischief of Haman, and what he had devised against the Jews.
EST 8:4 And when the king stretched forth the golden sceptre to Esther, she arose and stood near the king
EST 8:5 and said, If it seemeth good to thee, and I have found favour, let despatches be sent to reverse the letters sent by Haman, which were written to destroy the Jews who are in thy kingdom.
EST 8:6 For how can I see the calamity of my people? or how can I survive the destruction of my kindred?
EST 8:7 Thereupon the king said to Esther, If I have given thee all the substance of Haman; and to gratify thee have caused him to be hanged on a gallows, because he laid his hands on the Jews, what more dost thou desire?
EST 8:8 Write ye yourselves what you please in my name, and seal it with my ring. For what is written by the king's order, and sealed with my ring cannot be reversed.
EST 8:9 So the secretaries were convened in the first month which is Nisan, on the three and twentieth day thereof in the same year, and a letter was written to the Jews reciting all that had been given in charge to the lieutenants and to the chief governors of the provinces from India to Ethiopia, a hundred and twenty seven provinces, to every province as they could read it,
EST 8:10 then it was written by the king's command and sealed with his ring, [and these letters were sent by posts]
EST 8:11 that he ordered them to use their own laws in every city, and to assist each other, and to use their adversaries, and them who assaulted them as they pleased,
EST 8:12 on a certain day, the thirteenth of the twelfth month Adar, throughout the whole kingdom of
EST 8:13 Artaxerxes; that these subsequent writings were to counterbalance the former letter; and that these counterbalancing writings should be exposed to publick view throughout the whole kingdom, that the Jews might be ready against that day to combat their adversaries.
EST 8:14 So the horsemen set out in all haste to execute the king's orders. And when the decree was published at Susoi,
EST 8:15 Mordecai went forth, arrayed in a royal robe, wearing a crown of gold and a turban of purple cotton. And upon seeing him the inhabitants of Susoi rejoiced.
EST 8:16 And among the Jews, there was light and joy in every city and province where the decree was published.
EST 8:17 Wherever proclamation was made, there was joy and gladness among the Jews, feasting and mirth; so that many of the nations were circumcised and became Jews, for fear of the Jews.
EST 9:1 For in the twelfth month, on the thirteenth of the month Adar, the letters of the king having arrived,
EST 9:2 they who assaulted the Jews on that day were destroyed. For none withstood them and the terror of them continued;
EST 9:3 for the great lords and petty princes, and the king's secretaries, honoured the Jews; for the dread of Mordecai fell upon them;
EST 9:4 for the decree of the king had caused his name to be known throughout the whole kingdom.
EST 9:5 [Omitted]
EST 9:6 Now in the city Susoi, the Jews slew five hundred men,
EST 9:7 including Pharsanes and Delphon, and Phasga
EST 9:8 and Pharadatha, and Barea and Sarbaka,
EST 9:9 and Marmasima and Ruphaias, and Arsaius and Zabuthaias,
EST 9:10 the ten sons of Hainan of Amadathu the Bugaian, the enemy of the Jews, and rifled them.
EST 9:11 On that very day, when a return was made to the king of the number slain at Susoi,
EST 9:12 the king said to Esther, The Jews have slain in the city Susoi five hundred men, how then, thinkest thou, have they behaved in the rest of the kingdom! What therefore dost thou request farther, and it shall be granted thee?
EST 9:13 Thereupon Esther said to the king, Let the Jews be allowed to use to-morrow in like manner, that they may hang up the ten sons of Haman.
EST 9:14 Accordingly he granted them leave to do so, and ordered the bodies of the ten sons of Hainan, to be thrown out to the Jews to be hanged up.
EST 9:15 So the Jews at Susoi assembled on the fourteenth day of the month Adar, and slew three hundred men, but took no spoil.
EST 9:16 Now the rest of the Jews who were in the kingdom, assembled and assisted each other, and had rest from their enemies, for they slew fifteen thousand of them on the thirteenth of the month Adar, but took no spoil.
EST 9:17 And having rested on the fourteenth of the month, they kept it as a day of rest with joy and gladness.
EST 9:18 But the Jews of Susoi having assembled on the fourteenth and then rested, kept the fifteenth with joy and gladness.
EST 9:19 Therefore because the Jews, who were scattered through all the distant provinces, keep the fourteenth of the month Adar, as a holy day, with joy, sending portions to one another,
EST 9:20 Mordecai wrote an account of these matters in a book, and sent it to all the Jews who were in the kingdom of Artaxerxes far and near,
EST 9:21 to set apart as holy days and to keep both the fourteenth and the fifteenth of the month Adar,
EST 9:22 for in those days the Jews had rest from their enemies: And with regard to the month Adar, in which they had a change from grief to joy and from sorrow to gladness, to keep the whole month as good days of weddings and joy, sending portions to their friends and to the poor.
EST 9:23 And the Jews took this upon them. As Mordecai wrote to them
EST 9:24 how Haman of Amadathu, the Macedonian, warred against them; as he made calculations and cast lots to destroy them,
EST 9:25 and as he went to the king with an intention to hang Mordecai, but all the evils he endeavoured to bring on the Jews, fell upon himself, and he and his sons were hanged;
EST 9:26 therefore these days were called Phrouri, because of the lots, which in their language are called Phrouri. On the account of the things contained in that letter and of all that they suffered in consequence thereof, and all that happened to them, as he instituted,
EST 9:27 so the Jews took upon themselves and their posterity, and upon all that joined them, never to use them in any other manner.
EST 9:28 Therefore let these days be a lasting memorial from generation to generation, in every city, country and province; and let these days of Phrouri be kept forever; and let the memorial of them never perish from among their generations.
EST 9:29 Then Esther the queen, the daughter of. Aminadab, and Mordecai the Jew, wrote all that they did, and a confirmation of the letter respecting the Phrouri,
EST 9:30 [Omitted]
EST 9:31 which Mordecai and Esther the queen enjoined on themselves, to their own prejudice, having at that time established their counsel against their health.
EST 9:32 Thus did Esther actually establish it, and it was written to be kept in remembrance.
EST 10:1 Then the king laid a tribute upon the dominion both of the land and the sea.
EST 10:2 But with regard to his power and his valour and the riches and the glory of his kingdom, behold they are written in the book of the kings of the Persians and the Medes to be kept in remembrance.
EST 10:3 Now Mordecai was viceroy of king Artaxerxes, and was great in the kingdom, and being honoured by the Jews and beloved, he enforced the observance of their religion on all his nation. And Mordecai said, These things have been done by God; for I remember the dream I had concerning these matters, and not one particular has failed [to occur]. A little fountain became a river, and there was light, and the sun, and much water. This river is Esther, whom the king married, and made queen; and the two dragons are myself and Haman. And the nations were those that gathered to destroy the name of the Jews; and my nation is Israel, they that cried unto God and were delivered. For the Lord hath delivered His people, and the Lord hath saved us from all these evils. And God hath wrought signs and great wonders that have not been performed among the gentiles. Therefore hath he ordained two lots; one for the people of God and another for all the gentiles. And these two lots came in an hour and time and day of judgment before the face of God, and for all nations. And God remembered His people, and vindicated His inheritance. And they shall observe those days in the month Adar-the fourteenth and fifteenth day of the month-with an assembly, and joy and gladness before God, among His people Israel throughout the generations forever. In the fourth year of the reign of Ptolemy and Cleopatra, Dositheos, who said he was a priest and a Levite, and his son, Ptolemy, brought this published epistle of Phrurai, which they said was the same [as the original by Mordecai], and which Lysimachos, the son of Ptolemy [Dositheos' son], had interpreted.
JOB 1:1 There was a man in the country of Ausitis whose name was Job. He was a man of truth and integrity, just, pious, and who abstained from every thing that was evil.
JOB 1:2 He had seven sons and three daughters; and his cattle were seven thousand sheep, three thousand camels, five hundred yoke of oxen, five hundred breeding asses.
JOB 1:3 His attendants were numerous, and his works great in the country. He was also a man of illustrious birth, among the people of the east.
JOB 1:4 Now his sons had a custom of meeting at each others houses, and making an entertainment, each on his day, taking along with them their three sisters to eat and drink with them.
JOB 1:5 And soon as the days of the entertainment were over, Job sent for, and purified them early the next morning, and offered sacrifices for them according to their numbers; a young bull for a sin offering for each of them; for Job said, Perhaps my children have in their mind conceived evil before God. In this manner therefore Job acted after every of those days.
JOB 1:6 And it came to pass that on the same day, when lo! the angels of God came to present themselves before the Lord, Satan also came with them;
JOB 1:7 and the Lord said to Satan, Whence comest thou? And Satan in reply said to the Lord, Having gone round the earth, and roved the whole of it under heaven, I am come here.
JOB 1:8 And the Lord said to him, Hast thou harboured in thy mind any thing against my servant Job? For there is not like him on the earth, a man unblameable, true, pious, abstaining from every thing evil.
JOB 1:9 And Satan in reply said before the Lord, Doth Job worship the Lord for nothing?
JOB 1:10 Hast thou not made a hedge about all that he hath, abroad and at home, and about all that belong to him round about, and blessed the works of his hands, and multiplied his cattle on the earth?
JOB 1:11 But put forth thine hand and touch all that he hath, he will indeed openly renounce thee.
JOB 1:12 Then the Lord said to Satan, Behold all that he hath I deliver into thine hand; but himself thou must not touch. So Satan went out from the Lord,
JOB 1:13 and after that, on the same day, when the sons and daughters of Job were drinking wine at their elder brother's house,
JOB 1:14 lo! a messenger came to Job, and said to him, The oxen were ploughing and the asses feeding near them,
JOB 1:15 and the plunderers came and carried them off. Thy servants also they slew with the sword, and I alone having escaped, am come to tell thee.
JOB 1:16 While he was yet speaking, another messenger came, and said to Job; Fire hath fallen from heaven and burned up the sheep, and devoured the shepherds likewise; and I, alone having escaped, am come to tell thee.
JOB 1:17 While this one was still speaking, another messenger came and said to Job, The horsemen, having formed three bands against us, surrounded the camels and have carried them off, and slain thy servants with the sword; and I, alone having escaped, am come to tell thee.
JOB 1:18 While he was still speaking, another messenger came, and said to Job, While thy sons and thy daughters were eating and drinking at their eldest brother's,
JOB 1:19 a great blast of wind came up suddenly from the wilderness, and took the four corners of the house, so that the house fell upon thy children, and they are dead, and I, alone having escaped, am come to tell thee.
JOB 1:20 Upon this Job rising up rent his clothes, and shaved his head, and falling on the ground he worshipped
JOB 1:21 and said, Naked I came from my mother's womb, and naked I shall depart hence. The Lord gave and the Lord hath taken away. As it pleased the Lord so hath it come to pass. Blessed be the name of the Lord.
JOB 1:22 In all these things which befel him, Job transgressed not against the Lord, nor imputed indiscretion to his God.
JOB 2:1 Again on the day when the angels of God came to present themselves before the Lord, Satan also came among them to present himself before the Lord.
JOB 2:2 And the Lord said to Satan, Whence comest thou? And Satan said before the Lord, Having traversed that under heaven, and roved through the whole of it, I am come here
JOB 2:3 And the Lord said to Satan, Thou hast therefore attended to my servant Job; that there is not of those on the earth a man like him, guiltless, true, unblameable, abstaining from all evil. Still he retaineth his innocence; so that thou hast ordered the destruction of his property, without accomplishing thy purpose.
JOB 2:4 In reply to which Satan said to the Lord, Skin for skin. All that a man hath he will give for his life.
JOB 2:5 Only put forth thy hand, and touch his bones and his flesh, he will indeed openly renounce thee.
JOB 2:6 Then the Lord said to Satan, Behold I deliver him up to thee, only preserve his life.
JOB 2:7 Thereupon Satan withdrew from the presence of the Lord, and smote Job with foul ulcers from head to foot,
JOB 2:8 so that he took a shell to scrape away the ichor, and sat down in an unclean place without the city.
JOB 2:9 And much time having elapsed, his wife said to him, How long wilt thou persist saying, Behold I will wait yet a little longer, in hope and expectation of my deliverance? For behold the memorial of thee; those sons and daughters, whom I brought forth with pangs and sorrow, and for whom I toiled in vain, are vanished from the earth; and thou thyself sittest among the putrefaction of worms, all night long in the open air, while I am wandering about, or working for wages, from place to place and from house to house, wishing for the setting of the sun, that I may rest from the labours and sorrows I endure. Do but say something for the Lord and die.
JOB 2:10 Whereupon he looking stedfastly at her said, Like one of the women without understanding hast thou spoken? If we have received good things at the hand of the Lord, shall we not bear up under afflictions? In all these things which befel him, Job transgressed not with his lips against God.
JOB 2:11 Now when his three friends heard of all the calamities which were come upon him, they came to him each from his own country, namely, Eliphaz the king of the Thaimanites, Baldad the sovereign of the Saucheans, and Sophar the king of the Minaians. Having made an appointment they came to him to comfort and take care of him,
JOB 2:12 but seeing him at a distance they did not know him. Then raising their voices they wept aloud, and having rent each his robe and sprinkled themselves with dust,
JOB 2:13 they sat down by him seven days and seven nights. And none of them spoke. For they saw that the stroke was grievous and very great.
JOB 3:1 After this Job opened his mouth and cursed his day,
JOB 3:2 saying,
JOB 3:3 Perish the day in which I was born; and the night in which they said, It is a male!
JOB 3:4 Let that night be darkness: let not the Lord from above regard it, nor splendour come upon it:
JOB 3:5 but let darkness and the shadow of death cover it: upon it let there come a thick darkness. May the day be execrated!
JOB 3:6 And as for that night, may a pitchy darkness sweep it away! May that never come into the days of the year; nor be numbered among the days of months.
JOB 3:7 But as for that night, may it be sorrow, and may there never come upon it gladness or mirth!
JOB 3:8 But let him curse it who curseth the day; him who is to attack the great sea monster.
JOB 3:9 May the stars of that night be obscured in darkness: may it long for light but never reach it; nor see the rising of the morning star:
JOB 3:10 because it shut not up the door of my mother's womb: for that would have removed sorrow from mine eyes:
JOB 3:11 for why did I not end my days in the womb? Or when I came forth from the belly why did I not instantly perish?
JOB 3:12 Why was I dandled upon the knees? And why have I sucked the breasts?
JOB 3:13 I might now have lain still and been quiet; I might have gone to sleep and been at rest;
JOB 3:14 with despots of the earth who gloried in their swords:
JOB 3:15 or with chiefs who abounded in gold; who filled their houses with silver;
JOB 3:16 or like an untimely birth sent forth from its mother's womb: or like infants which never saw the light.
JOB 3:17 There the wicked have ceased to be a terror: there the weary have got rest for their body:
JOB 3:18 and they of old who are assembled there together; have never heard the exactor's voice.
JOB 3:19 Small and great are there on a level; the servant, with his dreaded lord.
JOB 3:20 For why is light given to them in misery; or life to souls distressed with sorrow,
JOB 3:21 who long for death but find it not; though they dig for it as for treasures;
JOB 3:22 and would rejoice exceedingly if they should chance to find it.
JOB 3:23 For God hath shut up death from a man; to whom it would have been a repose.
JOB 3:24 For my groaning cometh before my meat; and I pour forth tears, begirt with sorrow.
JOB 3:25 For the terror, which I dreaded, is come upon me; and that, of which I was afraid, hath befallen me.
JOB 3:26 Did I not cultivate peace? was I not quiet? was I not at rest? Yet wrath is come upon me.
JOB 4:1 Here Eliphaz the Thaimianite interrupting him, said,
JOB 4:2 Should frequent replies be made to thee in distress? But o who can bear the vehemence of thy words?
JOB 4:3 For if thou hast instructed many; and strengthened hands which were weak; and raised up with words them who were fainting;
JOB 4:4 and given courage to knees which were strengthless:
JOB 4:5 but now, when trouble hath come upon thee and touched thee, thou art impatient:
JOB 4:6 is not either thy fear grounded on folly; or thy hope? And this calamity the effect of thy conduct?
JOB 4:7 Recollect therefore. Who ever perished, being innocent? Or when were the righteous utterly destroyed?
JOB 4:8 As I have seen men ploughing improper grounds: they who sow such places shall reap sorrows.
JOB 4:9 By the decree of the Lord they shall perish; and by the blast of his ire be utterly consumed.
JOB 4:10 The strength of a lion and the roaring of a lioness and the boastful pride of dragons have been extinguished.
JOB 4:11 The myrmekoleon hath perished for want of food: and young lions have forsaken each other.
JOB 4:12 But had there been any truth in thy words; none of these evils would have happened to thee.
JOB 4:13 Should not my ear receive unusual things coming from him? At a dreadful sound by night, when terror appalleth men,
JOB 4:14 I was seized with a horror and trembling, which gave a violent shog to my bones.
JOB 4:15 A wind indeed blew full in my face, and my hair stood erect and my flesh quivered.
JOB 4:16 I started up, but could perceive nothing: I looked, but there was no form before my eyes. I only heard a sound and a voice, saying:
JOB 4:17 "What! can a mortal be pure before the Lord, or a man by his works be blameless?"
JOB 4:18 If in his servants he placeth not confidence, and in his angels perceiveth some blemish:
JOB 4:19 how should he treat them who dwell in houses of clay, [of which clay we indeed are] but as worms?
JOB 4:20 but from morning till noon: and they are no more.
JOB 4:21 Because they could not help themselves they were destroyed. For he blowed on them and they withered: they perished because they had not wisdom.
JOB 5:1 Appeal now, will any one answer. Or shalt thou see any of the holy angels?
JOB 5:2 Passion indeed transporteth the foolish, and envy killeth the wanderer.
JOB 5:3 Now I have seen the foolish taking root, but their sustenance was quickly consumed.
JOB 5:4 Let their children be but far from safety, and insulted at the gates of minors, there will then be none to deliver them.
JOB 5:5 For what they have collected the righteous shall eat. Nor will they themselves be exempt from wrongs, should their power be exhausted.
JOB 5:6 For trouble cannot come forth out of the earth; nor will affliction spring up from mountains.
JOB 5:7 [a] But man is born for trouble, as the young of the vulture soar aloft,
JOB 5:8 [b] No, indeed; but notwithstanding this, let me supplicate the Lord. And call upon the Lord, the master of all,
JOB 5:9 who doth great and unsearchable things; things glorious and wonderful, not to be numbered.
JOB 5:10 Who giveth rain on the earth and sendeth water on all under heaven.
JOB 5:11 Who setteth on high them who are low, and raiseth up them who have been ruined.
JOB 5:12 Who changeth the counsels of the crafty, so that their hands can perform no enterprise.
JOB 5:13 Who entangleth the wise in their wisdom, and defeateth the counsel of the artful.
JOB 5:14 In the day time, darkness shall meet them, that they may grope at noon day as at night,
JOB 5:15 and that they may perish in battle, and the weak escape from the hand of the mighty.
JOB 5:16 And that the feeble may have hope, and the mouth of the wicked be stopped.
JOB 5:17 But happy the man whom the Lord correcteth. Therefore despise not thou the correction of the Almighty.
JOB 5:18 For He causeth pain and again removeth it: and him whom he smote, his hands have healed.
JOB 5:19 From six distresses he will deliver thee, and in the seventh evil shall not touch thee.
JOB 5:20 In famine he will deliver thee from death, and in battle save thee from the edge of the sword.
JOB 5:21 He will hide thee from the scourge of the tongue: and thou need'st not be afraid of impending ills.
JOB 5:22 At the wicked and unrighteous thou shalt laugh;
JOB 5:23 and of savage beasts need'st not be afraid; for the beasts of the field shall be at peace with thee.
JOB 5:24 Thou shalt know that thy family is at peace, [a] An objection. [b] The answer. and that the provision for thy household shall not fail.
JOB 5:25 Thou shalt know also that thy seed shall be great: thy children shall be like the grass of the field.
JOB 5:26 And thou shalt come to the grave like ripe grain cut in due season; or like a heap from a threshing floor, carried home in time.
JOB 5:27 Behold these are the things which, by investigation, we have found to be so. These are things which we have heard: apply them to thyself, if thou hast done any thing.
JOB 6:1 To this, Job in reply said,
JOB 6:2 that some person would weigh my passion: and poise in a balance against it, my calamities.
JOB 6:3 But these would outweigh the sand of the sea, though you seem to think my words too vehement:
JOB 6:4 for the arrows of the Lord are in my body, the fury of which drinketh up my blood: when I attempt to speak they pierce me.
JOB 6:5 What! will a wild ass bray without cause? Will it do so, except when in search of food? Or will an ox low having fodder in his stall?
JOB 6:6 Can bread be eaten without salt, or is there any relish in vain words?
JOB 6:7 For my temper cannot be calm, while my meat is horrible as the smell of a lion.
JOB 6:8 O that he would grant! that my request might be complied with! that the Lord would grant me what I long for!
JOB 6:9 Let the Lord, having begun, wound me, but not utterly destroy me.
JOB 6:10 Let but the grave be my city, having got on its walls I will not be slack to enter, for I have not disputed the holy commands of my God.
JOB 6:11 For what is my strength that I should bear up! what my time2 that my life is prolonged?
JOB 6:12 Is my strength the strength of stones, or is this flesh of mine made of brass?
JOB 6:13 Or have I not confided in him? But help is far from me.
JOB 6:14 Mercy hath bidden me adieu. When the superintending care of the Lord overlooked me,
JOB 6:15 my nearest friends did not regard me: like a failing brook, or like a wave of the sea, they passed me by.
JOB 6:16 They who had assiduously paid me court, now made me a slight visit, like snow or hoar frost,
JOB 6:17 which melting at the approach of heat, the place where it was is not known.
JOB 6:18 Thus was I forsaken by all, and being undone, I became an outcast.
JOB 6:19 Take a view of the ways of the Thaimanites, ye who mark out the Sabean tracks!
JOB 6:20 and they who trust in cities and wealth must blush. But now when you have come to me, it is without compassion;
JOB 6:21 just to see my wound and be terrified. But why?
JOB 6:22 Have I asked anything of you, or do I crave any help from you?
JOB 6:23 to save me from mine enemies; or deliver me out of the hand of the mighty?
JOB 6:24 Teach me and I will hold my tongue. If I have erred, tell me plainly.
JOB 6:25 But my words, it seems, are devoid of truth, because I do not beg assistance from you.
JOB 6:26 Your reproof can neither stop my speaking, nor can I bear the tone of your oration:
JOB 6:27 because, you not only fall upon the orphan, but also insult your friend.
JOB 6:28 But now having looked you in the face I will not lie.
JOB 6:29 Sit down I pray you, and let there be no more reproaches. Indeed you again meet a righteous man.
JOB 6:30 For there are no reproaches on my tongue, and as for my palate, doth it not relish wisdom?
JOB 7:1 Is not the life of man on the earth a state of trial, and his days like the days of a hireling?
JOB 7:2 Is he not like a servant, who in a shade is afraid of his lord? Or like a hireling waiting for his hire?
JOB 7:3 Just so have I waited months in vain, and wearisome nights have been doled out to me.
JOB 7:4 When I lay me down to rest, I say, When will it be day? And soon as I rise; I again say, When will it be evening? I am full of pains from evening till morning;
JOB 7:5 and my body swarms with the putrefaction of worms: and I moisten the clods of earth with the ichor of ulcers.
JOB 7:6 Though my life is swifter than a word; yet it is destroyed with vain hope.
JOB 7:7 Remember therefore that my life is but a breath; and that mine eyes shall never return again to see good.
JOB 7:8 The eye of him who seeth me now shall not see me again. Thine eyes are upon me and I am gone.
JOB 7:9 I am like a cloud swept clean away from the sky. For when a man goeth down to the mansion of the dead;
JOB 7:10 he can never reascend again; he can never return again to his own house; nor shall his place know him any more.
JOB 7:11 For this cause then I will not refrain my mouth: I will speak though I am in anguish: though distressed, I will unfold the bitterness of my soul.
JOB 7:12 Am I a sea or a dragon, that thou hast set a guard over me?
JOB 7:13 Did I say my bed will comfort me; I will converse with myself privately on my bed?
JOB 7:14 Thou terrifiest me with dreams and affrightest me with visions.
JOB 7:15 Wilt thou drive away my life from my spirit; and yet keep my bones from death?
JOB 7:16 For I am not to live forever, that I should bear patiently. Withdraw from me; for my life is vanity.
JOB 7:17 For what is man, that thou hast magnified him; or that thou payest attention to him?
JOB 7:18 Wilt thou keep a watch upon him till the morning. And judge him to the time of going to rest?
JOB 7:19 How long wilt thou not let me alone: nor let me go, that I may swallow my spittle?
JOB 7:20 If I have sinned what can I do? thou who knowest the hearts of men; why hast thou set me up as thy mark to shoot at? Am I indeed a burden to thee?
JOB 7:21 Why hast thou not made an oblivion of my transgression; or a purification for my sin? Now therefore let me depart into the earth: and when thou risest in the morning, I am no more.
JOB 8:1 Here Baldad the Sauchean interposing said,
JOB 8:2 How long wilt thou speak such things? The breath of thy mouth is profuse of words.
JOB 8:3 Will the Lord in judging pass an unrighteous judgment? Or will he who made all things pervert justice?
JOB 8:4 If thy children have sinned in his sight, he hath dismissed them for their transgression:
JOB 8:5 But rise thou betimes and supplicate the Lord Almighty.
JOB 8:6 If thou art pure and upright, he will hear thy prayer; and render to thee the reward of righteousness.
JOB 8:7 Let thy beginning therefore be ever so small, thy end will be unspeakably great.
JOB 8:8 For inquire of the former generation; and search diligently among the race of fathers;
JOB 8:9 [for we are but of yesterday and know nothing; for our life on the earth is but a shadow]
JOB 8:10 will not they teach thee, and declare; and from the heart utter these maxims:
JOB 8:11 Can the papyrus grow without water?
JOB 8:12 Or can grass grow rank without drink? While grass is low it should not be mown. Before drinking doth not every herb wither?
JOB 8:13 Such therefore shall be the end of all who forget the Lord: for the hope of the ungodly shall perish.
JOB 8:14 For his house shall be uninhabited: and his tent shall fly away like a spider's web.
JOB 8:15 Though he prop up his house, it cannot stand: Though he take hold of it, it will not abide,
JOB 8:16 for is he somewhat green underneath the sun? Though a tender branch may start up from his rottenness; his bed is on a heap of stones:
JOB 8:17 and can he live among flint stones?
JOB 8:18 Should he wish to drink, the place will disappoint him. Hast thou not seen such things; that such is the catastrophe of the wicked?
JOB 8:19 But out of the ground he will cause another to spring up:
JOB 8:20 for the Lord will not cast off the innocent, nor from the ungodly accept a gift:
JOB 8:21 but he will fill the mouth of the upright with, laughter, and their lips with songs of thanksgiving:
JOB 8:22 and their enemies shall be clothed with shame; and the dwellings of the wicked shall come to naught.
JOB 9:1 To this Job replied,
JOB 9:2 Of a truth I know that it is so. For how can a mortal be righteous with the Lord?
JOB 9:3 For were it his pleasure to come to trial with him; he could not join issue to answer one charge of his in a thousand.
JOB 9:4 For he is wise in heart and strong and great. Who is hardy enough to stand up against him
JOB 9:5 who maketh mountains old insensibly; who overturneth them in his anger;
JOB 9:6 who shaketh the earth to its foundations, so that the pillars thereof totter;
JOB 9:7 who commandeth the sun and it riseth not; and who sealeth up against the stars;
JOB 9:8 who alone hath outspread the heaven; and who walketh on the sea as on a pavement;
JOB 9:9 who is the maker of the Pleiads and Hesperus,
JOB 9:10 and of Arcturus and the chambers of Notus; who doth things great and unsearchable; things glorious and wonderful not to be numbered?
JOB 9:11 When he passed over me I did not see him. When he passed by me, I did not know how.
JOB 9:12 If he dismiss who shall bring back? Or who shall say to him, What hast thou done?
JOB 9:13 For he himself slighted anger; by him the monsters under heaven were bowed down.
JOB 9:14 But if he will come to a trial with me, or will take cognisance of my affairs;
JOB 9:15 [for if I be righteous will he not hearken to me; shall I not supplicate his decision?
JOB 9:16 And if I call and he will not answer, I do not believe that he hath hearkened to my voice?]
JOB 9:17 Let him not break me with a tempest. But he hath multiplied my wounds without cause.
JOB 9:18 For he suffereth me not to take breath, and hath filled me with bitterness.
JOB 9:19 For because he is strong, he prevaileth. Who then can withstand his decrees?
JOB 9:20 For if I am righteous shall my mouth be wicked?
JOB 9:21 And if I am blameless, shall I go away crouching? For if I have acted wickedly, I am not conscious to myself: Nevertheless my life is taken away.
JOB 9:22 Say then, wrath destroyeth the great and powerful:
JOB 9:23 that the wicked fall by an untimely death. But the righteous are laughed to scorn:
JOB 9:24 for they have been delivered into the hands of the wicked. He covereth the faces of the judges of that wrath. If it is not he, who is it?
JOB 9:25 Now my days are swifter than a courier. They are gone without being perceived.
JOB 9:26 Is there any track left by ships in their passage? Or of an eagle flying in pursuit of its prey?
JOB 9:27 Now if I say, Let me forget speaking, let me bow down my face and groan:
JOB 9:28 I shudder in all my limbs; for I know that thou wilt not let me alone though innocent.
JOB 9:29 Now since I am wicked, why have I not died?
JOB 9:30 For though I have washed myself with snow, and purified myself with clean hands:
JOB 9:31 thou hast so thoroughly plunged me in filth that my very robes abhor me.
JOB 9:32 For thou art not a man as I am, with whom I can contend; that we may come together to a trial.
JOB 9:33 O that there were a mediator betwixt us; one to determine between and hear us both.
JOB 9:34 Let him remove his rod from me; and let not the dread of him terrify me;
JOB 9:35 Let me not be terrified, but speak, [for in that case I am not master of myself]
JOB 10:1 Weary of my life I would pour forth with groans my words before him: oppressed as I am I would speak in the bitterness of my soul,
JOB 10:2 and say to the Lord, Teach me not to be impious. Now, for what cause hast thou thus condemned me?
JOB 10:3 Is it agreeable to thee that I should commit iniquity; seeing thou hast rejected the works of thy hands; and favoured the counsel of the wicked?
JOB 10:4 As a mortal looketh dost thou look down? Or as a man looketh wilt thou behold?
JOB 10:5 Are thy days as the days of a mortal; or thy years, the years of a man;
JOB 10:6 that thou hast sought out mine iniquity, and diligently traced my sins?
JOB 10:7 For thou knowest that I am not impious: but who can deliver out of thy hands?
JOB 10:8 Thy hands have fashioned me and made me. After that thou hast changed thy mind and smitten me.
JOB 10:9 Remember that thou hast made me of clay, and art turning me again into mould.
JOB 10:10 Hast thou not churned me as milk, and curdled me as cheese;
JOB 10:11 and clothed me with skin and flesh; and fenced me with bones and sinews,
JOB 10:12 and granted me life and favour, and by thy visitation preserved my spirit?
JOB 10:13 As thou hast these things in thyself; I know that thou canst do all things, and that with thee nothing is impossible.
JOB 10:14 If I indeed have sinned inadvertently, thou hast me in custody, and hast not acquitted me of transgression.
JOB 10:15 If I indeed am impious, Woe is me.
JOB 10:16 And if I be righteous, I cannot hold up my head, for I am full of ignominy. For I am hunted as a lion for slaughter. For turning again furiously thou destroyest me.
JOB 10:17 Renewing the examination against me, thou hast exercised against me great wrath; and hast brought against me tortures.
JOB 10:18 Why then didst thou bring me forth from the womb? And why did I not die without an eye seeing me;
JOB 10:19 and become as if I never had existed? Why was I not carried from the womb to the grave?
JOB 10:20 Is not the term of my life of short duration? permit me to enjoy a little repose:
JOB 10:21 before I go, whence I shall not return;
JOB 10:22 to a land dark and gloomy; to a land of everlasting darkness; where there is no light; no seeing the life of mortals.
JOB 11:1 Here Sophar and Minaian answering said,
JOB 11:2 He who speaketh much should be answered: else the fine speaker thinketh himself just; and the short lived offspring of woman is blessed.
JOB 11:3 Be not profuse of words, because there is none to answer thee:
JOB 11:4 nor say I am pure in works and irreprehensible before him.
JOB 11:5 But how would the Lord speak to thee; were he to open his lips against thee?
JOB 11:6 Indeed were he to unfold to thee the power of wisdom; because it must needs be double to what are with thee: then thou wouldst know that what have come upon thee from the Lord are answerable to the sins which thou hast committed.
JOB 11:7 Canst thou trace the footsteps of the Lord? Or hast thou reached the extent of what the Almighty hath done?
JOB 11:8 The heaven is high, what then canst thou do? And there are things deeper than the mansion of the dead; what dost thou know?
JOB 11:9 Of greater extent than the measure of the earth or the breadth of the sea.
JOB 11:10 Now were he to overturn all these, who could say to him what hast thou done?
JOB 11:11 For he knoweth the works of the wicked, and on seeing wickedness will not overlook it.
JOB 11:12 But man vainly floateth about in words; but a mortal born of woman is like a wild ass.
JOB 11:13 For if thou hast made thy heart pure, and lift thy hands to him:
JOB 11:14 if there be any iniquity in thy hand, put it far from thee; and let not injustice lodge in thy dwelling.
JOB 11:15 For thus will thy countenance brighten like pure water: thou wilt disrobe thyself of filth, and no more be terrified:
JOB 11:16 thou shalt forget thy trouble like a wave that is past and not be afraid; and thy wish will spring up like the morning star;
JOB 11:17 and life will arise for thee from noon day:
JOB 11:18 and thou shalt be in a state of security because thou hast hope. And out of sorrow and care, peace will shine upon thee.
JOB 11:19 For thou shalt rest at ease, and none shall be at war with thee: and many, changing their conduct, will intreat thy favour.
JOB 11:20 But safety shall forsake them: for their hope shall be their destruction; and the eyes of the wicked shall melt away.
JOB 12:1 To this Job replied,
JOB 12:2 You, forsooth, are men, and wisdom will die with you.
JOB 12:3 But I indeed have understanding as well as you.
JOB 12:4 For a just man and one irreprehensible hath been made a mocking stock.
JOB 12:5 For it hath been ordered that for a time he shall fall beneath others: and that his houses shall be wasted by transgressors.
JOB 12:6 Nevertheless let no wicked man indulge a confidence that he shall escape condemnation. Whoever provoke the Lord to anger shall not they also undergo a trial?
JOB 12:7 But ask, I pray thee, the beasts of the field, if they could speak to thee; and the birds of the air, if they could tell thee;
JOB 12:8 speak to the earth, if it could converse with thee; even the fishes of the sea can tell thee.
JOB 12:9 Who then among all these doth not know that the hand of the Lord hath done these things?
JOB 12:10 Is not the life of all living beings in his hand; and the breath of every man?
JOB 12:11 The ear indeed discerneth words and the palate tasteth meats.
JOB 12:12 By length of time wisdom is acquired, and by long life, experience.
JOB 12:13 With him is wisdom and power; with him counsel and understanding.
JOB 12:14 If he demolish who can rebuild? If he shut against men, who can open?
JOB 12:15 If he withhold water he drieth the earth. And when he let it loose, he overthrew and destroyed it,
JOB 12:16 With him is strength and power; with him knowledge and understanding.
JOB 12:17 He hath led counsellors away captive. And confounded the judges of the earth.
JOB 12:18 It is he who settleth kings on thrones and girded their loins with a girdle;
JOB 12:19 who sendeth priests into captivity and overthrew the sovereigns of the earth;
JOB 12:20 who changeth the lips of liege men and knoweth the wisdom of elders;
JOB 12:21 who poureth contempt on princes and hath healed them who were low;
JOB 12:22 who revealeth deep things from darkness; and hath brought to light the shades of death;
JOB 12:23 who leadeth nations into error and destroyeth them; who prostrateth nations and conducteth them;
JOB 12:24 who changeth the hearts of the rulers of a land and hath caused them to wander in a way which they knew not:
JOB 12:25 That they might grope in darkness without light; and that they might stagger like a drunken man.
JOB 13:1 Behold these things mine eye hath seen and mine ear heard:
JOB 13:2 for I know all that you know and am not inferior to you in knowledge.
JOB 13:3 Nevertheless I would speak to the Lord; and argue before him, were it his pleasure.
JOB 13:4 Now you are all bad physicians and curers of maladies.
JOB 13:5 Could you hold your peace, it would be your wisdom.
JOB 13:6 Hear now the argument of my mouth and the pleading of my lips.
JOB 13:7 Are you not speaking in the presence of the Lord?
JOB 13:8 And do you in his presence utter deceit in a solemn manner? Or will you keep back any thing? Judge for yourselves.
JOB 13:9 For will it be well for you, if he mark your steps? For though feigning all these things you apply them for him:
JOB 13:10 he will, notwithstanding this, reprove you. And if you secretly respect persons;

JOB 13:12 And your boasting be dissipated like ashes; and your bodies be reduced to clay.

JOB 13:14 Taking my flesh in my teeth I will put my life in my hand.

JOB 13:27 and put my feet in a clog and watched all my doings; and hast tracked the soles of my feet.
JOB 14:1 He who is born of a woman waxeth old like a leathern bag: or like a garment which is moth eaten; for he is mortal, short lived and full of disquiet:
JOB 14:2 or like a flower which fell when in bloom. He glideth away indeed like a shadow and can make no stay.
JOB 14:3 And is it not such a one thou hast called to account; and caused such a one to come to trial before thee?
JOB 14:4 For who can be free from stain? Surely none.
JOB 14:5 Whether the course of his life on earth be one day; or months be numbered out for him, he cometh to the term thou hast set, but cannot pass it.
JOB 14:6 Turn away from him, that he may take rest, and comfort his life like a hireling.
JOB 14:7 For there is hope for a tree; for if lopped, it may sprout again, and the tender branch may not fail.
JOB 14:8 And if its root become old in the earth, or die on a rock:
JOB 14:9 its stem by the scent of water may blossom; and produce a crop like a tree lately planted.
JOB 14:10 But when a man dieth he is gone: when a mortal falleth, he is no more.
JOB 14:11 For in a course of time a sea is spent; and a river when unsupplied is dried up:
JOB 14:12 and man when composed in the grave cannot rise again; until the heaven be folded up; they shall not be awakened from their sleep.
JOB 14:13 O! that thou hadst kept me in the mansion of the dead; and hid me till thine indignation should cease: and that thou wouldst set me a time when thou wouldst remember me;
JOB 14:14 [for though a man die he may be revived, after finishing the days of this life of his,] I would wait patiently, until I come again into existence.
JOB 14:15 Then call and I will answer. But reject not the works of thy hands.
JOB 14:16 Now thou hast numbered up my devices, and not one of my inadvertencies could escape thee.
JOB 14:17 Thou hast sealed up mine iniquities in a bag; and set a mark on every transgression, which I inadvertently committed.
JOB 14:18 But not to mention that a falling mountain will continue its fall; even a rock may by force be removed from its place.
JOB 14:19 Waters have worn stones smooth; and waters have washed away mounds of earth; and thou hast destroyed the patience of man.
JOB 14:20 Thou hast brought him to an end, and he is gone: thou hast set thy face against him and dismissed him.
JOB 14:21 And though his children be multiplied, he knoweth it not: and if they become few in number, he doth not perceive it.
JOB 14:22 His flesh hath been for nothing but to suffer pain; and his soul only to suffer grief.
JOB 15:1 Here Eliphaz the Thaimanite taking up the argument said:
JOB 15:2 Will a wise man give the wind of knowledge for an answer; though he hath therewith filled his labouring belly?
JOB 15:3 Or in pleading use arguments which he ought not; and words in which there is no profit?
JOB 15:4 Hast thou not cast off fear, and used such arguments before the Lord?
JOB 15:5 By the arguments of thine own mouth thou art guilty; and hast not discerned the arguments of the mighty.
JOB 15:6 Let thine own mouth and not me convict thee: thine own lips indeed will testify against thee.
JOB 15:7 What! wast thou born before men? Or wast thou brought into being before the hills?
JOB 15:8 Or hast thou heard the established system of the Lord? Or hath God used thee as his counsellor? Or hath wisdom made application to thee?
JOB 15:9 For what knowest thou, which we do not know? Or what dost thou understand which we do not?
JOB 15:10 Among us indeed are elders and aged men, more venerable for years than thy father.
JOB 15:11 Thou hast been chastised less than thy sins deserve.
JOB 15:12 Thou hast spoken with excessive haughtiness. To what a pitch of boldness is thy heart raised; or at what have thine eyes taken aim;
JOB 15:13 that thou shouldst vent wrath before the Lord, and utter such words from thy mouth?
JOB 15:14 For who being mortal can be irreprehensible? Or can the offspring of woman be righteous?
JOB 15:15 If in his holy ones he placeth not confidence; and the heaven is not pure in his sight;
JOB 15:16 how abominable and filthy must man be; who drinketh iniquity in, like water!
JOB 15:17 But let me tell thee; hear what I have seen;
JOB 15:18 let me tell thee what the wise say, and their fathers have not concealed;
JOB 15:19 They, to whom alone the earth was given; and no stranger came among them.
JOB 15:20 The whole life of the wicked is spent in anxiety. Though a certain number of years is given to the oppressor:
JOB 15:21 yet the sound of terror is in his ears. When he seemeth to be at peace his destruction shall come.
JOB 15:22 Let him not hope to return out of darkness; for he is already doomed to the edge of the sword;
JOB 15:23 and destined to be food for vultures. He knoweth within himself that he waiteth for a fall; and a dark day will torture him.
JOB 15:24 Distress and anguish will overwhelm him; like a general at the head of troops falling upon him.
JOB 15:25 Because he lifted up his hands against the Lord, and hardened his neck against the Lord Almighty:
JOB 15:26 therefore he ran upon him contemptuously, with the thick boss of his buckler.
JOB 15:27 Because he covered his face with fatness; and made collops of fat upon his thighs:
JOB 15:28 let him therefore lodge in deserted cities; and go into uninhabited houses: and what they had got ready, let others carry off.
JOB 15:29 Let him neither be enriched, nor what he hath continue.
JOB 15:30 Let him never cast a shadow on the ground, nor escape out of darkness.
JOB 15:31 Let the wind blast his bud, and his blossom fall prematurely. Let him not hope to continue, for vanity shall be his portion.
JOB 15:32 Let his branch lopped unseasonably, die; and let not his young shoot flourish.
JOB 15:33 Let him be gathered like unripe grapes before his time, and fall like the olive blossom.
JOB 15:34 For death is the testimonial of a wicked man: and a fire shall consume the tents of bribery. He shall conceive sorrows and bring forth vanity, and his belly shall produce an illusion.
JOB 16:1 To this Job replied,
JOB 16:2 I have heard many such things, ye miserable comforters all!
JOB 16:3 what! Have words of wind a regular succession? Or can they give thee offence, considering thine answer?

JOB 16:5 And should there be strength in my mouth; would I not spare moving my lips?

JOB 16:10 When with the darts of his eyes he had transfixed me; with his spear had brought me on my knees: they with one consent rushed upon me.
JOB 16:11 The Lord hath indeed delivered me up to the unrighteous; and turned me over to the ungodly.
JOB 16:12 When I was at peace he broke me up; taking me by the hair he shook me; he set me up as a mark.

JOB 16:14 They shot me, one deadly wound on another; they ran against me with all their might.
JOB 16:15 They sewed sackcloth on my skin: and my strength was extinguished in the dust.
JOB 16:16 My belly was burned up with wailing; and on mine eyelids were the shades of death:
JOB 16:17 yet there was no iniquity in my hands. And my prayer was pure.
JOB 16:18 O earth, cover not the blood of my flesh, nor let there be a place for this cry of mine.
JOB 16:19 Even now, behold my witness is in heaven; and he who hath a perfect knowledge of me is on high.
JOB 16:20 O that my suit could come before the Lord, and that before him mine eye could drop a tear!
JOB 16:21 That a man could plead before the Lord, as a son of man may with his neighbour!
JOB 16:22 But my numbered days are come, and I must go the way, by which I cannot return.

JOB 19:1 To this Job replied,
JOB 19:2 How long will you make my soul sorrowful? You are indeed destroying me with words. Know at least; because the Lord hath dealt thus with me;
JOB 19:3 you speak against me; without shame you fall upon me.
JOB 19:4 Take it for granted that I have erred [though my error remaineth with myself] in speaking words which I ought not: and that my words are erroneous and unseasonable: but granted also,
JOB 19:5 That you magnify yourselves against me, and insult me with reproach.
JOB 19:6 Know then, That it is the Lord who hath terrified me, and raised his bulwark against me.
JOB 19:7 Behold I laugh at reproach; I will not speak; I will cry aloud, There is no judgment.
JOB 19:8 I am fenced about and cannot get out. Before me he hath placed darkness.
JOB 19:9 He hath stripped me of my glory, and hath taken the crown from my head.
JOB 19:10 He broke me on every side and I fled: and he hath cut down my hope like a tree.
JOB 19:11 When he exercised great wrath against me, and counted me as an enemy:
JOB 19:12 With one consent his troops fell upon me; they who were in ambush beset my ways.
JOB 19:13 My brethren stood aloof from me, they acknowledged strangers rather than me; and my friends were not compassionate.
JOB 19:14 My nearest relations paid me no attention: and they who knew my name forgot me.
JOB 19:15 As for my domesticks and maid servants, in their view I was a stranger.
JOB 19:16 When I called my servant, he did not answer me.
JOB 19:17 When with my mouth I entreated and supplicated my wife, and called affectionately the children of my concubines:
JOB 19:18 they renounced me forever. When I insist, they speak against me.
JOB 19:19 They who saw me, abhorred me; and they whom I loved rose up against me.
JOB 19:20 The flesh next my skin became rotten, and my bones begin to be corroded.
JOB 19:21 Pity me, pity me, O my friends, for the hand of the Lord hath touched me.
JOB 19:22 Why do you persecute me as the Lord doth, and are not satisfied with my flesh?
JOB 19:23 O that my words were written and recorded in a book forever!
JOB 19:24 That they were engraven with a graver of iron on lead, or on rocks!
JOB 19:25 For I know that he is eternal,

JOB 19:27 For from the Lord those things have been done to me, of which I alone am conscious; which mine eyes have seen, and no other; and which have all been done to me in my bosom.

JOB 19:29 Stand in awe, I beseech you, of the developing scene; for wrath will come upon the unrighteous, and it shall then be known, where their filthiness is.
JOB 20:1 Then answered Sophar the Minaian and said,
JOB 20:2 I did not suppose that thou wouldst return such an answer, but do not you feel it more than I?
JOB 20:3 Am I to hear my modesty corrected? And is a spirit from its consciousness to answer me?
JOB 20:4 Thou hast never known such things heretofore, from the time man was placed on the earth!
JOB 20:5 But the mirth of the wicked is sudden ruin, and the joy of transgressors, destruction,
JOB 20:6 though his gifts mount up to heaven, and his sacrifice reach the clouds.
JOB 20:7 For when he thinketh that he is now firmly established, then shall he be utterly destroyed; and they who have seen him will say, Where is he?
JOB 20:8 Like a dream which is gone, he cannot be found. He is vanished, like a spectre in the night.
JOB 20:9 The eye which saw him, shall see him no more; and his place shall no more him observe.
JOB 20:10 Let minors destroy his children, and his own hands light up the signals of distress.
JOB 20:11 His bones were full of his youth, but with him it shall go to rest beneath the mound.
JOB 20:12 If wickedness be sweet in his mouth, he will hide it under his tongue.
JOB 20:13 He will not be sparing of it, nor forsake it, but will gather it together in his mouth; therefore let him not be able to help himself.

JOB 20:20 There is no security for his possessions; nor shall he be saved by what he valueth highly.
JOB 20:21 Not a scrap of his provisions is left. His good things shall not, on this account, be renewed.
JOB 20:22 In the fullness of his sufficiency he shall be afflicted, and all manner of distress shall come upon him.
JOB 20:23 If by any means he be permitted to fill his belly; may he send against him fiery indignation, and pour upon him sorrows!

JOB 20:27 may the heaven disclose his iniquities, and the earth rise up against him!
