JOB 22:30 He indeed will save the innocent. Save thyself therefore, with clean hands.
JOB 23:1 In reply to this, Job said,
JOB 23:2 I know very well, this trial is not in my disposal. And that his hand is made heavy by my groaning.
JOB 23:3 But O that some person would let me know, that I might find him, and come to an issue;
JOB 23:4 that I might order the trial of myself, and that he would stop my mouth with arguments
JOB 23:5 That I might know what remedies he will prescribe for me, and understand what he will announce to me!
JOB 23:6 Though he may come against me with great majesty, he will not employ it in threatening me.
JOB 23:7 For truth and argument proceed from him; and he would bring my cause to an issue.
JOB 23:8 For if I am to go first and am no more, how do I know what will be at the last?
JOB 23:9 When he wrought on my left, I comprehended not; he may encompass my right and I not see.
JOB 23:10 For he already knoweth my way and hath tried me like gold.
JOB 23:11 And I will come out at his commands; for I have kept his ways, and will not turn aside from his commands,
JOB 23:12 nor transgress in my bosom: indeed I have hid his words.
JOB 23:13 But if he hath judged thus, who can gainsay him? For he hath done what was his pleasure.
JOB 23:14 For this cause my shuddering is at him; and on being chastened, I thought of him.
JOB 23:15 For this cause I am to be awed at his presence; I am to meditate on and be in dread of him.
JOB 23:16 It is the Lord indeed who hath softened my heart. It is the Almighty who hath made me shudder.
JOB 23:17 For I had no knowledge of darkness coining upon me; and he had hid from my view thick darkness before me.
JOB 24:1 But why have set times escaped the notice of the Lord;
JOB 24:2 and the wicked transgressed all bounds; and ravaged both the flock and the shepherd?
JOB 24:3 They have driven away the ass of the fatherless; and taken the widow's cow for a pledge.
JOB 24:4 They have turned the weak out of the right way; and with one consent the meek of the land are hidden
JOB 24:5 and are gone away like asses in a field. They are sprung up above me in their own order. To one, bread is sweetened for his children;
JOB 24:6 others have reaped before dawn a field not their own; exhausted of strength have Worked the vineyards of the wicked without wages and without food.
JOB 24:7 They have caused many to sleep naked without covering; they have stripped them of clothing necessary for life.
JOB 24:8 These are wet with the dew of the mountains: and having no shelter they cling to a rock.
JOB 24:9 They have torn the orphan from the breast: and him who had fallen they have pressed down.
JOB 24:10 They have by injustice caused some to be naked; and robbed the hungry of their morsel.
JOB 24:11 They have entrapped some unjustly in straits, and the path of justice they did not know.
JOB 24:12 Some are expelled from the city and their own houses: and the soul of babes heave heavy groans.
JOB 24:13 Now why hath he not called these to account while on earth? Though they did not acknowledge; though they did not know the way of justice; did they not still go on in their courses?
JOB 24:14 And hath he who knew their works delivered them up to darkness? And will he be as a thief in the night?
JOB 24:15 When the eye of the adulterer watched for darkness; saying, No eye shall discover me; when he having put a mask on his face
JOB 24:16 digged through houses in the dark: [during the day they had shut themselves up; they had no acquaintance with light]
JOB 24:17 because the morning is to all these as the shadow of death; because the terror of the shadow of death should acknowledge them;
JOB 24:18 is it swift on the face of the water? The portion of these on the earth should be cursed
JOB 24:19 and their plants exposed dry on the ground: for they plundered the sheaf of orphans.
JOB 24:20 Now was such a one's sin brought to remembrance? Though he was dark as the darkness of night; retribution should be made for what he hath done: and every wicked man should be broken; like a tree which cannot be healed.
JOB 24:21 Because lie did not treat the barren with tenderness, and had no compassion for a poor weak woman.
JOB 24:22 But overthrew the helpless with wrath: therefore when he riseth he should have no security for his own life:
JOB 24:23 when sick, he should have no hopes of recovery: but should perish by his disorder.
JOB 24:24 As his exaltation afflicted many: he should wither like mallows by heat: or like an ear of corn which fell of itself from the stalk.
JOB 24:25 Now if this is not the case; who can say I have spoken falsehoods: and set my words at naught?
JOB 25:1 Hereupon Baldad the Sauchean answered and said,
JOB 25:2 What! Is there any apology, or fear with him; who made the universe and is supreme?
JOB 25:3 For let none suppose, because robbers have a respite; that snares shall not come from him on any.
JOB 25:4 For how can a mortal be just before the Lord or any offspring of woman make himself clean?
JOB 25:5 If he setteth the moon beside him, it shineth not: and the stars are not pure in his sight.
JOB 25:6 Grant then that man is rottenness and that the son of man is a worm.
JOB 26:1 To this Job replied,
JOB 26:2 Whom dost thou assist, or whom art thou going to help? Is it not him, who hath mighty power and whose arm is strong?
JOB 26:3 For whom hast thou been acting as counsellor? Is it not for him who hath all wisdom? Whom art thou about to follow? Is it not him, whose army is beyond compare?
JOB 26:4 For whom hast thou announced dictates? And whose breath is it which proceeded from thee?
JOB 26:5 Are giants going to rise up from beneath the water and the places in its neighbourhood?
JOB 26:6 The mansion of the dead is naked before him: and destruction hath no covering.
JOB 26:7 He it is, who stretcheth out Boreas over empty space; who suspendeth the earth upon nothing;
JOB 26:8 who bindeth up water in his clouds; and the cloud under it is not rent;
JOB 26:9 who taketh possession of the front of his throne and over it spreadeth his cloud.
JOB 26:10 His decree had drawn a circle on the face of the water; at the confines of light and darkness.
JOB 26:11 The pillars of heaven flutter and are struck with consternation at his rebuke.
JOB 26:12 By his power he calmed the sea; and by his knowledge the monster was overthrown.
JOB 26:13 The bars of heaven were terrified at him; and by a decree he doomed to death the apostate dragon.
JOB 26:14 Behold these are parts of his ways. But let us hear the least breath of reason for him. As for the strength of his thunder; who knoweth when he shall employ it?
JOB 27:1 Furthermore Job proceeded and by way of preface said,
JOB 27:2 As God liveth, who hath thus condemned me; even the Almighty who hath made my life bitter:
JOB 27:3 while I have the power of breathing and the breath of God is in my nostrils;
JOB 27:4 my lips shall not speak wickedness, nor shall my soul contrive mischief.
JOB 27:5 Far be it from me to acknowledge you to be right; for till I die, I will not give up mine innocence.
JOB 27:6 And for asserting my righteousness I make no apology; for I am not conscious to myself of having done amiss.
JOB 27:7 Should not mine enemies then be as the overthrow of the wicked? And they who rise up against me as the destruction of transgressors?
JOB 27:8 Now whatever hope a wicked man hath, that he persisteth; shall he who hath trusted in the Lord be indeed safe?
JOB 27:9 Or will God hear his prayer? Or when trouble cometh upon him,
JOB 27:10 hath he any assurance before him? Or upon his calling, will he hearken to him?
JOB 27:11 But now let me tell you what is by the hand of the Lord. What are from the Almighty I will not falsify.
JOB 27:12 Behold you all know that you heap vanity on vanities, saying,
JOB 27:13 "This is the portion of a wicked man from the Lord: and the possession of oppressors, which shall come to them from the Almighty.
JOB 27:14 If their children be many they shall be for slaughter; and if they grow up to men, they shall be beggars.
JOB 27:15 Those who are about him shall die by pestilence: and their widows none shall compassionate.
JOB 27:16 Though he heap up silver as dust; and store up gold as clay:
JOB 27:17 the righteous shall take charge of all these; and men of truth shall enjoy his wealth.
JOB 27:18 His house is gone like moths or like a cobweb.
JOB 27:19 He shall lie down rich but shall not continue so. He hath opened his eyes, and all is gone.
JOB 27:20 Sorrows flowed in upon him like water. In a night a tempest swept him away.
JOB 27:21 A burning wind shall take him up and go he must. It shall blow him away out of his place.
JOB 27:22 He will dash upon him and will not spare. Should he by flight flee from his hand,
JOB 27:23 he will cause them to clap their hands at him and will hiss him out of his place."
JOB 28:1 There is indeed a place, from which silver is got; and a place from which gold is strained.
JOB 28:2 Iron indeed is made out of the earth, and brass is hewn from a quarry like stones.
JOB 28:3 He hath assigned a station for darkness: but every boundary he assigned is diligently explored; stones, darkness and the shadow of death;
JOB 28:4 the channels of brooks choked up with sand: where to such as know not the right way; strength is unavailing and they are removed from among men.
JOB 28:5 As for the earth out of which bread cometh; from underneath it something like fire hath been turned up.
JOB 28:6 The stones thereof is the place of the sapphire. And the dust thereof supplieth man with gold.
JOB 28:7 A path is explored which no bird knew; and which the vulture's eye hath not seen;
JOB 28:8 which the race of boasters have not travelled; and over which the lion hath not stalked
JOB 28:9 One hath stretched forth his hand with a pick and hath overturned mountains from the roots.
JOB 28:10 Another hath broken through the whirlpools of rivers: and mine eye hath seen every precious thing.
JOB 28:11 Another hath laid bare the bottoms of rivers and given manifest proofs of his power.
JOB 28:12 But where is wisdom to be found? And where is the place of understanding?
JOB 28:13 A mortal knoweth not the way thereof; nor hath it indeed been found out by men.
JOB 28:14 The abyss said, It is not in me: and the sea said, It is not in me.
JOB 28:15 would not one give for it all he hath got?
JOB 28:16 But silver cannot be weighed as its price; nor can it be purchased with the gold of Sophir; with the precious onyx or the sapphire.
JOB 28:17 Gold and chrystal cannot equal it in value; nor can jewels of gold be a barter for it.
JOB 28:18 Things above need not be mentioned: but prize thou wisdom above all things below.
JOB 28:19 The topaz of Ethiopia cannot equal it in value: nor is it to be rated by pure gold.
JOB 28:20 But where can wisdom be found? And where is the place of understanding?
JOB 28:21 It hath escaped the knowledge of every man; and is hid from the birds of the air.
JOB 28:22 Destruction and death said, We have heard the fame of it.
JOB 28:23 God is perfectly acquainted with its way and knoweth its place.
JOB 28:24 For he surveyeth the whole world; and knoweth all on the earth;
JOB 28:25 all that he hath made; the weight of winds and the measures of water.
JOB 28:26 When he had made and seen and numbered them; and also a way for the pealing thunder:
JOB 28:27 then did he see it and declare it: and having prepared and traced it,
JOB 28:28 he said to man, "Behold the worshipping of God is wisdom: and to abstain from evil is understanding."
JOB 29:1 Job still further continued his speech, with this exordium:
JOB 29:2 O that I were reinstated as in times past! As in the days of the months when God preserved me;
JOB 29:3 when his lamp shined over my head; when by his light I walked through darkness;
JOB 29:4 when I was making my ways conspicuous; when God watched over my family;
JOB 29:5 when I was thick set with branches, and my servants were around me;
JOB 29:6 when my ways abounded in butter, and my mountains flowed with milk;
JOB 29:7 when I walked early through the city; and a seat was set for me in the streets!
JOB 29:8 The young when they saw me hid themselves; and all the aged stood up.
JOB 29:9 The nobles forbore talking and put their finger on their mouth.
JOB 29:10 And while they who heard me were blessing me, their tongue cleaved to the roof of their mouth.
JOB 29:11 When the ear heard me it blessed me; and the eye when it saw me, turned aside:
JOB 29:12 for I saved the poor from the hand of the mighty; and assisted the orphan who had no helper.
JOB 29:13 The blessing of him who was perishing came upon me: and the mouth of the widow blessed me.
JOB 29:14 I put on righteousness and cloathed myself with justice as with a mantle.
JOB 29:15 I was eyes to the blind and feet to the lame.
JOB 29:16 I was a father to those in distress; and the cause which I knew not I searched out.
JOB 29:17 And I broke the jaws of the unrighteous; and plucked the prey from betwixt their teeth.
JOB 29:18 Therefore I said, My youth shall advance to old age. Like the stock of a palm, I shall live long.
JOB 29:19 My root is spread out by the water; and the dew will abide on my produce.
JOB 29:20 This vain glory of mine shall attend me: my bow is directed by his hand.
JOB 29:21 They who heard me paid close attention;
JOB 29:22 and at my counsel they were silent. To my decree they added nothing But were overjoyed when I spoke to them.
JOB 29:23 As the thirsty earth receiveth rain, so did they my speech.
JOB 29:24 If I smiled on them they could scarce believe it. And the light of my countenance was not lost.
JOB 29:25 I chose their way and sat as chief, and dwelt as a king among warriors; as one who comforteth the afflicted.
JOB 30:1 But now the meanest have me in derision: now, those undertake to admonish me; whose fathers I held in contempt: whom I did not think worthy the dogs of my flocks.
JOB 30:2 What in deed was the strength of their hands to me? Destruction would have been lost upon them.
JOB 30:3 By reason of want and famine it was useless. Already they were fleeing ineffectually from distress and misery:
JOB 30:4 they were crouding round the samphire on the sounding shore; and feeding on sea weeds as their food; despicable and contemned and in want of every thing good, they through extreme want were chewing even the roots of trees.
JOB 30:5 Against me thieves have risen up,
JOB 30:6 whose habitations were the clefts of rocks.
JOB 30:7 Amidst this tuneful choir, are to be heard the brawls of them who lived under hedges.
JOB 30:8 A race of fools and despicable wretches, whose name and honour are extinguished from the earth.
JOB 30:9 But now I am become their song: and they have me for their by-word:
JOB 30:10 and have abhorred me and stood at a distance: and have not spared to spit in my face.
JOB 30:11 Because he opened his quiver and afflicted me: therefore they have cast off the restraint, which they were under at my presence.
JOB 30:12 At the right of their brood they have taken their stand: they have stretched out their foot; and vindicated against me their destructive ways.
JOB 30:13 My ways are destroyed; for I am stript of my robe. With his darts he hath pierced me;
JOB 30:14 he hath used me at his pleasure. I am become loathsome by sorrows.
JOB 30:15 My sorrows roll back upon me. My hope is gone like a breath, and like a cloud, my safety.
JOB 30:16 And now my soul is melting within me. Days of sorrow take hold of me;
JOB 30:17 and at night my bones are melted and my sinews are quite dissolved.
JOB 30:18 With great force he took hold of my garment; and girded me about like the collar of my vest.
JOB 30:19 Thou hast accounted me as dirt: and my portion is in dust and ashes.
JOB 30:20 Though I have cried to thee, thou hearest me not: but they stood up and observed me;
JOB 30:21 and came upon me without mercy. Thou hast chastised me with a heavy hand;
JOB 30:22 and placed me among sorrows; and cast me away far from safety.
JOB 30:23 For I know that death will destroy me: for earth is the house for every mortal.
JOB 30:24 For! how I wish that I might lay violent hands on myself; or beseech another to do this for me.
JOB 30:25 As for me I indeed wept for every one in trouble; and sighed, when I saw a man in distress.
JOB 30:26 But when I expected  prosperity: behold days of affliction came upon me.
JOB 30:27 My bowels have boiled and could not rest: days of misery have prevented me.
JOB 30:28 I have gone mourning without restraint; and have stood in the congregation and cried.
JOB 30:29 I have been made a brother to jackals, and a companion to ostriches.
JOB 30:30 My skin is become very black; and my bones are burning with heat.
JOB 30:31 My kithara is turned into mourning, and my song to wailing for myself.
JOB 31:1 I made a covenant with mine eyes, that I would not gaze on a virgin:
JOB 31:2 yet what portion hath God dealt out from above?
JOB 31:3 And what, alas! the lasting portion on high? "Destruction is for the wicked and banishment for transgressors."
JOB 31:4 Why will he not behold my way and number all my steps?
JOB 31:5 Have I walked with scoffers or hath my foot hasted to deceit?
JOB 31:6 For I have been weighed in a just balance; and the Lord knoweth mine integrity.
JOB 31:7 If my foot hath deviated from the way or my heart gone astray after mine eyes; or if with my hands I have touched bribes:
JOB 31:8 may I sow and others eat; and let me have no root in the land.
JOB 31:9 If my heart hath gone after another man's wife, or if I have lain in wait at her gates;
JOB 31:10 let my wife gratify another, and mine infant children be dishonoured.
JOB 31:11 For the defiling of another man's wife exciteth a fury of wrath not to be restrained.
JOB 31:12 For it is a fire burning in all the limbs; which will not go out, till it hath utterly consumed.
JOB 31:13 If I have slighted the cause of my man servant or maid servant when they had a controversy with me,
JOB 31:14 what shall I do when the Lord maketh inquest? And when he visiteth, what answer shall I make?
JOB 31:15 Was not I formed in the womb as they were? And were we not alike fashioned in the belly?
JOB 31:16 Far from depriving the poor of what they had, or causing the heart of a widow to fail;
JOB 31:17 if I have eaten my morsel alone, and have not shared it with the orphan;
JOB 31:18 [for from my youth I as a father nourished them, and was their guide from my mother's womb]
JOB 31:19 If I have seen the naked perishing and have not clothed them;
JOB 31:20 and if the poor have not blessed me, and their shoulders been warmed with the fleece of my lambs;
JOB 31:21 If I have raised a hand against the fatherless, because I had around me greater support:
JOB 31:22 may my shoulder bone be dislocated, and my arm broken at the elbow.
JOB 31:23 For the fear of the Lord restrained me, and the burden of that I could not endure.
JOB 31:24 If I have made gold my measure, or placed my confidence in precious stones:
JOB 31:25 or if I have exulted because my wealth was great, or laid my hand on what was not counted out to me:
JOB 31:26 or, [do we not see the refulgent sun sometimes eclipsed, and the moon continually changing? for it is not in them:]
JOB 31:27 if then my heart hath been secretly enticed, and I have laid my hand on my mouth and kissed it
JOB 31:28 let this be reckoned to me as the greatest transgression, that I have lied in the presence of the Lord, the Most High.
JOB 31:29 If I have rejoiced at the downfall of mine enemies, and my heart hath said, Aha!
JOB 31:30 Let mine ear hear myself cursed, and let me be a by-word among the people, when I am afflicted.
JOB 31:31 If my maid servants have often said, that we had some of his flesh meat to eat! while I was living luxuriously:
JOB 31:32 [indeed the stranger lodged not in the street, and my door was open to every comer:]
JOB 31:33 If when I sinned inadvertently, I concealed my sin;
JOB 31:34 for I was not so awed by the multitude as not to mention it before them; [Now if I had suffered a poor man to go from my door with an empty lap,
JOB 31:35 who could have heard me with patience?] And if I had not feared the hand of the Lord
JOB 31:36 I would have put on my shoulders the writing which I had against any one, and have acknowledged it as a crown:
JOB 31:37 But if I did not tear it in pieces and give it up, without taking any thing from the debtor:
JOB 31:38 if ever my ground hath cried out against me, and the furrows thereof joined in the complaint:
JOB 31:39 if I have eaten alone the strength thereof without money, and by rapine caused the heart of the owner of the soil to grieve:
JOB 31:40 let nettles spring up for me instead of wheat, and bramble bushes instead of barley.
JOB 32:1 Here Job closed his speech, and his three friends ceased from making further reply to him; for he was righteous in their sight.
JOB 32:2 Then was kindled the wrath of Elius the son of Barachiel the Buzite, of the family of Earn, of the country of Ausitis. His wrath was kindled against Job to a high degree, because he had declared himself just before the Lord:
JOB 32:3 And with the three friends he was very angry, because they were not able to answer Job's defence: though they had charged him with being wicked.
JOB 32:4 Now Elius had waited to answer Job, because they were older than he.
JOB 32:5 But when he saw that there was no answer in the mouth of the three men, he was fired with indignation;
JOB 32:6 therefore Elius the son of Barachiel the Buzite taking up the argument, said, I indeed am young and you are old; therefore I kept silence and was afraid to give my opinion.
JOB 32:7 For I said, Is it not age which speaketh? And by many years they have gained wisdom.
JOB 32:8 But there is a spirit in mortals; and it is the inspiration of the Almighty which teacheth.
JOB 32:9 They who live longest are not the wisest, nor is the knowledge of judgment confined to the aged.
JOB 32:10 Wherefore I said, Hear me, and I will tell you what I know.
JOB 32:11 Listen attentive to my words, for I will speak in your hearing that you may examine them.
JOB 32:12 Even now I could wish to attend to you: but behold there is none who convicteth Job; none of you who refuteth his arguments:
JOB 32:13 that you might not say, We the Lord's advocates have found wisdom.
JOB 32:14 And you have left a man at liberty to use hereafter the same arguments.
JOB 32:15 They were daunted. They answered not again. They have antiquated their own speeches.
JOB 32:16 I waited patiently: for I had not spoken. Because they stopped and made no reply,
JOB 32:17 therefore Elius interposing, saith, I will speak again,
JOB 32:18 for I am full of words; for I am pained with a spirit within me;
JOB 32:19 for I am like a vessel full of new wine, in fermentation, without vent; or like the labouring bellows of a smith.
JOB 32:20 I will speak that I may have ease, by opening my lips.
JOB 32:21 For I should not be awed by man: nor put to the blush because of a mortal.
JOB 32:22 For I am not apt to admire persons. Will not Worms devour them as well as me.
JOB 33:1 Now therefore, Job, hear thou my words, and listen attentively to my speech;
JOB 33:2 for lo! I have opened my mouth, and my tongue hath begun to speak.
JOB 33:3 My words shall proceed from a pure heart; and the sentiments of my lips shall be pure.
JOB 33:4 It is the divine spirit, which made me, even the inspiration of the Almighty, which teacheth me.
JOB 33:5 If thou art able, give me an answer; come to trial, and let us stand face to face.
JOB 33:6 Thou art formed out of clay, and so am I: we are both made of the same material.
JOB 33:7 By the dread of me thou wilt not be terrified; nor will this hand of mine be heavy on thee.
JOB 33:8 Now thou hast said in my hearing; I heard the sound of thy words: for thou saidst,
JOB 33:9 "I am pure, I have not sinned; I am irreprehensible, for I have not transgressed.
JOB 33:10 But he hath invented an accusation against me, and hath accounted me as an enemy.
JOB 33:11 He hath put my foot in a clog, and watched all my ways."
JOB 33:12 For how, dost thou say, I am righteous, yet he hath not hearkened to me. For He, who is over mortals, is eternal.
JOB 33:13 And dost thou say, Why in my trial, hath he not hearkened to me on every matter?
JOB 33:14 For the Lord may have spoken once, and again;
JOB 33:15 In a dream, for instance, or in a nightly vision: As when a dread horror falleth on men, during their slumbers on a bed;
JOB 33:16 then doth he open the understanding of men.
JOB 33:17 With such appearances of terror he frighted them, to turn man away from iniquity. Again he hath saved his body from a fall,
JOB 33:18 and hath rescued his soul from death; and hath not suffered him to fall in battle.
JOB 33:19 Again he hath rebuked him with sickness on a bed, and benumbed all his bones;
JOB 33:20 so that he cannot take any nourishment, [though his soul longeth for food]
JOB 33:21 until his flesh become rotten, and he can show his bones bare.
JOB 33:22 When his soul hath come near to death, and his life near to the mansion of the dead,
JOB 33:23 though there may be a thousand messengers of death, not one of them can mortally wound him.
JOB 33:24 If he determine in his heart to turn to the Lord, when he shall have shewn man his charge against him, and pointed out to him his folly, he will support him, that he may not fall to death,
JOB 33:25 and renew his body like the plaistering on a wall, and will fill his bones with marrow; and make his flesh soft like that of an infant, and restore him to full strength among men.
JOB 33:26 And when he hath prayed to the Lord, and shall enjoy acceptable things, he will come with a cheerful countenance and with thanks: and render justice to men.
JOB 33:27 Then will such a man blame himself, and say, What I have done! He hath not chastened me, as my sins deserve!
JOB 33:28 Save my soul, that it may not go to destruction, and let my life see light.
JOB 33:29 Behold in these three ways the Almighty doth all these things with man.
JOB 33:30 He hath indeed delivered my soul from death; that in light my life may praise him.
JOB 33:31 Listen attentively, Job, and hear me: keep silence that I may speak.
JOB 33:32 If thou hast any thing to say, answer me: speak; for I wish thee to be justified.
JOB 33:33 If not: hearken to me: keep silence and I will teach thee.
JOB 34:1 Then Elius proceeded and said,
JOB 34:2 Hearken to me, ye wise men, and ye who have knowledge listen attentively.
JOB 34:3 For the ear trieth words and the palate tasteth meats.
JOB 34:4 Let us take upon us the right of judging: Let us know among ourselves what is good.
JOB 34:5 For Job hath said, "I am righteous: the Lord hath removed from me the trial;
JOB 34:6 and hath disappointed me of my trial. My wound is grievous without transgression."
JOB 34:7 What man is there like Job, who drinketh up scorning like water;
JOB 34:8 who hath neither sinned, nor been guilty of impiety; nor associated with the workers of iniquity to walk with impious men?
JOB 34:9 For thou shouldst not say, There shall be no visitation of man. He shall indeed have a visitation from the Lord.
JOB 34:10 Therefore hearken to me, ye who are wise in heart. Far be it from me to be profane before the Lord; or before the Almighty to disturb the course of justice.
JOB 34:11 "But he should render to every man according to each one's work; so that in his own paths every man may find him."
JOB 34:12 But dost thou think that the Lord will do improper things? Or will the Almighty who made the earth, pervert judgment?
JOB 34:13 Now who is this maker of the World and of all the things therein?
JOB 34:14 For were it his pleasure to confine, and keep to himself, the wind,
JOB 34:15 all flesh would expire together; and every mortal would return to earth, of which they were formed.
JOB 34:16 See that thou be not chastened. Hear these things; listen attentively to the sound of words.
JOB 34:17 Consider that he who hateth iniquity; and that he who destroyeth the wicked, being eternal, is just.
JOB 34:18 He is irreverent, who saith to a king, Thou transgressest: to princes, you are acting impiously.
JOB 34:19 Who hath no respect for the person of an honourable man; nor knoweth how to honour nobles by respecting their persons."
JOB 34:20 But it should be in vain for them to cry or to entreat a man, for they behaved wickedly in turning aside the weak.
JOB 34:21 For he is the observer of men"s actions, and nothing that they do can escape his notice:
JOB 34:22 nor can there be a place, where the workers of iniquity can be concealed."
JOB 34:23 That he will not yet set himself against a man;
JOB 34:24 is because the Lord superintended all in ways unsearchable; glorious and wonderful, not to be numbered.
JOB 34:25 "As he knoweth their works: he should bring on night and they should be humbled.
JOB 34:26 But hath he extinguished the wicked though they are visible before him?
JOB 34:27 Because they turned aside from the law of God and did not acknowledge his judgments,
JOB 34:28 when they cause the cry of the poor to ascend to him, he should hearken to the cry of the poor."
JOB 34:29 But when he giveth rest, who shall call him to account? When he hideth his face, who can see him? Both against a nation, and against a man at the same time,
JOB 34:30 he maketh a hypocritick man king; because of the perverseness of a people.
JOB 34:31 Because one saith to the Almighty, "I have taken, I will not again take a pledge:
JOB 34:32 I will look beyond myself; do thou shew me: If I have done iniquity, I will do so no more."
JOB 34:33 Will he for thee punish that iniquity? Because thou must deny; because thou must draw the conclusion, not I: therefore speak what thou knowest.
JOB 34:34 For they who are wise in heart will say the same: and a wise man hath heard this word of mine.
JOB 34:35 Job indeed hath not spoken with wisdom: his words are not with understanding.
JOB 34:36 Therefore let Job learn and no more make reply like the foolish;
JOB 34:37 that we may not add to our transgressions. For iniquity will be charged to our account; if we multiply speeches before the Lord.
JOB 35:1 Then Elius proceeded and said,
JOB 35:2 What thinkest thou of this in thy pleading? Who art thou that thou shouldst say, "I am righteous before the Lord?"
JOB 35:3 Or wilt thou say, "What can I do if I sin?"
JOB 35:4 I will answer thee and these three friends of thine.
JOB 35:5 Look up to yonder heaven and see; and observe the clouds, how high above thee they are.
JOB 35:6 If thou hast sinned, what canst thou do? And if thou hast multiplied transgressions, what canst thou effect?
JOB 35:7 If thou art righteous, what canst thou give him? Or will he receive any thing at thy hands?
JOB 35:8 Thy wickedness may affect a man like thyself: and thy righteousness, a son of man .
JOB 35:9 On the account of a multitude, they who are falsely accused will scream: They will call aloud because of the arm of many,
JOB 35:10 but none said, where is the God who made me;
JOB 35:11 who regulateth the watches of the night; who distinguisheth me from the beasts of the earth and from the birds of the air?
JOB 35:12 There let them scream. He indeed may not hearken even at the abuse of bad men.
JOB 35:13 "Since it is not the Lord's desire to see improper things; since he, the Almighty,
JOB 35:14 is the observer of them who do injustice; he should save me:" but be judged before him. Canst thou praise him as things are?
JOB 35:15 Because he doth not regard Job's anger; and hath not severely animadverted on some offence:
JOB 35:16 therefore Job vainly openeth his mouth; he loadeth his speeches with folly.
JOB 36:1 Then Elius proceeded further and said,
JOB 36:2 Bear with me a little longer that I may teach thee: for I have still something further to say;
JOB 36:3 taking my knowledge from abroad and from my own works,
JOB 36:4 I will speak righteous things with truth, without considering in an unjust manner things which are unjust.
JOB 36:5 Know then that the Lord, who is mighty in power and wisdom;
JOB 36:6 will not reject the innocent, nor save the wicked: and that he will administer justice to the oppressed.
JOB 36:7 He will not withdraw his eyes from the righteous, but will seat them at last with kings on a throne and they shall be exalted.
JOB 36:8 When they shall be bound with fetters or held with cords of affliction,
JOB 36:9 he will shew them their works and their transgressions, that they bear;
JOB 36:10 But he will hearken to what is just, and hath ordered them to turn from iniquity.
JOB 36:11 If they hearken and serve; they shall end their days in prosperity and their years in the enjoyment of things convenient.
JOB 36:12 But the impious he saveth not: because they would not know the Lord, and because, when they were admonished, they were disobedient,
JOB 36:13 the hypocrites in heart shall incur wrath: they will not cry because he bound them:
JOB 36:14 Let their soul therefore perish in youth and their life be wounded by angels.
JOB 36:15 Because they afflicted the weak and feeble, he will support the cause of the meek.
JOB 36:16 Though the abyss from the mouth of an enemy;
JOB 36:17 the overflow of that from underneath hath deceived thee; and thy table which was full of fatness hath fallen: yet the cause of the righteous shall not fail.
JOB 36:18 But there shall be wrath against the ungodly, on account of the wicked bribes which they received for injustice.
JOB 36:19 Let not the earnest entreaty of the weak in distress turn aside thee and all those in the exercise of authority.
JOB 36:20 Do not spin out the night that crowds may come to their assistance.
JOB 36:21 But be careful not to do improper things: for by such a conduct thou wilt extricate thyself from distress.
JOB 36:22 Behold the Almighty will strengthen with his strength: for who is powerful as he? Or who can examine his works?
JOB 36:23 Or who can say, He hath done unjust things?
JOB 36:24 Remember that his works are greater than what men have attempted.
JOB 36:25 Every man hath seen by himself how many mortals are wounded.
JOB 36:26 Behold the Almighty is multifarious in operations beyond our comprehension. The number of his years are indeed infinite
JOB 36:27 and by him the particles of rain can be counted.
JOB 36:28 When they are collected into a cloud for rain, the heavens will pour down. But when the clouds cast a shade over the dumb creation he impressed a care on beasts, and they know the order for going to bed.
JOB 36:29 At all these things is not thine understanding confounded? And is not thy heart starting from the body? Now though the outspread cloud be rushing together, to the whole extent of his pavilion,
JOB 36:30 behold! with a clap of thunder he will expand it over him. He hath indeed covered the out branchings of the sea!
JOB 36:31 For with what he judgeth nations he can give food in abundance.
JOB 36:32 When with his hands he hath covered the light, and hath given provisional orders concerning food;
JOB 36:33 the Lord will warn his friend that there is a portion also for injustice. Therefore
JOB 37:1 on the account of this my heart was troubled, and moved violently out of its place.
JOB 37:2 Hear the report made by the fierce anger of the Lord! when a threat shall proceed from his mouth;
JOB 37:3 as his dominion extendeth over all under heaven, and his light over the wings of the earth;
JOB 37:4 after it he will thunder with a voice; he will thunder with the voice of his indignation. [And should it not make a change in those men when he shall cause his voice to be heard?]
JOB 37:5 With his voice the Almighty will thunder to our astonishment; for he hath done great things which we cannot comprehend;
JOB 37:6 issuing a command to snow, be thou on the earth; When the tempest and storms of rain, under his command
JOB 37:7 seal up against the hand of every man, that every man may know his own weakness;
JOB 37:8 when the beasts have entered their coverts, and have gone to rest on their beds;
JOB 37:9 sorrows issue forth from their chambers, and cold from its lofty summits;
JOB 37:10 which by the blast of the Almighty produce frost, and governeth the water as he pleaseth.
JOB 37:11 But when a cloud covereth a man of his choice, his light can disperse the cloud:
JOB 37:12 and he at his sovereign pleasure, can cause the revolving agents to return to their works.
JOB 37:13 What things soever he giveth them in charge: these are ordered by him on the earth; and whether they be for correction, or for the benefit of the earth; or for mercy, he is to be found in them.
JOB 37:14 Hearken, Job, to these things and stand instructed with regard to the power of the Lord.
JOB 37:15 We know that God hath disposed his works; that he hath made light out of darkness;
JOB 37:16 That he knoweth the different purposes of clouds, and the miraculous fall of wicked men.
JOB 37:17 Now thy cloathing is warm and there is peace in the land.
JOB 37:18 With him are powerful cordials for inveterate disorders: what an appearance of an infusion!
JOB 37:19 Therefore teach me what we shall say to him. And let us refrain from much speaking.
JOB 37:20 Have I had a book or a scribe by me, that by stopping the man I could be silent?
JOB 37:21 Though the light is not visible to all, there is a brightening in the heavens, like that which cometh in clouds from him.
JOB 37:22 From the north the clouds brighten like fulgent gold.
JOB 37:23 For these things great is the glory and honour of the Almighty. As we cannot find another equal to him in majesty; dost thou not think that he who judgeth righteously will hear?
JOB 37:24 Men therefore ought to fear him. They indeed who are wise in heart, will fear him.
JOB 38:1 After Elius had finished his speech, the Lord from a whirlwind and clouds, said to Job,
JOB 38:2 Who is this who is concealing counsel from me, and who hiding words in his heart thinketh to hide them from me?
JOB 38:3 Gird up thy loins like a man and I will question thee and answer thou me.
JOB 38:4 Where wast thou, when I laid the foundations of the earth? And tell me, if thou hast understanding,
JOB 38:5 who settled the measures of it? Dost thou know? Or who stretched the line upon it?
JOB 38:6 To what are the hooks of it fastened? And who laid the corner stone thereof?
JOB 38:7 When the stars were made, all my angels praised me with a loud voice.
JOB 38:8 It was I who shut up the sea with gates, when it rushed eagerly from its mother's womb.
JOB 38:9 It was I who made a cloud its cloathing; and thick darkness its swaddling bands.
JOB 38:10 It was I who set bounds to it; surrounded it with bars and gates;
JOB 38:11 and said to it, Thus far thou shalt come and no farther: but in thyself thy waves shall be spent.
JOB 38:12 Was it in concert with thee that I ordered the morning light; and that the day spring knew its appointed time
JOB 38:13 to tinge the wings of the earth; to scare the wicked from it?
JOB 38:14 Didst thou take clay of the earth and form an animal and place on the earth a creature endowed with speech?
JOB 38:15 Hast thou withdrawn the light from the wicked, and broken in pieces the arms of the haughty?
JOB 38:16 Hast thou gone to the head spring of the sea; and walked in the footsteps of the abyss?
JOB 38:17 Are the gates of Hades opened to thee through fear, and are the porters of Hades struck with awe at seeing thee?
JOB 38:18 Hast thou informed thyself of the breadth of that under heaven? Tell me then what is the extent of it.
JOB 38:19 In what country doth light make its abode, and of what sort is the place of darkness?
JOB 38:20 If thou wouldst lead me to their borders, and if thou knewest their paths;
JOB 38:21 I would know that thou wast then born, and that the number of thy years is great.
JOB 38:22 Hast thou gone to the treasuries of snow, or hast thou seen the treasuries of hail?
JOB 38:23 Are they stored up for thee, for a time of enemies; for a day of battles and combat?
JOB 38:24 From what place doth hoar frost issue, or whence is the south wind scattered over the earth?
JOB 38:25 Who hath prepared a course for the tempest,
JOB 38:26 and a way for impetuous storms to water the ground, where there is not a man; the desert where no man dwelleth; to saturate an untrodden, uninhabited land
JOB 38:27 and cause the bud of the tender herb to spring?
JOB 38:28 Who is the father of rain, and who hath begotten the drops of dew?
JOB 38:29 From whose womb doth ice proceed, and who in the sky hath brought forth hail
JOB 38:30 which descendeth like a shower? Who hath struck with terror the face of the wicked?
JOB 38:31 Dost thou know the band of Pleias, or hast thou opened the hedge of Orion?
JOB 38:32 Canst thou cause Mazouroth to come forth in his season, or drag out Hesperus by his hair?
JOB 38:33 Dost thou know the revolutions of heaven, or the things on earth corresponding to them?
JOB 38:34 Canst thou summon a cloud with thy voice, and will it, with the trembling of a water spout, answer thee?
JOB 38:35 Canst thou despatch thunders, that they may go, and will they say to thee, Here we are?
JOB 38:36 Who hath given woman a skill in weaving, and a knowledge of the art of embroidering?
JOB 38:37 Who is it who numbereth the clouds with wisdom, and hath caused the heaven to incline to the earth,
JOB 38:38 when the earth was poured out like dust, and when I have glued the very clod as for a stone?
JOB 38:39 Wilt thou hunt the prey for lions, or satisfy the appetites of dragons?
JOB 38:40 For they are trembling for fear in their dens, and lying in ambush in their coverts.
JOB 38:41 Who hath provided food for the raven? For his young have cried to the Lord, wandering about in search of provisions.
JOB 39:1 Hast thou known the time of the rock-goat's delivery, and watched the pangs of hinds in travail?
JOB 39:2 Hast thou numbered the months they go with young, and hast thou dismissed their pangs?
JOB 39:3 Hast thou brought up their young, devoid of fear, and wilt thou dismiss their pangs also?
JOB 39:4 Shall they cast off their young, and be encreased with a new progeny, and shall they go forth and no more return to them?
JOB 39:5 Who hath sent forth the wild ass free, and who hath loosed his bands?
JOB 39:6 As I made the desart his habitation, and the saltish soil his place of encampment;
JOB 39:7 he scorneth the crowds of a city, and regardeth not the clamours of a driver.
JOB 39:8 The range of mountains he will consider as his pasture, and he search eth after every thing green.
JOB 39:9 Will the unicorn condescend to serve thee, or to go to rest at thy stall?
JOB 39:10 Canst thou bind his yoke with thongs, or will he draw thy furrows in the field?
JOB 39:11 Hast thou relied on him because his strength is great?
JOB 39:12 Wilt thou leave thy labours to him, and trust that he will carry out thy seed, and bring home thy threshed grain?
JOB 39:13 Why is the wing of the ostrich that of the sportive? For though it comprehendeth that of the stork and falcon,
JOB 39:14 yet she will commit her eggs to the ground, and hatch them in the dust;
JOB 39:15 not remembering that the foot may crush, and wild beasts trample them.
JOB 39:16 She hardened herself against her young, as if not her's; she laboured in vain without fear;
JOB 39:17 because God had silenced wisdom in her. But did he not impart to her some understanding?
JOB 39:18 At a suitable occasion she will rear herself aloft; she will laugh to scorn the horse and his rider.
JOB 39:19 Hast thou invested the horse with strength, and clothed his neck with terror?
JOB 39:20 When thou arrayedst him with armour didst thou inspire his dauntless breast with courage?
JOB 39:21 Pawing in the plain he swelleth with pride, and rusheth impetuous to the field.
JOB 39:22 Meeting a king he meeteth him with scorn, and turneth not back for fear of the sword.
JOB 39:23 On him the bow and the sword swell with pride; and his rage will cause the ground to vanish,
JOB 39:24 nor will he believe till the trumpet sounds:
JOB 39:25 but at the sound of the trumpet he saith, Aha, and snuffeth the battle from afar, with a bound and neighing.
JOB 39:26 Hath the hawk by thy wisdom poised herself aloft with wings expanded, unmoved, surveying the regions of the south?
JOB 39:27 At thy command doth the eagle soar, and the vulture abide seated on its nest,
JOB 39:28 on the high crag of a rock, and in secret,
JOB 39:29 and continuing there seek its food? Its eyes take an extensive survey,
JOB 39:30 and its young are besmeared with blood. Wherever carcasses are, there are they suddenly found.
JOB 40:1 Then the Lord God addressing Job, said,
JOB 40:2 1 Doth he decline a trial with the Almighty? Surely he who commenceth a suit against God, should support it.
JOB 40:3 Whereupon Job, in reply, said to the Lord,
JOB 40:4 Why should I continue the debate any further? I stand corrected for commencing a suit against the Lord. On hearing such things, what answer can I, who am nothing, make to Thee? I will lay my hand on my mouth.
JOB 40:5 Once I have spoken, but I will not proceed a second time. I heard of Thee before, with the hearing of the ear; but now mine eye hath seen Thee, therefore I abhor myself, and am ready to drop into dissolution, and account myself as dust and ashes.
JOB 40:6 Whereupon the Lord further said to Job from the cloud:
JOB 40:7 No, but gird now up thy loins like a man, and let Me question thee; and do thou answer Me.
JOB 40:8 Decline not the trial with Me. Dost thou think that I have spoken to thee for any other purpose, but that thou mayst appear justified?
JOB 40:9 Hast thou an arm to contend against the Lord, or dost thou thunder with a voice against Him?
JOB 40:10 Assume then majesty and power, and array thyself with glory and excellence;
JOB 40:11 and send forth angels in wrath, and humble everyone who is insolent.
JOB 40:12 Extinguish also the haughty, and turn the wicked into instant corruption.
JOB 40:13 Hide them in the earth together, and cover their faces with dishonour.
JOB 40:14 Then will I confess that thine own right hand can save thee.
JOB 40:15 But behold now the wild beasts around thee, which feed upon grass like cattle;
JOB 40:16 behold that one in particular whose strength is in his loins, and whose power is in the navel of his belly.
JOB 40:17 He hath raised his tail like a cypress, and his sinews are plaited together.
JOB 40:18 His ribs are ribs of brass, and his back bone is molten iron;
JOB 40:19 he is a chief of the Lord's fashioning, made to be insulted by his angels only.
JOB 40:20 When he went up to the craggy mountain, he gave joy to the four footed beasts in the vale.
JOB 40:21 They go to rest under trees of every sort, by the papyrus, the reed and the bulrush:
JOB 40:22 But by him large trees with branches, and the bushes of the field are overshadowed.
JOB 40:23 Should there come a flood he would not regard it; he is confident the Jordan can roll into his mouth.
JOB 40:24 Can one look steadily at him, can one craftily bore his nose?
JOB 41:1 Canst thou draw out Dragon with a hook, or put a bandage round his nostrils?
JOB 41:2 Or canst thou fasten a ring in his snout, or bore his lip for a jewel?
JOB 41:3 Will he speak to thee with entreaties; with soothing supplications?
JOB 41:4 Will he make a covenant with thee? And wilt thou take him for a perpetual servant?
JOB 41:5 Wilt thou play with him as with a bird, or bind him as a sparrow for a child?
JOB 41:6 Do the nations feed upon him, or the Phoenicians divide him among them?
JOB 41:7 With their whole fleet they could not carry the first skin of his tail, nor his head in their fishing barks.
JOB 41:8 Wilt thou lay thine hand on him, recollecting the battle made by his mouth? Do not so again.
JOB 41:9 Hast thou not seen him? Hast thou not been amazed at what is said of him? Hast thou not been afraid that he was prepared against me?
JOB 41:10 But who is there, who hath risen up against me;
JOB 41:11 or who can rise up against me and stand to it? If the whole world is mine,
JOB 41:12 I cannot be put to silence by him. On the account of his power one may pity his equal.
JOB 41:13 Who can strip off his outer robe, or who can come within the folds of his breast plate?
JOB 41:14 Who can open the doors of his mouth? His teeth are encompassed with terror.
JOB 41:15 His scales are shields of brass; and his ligature, like a smyrite stone.
JOB 41:16 They are glued one to another, so that no air may pass through to him.
JOB 41:17 They are to adhere close to each other; they stick so close that they cannot be torn asunder.
JOB 41:18 At his sneezing lightnings flash: and his eyes have the lustre of the morning star.
JOB 41:19 Out of his mouth issue as it were burning lamps; and flaky flames, in appearance, are belched out.
JOB 41:20 From his nostrils issueth the smoke of a furnace,
JOB 41:21 flaming with a fire of burning coals. His animal life is glowing coals; and a flame proceedeth out of his mouth.
JOB 41:22 In his neck, strength maketh its abode; and destruction runneth before him.
JOB 41:23 The flesh of his body is glued together; it is so abundant that he cannot be shaken.
JOB 41:24 His heart is hard as a stone, and firm as an immoveable anvil.
JOB 41:25 When he turneth himself about, all the four footed beasts on the earth shrink with fear. Though spears oppose him,
JOB 41:26 they effect nothing; for with regard to the lance and the breast plate,
JOB 41:27 he considereth iron as straw, and brass as rotten wood.
JOB 41:28 The bow of steel cannot wound him; and stones from a sling he considereth as grass.
JOB 41:29 Battering rams are accounted as stubble; and he laugheth at the shock of eruptive fire.
JOB 41:30 His bed is sharp pointed obelisks; and all the gold in the sea under him, is but as dirt.
JOB 41:31 He causeth the deep to boil like a cauldron; and considereth the sea as a pot of ointment.
JOB 41:32 The deepest gulf of the sea he accounteth his captive; and reckoneth the abyss itself as his parade.
JOB 41:33 Upon the earth there is not his fellow; made to be insulted only by my angels.
JOB 41:34 He beholdeth every thing that is high; and he is king over all that are in the waters.
JOB 42:1 Then Job in reply, said to the Lord,
JOB 42:2 I know that thou canst do all things, and that with thee nothing is impossible.
JOB 42:3 Who indeed can conceal counsel from thee? Though he forbeareth to speak, can he think to hide it from thee? But who will tell me those things which I did not know; those great and wonderful things which I did not understand.
JOB 42:4 Hear me, O Lord, that I may speak. And let me ask, and do thou teach me.
JOB 42:5 I heard of thee before, with the hearing of the ear; but now mine eye hath seen thee,
JOB 42:6 therefore I abhor myself, and am ready to drop into dissolution, and account myself as dust and ashes.
JOB 42:7 Now after the Lord had spoken all these things to Job, the Lord said to Eliphaz, the Thaimanite, Thou hast sinned and thy two friends. For you have not spoken any thing true before me, as my servant Job hath.
JOB 42:8 Now therefore take seven young bulls and seven rams, and go to my servant Job, and he will make an offering for you; and my servant Job will pray for you. For him only I will accept; for were it not for his sake, I would destroy you, because you have not spoken what is true against my servant Job.
JOB 42:9 So Eliphaz the Thaimanite, and Baldad the Sauchean, and Sophar the Minaian, went and did as the Lord commanded them, and he forgave them their sin for Job's sake.
JOB 42:10 And the Lord increased Job. upon his making supplication for his friends, the Lord forgave them their sins, and the Lord gave Job twice as much as he had before.
JOB 42:11 When all his brethren and his sisters heard what had befallen him, they came to him, together with all those who were formerly acquainted with him, and having eaten and drank at his house, they comforted him, and expressed their amazement at all that the Lord had brought upon him. And every one presented him a lamb, and a quarter of a drachm of gold bullion.
JOB 42:12 And the Lord blessed the latter days of Job more than the former; so that his stock was fourteen thousand sheep, six thousand camels, a thousand yoke of oxen, a thousand breeding asses.
JOB 42:13 And he had seven sons born to him, and three daughters, the eldest of whom he called Hemera, and the second Kasia,
JOB 42:14 and the third Amalthaiakeres.
JOB 42:15 And in all the land there were no women found so fair as the daughters of Job. And their father gave them an inheritance among their brothers.
JOB 42:16 And Job lived after this affliction a hundred and seventy years. So that all the years which he lived were two hundred and forty. And Job saw his children and his children's children, to the fourth generation,
JOB 42:17 and died an old man and full of days. And it is written that he will rise again with them whom the Lord raiseth up. This is translated out of a book in the Syrian language: For he dwelt in the land of Ausitis, on the confines of Idumea and Arabia. His first name was Jobab, and having married an Arabian woman, he had by her a son whose name was Ennon. Now he himself was a son of father Zare, one of the sons of Esau, and his mother"s name was Bosorra: so that he was the fifth in descent from Abraham. Now these were the kings who reigned in Edom, over which country he also bore rule. The first was Balak, the son of Beor, and the name of his city was Dannaba. And after Balak, Jobab, who is called Job; and after him, Asom who was general from the region of Thaimanitis; and after him, Adad, son of Barad, who smote Madiam in the plain of Moab; and the name of his city was Gethaim. And the friends who came to Job were Eliphaz, of the sons of Esau, the king of the Thaimanites; Baldad, the sovereign of the Saucheans, and Sophar, the king of the Minaians.
PSA 1:1 Happy the man, who hath not walked by the counsel of the wicked; nor stood in the way of sinners; nor sat in the seat of the scornful.
PSA 1:2 His delight will be in the law of the Lord only. And on his law he will meditate day and night.
PSA 1:3 And he will be like the tree planted by the streams of water, which will yield its fruit in due season, and its fruit shall not fall untimely. In all that he doth he shall be prospered.
PSA 1:4 Not so the wicked; not so. They are like the chaff, which the wind driveth from the face of the earth.
PSA 1:5 Therefore the wicked shall not stand in judgment, nor sinners in the counsel of the righteous.
PSA 1:6 For the Lord knoweth the way of the righteous: and the way of the ungodly shall perish.
PSA 2:1 Why did nations rage? And tribes meditate vain things?
PSA 2:2 The kings of the earth combined; and the chiefs assembled together, against the Lord and against his Anointed, [saying]
PSA 2:3 "Let us break their bands asunder and throw off from us their yoke."
PSA 2:4 He who dwelleth in heaven will laugh them to scorn; the Lord will treat them with derision.
PSA 2:5 Then will he speak to them in his wrath and trouble them with his sore displeasure.
PSA 2:6 But as for me, by him I am appointed king on Sion his holy mountain.
PSA 2:7 I proclaim the decree of the Lord; to me the Lord said, "Thou art my Son, this day I have begotten thee,
PSA 2:8 "Ask of me, and I will give thee nations for thine inheritance, and the uttermost parts of the earth for thy possession.
PSA 2:9 Thou shalt rule them with a rod of iron. Thou shalt break them to pieces like a potter's vessel."
PSA 2:10 Now therefore, O kings, be wise: Be instructed, all ye, who judge the earth.
PSA 2:11 Serve the Lord with fear: and rejoice for him with trembling.
PSA 2:12 Keep fast hold of instruction; the Lord may be angry and you may perish out of the right way. When his anger suddenly blazeth forth, happy are all they who have trusted in him.
PSA 3:1 A Psalm by David, when he fled from the presence of his son Abessalom. Lord! why have they who afflicted me multiplied? Many are risen up against me.
PSA 3:2 Many say respecting my life, In this God of his he hath no safety.
PSA 3:3 But thou, Lord, art my protector; my glory, and the lifter up of my head.
PSA 3:4 With my voice I cried to the Lord, and from his holy mount he heard me.
PSA 3:5 I laid me down to rest and slept; I awoke. Because the Lord will protect me,
PSA 3:6 I will not be afraid of myriads of people; of them who are besetting me round about.
PSA 3:7 Arise, Lord; save me, my God! Because thou hast smitten all them, who foolishly were mine enemies; hast broken the teeth of sinners:
PSA 3:8 this deliverance is the Lord's: let thy blessing be upon thy people also.
PSA 4:1 For the conclusion with psalms. An Ode by David. When I made my supplication; my righteous God heard me: thou hast enlarged me in distress: be gracious to me and hear my prayer.
PSA 4:2 Sons of men! how long will you be stubborn! why love ye vanity and seek falsehood?
PSA 4:3 Know that the Lord hath made his holy one Wonderful. The Lord will hearken to me when I cry to him.
PSA 4:4 Are you provoked to wrath? Do not therefore commit sin. What you say in your hearts be sorry for, on your beds.
PSA 4:5 Offer a sacrifice of righteousness and trust in the Lord.
PSA 4:6 Many say, Who will shew us good things? On us, Lord, is marked the light of thy countenance:
PSA 4:7 thou hast put gladness in my heart. Because of the increase of their corn and wine and oil they are filled;
PSA 4:8 while I will lay me down in peace and sleep because thou, Lord, hast only caused me to dwell in hope.

PSA 5:3 In the morning thou shalt hear my voice: in the morning I will wait on thee and look up.
PSA 5:4 Because thou art not a God pleased with iniquity; therefore he who is wicked cannot dwell near thee:
PSA 5:5 nor shall transgressors continue in thy presence. Thou Lord, hatest all the workers of iniquity:
PSA 5:6 thou wilt destroy all them who speak lies; a bloody and deceitful man the Lord abhorreth.
PSA 5:7 As for me, I through thine abundant mercy, will go to thy house: I will worship before thy holy temple, in thy fear.
PSA 5:8 Lead me, Lord, in thy saving goodness: direct my way before thee, because of mine enemies; because there is no truth in their mouth.

PSA 5:11 But let all, whose hope is in thee, rejoice. They shall exult forever, and thou wilt dwell among them: and all who love thy name will glory in thee;
PSA 5:12 because thou wilt bless the righteous. Thou, Lord, hast covered us as with armour of favour.
PSA 6:1 For the conclusion, among Hymns for the eighth day. A Psalm by David. O Lord, rebuke me not in thy wrath; nor chasten me in thine anger.
PSA 6:2 Pity me, Lord, for I am weak. Heal me, Lord, for my bones are troubled.
PSA 6:3 My soul is troubled exceedingly: but Lord, for how long?
PSA 6:4 Return, Lord; deliver my soul: save me for thy mercy's sake.
PSA 6:5 For in death none can make mention of thee. In the mansion of the dead, who can give thee thanks?
PSA 6:6 I am weary with my groaning. Am I every night to bedew my bed and water my couch with my tears?
PSA 6:7 Mine eye is troubled with indignation: I am grown old among all mine enemies.

PSA 6:9 the Lord hath heard my supplication: the Lord hath received my petition.
PSA 6:10 Let all mine enemies be shamed and greatly troubled. Let them be turned back and instantly put to shame.

PSA 7:2 perhaps he like a lion may tear my soul; if there be none to redeem; none to deliver.

PSA 7:9 Let the wickedness of sinners be brought to an end. Thou wilt indeed direct the righteous: thou art the God who searcheth hearts and reins.

PSA 7:11 God, who is a judge just and powerful; [though he is long suffering and doth not execute vengeance every day]

PSA 7:13 and hath fitted to it the instruments of death; those flaming bolts of his which he hath forged.

PSA 7:15 he hath digged a pit and covered it: into the pit which he made he will fall:
PSA 7:16 his mischief will return on his own head; on his own head his injustice will come down.
PSA 7:17 I shall praise the Lord for his loving kindness. I shall sing to the name of the Lord Most High.
PSA 8:1 For the conclusion. For the wine presses. A Psalm by David. Lord, our Lord, how thy name ought to be admired in all the earth, since thine excellence is exalted above the heavens!
PSA 8:2 From the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise, on account of thine enemies; [on account] of destroying an enemy and a revenger.
PSA 8:3 When I behold the heavens, the work of thy fingers; the moon and stars which thou hast established,
PSA 8:4 what is man that thou shouldst be mindful of him, or a son of man that thou shouldst visit him!
PSA 8:5 Thou madest him a little lower than angels, with glory and honour thou hast crowned him,
PSA 8:6 and set him over the works of thy hands. Thou hast put all things under his feet;
PSA 8:7 flocks and herds of all sorts; also the beasts of the field;
PSA 8:8 the birds of the air, and fishes of the sea; whatever travel the paths of the seas.
PSA 8:9 O Lord, our Lord, how thy name ought to be admired in all the earth!
PSA 9:1 For the conclusion. On the mysteries of the Son. A Psalm by David. I Will praise thee, Lord, with my whole heart, I will relate all thy Wondrous works.
PSA 9:2 Let me be gladdened and rejoice in thee; to thy name I will sing, O thou Most High.
PSA 9:3 When this enemy of mine is turned back, at thy presence they shall faint and perish;
PSA 9:4 because thou hast maintained my right and my cause. Thou the righteous judge hast sat on the throne;
PSA 9:5 thou hast rebuked nations, and the wicked one is destroyed. Thou hast blotted out their Name forever and ever.
PSA 9:6 The enemy's swords have utterly failed, and thou hast completely destroyed cities, the memorial of them with their din is gone.
PSA 9:7 But the Lord will endure forever: he hath prepared his throne for judgment;
PSA 9:8 he will judge the World with righteousness; with rectitude he will judge tribes.
PSA 9:9 The Lord was a refuge for the distressed, a seasonable helper in adversity.
PSA 9:10 Let them who know thy name confide in thee; For thou, Lord, hast not forsaken them who seek thee.
PSA 9:11 Sing to the Lord who dwelleth in Sion; among the nations proclaim his designs,
PSA 9:12 for in making inquisition for blood, he had them in remembrance; he forgot not the prayer of the distressed.
PSA 9:13 Have mercy upon me, O Lord! Behold my affliction, because of mine enemies, O thou who raisest me up from the gates of death,
PSA 9:14 that I may proclaim all thy praises in the gates of the daughter of Sion. Let me exult with joy for thy salvation.
PSA 9:15 The nations were completely entrapped by the destruction which they contrived; in the gin which they hid, their foot is caught.
PSA 9:16 The Lord is known by executing judgments; by the works of his own hands the sinner is taken.
PSA 9:17 [17-20 A responsive Ode.] Let the sinners be turned back to the mansion of the dead; all the nations who forget God.
PSA 9:18 For the poor shall not be quite forgotten; the expectation of the needy shall never perish.
PSA 9:19 Arise, Lord, let not man prevail; let nations be judged in thy presence.
PSA 9:20 Appoint, O Lord, a legislator over them; let nations know that they are men.
PSA 10:1 Why, O Lord, hast thou stood at a distance; dost thou overlook at proper occasions; in adversity?
PSA 10:2 When the wicked exulteth with pride, the poor is set on fire; they are caught by the counsels which they devise.
PSA 10:3 Because the sinner is praised for the desires of his soul; therefore he who committeth injustice is blessed.
PSA 10:4 The sinner hath greatly provoked the Lord; according to his great anger will he not make inquisition? God is not before his eyes;
PSA 10:5 his ways are polluted on every occasion. Thy judgments are removed from his sight; shall he have a mastery over all his enemies?
PSA 10:6 For he said in his heart, I shall not he moved and I shall never be in adversity.
PSA 10:7 Is not his mouth full of cursing, and bitterness and deceit?
PSA 10:8 Under his tongue there is mischief and sorrow. He sat in secret places with the rich to slay the innocent; His eyes are on the watch for the distressed.
PSA 10:9 He lurketh in secret like a lion in his den; He lurketh to make a prey of the poor. To make a prey of the poor when he hath drawn him in; in his net he will humble him.
PSA 10:10 He will stoop and crouch at his tyrannising over the poor;
PSA 10:11 For he said in his heart God hath forgotten; He hath turned his face from ever seeing.
PSA 10:12 Arise, Lord God, let thy hand be lifted up; Forget not the oppressed.
PSA 10:13 Why hath the wicked provoked God?; For he said in his heart, He will not make inquisition.
PSA 10:14 Thou seest [for thou observest mischief and wrath]; That they have delivered themselves into thy hands. To thee the poor hath committed himself; Thou art the helper of the fatherless.
PSA 10:15 Break the arm of the sinful and malicious man. Let his sin be sought out till no more can be found.
PSA 10:16 Let the Lord reign for ever and ever! Perish ye nations out of his land!
PSA 10:17 The Lord hath hearkened to the desire of the oppressed: Thine ear hath attended to the preparation of their heart;
PSA 10:18 to administer justice to the fatherless and the weak: That man may no longer continue his insolence in the land.

PSA 11:2 For behold the sinners have bent a bow: they have provided arrows for a quiver; to shoot privily the upright in heart.
PSA 11:3 For what thou didst build up, they have pulled down." Now what hath the righteous done?
PSA 11:4 The Lord is in his holy temple. The Lord, whose throne is in heaven; whose eyes look down on the needy; whose eye lids examine the sons of men;
PSA 11:5 the Lord examineth both the righteous and the wicked. He then who loveth iniquity hateth his own soul.
PSA 11:6 Upon the wicked he will rain snares. Fire and brimstone and a tempestuous wind, shall be the portion of their cup.
PSA 11:7 Because the Lord is righteous, therefore he loved righteousness; his countenance beheld uprightness.

PSA 12:2 They spoke vanities one to another: their lips are deceitful, they spoke with a double heart:
PSA 12:3 May the Lord destroy all deceitful lips; and the tongue which speaketh swelling words;
PSA 12:4 them who say, "We will magnify our tongue: our lips are our own: who is Lord over us?"
PSA 12:5 Because of the oppression of the poor; because of the groans of the needy; now will I arise, saith the Lord; I will set in safety and speak boldly.
PSA 12:6 The oracles of the Lord are pure oracles; tried silver, clear of dross, seven times purified.
PSA 12:7 Thou, Lord, wilt keep us and preserve us, from this generation, and forever.

PSA 13:2 How long shall I revolve counsels in my mind, and sorrows in my heart? For years? How long shall mine enemy be exalted over me?

PSA 13:5 As for me, I have trusted in thy mercy; let my heart rejoice in thy salvation:

PSA 14:1 For the conclusion. A Psalm by David. The fool said in his heart, There is no God. They are corrupt and by their works abominable: there is none who doeth good. No not one.
PSA 14:2 The Lord looked down from heaven on the children of men; to see if any had understanding or were seeking God.
PSA 14:3 They had all gone aside, they were altogether become vile: there is none who doeth good; no not one. Their throat is an open sepulchre: with their tongues they practised deceit: the poison of asps is under the lips of them whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness: their feet are swift to shed blood: destruction and misery are in their ways: and the way of peace they did not know: there is no fear of God before their eyes.
PSA 14:4 Will they all continue senseless? They are going on in a course of iniquity: they are eating up my people as they do bread: they have not called on the Lord.
PSA 14:5 They were seized with terror, where there was no fear; because God was among a righteous generation.
PSA 14:6 Have you despised the counsel of the poor; because his trust is in the Lord?
PSA 14:7 that he would for Sion's sake send deliverance to Israel! When the Lord hath brought back the captives of his people: Let Jacob rejoice and let Israel be glad.
PSA 15:1 A Psalm by David. Lord! who shall sojourn at thy tabernacle? And who shall dwell on thy holy mountain?
PSA 15:2 He who walketh blameless and Worketh righteousness: And who speaketh truth from his heart.
PSA 15:3 Who hath not deceived with his tongue; nor done evil to his neighbour; nor taken up a reproach against his neighbours.
PSA 15:4 In whose sight an evil doer is contemned; but who honoureth them who fear the Lord: who sweareth to his neighbour; and doth not violate his engagements:
PSA 15:5 who hath not lent his money on usury; nor taken bribes against the innocent. He whose practise is such, shall never be moved.
PSA 16:1 An inscription for a pillar. By David. Preserve me, Lord: for in thee I have trusted.
PSA 16:2 I said to the Lord, Thou art my Lord: thou hast no need of my goods.
PSA 16:3 By the hallowed things in this land of his he had marvellously displayed all his designs.
PSA 16:4 Their infirmities were multiplied: after these hallowed things they hastened. I will no more assemble their congregations for blood, nor make mention of their names with my lips.
PSA 16:5 The Lord is the portion of mine inheritance and of my cup: thou art he who restoreth me mine inheritance.
PSA 16:6 The lines have fallen to me in the best places: for this inheritance of mine is the best for me.
PSA 16:7 I will bless the Lord who hath given me understanding: even now at night my reins have instructed me.
PSA 16:8 I saw the Lord continually before me. Because he is at my right hand that I may not be moved;
PSA 16:9 therefore my heart was gladdened; and my tongue exulted with joy: moreover my flesh also will dwell in hope;
PSA 16:10 that thou wilt not leave my soul in the mansion of the dead nor suffer thine Holy One to see corruption.
PSA 16:11 Thou hast made known to me the ways of life: thou with thy presence wilt fill me with joy. At thy right hand are pleasures for evermore.
PSA 17:1 A Prayer of David. Hearken, Lord, to my justification; attend to my supplication: give ear to my prayer which is not made with feigned lips.
PSA 17:2 Let my sentence come forth from thy presence: Let mine eyes behold righteous decisions.
PSA 17:3 Thou hast proved my heart: thou hast watched me by night: thou hast tried me: and in me there was found no injustice.
PSA 17:4 That my mouth might not speak the works of these men; I, because of the words of thy lips, kept rugged ways.
PSA 17:5 Establish my footsteps in thy paths; that my footsteps may not be moved.
PSA 17:6 I have cried, because thou, O God, didst hear me: incline thine ear to me and hear my words.
PSA 17:7 Display marvellously thy mercies, O thou, who, with thy right hand, savest from adversaries them who trust in thee.
PSA 17:8 Keep me as the apple of an eye: with the cover of thy wings
PSA 17:9 thou wilt shelter me from the face of the wicked who afflict me. These enemies of mine beset my soul:
PSA 17:10 they shut up their fat; their mouth spoke proudly.
PSA 17:11 Having driven me out they now enclosed me. They set their eyes inclining to the ground.
PSA 17:12 They observed me, like a lion eager for prey, and like a young lion lurking in coverts.
PSA 17:13 Arise, Lord, prevent them and cause them to stumble. Deliver my soul from the wicked: wrest thy sword
PSA 17:14 from thine enemies hand Dismiss them, Lord, from the land: disperse them in their life time. Though their belly was filled with thy stores; they glutted themselves with swine's flesh, and left the relicks for their children.
PSA 17:15 But as for me, let me appear righteous before thee; let me be satisfied with a display of thy glory.
PSA 18:1 For the conclusion. By David the servant of the Lord: who spake to the Lord the words of this Ode on the day when the Lord delivered him out of the hand of all his enemies, and out of the hand of Saul; and he said: I Will love thee, Lord, my strength!
PSA 18:2 The Lord is my support, my refuge and my deliverer. My God is my helper, in him I will trust: my protector, the horn of my salvation and my defender.
PSA 18:3 In songs of praise I will call on the Lord, and I shall be saved from mine enemies.
PSA 18:4 The pangs of death encompassed me; and floods of iniquity startled me.
PSA 18:5 The pangs of Hades surrounded me, and the snares of death were before me.
PSA 18:6 In my distress I called on the Lord, and to my God I raised my cry. From his holy temple he heard my voice; and my cry before him reached his ears.
PSA 18:7 Then was the earth shaken: it trembled; and the foundations of the hills were convulsed and shaken; because at mine enemies God was incensed.
PSA 18:8 A smoke ascended in his ire, and at his presence a fire flamed, by which coals were kindled to a glow.
PSA 18:9 And he bowed the heaven and came down, and darkness was under his feet.
PSA 18:10 He mounted on cherubs and flew; he flew on the wings of winds.
PSA 18:11 But he made darkness his covering, His tent around him was dark water in clouds of air.
PSA 18:12 At the flash of the lightning before him, the clouds burst. Hail stones and coals of fire!
PSA 18:13 Then the Lord thundered from heaven, the Most High uttered his voice:
PSA 18:14 He sent forth his bolts and scattered them: he multiplied his lightnings and confounded them.
PSA 18:15 Then were seen the head springs of waters, and the foundations of the World were disclosed, at thy rebuke. Lord; at the blowing of the blast of thine anger.
PSA 18:16 He sent from on high and took me; he took me to himself from many waters.
PSA 18:17 He will deliver me from my potent enemies; and from them who hate me; because they are stronger than I.
PSA 18:18 They surprised me in the day of my distress; but the Lord was my firm support;
PSA 18:19 and brought me out to a large place. He will deliver me because he delighted in me.
PSA 18:20 The Lord will reward me according to my righteousness, and recompense me according to the cleanness of my hands.
PSA 18:21 Because I have kept the ways of the Lord, and have not wickedly departed from my God;
PSA 18:22 because all his judgments were before me, and his rules of rectitude were not far from me;
PSA 18:23 therefore with him I shall be unblemished, and I will guard myself from mine iniquity;
PSA 18:24 and the Lord will reward me according to my righteousness, and according to the cleanness of my hands in his sight.
PSA 18:25 With the merciful thou will shew thyself merciful,
PSA 18:26 and with a harmless man thou wilt be harmless; with a warrior thou wilt be a warrior, and with the wily, thou wilt practise wiles.
PSA 18:27 Because thou wilt save a dejected people; therefore the eyes of the lofty thou wilt humble.
PSA 18:28 Because thou, Lord, wilt light my lamp; thou, my God, wilt enlighten my darkness;
PSA 18:29 by thee therefore I shall be delivered from a roving band; and by my God I shall overleap a wall.
PSA 18:30 As for my God, his way is spotless; the oracles of the Lord are tried, he is the protector of all who trust in him.
PSA 18:31 For who is God, besides the Lord? And who is God, save our God?
PSA 18:32 It is thou, God, who girdest me with strength, and hast made my way spotless;
PSA 18:33 who makest my feet like those of a hind, and who steadiest me on high places;
PSA 18:34 who instructest my hands for battle, and hast made my arms like a bow of steel,
PSA 18:35 and given me a defence for my safety; and thy right hand hath helped me, and thy discipline hath upheld me to the last: this discipline of thine will still teach me.
PSA 18:36 Thou hast enlarged my steps under me, and my tread was not unsteady.
PSA 18:37 I shall pursue mine enemies and overtake them, and not turn back till they are destroyed.
PSA 18:38 I shall harass them that they may not be able to stand; they shall fall down under my feet.
PSA 18:39 For thou hast girded me with strength for battle, and subdued under me all that rose up against me.
PSA 18:40 Thou hast given me the backs of mine enemies, and utterly destroyed them who hate me.
PSA 18:41 They cried aloud, but there was no saviour; to the Lord, but he hearkened not to them.
PSA 18:42 So that I shall beat them small as dust before the wind, and trample them down like dirt in the street.
PSA 18:43 Deliver me from the contentions of the people. Thou wilt set me at the head of nations. A people whom I knew not, have served me.
PSA 18:44 Soon as they heard, they obeyed me.
PSA 18:45 Strange children have paid me feigned obedience. Strange children became old and limped from their paths.
PSA 18:46 Live the Lord! and blessed be my God! and let the God of my salvation be exalted:
PSA 18:47 The God who hath executed vengeance for me: and subjected peoples under me;
PSA 18:48 my deliverer from outrageous enemies. From them who rise up against me, thou wilt lift me up; from the man of violence thou wilt deliver me.
PSA 18:49 For this cause I will praise thee, Lord, among the nations: And sing melodiously to thy name.
PSA 18:50 He is magnifying the deliverances of his king, and shewing mercy to his anointed; to David and his seed forever.
PSA 19:1 For the conclusion. A Psalm by David. The heavens declare the glory of God, and the firmament proclaimeth the work of his hands.
PSA 19:2 Day to day pronounceth a decree; and night to night proclaimeth knowledge.
PSA 19:3 Are they not speeches and are they not words, of which is not their utterance heard?
PSA 19:4 To every land their sound is gone forth: and their doctrines to the limits of the World.
PSA 19:5 In the sun he placed his tabernacle. And he is like a bridegroom coming forth from his chamber. He will rejoice as a giant to run his course.
PSA 19:6 His going forth is from the summit of heaven; and his course is to the summit thereof, and from his heat none can be hid.
PSA 19:7 The law of the Lord is perfect, it restoreth souls: The testimony of the Lord is faithful, it maketh infants wise.
PSA 19:8 The statutes of the Lord are right, they rejoice the heart. The commandment of the Lord is clear, it enlighteneth the eyes.
PSA 19:9 The fear of the Lord is pure, it endureth forever. The judgments of the Lord are true, they are justified for being so.
PSA 19:10 They are more to be desired than gold, or many precious stones; and sweeter than honey or the honey comb.
PSA 19:11 These indeed thy servant keepeth; for keeping them there is a great reward.
PSA 19:12 Who can understand his errors? Cleanse thou me from those of mine which are hid;
PSA 19:13 and for those of others, spare thy servant. If they gain not a dominion over me: then shall I be spotless, and clean from great transgression.
PSA 19:14 And the words of my mouth and the meditations of my heart, will be continually acceptable in thy sight: Lord, my helper and my redeemer.
