PSA 22:1 For the conclusion. On the help of the morning. A Psalm by David. God, my God! attend to me! why hast thou forsaken me? have the acts of my transgressions [removed thee] far from saving me?
PSA 22:2 my God, shall I cry to thee by day, and thou not listen, and by night, and thou not hear me?
PSA 22:3 Thou indeed dwellest in a holy place; thou art the praise of Israel.
PSA 22:4 In thee our fathers placed their trust; they trusted and thou didst deliver them. To thee they cried and they were saved;
PSA 22:5 in thee they trusted and were not put to shame.
PSA 22:6 As for me, I am a Worm, and no man; the scorn of men and the people's contempt.
PSA 22:7 All that see me have laughed me to scorn; they said with their lips while they shaked their head,
PSA 22:8 "He trusted in the Lord, let him deliver him; let him save him, since he delighteth in him."
PSA 22:9 Because thou art he, who drew me forth from the womb: my hope, when at the breasts of my mother;
PSA 22:10 I was cast on thy care from my very birth; from my mother's womb thou art my God;
PSA 22:11 stand not at a distance from me; for trouble is near; for there is no helper.
PSA 22:12 Many bulls have encompassed me; fat bulls have beset me around.
PSA 22:13 Against me they have opened their mouth, like a ravening and roaring lion.
PSA 22:14 I am poured out like water, and all my bones are torn asunder: my heart within me is melted like wax.
PSA 22:15 My strength is dried up like a potsherd, and my tongue cleaveth to my palate; thou hast indeed brought me to the dust of death.
PSA 22:16 Because many dogs have encompassed me, an assembly of wicked men have beset me; have pierced my hands and my feet;
PSA 22:17 have counted all my bones, and have stared and looked at me;
PSA 22:18 they have parted my garments among them, and for my vesture have cast lots;
PSA 22:19 Therefore, Lord, delay not thou my help, draw near to my assistance;
PSA 22:20 rescue my soul from the sword; this only begotten of mine from the paw of a dog.
PSA 22:21 Save me from the mouth of a lion, and this lowliness of mine from the unicorn's horns.
PSA 22:22 I will declare thy name to my brethren: in the midst of a congregation I will sing praise to thee.
PSA 22:23 Praise him, ye who fear the Lord praise him, all ye seed of Jacob. Let all the seed of Israel fear him;
PSA 22:24 for he hath not slighted, nor abhorred the prayer of the distressed; nor turned away his face from me: but hearkened to me when I cried to him.

PSA 23:1 A Psalm by David. The Lord is my shepherd, I shall want nothing.
PSA 23:2 In a verdant pasture he hath fixed my abode. He hath fed me by gently flowing water
PSA 23:3 and restored my soul. He hath led me in paths of righteousness for his name's sake.
PSA 23:4 For though I walk amidst the shades of death: I will fear no ills, because thou art with me; thy rod and thy staff have been my comfort.
PSA 23:5 Thou hast spread a table before me; in the presence of them who afflict me. With oil thou hast anointed my head; and thine exhilarating cup is the very best.
PSA 23:6 Thy mercy will surely follow me all the days of my life; and my dwelling shall be in the house of the Lord to length of days.

PSA 24:10 Who is this glorious king? The Lord of Hosts. He is the king of glory.

PSA 25:5 Lead me to thy truth, and teach me: for thou, God, art my saviour, and for thee I have waited all the day long.
PSA 25:6 Lord, remember thy compassion and thy tender mercies; for they are from everlasting.

PSA 25:13 his life shall be spent in the enjoyment of good things and his offspring shall inherit the land.

PSA 25:20 preserve my soul and deliver me: let me not be shamed, because I have trusted in thee.

PSA 27:2 When evil doers approached me, to devour my flesh; they, who afflicted me, even mine enemies fainted and fell.
PSA 27:3 Though a host be drawn up against me, my heart will not be dismayed; though war rise up against me, still I exercise hope.

PSA 27:7 Hear, Lord, my voice when I cry; have mercy on me and hearken to me.
PSA 27:8 To thee my heart said, I have sought thy lace; thy face, O Lord, I will seek.

PSA 27:10 Since my father and my mother have left me; and the Lord hath taken me to himself:
PSA 27:11 instruct me in thy way and lead me in the right path, because of mine enemies.
PSA 27:12 Deliver me not up to the will of them who are afflicting me. Because false witnesses have risen up against me and injustice hath belied itself;
PSA 27:13 I am confident of seeing the goodness of the Lord, in the land of the living.
PSA 27:14 Wait for the Lord and be of good courage; let thy heart be strengthened and wait for the Lord.

PSA 28:5 Because they did not regard the works of the Lord; nor the operations of his hands: thou wilt utterly destroy them and not build them up again.

PSA 28:9 Save thy people and bless thine inheritance; feed them also and lift them up forever.

PSA 30:1 For the conclusion. The Psalm of an Ode at the dedication of David's house. I Will extol thee, Lord, because thou hast upheld me, and hast not suffered mine enemies to rejoice over me.
PSA 30:2 O Lord my God, to thee I cried and thou didst heal me.
PSA 30:3 Thou, Lord, hast brought my soul up out of Hades; and saved me from among them who go down to the pit.
PSA 30:4 Sing to the Lord, ye his saints; and give thanks at the remembrance of his holiness.
PSA 30:5 Because at his wrath there is vexation; but in his favour, life; in the evening weeping may pitch its tent; and in the morning, joy.
PSA 30:6 As for me, I, in my prosperity, said, I can never be moved:
PSA 30:7 [To my comeliness, thou, Lord, in thy good pleasure hadst added strength] but thou didst turn away thy face, and I was involved in trouble.
PSA 30:8 To thee, Lord, I cried and to my God made supplication;
PSA 30:9 what profit is there in my blood; by my going down to corruption? Can dust celebrate thy praise; or can it proclaim thy truth?
PSA 30:10 The Lord heard and compassionated me: the Lord became my helper.
PSA 30:11 Thou didst turn my mourning into joy; thou didst rend in pieces my sackcloth and gird me with gladness,
PSA 30:12 that my glory might sound thy praise; and that I might not be absorpt in grief. Lord, my God, to thee I will give thanks for evermore.
PSA 31:1 For the conclusion. A Psalm by David, on a surprise. In thee, Lord, I have trusted. Let me never be put to shame. In thy saving mercy rescue me and deliver me;
PSA 31:2 Incline thine ear to me! haste to deliver me. Be thou to me a protecting God; a house of refuge to save me.
PSA 31:3 Because thou art my strength and my refuge; thou therefore, for thy name's sake, wilt guide and nourish me:
PSA 31:4 thou wilt extricate me from this snare; which they have privily laid for me. Because thou, Lord, art my protector;
PSA 31:5 into thy hands I will commit my spirit. Thou, Lord the God of truth hast redeemed me.
PSA 31:6 Thou hatedst them who fruitlessly regard vanities; but I have trusted in the Lord.
PSA 31:7 I will exult with joy and rejoice in thy mercy: because thou hast looked on my humiliation; hast delivered my soul from these distresses;
PSA 31:8 hast not shut me up into an enemy's hand; hast set my feet in a roomy place.
PSA 31:9 Pity me, Lord, for I am afflicted: with indignation mine eye was troubled; my soul and all within me.
PSA 31:10 Because my life was spent with grief, and my years with sighing; with affliction my strength was exhausted and my bones were troubled;
PSA 31:11 among all mine enemies I became a reproach; and to my neighbours especially, and to my acquaintance, a terror. They who saw me abroad fled from me;
PSA 31:12 like a dead man out of mind I was quite forgotten: I became like a broken vessel.
PSA 31:13 Because I heard the whispers of many who dwell around me; when they assembled together against me they consulted how to take my life;
PSA 31:14 but as for me, I put my trust in thee O Lord; I said, Thou art my God;
PSA 31:15 in thy hands are my lots; deliver me from the hand of mine enemies, and from them who are persecuting me.
PSA 31:16 Let thy face shine upon thy servant: save me for thy mercy's sake.
PSA 31:17 Lord, let me not be shamed, because I have invoked thee. Let the wicked be shamed and driven down to the mansion of the dead.
PSA 31:18 Let those deceitful lips become speechless, which speak injustice against the righteous with pride and contempt.
PSA 31:19 How great, Lord, is the abundance of thy kindness, which thou hast laid up in store for them who fear thee; hast provided for them who trust in thee before the sons of men.
PSA 31:20 In the secret of thy presence thou wilt hide them from the trouble of men; thou wilt shelter them in a pavilion from the strife of tongues.
PSA 31:21 Blessed be the Lord, because he hath marvellously displayed his mercy in a city besieged.
PSA 31:22 As for me, on my surprisal I said, I am cast far from thy presence; therefore thou, Lord, didst hear the voice of my supplication when I cried to thee.
PSA 31:23 Love the Lord, all ye his saints, for the Lord searcheth out truth, and retributeth largely to the insolent.
PSA 31:24 Take courage and let your hearts be strong, all ye whose trust is in the Lord.
PSA 32:1 On understanding. By David. Happy they whose iniquities are forgiven, and whose sins are covered.
PSA 32:2 Happy the man, to whose account the Lord will not charge sin, and in whose mouth there is no guile.
PSA 32:3 Because I kept silence, my bones were consumed; by reason of my crying all the live long day.
PSA 32:4 Because day and night thy hand was heavy on me, I was reduced to misery by a piercing thorn.
PSA 32:5 I acknowledged my sin and did not conceal mine iniquity. I said, Against myself I will confess mine iniquity to the Lord, thereupon thou didst forgive the wickedness of my heart.
PSA 32:6 For this every pious man should pray to thee in due time. Moreover in a flood of many waters, are they not to draw near to him?
PSA 32:7 Thou art my refuge from affliction, which surroundeth me; my jubilee to redeem me from them who encompass me.
PSA 32:8 Let me instruct thee and teach thee the way thou shouldst go. I will fix steadily mine eyes upon thee.
PSA 32:9 Be not like a horse or a mule, which have no understanding, the mouths of which, when they come not to thee, thou must strain with a bridle or a cavesson.
PSA 32:10 Many are the chastisements of the sinner; but mercy will encompass him who trusteth in the Lord.
PSA 32:11 Rejoice in the Lord and exult ye righteous, and shout for joy all ye who are upright in heart.
PSA 33:1 By David. Rejoice ye righteous in the Lord: praise becometh the upright.
PSA 33:2 Praise the Lord with the kithara; with the ten stringed psaltery sing praises to him.
PSA 33:3 Sing to him a new song; sing in harmonious and triumphant strains.
PSA 33:4 For the word of the Lord is right, and all his works are true.
PSA 33:5 He loveth mercy and judgment; the earth is full of the mercy of the Lord.
PSA 33:6 By the word of the Lord the heavens were established, and all their host by the breath of his mouth.
PSA 33:7 He gathered as in a vessel the waters of the sea; he laid up the deeps in store houses.
PSA 33:8 Let all the earth fear the Lord; and all the inhabitants of the World stand in awe of him;
PSA 33:9 for he spake and they were brought into being: he commanded and they were created.
PSA 33:10 The Lord dissipateth the counsels of nations, and disannulleth the devices of peoples. He disannulleth also the counsels of chiefs.
PSA 33:11 But the counsel of the Lord shall endure forever, the thoughts of his heart from generations to generations.
PSA 33:12 Happy is the nation, whose God is the Lord; the people, whom he hath chosen for his heritage.
PSA 33:13 Out of heaven the Lord looked down; he took a view of all the children of men.
PSA 33:14 He looked down from his fixed habitation on all the inhabitants of the earth.
PSA 33:15 It is he alone who formed their hearts: he knoweth completely all their works.
PSA 33:16 A king is not saved because of a numerous army: nor can a giant be saved by his abundant strength.
PSA 33:17 A horse is a false thing for safety; nor can he with all his power save himself.
PSA 33:18 Behold the eyes of the Lord are on them who fear him; on them who confide in his mercy;
PSA 33:19 to deliver their souls from death; and to nourish them in a famine.
PSA 33:20 Let our soul wait for the Lord; because he is our helper and our protector.
PSA 33:21 Because by him our heart can be made glad, therefore in his holy name we have trusted.
PSA 33:22 Let thy mercy, Lord, be upon us as we have put our trust in thee.

PSA 35:1 By David. Judge them, Lord, who do me wrong. Fight against them who are at war with me.
PSA 35:2 Take hold of the shield and buckler; and stand up in my defence.
PSA 35:3 Unsheath the sword and stop my pursuers: say to my soul, I am thy safety.
PSA 35:4 Let them who seek my life be shamed and confounded: let them be turned back and put to shame;
PSA 35:5 who are devising evils against me. Let them be like dust before the wind, when the angel of the Lord is afflicting them.
PSA 35:6 Let their way be dark and slippery, when the angel of the Lord is pursuing them.
PSA 35:7 Seeing they have without cause, hid for me their destructive snare; have, without reason, reproached my soul;
PSA 35:8 let a snare, which they know not, come upon them, and the gin catch them, which they have hidden; and by that very snare let them fall.
PSA 35:9 But let my soul rejoice in the Lord, and be delighted with his salvation.
PSA 35:10 Let all my bones say, Lord, who is like thee, who deliverest the afflicted from the hand of them who are stronger than he; the afflicted and needy from them who spoil him?
PSA 35:11 False witnesses having risen up against me, laid to my charge things which I knew not;
PSA 35:12 they returned me evil for good, even bereavement to my soul.
PSA 35:13 As for me, while they were raising troubles against me I cloathed myself with sackcloth, and humbled my soul with fasting. Though my prayer is to return into mine own bosom,
PSA 35:14 as I would a friend, as I would an own brother, so did I endeavour to conciliate. I humbled myself as one in mourning and deep sorrow.
PSA 35:15 But against me they rejoiced and gathered together; for me, scourges were collected and I did not know: they were split; and they had no compunction.
PSA 35:16 They tortured me; with scoffs they derided me; they gnashed their teeth at me.
PSA 35:17 Lord, when wilt thou look down; rescue my soul from their malice. This only begotten of mine, from lions.
PSA 35:18 I will render thee thanks in a great congregation; among a mighty people I will praise thee.
PSA 35:19 Over me, let not these, my bitter enemies, vainly rejoice; who hate me without cause, and give assent with their eyes.
PSA 35:20 For to me indeed they spoke words of peace, while with wrath they were contriving plots.
PSA 35:21 Then they opened their month wide against me; they said, Aha! aha! our eyes have seen.
PSA 35:22 Thou, Lord, hast seen; keep silence no longer. Lord, stand not at a distance from me.
PSA 35:23 Arise, Lord, and attend to my trial, my God and my Lord, for my justification.
PSA 35:24 Judge me, Lord, according to thy righteousness, Lord my God! and let them not rejoice over me.
PSA 35:25 Let them not say in their hearts, "Aha! aha! it is to our mind;" nor let them say, "We have swallowed him up."
PSA 35:26 Let them who rejoice at my calamities be shamed, and confounded together; let them be cloathed with shame and confusion, who magnify themselves against me.
PSA 35:27 Let them who desire my justification, exult with joy and be gladdened. Let them who wish the peace of thy servant, say continually, The Lord be magnified.
PSA 35:28 So shall my tongue speak of thy righteousness; of thy praise all the day long.
PSA 36:1 For the conclusion. By David the servant of the Lord. The transgressor, in order that he may sin, saith within himself, "He hath, before his eyes, no fear of God's finding out and hating his iniquity:"
PSA 36:2 because, before him, he hath acted with deceit.
PSA 36:3 The words of his mouth are iniquity and deceit. He would not be wise to do good.
PSA 36:4 He contrived mischief on his bed; he persisted in every course which was not good, and did not abhor wickedness.
PSA 36:5 Lord, thy mercy is in the heavens, and thy truth reacheth to the clouds.
PSA 36:6 Thy saving goodness is like the mountains of God, and thy judgments like the vasty deep. Thou, O Lord, preservest men and beasts.
PSA 36:7 As thou, Lord, hast multiplied thy mercy: let the sons of men therefore trust in the shelter of thy wings.
PSA 36:8 With the fatness of thy house they shall be plentifully fed; and thou wilt give them for drink, the full flowing stream of thy pleasures:
PSA 36:9 for with thee there is a fountain of life, and by thy light we shall see light.
PSA 36:10 Extend thy mercy to them that know thee, and thy goodness to them who are upright in heart.
PSA 36:11 Let not the foot of pride come against me, nor the hand of sinners shake me.
PSA 36:12 There all the workers of iniquity are fallen! they were thrust out and could not stand.
PSA 37:1 By David. Fret not because of evil doers: nor envy them who commit iniquity.
PSA 37:2 For like grass, they shall quickly wither: and like the tender herb, they shall quickly fall.
PSA 37:3 Trust in the Lord and exercise kindness; dwell in the land and thou shalt be fed with the riches thereof.
PSA 37:4 Indulge thyself with delight in the Lord, and he will give thee the desires of thy heart.
PSA 37:5 Lay open thy way before the Lord, and trust in him; and he will accomplish;
PSA 37:6 he will indeed bring forth thy righteousness like light, and thy judgment, as the noon day.
PSA 37:7 Submit thyself to the Lord, and supplicate him; fret not at the man who prospereth in his way; at the man who committeth iniquity.
PSA 37:8 Cease from anger and forsake wrath; be not fretted so as to do evil;
PSA 37:9 for they who do evil shall be cut off: but they who wait for the Lord shall inherit the land.
PSA 37:10 Yet a little while, and the sinner shall be no more; though thou mayst seek his place, thou shalt not find it.
PSA 37:11 But the meek shall inherit the land, and delight themselves in the abundance of peace.
PSA 37:12 The sinner may watch the righteous, and gnash his teeth at him;
PSA 37:13 but the Lord will laugh him to scorn, for he foreseeth that his day will come.
PSA 37:14 The sinners drew the sword; they bent their bow, to overthrow the afflicted and needy; to slay the upright in heart.
PSA 37:15 Let their sword pierce their own heart; and their bows be broken to shivers.
PSA 37:16 Better is the little which a righteous man hath, than the abundant wealth of sinners.
PSA 37:17 For the arms of sinners shall be broken; but the Lord supporteth the righteous.
PSA 37:18 The Lord knoweth the ways of the spotless; and their inheritance shall last forever.
PSA 37:19 In time of troubles they shall not be shamed, and in days of famine they shall be plentifully fed.
PSA 37:20 Because the sinners shall perish. Therefore when the enemies of the Lord were exalted and glorified; they were flitting away like smoke, and vanishing.
PSA 37:21 The sinner borroweth and will not repay; but the righteous sheweth mercy and giveth.
PSA 37:22 Hence they who bless him shall inherit the land; but they who curse him shall be rooted out.
PSA 37:23 The steps of a man will be directed by the Lord, when he taketh delight in his way.
PSA 37:24 When he happeneth to fall, he shall not fall with violence; for the Lord is a stay to his hand.
PSA 37:25 I have been young and am now old, yet I have never seen the righteous utterly forsaken, nor his seed begging bread.
PSA 37:26 All the day long he is merciful and lendeth, and his seed shall be entitled to a blessing.
PSA 37:27 Depart from evil and do good and dwell for evermore.
PSA 37:28 Because the Lord loveth judgment and will not forsake his saints; they shall be preserved forever. The spotless shall be avenged, when the seed of the wicked shall be utterly cut off;
PSA 37:29 the righteous shall inherit the land, and dwell therein forever.
PSA 37:30 The mouth of the righteous will speak wisdom, and his tongue will talk of justice.
PSA 37:31 The law of his God is in his heart, and his footsteps shall not slide.
PSA 37:32 The sinner watcheth the righteous, and seeketh to kill him;
PSA 37:33 but the Lord will not leave him in his hand, nor suffer him to condemn him when he is judged.
PSA 37:34 Wait on the Lord and keep his way: and he will exalt thee to inherit the land. When sinners are cut off, thou shalt see it.
PSA 37:35 I have seen the wicked highly exalted, towering aloft like the cedars of Lebanon.
PSA 37:36 Again I passed by, and lo! he was gone. Though I sought him, his place could not be found.
PSA 37:37 Preserve innocence and eye rectitude; for there is a remnant for the man of peace.
PSA 37:38 But transgressors shall be cut off together; the remnants of the wicked shall be rooted out.
PSA 37:39 The safety of the righteous is from the Lord; and he is their protector in time of trouble.
PSA 37:40 The Lord will help them and deliver them; he will rescue them from sinners, and save them: because in him they have put their trust.

PSA 38:2 For in me thy shafts are deeply fixed; and on me thou hast heavily laid thy hand.
PSA 38:3 There is no soundness in my flesh because of thine anger; no rest to my bones, because of my sins.
PSA 38:4 Because mine iniquities mounted above my head; like a heavy burden they were heavy on me.
PSA 38:5 The Wounds, on account of my folly putrefied and became corrupt.
PSA 38:6 I was in misery and wholly bent down: all the longsome day I went mourning.
PSA 38:7 For my soul was filled with illusions; and there was no soundness in my flesh.
PSA 38:8 I was afflicted and exceedingly depressed: I roared because of the groans of my heart.
PSA 38:9 Now all my desire was before thee, and my groans were not hid from thee.
PSA 38:10 My heart panted, my strength failed me: and the light of mine eyes is no more with me.
PSA 38:11 My friends and my neighbours stood over against me: they drew near and stopt; even my near relations stood aloof.
PSA 38:12 But they who seek my life pressed forward: and they who seek my ruin spake vanities. All the day long they studied deceits.
PSA 38:13 As for me, I, as if deaf, did not hear: and like one dumb I opened not my mouth.
PSA 38:14 I became indeed like a man who heareth not; and in whose mouth there are no reproofs;
PSA 38:15 for in thee, Lord, I put my trust. [Thou Lord my God wilt hearken;]
PSA 38:16 for I said, Perhaps mine enemies may rejoice over me: [Indeed when my feet slipped, they used swelling words against me]
PSA 38:17 for I was prepared for stripes, and my sorrowful situation was continually before me;
PSA 38:18 that I might declare mine iniquity, and express my sorrow for my sin.
PSA 38:19 But as for mine enemies they live and are stronger than I: and they who hate me wrongfully are multiplied.
PSA 38:20 They who reward me evil for good, traduced me: because I followed righteousness.
PSA 38:21 Forsake me not utterly, Lord, my God: stand not at a distance from me.
PSA 38:22 Draw near to my assistance, Lord of my salvation.
PSA 39:1 For the conclusion. For Idithun. An Ode by David. I Said, Let me watch my ways; that I may not sin with my tongue. I set a guard on my mouth; when the sinner stood before me.
PSA 39:2 I was dumb and humbled and silent from good things; and my grief was renewed.
PSA 39:3 My heart was warmed within me. That by my meditation a fire might be kindled; I spake with my tongue;
PSA 39:4 Make known to me, Lord mine end; and the number of my days, what it is. That I may know what I lack of it.
PSA 39:5 Behold thou hast made my days old; and mine existence is as nothing before thee. The universe; every man living is vanity.
PSA 39:6 Man indeed walketh about as an image; still he troubleth himself in vain. He heapeth up treasures and knoweth not for whom he is to gather them.
PSA 39:7 Now then what is my expectation? Is it not the Lord? In thee is my hope.
PSA 39:8 Deliver me from all my transgressions. Thou hast made me the reproach of a fool:
PSA 39:9 I was dumb and opened not my mouth: because thou art he who didst make me.
PSA 39:10 Remove thy scourges from me: by the blow of thy hand I fainted.
PSA 39:11 With rebukes thou hast corrected man for iniquity; and caused his life to waste like a spider. Still every man troubleth himself in vain.
PSA 39:12 Hearken, Lord, to my prayer: give ear to my supplication: hold not thy peace at my tears: since I am a sojourner in the land; and a stranger as all my fathers were;
PSA 39:13 O spare me that I may recover strength; before I go hence and be no more.
PSA 40:1 For the conclusion. A Psalm by David. I Waited patiently for the Lord and he attended to me and heard my prayer:
PSA 40:2 and brought me up from a horrible pit and from miry clay; and set my feet on a rock and directed my steps,
PSA 40:3 and put in my mouth a new song; a hymn to our God. Many will see and be struck with awe, and trust in the Lord.
PSA 40:4 Happy the man, whose hope is the name of the Lord, and who hath not looked to vanities and lying fooleries.
PSA 40:5 Many are thy wonders which thou, Lord my God, hast wrought; and for thy thoughts there is none to be compared to thee. I have declared and spoken. They are multiplied beyond computation.
PSA 40:6 Sacrifice and offerings thou didst not desire, but preparedst for me a body; whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin thou didst not require.
PSA 40:7 Then I said, Behold I come; [in the volume of a book it is written respecting me]
PSA 40:8 to perform, my God, thy will, I was determined, even that law of thine, within my heart.
PSA 40:9 I have published the good news of thy righteousness, in a great congregation. Behold I will not refrain my lips; thou, Lord, knowest my righteousness.
PSA 40:10 I have not hid thy truth in my heart, but have mentioned thy salvation; I have not concealed thy mercy and thy truth from a great congregation.
PSA 40:11 Withhold not thou then, Lord, thy tender mercies from me. Thy mercy and thy truth have continually upheld me.
PSA 40:12 Because evils without number encompassed me; mine iniquities had overtaken me, therefore, I was notable to look up; they were multiplied above the hairs of my head, therefore my heart failed me.
PSA 40:13 Be pleased, Lord, to deliver me. Lord, draw near to my assistance.
PSA 40:14 Let them who seek my life to destroy it, be shamed and confounded together. Let them be turned back and shamed who wish me evil;
PSA 40:15 let those quickly bear their shame who say to me, Ha! ha!
PSA 40:16 Let all who seek thee, Lord, rejoice and be glad for thee; let them who love thy salvation say continually, The Lord be magnified!
PSA 40:17 As for me, I am distressed and needy, the Lord will care for me. Thou art my helper and my protector, my God, make no delay.

PSA 41:2 May the Lord preserve him and keep him alive, and make him happy in the land, and may he never deliver him into the hands of his enemy!
PSA 41:3 May the Lord support him on his bed of languishing! thou hast made all his bed in this sickness of his.
PSA 41:4 I said, "Lord be merciful to me: heal my soul, for I have sinned against thee."
PSA 41:5 Mine enemies said wickedly of me, "When will he die and his name perish?"
PSA 41:6 And if one came to see me, his heart spoke vainly. He collected iniquity for himself; he went abroad and spoke for that purpose.
PSA 41:7 All mine enemies spread whispers against me; against me, they devised things hurtful to me.
PSA 41:8 They came to a wicked determination against me. "Now he is confined to his bed, let him never rise again."
PSA 41:9 Nay, mine own familiar friend, in whom I trusted; who ate of my bread, lifted up his heel against me.
PSA 41:10 But thou, O Lord, have compassion on me, and raise me up, that I may requite them.
PSA 41:11 By this, I know that thou hast delighted in me, because mine enemy hath not triumphed over me.
PSA 41:12 And for mine innocence thou hast upheld me; and established me before thee for ever.
PSA 41:13 Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel, from everlasting to everlasting. Amen. Amen.

PSA 44:1 For the conclusion. For the sons of Kore. A Psalm for Understanding. O God, we have heard with our ears: our fathers have told us the work which thou didst in the days of old.
PSA 44:2 When thy hand had extirpated nations, thou didst plant them: thou didst afflict nations and drive them out.
PSA 44:3 For they took not possession of the land with their own sword: nor was it their own arm that saved them: but thy right hand and thine arm, and the light of thy countenance, because thou tookest pleasure in them.
PSA 44:4 Thou, who didst command the deliverances of Jacob; even thou art my king and my God.
PSA 44:5 By thee we can push down our enemies, and through thy name, scorn them who rise up against us.
PSA 44:6 For in mine own bow I will not put trust, nor is it mine own sword that can save me.
PSA 44:7 For thou hast saved us from our enemies, and hast put to shame them who hated us.
PSA 44:8 In God let us boast, all the day long: and to thy name give thanks forever.
PSA 44:9 And hast thou now cast us off and put us to shame, and wilt not go forth with our armies!
PSA 44:10 Thou hast turned us back before our enemies; and they who hate us have spoiled for themselves.
PSA 44:11 Thou hast delivered us up as sheep, to be devoured, and hast scattered us among the nations.
PSA 44:12 Thou hast sold thy people for nought; the shouts of victory gave no abundance.
PSA 44:13 Thou hast made us a reproach to our neighbours; a scoff and derision to those around us.
PSA 44:14 Thou hast made us a by word among the nations; a shaking of the head among the tribes.
PSA 44:15 All the day long, my confusion is before me, and the shame of my face hath covered me,
PSA 44:16 because of a reproacher's and a defamer's voice; and by reason of an enemy and an avenger.
PSA 44:17 All these things have come upon us, though we have not forgotten thee; nor dealt falsely in thy covenant.
PSA 44:18 Though our heart hath not turned back, yet thou hast turned our steps from thy way.
PSA 44:19 Because thou hast humbled us in the place of affliction, and covered us with the shadow of death;
PSA 44:20 Have we forgotten the name of our God; or have we stretched out our hands to a strange god? Will not God search out these things,
PSA 44:21 for he knoweth the secrets of the heart?
PSA 44:22 Since for thy sake we are killed all the day long, and accounted as sheep for slaughter:
PSA 44:23 awake: why sleepest thou, O Lord? Arise and cast us not off forever.
PSA 44:24 Why turnest thou away thy face forgetting our distress and our affliction?
PSA 44:25 Because our soul is humbled to the dust, and our belly cleaveth to the ground;
PSA 44:26 arise Lord; come to our assistance and deliver us for the sake of thy name.

PSA 63:6 If I recollected thee on my bed: in the morning watches I meditated on thee.
PSA 63:7 Because thou hast been my helper: therefore in the shadow of thy wings I will rejoice.

PSA 63:9 But as for these who sought my life in vain; they shall go to the lowest parts of the earth.
PSA 63:10 They shall be delivered up to the edge of the sword: they shall be portions for jackals.
PSA 63:11 But the joy of the king will be in God. Every one who sweareth by him shall glory; because the mouth of them who speak lies is stopped.

PSA 73:1 A Psalm by Asaph. How good is God to Israel! To such as are upright in heart!
PSA 73:2 But as for me, my feet were almost gone: my steps had well nigh slipped;
PSA 73:3 for I envied the unrighteous; when I saw the prosperity of sinners.
PSA 73:4 For there is no lifting up of eyes in their death: and in their affliction they have support.
PSA 73:5 They are not in trouble like other men; nor with other men to be scourged.
PSA 73:6 Therefore haughtiness hath got a mastery over them; they have clothed themselves with their iniquity and impiety.
PSA 73:7 Their iniquity springeth up as it were out of fatness; they passed on to the purpose of their heart.
PSA 73:8 They thought and spoke wickedly; they spoke injustice with a lofty air.
PSA 73:9 They set their mouth against heaven; and their tongue passed on over the earth.
PSA 73:10 Shall my people therefore turn to this; and will full days be found by them?
PSA 73:11 They indeed said, How doth God know? and, Is there any knowledge in the Most High?
PSA 73:12 Behold these who are sinful men; are always prosperous and have gotten wealth.
PSA 73:13 Nay, I myself said, Have I then in vain kept my heart just; and washed my hands in innocence.
PSA 73:14 All the day long I have been scourged; and the accusation against me is renewed every morning.
PSA 73:15 Had I said, I will make such a declaration openly: I should have been treacherous to the generation of thy children.
PSA 73:16 I therefore supposed, the trouble of knowing this is before me.
PSA 73:17 When I go to the sanctuary of God; I may understand the final issue.
PSA 73:18 It is but for their frauds thou hast dealt thus with them. Thou hast overthrown them by their exaltation.!
PSA 73:19 how they were for destruction! They are gone in a moment! They perished for their iniquity!
PSA 73:20 As a dream of one awaked out of sleep. Thou, Lord, in thy city wilt spurn their ghost;
PSA 73:21 therefore my heart was cheered and my reins were changed.
PSA 73:22 I indeed was despicable for my want of knowledge; I was brutish as a beast before thee.
PSA 73:23 As for me I shall be with thee continually: thou hast held me by my right hand:
PSA 73:24 with thy counsel thou hast guided me, and taken me to thyself with glory.
PSA 73:25 For what is there in heaven for me; or what on earth have I desired, besides thee?
PSA 73:26 Hath my heart and my flesh failed? God is the strength of my heart; God is my portion forever.
PSA 73:27 Seeing they who withdrew themselves from thee, shall perish; thou hast cut off every one who goeth a whoring from thee:
PSA 73:28 It is therefore good for me to cleave to God; to place my hope upon the Lord: that I may publish all thy praises in the gates of the daughter of Sion.

PSA 74:23 Forget not the voice of thy suppliants: let the pride of them, who hate thee, ascend continually before thee.

PSA 77:1 For the conclusion. For Idithun. A Psalm by Asaph. With my voice I cried to the Lord, and my voice was to God, and he hearkened to me.
PSA 77:2 In the day of my affliction I sought God with my hands in the night before him; and I was not disappointed. My soul had refused to be comforted;
PSA 77:3 I remembered God and was made glad; I meditated, though my spirit was in despondency.
PSA 77:4 All mine enemies had previously mounted guard; I was troubled and did not speak.
PSA 77:5 I considered the days of old: I recollected the years of ancient times;
PSA 77:6 I meditated at night; I conversed with my heart; I searched my spirit diligently.
PSA 77:7 Will the Lord cast off forever, and will he no more be favourable?
PSA 77:8 Will he entirely cut off mercy, from generation to generation?
PSA 77:9 Will God forget to be gracious? Will he in his anger restrain his compassion?
PSA 77:10 Then I said, I have now made a beginning; this is the change of the right hand of the Most High.
PSA 77:11 I called to remembrance the works of the Lord. Seeing I can remember thy wonders of old:
PSA 77:12 let me therefore meditate on all thy works, and muse on thine institutions.
PSA 77:13 God, thy way is in that which is holy; what God is great as our God?
PSA 77:14 Thou art the God who worketh miracles: thou hast made thy power known among the tribes.
PSA 77:15 With thine arm thou didst redeem this people of thine; the children of Jacob and Joseph.
PSA 77:16 The waters saw thee, God!; the waters saw thee and were terrified, and the deep gulphs were troubled.
PSA 77:17 Great was the roaring of the waters; the clouds uttered a sound: for thy bolts were passing through them.
PSA 77:18 The sound of thy thunder was in the round expanse: thy lightnings illumed the World; the earth shook and trembled.
PSA 77:19 Thy way was through the sea, and thy paths through many waters; but thy footsteps could not be known.

PSA 78:1 On understanding. By Asaph. Attend, my people, to my law; incline your ears to the words of my mouth.
PSA 78:2 I will open my mouth with parables; I will utter dark sayings of old;
PSA 78:3 such as we have heard and known, which our fathers have related to us.
PSA 78:4 They were not hid from their children: one generation told another the praises of the Lord, his acts of power, and the wonders which he hath done.
PSA 78:5 Thus he raised up a testimony in Jacob, and established a law in Israel, which he commanded our fathers to make known to their children:
PSA 78:6 that the succeeding generation; the children to be born, might know it, and rise and tell the same to their children:
PSA 78:7 that they might put their trust in God, and not forget the works of God, but seek diligently his commandments;
PSA 78:8 that they might not be like their fathers; a perverse and rebellious generation; a generation which set not their hearts aright, and whose spirit was not stedfast with God.
PSA 78:9 The sons of Ephraim, who bend and shoot the bow, were turned back in the day of battle.
PSA 78:10 They did not keep the covenant of God, and would not walk in his law.
PSA 78:11 They indeed forgot his acts of kindness; those wonders of his which he had shewn them;
PSA 78:12 wonders which he did in the sight of their fathers: in the land of Egypt, in the plain of Tanis.
PSA 78:13 He had cleft the sea and led them through it; he had stayed the waters as in a bottle.
PSA 78:14 He had led them with a cloud by day, and all the night long with a light of fire;
PSA 78:15 he had cleft a rock in the wilderness, and given them drink as from a great abyss;
PSA 78:16 he had brought water out of a rock, and caused streams to flow down like rivers:
PSA 78:17 But still they proceeded to sin against him; they provoked the Most High in a desert.
PSA 78:18 Still they made trial of God in their hearts, by asking for meats to their appetites.
PSA 78:19 Nay, they spoke against God and said, "Can God provide a table in a desert?
PSA 78:20 When he smote a rock, waters gushed out, and streams swelled to an overflowing flood. But can He also give bread, or provide a table for his people?"
PSA 78:21 Therefore the Lord heard and was provoked; and a fire was kindled among Jacob; and wrath came up against Israel.
PSA 78:22 Because they believed not in God, nor trusted in his salvation.
PSA 78:23 Though he had commanded the clouds above, and had opened the doors of heaven,
PSA 78:24 and had rained down manna for them to eat, and had given them the bread of heaven,
PSA 78:25 [Man was eating the bread of angels] he sent meat for them to satiety.
PSA 78:26 He removed the south east wind out of heaven, and by his power brought on the south west:
PSA 78:27 and rained upon them flesh, like dust: and feathered fowls as the sand of the sea;
PSA 78:28 they fell in the midst of their encampment, and all around their habitation.
PSA 78:29 Though they ate and were filled abundantly, and he had given them their desire;
PSA 78:30 their longing desire was not stayed; therefore while the meat was still in their mouth,
PSA 78:31 the anger of God came up against them, and slew them amidst their fat viands, and fettered the chosen men of Israel.
PSA 78:32 Notwithstanding all these things they still sinned, and did not believe his wonderous works;
PSA 78:33 therefore their days glided away in vanity, and their years were attended with impatience.
PSA 78:34 When he smote them and they sought him, and returned and inquired early after God,
PSA 78:35 and remembered that God was their helper, and that God the Most High was their redeemer;
PSA 78:36 though they expressed love for him with their mouth, they lied to him with their tongue,
PSA 78:37 and their heart was not right with him, nor were they stedfast in his covenant.
PSA 78:38 But he being merciful forgave their sins, and would not utterly destroy them. Yea, many a time did he turn away his wrath, and would not suffer all his wrath to blaze forth;
PSA 78:39 for he remembered that they were flesh; a breath going out and not again returning.
PSA 78:40 How often did they provoke him in the wilderness, and excite him to anger in the desert?
PSA 78:41 They actually turned back and tempted God, and provoked to wrath the holy One of Israel.
PSA 78:42 They remembered not his hand, on the day when he rescued them out of the hand of an oppressor;
PSA 78:43 how he had displayed his signs in Egypt, and his wonders in the plain of Tanis;
PSA 78:44 and had turned their rivers into blood, and their cisterns so that they could not drink;
PSA 78:45 had sent against them the dog fly which devoured them, and swarms of frogs which destroyed them;
PSA 78:46 and had given their crops to the canker Worm, and their labours to the locust;
PSA 78:47 had smitten their vineyards with hail, and their sycamine trees with frost;
PSA 78:48 and delivered up their cattle to hail, and their substance to the fire;
PSA 78:49 having sent out against them his fierce anger, wrath and indignation and affliction; a mission executed by evil angels:
PSA 78:50 he paved a way for his vengeance; he spared not their lives from death: he delivered up their cattle to pestilence,
PSA 78:51 and smote every first born in the land of Egypt; the first fruits of their labours in the tents of Cham;
PSA 78:52 and brought out his people like sheep, and led them like a flock in the desert,
PSA 78:53 and guided them safely, so that they were not afraid, though the sea overwhelmed their enemies;
PSA 78:54 and brought them to the mount of his holiness; to this mountain which his right hand purchased;
PSA 78:55 and drove out nations from before them, and gave them by lot their several portions, and settled in their dwellings the tribes of Israel.
PSA 78:56 Still they tempted and provoked God the Most High, and did not keep his testimonies;
PSA 78:57 but turned back and broke covenant like their fathers. They turned aside like a deceitful bow.
PSA 78:58 They provoked him with their mounts, and with their graven images moved him to jealousy.
PSA 78:59 God heard and despised them and greatly contemned Israel,
PSA 78:60 and he abandoned the tabernacle of Selom; the tent in which he had dwelt among men;
PSA 78:61 and delivered up their strength to captivity, and their glory into an enemy's hand;
PSA 78:62 and gave up his people to the sword, and slighted his inheritance.
PSA 78:63 A fire consumed their young men, and their virgins made no lamentation.
PSA 78:64 Their priests fell by the sword and their widows are not to bewail them.
PSA 78:65 At length the Lord awaked as one out of sleep, as a mighty man recovered from wine;
PSA 78:66 and he smote his enemies in the hinder parts, and cast an everlasting reproach on them.
PSA 78:67 But he rejected the habitation of Joseph, and did not chuse the tribe of Ephraim;
PSA 78:68 but made choice of the tribe of Juda; of this mount Sion which he loved,
PSA 78:69 and built his sanctuary like that of unicorns; in this land he founded it for this age,
PSA 78:70 and he chose David his servant and took him from the flocks of sheep;
PSA 78:71 he took them from tending the ewes with young to feed his servant Jacob and Israel his inheritance.
PSA 78:72 And he fed them in the integrity of his heart, and guided them by the skill of his hands.

PSA 88:17 they have encompassed me like water: all the day long they begirt me at once.

PSA 90:1 A prayer of Moses the man of God. LORD, thou hast been a refuge for us, from one generation to another.
PSA 90:2 Before the mountains were brought forth; or the earth or the world was formed: even from everlasting to everlasting thou existest.
PSA 90:3 Wilt thou turn man away to despondency; when thou hast said, Return ye sons of men?
PSA 90:4 Since in thy sight a thousand years are but as yesterday which is past; or as a watch in the night:
PSA 90:5 shall these trifling years of theirs be as if in the morning, a green herb passed away?
PSA 90:6 Should it in the morning bloom and pass away? In the evening it would have fallen, withered and become dry.
PSA 90:7 Because we have fallen short by thine anger, and by thine indignation have been troubled;
PSA 90:8 thou hast placed our iniquities before thee: let this age of ours be for the light of thy countenance.
PSA 90:9 Because all our days have fallen short; and we have failed by thine indignation; our years have exercised themselves like a spider.
PSA 90:10 The days of these years of ours are seventy years: and if by reason of strength they be eighty years; still the surplus of them is labour and sorrow. Because gentleness hath come upon us: let us, therefore,
PSA 90:11 whoever knoweth the power of thine anger, be taught, on the account of the terror of thy wrath,
PSA 90:12 so to number them. Thus make known thy right hand; and them whose hearts are instructed in wisdom.
PSA 90:13 Return, Lord. How long shall it first be? And be pacified with thy servants.
PSA 90:14 In the morning we were filled with thy mercy. We indeed rejoiced and were made glad.
PSA 90:15 During all these days of ours may we be gladdened; in lieu of the days wherein thou hast humbled us; and of the years in which we have seen evils.
PSA 90:16 And look upon these thy servants and on thy works: and be thou the guide of their children.
PSA 90:17 And let the splendor of the Lord our God be over us: and do thou direct for us the works of our hands.

PSA 91:11 For he will give his angels a charge concerning thee; to keep thee in all thy ways;
PSA 91:12 with their hands they shall bear thee up; shouldst thou chance to strike thy foot against a stone.

PSA 91:15 He will call on me, and I will answer him: I am with him in affliction: I will deliver him and honour him.

PSA 103:10 He hath not dealt with us according to our sins; nor retributed to us according to our iniquities.
PSA 103:11 For high as the heaven is from the earth; the Lord hath enlarged his mercy for them who fear him.
PSA 103:12 Far as the east is distant from the west, he hath removed from us our transgressions.
PSA 103:13 As a father pitieth his children; the Lord hath pitied them who fear him,
PSA 103:14 because he knew our formation. O remember that we are dust.
PSA 103:15 As for man, his days are like grass; like a flower of the field, so he may bloom.
PSA 103:16 Because a blast of wind passed over it, it is gone. It shall no more know its place.
PSA 103:17 But the mercy of the Lord is from age to age over them who fear him: and his saving goodness over children's children,
PSA 103:18 for them who keep his covenant, and remember his commands to do them.
PSA 103:19 The Lord hath established his throne in heaven, and his dominion is exercised over all.
PSA 103:20 Bless the Lord, all ye his angels; ye mighty powers, who execute his word, on hearing the voice of his commands.
PSA 103:21 Bless the Lord, all ye his armies: ye ministers of his, who perform his will.
PSA 103:22 Bless the Lord all ye his works, in every place of his dominion. O my soul, bless thou the Lord.
PSA 104:1 By David. Bless the Lord O my soul. O Lord my God, thou art very great. Thou hast robed thyself with honour and majesty;
PSA 104:2 clothing thyself with light as with a mantle; stretching out the heaven as a tent.
PSA 104:3 Thou art he who covereth his chambers with waters who maketh clouds his chariot; who walketh on the wings of winds;
PSA 104:4 Who maketh winds his messengers, and flaming fire his ministers;
PSA 104:5 Who founded the earth on its firm basis, that it may not be moved forever.
PSA 104:6 Is the abyss like a garment to be its covering; are waters to stand above the mountains?
PSA 104:7 At thy rebuke they shall flee; at the peal of thy thunder they will tremble.
PSA 104:8 They ascend mountains, they go down vallies; to the place which thou hast founded for them.
PSA 104:9 Thou has set a bound which they shall not pass; nor shall they return to cover the earth.
PSA 104:10 Thou art he who sendeth forth springs in vallies. Waters shall flow down between the mountains;
PSA 104:11 and give drink to all the beasts of the field. Wild asses will expect them to quench their thirst.
PSA 104:12 By them the birds of the air will abide: from among the rocks they will utter a sound.
PSA 104:13 Thou art he who watereth mountains from his chambers. With the fruit of thy works the earth will be satisfied.
PSA 104:14 Thou art he who causeth grass to grow for cattle; even verdant grass for the service of man. That he may bring food out of the earth:
PSA 104:15 wine cheereth the heart of man: that he might exhilarate his countenance with oil; the heart of man is strengthened with bread.
PSA 104:16 The trees of the plain shall be fully satisfied; the cedars of Lebanon, which he hath planted.
PSA 104:17 There the birds will build their nests. The family of the stork account them their own.
PSA 104:18 The lofty mountains are for the hinds; a rock is the refuge of the choirogryllus.
PSA 104:19 He hath appointed the moon for seasons: the sun knoweth his time for going down.
PSA 104:20 Thou hast stationed darkness and there was night: in it all the beasts of the forest will come forth;
PSA 104:21 Lions roaring for prey, seeking their food from God.
PSA 104:22 When the sun is risen, they will assemble and lay themselves down in their dens;
PSA 104:23 Man will go forth to his labour and continue at it till evening.
PSA 104:24 How manifold are thy works, Lord, with wisdom thou hast done them all. The earth is filled with thy creatures;
PSA 104:25 So is the great and spacious sea: in this are moving things innumerable; living creatures small and great.
PSA 104:26 There ships sail: there is that dragon, which thou hast formed to sport therein.
PSA 104:27 All wait on thee to give them food in due season.
PSA 104:28 When thou givest them, they gather; by opening thy hand all are bountifully supplied.
PSA 104:29 But when thou deniest, they are troubled. Withdraw their breath, they die and return to their dust:
PSA 104:30 send forth thy breath and they are created: thou indeed canst renew the face of the earth.
PSA 104:31 Let the glory of the Lord endure forever; let the Lord rejoice over his works.
PSA 104:32 When he looketh at the earth, he causeth it to tremble; when he toucheth the mountains, they smoke.
PSA 104:33 I will sing to the Lord as long as I live, I will praise my God while I have a being.
PSA 104:34 Let my meditation be acceptable to him, and I will rejoice in the Lord.
PSA 104:35 Let sinners be consumed from the earth, and the wicked so as to be no more; my soul, bless thou the Lord.
PSA 105:1 An Alleluia, or alternate Song of Precise to the Lord. Give thanks to the Lord and invoke his name: proclaim his works among the nations.
PSA 105:2 Sing to him and sing with instrumental musick; relate all his wonderous works.
PSA 105:3 Sing praises to his holy name. Let the heart of them, who seek the Lord, be glad.
PSA 105:4 Seek the Lord and be confirmed in strength; seek his face continually.
PSA 105:5 Remember his wonders which he hath done; his miracles and the judgments of his mouth.
PSA 105:6 ye seed of Abraham, his servants; ye children of Jacob, his chosen ones;
PSA 105:7 he is the Lord, our God, in all this land are his judgments.
PSA 105:8 He remembered forever his covenant; a word which he gave in charge for a thousand generations:
PSA 105:9 the covenant which he made with Abraham, and that oath of his to Isaak,
PSA 105:10 which he confirmed to Jacob for a law, and to Israel for an everlasting covenant;
PSA 105:11 saying, To thee I will give the land of Chanaan to be the lot of your inheritance.
PSA 105:12 When they were few in number; of little account and sojourners therein;
PSA 105:13 when they passed through from nation to nation; from one kingdom to another people;
PSA 105:14 he suffered no man to injure them; he reproved kings for their sake,
PSA 105:15 "touch not mine anointed ones, and to my prophets do no harm."
PSA 105:16 When he called for a famine on the land; broke all the stay of bread,
PSA 105:17 he had sent before them a man, Joseph was sold for a servant.
PSA 105:18 They had humbled his feet with fetters, his life was spent in irons;
PSA 105:19 until his word came to pass; till the oracle of the Lord tried him.
PSA 105:20 The king had sent and loosed him; the chief of peoples had set him at liberty;
PSA 105:21 had appointed him lord of his house, and ruler of all his possessions;
PSA 105:22 that he like himself might instruct princes, and teach his senators wisdom:
PSA 105:23 then Israel went down to Egypt, and Jacob sojourned in the land of Cham.
PSA 105:24 When he had encreased his people to a great degree, and made them stronger than their enemies;
PSA 105:25 and had turned their hearts to hate his people, to deal deceitfully with his servants;
PSA 105:26 he sent forth Moses his servant; Aaron whom he had chosen:
PSA 105:27 to them he committed the words of his signs; of his wonders in the land of Cham.
PSA 105:28 He sent forth darkness and it was dark. When they made his words bitter,
PSA 105:29 he turned their waters into blood, and made a slaughter of their fishes;
PSA 105:30 their land swarmed with frogs, in the inmost chambers of their kings.
PSA 105:31 He spake and the dog fly came, and stinging gnats in all their borders;
PSA 105:32 he made his showers, hail, flaming fire in all their land;
PSA 105:33 he smote their vines and their fig trees, and broke every tree of their border.
PSA 105:34 He spake, and the grasshopper came, and the brouchus locust in swarms innumerable,
PSA 105:35 and devoured every herb in their country, and ate up the fruit of their land.
PSA 105:36 Then he smote every first born of their land; the first fruits of all their labour;
PSA 105:37 and brought out his people with silver and gold, and there was not a feeble person among their tribes.
PSA 105:38 Egypt rejoiced at their going out, for the dread of these had fallen on them.
PSA 105:39 He spread out a cloud to shelter them, and a fire to illuminate the night for them.
PSA 105:40 They asked, and flocks of quails came; and he satisfied them with the bread of heaven.
PSA 105:41 He split a rock and waters gushed out, and rivers ran in dry places.
PSA 105:42 Because he remembered his holy promise; that which he made to Abraham his servant;
PSA 105:43 therefore he brought out his people with joy; even his chosen ones with gladness;
PSA 105:44 and gave them the countries of nations, and they inherited the labours of peoples;
PSA 105:45 that they might keep his rules of rectitude, and that they might diligently seek his law.
PSA 106:1 An Alleluia. Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good; for to everlasting his mercy endureth.
PSA 106:2 Who can express the mighty acts of the Lord? Who can publish all his praises?
PSA 106:3 Happy they, who keep judgment, and who do justice at all times.
PSA 106:4 Remember us, Lord, affectionately as thy people, visit us with thy salvation;
PSA 106:5 that we may see it in the felicity of thy chosen; that we may be gladdened with the joy of thy nation; that we may sing praises with thy heritage.
PSA 106:6 We with our fathers have sinned; we have committed iniquity; we have done wickedly.
PSA 106:7 Our fathers minded not thy wonders in Egypt, they did not remember the multitude of thy mercies. Though in coming up they were refractory at the Red sea,
PSA 106:8 yet he saved them for his name's sake, that he might make known his mighty power.
PSA 106:9 He rebuked the Red sea and it was dried up; and he led them through the deep as through a wilderness;
PSA 106:10 and saved them from the hand of those who hated them, and delivered them out of an enemy's hand.
PSA 106:11 The water covered those who afflicted them, not an individual of them was left.
PSA 106:12 Though they believed his words, though they sang his praise;
PSA 106:13 they soon forgot his works, they waited not for his counsel.
PSA 106:14 They indulged a longing desire in the desert, and tried God in a place without water.
PSA 106:15 Though he granted them their request, and sent satiety to their soul;
PSA 106:16 yet they provoked Moses in the camp and Aaron the consecrated of the Lord.
PSA 106:17 The earth opened and swallowed up Dathan, and covered the company of Abeiron;
PSA 106:18 and a fire was kindled in their assembly, and a flame burned up the wicked.
PSA 106:19 Even at Choreb they made a calf, and worshipped the graven image;
PSA 106:20 and exchanged their glory for the image of an ox which eateth grass.
PSA 106:21 They forgot God their saviour, who had done great things in Egypt;
PSA 106:22 wonderful things in the land of Cham, and terrible things at the Red sea:
PSA 106:23 whereupon he spake of destroying them, had not his chosen Moses stood before him in the breach, to turn him from his fierce indignation, that he might not utterly destroy.
PSA 106:24 When they despised the pleasant land and did not confide in his word:
PSA 106:25 but murmured in their tents; and hearkened not to the voice of the Lord:
PSA 106:26 he lifted up his hand against them; to overthrow them in the desert;
PSA 106:27 and cast back their seed among the nations; and disperse them in the countries.
PSA 106:28 When they consecrated themselves to Belphegor; and ate the sacrifices offered to dead men;
PSA 106:29 and provoked him with their devices; and the plague was raging among them:
PSA 106:30 Phineas stood up and made atonement; and the plague was stayed:
PSA 106:31 and it was counted to him for righteousness to all generations forever.
PSA 106:32 When they provoked him at the water of strife it went ill with Moses on their account.
PSA 106:33 For they provoked his spirit and he spake unadvisedly with his lips.
PSA 106:34 They did not root out the nations which the Lord had mentioned to him:
PSA 106:35 but mingled with those nations; and learned their works.
PSA 106:36 And served their graven images which became to them a stumbling block.
PSA 106:37 They actually sacrificed their sons and their daughters to demons:
PSA 106:38 and shed innocent blood; the blood of their sons and daughters, whom they sacrificed to the graven idols of Chanaan. And the land was polluted with blood and
PSA 106:39 defiled by their works: and they went a whoring with their devices.
PSA 106:40 Therefore the Lord was incensed against his people, and abhorred his inheritance.
PSA 106:41 And he delivered them into the hands of enemies; and they who hated them ruled over them.
PSA 106:42 When their enemies afflicted them; and they were humbled under their hands:
PSA 106:43 many a time did he deliver them. But they provoked him with their counsel. When they were humbled for their iniquities;
PSA 106:44 the Lord beheld when they were afflicted. When he heard their supplication,
PSA 106:45 he remembered his covenant and according to the multitude of his mercies;
PSA 106:46 he relented and excited compassion for them among all those who had captivated them.
PSA 106:47 Save us, Lord, our God; and gather us from among the nations; that we may give thanks to thy holy name; that we may triumph in thy praise.
PSA 106:48 Blessed be the Lord the God of Israel from everlasting to everlasting: and let all the people say, Amen, Amen.
PSA 107:1 An Alleluia, Give thanks to the Lord, for he is good: for to everlasting his mercy endureth.
PSA 107:2 Let this be said by them whom the Lord hath redeemed; whom he hath redeemed from an enemy's hand;
PSA 107:3 whom he hath gathered out of the countries; from the east and west and north and sea.
PSA 107:4 They had wandered in the desert in a land without water; they found no way to a city of habitation.
PSA 107:5 They were hungry and thirsty. Their soul within them fainted:
PSA 107:6 then they cried to the Lord in their affliction; and he delivered them from their distresses:
PSA 107:7 and conducted them to a straight road; that they might go to a city of habitation.
PSA 107:8 O let them praise the Lord for his mercies; and for his wonderful dealings with the sons of men:
PSA 107:9 because he hath satisfied the longing soul; and filled the hungry with good things.
PSA 107:10 As for them who sat in darkness and the shadow of death; bound with affliction and irons;
PSA 107:11 because they rebelled against the oracles of God; and contemned the counsel of the Most High:
PSA 107:12 when their heart was brought low by troubles; when they were weak and there was no helper:
PSA 107:13 then they cried to the Lord in their affliction; and he saved them from their distresses;
PSA 107:14 and brought them out of darkness and the shadow of death; and burst their chains asunder.
PSA 107:15 let them praise the Lord for his mercies, and for his wonderful dealings with the sons of men;
PSA 107:16 for he hath dashed to shivers the gates of brass, and broken asunder the bars of iron.
PSA 107:17 He helped them out of the way of their transgression: for on account of their iniquities they were brought low.
PSA 107:18 Their soul abhorred all manner of food, and they drew near to the gates of death.
PSA 107:19 Then they cried to the Lord in their affliction, and he saved them from their distresses.
PSA 107:20 He sent forth his word and healed them; and delivered them from their destructions.
PSA 107:21 O let them praise the Lord for his mercies, and for his wonderful dealings with the sons of men;
PSA 107:22 and let them offer him a sacrifice of thanksgiving, and publish his works with joy.
PSA 107:23 As for them who go to sea in ships, and traffick on the mighty waters;
PSA 107:24 they see the works of the Lord, and his wonders in the deep.
PSA 107:25 He spake, and up rose a tempestuous wind: and its waves are lifted high;
PSA 107:26 they mount up to the heavens: then down they descend into the depths; with perils, their souls are melted;
PSA 107:27 they reel and stagger like one drunk, and all their skill is swallowed up.
PSA 107:28 Then they cried to the Lord in their affliction, and he brought them out of their distresses.
PSA 107:29 He rebuked the tempest, and it stopt in a still calm; and its waves were lulled to silence.
PSA 107:30 And they were glad, because they were at rest. And he conducted them to their desired port.
PSA 107:31 let them praise the Lord for his mercies, and for his Wonderful dealings with the sons of men.
PSA 107:32 Let them extol him in the congregation of the people: and praise him in the assembly of Elders.
PSA 107:33 He hath turned rivers into a wilderness: and outlets of water into a thirsty land;
PSA 107:34 a fruitful country into barrenness: for the wickedness of them who dwell therein.
PSA 107:35 He hath turned a desert into pools of water, and a thirsty soil into water springs:
PSA 107:36 and caused the hungry to dwell there. And they have erected abiding cities:
PSA 107:37 and have sown fields and planted vineyards, which have yielded them the fruits of increase.
PSA 107:38 And he hath blessed them and they have multiplied greatly, and their cattle have not decreased.
PSA 107:39 Again they have been diminished, and brought low by oppressions, afflictions, and sorrow.
PSA 107:40 Contempt hath been poured on their princes: and he hath caused them to wander in a trackless desert.
PSA 107:41 Then out of affliction he hath helped the needy, and hath made families like a flock.
PSA 107:42 Let the righteous see and rejoice, and let all iniquity stop its mouth.
PSA 107:43 Whosoever is wise and will observe these things, he will understand the mercies of the Lord.
