PSA 133:3 It is like the dew of Hermon, which descendeth on the mountains of Sion; for there the Lord commanded the blessing, Life for evermore.
PSA 134:1 A Song of the steps. Attend! bless the Lord, all ye servants of the Lord, who stand in the house of the Lord; in the courts of the house of our God.
PSA 134:2 At night, lift up your hands to the holies and bless the Lord.
PSA 134:3 May the Lord out of Sion bless thee: he who made the heaven and the earth.
PSA 135:1 An Alleluia. Praise the name of the Lord; praise the Lord, ye his servants,
PSA 135:2 who wait in the house of the Lord; in the courts of the house of our God.
PSA 135:3 Praise the Lord; for the Lord is good; with instruments of musick praise his name; for it is good.
PSA 135:4 For the Lord hath made choice of Jacob for himself; of Israel for his peculiar treasure.
PSA 135:5 For I know that the Lord is great, and that our Lord is above all the Gods.
PSA 135:6 All that the Lord pleased he hath done in heaven and on earth: in the seas and in all the deeps.
PSA 135:7 When he brought clouds from the end of the earth; he made lightnings for the purpose of rain. He it is who bringeth winds out of his treasuries:
PSA 135:8 who smote the first born of Egypt: the first born both of man and beast.
PSA 135:9 Amidst thee, Egypt, he sent his signs and wonders, on Pharao and on all his servants.
PSA 135:10 It was he who smote many nations; and slew kings of mighty power;
PSA 135:11 Seon king of the Amorites, and Og, the king of Basan, and all the kingdoms of Chanaan;
PSA 135:12 and gave their land for an inheritance; for an inheritance for his people Israel.
PSA 135:13 Lord, thy name is forever, and the memorial of thee to all generations;
PSA 135:14 for the Lord will judge his people, and take comfort in his servants.
PSA 135:15 The idols of the nations are gold and silver; the workmanship of men's hands.
PSA 135:16 They have a mouth, but cannot speak: eyes they have, but they cannot see;
PSA 135:17 they have ears, but they cannot hear; nor is there any breath in their mouth.
PSA 135:18 May they who make them be like them; and all they who have trusted in them.
PSA 135:19 O house of Israel, bless ye the Lord: bless the Lord ye of the house of Aaron.
PSA 135:20 O house of Levi, bless ye the Lord; bless him, ye who fear the Lord.
PSA 135:21 Blessed be the Lord in Sion; he who inhabiteth Jerusalem.
PSA 136:1 An Alleluia. Give thanks to the Lord for he is good; for his mercy endureth forever.
PSA 136:2 O give thanks to the God of Gods, for his mercy endureth forever.
PSA 136:3 Give thanks to the Lord of Lords; for his mercy endureth forever.
PSA 136:4 To him who alone hath done great wonders; for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:5 to him who made the heavens with wisdom: for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:6 to him who established the earth on the waters: for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:7 to him who alone made the great lights: for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:8 the sun to rule the day: for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:9 the moon and the stars to rule the night; for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:10 to him who smote Egypt with their first born; for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:11 and brought out Israel from among them; for his mercy endureth forever:
PSA 136:12 with a strong hand and an outstretched arm; for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:13 to him who divided the Red sea into parts; for his mercy endureth forever.
PSA 136:14 And led Israel through the midst thereof: for his mercy endureth forever:
PSA 136:15 but shook off Pharao and his hosts into the Red sea; for his mercy endureth forever:
PSA 136:16 to him, who led his people through the desert; for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:17 to him who smote great kings; for his mercy endureth forever:
PSA 136:18 and slew kings of mighty power: for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:19 Seon king of the Amorites; for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:20 And Og the king of Basan; for his mercy endureth forever:
PSA 136:21 and gave their land for an inheritance; for his mercy endureth forever:
PSA 136:22 an inheritance for Israel his servant; for his mercy endureth forever:
PSA 136:23 because in our affliction the Lord remembered us; for his mercy endureth forever;
PSA 136:24 and redeemed us from our enemies; for his mercy endureth forever.
PSA 136:25 He it is who giveth food to all flesh: for his mercy endureth forever.
PSA 136:26 give thanks to the God of heaven: for to everlasting his mercy endureth.
PSA 137:1 For David, a Psalm of Jeremias. By the rivers of Babylon there we sat down and wept, when we remembered Sion.
PSA 137:2 Upon the willows in the midst of it we hung up our harps;
PSA 137:3 for there they who had captivated us, asked of us the words of a song: and they who had led us away, asked for a hymn, saying, Sing for us some of the odes of Sion.
PSA 137:4 How can we sing the song of the Lord in a strange country?
PSA 137:5 Jerusalem, if I forget thee, let my right hand be forgotten.
PSA 137:6 Let my tongue cleave to the roof of my mouth, if I do not remember thee; if I set not Jerusalem foremost, as the chief object of my joy.
PSA 137:7 Remember, Lord, the children of Edom; who in the day of Jerusalem said, Rase! Rase! down to its foundations!
PSA 137:8 O daughter of Babylon the miserable! Happy he who shall render thee thy recompense; for what thou hast done to us!
PSA 137:9 Happy be who shall seize and dash thy infants against stones!
PSA 138:1 A Psalm by David, used by Aggaius and Zacharias. I Will adore thee, Lord, with my whole heart. And with instrumental musick sing to thee before angels: because thou hast heard all the words of my mouth.
PSA 138:2 I will worship before thy holy temple; and adore thy name for thy mercy and thy truth; because thou hast magnified above all thy holy name.
PSA 138:3 On the day when I invoke thee, answer me speedily: thou canst strengthen me in my soul with thy strength;
PSA 138:4 let all the kings of this land adore thee, Lord, because they have heard all the words of thy mouth.
PSA 138:5 And let them sing in the ways of the Lord: because the glory of the Lord is great.
PSA 138:6 For the Lord is high and looketh down on the things which are low: and from afar he knoweth the things which are high.
PSA 138:7 Though I walk in the midst of trouble, thou canst keep me alive. Against the rage of enemies thou hast stretched forth thy hand: and thy right hand hath saved me.
PSA 138:8 Thou, Lord wilt retribute for me. Lord, thy mercy endureth forever; overlook not the works of thy hands.
PSA 139:1 For the conclusion. A Psalm by David. LORD, thou hast proved me and known me.
PSA 139:2 Thou knowest my sitting down and my rising up. Thou from afar understandest my thoughts.
PSA 139:3 Thou has tracked my path and my line: and hast seen distinctly all my ways;
PSA 139:4 that there is not an evil word on my tongue. Behold thou, Lord, knowest all things;
PSA 139:5 the last and the things of earliest date. Thou hast formed me and laid thy hand on me.
PSA 139:6 This knowledge of thine is too wonderful for me. It is great beyond my comprehension.
PSA 139:7 Whither can I go from thy spirit? And from thy presence whither can I flee?
PSA 139:8 If I ascend up to heaven, thou art there. If I go down to the mansion of the dead, there thou art.
PSA 139:9 If I wing my flight towards the morning; or dwell at the extremes of this sea;
PSA 139:10 even there thy hand will guide me; and thy right hand will restrain me.
PSA 139:11 When I said, Darkness will surely trample me down: then to my great joy, night was luminous.
PSA 139:12 For darkness cannot darken from thee; even night can be made light as day: the darkness of that, as the light of this.
PSA 139:13 Because thou, Lord, hast possessed my reins; hast supported me from my mother's womb;
PSA 139:14 I will adore thee, for thou art awfully wonderful. Thy works are wonderful; as my soul well knoweth.
PSA 139:15 From thee was not concealed this bone of mine; which thou in secret didst fashion.
PSA 139:16 When my substance was in the lowest parts of the earth; thine eyes beheld the unwrought part of me. When on thy book all shall be enrolled; they will day by day be fashioned.
PSA 139:17 When none among these were yet in being; for me these friends of thine, God, were highly prized: their principalities were made very strong.
PSA 139:18 Were I to number them, they would surpass the sand. I have been raised up and am still with thee.
PSA 139:19 Since thou, God, slayest sinners: begone from me ye bloody men.
PSA 139:20 For in answer to their reasoning thou wilt say, In vain shall they take these cities of thine.
PSA 139:21 Have I not, Lord, hated them who hate thee; and been melted for them who are thine enemies!
PSA 139:22 With perfect hatred I have hated them; I have accounted them mine enemies.
PSA 139:23 Try me, O God, and know my heart: examine me and know my ways;
PSA 139:24 and see if there be in me any trace of iniquity; and lead me in an everlasting way.
PSA 140:1 For the conclusion. A Psalm. By David. Deliver me, Lord, from a wicked commoner: from an unjust man of rank, preserve me;
PSA 140:2 who hath contrived mischief in their heart. All the day long they prepared battles:
PSA 140:3 they sharpened their tongue like that of a serpent: the poison of asps was under their lips.
PSA 140:4 Keep me, Lord, from the hand of a sinner: deliver me from unjust men; who have formed contrivances to supplant my steps.
PSA 140:5 The haughty hid a snare for me; they spread out nets for my feet; close by the way they laid for me a stumbling block.
PSA 140:6 I said to the Lord, Thou art my God. Hear Lord, the voice of my supplication.
PSA 140:7 O Lord, Lord, the strength of my salvation! Thou hast covered my head in the day of battle.
PSA 140:8 Deliver me not up to the wicked from my desire. Against me they have formed devices: Forsake me not, lest they be exalted.
PSA 140:9 Let the amount of their compassings; the labour of their lips cover them.
PSA 140:10 On them shall fall coals of fire in the land; and thou wilt overthrow them with miseries; that they may not rise up again.
PSA 140:11 A tattling chief cannot prosper in the land: evils will hunt to destruction a man of violence.
PSA 140:12 I know that the Lord will maintain the cause of the afflicted and the right of the needy:
PSA 140:13 moreover, that the righteous will adore thy name; that the upright shall dwell in thy presence.
PSA 141:1 A Psalm by David. TO thee, Lord, I have cried, hearken to me; attend to the sound of my supplication. When I cry to thee;
PSA 141:2 let my prayer come before thee as incense; and the lifting up of my hands as an evening sacrifice.
PSA 141:3 Set a watch, Lord, on my mouth; and guard the door of my lips.
PSA 141:4 Let not my heart turn aside to wicked deeds; to form excuses for sins with men who work iniquity: nor let me associate with their chosen bands.
PSA 141:5 Let a righteous man correct me with mercy; and he will work conviction in me: but let not the oil of a sinner [for this shall still be my prayer] anoint my head at their pleasure.
PSA 141:6 Their strong men were swallowed up near a rock: let them hear my words for they were sweet.
PSA 141:7 As if a lump of earth was broken on the ground; our bones were scattered at the grave's mouth.
PSA 141:8 Since mine eyes are to thee, O Lord, Lord; in thee I have placed my confidence; deliver not my soul to destruction.
PSA 141:9 Keep me from the snare they have laid for me: and from the stumbling blocks of the workers of iniquity.
PSA 141:10 The wicked shall fall by their own net, I am in private till I can escape.
PSA 142:1 On understanding. By David when he was in the cave. A Prayer. With my voice I cried to the Lord; to the Lord I made supplication with my voice.
PSA 142:2 Before him I pour out my prayer: before him I will declare my affliction.
PSA 142:3 When my spirit fainted thou knewest my paths. In the way I was going they hid a snare for me.
PSA 142:4 I looked to the right; and observed that none was there, who knew me. Flight was cut off from me; and is he not earnestly seeking my life?
PSA 142:5 To thee, O Lord, I cried and said, Thou art my hope; my portion in the land of the living.
PSA 142:6 Attend to my supplication; for I am brought very low: deliver me from my persecutors; for they are stronger than I.
PSA 142:7 Bring my soul out of prison, that I may adore thy name, Lord. Let the righteous wait for me, till thou shalt reward me.
PSA 143:1 A Psalm by David, when his son was pursuing him. O LORD, hearken to my prayer! Listen to my supplication in thy truth; answer me in thy saving goodness;
PSA 143:2 and enter not into judgment with thy servant; for in thy sight no man living can be justified.
PSA 143:3 Because the enemy hath earnestly sought my life; hath humbled my life to the ground; hath caused me to sit in dark places, like them who have been long dead;
PSA 143:4 therefore my spirit was overwhelmed with grief; my heart within me was troubled and
PSA 143:5 I remembered the days of old. I meditated on all thy works; I mused on the works of thy hands.
PSA 143:6 I spread forth my hands to thee; for thee my soul thirsted like land without water.
PSA 143:7 Hear me speedily, Lord; my spirit hath failed. Turn not away thy face from me; nor let me be like them who go down to the pit.
PSA 143:8 Cause me to hear thy kindness in the morning; for in thee I have placed my confidence. O Lord, let me know which way I shall go; for to thee I have lifted up my soul.
PSA 143:9 Deliver me, O Lord, from mine enemies; for to thee I have fled for refuge.
PSA 143:10 Teach me to do thy will; for thou art my God. Let thy good spirit lead me in the right way.
PSA 143:11 For the sake of thy name, thou, Lord, wilt keep me alive; in thy saving goodness thou wilt bring my soul out of trouble,
PSA 143:12 and in thy mercy cut off mine enemies, and destroy all them that afflict my soul; for I am thy servant.
PSA 144:1 By David. On Goliath. Blessed be the Lord my God, who teacheth my hands to war and my fingers to fight.
PSA 144:2 He is my mercy and my refuge; my support and my deliverer, my protector in whom I trusted, who subdueth the people under me.
PSA 144:3 Lord, what is man that thou shouldst acknowledge him, or a son of man that thou shouldst regard him!
PSA 144:4 Man is like vanity, his days glide away like a shadow.
PSA 144:5 O Lord, bow thy heaven and come down: touch the mountains and let them smoke.
PSA 144:6 Flash lightnings and thou wilt scatter them; dart thy bolts and thou wilt discomfit them;
PSA 144:7 stretch forth thy hand from on high; rescue me and deliver me from many waters; out of the hand of the children of strangers,
PSA 144:8 whose mouth hath uttered falsehood, and whose right hand is a right hand of deceit
PSA 144:9 O God, to thee I will sing a new song; to thee I will play on a ten stringed psaltery,
PSA 144:10 to him who giveth salvation to kings, who hath redeemed his servant David from the hurtful sword.
PSA 144:11 Rescue me and deliver me out of the hand of the children of strangers, whose mouth hath uttered falsehood, and whose right hand is a right hand of deceit;
PSA 144:12 whose sons are like trees well planted when young; their daughters beauteous, adorned like shrines;
PSA 144:13 their store houses full and overflowing; their flocks prolific, abounding in their outwalks;
PSA 144:14 their herds fat. There is no destruction of enclosures; no breaking out; no screaming in their folds.
PSA 144:15 The people who had such things were hailed happy; but happy is the people, whose God is the Lord.
PSA 145:1 A Psalm of praise. By David, I will extol thee, my God, my king: and bless thy name for ever and ever.
PSA 145:2 Day by day I will bless thee, and praise thy name for ever and ever.
PSA 145:3 The Lord is great and greatly to be praised; and of his greatness there is no end.
PSA 145:4 Let generation after generation praise thy works, and proclaim thy mighty power:
PSA 145:5 Let them speak of the transcendant glory of thy majesty, and relate thy wonderous works.
PSA 145:6 Let them express the might of thine awful dealings, and rehearse thy greatness.
PSA 145:7 Let them make mention of thine abundant goodness, and exult with joy in thy saving mercy.
PSA 145:8 The Lord is gracious and merciful: long suffering and abundant in kindness.
PSA 145:9 The Lord is kind to them who wait, and his mercies are over all his works.
PSA 145:10 Let all thy works, O Lord, praise thee, and let thy saints bless thee;
PSA 145:11 let them speak of the glory of thy kingdom, and talk of thy government:
PSA 145:12 to make known thy government to the sons of men, and the transcendant glory of thy kingdom.
PSA 145:13 Thy kingdom is an everlasting kingdom, and thy dominion, throughout all generations.
PSA 145:14 The Lord is faithful in his words, and bountiful in all his works.
PSA 145:15 The Lord upholdeth all that are falling, and raiseth up all who are broken down.
PSA 145:16 The eyes of all wait upon thee: and thou givest them their food in due season; thou openest thy hands, and satisfiest the desire of every living thing.
PSA 145:17 The Lord is righteous in all his ways, and bountiful in all his works.
PSA 145:18 The Lord is near to all who invoke him; to all that call upon him with truth.
PSA 145:19 He will fulfil the desire of them who fear him: he will hear their prayer and save them.
PSA 145:20 The Lord keepeth all them who love him; but all the wicked he will utterly destroy.
PSA 145:21 Let my mouth speak the praise of the Lord: and let all flesh bless his holy name, for ever and for evermore.
PSA 146:1 An Alleluia, of Aggaius and Zacharias. Praise the Lord, my soul: while I live I will praise the Lord.
PSA 146:2 I will sing praises to God, while I have a being.
PSA 146:3 Trust not in chiefs, nor in sons of men, in whom there is no safety.
PSA 146:4 His breath goeth out and he shall return to his earth; on that day all his projects shall perish.
PSA 146:5 Happy he whose helper is the  God of Jacob: his hope is in the Lord his God,
PSA 146:6 who made the heaven and the earth, the sea and all the things in them;
PSA 146:7 who keepeth truth forever, executing judgment for the aggrieved, giving food to the hungry.
PSA 146:8 The Lord looseth them who were bound. The Lord causeth the blind to see clearly. The Lord raiseth up them who were broken down. The Lord loveth the righteous.
PSA 146:9 The Lord preserveth the strangers. He will support the orphan and the widow, and destroy the way of the wicked.
PSA 146:10 The Lord will reign forever; thy God, Sion, throughout all generations.
PSA 147:1 An Alleluia, of Aggaius and Zacharias. Praise the Lord, for good is a song of praise; to our God let praise be sweetly sung.
PSA 147:2 The Lord is rebuilding Jerusalem; and he will gather the dispersions of Israel.
PSA 147:3 He healeth the broken hearted, and bindeth up their wounds;
PSA 147:4 he numbereth the multitudes of stars, and calleth them all by their names.
PSA 147:5 Great is our Lord and great his power; and infinite in his understanding.
PSA 147:6 The Lord raiseth up the meek; and humbleth sinners to the ground.
PSA 147:7 Sing alternately to the Lord with thanksgiving. In concert with the kithara, sing praises to our God;
PSA 147:8 to him who covereth the heaven with clouds; to him who provideth rain for the earth; to him who causeth grass to grow on mountains, and bladed corn for the use of man;
PSA 147:9 and who giveth suitable food to cattle, and to the young ravens which call on him.
PSA 147:10 In the courage of the horse he will not delight, nor is he pleased with the agility of the warrior.
PSA 147:11 The Lord delighteth in them who fear him, and in all them who trust in his mercy.
PSA 147:12 An Alleluia, of Aggaius and Zacharias. Praise the Lord, Jerusalem: Sion, praise thy God;
PSA 147:13 for he hath strengthened the bars of thy gates; he hath blessed thy children within thee.
PSA 147:14 He maketh thy borders peace, and feedeth thee with the finest wheat;
PSA 147:15 He is sending his oracle to this land: his word shall run with speed.
PSA 147:16 When he giveth snow like wool; when he scattereth the hoar frost like ashes;
PSA 147:17 when he sendeth down like morsels his chrystal hail; who can stand before his cold?
PSA 147:18 Let him but send forth his word and he will melt them; let him but blow his breath and the waters will flow.
PSA 147:19 He is sending his word to Jacob; his statutes and his judgments to Israel.
PSA 147:20 He hath not dealt thus with any nation, nor hath he laid open to them his judgments.

PSA 148:2 Praise him all ye his angels: praise him all ye his hosts.
PSA 148:3 Sun and moon! Praise him: praise him all ye stars and light.

PSA 148:5 let them praise the name of the Lord; for he spake and they were produced: he commanded and they were created.
PSA 148:6 He established them forever and ever: he made a decree and it shall not pass away.

PSA 148:8 Fire, hail, snow, ice, tempestuous wind, which execute his commands!
PSA 148:9 Mountains, and all hills! fruit trees and all cedars!
PSA 148:10 wild beasts and all cattle! creeping things and winged fowls!
PSA 148:11 Kings of the earth, and all peoples! chiefs and all judges of the earth!
PSA 148:12 youths and virgins! elders with them of younger years!
PSA 148:13 let them praise the name of the Lord; for his name alone is exalted. To him belongeth thanksgiving, on earth and in heaven.
PSA 148:14 When he shall exalt the horn of his people, let there be a song of praise among all his saints; among the children of Israel; a people who draw near to him.

PSA 149:2 Let Israel rejoice in his maker; and the children of Sion exult in their king.

PSA 150:1 An Alleluia. Praise God in his holies; praise him in the firmament of his power.
PSA 150:2 Praise him for his mighty acts: praise him according to his abundant majesty:
PSA 150:3 praise him with the sounding trumpet: praise him with the psaltery and kithara:
PSA 150:4 praise him with the tympanum and chorus: praise him with stringed instruments and organs;
PSA 150:5 praise him with soft sounding cymbals: praise him with the cymbals of triumph:
PSA 150:6 let every breath praise the Lord. Psalm 151 N.B. There is in the Septuagint another Psalm, with this title: This Psalm on David was written by himself in prose, when he fought in single combat with Goliath.  I was little among my brethren, and the youngest of my father's family. I fed my father's flocks. My hands had made an organ; and my fingers had tuned a psaltery. But who will tell my Lord. My Lord himself heareth. He sent his messenger and took me from my father's flocks and anointed me with anointing oil. My brothers were comely and great; but the Lord did not delight in them. I went out to meet the Philistine, and he cursed me by his idols. But I drew his own sword and cut off his head, and took away reproach from the children of Israel.
PRO 1:1 The Proverbs of David's son Solomon, who reigned over Israel,
PRO 1:2 to give a knowledge of wisdom and instruction; the perception of the words of prudence;
PRO 1:3 the interpretation of sentences; a discernment of true justice; and to direct judgment,
PRO 1:4 that he might give sagacity to the innocent; and to the youth knowledge and discretion:
PRO 1:5 for by attending to them a wise man will become wiser; and a man of understanding will possess a ride of government
PRO 1:6 and will understand a proverb and dark speech and the sayings of the wise and parables.
PRO 1:7 The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom. And all who practise this have good understanding. And piety towards God is the beginning of discernment: but the wicked despise wisdom and instruction.
PRO 1:8 My son, hear the instruction of thy father and reject not the maxims of thy mother:
PRO 1:9 for thou wilt receive a graceful crown for thy head; and a chain of gold for thy neck.
PRO 1:10 My son, let not wicked men lead thee astray. Consent not when they advise thee,
PRO 1:11 saying, Come with us; partake of blood; and let us hide in the earth an innocent man without cause,
PRO 1:12 and swallow him up alive, as the grave, and take away from earth the remembrance of him.
PRO 1:13 Let us seize his precious substance and fill our houses with spoils.
PRO 1:14 Cast in thy lot among us, and let us all have a common purse. Let one scrip serve us.
PRO 1:15 Go not thou in the way with them; but turn thy foot from their paths.
PRO 1:16 [Omitted]
PRO 1:17 For nets are not spread for birds unjustly.
PRO 1:18 For they who are accomplices to murder, treasure up evils for themselves. And doleful is the destruction of wicked men.
PRO 1:19 Such are the ways of all who commit iniquitous deeds. For by wickedness they destroy their own soul.
PRO 1:20 Wisdom uttereth her song at the gates and in the streets speaketh boldly;
PRO 1:21 and on the tops of walls she maketh proclamation; and at the gates of mighty men taketh a seat and at the gates of a city with confidence saith,
PRO 1:22 "While the innocent adhere to justice they shall not be put to shame: but as for fools who delight in mischief, having become wicked they hated knowledge and are become liable to censures.
PRO 1:23 Behold I will pour forth to you the dictate of my spirit: and teach you this word of mine;
PRO 1:24 seeing I have called and you have not answered: and though I continued my speech, you did not attend:
PRO 1:25 but set at naught my counsels and disregarded my reproofs:
PRO 1:26 therefore I will laugh at your calamity; and mock when your destruction cometh.
PRO 1:27 Yes, when tumult shall suddenly come upon you; and destruction like a whirlwind shall be at hand; even when tribulation and siege approach you; or when destruction is advancing upon you.
PRO 1:28 For when you call upon me I will not listen to you. The wicked may seek me, but they shall not find me.
PRO 1:29 For they hated wisdom and did not chuse the word of the Lord:
PRO 1:30 nor would they attend to my counsels, but contemned my reproofs:
PRO 1:31 Let them eat, therefore, the fruits of their own way; and be filled with their own iniquity.
PRO 1:32 For, because they wronged infants they shall be slain: and a rigorous inquest shall destroy the wicked.
PRO 1:33 But he who hearkeneth to me shall dwell with hope; and rest secure from all evil."
PRO 2:1 My son, if thou wilt receive the dictate which I enjoin and hide it with thee,
PRO 2:2 thine ear will hearken to wisdom; and thou wilt apply thy heart to understanding, and transmit it for instruction to thy son.
PRO 2:3 For if thou wilt call upon wisdom: and utter thy voice for understanding;
PRO 2:4 if thou wilt seek for it as silver; and search for it as for treasures;
PRO 2:5 then thou shalt understand the fear of the Lord; and find the knowledge of God.
PRO 2:6 For the Lord giveth wisdom; and from his presence is knowledge and understanding:
PRO 2:7 and he treasureth up salvation for the upright. He will protect their going,
PRO 2:8 that they may keep the paths of rectitude. And he will guard the way of them who reverence him.
PRO 2:9 Then thou shalt understand judgment and justice; and direct all thy wheels right.
PRO 2:10 For when wisdom entereth into thine understanding: and knowledge appeareth pleasant to thy soul:
PRO 2:11 good counsel will keep thee, and holy prudence will guard thee:
PRO 2:12 that she may deliver thee from an evil way and from a man who speaketh perversely.
PRO 2:13 Alas for them who leave straight paths to walk in the ways of darkness;
PRO 2:14 who are delighted with evils and have joy in evil perversion;
PRO 2:15 whose ways are crooked, and whose paths turn aside to lead thee far from the straight road
PRO 2:16 and estrange thee from a just determination.
PRO 2:17 My son, let not evil counsel, who hath forsaken the discipline of youth and hath forgotten the divine covenant, take hold of thee.
PRO 2:18 For she hath placed her house near death; and her wheels with the earth born near the mansion of the dead.
PRO 2:19 None who walk by her direction can ever return; nor ever recover the right paths.
PRO 2:20 For they are not taken hold of by years of life. If they indeed had walked in good ways: they would have found the paths of justice smooth.
PRO 2:21 Because the upright shall inhabit the land; and the holy shall be left in it;
PRO 2:22 the ways of the wicked shall be destroyed from the land; and the transgressors shall be driven out of it.
PRO 3:1 My son, forget not my laws; but let thy heart keep my commandments.
PRO 3:2 For they will add to thee length of days and years of life and peace.
PRO 3:3 Let not acts of kindness and faithfulness forsake thee: but bind them about thy neck
PRO 3:4 and thou shalt find favour. Be provident in regard to things good in the sight of the Lord and of men.
PRO 3:5 Trust in God with thy whole heart; and be not elated for thine own wisdom.
PRO 3:6 Shew it in all thy ways, that it may make thy paths straight.
PRO 3:7 Be not wise in thine own conceit; but fear God and depart from all evil:
PRO 3:8 then shall thy body have health and thy bones a cure.
PRO 3:9 Honour the Lord with some of thy righteous labours: and set apart for him some of thy fruits of righteousness:
PRO 3:10 that thy barns may be plenteously filled with corn; and that thy vats may overflow with wine.
PRO 3:11 My son, slight not the correction of the Lord; nor faint when reproved by him:
PRO 3:12 for whom the Lord loveth he reproveth: and chastiseth every son whom he receiveth.
PRO 3:13 Happy the man, who hath found wisdom: and the mortal who hath seen prudence:
PRO 3:14 for it is better to traffick for her, than for treasures of gold and silver.
PRO 3:15 She is more precious than costly stones: and nothing evil can be compared to her. She is easily known by all who approach her; but no price is equal to her in value.
PRO 3:16 For length of days and years of life are in her right hand; and in her left, riches and glory. Out of her mouth proceedeth righteousness: and on her tongue she carrieth law and mercy.
PRO 3:17 Her ways are ways of pleasantness and all her paths are peace.
PRO 3:18 She is a tree of life to all who take hold of her; and safe for them who rely on her, as on the Lord.
PRO 3:19 By wisdom God founded the earth; and by understanding he furnished the heavens.
PRO 3:20 By knowledge the deeps were broken up and the clouds distilled dew.
PRO 3:21 My son, be not wanting in retention: but keep my counsel, namely, the sentiment:
PRO 3:22 that thy soul may live and that grace may be around thy neck: and it will be health to thy flesh and a cure for thy bones;
PRO 3:23 that thou mayst proceed on in all thy ways in peace and security; and that thy foot may not stumble.
PRO 3:24 For when thou liest down, thou shalt be free from fear: and when thou sleepest, thou shalt sleep sweetly;
PRO 3:25 and shalt not fear the bursting in of terror; nor the sudden assaults of wicked men.
PRO 3:26 For the Lord will be over all thy ways, and will support thy foot that thou mayst not be shaken.
PRO 3:27 Delay not to do good to the needy, when it is in the power of thy hand to help.
PRO 3:28 Do not say, Go away and come again: tomorrow I will give; when thou hast it in thy power to do good: for thou knowest not what to-morrow will bring forth.
PRO 3:29 Devise not evils against thy friend; who sojourneth with thee and confideth in thee.
PRO 3:30 Be not at enmity with a man without cause; lest he do thee some mischief.
PRO 3:31 Acquire not the reproaches of bad men, nor be fond of their ways.
PRO 3:32 For every transgressor is impure in the sight of the Lord; and among the righteous he taketh not a seat.
PRO 3:33 The curse of God is in the houses of the wicked: but the folds of the righteous are blessed.
PRO 3:34 The Lord resisteth the proud; but he granteth favour to the humble.
PRO 3:35 The wise shall inherit glory; but the wicked have extolled dishonour.
PRO 4:1 Hear, children, the instructions of a father; and attend to know the meaning:
PRO 4:2 for I am giving you a good gift: forsake not my law:
PRO 4:3 for I was a son obedient to a father; and beloved in the sight of a mother:
PRO 4:4 and they said when they taught me, "Let our words sink deep in thy heart. Keep our commandments; do not forget;
PRO 4:5 overlook not the dictate of my mouth:
PRO 4:6 forsake it not, and it will defend thee: love it and it will preserve thee:
PRO 4:7 [Omitted]
PRO 4:8 secure it and it will exalt thee: honour it that it may embrace thee:
PRO 4:9 that it may be to thy head a crown of graces and cover thee with a crown of pleasure.
PRO 4:10 Hear my son and receive my words; that, when the years of thy life shall be multiplied, thou mayst have many ways of livelihood:
PRO 4:11 for I am teaching thee ways of wisdom; and confirming thee in right paths.
PRO 4:12 For when thou goest, thy steps will not be straitened: and when thou runnest thou shalt not be tired.
PRO 4:13 Take fast hold of mine instruction, let it not go: but keep it for thyself during thy life.
PRO 4:14 Go not in the ways of wicked men; nor be fond of the ways of transgressors.
PRO 4:15 In what place soever they encamp, go not thither: but turn away from them and keep at a distance:
PRO 4:16 for they cannot sleep. Unless they do evil; their sleep is taken from them and they cannot lie down to rest.
PRO 4:17 For they eat the bread of wickedness; and drink plentifully of the wine of violence.
PRO 4:18 But the paths of the just shine like light; shining more and more until it is perfect day.
PRO 4:19 But the ways of the wicked being dark; they know not at what they stumble.
PRO 4:20 Attend, my son, to my speech, and incline thine ear to my words.
PRO 4:21 That thy fountains may not fail thee, keep them in thy heart;
PRO 4:22 for they are life to them who find them and health to all flesh.
PRO 4:23 Guard thy heart with all diligence; for out of these are the issues of life.
PRO 4:24 Put away from thee a froward mouth, and put perverse lips far from thee.
PRO 4:25 Let thine eyes look straight forward and thine eyelids wink justly.
PRO 4:26 Make straight paths with thy feet and order all thy ways right.
PRO 4:27 Turn not to the right, nor the left; but turn away thy foot from an evil way; for God knoweth the ways on the right, but those on the left are crooked. But he will make thy paths straight and conduct thy steps in peace.
PRO 5:1 My son, attend to my wisdom, and incline thine ear to my words,
PRO 5:2 that thou mayst keep a good understanding. Now the sense of my lips giveth thee this injunction; listen not to an abandoned woman;
PRO 5:3 for honey droppeth from the lips of a harlot, which for a while pleaseth thy palate;
PRO 5:4 but in the end thou wilt find it bitterer than gall, and sharper than a two edged sword.
PRO 5:5 For the feet of folly lead them, who indulge themselves with her, down with death to the mansion of the dead. Her steps indeed are not established,
PRO 5:6 for she walketh not in the ways of life. Her paths are slippery and not easily known.
PRO 5:7 Now therefore, my son, hearken to me and slight not my words.
PRO 5:8 Remove thy way far from her, go not near the doors of her house;
PRO 5:9 That thou mayst not give thy life to others, and thy substance to the cruel:
PRO 5:10 that strangers may not be filled with thy wealth, and thy labours go into the houses of strangers,
PRO 5:11 and thou at last be grieved. When the flesh of thy body is consumed,
PRO 5:12 then thou wilt say, "How have I hated instruction, and my heart despised reproof!
PRO 5:13 I hearkened not to the voice of him who instructed me and taught me; nor have I inclined mine ear.
PRO 5:14 I have been almost in all evil, in the midst of the assembly and congregation."
PRO 5:15 Drink water from thine own vessels, and from the wells of thine own fountain.
PRO 5:16 Let not the waters from thy fountain over flow for thee; but let thy waters run in thine own streets.
PRO 5:17 Let them be for thyself only, and let no stranger partake with thee.
PRO 5:18 Let thy fountain of water be appropriate to thyself; and rejoice with the wife of thy youth.
PRO 5:19 Let thy loving hind and graceful fawn converse with thee; and let her be accounted peculiarly thine, and be with thee on all occasions. For ravished with her love thou wilt become a numerous family.
PRO 5:20 Be not devoted to a strange woman, nor embraced in the arms of one not thine own.
PRO 5:21 For the ways of a husband are before the eyes of God, and he examineth narrowly all his paths.
PRO 5:22 Iniquities hunt a man; but every one is caught by the cords of his own sins.
PRO 5:23 Such a one dieth with the uninstructed, but from his plentiful means of living he was cast out, and perished by reason of folly.
PRO 6:1 My son, if thou become surety for thy friend, thou wilt deliver up thy hand to an enemy.
PRO 6:2 For a man's own lips are a powerful snare, and he is caught by the words of his own mouth.
PRO 6:3 Do, my son, what I enjoin thee, and save thyself; for thou art come into the hands of bad men on thy friend's account. Be not remiss, but importune thy friend for whom thou art surety.
PRO 6:4 Give no sleep to thine eyes, nor slumber to thine eyelids,
PRO 6:5 that thou mayst be saved like a roe from a toil, and like a bird from a snare.
PRO 6:6 Go to the ant, thou sluggard; and having seen its ways follow the example and be wiser than it.
PRO 6:7 For having no cultivated field, no driver, nor master,
PRO 6:8 it provideth its food in summer, and layeth up a plentiful supply in harvest. Or go to the bee and learn what a Worker she is: and how seriously she performeth her work, to the labours of which both kings and subjects apply themselves as far as health permits; and to all it is agreeable and honourable. And though her strength be small, having honoured wisdom she is diligently employed.
PRO 6:9 How long wilt thou sleep, sluggard, and when wilt thou rouse from sleep?
PRO 6:10 Thou art sleeping a little; but resting a little; but taking a short nap; but folding thy hands a little while on thy breast!
PRO 6:11 But is not poverty coming upon thee like an unwelcome traveller? And want like a speedy courier? Whereas if thou be diligent; thy harvest will come like a fountain, and want like a bad courier will run away.
PRO 6:12 A man void of understanding, and a transgressor, walketh in ways which are not good.
PRO 6:13 But he winketh with his eye and maketh a sign with his foot; and teacheth, by pointing his fingers;
PRO 6:14 his depraved heart contriveth mischief. Such a one is continually raising tumults in a city.
PRO 6:15 For this cause his destruction cometh suddenly; Wounds and incurable bruises.
PRO 6:16 Because he delighteth in all those things which God hateth: therefore he is destroyed for the depravity of his soul.
PRO 6:17 His eye is that of a scorner; his tongue is false; his hands are employed in shedding innocent blood;
PRO 6:18 his heart contriveth wicked purposes, and his feet are swift to do evil:
PRO 6:19 as a false witness he spreadeth lies, and soweth discord among brethren.
PRO 6:20 My son, keep the laws of thy father, and reject not the maxims of thy mother.
PRO 6:21 Bind them continually on thy mind: and tie them as a chain around thy neck.
PRO 6:22 When thou walkest, take this along and let it be with thee: and when thou sleepest, let it guard thee; that when thou awakest, it may talk with thee.
PRO 6:23 For the command of a law is a lamp and light; and reproof and instruction is the way of life,
PRO 6:24 to keep thee from a married woman; and from the flattering tongue of a strange woman.
PRO 6:25 Let not a lust for beauty overcome thee: be not captivated by thine eyes, nor ensnared by her eyelids.
PRO 6:26 For the price of a harlot is scarce that of a single loaf; but an adulteress hunteth for the precious lives of men.
PRO 6:27 Can any one put fire in his bosom and not burn his clothes?
PRO 6:28 Or can one walk on coals of fire and not burn his feet?
PRO 6:29 So he who goeth in, to a married woman, cannot escape punishment; no, nor any one who toucheth her.
PRO 6:30 It exciteth no wonder, if one be caught stealing; for a hungry man stealeth to satisfy his soul;
PRO 6:31 but if he be caught, he is to pay seven fold; and by giving all that he hath, he will deliver himself.
PRO 6:32 But he, who through want of understanding, committeth adultery, provideth destruction for his soul.
PRO 6:33 He suffereth pangs and dishonour; and his reproach can never be wiped away.
PRO 6:34 For the rage of her husband being full of jealousy, will not spare in the day of vengeance;
PRO 6:35 nor will he abate his enmity for any ransom; nor be appeased by many gifts.
PRO 7:1 My son keep my words and lay up my commandments with thee. My son, honor the Lord and thou shall be strong; but besides him, fear no other.
PRO 7:2 Keep my commandments, that thou mayst live; and my words as the apple of thine eye.
PRO 7:3 Bind them about thy fingers, and write them on the table of thy heart.
PRO 7:4 Implore Wisdom to be thy sister, and make Understanding thine acquaintance:
PRO 7:5 that she may keep thee from a strange and wicked woman, in case she, with alluring words should attack thee.
PRO 7:6 For through a lattice she looketh out of her house into the streets;
PRO 7:7 and if among the simple youths she chanceth to see a young man, void of understanding,
PRO 7:8 walking near a corner in the passages to her house,
PRO 7:9 and talking in the twilight, when the evening is still and duskish:
PRO 7:10 then this woman, who maketh the hearts of young men flutter, meeteth him, in the attire of a harlot.
PRO 7:11 Indeed she is ever on the wing and insatiable, and her feet abide not at home.
PRO 7:12 For sometimes she roveth abroad: and sometimes lieth in wait in the streets, at every corner.
PRO 7:13 Ha! she hath caught him and kissed him, and with an unblushing countenance, said to him:
PRO 7:14 "I have a peace offering; today I am paying my vows:
PRO 7:15 for this reason I came out to meet thee: earnestly longing to see thee.
PRO 7:16 I have found thee. With cords I have stretched my bed, and decked it with tapestry from Egypt.
PRO 7:17 I have perfumed my bed with saffron, and my house with cinnamon:
PRO 7:18 come, and let us take our fill of love till the morning: come and let us solace ourselves with love.
PRO 7:19 For my husband is not at home, he is gone a long journey;
PRO 7:20 he took in his hand a roll of silver, and will return to his house after many days."
PRO 7:21 So with much fawning discourse she led him astray; and with the flattery of her lips inveigled him.
PRO 7:22 And he is gone after her, attracted by her; as an ox is led to slaughter, or as a dog to be chained: or like a deer pierced through the liver with a dart.
PRO 7:23 And he hasteth like a bird to a snare; not knowing that he is running the risk of his life.
PRO 7:24 Now therefore ray son hearken to me; and attend to the words of my mouth.
PRO 7:25 Let not thy heart turn aside to her ways:
PRO 7:26 for she hath wounded and brought down many; and innumerable are they whom she hath slain.
PRO 7:27 Her house is the highway to Hades, leading down to the chambers of death.
PRO 8:1 As for thee thou art to proclaim wisdom; that understanding may attend thee.
PRO 8:2 For she is on the lofty summits; and hath taken her stand in the middle of highways.
PRO 8:3 For at the gates of the mighty she hath taken a seat, and at the entrance thereof chanteth her song.
PRO 8:4 "To you, men, I call, and utter my voice to the sons of men.
PRO 8:5 Ye who are innocent learn discretion: and ye who are uninstructed give attention.
PRO 8:6 Hearken to me, for I will speak solemn things; and with my lips disclose things which are right.
PRO 8:7 For my mouth shall speak truth; lying lips are indeed abominable in my sight.
PRO 8:8 All the words of my mouth are with righteousness; they have nothing crooked; nothing deceitful in them.
PRO 8:9 They are all plain to men of understanding: and right to them who find knowledge.
PRO 8:10 Receive instruction in preference to silver, and knowledge rather than fine gold.
PRO 8:11 For wisdom is better than precious stones: and no costly thing is equal to it in value.
PRO 8:12 I wisdom have inhabited counsel and knowledge; and I have made an appeal to understanding.
PRO 8:13 The fear of the Lord hateth injustice and insolence and haughtiness and the ways of the wicked: and I have hated the crooked ways of bad men.
PRO 8:14 To me belong counsel and safety. Prudence is mine; mine is fortitude.
PRO 8:15 By me kings reign and princes decree justice.
PRO 8:16 By me potentates are exalted; and by me sovereigns rule the earth.
PRO 8:17 Them who love me, I love: and they who seek me shall find me.
PRO 8:18 With me are riches and glory; even great possessions and righteousness.
PRO 8:19 My fruit is better than gold and precious stones: and my productions are better than choice silver.
PRO 8:20 I walk in the ways of righteousness; and am conversant in the paths of judgment:
PRO 8:21 that I may distribute wealth to them who love me; and fill their treasuries with good things. Having told you things which happen daily; I will now remember to reckon up things of old.
PRO 8:22 The Lord created me, the beginning of his ways for his works.
PRO 8:23 Before this age he founded me; in the beginning; before he made the earth
PRO 8:24 and before he made the deeps: before the fountains of water issued forth;
PRO 8:25 before the mountains were established; and before all the hills, he bringeth me forth.
PRO 8:26 The Lord made fields and uninhabited wilds; and the habitable heights of the earth.
PRO 8:27 When he furnished the heaven, I was with him; and when he set apart his own throne on the winds:
PRO 8:28 and when he strengthened the clouds above:
PRO 8:29 and when he secured the fountains of the earth below; And when he made the foundations of the earth strong:
PRO 8:30 I was harmonizing with him. I was the one in whom he delighted;
PRO 8:31 and I was daily gladdened by his presence on all occasions; when he finished the World and was pleased therewith; and when he was pleased with the sons of men.
PRO 8:32 Now therefore, my son hearken to me:
PRO 8:33 [Omitted]
PRO 8:34 happy is the man who will hearken to me: and the man who will keep my ways; watching daily at my gates, waiting at the posts of my doors.
PRO 8:35 For my ways are the ways of life; and volition is obtained from the Lord.
PRO 8:36 But they who sin against me act wickedly against their own souls; and they who hate me love death."
PRO 9:1 Wisdom hath built herself a house, and fixed underneath it seven pillars.
PRO 9:2 She hath slain her victims. She hath mixed her wine for the cup and furnished her table.
PRO 9:3 She hath sent out her servants, and with a loud proclamation hath given an invitation to her entertainment, saying,
PRO 9:4 "Whosoever is simple, let him come to me." And to them who want understanding she saith,
PRO 9:5 "Come, eat of my bread and drink the wine which I have mixed for you.
PRO 9:6 Forsake folly, that you may reign forever: and seek prudence and build up understanding with knowledge."
PRO 9:7 He who instructeth the wicked shall receive for himself dishonour; and he who reproveth
PRO 9:8 the ungodly will blemish himself. Rebuke not the wicked, lest they hate thee; rebuke a wise man and he will love thee.
PRO 9:9 Give a wise man a hint and he will be wiser; an intimation to a righteous man and he will proceed to take it.
PRO 9:10 The fear of the Lord is the beginning of wisdom; and knowledge is the counsel of the holy. For to know the law is a characteristick of a good understanding;
PRO 9:11 for by this means thou shalt live long, and years of life will be added to thee.
PRO 9:12 My son, if thou art wise for thyself, thou wilt be wise also for thy neighbours. But if thou become wicked, thou alone shalt draw up evils. He who leaneth upon lies, feedeth on the wind, and he shall pursue flying birds; for he hath left the walks of his own vineyard, and wandered out of the paths of his own field, and traverseth a desert without water, and a land destined to thirst; and with his hands gathereth sterility.
PRO 9:13 A woman who is foolish and bold needeth a curb; she hath no sense of shame.
PRO 9:14 She sat at the doors of her house; on a seat open to view in the streets;
PRO 9:15 calling to passengers who were going right on their ways,
PRO 9:16 "Let him who is the simplest of you turn aside to me; and them who want prudence I exhort saying,
PRO 9:17 Taste sweetly bread in secret and water sweeter for being stolen.
PRO 9:18 He indeed did not know that with her the earth born perish; that he is lighting upon the perch of death. But fly thou away speedily; tarry not in that place, nor fix thine eyes upon her; for in this manner thou shouldst pass by strange water. Abstain from strange water, and drink not of a strange fountain; that thou mayst live long, and that years of life may be added to thee.
PRO 10:1 A wise son maketh a father glad; but a foolish son is a grief to the mother.
PRO 10:2 Treasures cannot profit the wicked; but righteousness will deliver from death.
PRO 10:3 The Lord will not kill with hunger a righteous soul; but he will overthrow the life of the wicked.
PRO 10:4 Want humbleth a man; but the hands of the diligent enrich. A well instructed son will be wise, and shall have the simple for a servant.
PRO 10:5 A prudent son is safe from heat; but a transgressing son is blasted in harvest.
PRO 10:6 The blessing of the Lord is on the head of the righteous; but untimely grief shall stop the mouth of the wicked.
PRO 10:7 The just are remembered with praises; but the name of the wicked is extinguished.
PRO 10:8 The wise in heart will receive commandments; but a prevaricating babbler shall be subverted.
PRO 10:9 He who walketh uprightly walketh securely; but he who perverteth his ways shall be known.
PRO 10:10 He who winketh deceitfully with his eyes, collecteth sorrows for men; but he who reproveth freely maketh peace.
PRO 10:11 There is a fountain of life in the hand of the righteous; but destruction will stop the mouth of the wicked.
PRO 10:12 Hatred stirreth up contention; but friendship covereth all them who are not contentious.
PRO 10:13 He who from his lips uttereth wisdom, smiteth an imprudent man with a rod.
PRO 10:14 Wise men will lay up knowledge; but the mouth of the rash is near destruction.
PRO 10:15 The wealth of the rich is a strong city: but penury is the destruction of the wicked.
PRO 10:16 The works of the righteous produce life; but the hands of the wicked produce sins.
PRO 10:17 Instruction keepeth the just ways of life; but unexamined instruction leadeth astray.
PRO 10:18 Honest lips hide hatred; but they who utter reproaches are the greatest fools.
PRO 10:19 In speaking much thou canst not avoid sin; but if thou art sparing of thy lips, thou wilt be wise.
PRO 10:20 The tongue of the righteous is tried silver; but the heart of the wicked will not stand the test.
PRO 10:21 The lips of the righteous are skilled in things lofty; but those devoid of understanding die of want.
PRO 10:22 The blessing of the Lord is on the head of the righteous; it maketh rich, and to it no sorrow of heart shall be joined.
PRO 10:23 A fool doth mischief in sport; but for man wisdom bringeth forth prudence.
PRO 10:24 A wicked man is whirled about by destruction; but the desire of the righteous is acceptable.
PRO 10:25 In a passing tempest a wicked man vanisheth; but the righteous turn aside and are safe forever.
PRO 10:26 As vinegar is hurtful to the teeth; and smoke to the eyes; so is transgression to them who commit it.
PRO 10:27 The fear of the Lord prolongeth days; but the years of the wicked shall be shortened.
PRO 10:28 Joy maketh a long abode with the righteous; but the hope of the wicked shall perish.
PRO 10:29 The fear of the Lord is the holy man's bulwark; but destruction is for the workers of iniquity.
PRO 10:30 The righteous shall never transfer; but the wicked shall not inhabit the land.
PRO 10:31 The mouth of the righteous distilleth wisdom; but the tongue of the wicked shall be destroyed.
PRO 10:32 The lips of righteous men distil graces; but the mouth of the wicked is perverse.
PRO 11:1 A deceitful balance is an abomination to the Lord: but a just weight is his delight.
PRO 11:2 Where pride entereth, there dishonour [entereth] also. But the mouth of the lowly speaketh wisdom.
PRO 11:3 A righteous man dying left sorrow behind him; but the destruction of the wicked cometh suddenly and giveth joy.
PRO 11:4 [Omitted]
PRO 11:5 Righteousness maketh spotless ways straight: but wickedness falleth by iniquity.
PRO 11:6 The righteousness of upright men delivereth them: but transgressors are caught by their destruction.
PRO 11:7 When a righteous man dieth, hope is not lost: but the boast of the wicked perisheth.
PRO 11:8 A righteous man escapeth a snare: and in his stead the wicked is delivered up.
PRO 11:9 In the mouth of the wicked is a snare for citizens: but the knowledge of the righteous conduceth to prosperity.
PRO 11:10 By the good acts of the just a city flourished:
PRO 11:11 but by the mouth of the wicked it was overthrown.
PRO 11:12 A man void of wisdom derideth fellow citizens: but a prudent man enjoyeth quiet.
PRO 11:13 A double tongued man revealeth cabinet counsels: but one of a faithful spirit concealeth matters.
PRO 11:14 They, who have no government, fall like leaves: but in much counsel there is safety.
PRO 11:15 A wicked man doth hurt, when he associateth with the just: but he hateth the sound of safety.
PRO 11:16 A virtuous woman raiseth honour for her husband: but a woman who hateth righteousness is a throne of disgrace. The slothful though rich, become indigent: but the diligent are supported with wealth.
PRO 11:17 A merciful man doth good to his own soul: but the merciless destroyeth his own body.
PRO 11:18 A wicked man doth works of injustice: but the seed of the righteous is a reward of truth.
PRO 11:19 A righteous son is born to live; but the pursuit of the wicked tendeth to death.
PRO 11:20 Crooked ways are an abomination to the Lord: but all who are blameless in their ways are his delight.
PRO 11:21 He who wickedly joineth hand to hand shall not go unpunished: but he who soweth righteousness shall receive a just reward.
PRO 11:22 As a jewel in the snout of a swine; so is beauty in a woman void of discretion.
PRO 11:23 The desire of the righteous is altogether good; but the hope of the wicked shall perish.
PRO 11:24 There are some who scattering their substance make it more: and some who gather and make it less.
PRO 11:25 A soul is blessed which is altogether sincere: but a passionate man is not respected.
PRO 11:26 May he who with holdeth corn leave it to the nations! But blessing be on the head of him who distributeth!
PRO 11:27 The contriver of good things seeketh favour: but him, who seeketh mischief, mischief shall overtake.
PRO 11:28 He who trusteth in riches shall fall; but he who helpeth the righteous shall nourish.
PRO 11:29 He who hath no cover for his own house shall inherit the wind; and a fool shall be a servant to the prudent.
PRO 11:30 From the fruit of righteousness springeth up the tree of life: but the lives of transgressors are prematurely destroyed.
PRO 11:31 If the righteous man scarcely escapeth: where shall the ungodly and sinner appear?
PRO 12:1 He who loveth instruction loveth knowledge: but he who hateth reproofs is a fool.
PRO 12:2 He who hath found favour with the Lord groweth better; but the transgressor shall be put to silence.
PRO 12:3 A man cannot prosper by wickedness: but the roots of the righteous shall not be moved.
PRO 12:4 A virtuous woman is a crown to her husband: but a mischievous woman, like a Worm in wood, ruineth her husband.
PRO 12:5 The thoughts of the righteous are judgments: but the wicked manage deceits.
PRO 12:6 The words of the wicked are deceitful: but the mouth of the upright shall deliver them.
PRO 12:7 When the wicked is overthrown, he vanisheth: but the houses of the righteous shall remain.
PRO 12:8 The mouth of the wise is praised by man: but the stupid heart is despised.
PRO 12:9 Better is the man, who unhonoured serveth himself: than he who honoureth himself and wanteth bread.
PRO 12:10 A righteous man regardeth the lives of his beasts: but the mercies of the wicked are cruel.
PRO 12:11 He who tilleth his own ground shall be satisfied with bread: but they who pursue vanities are void of understanding. He who taketh pleasure in taverns shall leave disgrace in his own fortresses.
PRO 12:12 The desires of the wicked are evil: but the roots of the righteous are in secure places.
PRO 12:13 By the transgression of his lips a sinner falleth into snares: but out of them a righteous man maketh his escape. He whose looks are mild will gain compassion: but he who contendeth in the gates will afflict souls.
PRO 12:14 From the fruits of his mouth the soul of man shall be satisfied with good things; and the recompence of his lips shall be given him.
PRO 12:15 The ways of fools are right in their own eyes: but a wise man hearkeneth to advice.
PRO 12:16 A fool presently sheweth his wrath: but a prudent man concealeth his dishonour.
PRO 12:17 A righteous man declareth the truth as it appeareth to him: but a false witness is deceitful.
PRO 12:18 They who wound with their speeches are swords: but the tongues of the wise are healing.
PRO 12:19 True lips establish testimony: but a hasty witness hath an unrighteous tongue.
PRO 12:20 Deceit is in the heart of him, who contriveth evils: but the counsellors of peace shall have joy.
PRO 12:21 Nothing unjust can please a righteous man: but the wicked can fill themselves with mischief.
PRO 12:22 Lying lips are an abomination to the Lord: but he who dealeth faithfully is acceptable to him.
PRO 12:23 A prudent man is a throne of knowledge: but the heart of fools will encounter curses.
PRO 12:24 The hand of the valiant can easily conquer: but the deceitful shall be for a prey.
PRO 12:25 Awful news trouble the heart of a righteous man: but good news make him glad.
PRO 12:26 A righteous judge will be a friend to himself: but evils shall pursue sinners: and the way of the wicked shall deceive them.
PRO 12:27 A deceitful man shall not enjoy what he hath caught; but as for a pure man, his acquisition is precious.
PRO 12:28 In the ways of righteousness there is life; but the ways of the revengeful lead to death.
PRO 13:1 A wise son is obedient to his father; but a disobedient son is in the way to destruction.
PRO 13:2 A good man eateth of the fruits of righteousness: but the souls of transgressors shall perish untimely.
PRO 13:3 He who guardeth his mouth preserveth his life; but he who is rash with his mouth, shall bring on himself terror.
PRO 13:4 Every sluggard is employed in wishing: but the hands of the diligent, in procuring.
PRO 13:5 A righteous man hateth a false word; but the wicked is shamed and shall not have confidence.
PRO 13:6 [Omitted]
PRO 13:7 Some pretend to be rich, having nothing; and some feign themselves poor, in great wealth.
PRO 13:8 The ransom of a man's life is his wealth; but a poor man is not subject to threats.
PRO 13:9 The righteous have light continually; but the light of the wicked is extinguished. Deceitful souls are led astray by sins; but the righteous exercise pity and compassion.
PRO 13:10 A wicked man doth mischief with haughtiness; but wise men are their own judges.
PRO 13:11 Wealth acquired by injustice, diminisheth; but he who gathereth for himself with piety, shall be satisfied. A righteous man sheweth mercy and lendeth.
PRO 13:12 Better is he who heartily beginneth to help, than he who promiseth and giveth expectation; for good desire is a tree of life.
PRO 13:13 He who despiseth business shall be despised by it; but he who feareth a commandment is safe. To a deceitful son nothing can be good: but the actions of a wise servant are prosperous, and his way will be prospered.
PRO 13:14 The law of the wise is a fountain of life; but the fool shall die by a snare.
PRO 13:15 A good understanding giveth favour: and to know the law is a proof of good understanding; but the ways of impostors end in destruction.
PRO 13:16 Every prudent man acteth with knowledge; but the fool hath laid open his wickedness.
PRO 13:17 A daring king will involve himself in evils; but a wise ambassador will deliver him.
PRO 13:18 Instruction removeth poverty and disgrace; and he who regardeth reproofs shall be honoured.
PRO 13:19 The desires of the pious sweeten life: but the works of the wicked are far from knowledge.
PRO 13:20 By walking with the wise thou wilt be wise; but he who walketh with fools will be known.
PRO 13:21 Evils shall pursue sinners, but good will overtake the righteous.
PRO 13:22 A good man shall leave an inheritance to his children; but the wealth of the wicked is treasured up for the righteous.
PRO 13:23 The righteous shall spend many years in wealth; but the unrighteous shall perish in a short time.
PRO 13:24 He who spareth the rod hateth his son; but he who loveth him correcteth diligently.
PRO 13:25 A righteous man eateth and satisfieth his soul; but the souls of the wicked are insatiate.
PRO 14:1 Wise women have built houses; but the foolish hath pulled them down with her hands.
PRO 14:2 He who walketh uprightly, feareth the Lord; but he who is perverse in his ways, shall be dishonoured.
PRO 14:3 From the mouth of fools there is a rod of pride; but the lips of the wise preserve them.
PRO 14:4 Where there are no cattle the stalls are clean; but where there is much provender, the ox's strength is manifest.
PRO 14:5 A faithful witness doth not lie; but a false witness kindleth lies.
PRO 14:6 Thou mayest seek wisdom among the wicked, but shalt not find it; but knowledge is easily found among the prudent.
PRO 14:7 All things are contrary to a foolish man: but wise lips are the arms of knowledge.
PRO 14:8 The wisdom of the prudent will give them a knowledge of their ways; but the folly of fools is in error.
PRO 14:9 The houses of transgressors need purifying; but the houses of the righteous are acceptable.
PRO 14:10 The heart of a man who hath sensibility; the soul of him who hath a feeling for pain, when he is made glad, mingleth not with pride.
PRO 14:11 The houses of the wicked shall vanish; but the tents of the upright shall stand.
PRO 14:12 There is a way which seemeth right to a man; but the end of it is at the bottom of Hades.
PRO 14:13 Grief mixeth not with pleasures; but extreme joy tendeth to sorrow.
PRO 14:14 A bold hearted man will be satisfied with his own ways; but a good man, with his intentions.
PRO 14:15 A man without guile, believeth every thing: but a prudent man cometh for a change of mind.
PRO 14:16 A wise man, when terrified, declineth from evil: but the fool, confident in himself, mixeth with transgressors.
PRO 14:17 A passionate man acteth without counsel; but a prudent man beareth many things.
PRO 14:18 Fools partake of wickedness; but the prudent will lay hold of knowledge.
PRO 14:19 Let the bad fall before the good; and the wicked attend at the gates of the righteous!
PRO 14:20 Friends will hate poor friends; but the friends of the rich are many.
PRO 14:21 He who despiseth the poor, sinneth: but he who compassionateth the poor is blessed.
PRO 14:22 They who are led astray devise mischief; but the good devise mercy and truth. The contrivers of mischief know neither mercy nor truth; but acts of kindness and truth are with them, who contrive good.
PRO 14:23 With all who are careful there is abundance; but he who is delicate and taketh no trouble shall be in want.
PRO 14:24 A prudent man is a crown to the wise; but the conversation of fools is evil.
PRO 14:25 A true witness will deliver a soul from evils; but a deceitful witness kindleth lies.
PRO 14:26 In the fear of the Lord a man hath hope of strength; and to his children he leaveth a support.
PRO 14:27 The commandment of the Lord is a fountain of life; and it causeth to decline from the snare of death.
PRO 14:28 In the multitude of a nation is the glory of a king: but in the failure of a people is the destruction of a prince.
PRO 14:29 A man slow to wrath, is of great understanding; but a passionate man is egregiously foolish.
PRO 14:30 A meek minded man is a physician of the heart; but a heart of sensibility is a corroder of the bones.
PRO 14:31 He who oppresseth the poor, provoketh his maker; but he who honoureth him, compassionateth the distressed.
PRO 14:32 A wicked man shall be driven away by his wickedness; but in his sanctity the righteous is secure.
PRO 14:33 In the good heart of a man there is wisdom; but in the heart of fools it is not discernable.
PRO 14:34 Righteousness exalteth a nation, but sins diminish tribes.
PRO 14:35 A wise minister is acceptable to a king: but by his own good conduct he removeth disgrace.
PRO 15:1 Wrath destroyeth even the prudent; now a soft answer turneth away wrath; but a harsh word stirreth up anger.
PRO 15:2 The tongue of the wise knoweth good things; but the mouth of fools poureth out evils.
PRO 15:3 The eyes of the Lord are in every place, they behold both the evil and the good.
PRO 15:4 A healing tongue is a tree of life; and he who keepeth it shall be filled with the spirit.
PRO 15:5 A fool despiseth the instruction of a father: but he who keepeth commands is more prudent. Where righteousness aboundeth there is much power: but the wicked being utterly rooted out of the land, shall perish.
PRO 15:6 In the houses of the righteous there is much power; but the fruits of the wicked shall perish.
PRO 15:7 The lips of the wise are devoted to knowledge; but the hearts of fools are not safe.
PRO 15:8 The sacrifices of the wicked are an abomination to the Lord; but the prayers of the upright are acceptable to him.
PRO 15:9 The ways of the wicked are an abomination to the Lord; but he loveth them who follow righteousness.
PRO 15:10 The correction of the innocent is remarked by them who pass by; but they who hate reproofs die dishonourably.
PRO 15:11 The mansion of the dead, and destruction, are open to the view of the Lord; how much more then the hearts of men!
PRO 15:12 An uninstructed man will not love them who reprove him, nor will he associate with the wise.
PRO 15:13 When the heart is glad the countenance is cheerful; but when in sorrow, it is sad.
PRO 15:14 An upright heart seeketh knowledge; but the mouth of the uninstructed will taste evils.
PRO 15:15 The eyes of the wicked are continually looking for evils; but the good are continually at rest.
PRO 15:16 Better is a small portion with the fear of the Lord, than great treasures without that fear.
PRO 15:17 Better is a dinner on herbs, with friendship and favour, than a feast on young bulls, with enmity.
PRO 15:18 A wrathful man prepareth battles; but he who is slow to anger appeaseth the rising quarrel. A man slow to anger will extinguish law suits; but the wicked rather promote them.
PRO 15:19 The ways of the slothful are strewed with thorns; but those of the diligent are well beaten.
PRO 15:20 A wise son maketh a glad father; but a foolish son mocketh his mother.
PRO 15:21 The paths of the foolish are destitute of understanding; but a prudent man walketh uprightly.
PRO 15:22 They who do not honour councils, substitute thoughts: but by the understanding of counsellors, counsel will endure.
PRO 15:23 A wicked man will not hearken to it, nor can he say any thing in season, or for the publick good.
PRO 15:24 The determinations of the wise are ways of life; that he may turn from the mansion of the dead and be saved.
PRO 15:25 The Lord destroyeth the houses of the haughty: but the border of the widow he hath established.
PRO 15:26 An evil thought is an abomination to the Lord: but the speeches of the chaste are grave.
PRO 15:27 He who receiveth bribes destroyeth himself: but he who hateth the receiving of bribes is safe. By acts of kindness and faithfulness sins are purged away: and by the fear of the Lord every one will decline from evil.
PRO 15:28 The hearts of the righteous study faithfulness: but the mouth of the wicked poureth out evil things. The ways of the righteous are acceptable to the Lord: and by them enemies are made friends.
PRO 15:29 God is far removed from the wicked: but he hearkeneth to the prayers of the righteous. Better is a small portion with righteousness; than much produce with injustice. Let the heart of man devise righteous things, that his steps may be directed by God.
PRO 15:30 The eye which beholdeth good things rejoiceth the heart: And a good reputation maketh the bones fat.
PRO 15:31 [Omitted]
PRO 15:32 He who rejecteth instruction hateth himself: but he who regardeth reproofs loveth his soul.
PRO 15:33 The fear of the Lord is instruction and wisdom: and the beginning of glory will be answerable thereto.

PRO 16:2 All the works of the humble are manifest in the sight of God; but the wicked shall perish in an evil day.
PRO 16:3 [Omitted]
PRO 16:4 [Omitted]
PRO 16:5 Every lofted minded man is impure in the sight of God: and he who hath joined hand to hand unjustly shall not go unpunished.
PRO 16:6 [Omitted]
PRO 16:7 The beginning of a good way is to do things just and acceptable in the sight of God, rather than to offer sacrifices.
PRO 16:8 He who seeketh the Lord shall find knowledge with righteousness. And they who seek him early shall find peace.
PRO 16:9 All the works of the Lord are with righteousness: but the wicked is kept for an evil day.
PRO 16:10 Divine sentence is in the mouth of a king: therefore his mouth should not err in judgment.
PRO 16:11 Justice is that which turneth the scales with the Lord. And his works are of just weight.
PRO 16:12 An evil doer is an abomination to a king: for the throne of government is established by righteousness.
PRO 16:13 Righteous lips are acceptable to a king; and he loveth right words.
PRO 16:14 The wrath of a king is a messenger of death: but a wise man can pacify it.
PRO 16:15 The son of a king is in the light of life: and they who are acceptable to him are as an evening cloud.
PRO 16:16 The productions of wisdom are better than gold: and the productions of prudence are better than silver.
PRO 16:17 The paths of life turn aside from evils: and the ways of righteousness are length of life. He who receiveth instruction shall enjoy good: and he who regardeth reproofs shall be wise. He who watcheth his own ways preserveth his soul: and he who loveth his life will be sparing of his mouth.
PRO 16:18 Pride goeth before destruction: and a haughty spirit before a fall.
PRO 16:19 A man of a gentle spirit with humility is better than he who divideth spoils with scorners.
PRO 16:20 A man intelligent in business is an inventer of good things: but most happy is he whose trust is in God.
PRO 16:21 The wise and prudent are called crafty; and they who are sweet in discourse will be more listened to.
PRO 16:22 Understanding is a fountain of life to them who possess it: but the instruction of fools is evil.
PRO 16:23 The heart of a wise man will consider the words of his mouth: and on his lips he will carry knowledge.
PRO 16:24 Good words are a honey comb: and the sweetness thereof is health to the soul.
PRO 16:25 There are ways which seem right to a man: but the latter ends of them look to the bottom of Hades.
PRO 16:26 A man by labour laboureth for himself; and wardeth off his own destruction.
PRO 16:27 He who is utterly perverse carrieth destruction in his mouth. A man void of understanding diggeth up evils for himself; and treasureth up fire with his lips.
PRO 16:28 A froward man spreadeth mischief. He will light up a lamp of deceit for evils; and he separateth them who were friends.
PRO 16:29 The man who is a transgressor enticeth friends; and leadeth them in ways which are not good.
PRO 16:30 But he who fixeth his eyes and deviseth froward things; and with his month enforceth all his evil purposes; is a very furnace of wickedness.
PRO 16:31 Old age is a crown of glory, when found in the ways of righteousness.
PRO 16:32 A man who is slow to wrath is better than the mighty; and he who subdueth anger is better than he who taketh a city,
PRO 16:33 All things come upon the wicked into their bosoms: but from the Lord all things which are just.
PRO 17:1 Better is a morsel with pleasure in peace; than a house full of goods and ill gotten dainties, with contention.
PRO 17:2 A wise servant will rule over foolish masters; and divide portions among brothers.
PRO 17:3 As silver and gold are tried in a furnace; so are chosen hearts, by the Lord.
PRO 17:4 A wicked man hearkeneth to the tongue of transgressors: but a righteous man payeth no attention to lying lips.
PRO 17:5 He who derideth a man in distress provoketh his maker; and he who rejoiceth at another's ruin shall not go unpunished: but he who sheweth compassion shall find mercy.
PRO 17:6 Children's children are the crown of old men: and the boast of children, is their fathers. Every ornament of wealth belongeth to the faithful; but to the unfaithful, not a farthing.
PRO 17:7 Faithful lips will not harmonize with a fool; nor lying lips with a righteous man.
PRO 17:8 Instruction is a precious reward to them who use it: and whithersoever it turneth it will prosper.
PRO 17:9 He who hideth transgressions seeketh friendship: but he who hateth to conceal, setteth friends and relations at varriance.
PRO 17:10 A threat affecteth the heart of the prudent: but a fool, though scourged, is not made sensible.
PRO 17:11 Every wicked man stirreth up contention: but the Lord will send him a cruel messenger.
PRO 17:12 Trouble may befal a prudent man: but the foolish will devise mischief.
PRO 17:13 Whosoever returneth evil for good; from his house evils shall not depart.
PRO 17:14 A righteous government giveth force to words: but sedition and quarrelling are the forerunners of want.
PRO 17:15 He who acquitteth the wicked and condemneth the just, is unclean and abominable in the sight of God.
PRO 17:16 Why should a fool have wealth? For the stupid cannot purchase wisdom. He who buildeth his house high seeketh destruction: and he who is backward to learn shall fall into evils.
PRO 17:17 For every occasion have a friend; but in distress let brothers be assistant: for they are born for this purpose.
PRO 17:18 A man void of understanding clappeth his hands and applaudeth himself on becoming surety for his friends,
PRO 17:19 He who is fond of sinning delighteth in quarrels:
PRO 17:20 but he who is stubborn doth not meet with good. A man of a changeable tongue will fall into evils: but the heart of a fool is sorrow to him who hath it.
PRO 17:21 A father hath no joy in an unteachable son: but a prudent son is the joy of his mother.
PRO 17:22 A cheerful heart promoteth health; but the bones of a heart wounded man are dried up.
PRO 17:23 When one unrighteously receiveth gifts in his bosom; his ways will not be straight. But a wicked man perverteth the ways of justice.
PRO 17:24 The countenance of a wise man is intelligent; but the fool's eyes are on the ends of the earth.
PRO 17:25 A foolish son is a vexation to a father; and sorrow to her who bore him.
PRO 17:26 To fine a righteous man is not good: nor is it consistent with piety to plot against righteous rulers.
PRO 17:27 He who forbeareth to utter a harsh word is prudent: and he who is slow to anger is a man of understanding.
PRO 17:28 Wisdom will be imputed to a fool, who inquireth after wisdom: and he who imposeth silence on himself will be esteemed wise.
PRO 18:1 He who desireth to part with friends seeketh excuses; but he will always be liable to reproach.
PRO 18:2 He who is void of understanding hath no use for wisdom; for he is rather led by folly.
PRO 18:3 When a wicked man cometh to a depth of evils he sheweth contempt; but ignominy and reproach come upon him.
PRO 18:4 A speech in a man's heart is deep water; but a stream issueth forth and a flowing spring.
PRO 18:5 To respect the person of a wicked man is not good; nor is it consistent with piety to pervert justice in judgment.
PRO 18:6 The lips of a fool lead him into trouble; and his mouth when bold provoketh death.
PRO 18:7 The mouth of a fool is his destruction, and his lips are a snare for his soul.
PRO 18:8 Fear depresseth the slothful; and the souls of the effeminate shall suffer want.
PRO 18:9 He who doth not use his endeavours to cure himself is brother to him who destroyeth himself.
PRO 18:10 The name of the Lord is of majestic power; and the righteous having recourse to it shall be exalted.
PRO 18:11 A rich man's wealth is a strong city, and the glory of it casteth a great shadow.
PRO 18:12 Before destruction a man's heart is haughty, and before honour it is humble.
PRO 18:13 He who answereth a matter before he heareth it, exposeth his folly and incurreth contempt.
PRO 18:14 A wise servant appeaseth a man's anger; but a mean spirited man who can bear?
PRO 18:15 The heart of a prudent man getteth knowledge; and the ears of the wise seek understanding.
PRO 18:16 A man's gift maketh room for him, and procureth him a seat among the mighty.
PRO 18:17 A just man is his own accuser in his first speech; but when he is accused his adversary is refuted.
PRO 18:18 The silent lot putteth an end to contention, and determineth among the mighty.
PRO 18:19 A brother assisted by a brother is like a fortified and lofty city, and is strong as a well founded palace.
PRO 18:20 With the fruits of his mouth a man filleth his belly, and with the fruits of his lips he shall be satisfied.
PRO 18:21 Death and life are in the power of the tongue; and they who have the command of it shall eat the fruits thereof.
PRO 18:22 He who hath found a good wife hath found favour, and hath received joy from God. He who putteth away a good wife, putteth away good things; but he who retaineth an adulteress is foolish and wicked.

PRO 19:8 He who procureth wisdom loveth himself; and he who keepeth it shall find good things.

PRO 19:11 A merciful man is slow to wrath; and his boast is over transgressors.
PRO 19:12 The threat of a king is like the roaring of a lion; but his favour is like dew on the grass.

PRO 19:27 A son who ceaseth to keep the instruction of a father; will meditate on evil sayings.
PRO 19:28 He who is surety for a foolish son, shall rail at the statute; but the mouth of the wicked shall swallow decisions.
PRO 19:29 Rods are prepared for the profligate: and punishments in like manner for fools.

PRO 20:5 Counsel in the heart of a man is deep water; but a man of understanding will draw it up.
