PRO 21:1 The heart of a king is in the hand of God; like a canal of water, he turneth it whithersoever he pleaseth.
PRO 21:2 Every man appeareth righteous in his own eyes: but the Lord directeth hearts.
PRO 21:3 To do justice and to adhere to truth are more acceptable to God than the blood of victims.
PRO 21:4 A high minded man is contentious and stubborn: but sin is the lamp of the wicked.
PRO 21:5 [Omitted]
PRO 21:6 He who getteth treasures by a lying tongue, pursueth vanity to the snares of death.
PRO 21:7 Destruction shall lodge with the wicked; because they refuse to do justice.
PRO 21:8 To the perverse God sendeth crooked ways: for his works are pure and right.
PRO 21:9 It is better to dwell in a corner in the open air; than in apartments plaistered with injustice; and in a house which is not clean.
PRO 21:10 The soul of the wicked will not be pitied by any man.
PRO 21:11 When a profligate is punished the innocent become more cautious; and the intelligent wise man will gain knowledge.
PRO 21:12 A just man discerneth the hearts of the wicked; and despiseth the wicked for their wickedness.
PRO 21:13 He who stoppeth his ears that he may not hear the distressed shall himself cry, and there shall be none to answer.
PRO 21:14 A gift given secretly pacifieth resentments: but he who is sparing of gifts exciteth strong wrath.
PRO 21:15 It is the joy of the righteous to execute judgment: but in the view of the wicked a holy man is unclean.
PRO 21:16 A man who wandereth from the path of justice, shall go to rest among the congregation of giants.
PRO 21:17 A needy man loveth pleasure. He wisheth to have wine and oil for his riches:
PRO 21:18 and a transgressor wisheth to be acquitted as a righteous man.
PRO 21:19 It is better to dwell in the wilderness than with a quarrelsome, clamorous and passionate wife.
PRO 21:20 A desirable treasure will rest in the mouth of the wise: but men who are foolish will swallow it.
PRO 21:21 The way of justice and mercy will lead to life and glory.
PRO 21:22 A wise man hath scaled strong cities and demolished fortifications in which the wicked trusted.
PRO 21:23 He who guardeth his mouth and tongue keepeth his soul from trouble.
PRO 21:24 He who is bold, selfwilled and boastful is called loimos [a pest;] and he who harboureth mischief is called a transgressor.
PRO 21:25 Wishing killeth the slothful; for his hands do not chuse to labour.
PRO 21:26 All the day long a wicked man indulgeth wicked desires; but the righteous unsparingly exerciseth pity and compassion.
PRO 21:27 The sacrifices of the wicked are an abomination to the Lord; because they offer them unrighteously.
PRO 21:28 A false witness shall perish; but a man who is a witness will speak guardedly.
PRO 21:29 A wicked man impudently hardeneth his face: but the upright will himself consider his ways.
PRO 21:30 There is no wisdom, there is no fortitude, no counsel in the wicked.
PRO 21:31 A horse is provided for the day of battle: but help cometh from the Lord.

PRO 22:6 [Omitted]
PRO 22:7 The rich rule over the poor; though servants lend to their own masters.
PRO 22:8 He who soweth iniquity shall reap evils; and compleat the punishment of his deeds. God blesseth a cheerful giver; and will supply the deficiency of his works.
PRO 22:9 He who compassionateth the poor shall be fed; for he gave of his own bread to the poor. He who giveth gifts secureth victory and honour. He indeed taketh away the soul of the receivers.
PRO 22:10 Expel from council an overbearing man; and contention will go out with him: for if he sitteth in council he dishonoureth all.
PRO 22:11 The Lord loveth holy hearts; and all the unspotted are acceptable to him. A king feedeth with his lips;
PRO 22:12 but the eyes of the Lord diligently watch the sentiment: and a transgressing word setteth it at naught.
PRO 22:13 A slothful man maketh excuse and saith, There is a lion in the highways and murderers in the streets.
PRO 22:14 The mouth of a transgressor is a deep ditch; and he who is hated of the Lord shall fall into it. There are bad ways before a man and he loveth not to avoid them: but he ought to avoid a crooked and bad way.
PRO 22:15 Folly is bound up in the heart of a child: but a rod and instruction will drive it from him.
PRO 22:16 Some plunder the poor to increase their wealth and give to the rich to lessen it.
PRO 22:17 Incline thine ear to the words of the wise; and hear my discourse and apply thy heart;
PRO 22:18 that thou mayst know that they are good. If thou indeed wilt lay them up in thy heart; they will give thee delight and be on thy lips.
PRO 22:19 In order that thy hope may be upon the Lord; and that he may make known to thee thy way.
PRO 22:20 Write thou them for thyself three times over; for counsel and knowledge, on the table of thy heart.
PRO 22:21 For this purpose I teach thee sound doctrine and knowledge good to be listened to: that thou mayst answer them who propound to thee words of truth.
PRO 22:22 Oppress not the needy because he is poor: nor treat with disrespect at the gates one who is weak.
PRO 22:23 For the Lord will judge his cause; and thou shouldst preserve thy life safe and secure.
PRO 22:24 Have no fellowship with a man addicted to wrath; nor lodge with a friend who is passionate:
PRO 22:25 lest thou learn his ways and lay a snare for thine own life.
PRO 22:26 Do not out of respect for a person become surety.
PRO 22:27 For if thou hast not wherewithal to pay, thy bed will be taken from under thee.
PRO 22:28 Remove not ancient boundaries which thy fathers have set.
PRO 22:29 A man clear in his perceptions and quick in the despatch of business should stand before kings and not wait on slothful men.
PRO 23:1 When thou sittest down to eat at the table of a ruler; observe diligently what are set before thee:
PRO 23:2 and put to thy hand, knowing that thou must provide the like. But if thou hast an appetite not easily satisfied;
PRO 23:3 desire not his dainties; for they give false life.
PRO 23:4 If thou art poor, enter not into competition with one who is rich: but be restrained by thine own prudence
PRO 23:5 If thou fix thy view toward him, he is out of sight: for he is provided with wings as of an eagle; and directeth his course to the house of one who is before him.
PRO 23:6 Eat not with an envious man, nor desire his meats:
PRO 23:7 for he eateth and drinketh as one swallowing a hair. Neither invite him to thy house, nor eat thy morsel with him:
PRO 23:8 for it will cause him to vomit and he will blame thy kind invitations.
PRO 23:9 Make no addresses to a man void of understanding: lest he peradventure mock thy judicious discourse.
PRO 23:10 Remove not ancient land marks, nor encroach upon the possession of the fatherless.
PRO 23:11 For the Lord who is their redeemer is strong; and will plead their cause with thee.
PRO 23:12 Apply thy heart to instruction; and prepare thine ears for the words of knowledge.
PRO 23:13 Refrain not from correcting a child: for if thou beat him with a rod, thou mayst prevent his death.
PRO 23:14 For thou wilt beat him with a rod and deliver his soul from death.
PRO 23:15 My son, if thy heart be wise, thou wilt gladden my heart.
PRO 23:16 And thy lips, if they be right, will hold long conversation with mine.
PRO 23:17 Let not thy heart envy sinners: but be thou in the fear of the Lord all the day long.
PRO 23:18 If thou indeed keep these instructions: they will be a progeny to thee and thy hope shall not perish.
PRO 23:19 Hear, my son and be wise and direct the thoughts of thy heart aright.
PRO 23:20 Be not a wine bibber, nor devoted to clubs: and to the purchasing of flesh meat.
PRO 23:21 For every one addicted to revelling and stews shall come to beggary: and every one given to sleep shall be clothed with rags and tatters.
PRO 23:22 Hearken, my son, to the father who begot thee: and despise not thy mother because she is old.
PRO 23:23 [Omitted]
PRO 23:24 A righteous father nourisheth thee well; and his soul rejoiceth in a wise son.
PRO 23:25 Let thy father and thy mother have joy in thee: and let her who bare thee rejoice.
PRO 23:26 My son, give me thy heart; and let thine eyes observe my ways.
PRO 23:27 For a strange house is a hogshead full of holes: and a strange well is narrow.
PRO 23:28 For that will quickly perish; and every transgressor shall be destroyed.
PRO 23:29 Who hath Woes? Who hath trouble? Who hath law suits? Who hath vexations and squabbles? Who hath Wounds with out cause? Whose are the eyes suffused with blood?
PRO 23:30 Are they not theirs who tarry long at wine; who frequent the places where there are revels? Be not drunk with wine; but converse with righteous men: and converse in the publick walks.
PRO 23:31 For if thou givest thine eyes to cups and goblets; thou wilt go about afterwards naked as a pestle:
PRO 23:32 and be, at last, like one swollen by the bite of a serpent; or as one stung by a basilisk.
PRO 23:33 When thine eyes behold a strange woman; then will thy mouth speak perversely.
PRO 23:34 And thou wilt lie as in the midst of the sea: and like a pilot in a mighty storm.
PRO 23:35 And thou wilt say, They have beaten me and I felt no pain; they insulted me and I was not sensible of it. When will it be day; that I may go and seek with whom I can have a meeting.
PRO 24:1 My son, envy not bad men, nor desire to be with them:
PRO 24:2 for their hearts study falsehood; and their lips utter mischief.
PRO 24:3 By wisdom a house is built; and by understanding it is established.
PRO 24:4 By knowledge chambers are filled with all precious and pleasant riches.
PRO 24:5 Better is a wise man than one who is strong: and the man who hath understanding, than he who hath a large cultivated field.
PRO 24:6 By government war is conducted! and help is the attendant of a heart instructed by counsel.
PRO 24:7 Wisdom and good understanding are in the gates of the wise: the wise turn not away from the commandment of the Lord:
PRO 24:8 but they consult in counsels.
PRO 24:9 Death meeteth the uninstructed and a fool dieth by sins.
PRO 24:10 In a man who is self willed, arrogant and boastful there is impurity: in an evil day and a day of adversity, he will be stained deeper and deeper, until he utterly faint.
PRO 24:11 Deliver them who are to be led away to death; and intercede for them who are to be slain, make no delay.
PRO 24:12 If thou should say, I do not know this man: know that the Lord knoweth the hearts of all: and that he, who gave breath to all, knoweth all things: and will render to every one according to his works.
PRO 24:13 My son, eat honey [for a honey comb is good] that thy palate may be sweetened.
PRO 24:14 In like manner let thy soul taste wisdom; for if thou find it, thy end will be good and hope will not forsake thee.
PRO 24:15 Lead not the wicked to the pasture of the righteous; nor be led astray for a belly full.
PRO 24:16 For a righteous man may fall seven times and rise again; but in calamities the wicked shall be without strength.
PRO 24:17 If thine enemy fall rejoice not over him; nor be elated at his stumbling:
PRO 24:18 for the Lord will see and it will displease him, and he will turn away his wrath.
PRO 24:19 Rejoice not over evil doers nor envy sinners.
PRO 24:20 For the posterity of an evil one cannot continue; and the lamp of the wicked shall be extinguished.
PRO 24:21 My son, fear God and the king and be not disobedient to either of them.
PRO 24:22 For they can suddenly punish the wicked; and their punishments who can know? A son who keepeth the word shall be far from destruction; for he hath received it to effect. Let no falsehood be uttered from the mouth of a king, and from his mouth let no falsehood proceed. The tongue of a king is a sword and not flesh; whoever is delivered up to it shall be destroyed. For if his wrath be sharpened, it consumeth men with thongs, and devoureth the bones of men; or like a flame, burneth them up, so that they cannot be devoured by young eagles. My son, be awed by these words of mine, receive them and reform.
PRO 24:23 But this I say to you who are wise to know, it is not good to respect a person in judgment.
PRO 24:24 He who saith of the wicked, " He is not guilty, " shall be cursed by the tribes and hateful to the nations:
PRO 24:25 but they who reprove shall appear better; and upon them a blessing shall come.
PRO 24:26 Lips will kiss the things which convey good words.
PRO 24:27 Prepare thy works for the time of going out, and be in complete preparation for the field and come after me; then thou shalt build thyself a house.
PRO 24:28 Be not a false witness against thy fellow citizen, nor give a loose to thy lips.
PRO 24:29 Do not say, "I will use him as he hath used me; and punish him for the injuries he hath done me."
PRO 24:30 A fool is like a field, and a man void of understanding, like a vineyard;
PRO 24:31 if thou lettest them alone, they will be overrun with weeds and grass, and become useless, and their stone fences will be thrown down.
PRO 24:32 I have at length repented and looked about, with a view to chuse instruction.
PRO 24:33 I am dozing a little: just taking a short nap; just infolding my breast with my hands.
PRO 24:34 If such indeed be thy conduct; poverty will come upon thee like a traveller and want like a swift courier.
PRO 25:1 These are the detached instructions of Solomon which the friends of Hezekias king of Judea copied out.
PRO 25:2 The glory of God obscureth a matter: but the glory of a king giveth a lustre to actions.
PRO 25:3 Heaven is high and the earth is deep: and the heart of a king is unsearchable.
PRO 25:4 Beat drossy silver and all that is pure will be purified.
PRO 25:5 Slay the wicked from the presence of a king and his throne will be established in righteousness.
PRO 25:6 Boast not in the presence of a king; nor range thyself in the places of princes:
PRO 25:7 For it is better it should be said to thee; "Come up hither;" than that thou shouldst give place at the presence of a prince. Tell what thine eyes have seen.
PRO 25:8 Enter not hastily into a quarrel: lest thou repent at the last when thy friend shall upbraid thee.
PRO 25:9 In yielding shew no contempt,
PRO 25:10 lest thy friend upbraid thee: in which case thy quarrel and enmity will not cease, but last till death. Favour and friendship give freedom. Keep these for thyself that thou mayst not be exposed to reproach. But keep thy ways with a placable temper.
PRO 25:11 It is an apple of gold in a sardine bracelet, thus to speak a word.
PRO 25:12 A precious sardius is bound to an ear-ring of gold; and a word of wisdom to an obedient ear.
PRO 25:13 As the coming out of snow in harvest is grateful according to the degree of heat: so is a faithful messenger to them who send him: for he refresheth the souls of them who employ him.
PRO 25:14 As winds and clouds and rain are conspicuous things; so is he who boasteth for a false gift.
PRO 25:15 By patience kings have a prosperous journey: and a soft tongue breaketh bones.
PRO 25:16 Having found honey eat just what is sufficient: lest being glutted thou vomit it up.
PRO 25:17 Go seldom to the house of thy friend: lest he be cloyed with thee and hate thee.
PRO 25:18 Sharp is a nail and a sword and an arrow: so is a man who beareth false witness against his friend.
PRO 25:19 The way of a bad man and the foot of a transgressor shall be destroyed in an evil day.
PRO 25:20 As vinegar is hurtful to a boil; so bodily disease giveth pain to the heart. As a moth in a garment and a Worm in wood: so a man's grief hurteth the heart.
PRO 25:21 If thine enemy hunger feed him; if he be thirsty give him drink:
PRO 25:22 for by doing this thou wilt use the means to melt him; and the Lord will reward thee with good.
PRO 25:23 The north wind raiseth clouds: and an impudent countenance irritateth the tongue.
PRO 25:24 It is better to dwell in a corner of the house top, than with a scolding wife in a wide house.
PRO 25:25 As cold water is grateful to a thirsty soul; so is good news from a distant country.
PRO 25:26 As if one should stop up a fountain and destroy an outlet of water: so is it disorderly for a righteous man to fall before the wicked.
PRO 25:27 It is not good to eat too much honey: but we ought to honour glorious words.
PRO 25:28 A man who doth any thing without counsel; is like a city which hath the foundations of walls laid and is without walls.
PRO 26:1 As dew at the ingathering of fruit and as rain in harvest: so is honour for a fool.
PRO 26:2 As birds and ostriches fly away; so a vain curse will not light on any one.
PRO 26:3 As a whip for a horse and a goad for an ass; so is a scourge for a sinful nation.
PRO 26:4 Answer not a fool conformably to his folly; let thou become like him.
PRO 26:5 But answer a fool according to his folly; that he may not think himself wise.
PRO 26:6 He who sendeth a message by a foolish messenger; by his own ways procureth disgrace.
PRO 26:7 As well take walking from the legs; as transgression from the mouth of fools.
PRO 26:8 He who bindeth a stone in a sling is like him who giveth honour to a fool.
PRO 26:9 Thorns stick in the hands of a drunken man; and slavery in the hand of fools.
PRO 26:10 All the flesh of fools is in a tempest: for their soundest sleep is broken.
PRO 26:11 As a dog becometh odious when he returneth to his vomit; so is a fool for his wickedness, when he returneth to his sin. There is a shame which leadeth to sin: and a shame which procureth glory and honour.
PRO 26:12 I have seen a man who thought himself wise: but there was more hope of a fool than of him.
PRO 26:13 A slothful man sent on a journey saith, There is a lion in the way and murderers in the streets.
PRO 26:14 As a door turneth on its hinges so doth a slothful man on his bed.
PRO 26:15 A slothful man having hid his hand in his bosom cannot bring it out to his mouth.
PRO 26:16 A slothful man thinketh himself wiser than him who in plenty carrieth a message.
PRO 26:17 He who meddleth with another's strife, is like one who taketh a dog by the tail.
PRO 26:18 As they who undertake to cure throw out words for men; and he who falleth in with the proposal will be first supplanted;
PRO 26:19 so all who ensnare their friends, when they are found out say, "I did it in sport."
PRO 26:20 By much fuel a fire is nourished: but where there is no stirrer up of quarrels, contention ceaseth.
PRO 26:21 A hearth is for coals and fuel for fire: and a contentious man for the bustle of strife.
PRO 26:22 The words of the crafty are soft: but they pierce the inmost recesses of the soul.
PRO 26:23 Silver given with deceit, should be accounted as a potsherd. Smooth lips disguise a wicked heart.
PRO 26:24 A weeping enemy assenteth to every thing with his lips: but in his heart he contriveth deceit.
PRO 26:25 Though an enemy intreat thee with a loud voice, believe him not: for in his heart there is seven fold wickedness.
PRO 26:26 He who concealeth enmity practiseth deceit; but being found out he discloseth his sins in publick assemblies.
PRO 26:27 May he who diggeth a pit for his neighbour fall into it; and he who rolleth a stone, roll it on himself.
PRO 26:28 A lying tongue hateth truth; and a flattering mouth Worketh ruin.
PRO 27:1 Boast not of things of tomorrow; for thou knowest not what the coming day will bring forth.
PRO 27:2 Let a neighbour praise thee and not thine own mouth; a stranger and not thine own lips.
PRO 27:3 A stone is heavy and sand is weighty; but a fool's anger is heavier than both.
PRO 27:4 Wrath is cruel and anger outrageous: but nothing can withstand envy.
PRO 27:5 Open rebukes are better than concealed love.
PRO 27:6 More faithful are the Wounds of a friend; than the feigned kisses of an enemy.
PRO 27:7 A full soul loatheth a honey comb: but to a hungry soul even bitter things are sweet.
PRO 27:8 As a bird when taken hooded from its nest; so is a man reduced to slavery, when removed from his country.
PRO 27:9 With myrrh and wine and perfumes the heart is cheered: but with misfortunes the spirit is broken.
PRO 27:10 Thine own friend and thy father's friend forsake not; but when unfortunate go not to the house of thy brother. Better is a friend near at hand, than a brother far off.
PRO 27:11 Be wise, my son that thy heart may rejoice, and remove from thee reproachful speeches.
PRO 27:12 When ills approach, a prudent man is hidden: but the simple pass on to their sorrow.
PRO 27:13 Take away his mantle, for a scorner passed by who wasteth the property of others.
PRO 27:14 He who blesseth a friend with a loud voice, rising early, will appear not unlike one who curseth him.
PRO 27:15 A continual dropping driveth a man out of his house in a rainy day: and so doth a contentious wife.
PRO 27:16 Boreas is a harsh wind, though it be called by an honourable name.
PRO 27:17 Iron sharpeneth iron, but a man exasperateth the face of a companion.
PRO 27:18 He who planteth a fig tree shall eat of its fruit; and he who guardeth his master shall be honoured.
PRO 27:19 As faces do not resemble faces: so neither do the thoughts of men.
PRO 27:20 The grave and destruction are never satisfied: in like manner the eyes of men are insatiable. He who hath staring eyes, and fools who cannot govern their tongue; are an abomination to the Lord.
PRO 27:21 Fire is the trier of gold and silver: but a man is tried by the mouth of them who praise him. The heart of a transgressor seeketh evils: but a righteous heart seeketh knowledge.
PRO 27:22 Though thou shouldst whip a fool publickly and disgrace him: thou canst not take away his folly.
PRO 27:23 Be careful to know the state of thy flock; and pay close attention to thy herd:
PRO 27:24 for wealth and power do not continue with a man forever; nor can he transmit them from one generation to another.
PRO 27:25 Take care of the herbage in thy field: mow grass and collect provender from the hills:
PRO 27:26 that thou mayst have sheep for clothing. Honour the field that thou mayst have lambs.
PRO 27:27 My son, thou hast sayings from me powerfully conducive to thy life: and the life of thy servants.
PRO 28:1 The wicked fleeth when none pursueth: but the righteous is bold as a lion.
PRO 28:2 Contentions are raised by the sins of the wicked: but a prudent man extinguisheth them.
PRO 28:3 A mighty man by wicked acts oppresseth the poor. As a sweeping rain is indeed unprofitable,
PRO 28:4 so are they who forsake the law and applaud iniquity: but they who love the law encompass themselves with a wall.
PRO 28:5 Bad men will not understand judgment: but they who seek the Lord will be wise in every thing.
PRO 28:6 Better is a poor man who walketh in truth than a rich liar.
PRO 28:7 A wise son keepeth the law; but he who feedeth prodigality dishonoureth his father.
PRO 28:8 He who increaseth his wealth by usury and unjust gain; gathereth it for him who will pity the poor.
PRO 28:9 As for him who turneth away his ear from hearkening to the law; even his prayer is an abomination.
PRO 28:10 He who causeth the righteous to wander in an evil way shall himself fall into destruction. The upright shall have good things in possession: but the unrighteous shall pass by good things and shall not enter into them.
PRO 28:11 A rich man is wise in his own conceit. But a poor man who hath understanding will find him out.
PRO 28:12 For helping the righteous there is great glory: but in the places of the wicked; men are entrapped.
PRO 28:13 He who covereth his wickedness shall not prosper; but he who confesseth and forsaketh will be beloved.
PRO 28:14 Happy the man who piously feareth all things: but he who is of an intractable temper will fall into evils.
PRO 28:15 He who ruleth over a poor nation, himself being poor, is a hungry lion and a ravening wolf.
PRO 28:16 A king straitened in his revenue is a great oppressor: but he who hateth injustice shall live long.
PRO 28:17 He who is bail for a man in a case of murder, shall be a fugitive, but not in safety. Correct a son and he will love thee and be an ornament to thy life. He will not hearken to an unrighteous nation.
PRO 28:18 He who walketh righteously will be helped: but he who walketh in crooked ways will be entangled.
PRO 28:19 He who tilleth his own ground shall have plenty of bread; but he who followeth idleness, shall have plenty of poverty.
PRO 28:20 A faithful man will be much praised; but the wicked shall not escape punishment.
PRO 28:21 He who regardeth not the persons of the righteous, is not good: such a one will deliver up a man for a morsel of bread.
PRO 28:22 An envious man hasteth to be rich, and knoweth not that the bountiful shall have mastery over him.
PRO 28:23 He who reproveth a man's ways shall have more thanks than he who hath a flattering tongue.
PRO 28:24 He who casteth off a father or mother and thinketh that he doth not sin; is indeed the partner of an impious man.
PRO 28:25 A faithless man judgeth rashly: but he who trusteth in the Lord will be careful.
PRO 28:26 He who putteth confidence in the boldness of his heart is a fool: but he who walketh wisely shall be saved.
PRO 28:27 He who giveth to the poor shall not be in want: but he who turneth away his eyes shall be indigent.
PRO 28:28 In the places of the wicked, the righteous groan: but by their destruction, the righteous will be multiplied.
PRO 29:1 Better is a man of experience, than a man who is stiff-necked: for when the latter is suddenly burned, there is no healing him.
PRO 29:2 When the righteous are applauded the people will rejoice: but when the wicked bear rule, men will mourn.
PRO 29:3 When a man loveth wisdom his father is gladdened: but he who feedeth harlots spendeth his substance.
PRO 29:4 A righteous king raiseth a country; but a transgressor overthroweth it.
PRO 29:5 He who shall provide a net to catch his friend; spreadeth it for his own feet.
PRO 29:6 For a mighty transgressor there is a great snare; but the just shall have joy and gladness.
PRO 29:7 A righteous man is skilled in administering justice to the poor: but the wicked doth not take due cognisance: nor hath he a feeling heart for the poor.
PRO 29:8 Men regardless of law, set a city in a flame: but wise men avert wrath.
PRO 29:9 A wise man shall judge nations: but a fool when angry is derided and terrifieth not.
PRO 29:10 Men stained with blood hate one who is holy: but the upright will make strict inquest for his life.
PRO 29:11 A fool sheweth all his wrath; but a wise man dispenseth it gradually.
PRO 29:12 When a king hearkeneth to falsehood, all under him are transgressors.
PRO 29:13 When creditor and debtor meet each other; the Lord hath a watch over both.
PRO 29:14 When a king judgeth the poor faithfully; his throne will be established for a memorial.
PRO 29:15 The rod and reproofs give wisdom: but a child led astray shameth his parents.
PRO 29:16 When the wicked abound, transgressions are multiplied: but when they fall, the righteous are awed.
PRO 29:17 Correct thy son and he will give thee rest; and add honour to thy life.
PRO 29:18 With a sinful nation an instructor can not continue: but he who keepeth the law is most happy.
PRO 29:19 A stubborn servant will not be instructed bywords: for though he may understand he will not obey.
PRO 29:20 If thou seest a man hasty in his words: be assured there is more hope of a fool than of him.
PRO 29:21 He who feedeth delicately from his youth, shall be a servant and at last afflicted with sorrow.
PRO 29:22 A passionate man stirreth up strife: but a furious man is a digger up of sin.
PRO 29:23 A man's pride will bring him low: but the Lord will gloriously support the humble.
PRO 29:24 He who is partner with a thief hateth his own soul: and so do they, who hear an oath administered, if they do not make discovery.
PRO 29:25 They who fear and reverence men have been supplanted: but he whose trust is in the Lord shall be gladdened. Impiety causeth a man to fall: but he who trusteth in the Lord shall be safe.
PRO 29:26 Many court the favour of princes: but justice cometh to a man from the Lord.
PRO 29:27 A righteous man is an abomination to an unjust man: and a straight course is an abomination to a transgressor.
PRO 30:1 Thus saith the man to them who trust in God; but I stop.
PRO 30:2 For I am the most foolish of all men. And I have not the understanding of man in me.
PRO 30:3 God hath taught me wisdom: and I have gained a knowledge of holy things.
PRO 30:4 Who hath ascended up to heaven and come down? Who hath collected the winds in his bosom? Who hath infolded the water in a mantle? Who hath a dominion over all the ends of the earth? What is his name? or what the name of his sons?
PRO 30:5 Since all the words of God are tried, and he is a shield to them who revere him;
PRO 30:6 add not to his words lest he reprove thee and thou be found a liar.
PRO 30:7 two things I beg of thee: deprive me not of favour before I die; remove far from me vanity and lying.
PRO 30:8 Give me neither riches nor poverty, but order for me things necessary and convenient;
PRO 30:9 that when I am filled I may not become false and say, Who seeth me? Or being in want, steal and swear by the name of God.
PRO 30:10 Deliver not up a servant into the hands of a master; lest he curse thee and thou be removed out of sight.
PRO 30:11 A wicked progeny curse their father and bless not their mother.
PRO 30:12 A wicked progeny judge themselves righteous, but have not purged their ways.
PRO 30:13 A wicked progeny have lofty eyes and uplifted eyebrows.
PRO 30:14 A wicked progeny have teeth like swords and grinders like cleavers, so as to consume and devour the poor from the earth, and the needy from among men.
PRO 30:15 The leech had three daughters greatly beloved, but these three did not satisfy her; nay even the fourth did not suffice for her to say, There is enough.
PRO 30:16 The grave, and lust for women, and land unsatiated with water: nay water and fire will never say, There is enough.
PRO 30:17 The eye which derideth a father and despiseth the old age of a mother, may the ravens of the valley pick it out, and the young eagles devour it.
PRO 30:18 There are three things which I cannot perceive, and a fourth which I do not know:
PRO 30:19 the tracks of an eagle in its flying; the footsteps of a serpent on a rock; the marks of a ship crossing the sea; and the ways of a man in youth.
PRO 30:20 Such is the way of an adulterous woman, who having committed the act and washed herself, saith, that she hath done nothing improper.
PRO 30:21 By three things a land is disturbed, and a fourth it cannot bear:
PRO 30:22 a servant when he reigneth; a fool when filled with meat;
PRO 30:23 a handmaid when she expelleth her mistress; and an odious woman when she hath a good husband.
PRO 30:24 There are four things on the earth which are very small, yet they are wiser than the wise:
PRO 30:25 the ants, which not having strength, provide their food in summer;
PRO 30:26 the choirogryllus, which being a feeble nation have built their houses among rocks;
PRO 30:27 the locusts, which having no king encamp regularly at the word of command;
PRO 30:28 and the calabotes, which depending on its feelers and being easily caught maketh its abode in the fortresses of kings.
PRO 30:29 There are three things which march well and a fourth which is stately in its gait;
PRO 30:30 a young lion the strongest of beasts which turneth not aside nor feareth any beast;
PRO 30:31 and a cock strutting magnanimously among his females; and a he-goat marching at the head of a flock; and a king harranguing a nation.
PRO 30:32 If thou sufferest thyself to be elated with joy and engages in battle thou wilt incur disgrace.
PRO 30:33 Churn milk and there will be butter, and if thou wringest the nose, blood will issue forth; so if thou usest provoking language contentions and quarrels will ensue.
PRO 31:1 These words of mine have been dictated by God, they are the prophecy of a king whom his mother instructed
PRO 31:2 What wilt thou keep my son? What! keep the dictates of God. One right of primogeniture I tell thee, my son. What is it thou son of my womb? What is it thou son of my vows?
PRO 31:3 Give not thy wealth to women; nor thine understanding and thy life for that which will bring sorrow. Do all things with counsel. Drink wine with counsel.
PRO 31:4 Princes are passionate, therefore let them not drink wine,
PRO 31:5 lest by drinking they forget wisdom, and become incapable of administering justice to the oppressed.
PRO 31:6 Give strong drink to those in trouble, and wine to be drunk by them who are in sorrow;
PRO 31:7 that they may forget their distress and no more remember their troubles.
PRO 31:8 Open thy mouth with the word of God, and administer justice to all with a sound understanding.
PRO 31:9 Open thy mouth and judge righteously, and plead the cause of the weak and needy.
PRO 31:10 Who can find a virtuous woman? Such a one is indeed more valuable than precious stones.
PRO 31:11 The heart of her husband trusteth in her: such a one hath no need of spoils:
PRO 31:12 for she laboureth for her husband's good all her life long.
PRO 31:13 Having spun wool and flax she made a useful work with her hands.
PRO 31:14 She was like a merchant vessel which bringeth riches from afar:
PRO 31:15 She arose by night and gave food to her household and work to her maids.
PRO 31:16 Having viewed a field she bought it, and with the fruits of her hands planted the purchase.
PRO 31:17 Having girded herself tight about the waist, she strengthened her arms for work.
PRO 31:18 And finding that it was good to work, her lamp is not extinguished the whole night.
PRO 31:19 Her elbows she extendeth over the spindle; and her hands she keepeth at the distaff.
PRO 31:20 But she opened her hand to the needy; and stretched out her handful to the distressed.
PRO 31:21 Her husband when long abroad is not concerned for those at home: for all with her are well clothed.
PRO 31:22 She made for her husband double garments; and for herself robes of cotton and purple.
PRO 31:23 And her husband is distinguished in the gates; when he sitteth in council with the elders of the land.
PRO 31:24 She made sindons and sold girdles to the Chananites. She opened her mouth sparingly and with propriety; and had her tongue in due subjection.
PRO 31:25 She clothed herself with majesty and excellence, and enjoyed delights in her latter days.
PRO 31:26 The gates of her house were kept close shut; and she eateth not the bread of idleness.
PRO 31:27 She openeth her mouth with wisdom, and maxims of prudence.
PRO 31:28 Her bounty caused her children to honour her; for they were rich, and her husband praised her.
PRO 31:29 Many daughters have possessed wealth, many have acted virtuously: but thou hast surpassed: thou hast excelled all.
PRO 31:30 False are allurements, and vain the beauty of a wife. For a woman of understanding is blessed. Let her therefore praise the fear of the Lord.
PRO 31:31 Give her of the fruits of her hands; and let her husband be praised in the gates.
ECC 1:1 The words of the preacher the son of David, king of Israel in Jerusalem.
ECC 1:2 Vanity of vanities, said the preacher. Vanity of vanities. All is vanity.
ECC 1:3 What lasting advantage hath a man by all the labour with which he toileth under the sun?
ECC 1:4 One generation passeth away and another cometh. But the earth hath continually kept its station.
ECC 1:5 The sun riseth and the sun setteth and cometh round to his place.
ECC 1:6 Rising there he marcheth southward, then wheeleth about to the north. The wind wheeleth in circuits, and in its circuits it returneth.
ECC 1:7 All the rivers run into the sea, yet the sea is not filled. To the place whence the rivers come, thither they return to continue their course.
ECC 1:8 All these considerations are wearisome. Man cannot recount them: nor can the eye be satisfied with seeing; nor the ear filled with hearing.
ECC 1:9 What is that which hath been? The very same which shall be. And what is that which hath been done? The very same which shall be done: for there is nothing entirely new under the sun.
ECC 1:10 Who can speak and say, Behold this is entirely new. It hath been already in the ages past which were before us.
ECC 1:11 There is no remembrance of former things: and of those things which shall happen hereafter, there will be no remembrance among them who shall be born at a remote period.
ECC 1:12 I the preacher was king over Israel in Jerusalem;
ECC 1:13 and I applied my heart to seek and make diligent search by wisdom concerning all the things which are done on the earth. Because God hath assigned to the sons of men painful employment, that they may be kept employed,
ECC 1:14 I took a view of all the different sorts of work which are done under the sun. And behold they are all vanity and vexation of spirit.
ECC 1:15 That which is crooked cannot be made straight, nor can wants be numbered.
ECC 1:16 I communed with my heart, saying, Behold I am become great and have made advances in wisdom above all who were before me in Jerusalem. And I have applied my mind to know wisdom and knowledge.
ECC 1:17 And my mind hath taken a view of many things; of wisdom and knowledge; of parables and science. I have found by experience that this also is indeed vexation of spirit.
ECC 1:18 Because by much wisdom there is much knowledge; and he who addeth to his knowledge will add to his sorrow;
ECC 2:1 I said in my heart, Come now let me try thee with pleasure. Take a view of that considered as a good. But behold this also is vanity.
ECC 2:2 To laughter I said, It is madness; and to mirth, What is this thou art doing?
ECC 2:3 Now I had examined whether my mind could lead my flesh to wine; and my mind had led it with wisdom, retaining a command over pleasure, until I should see of what sort that good is, which the sons of men are to pursue under the sun, all the days of their life.
ECC 2:4 I enlarged my plan of operations. I built me houses. I planted me vineyards.
ECC 2:5 I made me gardens and orchards and planted therein all sorts of fruit trees.
ECC 2:6 I made me pools of water, to water from them my blooming nurseries.
ECC 2:7 I purchased men servants and maid servants; and had servants born in my family. And my stock of herds and flocks was great above all who were before me in Jerusalem.
ECC 2:8 I collected also for myself silver and gold and the choicest treasures of kings and countries. I got me men singers and women singers, and the delights of the sons of men; a butler and the requisites to entertainments.
ECC 2:9 And I was great and surpassed all who had been before me in Jerusalem; and still my wisdom continued with me.
ECC 2:10 And whatever mine eyes desired I withheld not from them, nor did I restrain my heart from all my pleasure. Because my heart had been gladdened with all my labour, [now this was my portion from all my labour]
ECC 2:11 therefore I looked back on all the works which my hands had done, and on the labour with which I had toiled to execute them; and behold all was vanity and vexation of spirit and there is no lasting advantage under the sun.
ECC 2:12 Then I looked back to take a view of wisdom and madness and folly. In all the particulars which formed this deliberation [for who is the man equal to a compleat investigation]
ECC 2:13 I saw indeed that there is an advantage in wisdom above folly, like the advantage of light above darkness.
ECC 2:14 The wise man's eyes are in his head; but the fool walketh in darkness. Nevertheless I knew that one event will happen to them all.
ECC 2:15 Therefore I said in my heart, As the same event will happen to me as happeneth to the fool, why have I studied wisdom? Why communed abundantly with my heart? Because even this is vanity; [since out of an abundance the fool speaketh]
ECC 2:16 because there is no remembrance forever of the wise man more than of the fool [seeing the days are now coming when all shall be for gotten and the wise must die as well as the fool]
ECC 2:17 therefore I hated the whole of this life; because the work which was done under the sun was toilsome to me; because all are vanity and vexation of spirit:
ECC 2:18 and I hated all this labour of mine for which I am toiling under the sun; because I must leave it to a man who is coming after me;
ECC 2:19 and who knoweth whether he shall be a wise man or a fool? Now if he hath power over all my labour for which I have toiled and in which I have displayed wisdom under the sun; surely this is vanity.
ECC 2:20 Then I turned about that my heart might state distinctly in every labour of mine in which I had toiled under the sun;
ECC 2:21 that here is a man whose labour hath been with wisdom and with knowledge, and with ability; and there is a man to whom, though he did not labour fur him, he shall give his portion. Surely this is vanity and a great vexation;
ECC 2:22 That such is the case with another man by all his labours and the vexation of his heart with which he toileth under the sun,
ECC 2:23 that all his days are days of sorrow and his employment grief, and even at night his heart hath no rest. Surely this is vanity.
ECC 2:24 [a] Hath not a man something good which he can eat and drink and which he can point out to his soul as a good by his labour? [b] With respect to that I saw indeed that even this is from the hand of God;
ECC 2:25 for who can eat or who can drink without him?
ECC 2:26 For to the man who is good in his sight he hath given wisdom and knowledge and joy; and to the sinner he hath given the trouble of gathering and heaping up to give to him who is good in the sight of God. So that this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
ECC 3:1 Time is for all things: but there is a particular portion of time for every particular affair under heaven;
ECC 3:2 a time to be born and a time to die; a time to plant and a time to root up what was planted;
ECC 3:3 a time to kill and a time to heal; a time to pull down and a time to build up;
ECC 3:4 a time to weep and a time to laugh; a time to mourn and a time to dance;
ECC 3:5 a time to cast away stones and a time to gather stones together; a time to embrace and a time to refrain from embracing;
ECC 3:6 a time to seek and a time to lose; a time to keep and a time to throw away;
ECC 3:7 a time to rend and a time to sew; a time to be silent and a time to speak;
ECC 3:8 a time to love and a time to hate; a time of war and a time of peace.
ECC 3:9 What is the lasting advantage of the agent from the things in which he laboureth?
ECC 3:10 I have taken a collective view of all the business which God hath assigned to the sons of men to be exercised therewith.
ECC 3:11 All the things which he made, considered as a whole, are good in his time. But with regard to all things considered as one whole, to them he hath assigned the whole age; so that no man can find out the work which God hath done from beginning to end.
ECC 3:12 I have found that there is no good in them
ECC 3:13 [I mean in regard to every man who eateth and drinketh, and can see good in all his labour] if there is not a gift of God that he may be made glad and do good in his life.
ECC 3:14 I have found that all the things which God hath made shall continue their age; there is no adding to it nor taking from it; and that God hath acted that they may be awed at his presence.
ECC 3:15 What hath been is now; and what are to be have already been; and God will find out him who is persecuted:
ECC 3:16 and yet I saw under the sun a place of judgment; was the [[a] an objection, [b] the answer.] wicked there? and a place for the just; was the pious there?
ECC 3:17 Then I said in my heart God will judge the whole class of the righteous, and the whole class of the wicked. For there is a time for every thing; and he is there over all the work.
ECC 3:18 I communed with my heart concerning a saying of the sons of men, "That God distinguisheth them." Now in order to shew that they themselves are beasts,
ECC 3:19 that at least which befalleth man, befalleth them; and that which befalleth the beast befalleth man. The same event happeneth to both. As the one dieth, so doth the other. And they have all one breath. What advantage then hath man over the beast? None: for all are vanity.
ECC 3:20 They are all for one place. They were all from dust: and to dust they shall all return.
ECC 3:21 And who hath seen the breath of the sons of men whether it ascendeth upwards; and the breath of the beast, whether it descendeth downwards into the earth?
ECC 3:22 So I saw that there is nothing good in the works of man, but that by which he can be made glad; for that is his portion, for who will bring him to see what will be after him?
ECC 4:1 Then I turned and took a view of all the different sorts of oppression under the sun; and behold the tear of the oppressed and they have no comforter. Though from the hand of oppressors some have relief; yet others have no comforter.
ECC 4:2 Therefore I praised the whole body of the dead; those who were already dead, above the living; those who are still alive:
ECC 4:3 but better than both is he who hath never been; who hath not seen all the evil work which is done under the sun.
ECC 4:4 In the review of labour in general, I took a view in particular of manly exertion in executing. Because this causeth a man to be envied by his neighbour, this therefore is vanity and vexation of spirit.
ECC 4:5 The fool folded his hands and devouring his flesh said,
ECC 4:6 "Better is one handful of rest than two handfuls of labour and vexation of spirit."
ECC 4:7 Then I turned and took a view of a vanity under the sun;
ECC 4:8 Here is a single individual who hath no second; at least he hath neither son nor brother, yet there is no end to all his labour. His eye is not satisfied with riches, yet doth he say, For whom do I labour and deprive my soul of good? Surely this is vanity and a sore vexation.
ECC 4:9 two are better than one. They have a better reward for their labour.
ECC 4:10 For if they chance to fall the one can raise up his fellow. But alas for him who is alone, when he falleth and hath not another to raise him up.
ECC 4:11 Again if two lie together they have warmth: but how can one be warm who is alone?
ECC 4:12 Again though one should be strong the two may withstand him, and a three fold cord cannot easily be broken.
ECC 4:13 Better is a poor and wise subject than an old and foolish king who hath not yet learned how to conduct himself;
ECC 4:14 for out of prison he may come to reign. Because even in his own kingdom he was needy,
ECC 4:15 I took a view of the whole body of the living who were walking under the sun with the youth second in rank who is to succeed him.
ECC 4:16 There is no end of all the people; of all who resorted to them. Yet they who come last will have no joy in him. Surely this also is vanity and vexation of spirit.
ECC 5:1 Keep thy foot when thou goest to the house of God, and let thy sacrifice be a readiness to hear rather than the oblation of fools. Because they are not sensible that they do amiss,
ECC 5:2 be thou not rash with thy mouth; nor let thy heart be hasty to utter a word in the presence of God. Because God is in the heaven above, and thou art on the earth, let thy words there fore be few.
ECC 5:3 Because a dream cometh by much temptation, and a fool's voice with many words;
ECC 5:4 when thou vowest a vow to God delay not the performance of it. For in fools there is no fixed will. Pay thou therefore what thou vowest.
ECC 5:5 It is better not to vow, than to vow and not perform.
ECC 5:6 Suffer not thy mouth to cause thy flesh to sin, nor say in the presence of God, It was an inadvertence, that God may not be provoked to wrath by thy voice, and destroy the works of thy hands,
ECC 5:7 because it was with a multitude of dreams and vanities, and many words that thou fearest God.
ECC 5:8 If thou seest a frivolous accusation of a poor man, and a rigorous exaction of judgment and justice in a country, marvel not at the matter. Because there is a high one over a high one to watch, and high ones are for these things,
ECC 5:9 and the profit of land is for every one, a king is appendant to the cultivated field.
ECC 5:10 A lover of silver cannot be satisfied with silver; but did any one ever love what the abundance of this produceth? Surely this is vanity.
ECC 5:11 By an abundance of wealth they who consume it are multiplied. And what is the mighty advantage of the owner from it? That he hath the first sight of it with his eyes?
ECC 5:12 The sleep of the slave is sweet whether he eateth little or much. But the fulness of the rich suffereth him not to sleep.
ECC 5:13 There is a weakness which I have seen under the sun: riches kept by one for his descendant to his own hurt.
ECC 5:14 Yet these riches acquired with grievous vexation shall perish, and he hath begotten a son, and there is nothing in his hand.
ECC 5:15 As he came naked out of his mother's womb, he shall turn about and go as he came. He shall take nothing by his labour to go with him in his hand.
ECC 5:16 Surely this a grievous weakness; for as he came, so he must depart. What then is his lasting advantage, for which he laboureth in vain;
ECC 5:17 and for which all his days are in darkness and mourning, and much grief and weakness and repining?
ECC 5:18 Behold I have seen a good which is comely, namely to eat and drink, and to have a good enjoyment in all the labour with which one toileth under the sun, the number of the days of his life which God hath given him; for this is his portion.
ECC 5:19 And every man indeed to whom God hath given riches and wealth, and granted him power to eat thereof, and to take his portion, hath by means of his being made glad in his labour, this further gift of God,
ECC 5:20 that he will not much remember the days of his life, because God occupieth him with the joy of his heart.
ECC 6:1 There is an evil which I have seen under the sun, and itis common among men;
ECC 6:2 a man to whom God giveth riches and wealth and glory, so that he wanteth nothing for his soul of all that he can desire; but God granteth him not a power to eat thereof. In as much as a stranger is to devour it, this is vanity and grievous infirmity.
ECC 6:3 Though a man should beget a hundred children and live many years, if during that multitude of years which his days shall continue, his soul shall not be satisfied with an enjoyment of good, and he hath got no burying place, I conclude that an Abortive is better than he.
ECC 6:4 Grant that it came in vanity and goeth away in darkness; with darkness also his name shall be covered!
ECC 6:5 It indeed never saw the light; and he never knew rest: it hath an advantage over him
ECC 6:6 though he had lived the revolutions of a thousand years, if he never enjoyed good. Do not all go to one place?
ECC 6:7 All the labour of a man is for the mouth; yet the appetite will not be satisfied:
ECC 6:8 here then a wise man hath the advantage over a fool; since the poor man knoweth that to pass through life,
ECC 6:9 what he sees with the eyes is better for him than to be wandering after appetite, which is indeed vanity and vexation of spirit.
ECC 6:10 Whatever hath been is now called by its name, and it is known what man is who cannot contend with one who is stronger than he.
ECC 6:11 Since there are many arguments to prove the abundance of vanity; is there any one thing better than another for man?
ECC 6:12 Doth any one know what is good for man in this life? All the days of his life of vanity he hath indeed done these things under a shade; is there any who can tell him what will be after him under the sun?
ECC 7:1 A good name is better than precious oil; and the day of death, than a birth day.
ECC 7:2 It is better to go to a house of mourning than to a house of feasting. As that is the end of every man therefore the living will improve his understanding.
ECC 7:3 Grief is better than laughter; for by a sadness of countenance a heart may be made better.
ECC 7:4 The heart of the wise is in a house of mourning; but the heart of fools, in a house of mirth.
ECC 7:5 It is better for a man to hear the rebuke of the wise, than to listen to the song of fools.
ECC 7:6 Like the crackling of thorns under a pot, so is the laughter of fools. Surely this also is vanity.
ECC 7:7 Because oppression distracteth a wise man and destroyeth his good disposition, the final sentence is better than such a government.
ECC 7:8 Better is a patient man than one of a haughty spirit.
ECC 7:9 Be not apt to be grieved in spirit; for grief will rest in the bosom of fools.
ECC 7:10 Say not, How happened it that the former days were better than these? For thou hast not inquired wisely concerning this.
ECC 7:11 Wisdom is good with an inheritance; and it is an advantage to them who see the sun, that they are in the shade of it.
ECC 7:12 Wisdom is like the shade of money; but the advantage of the knowledge of wisdom is; it will give life to him who is a follower of it.
ECC 7:13 Contemplate the works of God; for who can make him straight whom God hath made crooked.
ECC 7:14 In the days of prosperity enjoy good; but consider in the day of adversity; consider that God hath made the one in due proportion to the other, forming a whole, as hath been said, that man cannot find out any of his ways.
ECC 7:15 In the days of my vanity I took a view of all classes. Here is a righteous man perishing for his righteous act: there a wicked man continuing in his wickedness.
ECC 7:16 Be not over righteous; nor dive too far into wisdom, lest peradventure thou be struck with astonishment.
ECC 7:17 Run not into an excess of wickedness nor become hardened, that thou mayst not die untimely.
ECC 7:18 It is good to restrain thyself in the one case; and surely for the other consideration thou shouldst not pollute thy hand. Because to them who fear God all things may happen,
ECC 7:19 wisdom will help the wise man more than ten mighty men who are in the city.
ECC 7:20 Because there is not a righteous man on earth who will do good and not commit sin,
ECC 7:21 therefore thou shouldst not pay too close attention to all the words which the wicked shall utter, that thou mayst not hear thy servant cursing thee.
ECC 7:22 For many a time he may revile thee and in many ways vex thy heart, because thou perhaps in like manner didst curse others.
ECC 7:23 Having proved all these things by wisdom, I said, Let me investigate the cause. But that was far removed from me; farther than it was.
ECC 7:24 It is indeed a deep depth, who can find it out?
ECC 7:25 I took a circuit with my heart to know and examine carefully and to seek wisdom and a mode of calculating, and to gain a knowledge of a particular folly and disquietude and madness of one destitute of the fear of God; and I find and an declare,
ECC 7:26 That bitterer than death is that whole class of women who are prostitutes. Though their heart is nets and their hands chains, he who is good in the sight of God shall be delivered from them; but a sinner shall be taken by them.
ECC 7:27 Behold this I found [said the preacher]
ECC 7:28 examining them one by one to find a class which my soul earnestly sought, but I did not find: though I found one man of a thousand, yet a woman among all these I did not find: but behold this I found, that
ECC 7:29 God made mankind upright; but they have found out many classes.
ECC 8:1 Doth any one know wise men? Doth any one know the solution of a matter? Wisdom will make his countenance shine; but one of an unblushing countenance will be hated.
ECC 8:2 Watch the mouth of a king, and in regard to the oath of God be not impatient.
ECC 8:3 From his presence thou mayst withdraw. Stay not when he giveth wicked orders; for he will do what he pleaseth,
ECC 8:4 as a king is absolute; and who can say to him, What dost thou?
ECC 8:5 He who keepeth a command will not acknowledge it to be; a wicked order; but a wise man's heart knoweth the time of judgment, that; there is a time and a judgment for everything.
ECC 8:6 Because the man's determination may be much against him;
ECC 8:7 because none knoweth what may happen, who can tell him what may come to pass?
ECC 8:8 No man is absolute commander over wind to stop the current of it, and over the day of death he hath no authority; nor is there a discharge in the day of battle; nor can wickedness save him who is under its sway.
ECC 8:9 Having taken a view of this as a whole, I applied my heart to every work which is done under the sun; to all those things in which man exerciseth authority over man to his hurt.
ECC 8:10 And I then saw wicked men carried to their graves, even out of this holy place; and when they were gone, they were praised in the city, because they had done as they did. Surely this is vanity.
ECC 8:11 Because those who do evil are not speedily called to an account, therefore the heart of the children of men is fully set in them to do evil.
ECC 8:12 He who sinned continued thenceforward to do evil, even because of the forbearance shewn to them. Now as I know that it is good for them who fear God, that they should be awed by his presence;
ECC 8:13 and that it cannot be well with the wicked; and that he who is not awed by the presence of God cannot prolong his days at ease;
ECC 8:14 this which is practised on earth is vanity. Because there are righteous men on whom cometh as it were the work of the wicked; and because there are wicked men on whom cometh, as it were, the work of the righteous, I said that this is also surely vanity;
ECC 8:15 and I praised pleasurable enjoyment, because there is nothing good for men under the sun; nothing save eating and drinking and being made glad; and this one may have conjoined with his labour all the days of his life which God giveth him under the sun.
ECC 8:16 In all those things to which I applied my heart to know wisdom and to take a view of the business which is done on the earth; because day and night this is never at rest,
ECC 8:17 therefore took a view of all the works of God in classes; for man is incapable of finding out the whole system of things under the sun. Let a man labour ever so much in the search he cannot find it out; and let a wise man say ever so much of knowing he cannot find it; for this cause I laid this whole system before my heart, and my heart took a view of it.
ECC 9:1 As the righteous and the wise and their works are in the hand of God, man indeed knoweth not what to love or what to hate: with regard to all things before him there is vanity in them all.
ECC 9:2 The same event happeneth to the righteous and to the wicked; to the good, and to the bad; to the clean and to the unclean; to him who sacrificeth and to him who sacrificeth not: as is the good, so is the sinner; as is he who sweareth, so is he who feareth the oath.
ECC 9:3 There is this evil in every thing done under the sun, that one event happeneth to them all, so that the heart of the children of men being filled with evil there is an instability in their heart during their life, and it followeth them to the dead.
ECC 9:4 Because whoever is in society with all the living hath hope; because the dog which is alive is better than the lion which is dead;
ECC 9:5 because they who are alive must know that they shall die; but the dead are not sensible of any thing and there is no more a portion for them; because the remembrance of these is forgotten,
ECC 9:6 and their love and their hatred and their envy are already perished and they have no more forever a portion in any thing done under the sun;
ECC 9:7 come eat thy bread with cheerfulness, and drink thy wine with a good heart: because God hath approved of thy works,
ECC 9:8 let thy garments be always white; and let not oil be wanting on thy head:
ECC 9:9 enjoy life also with the wife whom thou lovest all the days of thy life of vanity which are given thee under the sun: for this is thy portion in this life of thine, and this thy labour with which thou toilest under the sun.
ECC 9:10 Whatever thy hand findeth to do, do it with all thy might; since there is no work, nor device, nor knowledge nor wisdom in the mansion of the dead to which thou must go.
ECC 9:11 Having turned about, I saw under the sun that the race is not to the swift, nor the battle to the mighty; nay not even bread to the wise, nor riches to men of understanding; nor favour to men of knowledge; that time and chance will happen to them all as forming one whole.
ECC 9:12 That man indeed no more knoweth his time than the fishes which are enclosed in an evil dredge, or than birds which are caught in a net. Like them the sons of men are drawn into an evil time when it cometh upon them suddenly.
ECC 9:13 This also I saw under the sun in regard to wisdom which with me is in high estimation.
ECC 9:14 There was a small city and few men in it. And there came against it a mighty king who besieged it and built great ramparts against it;
ECC 9:15 but he happened to find in it a poor wise beggar, and this man by his wisdom saved the city; yet no man remembered the class of this poor beggar.
ECC 9:16 Now I have said, Wisdom is better than power, yet the wisdom of this poor man is despised and his words are not regarded.
ECC 9:17 The words of wise men in a time of rest are more minded than the shout of men exercising authority in the bustles of folly. Wisdom is better than implements of war. One sinner indeed will destroy much good.
ECC 10:1 Dead flies will spoil the best prepared perfumes: but the smallest portion of wisdom is of more value than the greatest glory of folly.
ECC 10:2 The heart of a wise man is on his right: but the heart of a fool is at his left.
ECC 10:3 In every way at least when a fool is on his march his heart will fail him so that all which he shall devise is folly.
ECC 10:4 If the spirit of a ruler rise up against thee, resign not thy place: for a reconciliation will mollify great offences.
ECC 10:5 There is an evil which I have seen under the sun as if something involuntary came forth from the presence of a person in authority.
ECC 10:6 The fool is set in high stations while the rich shall sit in a low place.
ECC 10:7 I have seen slaves on horseback and princes walking like slaves on the ground.
ECC 10:8 He who diggeth a pit may fall into it; and him, who is clearing away a hedge, a serpent may bite.
ECC 10:9 He who raiseth stones high may be overpowered by them; and he who cleareth wood will thereby incur danger.
ECC 10:10 If the axe shall fall, or one blunteth its edge and redoubled force is to be applied; the advantage will be in favour of the man who hath skill.
ECC 10:11 If a serpent biteth at an interval of charming, there is then no advantage in him who charmeth.
ECC 10:12 The words of a wise man's mouth are a charm; but the lips of a fool will swallow up himself.
ECC 10:13 The beginning of the words of his mouth is folly and the end of his talk is malicious madness.
ECC 10:14 Though the fool multiplieth words, a man doth not know what the matter is; and what that shall be which will follow who can tell him.
ECC 10:15 The labour of the foolish will tire them like that of one who knoweth not the way to a city.
ECC 10:16 Alas for thee, city, whose king is a novice and whose chiefs eat in the morning.
ECC 10:17 Happy thou, land, whose king is a son of freemen and whose chiefs eat in due season for strength: and that they may not be put to shame.
ECC 10:18 By slothfulness the roof will fall, and by idleness of hands a house will become leaky,
ECC 10:19 so as to excite a derision of them who are providing bread and wine and oil that they may be regaled while living. But to the subjection of money all things will be obedient.
ECC 10:20 Therefore curse not a king in thy mind, and in the inmost recesses of thy bed chamber curse not a rich man: for a bird of the air will carry thy voice, and that which hath wings will tell thy saying.
ECC 11:1 Send away thy bread on the face of the water; for after many days thou shalt find it.
ECC 11:2 Give a portion to seven and even to eight; for thou knowest not what evil may be on the earth.
ECC 11:3 When the clouds are filled with rain they empty themselves on the earth: and if a tree falleth, whether it be to the south or north, in the place where it shall fall there it shall be.
ECC 11:4 He who observeth the wind will not sow; and he who looketh at the clouds will not reap.
ECC 11:5 In these cases there is no knowing which way the wind will blow. As thou knowest not how bones are formed in the womb of her who is with child; so thou canst not know the works of God; all that he shall do forming one system.
ECC 11:6 In the morning sow thy seed; and in the evening let not thy hand forbear; for thou knowest not which will succeed, whether this or that; and should both prosper alike, they are good.
ECC 11:7 Light is indeed sweet, and it is grateful to the eyes to view the solar system;
ECC 11:8 yet because, though a man may live many years and be delighted in them all, he will still remember that the days of darkness are many; that all that is coming is vanity;
ECC 11:9 rejoice then, young man, in thy youth, and let thy heart cheer thee in the days of thy youth, and walk in the ways of thy heart spotless and not by the sight of thine eyes, and know that for all these things God will bring thee to judgment.
ECC 11:10 Therefore remove wrath from thy heart and put away evil from thy flesh.
ECC 12:1 Because youth and thoughtlessness is vanity, therefore remember thy Creator in the days of thy youth; before the evil days come and the years draw nigh in which thou shalt say, I have no pleasure in them.
ECC 12:2 So long as the sun and the light and the moon and the stars are not involved in darkness, the clouds will return after rain.
ECC 12:3 When once the guards of the house are shaken, and the men of valour put to flight, and the grinding maids are idle, because reduced to a few, then shall the maids who look out at the windows be darkened,
ECC 12:4 and the doors of the market place will be shut at the feebleness o the voice of the grinding maid, which will be raised to the plaintive tone of the young ostrich; and all the daughters of the song will be brought low;
ECC 12:5 and they will look up to the height and there are terrors in the way. Though the almond tree shall have bloomed and the locust hath been fattened and the caper bush is shed, because the man is gone to his long home, therefore the mourners have made a circuit in the market place.
ECC 12:6 Until the silver cord can be wound up no more, and the golden bowl be broken, and the bucket broken at the well, and the wheel on the well shall run down with it,
ECC 12:7 and dust return to dust as it was, and the spirit return to God who gave it;
ECC 12:8 vanity of vanities, said the preacher; all things are vanity.
ECC 12:9 And moreover, because the preacher was wise, because he taught mankind wisdom; that the ear might find what is comely from parables,
ECC 12:10 the preacher made diligent search to find pleasing words and a writing of rectitude; words of truth.
ECC 12:11 The words of the wise are like goads and nails ready made, which have been laid up in repositories from one shepherd to another.
ECC 12:12 What remaineth of them, my son, keep thou. There is no end of making many books. And much study is a weariness to the flesh.
ECC 12:13 As a conclusion of the discourse, hear thou the whole sum and substance: Fear God and keep his commandments: for this conclusion every man should draw,
ECC 12:14 That God will bring the whole work into judgment in every case not taken notice of, whether it be good or whether it be evil.
SOL 1:1 A Song of Songs which is Solomons.
SOL 1:2 Let him kiss me with the kisses of his mouth. Because thy breasts are better than wine;
SOL 1:3 and the fragrance of thine odours is above all perfumes; Thy name out poured oil, therefore the virgins have loved thee.
SOL 1:4 Thou art drawn: after thee we will run to the fragrance of thy perfumes. The king brought me into his inner apartment. Let us rejoice and be gladdened by thee. We will love thy breasts better than wine: rectitude hath loved thee.
SOL 1:5 I am brown but comely, daughters of Jerusalem; like the tents of Kedar; like the curtains of Solomon.
SOL 1:6 Look not on me, because I am of a dark complexion; Because the sun hath looked upon me. My mother's children quarrelled with me; They made me a keeper in the vineyards. Mine own vineyard I did not watch.
SOL 1:7 Tell me thou whom my soul loveth, where thou tendest thy flock; Where thou causest it to rest at noon, perhaps I may be like a wanderer among the tents of thy companions.
SOL 1:8 If thou wouldst not make thyself known, fairest of women; go out by thyself in the track of the flock; and feed thy kids by the shepherds tents.
SOL 1:9 To that steed of mine in Pharao's chariot I have compared thee, my love!
SOL 1:10 What! thy cheeks are beautiful as a turtle dove's: and thy neck as strings of pearls.
SOL 1:11 We will make for thee suitable figures of gold with spangles of silver.
SOL 1:12 While the king was at his banquet, my spikenard sent forth its odour.
SOL 1:13 My dear brother is to me a nosegay of stacte: it shall be lodged in my bosom.
SOL 1:14 My dear brother is to me a cluster of the cypress, in the vineyards of Engaddi.
SOL 1:15 Behold thou art fair, my love; behold thou art fair. Thine eyes are doves.
SOL 1:16 Behold thou art comely, my dear brother; beautiful indeed! Near our bed thou wast shaded.
SOL 1:17 The beams of our houses are cedar. Cypress our vaulted cielings.
SOL 2:1 I am a flower of the field, and a lilly of the vallies.
SOL 2:2 As a lilly among thorns, so is my consort among the daughters.
SOL 2:3 As the citron tree among the trees of the forests; so is my dear brother among the youths. In its shade I took great delight and sat, and its fruit was sweet to my taste.
SOL 2:4 conduct me to the house of wine, and order for me what I love.
SOL 2:5 Strengthen with perfumes; strew around me citrons, for I am wounded with love.
SOL 2:6 Let his left hand be under my head, and his right embrace me!
SOL 2:7 I have adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem, by the powers and virtues of the field, that you stir not up nor awake my love till she please.
SOL 2:8 It is the voice of my dear brother! lo he cometh, bounding over the mountains; skipping over the hills.
SOL 2:9 My dear brother is like a roe; or a young hart on the mountains of Baithor. Lo! he is behind our wall, looking in at the windows, taking a near view through the lattice.
SOL 2:10 My dear brother addressing me saith, "Arise my love, my fair one, my dove!
SOL 2:11 For lo! the winter is past; the rain is over: is gone.
SOL 2:12 The flowers appear on the earth; the pruning season is come. The voice of the turtle is heard in our land.
SOL 2:13 The fig tree hath put forth its green figs: the vines are in bloom; they have shed a fragrance. Arise, come my beloved, my fair one, my dove.
SOL 2:14 Yes, come thou dove of mine: in the shelter of the rock near the wall Shew me thy face and let me hear thy voice: for thy voice is sweet and thy countenance comely."
SOL 2:15 Catch for us the little foxes; that spoil vines: for our vines are in blossom.
SOL 2:16 My dear brother is mine and I am his: he is feeding among the lillies.
SOL 2:17 Till the day blow fresh and the shades be removed. Return; Be, my dear brother, like a Roe, or a young hart on the caverned mountains.
SOL 3:1 By night on my bed I sought him whom my soul loved. I sought him but did not find him. I called him but he made me no answer.
SOL 3:2 I will rise now and take a circuit in the city; in the places of publick resort and in the streets; and seek him whom my soul loveth. I sought him but did not find him.
SOL 3:3 The watchmen who take their rounds in the city, met me. Saw ye him whom my soul loveth?
SOL 3:4 It was but a little while after I parted from them, till I found him whom my soul loveth. I took hold of him and did not let him go till I brought him to my mother's house and into the chambers of her who conceived me.
SOL 3:5 I charged you, daughters of Jerusalem by the powers and virtues of the field, not to stir up nor awake my love till he please.
SOL 3:6 What is this coming up from the wilderness; like a column of smoke, fuming with myrrh and incense made of all the perfumer's powders?
SOL 3:7 It is the palanquin of Solomon, three score chiefs of the chiefs of Israel are around it.
SOL 3:8 All swordsmen expert in war. Every man with his sword on his thigh, for fear of danger by night.
SOL 3:9 King Solomon had made himself a palanquin of the wood of Libanus.
SOL 3:10 Its columns he made of silver, and his sofa was of gold. Its canopy was purple, and its inside carpeted with love, for the daughters of Jerusalem.
SOL 3:11 daughter of Sion go forth and view king Solomon; in the crown with which his mother crowned him; on the day of his espousals; Even on the day of the gladness of his heart.
SOL 4:1 Behold, thou art fair, my love! Behold thou art fair! Thine eyes are doves, now thy veil is removed! thy hair is like the flocks of goats which are seen from mount Galaad:
SOL 4:2 thy teeth like the flocks of shorn sheep; which have just come up from the washing pool: they are all twins and there is not one defective among them.
SOL 4:3 Thy lips are like a braid of scarlet and thy speech is graceful: as the skin of a pomegranate, so are thy cheeks, now thy veil is removed.
SOL 4:4 Thy neck is like the tower of David, which was built for an armoury: on it are hung a thousand shields; all the javelins of the worthies.
SOL 4:5 Thy two breasts are like two twin fawns of a roe; which are browzing among lillies.
SOL 4:6 Till the day breeze spring up and the shades are removed, I will go by myself to the mountain of myrrh, and to the hill of frankincense.
SOL 4:7 Thou art altogether fair, my love; and there is no blemish in thee.
SOL 4:8 Come from Libanus, my spouse; come from Libanus. Thou canst come, yes come safely from the top of Pistis; from the summit of Sanir and Hermon; from lions dens, from the leopards mountains.
SOL 4:9 Thou hast ravished my heart, my sister spouse: thou hast ravished my heart with a glance of thine eyes; with an endearing turn of thy neck.
SOL 4:10 How beautiful are thy breasts, my sister spouse! how much more pleasing than wine are thy breasts! and the smell of thy garments than all spices!
SOL 4:11 thy lips, my spouse, drop as a honey comb: honey and milk flow from thy tongue: and the fragrance of thy garments is like the smell of Lebanon.
SOL 4:12 Thou art an enclosed garden, my sister spouse: a close shut garden; a sealed fountain.
SOL 4:13 Thy productions are a paradise of pomegranates with delicious fruits; aromatic plants with the varieties of balsams;
SOL 4:14 spikenard and saffron, sweet cane and cinnamon; with all kinds of trees of incense; myrrh, aloes with all the principal spices.
SOL 4:15 A garden fountain and a well of living water, flowing with gentle murmurs from Libanus.
SOL 4:16 Awake north wind, come also, south wind and blow gently through my garden, and let my aromatic spices flow. Let my dear brother come down to his garden; and taste the delicious fruits thereof.
SOL 5:1 I have come to my garden, my sister spouse: I have gathered my myrrh with my spices: I have eaten my bread with my honey; I have drunk my wine with my milk. Eat, friends; drink; yes drink plentifully brethren.
SOL 5:2 . I SLEEP; but my heart is awake. The voice of my dear brother! he knocketh at the door! "Open to me, my sister, my dove, my consecrated one! for my head is filled with dew, and my locks with the drops of the night."
SOL 5:3 I have put off my garment; how can I put it on? I have washed my feet; how can I defile them?
SOL 5:4 My dear brother withdrew his hand from the hole in the door. Whereupon my bowels yearned for him.
SOL 5:5 I rose to open for my dear brother; my hands dropped myrrh; and my fingers myrrh plenteously on the handles of the bar.
SOL 5:6 I opened for my dear brother. He was gone! my soul melted for the speech of him. I sought him but did not find him: I called him but he made me no answer.
SOL 5:7 They who go the rounds in the city met me. They smote me; they wounded me. The keepers of the walls took my veil from me.
SOL 5:8 I adjured you, daughters of Jerusalem by the powers and virtues of the field. If you found my dear brother; What should you tell him; Tell him that I am sick of love.
SOL 5:9 "What is thy dear brother more than another brother, O fairest of women? What is thy dear brother more than another brother, that thou hast thus adjured us?"
SOL 5:10 My dear brother is white and ruddy, he is the chiefest among tens of thousands.
SOL 5:11 His head is gold of Kephas; his flowing locks black as a raven.
SOL 5:12 His eyes are like doves by streams of water; milk white doves sitting by streams.
SOL 5:13 His cheeks are like beds of spices emitting perfumes; his lips are lillies distilling myrrh plenteously.
SOL 5:14 His hands are of gold, finely turned, beset with chrysolites: his body, an ivory cabinet on a sapphire stone:
SOL 5:15 his legs, pillars of marble fixed on pedestals of gold: his countenance like Libanus, majestic as the cedars:
SOL 5:16 his mouth is sweetness itself. He is altogether lovely. Such is my dear brother, and such my love, daughters of Jerusalem.

SOL 6:3 I am my dear brother's and he is mine; he is feeding among the lillies!

SOL 6:10 Who is she that is looking out like the morning; fair as the moon, distinguishable as the sun, and dazzling as embattled hosts."
SOL 6:11 I Went down to the garden of nuts to look at the productions of the valley: to seek whether the vine had budded or the pomegranate blossomed:
SOL 6:12 I am there to grant thee my breasts. My soul did not recollect this. It made me like the chariots of Aminadab.
SOL 6:13 Return, return, Sunamite! return, return that we may see thee! What would you see in the Sunamite, who is coming like the moving bands of an army?

SOL 7:3 thy two breasts are like two twin fawns of a roe

SOL 7:5 thy head is like Carmel and the tresses of thy head like Purpura. The king is detained in the antichamber!

SOL 7:7 In respect to thy stateliness, thou hast been compared to the palm tree, and thy breasts to its clusters.

SOL 7:9 and the roof of thy mouth like choice wine; Which is poured out rightly for my dear brother properly adapted with my lips and my teeth.

SOL 7:11 Come, my dear brother, let us go out to the fields. Let us lodge in the villages:

SOL 7:13 The mandrakes have shed a fragrance: and in our hoards are all manner of delicious fruits, newly gathered as well as old. For thee, my dear brother I have kept them.

SOL 8:3 his left hand might be under my head and his right embrace me.
