ISA 1:1 A vision which Esaias son of Amos saw, [which he saw respecting Judea and Jerusalem] in the reign of Ozias, and Joatham and Achaz and Hezekias, who reigned over Judea.
ISA 1:2 Hearken, heaven! and hear earth! what the Lord hath spoken. "I have begotten children and brought them up; and they have rebelled against me.
ISA 1:3 The ox knoweth his owner, and the ass his master's crib; but Israel did not know me. And this people have not regarded me."
ISA 1:4 Ah! sinful nation; people full of sins! vile race! iniquitous children! you have utterly forsaken the Lord; and provoked to wrath the Holy One of Israel.
ISA 1:5 What! must you persisting in iniquity be smitten still more? The whole head is sick, and the whole heart faint:
ISA 1:6 from the feet to the head, there is no soundness therein. Is it not, here a wound, there a bruise, there a putrefying sore? there is no applying poultice, nor oil, nor bandages.
ISA 1:7 Your land is a desert: your cities are burnt with fire. As for your country, before your eyes strangers are devouring it; and it is laid waste, being subdued by foreign tribes.
ISA 1:8 Must the daughter of Sion be left as a shed in a vineyard: and as a lodge in a garden of cucumbers; as a city taken by siege?
ISA 1:9 Had not the Lord of Hosts left us a seed, we should have been as Sodom and made like Gomorra.
ISA 1:10 Hear a word of the Lord, chiefs of Sodom! Attend to the law of God, ye people of Gomorra!
ISA 1:11 "What is the multitude of your sacrifices to me?" saith the Lord: I am cloyed with whole burnt offerings of rams: in the fat of lambs and the blood of bulls and goats I have no delight;
ISA 1:12 nor should you come to appear before me: for who hath required these at your hands? You shall no more be admitted to tread my court.
ISA 1:13 Though you bring fine flour; it is a vain incense: it is an abomination to me. Your new moons and sabbaths and great day I cannot endure:
ISA 1:14 your fasting and cessation from labour; and your new moons and your festivals my soul hateth. You are become loathsome to me; I will no longer remit your sins.
ISA 1:15 When you stretch forth your hands, I will turn mine eyes from you: and though you multiply prayer, I will not hearken to you: for your hands are full of blood.
ISA 1:16 Wash and become clean: remove iniquities from your souls; in my presence, cease from your evil deeds;
ISA 1:17 learn to do good; seek judgment; deliver him who is injured; administer justice to the orphan, and plead the cause of the widow:
ISA 1:18 then come: [let our controversy be brought to issue, saith the Lord] and though your sins be as a purple stain; I will make you white as snow; though they be as a stain of scarlet; I will make you white as wool.
ISA 1:19 If you indeed be willing and will hearken to me, you shall eat the good things of the land:
ISA 1:20 but if you refuse and hearken not to me, the sword shall devour you; for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken these words."
ISA 1:21 How is the faithful city become a harlot? Sion that was full of justice! In it righteousness made its abode; but now murderers.
ISA 1:22 Your silver is not pure: thy vintners mix the wine with water.
ISA 1:23 The chiefs are rebellious; associates of thieves: they love gifts; they seek rewards: to orphans they do not administer justice; and to the cause of widows they do not attend.
ISA 1:24 Therefore thus saith the sovereign Lord of hosts. "Alas for the rulers of Israel; for my wrath against these adversaries shall not abate. On these enemies of mine I will execute judgment:
ISA 1:25 and I will bring my hand over thee, and purify thee with fire. Them who are disobedient I will destroy; and I will take away from thee all transgressors,
ISA 1:26 and establish thy judges as at the first: and thy counsellors as at the beginning: and after these things thou shalt be called The city of Righteousness, the faithful metropolis, Sion.
ISA 1:27 For in the exercise of judgment her captivity shall be saved: and in the exercise of mercy,
ISA 1:28 the lawless and sinful shall be crushed together; and they who have forsaken the Lord shall be utterly destroyed:
ISA 1:29 for they shall be exposed to shame for the idols on which they doted; as they have been for the gardens which they desired.
ISA 1:30 For they shall be like an ilex, which hath shed its leaves; and like a garden which hath no water:
ISA 1:31 and their strength shall be like tow; and their works like sparks of fire: and the lawless and sinful shall be burned up together; and there shall be no extinguisher."
ISA 2:1 The word which came to Esaias, son of Amos concerning Judea and concerning Jerusalem.
ISA 2:2 Because in the last days, the mount of the Lord will be conspicuous; and the house of God will be on the top of mountains; and exalted above the hills: therefore all the nations will come to it.
ISA 2:3 Many nations indeed, will go saying, "Come, let us go up to the mount of the Lord; and to the house of the God of Jacob. And he will teach us his way, and we will walk therein." For from Sion shall go forth a law; and the word of the Lord from Jerusalem.
ISA 2:4 And he will judge among the nations; and work conviction in many a people: and they shall beat their swords into plough shares; and their spears into pruning hooks: and nation shall not lift up a sword against nation; nor shall they learn war any more.
ISA 2:5 Now therefore, O house of Jacob; come, let us walk in the light of the Lord.
ISA 2:6 For he hath forgiven his people, the house of Israel "Because their land was filled as at first with divinations; like that of the Philistines and many strange children were born to them;
ISA 2:7 for their country was filled with silver and gold, and there was no counting their treasures; and their land was filled with horses, and there was no end to their chariots;
ISA 2:8 and the land was filled with abominations, the workmanship of their own hands; and they worshipped the things which their fingers had made,
ISA 2:9 and the commoner bowed down and the noble humbled himself; therefore I will not forgive them."
ISA 2:10 "Now therefore go into the rocks and hide yourselves in the earth, from the tremendous presence of the Lord; and from the glory of his majesty, when he shall arise, to crush the land."
ISA 2:11 "For the eyes of the Lord are lofty; but man is low; and the loftiness of these men shall be humbled; and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.
ISA 2:12 For the day of the Lord of hosts is against every scorner and haughty man; and against every one high and lofty, and they shall be humbled:
ISA 2:13 even against every of those high towering cedars of Lebanon; and against every oak of Basan;
ISA 2:14 and against every lofty mountain; and against every hill that is high;
ISA 2:15 and against every stately tower; and against every high raised wall;
ISA 2:16 and against every ship of the sea; and against every ensign of beauteous ships:
ISA 2:17 [[J] Jehovah] and every man shall be humbled; and the haughtiness of these men shall fall; and the Lord alone shall be exalted in that day.
ISA 2:18 Then will they hide all these handiworks,
ISA 2:19 carrying them into caverns and clefts of the rocks, and into the caves of the earth, from the tremendous presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his majesty, when he shall arise to crush the lands.
ISA 2:20 For on that day men will cast to the bats their abominations both of silver and gold, which they made to worship vanities;
ISA 2:21 that they may go into holes of the flinty rock: nay into the very clefts of the rock, from the tremendous presence of the Lord, and from the glory of his majesty, when he shall arise to crush the land.
ISA 3:1 Behold now the Sovereign Lord of hosts will remove, from Jerusalem and from Judea, all stay and support of every kind; the stay of bread and the stay of water;
ISA 3:2 the giant and mighty man and warrior; judge and prophet; instructor and elder;
ISA 3:3 the captain of fifty, and honourable counsellor; the skilful architect and intelligent scholar:
ISA 3:4 and I will make boys their princes; and scorners shall rule over them.
ISA 3:5 And upon one another the people will fall foul, and jostle every man against his neighbour; the boy against the elder and the base against the honourable.
ISA 3:6 Because a man will take hold of his brother, or the head of the house of his father, saying, "Thou hast clothing be thou our leader, and let me be supplied with food under thee."
ISA 3:7 Therefore on that day he will answer and say, "I will not be thy leader, for in my house there is neither bread nor raiment, I will not be the leader of this people."
ISA 3:8 Because Jerusalem is forsaken and Judea is fallen therefore their tongues concur with their transgression. They disbelieve the things relating to the Lord.
ISA 3:9 Because their glory is now humbled; and the shame of their countenance is risen up against them: their sin therefore, like the Sodomites, they proclaimed and openly avowed.
ISA 3:10 Alas for their souls! Because they have counselled an evil counsel against themselves, saying, "Let us bind the just one, for he is disagreeable to us;" let them therefore eat the fruits of their deeds.
ISA 3:11 Alas for the wicked! according to the works of his hands evils shall befal him. my people!
ISA 3:12 your task masters glean you; and exactors tyrannize over you. O my people! They who call you happy lead you astray; and disturb the path of your feet.
ISA 3:13 But the Lord will now arise to plead his cause; and he will arraign his people.
ISA 3:14 The Lord will himself come to a trial with the elders of the people and with their chiefs: "Why have you burned up my vineyard? And why is the plunder of the poor in your houses?
ISA 3:15 Why do you injure my people; and cover with shame the face of the poor.
ISA 3:16 Thus saith the Lord, Because the daughters of Sion are haughty and have walked with outstretched neck and wanton eyes, trailing with them in their gait flowing robes, and moving in set pace with their feet;
ISA 3:17 therefore God will humble the princely daughters of Sion and the Lord will expose their form to view.
ISA 3:18 On that day the Lord will take away the finery of their attire, the cauls and the curls and the crescents,
ISA 3:19 the solitaire and the ornament of the brow,
ISA 3:20 and the gorgeous wreathed tiar, and the necklaces and the bracelets, and the zone and the rings for the fingers, and the ornaments for the right arms,
ISA 3:21 and the earrings and the robes with purple borders,
ISA 3:22 and those the middle of which is purple, and the dresses worn at home, and the Laconian gauzes and cotton robes,
ISA 3:23 and those of purple and scarlet and cotton, embroidered with gold and purple; and the summer sofas:
ISA 3:24 and instead of perfumes there shall be ashes; and instead of a girdle thou shalt be girded with rushes; and instead of a golden headdress thou shalt have baldness, on the account of thy doings; and instead of the purple robe thou shalt gird on sackcloth.
ISA 3:25 And thy son the most beautiful whom thou lovest shall fall by the sword; and your mighty men shall fall by the sword and be laid low;
ISA 3:26 and your wardrobes shall mourn; and thou shalt be left solitary and shalt sit on the ground;
ISA 4:1 and seven women shall lay hold on one man, saying, "We will eat our own bread and wear our own raiment, let us only be called by thy name: take thou away our reproach."
ISA 4:2 But in that day God will with glorious counsel shine on the land, to exalt and dignify the remnant of Israel.
ISA 4:3 And it shall come to pass that what is left in Sion, and what is left in Jerusalem shall be called Holy. Namely all who are enrolled for life in Jerusalem.
ISA 4:4 Because the Lord will wash away the filth of the sons and the daughters of Sion, and cleanse the blood entirely from among them; by a spirit of judgment and a spirit of burning;
ISA 4:5 therefore when he shall come, every part of Sion and all around it shall be overshadowed by day with a cloud as of smoke, and by night with that of the light of blazing fire; and with all this glory it shall be covered;
ISA 4:6 and this will be a shade from heat, and it shall be in a shelter and covert from storm and rain."
ISA 5:1 Let me sing for the Beloved, a song of my Beloved to His vineyard. The beloved had a vineyard on a mountain in a rich soil,
ISA 5:2 and I hedged it around and trenched it; and planted it with the vine of Sorek; and in the midst of it built a tower, and hewed out therein a wine lake; and waited for its producing grapes, and it produced poisonous berries.
ISA 5:3 Now therefore, inhabitants of Jerusalem and men of Juda, judge between me and my vineyard.
ISA 5:4 What more could I do for my vineyard that I have not done for it? Because I expected that it would produce grapes, and it hath produced poisonous berries;
ISA 5:5 now therefore I will tell you, what I purpose to do with my vineyard; I take away the hedge thereof, and it shall be exposed to plunder; and I will demolish its wall, and it shall be for a common walk;
ISA 5:6 and I will abandon my vineyard that it may neither be pruned nor digged; and brambles shall overrun it as a waste; and I will give a charge to the clouds not to shed rain upon it.
ISA 5:7 For the vineyard of the Lord of Hosts is the house of Israel; and the men of Juda his beloved plant. I waited for their executing justice, but they committed injustice, and promoted not righteousness, but an outcry.
ISA 5:8 Woe unto them who join house to house, and who are bringing field nearer to field, that they may take something from their neighbour. Are you alone to dwell in the land?
ISA 5:9 For these things have come to the ears of the Lord of Hosts. For though there be many houses they shall be for desolation; though great and fair, there shall be no inhabitants therein.
ISA 5:10 For the ground Worked by ten yoke of oxen will not yield a bath of wine; and he who soweth six measures shall not raise three.
ISA 5:11 Woe to them, who rise early to follow strong drink, and continue at it till late at night; for the wine will inflame them.
ISA 5:12 For with kithara and psaltery, tabors and pipes, they drink wine; but they regard not the works of the Lord, nor consider the operations of his hands.
ISA 5:13 Therefore my people are become captives, because they did not know the Lord; and multitudes have died of famine and thirst;
ISA 5:14 and Hades hath enlarged its appetite, and opened its mouth, that there may be no want of room; and down shall go the honourable and the great, and the rich and the pestilent men of the land.
ISA 5:15 The commoner shall be humbled; and the noble dishonoured; and the lofty eyes shall be brought down;
ISA 5:16 and the Lord of Hosts shall be exalted in judgment; and God, the Holy One, shall be glorified by righteousness;
ISA 5:17 and they who have been plundered shall be fed like bulls, and lambs shall graze the waste places of them who have been removed.
ISA 5:18 Woe unto them who draw out sins as for a long cable: and iniquities as for an ox chain:
ISA 5:19 who say, "Let what he is to do approach speedily that we may see; and let the counsel of the Holy One of Israel come that we may know it."
ISA 5:20 Woe to them who call evil good; and good evil; who put darkness for light, and light for darkness; who put bitter for sweet; and sweet for bitter.
ISA 5:21 Woe to them who are wise in their own conceit, and in their own eyes prudent.
ISA 5:22 Woe to your mighty men who drink wine; and to your princes who mingle strong drink:
ISA 5:23 who justify the wicked for rewards; and deprive the just of his right.
ISA 5:24 For this cause, as stubble will be set on fire by a coal, and consumed by a neglected flame; their root shall be like touch wood, and their blossom shall ascend like dust: for they desired not the law of the Lord of Hosts: but provoked to wrath the manifestion of the Holy One of Israel.
ISA 5:25 Wherefore the Lord of Hosts was incensed against his people, and he stretched out his hand against them and smote them: and the mountains were convulsed, and their carcasses were as dung in the high way: and for all this his anger was not turned away; but still his hand is high.
ISA 5:26 Therefore he will erect a standard among the nations far off, and summon them from the extremity of the earth; and behold! with speed they are coming swiftly.
ISA 5:27 They will not hunger, nor will they be weary: they will not slumber, nor lie down to sleep; nor shall their girdles be loosed from their loins, nor the latchets of their sandals broken.
ISA 5:28 Their arrows are sharp; and their bows are bent: the hoofs of their horses have been accounted as flint, and the wheels of their chariots are like a whirlwind.
ISA 5:29 They growl like lions, and are at hand like young lions. He will seize and roar like a wild beast and drive out the people, and there shall be none to deliver them.
ISA 5:30 On that day he will roar against them like the roaring of the billowy sea; and they will look upwards to the heaven and down on the earth; and lo! distressful darkness in their tribulation.
ISA 6:1 In the year in which Ozias the king died I saw the Lord seated on a high and lofty throne; and the house was filled with his glory.
ISA 6:2 And seraphs stood around him, each having six wings; and with two they covered the face, and with two they covered the feet, and two they used in flying.
ISA 6:3 And they cried one to another and said, "Holy, holy, holy is the Lord of Hosts; the whole earth is filled with his glory."
ISA 6:4 And the lintel of the door was shaken with the sound of their cry, and the house was filled with smoke.
ISA 6:5 Whereupon I said, Ah! Woe is me! [for I was confounded] for being a man, and having unclean lips; and dwelling among a people of unclean lips, I have seen with mine eyes the king the Lord of Hosts.
ISA 6:6 Then one of the seraphs was sent to me and he had in his hand a live coal which he had taken from the altar with the tongs.
ISA 6:7 And having touched my lips he said, Behold this hath touched thy lips, and it will take away thine iniquities and purge away thy sins.
ISA 6:8 Then I heard the voice of the Lord, saying, Whom shall I send? And who will go to this people? And I said, Behold, here am I: send me.
ISA 6:9 And he said, "Go and say to this people; hearing you shall hear, though you may not understand: and seeing you shall see, though you may not perceive:
ISA 6:10 for the heart of this people is stupefied; and their ears are dull of hearing; and they have shut their eyes, that for a while they may not see with their eyes; and hear with their ears; and understand with their hearts; and return that I may heal them.
ISA 6:11 Whereupon I said, For how long? Lord! And he said, Until cities be wasted so as not to be habitable; and houses, so that there be no men; and the land be left utterly desolate:
ISA 6:12 And after this God will remove the men far away. They indeed who are left in the land shall be multiplied;
ISA 6:13 for still about the tenth is in it; and shall again be for a prey, and be like the ilex and like the oak when it hath fallen from its station.
ISA 7:1 In the days of Achaz the son of Joatham, the son of Ozias king of Judah, Rasin king of Aram and Phakee son of Romelias king of Israel came up against Jerusalem to war against it, but could not lay close siege to it.
ISA 7:2 When the house of David was informed that Aram had confederated with Ephraim, the heart of the king and the heart of his people was moved, as a tree in the forest is shaken by the wind.
ISA 7:3 Whereupon the Lord said to Esaias, Go out and meet Achaz, thou and Forsaken-jasub thy son, at the pool on the upper road to the fuller's field,
ISA 7:4 and thou shalt say to him, "Take heed and be quiet; be not terrified, nor let thy soul be dismayed on the account of these two smoaking firebrands: for when my fierce wrath is come I will again heal.
ISA 7:5 And as for the son of Aram and the son of Romelias; because they have taken evil counsel, saying,
ISA 7:6 "Let us go up to Judea and confer with the people and bring them into our measures; and let us make the son of Tabeel king over it,
ISA 7:7 thus saith the Lord of hosts. This counsel shall not stand; nor shall it take effect.
ISA 7:8 But the head of Aram shall be Damascus, and the head of Damascus, Rasin; but further, in three score and five years, the kingdom of Ephraim shall cease from being a people,
ISA 7:9 though Somoron is the head of Ephraim, and the son of Romelias, the head of Somoron, yes though you may not believe nor understand.
ISA 7:10 Moreover the Lord proceeded to speak to Achaz saying,
ISA 7:11 "Ask thee a sign from the Lord thy God in the depth or in the height."
ISA 7:12 And Achaz said, "I will not ask, nor will I try the Lord."
ISA 7:13 Thereupon he said, "Hear now, house of David, Is it a small matter for you to contend with men? How is it then that you contend with the Lord?
ISA 7:14 Therefore the Lord himself will give you a sign. Behold the virgin shall conceive and bear a son, and he shall be called Emmanuel.
ISA 7:15 Both this child, before it hath known to chuse good in preference to evil, eat butter and honey,
ISA 7:16 because previous to its knowing good or evil it disobeyeth evil to make choice of good? The land indeed which thou fearest on account of these two kings shall be relinquished;
ISA 7:17 but God will bring upon thee and upon thy people and upon the house of thy father days which have not yet come. From the day he hath taken Ephraim from Juda [he will bring] the king of the Assyrians.
ISA 7:18 It shall come to pass that at that time the Lord will utter a call to the flies; to that part of them which rule over the river of Egypt; and to the bee which is in the country of the Assyrians;
ISA 7:19 and they shall all come into the vallies of this country; and into the holes of the rocks; and into the caves and into every cleft.
ISA 7:20 On that day the Lord will shave with that razor; with that which was hired on the bank of the river; with that of the king of the Assyrians, the head and the hair of the feet: and take off the beard.
ISA 7:21 And it shall come to pass in that day, that a man will keep a young cow and two sheep;
ISA 7:22 and by reason of the abundance he will drink milk; butter and honey will be eaten by every one left in the land.
ISA 7:23 And it shall come to pass in that day every where, though there may be a thousand vineyards, each valued at a thousand shekels income: they shall be for briars and thorns.
ISA 7:24 With bows and arrows men will resort thither. Because the whole country shall be a waste of briars and thorns,
ISA 7:25 therefore every mountain which hath been ploughed will be ploughed, wherever terror could not come; for by reason of the country's being a waste of briars and thorns, it shall be a pasture for sheep and a range for the ox.
ISA 8:1 Again the Lord said to me, "Take thee a strip of a large new roll and write thereon with a man's pen "Speed quickly to the plunder of the spoil", for it is at hand.
ISA 8:2 And let faithful men Ourias and Zacharias son of Barachias be witnesses for me."
ISA 8:3 Now I had approached to the prophetess and she had conceived and when she brought forth a son, the Lord said to me, "Call his name Speed to the Spoil; haste to the prey"
ISA 8:4 for before this child shall know to pronounce father or mother, the van of the king of Assyria will take the army of Damascus and the spoils of Samaria.
ISA 8:5 Again the Lord spoke yet further to me saying,
ISA 8:6 Because this people reject the water of Siloam which floweth gently and chuse to have Rasin and the son of Romelias to rule over them;
ISA 8:7 therefore behold the Lord will bring upon you the water of the river which is strong and abundant; even the king of Assyria and his glory; and he will rise over all your channels, and over flow all your banks;
ISA 8:8 and sweep away from Judea every man who can raise his head, or is capable of executing any thing. And the circuit of his camp shall be such as to fill the breadth of thy country, Emmanuel.
ISA 8:9 Know this, nations, and be struck with consternation. Hearken ye who are in the remotest parts of the earth; be struck with consternation ye who have made yourselves strong; for though you should again become strong; with consternation you shall again be stricken,
ISA 8:10 and what counsel soever you may take, the Lord will defeat it; and what word soever you may speak shall not take effect among you; because God is with us:
ISA 8:11 Thus saith the Lord with the strong hand, to them who refuse to walk in the way of this people
ISA 8:12 saying, Perhaps they may order what is hard; [for whatever this people order is hard.] Be not ye terrified with the fear of them, nor dismayed;
ISA 8:13 hallow the Lord himself, and let him be thy fear:
ISA 8:14 for if thou hast put trust in him he will be to thee a sanctuary, and you shall not run against a stumbling stone, nor as under a falling rock. But as for the houses of Jacob, they are in a trap, and the inhabitants of Jerusalem are in a pit:
ISA 8:15 for this cause many among them shall be weak and fall and be trodden down and men will safely approach and take them.
ISA 8:16 Then shall they be manifest who seal up the law that it may not be learned. Then will one say, "I will wait for God, who hath turned away his face from the house of Jacob; and I will trust in him.
ISA 8:18 Here am I and the children whom God hath given me." Now when there shall be signs and wonders in the house of Israel from the Lord of hosts, who dwelleth on Mount Sion;
ISA 8:19 if they should say to you, "Apply to the belly speakers, and to them who cause a voice to proceed from the ground. Those vain babblers who speak from the belly: should not a nation apply to their God? Why consult they the dead concerning the living?
ISA 8:20 For he hath given a law for assistance; that they may not speak like such an oracle as this, which is not worth the giving of gifts for it.
ISA 8:21 Upon you indeed there shall come a grievous famine; and it shall come to pass that when you are hungry, you will fret and curse the ruler and the customs of your country. And they will look up to the heaven above,
ISA 8:22 then down on the earth beneath, and lo distress and darkness! tribulation and anguish and a gloom so as not to see!
ISA 9:1 But he who is in distress for a season shall not be abandoned to despair. Drink this first; do it quickly. With regard to the region of Zabulon, the land of Nephthaleim and the rest who inhabit the sea shore, and the banks of the Jordan, Galilee of the nations;
ISA 9:2 ye people who walk in darkness, behold! a great light! and ye who dwell in a region, the shade of death, on you a light shall shine.
ISA 9:3 With regard to the bulk of the people, whom thou hast brought back in thy joy, they shall rejoice in thy presence, like them who rejoice in the harvest, and like them who are dividing spoils;
ISA 9:4 because the yoke which lay upon them, is taken away, and the rod which was over their neck. For he hath broken the rod of the exactor, as in the day of Madiam:
ISA 9:5 for, with a renewal of friendship, they shall make compensation for every robe collected by deceit, and for every garment; and shall be willing to do so, if they were burned with fire:
ISA 9:6 because for us a child is born, and to us a son is given, whose government is on his own shoulder; and his name is called, "The Messenger of Great Counsel." For I will bring peace on the rulers and health for him.
ISA 9:7 His government shall be great and to his peace there is no boundary, on the throne of David and over his kingdom, to reestablish it, and support it with judgment and justice, henceforth and forever. The zeal of the Lord of hosts will do this.
ISA 9:8 THE LORD hath sent death against Jacob; and it hath come upon Israel.
ISA 9:9 And all the people of Ephraim shall know it, and all the inhabitants of Samaria, who with haughtiness and a lofty heart say,
ISA 9:10 "The bricks are fallen; but come, let us hew stones and let us cut down sycamines and cedars and build for ourselves a tower."
ISA 9:11 Though God will dash down them, who rise up against him on mount Sion; and disperse his enemies
ISA 9:12 Syria in the east, and the Greeks in the west, who are devouring Israel with open mouth; for all this his anger is not turned away, but still his hand is lifted high.
ISA 9:13 The people did not turn till they were smitten; as they indeed did not seek the Lord;
ISA 9:14 therefore the Lord cut off from Israel, head and tail, great and little in one day;
ISA 9:15 the aged and the honourable, this was the head; and the prophet who teacheth falsehood, he is the tail.
ISA 9:16 Still there will be deceivers, who will call this people happy, and lead them astray, that they may devour them;
ISA 9:17 therefore the Lord will have no pleasure in their young men; and on their orphans and their widows he will have no compassion; because they are all wicked and regardless of law, and every mouth speaketh perversely. For all this his wrath is not turned away but still his hand is lifted high.
ISA 9:18 Still iniquity will burn like a fire, and like dry stubble it shall be consumed by fire. It shall burn in the thickets of the forest, and consume all on the hills around.
ISA 9:19 By reason of the fierce anger of the Lord the whole country is in a flame; and the people shall be as fuel for the fire. A man will have no pity for his brother,
ISA 9:20 but will turn to the right because he is hungry, and devour on the left, but shall not be satisfied. Man is devouring the flesh of his brother's arm;
ISA 9:21 for Manasses is devouring Ephraim, and Ephraim, Manasses; for they will both together besiege Juda. For all this his anger is not turned away; but still his hand is lifted high.
ISA 10:1 Woe to them who write wickedness! For writers are writing wickedness;
ISA 10:2 turning aside the cause of the distressed; robbing the poor of my people, of their right; that the widow
ISA 10:3 may be their prey and the orphan, their spoil: what then shall they do in the day of visitation? For tribulation shall come upon you from afar; and to whom can you flee for succour? And where will you leave your glory,
ISA 10:4 that you may not fall into the captive band? For all this his anger is not turned away, but still his hand is lifted high.
ISA 10:5 Ho! Assyrians! The rod of my wrath, even mine anger is in their hands,
ISA 10:6 I will send this anger of mine to a lawless nation; and I will order this people of mine to gather spoil and take the prey, and to trample down cities and lay them in the dust.
ISA 10:7 But he did not harbour such thoughts; nor did he reason thus in his mind; but his mind will prompt him to destroy nations not a few.
ISA 10:8 Even though they should say to him, Thou alone art chief.
ISA 10:9 He indeed will say, "Have I not taken the whole country above Babylon and Chalene, where the tower had been builded? Nay have I not taken Arabia and Damascus and Samaria?
ISA 10:10 In the same manner as I have taken these; so will I take all the governments. Howl ye graven images in Jerusalem and in Samaria;
ISA 10:11 for as I have done to Samaria and her images, so will I do to Jerusalem and her idols."
ISA 10:12 But it shall come to pass, when the Lord hath accomplished his whole work on mount Sion and Jerusalem; that I will cast a look on the stout heart; on the chief ruler of the Assyrians, and on the loftiness of the glory of his eyes.
ISA 10:13 For he said, "With this power I will perform exploits; and by the wisdom of mine understanding I will remove the boundaries of nations, and make a prey of their strength,
ISA 10:14 and shake inhabited cities, and seize with my hand the whole World as a nest; and carry off the inhabitants like deserted eggs. There is none who can escape me or chirp against me."
ISA 10:15 Shall an axe boast without him who cutteth with it; or a saw lift itself up, without him who draweth it; as one could lift up a staff or a piece of wood? No; this shall not be permitted:
ISA 10:16 indeed the Lord of hosts will send disgrace on thy honour, and on thy glory a burning fire shall be kindled:
ISA 10:17 and the light of Israel shall be for a fire, and shall hallow him with a burning fire, and consume his substance like dry grass.
ISA 10:18 On that day there shall be an extinction of the mountains, and the hills, and the forests; and it shall consume from the soul even to the flesh: and he who fleeth shall be like one fleeing from blazing fire.
ISA 10:19 And those of them who are left shall be few in number, so that a child may write them down.
ISA 10:20 And it shall come to pass in that day that the remnant of Israel shall no more join, nor shall those of Jacob who have escaped, any more lean on them who have injured them; but they will place their confidence in God the Holy One of Israel, in truth
ISA 10:21 This remnant of Jacob shall indeed be for the Mighty God.
ISA 10:22 Yes: though the people of Israel be as the sand of the sea, this remnant of them shall be saved.
ISA 10:23 He is closing an account and making a deduction with saving goodness. Because with the whole land the Lord will make a reckoning from which a deduction hath been made,
ISA 10:24 therefore thus saith the Lord of Hosts, "O my people who dwell in Sion, be not daunted at the Assyrian, because he will smite thee with a rod; for I am bringing this stroke upon thee that thou mayst see the way of Egypt.
ISA 10:25 For yet a little while and mine indignation shall cease; and my wrath will be against their counsel;"
ISA 10:26 and God will raise against them a scourge similar to that of Madiam at the place of affliction. When his wrath shall be in the western road; in the high way leading to Egypt;
ISA 10:27 it shall come to pass in that day; that his yoke shall be taken from thy shoulder, and the terror of him from thee; his yoke shall be utterly destroyed from off thy shoulders.
ISA 10:28 For he will come to the city Aggai, and pass on to Mageddo; and at Machmas he will deposit his baggage:
ISA 10:29 then he will pass the valley and come to Aggai. Terror will seize Rama the city of Saul;
ISA 10:30 the daughter of Galleim will flee: he will be heard of at Laisa; he will be heard of at Anathoth.
ISA 10:31 When Madebena hath fainted; then, inhabitants of Gibbeir,
ISA 10:32 comfort with the news of his halting a day on his march with the hand comfort the mount, the daughter of Sion. And as for you, hills, which are in Jerusalem,
ISA 10:33 behold the sovereign Lord of hosts, with majesty confoundeth the glorious. They who are elated with arrogance shall be crushed; and the lofty shall be brought low;
ISA 10:34 yes, the lofty shall fall by the sword; and Libanus shall fall with the lofty.

ISA 11:2 and the spirit of God will rest upon him; a spirit of wisdom and understanding; a spirit of counsel and majesty; a spirit of knowledge and piety:
ISA 11:3 by this spirit he will be filled with the fear of God. He will not judge according to opinion, nor will he reprove according to report;
ISA 11:4 but he will administer justice to the lowly, and work conviction in the meek of the earth. And he will smite the earth with the word of his mouth, and with a breath from his lips destroy the wicked.
ISA 11:5 His loins will be girded with saving goodness, and his reins clothed with truth.
ISA 11:6 And a wolf shall pasture with a lamb; and a leopard shall lie down with a kid; and the calf, and bull and lion shall pasture together, and a little child shall tend them.
ISA 11:7 The cow and bear shall feed together; and together their young shall herd; and the lion shall eat chaff like an ox.
ISA 11:8 And the sucking child shall lay its hand on the holes of asps and on the bed of young asps.
ISA 11:9 And they shall not hurt nor have power to destroy any one on the mountain which is my sanctuary. Because the whole earth is filled with the knowledge of the Lord as abundant water covereth depths of seas;
ISA 11:10 therefore there shall be in that day, the root of Jesse, even he who riseth up to rule nations: in him nations will put their trust, and his resting place shall be glorious.
ISA 11:11 And it shall come to pass in that day, that the Lord will proceed to shew his hand to provoke to jealousy the remnant of his people; that residue which is left from the Assyrians and from Egypt and from Babylonia, and from Ethiopia and the Elamites, and from the risings of the sun and Arabia.
ISA 11:12 And he will erect a standard for the nations, and gather together the outcasts of Israel, and assemble the dispersed of Juda from the four quarters of the earth.
ISA 11:13 And the envy of Ephraim shall be taken away; and the enemies of Juda shall be destroyed: Ephraim shall not envy Juda; nor shall Juda vex Ephraim:
ISA 11:14 And they shall be wafted in the ships of foreign tribes; and they shall spoil both the sea and them of the east and Idumea; and upon Moab they shall first lay their hands; but the sons of Ammon shall first obey.
ISA 11:15 And the Lord will dry up the sea of Egypt, and lay his hand on the river with a vehement wind; and smite the seven channels, so that they may be crossed dry shod.
ISA 11:16 And there shall be a passage for my people left in Egypt. It shall be for Israel as on the day when they came up out of the land of Egypt.

ISA 12:2 Behold! my God is my Saviour, I will trust in him and not be afraid. Because the Lord is my glory and my praise; and hath become unto me salvation;

ISA 13:1 A vision which Esaias son of Amos saw respecting Babylon.
ISA 13:2 [J] On a mount in the plain, erect a standard; raise the voice to them; beckon with the hand. Open princes!
ISA 13:3 it is I who command. It is I, who am leading these on. Giants are coming to execute my wrath, rejoicing and at the same time arrogant.
ISA 13:4 [p] A sound of many nations on the mountains! A tumultuous sound of many nations. A sound of kings and nations gathered together! the Lord of hosts hath issued orders to a nation trained for battle.
ISA 13:5 They are come from a far distant country; from the extreme butment of heaven; the Lord and his trained warriors, to destroy all that inhabited land.
ISA 13:6 Raise the mournful cry! for the day of the Lord is at hand, and destruction from God will come:
ISA 13:7 therefore every hand shall be enfeebled; and every man's heart shall be dismayed.
ISA 13:8 The men in power shall be confounded; and pangs shall seize them, like those of a woman in travail. And they shall bewail their calamities, one to another, and be amazed; and their countenances will quiver like a flame.
ISA 13:9 For behold the remediless day of the Lord is coming; a day of wrath and indignation, to make the empire a desolation; and to destroy the sinners out of it.
ISA 13:10 For the stars of heaven; even Orion and the whole host of heaven, shall not give light; even that of the rising sun shall be darkened; and the moon shall not give her light.
ISA 13:11 [[J] Jehovah, [p] the prophet.} [J] I will indeed order evils for the whole empire, and on the wicked their transgressions; and destroy the arrogance of the wicked; and humble the haughtiness of the proud;
ISA 13:12 so that those left shall be more precious than tried gold and a man more precious than the ore of Souphir.
ISA 13:13 For the heaven shall be filled with wrath; and the earth shaken from its foundations; at the fierce anger of the Lord of Hosts, on the day when his wrath shall come:
ISA 13:14 and those left shall be like a chased roe and wandering sheep; and there shall be none to collect them together; so that they may return every man to his place, when every one shall be seeking his own country.
ISA 13:15 For whoever is overtaken shall be thrust through and those collected in a body shall fall by the sword.
ISA 13:16 And their infants shall be dashed to pieces before their eyes; and their houses shall be plundered and their wives ravished.
ISA 13:17 Behold I am raising up against you the Medes, who disregard silver and have no need of gold.
ISA 13:18 They shall break the bows of the young men, and on your infants they will have no compassion; nor will their eyes spare thee for thy children.
ISA 13:19 And Babylon, which is stiled Glorious, by the king of the Chaldeans, shall be as when God overthrew Sodom and Gomorra.
ISA 13:20 It shall not be inhabited for a great length of time, nor shall it be entered for many generations. The Arabians shall not pass through it; nor shall shepherds make their folds therein.
ISA 13:21 But wild beasts shall there go to rest; and the houses shall be filled with howling. There jackals shall make their abode; and there demons shall hold their revels.
ISA 13:22 And onocentaurs shall inhabit there; and porcupines shall breed in the houses. [p] He is coming quickly and will not tarry,
ISA 14:1 but the Lord will have mercy on Jacob, and will still make choice of Israel; and they shall rest in their own land; and the stranger shall be joined to them, and shall be added to the house of Jacob.
ISA 14:2 The nations shall take them and bring them to their place; and the house of Jacob shall possess them; when they shall multiplied in their land, for men servants and for maid servants: and they who captivated them shall be captives; and they who domineered over them shall be brought into subjection.
ISA 14:3 And it shall come to pass in that day when the Lord shall give thee rest from thy sorrow and thy grief; from that hard servitude of thine, with which thou hast served them,
ISA 14:4 that thou wilt take up this funeral song over the king of Babylon: [[c]the chorus] [c] How the extortioner is laid to rest! and a stop put to his demands!
ISA 14:5 The Lord hath broken the yoke of the sinners; the yoke of the rulers.
ISA 14:6 He smote a nation in wrath with an incurable wound; he smote a nation with a vengeful wound which did not spare. The confidant is gone to rest;
ISA 14:7 the whole earth shouteth for joy;
ISA 14:8 and the trees of Lebanon rejoice over thee; and the cedars of Lebanon say, "Since thou hast gone to rest, no feller is come up against us."
ISA 14:9 Hades from beneath was in uproar to meet thee; for thee were roused all the giants who had ruled the earth. Having roused from their thrones all the kings of nations,
ISA 14:10 they will all accost thee saying, "And art thou caught as we have been? And among us art thou enrolled?
ISA 14:11 Is thy pomp come down to Hades; all thy great festivity?" Beneath thee they will strew corruption for a bed; and Worms shall be thy covering.
ISA 14:12 How is Lucifer fallen from heaven! He who was harbinger of the morning; he who sent messages to all the nations is trampled down into the earth.
ISA 14:13 Thou indeed didst say in thy heart, I will ascend up into heaven; above the stars of heaven I will place my throne; I will seat myself on a lofty mountain; on the lofty mountains which face the north.
ISA 14:14 I will ascend above the clouds; I will be like the Most High.
ISA 14:15 But thou must now go down to the mansion of the dead; even down to the foundations of the earth.
ISA 14:16 They who see thee will express their amazement at thee and say, Is this the man who troubled the earth? who shook kings?
ISA 14:17 who made the World a desert? who, when he destroyed cities, never dismissed his captives?
ISA 14:18 All the kings of the nations have been composed to rest with honour, every man in his own house.
ISA 14:19 But thou shalt be cast out on the mountains, like an abominable corse, with dying crouds, pierced with the sword, descending down to the mansion of the dead.
ISA 14:20 As a mantle stained with blood cannot be clean; for the same cause neither canst thou be clean. Because thou hast destroyed this land of mine, and hast slain this my people; thou shalt not be of long continuance. Wicked seed,
ISA 14:21 prepare thy sons for slaughter, for the sins of their fathers; that they may not rise and possess the land, and fill the World with wars.
ISA 14:22 I will indeed rise up against them, saith the Lord of hosts, and destroy their name and remnant and seed. Thus saith the Lord,
ISA 14:23 "I will lay Babylonia waste: that porcupines may inhabit it; and it shall be a desolation. And I will plunge it in the miry gulf of destruction.
ISA 14:24 Thus saith the Lord of hosts, as I have spoken so it shall be; and as I have determined, so it shall stand.
ISA 14:25 I will destroy the Assyrians on this land of mine; and on these mountains of mine they shall be trodden down; and their yoke shall be removed from my people; and their reproach shall be taken from their shoulders.
ISA 14:26 [p] This is the counsel which the Lord hath taken against the whole empire, and this is the hand which is lifted high against all the nations.
ISA 14:27 For who can disannul what the holy God hath decreed? and his hand which is lifted high, who can turn aside?
ISA 14:28 In the year in which king Achaz died, this Oracle was delivered.
ISA 14:29 Rejoice not, foreign tribes, with one consent, because the yoke of him who smote you is broken; for from the seed of a serpent will come forth young asps, and their offspring will be flying serpents.
ISA 14:30 For the needy will be fed by him; and in peace the needy will repose. But with famine he will destroy thy seed; even the remnant of thy seed he will destroy.
ISA 14:31 Raise the mournful cry ye gates of cities; foreign tribes! let harassed cities scream with one consent: for a smoke is coming from the north, which cannot be endured;
ISA 14:32 what then will the kings of nations say in reply? "That the Lord hath founded Sion, and by him the poor of his people shall be saved."
ISA 15:1 The Oracle against Moab. In the night Moab is destroyed; for by night is destroyed the bulwark of Moab.
ISA 15:2 Be in bitterness for yourselves; for Debon also is destroyed. Where your altar is, thither you will go up to weep for Nabau of Moab, Raise the mournful cry. On every head be baldness; let all your arms be gashed with Wounds.
ISA 15:3 In the streets thereof, gird on sackcloth, and on its house tops make lamentation; and in the streets thereof and in its lanes, raise ye all the mournful cry with weeping;
ISA 15:4 because Esebon and Eleale have screamed: even to Jassa their voice hath been heard; therefore the lungs of Moab utter lowings; her soul will be afflicted.
ISA 15:5 The heart of Moab within her uttereth lowings, which reach Segor: for she is a three headed heifer. At the ascent of Louith weepers will come up to thee; by the way of Aroniim destruction and dismay are roaring.
ISA 15:6 The water of Nemereim will be dried up; and its grass will fail; there will be no green grass.
ISA 15:7 But even thus it shall not be saved; for I will bring the Arabs against that valley; and they shall take it.
ISA 15:8 For the cry of war touched the border of Moab at Agaleim, and the scream thereof reacheth even to the well of Aileim.
ISA 15:9 As for the water of Deimon, it shall be full of blood; for I will bring the Arabians against Deimon, and carry off the seed of Moab and Ariel; and the remnant of Adama
ISA 16:1 I will send away as reptiles on the earth. Is Petra a desert? There is the mountain of the daughter of Sion [to fly to]
ISA 16:2 for thou shalt be [like the young of a flown bird carried away] Thou, Moab, shalt be a vassal; and after that there will be a greater tribute of lambs.
ISA 16:3 Take counsel [O Sion] and make for her every where a shelter from grief. In midnight darkness they will flee. They are confounded. Be not thou incensed.
ISA 16:4 Let the fugitives of Moab sojourn with thee. They will be a shelter to you from the face of a pursuer. Because thy share in the war is taken away; and the chief who trampled down is destroyed from this land;
ISA 16:5 therefore a throne shall be established with mercy, and on it one shall be seated with truth; in the tabernacle of David, executing justice, and searching out judgment and promoting righteousness.
ISA 16:6 [s] "We have heard of the haughtiness of Moab; he is very insolent." [J] This haughtiness I have totally removed. "Is not this, is not this the oracle concerning thee?
ISA 16:7 Moab shall raise the mournful cry, for in the country of Moab they shall all utter the cry of Woe, but to them who dwell in the habitations of Seth thou shalt extend care and shalt not be ashamed."
ISA 16:8 The plains of Esebon shall mourn; the vineyard Sebama. Ye who drink up the nations, trample down her vineyards to Jazer. You need not march in close array: roam through the wilderness. They who were dispatched were wholly given up, for they passed through quite to the sea.
ISA 16:9 [p] Let me therefore weep, as with the weeping of Jazer, for the vineyards of Sebama. He hath cut down thy trees, Esebon and Eleale. [J] Because in harvest and at thy vintage I will trample down and all shall be laid prostrate;
ISA 16:10 therefore gladness and the shout of joy shall be taken from the vineyards. And in thy vineyards they shall not rejoice, nor tread out wine in thy cisterns, for a stop is put to the shout of joy.
ISA 16:11 [p] For Moab therefore will my bowels sound like a kithara, and my entrails, as when thou didst consecrate a wall;
ISA 16:12 but it will be for the purpose of making thee ashamed. Because Moab had tired himself at the altars, therefore he will go in to the works of his hands; that they may intercede; but they shall not be able to deliver him.
ISA 16:13 This is the decree which the Lord pronounced against Moab, when he spoke.
ISA 16:14 And now I say, within three years of the years of an hireling the glory of Moab shall be debased with all his abundant wealth; and he shall be left few in number and of no estimation.
ISA 17:1 The Oracle against Damascus. Behold Damascus shall be removed from among cities, and shall be for desolation;
ISA 17:2 left for ever for the folding of flocks, and for a resting place where none will scare them.
ISA 17:3 And it shall no more be a fortress for Ephraim to flee to; nor [s] [S=Sion.] shall there be again a regal government in Damascus; ever hereafter, of the Syrians. For thou art not better than the children of Israel; than that which was their glory. Thus saith the Lord of hosts,
ISA 17:4 there shall be in that day a diminution of the glory of Jacob; and the fatness of his glory shall be shaken;
ISA 17:5 and it shall be as when one gathereth the standing harvest and reapeth the ears of stalks; nay, it shall be as when one gathereth stalks in a sterile vale,
ISA 17:6 still a stalk may be left in it: or like the unripe berries of an olive tree, two or three may be left on the topmost bough, or four or five among the branches. Thus saith the Lord the God of Israel,
ISA 17:7 in that day let man trust in his maker, and his eyes look to the Holy One of Israel:
ISA 17:8 and let him no more put confidence in altars, nor in the works of their hands which their fingers have made, nor look to the groves nor to their abominations.
ISA 17:9 In that day thy cities shall be forsaken, as the Amorites and Evites forsook theirs because of the sons of Israel: and they shall become a desolation.
ISA 17:10 Because thou hast forsaken God thy Saviour, and hast not been mindful of the Lord thy helper, therefore thou shalt plant a faithless plant and a faithless seed.
ISA 17:11 On the day thou plantest thou shalt be deceived. Though thou sowest in the morning, shall it bloom for harvest? or on the day when thou shalt take possession, shalt thou as the father of man take possession for thy sons?
ISA 17:12 Alas! the multitude of many nations! Like the billowy sea so shall you be tossed, and the back of many nations shall sound like water.
ISA 17:13 The multitude of nations being like a great flood, their flight shall be like that of a mighty torrent rolling on impetuously. For he will repulse them with scorn, and pursue them to a great distance, like chaff before the wind when men winnow, or as a tempest driveth the dust of a wheel.
ISA 17:14 Toward evening there will be grief; before morning they shall be no more. This is the portion of them who have plundered you; and this the inheritance of them, who have taken possession of you.
ISA 18:1 Ah! wings of the land of ships! Thou who surpassest the Ethiopian streams,
ISA 18:2 thou who art sending pledges by sea, and paper messages on the water; for swift messengers will go to a lofty nation, and to a strange and fierce people. There is one far transcending it. With regard to the nation without hope and trodden down,
ISA 18:3 at this time, all ye streams of that land, like an inhabited country, their country shall be inhabited. As if a signal were displayed from a mountain, as with the sound of a trumpet,
ISA 18:4 let the news be spread. For thus hath the Lord said to me, "There shall be safety in this city of mine; like the light of noontide heat; and it shall be like a dewy cloud in a harvest day."
ISA 18:5 Before the vintage, when the blossom is perfect, and the young grape is swelling in the blossom; the diminutive bunches are to be cut off with pruning hooks, and the small shoots, to be nipped off and cut away,
ISA 18:6 and left together for the birds of the air, and for the wild beasts of the earth. And against them will be gathered all the birds of the air; and all the wild beasts of the earth will come upon it.
ISA 18:7 At that time gifts will be brought to the Lord of Hosts from a people afflicted and peeled; even on account of a people great from this time and forever. A nation having hope, though trodden down, which is in a part of the river of its country, will send them to the place of him, whose name is the Lord of Hosts, even to mount Sion.
ISA 19:1 A vision concerning Egypt. Behold the Lord is seated on a swift cloud; and he will come into Egypt; and the idols of Egypt shall be moved at his presence; and the heart of the people shall melt within them.
ISA 19:2 And they shall be stirred up, Egyptians against Egyptians, and shall fight; brother against brother and neighbour against neighbour, city against city, and nome against nome.
ISA 19:3 And the spirit of the Egyptians shall be troubled within them: and I will dissipate their counsel; and they will consult their gods and their idols; and them who cause a voice to proceed from the ground, namely the belly speakers.
ISA 19:4 And I will deliver Egypt into the hands of men: cruel lords; and fierce kings shall have dominion over them. Thus saith the Lord of Hosts,
ISA 19:5 The Egyptians drink water even that near the sea, but the river shall fail and be dried up;
ISA 19:6 both the streams and the canals of the river shall fail; and every collection of water shall be dried up, even every fen, where reeds and papyrus grow.
ISA 19:7 And all the quick springing herbage which is around the river, and every thing which is sown by the river shall be dried up and withered by the wind.
ISA 19:8 And the fisher men shall mourn; all who cast drags in the river shall mourn; and they who spread nets and they who are anglers shall grieve:
ISA 19:9 and shame shall seize them who work the split flax, and them who work up the cotton.
ISA 19:10 They who are employed in such works shall be in sorrow; and they who brew beer shall mourn and be grieved in soul.
ISA 19:11 The princes of Tanis shall be fools, those wise counsellors of the king, their counsel shall be turned into folly. How can you say to the king, We are sons of wise men, sons of ancient kings?
ISA 19:12 Where now are these wise men of thine? Let them tell thee publickly and declare what the Lord of hosts hath determined against Egypt.
ISA 19:13 The princes of Tanis have failed; and the princes of Memphis are exalted, and they will lead Egypt astray, tribe by tribe.
ISA 19:14 For the Lord hath mingled for them a spirit of error, and they with all their works have made Egypt reel, as a drunkard doth, when he is vomiting.
ISA 19:15 So that there shall be no work among the Egyptians, of which one can make head or tail, beginning or end.
ISA 19:16 And in that day the Egyptians shall be like women in fear and trembling because of the hand of the Lord of Hosts which he will lay upon them.
ISA 19:17 And the country of the Jews will be a terror to the Egyptians: when any one shall mention it to them, they will be in terror, because of the counsel which the Lord of Hosts hath determined against it.
ISA 19:18 In that day there shall be five cities in Egypt which shall speak the language of Chanaan. And swear by the name of the Lord of Hosts: and one of them shall be called the city of Asedek.
ISA 19:19 And in that day there shall be an altar for the Lord in the country of the Egyptians, and at its boundary a pillar for the Lord,
ISA 19:20 and it shall be an everlasting sign for the Lord, in the country of Egypt. Because they will cry to the Lord on account of their oppressors, therefore he will send them a man who will save them: he will vindicate their cause and deliver them.
ISA 19:21 And the Lord will be made known to the Egyptians, and the Egyptians will acknowledge the Lord in that day, and offer sacrifices and make vows to the Lord and perform them.
ISA 19:22 Thus will the Lord smite the Egyptians and heal them, and they shall be turned to the Lord, and he will hearken to them and heal them.
ISA 19:23 In that day this will be the highway from Egypt to Assyria; and Assyrians will come to Egypt and Egyptians to Assyria; and the Egyptians shall serve the Assyrians.
ISA 19:24 In that day Israel shall be a third, among the Egyptians and among the Assyrians, blessed in the land which the Lord of Hosts hath blessed
ISA 19:25 saying, "Blessed is my people which is in Egypt, and which is in Assyria and Israel which is mine inheritance."

ISA 21:1 The vision of the Desert. As, when a whirlwind having passed through a desert, is rushing out of a desert, the sight from the land is terrible;
ISA 21:2 this vision being also dreadful, was revealed to me. The treacherous dealeth treacherously; the transgressor transgresseth; the Elamites are upon me; and the elders of the Persians are coming against me. Am I now to groan and comfort myself?
ISA 21:3 For this cause my loins are filled with fainting; pangs have seized me like a woman in travail. I did wrong not to hear; I shuddered so that I could not see.
ISA 21:4 My heart is bewildered, transgression overwhelmeth me. My soul is on the brink of despair.
ISA 21:5 Prepare the table. Eat, drink ye chiefs. Having arisen prepare shields.
ISA 21:6 Because thus the Lord said to me, "Go set a watchman for thyself and proclaim what thou seest."
ISA 21:7 Thereupon I beheld a chariot with two riders, and a rider on an ass and a rider on a camel.
ISA 21:8 "Listen with the utmost attention, "said the Lord, "and call A fair breeze to the watch tower" I have kept my station all the day long, and by the camp I have stood the whole night;
ISA 21:9 and behold here cometh a man riding in a chariot, and addressing me he said, "It is fallen! Babylon is fallen! and all her images, and all the works of her hands are dashed on the ground."
ISA 21:10 Hear this ye who have been forsaken! and ye, who have been sorely grieved, hear what I have heard from the Lord of Hosts: what the God of Israel hath announced to us.
ISA 21:11 The vision concerning Idumea. TO me one calleth from Seir, "Guard ye the fortifications, "
ISA 21:12 I keep watch morning and night. If thou wouldst inquire; inquire and dwell near me.
ISA 21:13 Thou mayst go to rest in the western forest, or in the way to Dedan.
ISA 21:14 inhabitants of the country of Thaiman, bring out water to meet the thirsty;
ISA 21:15 meet with bread them who are fleeing, because of the multitude of the slain; and because of the multitude of dispersed: and because of the multitude of swords; and because of the multitude of bended bows; and because of the multitude of them who have fallen in battle.
ISA 21:16 For thus hath the Lord said to me, "Within a year, according to the year of an hireling, the glory of the children of Kedar shall fail;
ISA 21:17 and the remnant of the mighty bowmen of Kedar shall be small. For the Lord God of Israel hath spoken."
ISA 22:1 The Oracle concerning the valley of Sion. What aileth thee, that you are all now gone up to the house tops?
ISA 22:2 This vain city is full of people shouting. Thy slain are not slain with the sword; nor have thy dead died in battle.
ISA 22:3 All thy chiefs have fled and they who are taken are cruelly bound. Even the mighty men in thee have fled far away.
ISA 22:4 Therefore I said, "Let me alone; let me weep bitterly: labour not to comfort me, for this distress of the daughter of my people.
ISA 22:5 For it is a day of trouble and destruction and treading down. There is indeed some wandering from the Lord of Hosts; in the valley of Sion they are wandering about; from the least to the greatest they are wandering on the mountains.
ISA 22:6 But the Elamites have taken up their quivers; and the horsemen have mounted their horses; and the army is arrayed in order for battle;
ISA 22:7 and on they will come. Thy choicest valleys shall be filled with chariots; and the horsemen will block up thy gates,
ISA 22:8 and burst open the gates of Juda; and look, on that day, into the choicest houses of the city;
ISA 22:9 and lay open the stores of the houses of David's citadel. They indeed know that they are many, and that the water of the old pool is turned into the city,
ISA 22:10 and that the houses of Jerusalem have been pulled down, to fortify the wall in the city.
ISA 22:11 You have indeed provided water for yourselves, between the two walls nearer than the old pool, and have not looked to him who formed it of old, nor regarded him who created it.
ISA 22:12 Though the Lord of hosts, on that day, called for mourning, and lamentation, and for shaving of hair and girding with sackcloth,
ISA 22:13 yet they indulged themselves in joy and gladness, slaying oxen and sacrificing sheep, that they might eat flesh and drink wine, saying, "Let us eat and drink, for tomorrow we die."
ISA 22:14 Yes, these were their undisguised expressions, in the hearing of the Lord of hosts, therefore this sin will not be forgiven you till you die.
ISA 22:15 Thus saith the Lord of Hosts, Go to the treasury; to Somnas the steward, and say to him, "Why art thou here? and what hast thou here? that thou hast hewn out for thyself a monument, and hast made for thyself a sepulchre on high, and graved for thyself a tabernacle in a rock?"
ISA 22:17 Behold the Lord of hosts is now driving out and will utterly destroy men of rank, and he will take away thy robe and this gorgeous crown of thine,
ISA 22:18 and whirl thee into a large immeasurable country, and there thou shalt die. And he will bring to disgrace thy splendid chariot, and make the house of thy chief a publick walk.
ISA 22:19 And when thou shalt be removed from thine office and station:
ISA 22:20 it shall come to pass in that day, that I will call my servant Eliakim son of Chelkias,
ISA 22:21 and clothe him with thy robe. And this crown of thine I will confirm to him, and I will commit to his hands this office of thine: and he shall be as a father to the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and to them who dwell in Juda.
ISA 22:22 And I will give him the glory of David, and he shall rule and there shall be no antagonist; and on his shoulder I will lay the key of the house of David; and he will open and none shall shut; and he will shut and none shall open:
ISA 22:23 and I will make him a ruler in a sure place, and he shall be a throne of glory for the house of his father.
ISA 22:24 And on him will rely with confidence, every honourable man in his father's house, from the least even to the greatest. On him they shall be dependant in that day.
ISA 22:25 Thus saith the Lord of Hosts, The man who is now fixed in a sure place shall be removed and taken away and shall fall; and the glory which is on him shall be utterly destroyed for the Lord hath spoken it.
ISA 23:1 The Oracle concerning Tyre. Raise the mournful cry, ships of Carthage, for Tyre is destroyed and there are no arrivals from the land of the Kitians. She is carried away captive.
ISA 23:2 Who could be compared with the dwellers in this island; these merchants of Phoenicia, who traversed the ocean;
ISA 23:3 this offspring of merchants on many a water, who made a traffick of nations as of an ingathered harvest?
ISA 23:4 Be ashamed, Sidon, said the sea; even the strength of the sea said, "I did not travail nor did I bring her forth; nor did I nourish her youths, nor educate her virgins;
ISA 23:5 yet when the news shall reach Egypt, sorrow for Tyre will take hold on them."
ISA 23:6 Away to Carthage! Raise the mournful cry, ye who inhabit that isle!
ISA 23:7 Was not she your boast of old, before she was delivered up?"
ISA 23:8 Who hath taken this counsel against the Tyrians? Is she inferior? Or hath she not power? Her merchants are glorious chiefs of the earth."
ISA 23:9 The Lord of Hosts hath determined to destroy all the haughtiness of the glorious; and to bring to contempt every thing glorious on the earth.
ISA 23:10 work thy land: for ships no more arrive from Carthage,
ISA 23:11 nor is thy hand which vexed kings, any more powerful by sea. The Lord of Hosts hath given a command, concerning Chanaan, to destroy its power:
ISA 23:12 and shall it be said, You must not proceed to insult and distress the daughter of Sidon? Nay though thou shouldst go to the Kitians; yet even there thou shalt not have rest.
ISA 23:13 Away to the land of the Chaldeans, though it hath been wasted by the Assyrians; because its walls had fallen.
ISA 23:14 Raise the mournful cry, ships of Carthage, because your strong hold is destroyed.
ISA 23:15 And it shall come to pass in that day, that Tyre shall be forsaken seventy years, according to the days of a king, according to the time of a man. And it shall come to pass after seventy years, that Tyre shall be as the song of a harlot.
ISA 23:16 Take a kithara, stroll about, city, O harlot long forgotten! Play skilfully; sing many songs, that thou mayst be remembered.
ISA 23:17 And it shall come to pass after seventy years, that God will take account of Tyre, and she shall be restored to her former state, and be a mart for all the kingdoms of the World; which are on the face of the earth.
ISA 23:18 And her traffick and gain shall be holy to the Lord. All her gain shall not be treasured up for themselves, but for them who dwell before the Lord, that they may eat and drink and be filled, and for contributions to be kept in remembrance before the Lord.
ISA 24:1 Behold the Lord is about to destroy this inhabited land! He will lay it waste and uncover the face thereof and scatter abroad them who dwell therein.
ISA 24:2 And it shall be as with the people so with the priest; as with the servant, so with the master; as with the maid, so with the mistress; as with the buyer, so with the seller, as with the lender, so with the borrower; as with the debtor, so with the creditor.
ISA 24:3 With destruction the land will be destroyed, and with spoiling this land will be ransacked: for the mouth of the Lord hath spoken this.
ISA 24:4 The land mourned and this empire is destroyed; the lofty people of the land mourned.
ISA 24:5 As for the land, it transgressed by means of its inhabitants. Because they transgressed the law, and changed the institutions; the everlasting covenant,
ISA 24:6 therefore a curse devoureth the land. Because they who dwell therein have sinned, therefore the inhabitants of the land shall be distressed, and few are the men who shall be left.
ISA 24:7 The wine will mourn, the vineyard will mourn, and all that were merry hearted will sigh.
ISA 24:8 The mirth of the tabrets hath ceased, the sound of the kithara is no more.
ISA 24:9 They are confounded: they have drunk no wine. The palm wine was bitter to them who drank it.
ISA 24:10 Every city is desolated: the houses will be shut up that none may enter.
ISA 24:11 Raise the mournful cry every where for the wine. A stop is put to all the joy of the land; all the joy of the land is gone.
ISA 24:12 The cities will be left desolate, and the houses being forsaken will be destroyed.
ISA 24:13 All this shall come to pass in this land, in the midst of the nations. As when one shall shake an olive tree, so shall they be shaken: and when the vintage is over
ISA 24:14 a shout will be raised. But they who are left in the land shall be gladdened with the glory of the Lord. The water of the sea will be troubled:
ISA 24:15 for this cause the glory of the Lord will be in the isles of the sea. In the isles of the sea the name of the Lord will be glorious.
ISA 24:16 [c] "Lord the God of Israel! from the outskirts of the earth we have heard of thy wonders: there is hope for the righteous." [p] Let them say also, "Woe to the rebels who reject the law!"
ISA 24:17 Terror and a pit and a snare are for you who dwell in the land:
ISA 24:18 and it shall come to pass, that he who fleeth from the terror, shall fall into the pit; and he who getteth out of the pit, shall be caught by the snare. Because the flood gates of heaven are opened, therefore the foundations of the land shall be shaken.
ISA 24:19 With confusion the land will be confounded; with perplexity this land will be perplexed.
ISA 24:20 It reeled to and fro like a drunkard when intoxicated: like a lodge in a vineyard the land shall be shaken. For iniquity hath prevailed over it; and it shall fall and shall not be able to rise.
ISA 24:21 When God shall bring his hand on the hosts of heaven, even upon the kings of this land;
ISA 24:22 and the congregation thereof shall have been assembled for imprisonment, and shut up as chaff for many generations; of them there shall be a visitation.
ISA 24:23 [c] When the bricks shall have mouldered away, and the wall shall have fallen; because the Lord will commence his reign from Sion and from Jerusalem, and be glorified in the presence of the elders;
ISA 25:1 O Lord God, thee I will glorify: in songs of praise I will extol thy name. For thou hast executed wonderful things, a counsel of old immutably true.
ISA 25:2 Because thou hast reduced cities to a heap of ruins; cities made strong, that their foundations might not fall; [a city of wicked men cannot be built to last forever]
ISA 25:3 therefore the distressed people will bless thee and the cities of injured men will give thee thanks;
ISA 25:4 for thou hast been the support of every humble city and the defence of them who were dispirited; by reason of their weakness. From wicked men thou will deliver them. Thou art the support of the thirsty and the breath of men in distress.
ISA 25:5 [p] When dispirited men shall be thirsting in Sion on account of wicked men to whom thou hast delivered us up;

ISA 26:3 who support truth and keep peace; because their confidence is placed in thee, Lord!
ISA 26:4 who art to everlasting, the Mighty, the Eternal God,
ISA 26:5 who hast humbled and brought down them who dwell in lofty places. Fortified cities thou canst demolish and level them with the dust,
ISA 26:6 that the feet of the meek and lowly may trample them.
ISA 26:7 The way of the pious was straight; the way of the pious was well prepared;
ISA 26:8 for the way of the Lord is justice. We have trusted in thy name and in that remembrance
ISA 26:9 which is the desire of our soul by night. To thee, God, my spirit awaketh early, because thy statutes are a light on the earth. Learn righteousness ye dwellers on earth,
ISA 26:10 for the wicked one is no more. Whoever will not learn justice on earth, cannot act agreeably to truth. Let the wicked be removed that he may not see the glory of the Lord.
ISA 26:11 Thy hand, Lord, was lifted high; but they did not know it; but when they know they will be ashamed. Zeal will seize an uninstructed people; even now a fire devoureth the adversaries.

ISA 26:13 Lord, our God, take possession of us! Besides thee, Lord, we know none other. We celebrate thy name.

ISA 26:15 Heap evils on the vainglorious of the earth.
ISA 26:16 Lord, in affliction I remembered thee. Thine instruction to us was with a small affliction;
ISA 26:17 and as a woman in labour, when near delivery, crieth in her pangs, so have we been to thy beloved.
ISA 26:18 On account of the fear of thee, Lord, we conceived and suffered the pangs of child birth, and brought forth the spirit of thy salvation; for what we did in that land we are not to fall; but all the dwellers in that land are to fall.

ISA 28:4 And the flower which hath dropped from the hope of the Glory, on the top of the lofty mountain, shall be like the early fruit of a fig tree, which he who seeth it will wish to devour, before he can get it into his hand.

ISA 28:6 They shall be left for the spirit of Justice; to administer justice and destroy the power of the opposers.

ISA 28:8 A curse shall devour their counsel; for their counsel is for the sake of gain.

ISA 28:10 Expect affliction on affliction; hope on hope, yet a little While: yet a little while.
ISA 28:11 On account of the mockery of their lips; because they will speak to this people with a strange tongue, saying to them,
ISA 28:12 [f] The sententious speeches of the false prophets.] "This is the rest for him who is hungry: and this is the destruction, but they would not hear"
ISA 28:13 Therefore the oracle of God will be to them" Affliction on affliction; hope on hope, yet a little while, yet a little while" that they may proceed on and fall backwards; and they shall be broken and snared and caught.
ISA 28:14 Therefore hear the word of the Lord, ye afflicted men, and ye rulers of this people in Jerusalem!
ISA 28:15 Because you said, "We have made a covenant with death: and with the grave we have made a treaty: though the furious tempest may pass through, it will by no means reach us. We have made falsehood our refuge and by this falsehood we shall be saved."
ISA 28:16 Therefore thus saith the Sovereign Lord; behold I lay for the foundation of Sion a stone of inestimable worth; a chosen, precious corner stone for the foundations of it, and he who believeth shall not be ashamed.
ISA 28:17 And I will establish judgment for hope, and my mercy shall be for scales. But as for you who have vainly trusted in falsehood, that the tempest would not reach you;
ISA 28:18 and that it would not break your treaty with death; the hope which you have with respect to the grave shall not last: when the furious tempest cometh, by it you shall be beaten down.

ISA 28:22 As for you therefore, be not filled with joy, yet let not your bonds gather strength. For the things are complete and decisive which I have heard from the Lord of Hosts; which he will execute on all this land.

ISA 28:25 Doth he not, when he hath levelled the face of the soil, then sow the small dill or cummin? and again sow wheat and barley and millet and rye in all thy borders?
ISA 28:26 So thou shalt be corrected by the judgment of God; and be made glad.
ISA 28:27 For the dill is not cleaned with a corn drag; nor is the wheel of a wain to turn round on the cummin; but with a rod are beaten out the dill; and cummin. [J] Yet with bread they will be eaten.

ISA 29:3 I will indeed encompass thee as David did; and surround thee with a rampire; and erect towers around thee.
ISA 29:4 But when thy words shall be brought down to the ground; and shall be as if they sounded out of the earth; and thy voice on the ground shall be feeble;
ISA 29:5 then shall the riches of the wicked be as the dust of a wheel, and the multitude of thine oppressors as chaff blown away: and this shall be as in a moment, suddenly.
ISA 29:6 For from the Lord of Hosts there will be a visitation: a hurricane and a devouring flame of fire, with thunder and an earthquake and a mighty noise;
ISA 29:7 and the wealth of all the nations which encamped against Ariel, and all they who are warring against Jerusalem, and all who have been assembled against her, and those distressing her, shall be like one dreaming dreams by night:
ISA 29:8 and like men who in sleep are eating and drinking, but when they awake the dream is vain: even as a thirsty man dreameth that he drinketh, and when he waketh he is still athirst, his soul having trusted in a shadow: so shall be the wealth of all the nations, who have warred against mount Sion.
ISA 29:9 [p] Be sunk in dejection and stand astonished; be drunk and reel, not with wine nor strong drink;

ISA 29:11 all these prophesies will be to you like the words of a book which is sealed: which when they give to a man skilled in letters, saying, Read this: He will say, I cannot read it, for it is sealed.
ISA 29:12 And should the book be put in the hands of an illiterate man, and they say to him, Bead that, he will say, I do not know letters.

ISA 29:14 therefore, behold, I will proceed to the removal of this people and I will remove them; and destroy the wisdom of the wise, and darken the understanding of the prudent."
ISA 29:15 Alas! for them, who deeply form a design, but not by the Lord. Alas! for them, who form designs in secret, that their works may be in darkness; and who will say, "Who hath seen us, and who can find out us, or what we do?"
ISA 29:16 Are not you to be considered as the potter's clay? Shall the thing formed say to the former of it, thou hast not made me. Or shall the work say to the Workman thou hast not made me wisely?
ISA 29:17 Is it not a little while, ere Libanus shall be changed to a likeness of Mount Carmel? And Carmel be accounted a forest?
ISA 29:18 And in that day the deaf shall hear the words of a book, and they in darkness, even they in thick darkness; the eyes even of the blind shall see;
ISA 29:19 and the distressed shall exult with joy because of the Lord; and the disconsolate among men shall be filled with joy.
ISA 29:20 The lawless one hath failed, and the haughty one is destroyed, and these are utterly cut off who maliciously commit iniquity,

ISA 29:22 therefore, thus saith the Lord respecting the house of Jacob, whom he set apart from Abraham; "Jacob will not be ashamed now, nor will he now change his countenance;
ISA 29:23 but when his children shall see my works, because of me they will hallow my name. They will hallow the Holy One of Jacob, and tremble before the God of Israel.
ISA 29:24 And they who have erred in spirit will gain knowledge, and the murmurers shall be taught obedience, and the trifling tongues will learn to speak peace."

ISA 30:3 For the protection of Pharao will be your shame, and a disgrace to them who have trusted in Egypt.
ISA 30:4 Because generals are unwelcome messengers at Tanis,
ISA 30:5 they shall labour in vain with a people who will be of no service for assistance; but for a shame and disgrace.
ISA 30:6 This is the vision of the four footed beasts in the desert; A lion and a lion's whelp were in distress and difficulty; and from them went the asps and the brood of flying serpents, who carried their wealth on asses and camels to a nation which could not profit them.
ISA 30:7 In vain and to no purpose will the Egyptians help you. Announce to them, That this application of yours is vain.
ISA 30:8 Now therefore sit down and write these things in a tablet and make a book that they may be for the appointed time; even for the time to come.
ISA 30:9 Because this is a rebellious people; lying children, who would not hear the law of God,
