JER 51:50 ye who have escaped; and tarry not; ye who are far off, remember the Lord; and let Jerusalem recur to your mind.
JER 51:51 [c] We are ashamed; because we have heard our reproach, disgrace hath covered our face; strangers have entered our sanctuaries; into the house of the Lord.
JER 51:52 [J] Therefore behold the days are coming, saith the Lord, when I will execute vengeance on her graven images, and among all them her wounded shall fall in that land.
JER 51:53 For though Babylon should mount up to heaven; though she fortify her walls with all her might, from me shall come forth those who shall destroy her, saith the Lord.
JER 51:54 [p] A sound of screaming in Babylon! and great destruction in the land of the Chaldeans!
JER 51:55 For the Lord hath utterly destroyed Babylon, and put an end to her din, which was like the sound of great waters. Her din he hath given up to destruction.
JER 51:57 For misery is come upon Babylon. Her warriors are taken. Their bow is confounded; for God rendereth them retribution. [J] The Lord rendereth them retribution;  and he will make utterly drunk her leaders and her wise men and her generals, saith the king whose name is The Lord Almighty.
JER 51:58 Thus saith the Lord, The wall of Babylon was made broad; It shall be totally demolished and her lofty gates shall be burned with fire; and the peoples shall not labour in vain, though the nations may at first fail.
JER 51:59 The word which the Lord commanded Jeremias the prophet to deliver to Saraias son of Nerias son of Maasias when he was going from Sedekias king of Juda to Babylon in the fourth year of his reign. Now Saraias had the charge of the homage gifts.
JER 51:60 When Jeremias bad written in a book all the evils which were to come upon Babylon, even all the words above written against Babylon,
JER 51:61 Jeremias said to Saraias; When thou art come to Babylon and shalt have seen and read all these words,
JER 51:62 then thou shalt say, "O Lord, Lord, thou hast spoken against this place, that thou wilt destroy it utterly, so that none shall dwell therein, neither man nor beast; for it shall be a desolation forever."
JER 51:63 And when thou hast finished reading the book, then thou shalt tye a stone to it and throw it into the midst of the Euphrates,
JER 51:64 and say, "So shall Babylon sink and rise no more by reason of the evils which I bring upon it".
JER 52:1 Sedekias was twenty one years old when he began to reign, and he reigned eleven years in Jerusalem and his mother's name was Ameital. She was a daughter of Jeremias of Lobena.
JER 52:2 [Omitted]
JER 52:3 [Omitted]
JER 52:4 And it came to pass in the ninth year of his reign in the fifth month, on the tenth of the month, Nabuchodonosar king of Babylon, came with his whole army against Jerusalem, and they besieged it and built a wall around it of square stones,
JER 52:5 and the city was besieged until the eleventh year of king Sedekias.
JER 52:6 On the ninth day of the; month there was a grievous famine in the city and there was no bread for the people of the land.
JER 52:7 When a breach was made into the city, all the men who were warriors went out by night by the way of the gate between the outer and the inner wall, which was along the king's garden, [though the Chaldeans were all around the city;] and took the road to Araba.
JER 52:8 And the army of the Chaldeans pursued the king and overtook him on the borders of Jericho. And all his servants being dispersed from him,
JER 52:9 they took the king and carried him to the king of Babylon at Deblatha, who passed sentence on him.
JER 52:10 And the king of Babylon slew the sons of Sedekias before his eyes. He slew also all the chiefs of Juda at Deblatha.
JER 52:11 Then he put out the eyes of Sedekias and bound him with chains. And the king of Babylon led him to Babylon and committed him to the slave prison where he continued till the day of his death.
JER 52:12 And on the fifth month on the tenth of the month Nabouzardan the chief cook, who stood in the presence of the king of Babylon, came to Jerusalem
JER 52:13 and burned the house of the Lord and the king's house. He burned also with fire all the public buildings of the city and every stately house.
JER 52:14 And the army of the Chaldeans which was with the chief cook demolished all the wall of Jerusalem round about.
JER 52:15 [Omitted]
JER 52:16 But the chief cook left the remains of the people for vine dressers and husbandmen.
JER 52:17 The Chaldeans also broke to pieces the pillars of brass which were in the house of the Lord and the bases and the sea of brass which was in the house of the Lord, and took the brass and carried it to Babylon with the crown,
JER 52:18 and the cups and the flesh forks and all the utensils of brass with which they sacrificed;
JER 52:19 and the Apphoths and the Masmaroths and the oil vessels and the candlesticks and the censers and the cups: those which were of gold, or gilded, and those which were of silver, or plated, the chief cook took.
JER 52:20 As for the two pillars and the sea and the twelve oxen of brass under the sea, which king Solomon had made for the house of the Lord, there was no weighing the brass thereof.
JER 52:21 The height of each of the pillars was thirty five cubits and a fillet of twelve cubits encircled it, the thickness of which was four fingers all around.
JER 52:22 And there was a chapiter of brass on each of them of the height of five cubits with a ball on the top of each and a piece of net work and pomegranates around on each chapiter; all of brass; eight pomegranates to a cubit for the twelve cubits.
JER 52:23 So that there were ninety six pomegranates on the sides and all the pomegranates on the net work round about were one hundred.
JER 52:24 And the chief cook took the chief priest, and the priest who was second to him, and the three who guarded the way;
JER 52:25 and a eunuch who was over the men of war, and seven men of renown who attended in the king's presence, who were found in the city, and the scribe of the armies, who mustered the people of the land; and sixty chief men, of the people of the country, who were found in the city.
JER 52:26 These Nabuzardan the chief cook, took and brought to the king of Babylon at Deblatha.
JER 52:27 And the king of Babylon slew them at Deblatha in the land of Aimath.
JER 52:31 And it came to pass in the thirty seventh year of the captivity of Jechonias king of Juda, in the twelfth month, on the twenty fourth of the month, Oulaimadachar king of Babylon, in the first year of his reign, took and raised up the head of Jechonias king of Juda, and caused him to be shaven and released him from the prison, in which he was confined,
JER 52:32 and spoke kindly to him and set his seat above the kings, who were with him in Babylon.
JER 52:33 And changed his prison dress, and caused him to eat in his presence, all the days of his life.
JER 52:34 And he had a portion continually given to him, day by day, from the king of Babylon, to the day of his death.
LAM 1:1 After Israel was carried into captivity, and Jerusalem was laid waste; Jeremias sat down and wept, and sung this song of woe over Jerusalem, and said. How solitary sitteth the city which was full of people! she who was abundant among nations is become like a widow! the empress of provinces is become tributary!
LAM 1:2 She wept sore by night and her tears are on her cheeks: and of all her lovers there is none to comfort her. All her friends dealt treacherously with her. They became her enemies.
LAM 1:3 Judea is forced to emigrate. On account of her humiliation and because of her great servitude, she sat down among the nations; she found no rest. All her persecutors found her among them who were afflicting her.
LAM 1:4 The highways of Sion mourn; because none attend her festivals. All her gates are desolate. Her priests groan bitterly. Her virgins are carried away; and she is by herself in bitterness.
LAM 1:5 They who afflict her are become her head; and her enemies prosper. Because the Lord hath humbled her for the multitude of her transgressions; her children are gone into captivity before the oppressor.
LAM 1:6 From the daughter of Sion all her comeliness is taken away. Her chiefs were like rams which could find no pasture; and they came without strength in view of the pursuer.
LAM 1:7 In the days of her humiliation and rejection, Jerusalem remembered all the good things which she had in days of old. When her people fell into the hands of the oppressor, and there was none to help her; her enemies seeing this, laughed at her festivals held in commemoration of her settlement.
LAM 1:8 Jerusalem sinned grievously, therefore she became unstable as a wave. By all that honoured her she hath been humbled, for they saw her nakedness, while she sighing turned away her face.
LAM 1:9 Her unclean ness was before her feet. She was insensible to her extreme distress. He hath indeed lowered her haughtiness; there is none who comforteth her. Lord, behold my affliction because the enemy is magnified.
LAM 1:10 On all the objects of her desire the oppressor hath laid his hand; for into her sanctuary she saw nations entering, concerning whom thou hast commanded that they should not come into thy congregation.
LAM 1:11 All her people were sighing deeply, seeking bread. They gave up the objects of her desire, for meat to preserve life. Look down, O Lord, and see how she is dishonoured.
LAM 1:12 [s] Ho! all ye who travel the way turn and see! is there any sorrow like this of mine, which he hath denounced against me. The Lord hath humbled me in the day of his fierce indignation.
LAM 1:13 From his loftiness he hath sent a fire; he brought it in among my bones. He hath spread a net for my feet and turned me backwards. He hath made me desolate and full of sorrow, all the live long day.
LAM 1:14 He hath kept a watch on my transgressions. They are wreathed round my hands. They have reached up to my neck. My strength is enfeebled. For into my hands the Lord hath sent pains. I cannot stand.
LAM 1:15 From amidst me the Lord hath moved all my mighty men. He hath brought upon me the time for crushing my chosen bands. The Lord trod out a vat for the virgin daughter of Juda.
LAM 1:16 For these things I mourn. Mine eye hath flowed with water, because my comforter, he who is the supporter of my life, is far removed from me. My children are vanished because the enemy hath prevailed.
LAM 1:17 [p] Sion stretched forth her hand; there is none to comfort her. The Lord gave a command respecting Jacob; around him are they who afflict him. Jerusalem became among them, like one set apart as unclean.
LAM 1:18 [s] The Lord is righteous; for against his express commandment I rebelled. Hear I beseech you all ye peoples and behold my sorrow! my virgins and my young men are gone into captivity.
LAM 1:19 I called on my lovers; but they with false excuses deceived me. My priests and my elders expired in the city, because they sought food to support their lives, but found none.
LAM 1:20 Look, O Lord! because of my distress my bowels are troubled; and my heart within me is distracted, because I have grievously rebelled. Abroad the sword, and at home death have bereaved me of children.
LAM 1:21 Hear, I beseech thee! because I groan; there is none to comfort me. All mine enemies heard of my calamities, and rejoiced at what thou hast done. Thou hast brought on a day: thou hast proclaimed a time. They were like me,
LAM 1:22 let all their wickedness come before thee. Make search for them as they have made search for all my transgressions. For my groans are many, and my heart is afflicted with grief.
LAM 2:1 Oh! how the Lord hath in his wrath covered with darkness the daughter of Sion! he hath cast down, from heaven, upon the earth, the glory of Israel; and hath not remembered his own footstool.
LAM 2:2 In the day of his indignation the Lord overwhelmed and did not spare; in his wrath he destroyed all the comeliness of Jacob: he levelled to the ground the strong holds of the daughter of Juda. He brought contempt on her king, and her chiefs.
LAM 2:3 In his fierce anger he broke the whole horn of Israel: he turned back his right hand from before his enemy: he kindled in Jacob a flaming fire, which devoured all around.
LAM 2:4 He bent his bow like an opposing enemy; like an adversary he strengthened his right hand and slew all the desires of mine eyes. In the tent of the daughter of Sion he poured out his wrath like fire.
LAM 2:5 The Lord became like an enemy. He overwhelmed Israel. He sunk her palaces. He destroyed his own munitions, and multiplied on the daughter of Juda humiliation on humiliation.
LAM 2:6 He laid open like a vineyard his own dwelling; he marred his own festivals. The Lord forgot the festivals and sabbaths which he had established in Sion, and by the rebuke of his anger vexed king and priest and chief.
LAM 2:7 The Lord hath cast off his altar; he hath shaken off his sanctuary. With the hand of an enemy he hath demolished the wall of her palaces. They uttered a shout in the house of the Lord as on the day of a festival.
LAM 2:8 He turned back to destroy the wall of the daughter of Sion; he stretched out a measuring line: he withdrew not his hand from destruction; so the outer wall mourned and the inner wall languished with it.
LAM 2:9 Her gates were dashed to the ground: he destroyed and broke to pieces her bars, her king and her chiefs among the nations. Law is no more; and her prophets saw not a vision from the Lord.
LAM 2:10 The elders of the daughter of Sion sat on the ground. They were silent. They heaped dust on their heads; they girded themselves with sackcloth. He humbled to the ground the virgin princesses in Jerusalem.
LAM 2:11 Mine eyes failed with tears; my heart was astounded. My glory was poured on the ground for the distress of the daughter of my people when the infant and suckling expired in the streets of the city.
LAM 2:12 To their mothers they said, "Where is corn and wine, "when they were fainting like wounded men in the streets of the city; when they were pouring out their souls in their mothers' bosom.
LAM 2:13 What shall I take to witness for thee? Or to what shall I liken thee, daughter of Jerusalem? Who can save and comfort thee, virgin daughter of Sion? Because thy cup of ruin hath been large, who can heal thee?
LAM 2:14 Thy prophets saw vanities and follies for thee; they made no revelations against thine iniquity to turn away thy captivity, but saw for thee false burdens and expellings.
LAM 2:15 All that passed by clapped their hands for thee, they expressed the sound of pity and shaked their heads for the daughter of Jerusalem. Is this, say they, the city, the crown of joy of the whole earth!
LAM 2:16 Against thee all thine enemies opened their mouth; they hissed and gnashed their teeth and said, We have swallowed her up; but this is the day we looked for; we have found it; we have seen it.
LAM 2:17 The Lord hath done what he purposed. He hath executed his decree, what he enjoined in days of old. He hath destroyed and hath not spared. He hath caused an enemy to rejoice over thee. He hath exalted the horn of thine oppressor.
LAM 2:18 Their heart cried to the Lord.! walls of Sion cause tears to flow down like a torrent day and night. Give thyself no rest; let not the daughter of thine eyes be silent.
LAM 2:19 Arise, chant praise in the night at setting thy watch. Pour out thy heart like water before the Lord; lift up thy hands to him for the life of thine infants, who are perishing with hunger at the head of every street.
LAM 2:20 Look, O Lord, and see. For whom hast thou caused such a search to be made? Shall women eat the fruit of their womb! The cook hath made search! Shall infants at the breast be butchered? Wilt thou slay in the sanctuary of the Lord, priest and prophet?
LAM 2:21 On the high way lie the youth and the elder. My virgins and my young men are gone into captivity; with sword and with famine thou hast slain; in the day of thine anger thou hast slaughtered and hast not spared.
LAM 2:22 He called my sojourners from all around to a solemn festival, so that in the day of the indignation of the Lord none escaped or were left. As I excelled in power so have I multiplied all mine enemies.
LAM 3:1 I am a man who have seen affliction by the rod of his wrath
LAM 3:2 against me. He hath seized me and dragged me into darkness and there is no light.
LAM 3:3 But still he turned his hand against me all the day long.
LAM 3:4 He hath made my flesh and my skin old; he hath broken my bones.
LAM 3:5 He built up against me and encompassed my head and afflicted it with pain:
LAM 3:6 in dark mansions he placed me like the dead of old.
LAM 3:7 He built up against me so that I cannot get out. He made my chain heavy.
LAM 3:8 Though I scream and cry, he shut out my prayer.
LAM 3:9 He walled up my ways; he blocked up my paths;
LAM 3:10 he terrified me. He was as a bear lying in wait; to me he was like a lion in secret coverts.
LAM 3:11 He pursued me when I fled and stopped me. He removed me quite out of sight.
LAM 3:12 He bent his bow and set me up as a mark for his arrow.
LAM 3:13 He poured into my reins the darts of his quiver.
LAM 3:14 I became a subject of laughter to all my people; their song all the day long.
LAM 3:15 He glutted me with worm wood; he gave me a large draught of gall,
LAM 3:16 and broke my teeth with gravel. He drenched me with ashes.
LAM 3:17 He removed my soul far from peace. I forgot prosperity;
LAM 3:18 so my strength was destroyed and the hope which I had from the Lord.
LAM 3:19 I recollected because of mine affliction. When by reason of persecution, my bitterness and gall shall be remembered;
LAM 3:20 then on myself will my soul meditate.
LAM 3:21 I will lay this up in my heart.
LAM 3:22 On this account I will wait for the mercies of the Lord, because he hath not quite forsaken me; because his compassion is not exhausted. In the ensuing months, Lord, exercise compassion, since we are not quite consumed; since thy mercies are not exhausted.
LAM 3:23 New every morning is thine abundant faithfulness.
LAM 3:24 The Lord is my portion, saith my soul, therefore I will wait for him.
LAM 3:25 The Lord is gracious to them who wait for him for the soul, that will seek him,
LAM 3:26 there is good; let it therefore wait quietly for the salvation of the Lord.
LAM 3:27 It is good for a man when he hath borne a yoke in his youth.
LAM 3:28 He will sit solitary and be silent, because he hath taken it upon him.
LAM 3:29 [Omitted]
LAM 3:30 He will give his cheek to him who smiteth it; he will feed on reproaches;
LAM 3:31 because the Lord will not cast off forever;
LAM 3:32 because he who hath humbled will have compassion, even according to the multitude of his mercies.
LAM 3:33 He did not answer from his heart and humble the children of men
LAM 3:34 with an intent to crush under his feet all the prisoners of the earth;
LAM 3:35 to turn aside the cause of man from before the Most High.
LAM 3:36 To condemn a man when he is on his trial, the Lord hath not enjoined.
LAM 3:37 [a] Who ever enjoined thus; when it hath happened, hath not the Lord ordered it?
LAM 3:38 [b] From the mouth of the Most High shall not evils proceed as well as good?
LAM 3:39 Why should a living man murmur; a man for his sin offering?
LAM 3:40 Our way hath been searched and tried; let us then return to the Lord.
LAM 3:41 Let us offer up our hearts on our hands to Him who is High in heaven.
LAM 3:42 We have sinned; we have been guilty of impiety; and thou hast not been appeased.
LAM 3:43 Thou hast covered with wrath and discarded us; thou hast slain and hast not spared;
LAM 3:44 thou hast covered thyself with a cloud because of prayer, that I may shut mine eyes and
LAM 3:45 be cast off. Thou hast placed us in the midst of the peoples;
LAM 3:46 all our enemies have opened their mouths against us.
LAM 3:47 On us are come terror and wrath, desolation and destruction.
LAM 3:48 Let streams of water be collected by mine eye, for the destruction of the daughter of my people.
LAM 3:49 Mine eye is bathed in tears and I cannot keep silence that it may dry,
LAM 3:50 until the Lord look down from heaven and behold.
LAM 3:51 Let mine eye be more watchful for my life, than all the daughters of a city.
LAM 3:52 With eagerness all mine enemies have hunted me like an ostrich;
LAM 3:53 without cause they have condemned me to die in a dungeon, and placed a stone over me.
LAM 3:54 Water was poured above upon my head. I said, I am cast off.
LAM 3:55 I called on thy name, O Lord, out of the deepest dungeon.
LAM 3:56 Thou hast heard my voice; stop not thine ear against my supplication.
LAM 3:57 To my assistance thou didst draw near. On the day I called on thee, thou saidst to me, Fear not. [a] An objection, [b] The answer.
LAM 3:58 Thou, O Lord, hast pleaded the causes of my soul; thou hast redeemed my life.
LAM 3:59 Thou, Lord, hast seen my wrongs; thou hast decided my cause.
LAM 3:60 Thou hast seen all their vengeance; into all their devices against me.
LAM 3:61 Thou hast heard their reproach; all their charges against me;
LAM 3:62 the speeches of them who accused me; their studied harangues against me all the day long.
LAM 3:63 [Omitted]
LAM 3:64 At their sitting down and their rising up, look down on their eyes.
LAM 3:65 Thou, O Lord, wilt render them a recompence according to the works of their hands.
LAM 3:66 Thou wilt give them for a shield the sorrow of my heart. Thou wilt pursue them with indignation, and destroy them utterly from under heaven.
LAM 4:1 How gold can be tarnished! How pure silver can be changed! Holy stones were shot down at the head of all the outlets.
LAM 4:2 The sons of Sion who were precious, more precious than gold; how they have been accounted as earthen vessels, the works of a potter's hands.
LAM 4:3 Surely jackals drew out the breasts; their whelps suckled the daughters of my people, to make them unnatural as the ostrich in the desert.
LAM 4:4 The tongue of a sucking babe cleaved to the roof of its mouth for thirst: infants asked for bread, there is none who breaketh it for them.
LAM 4:5 They who had fed upon dainties perished in the highways; they who had been nursed in scarlet were covered with dung.
LAM 4:6 The transgression of the daughter of my people was greater than that of Sodom which was overthrown suddenly, without tiring hands with it.
LAM 4:7 Her Nazarites were purer than snow; they were whiter than milk. They were more ruddy than a sapphire. Behold their change!
LAM 4:8 Their visage became blacker than soot. They are not distinguished in the streets. Their skin is shrivelled to their bones. They are withered. They are become like a stick.
LAM 4:9 The victims of the sword are more beautiful than those slain by famine. These stalked about pierced through for want of the fruits of the field.
LAM 4:10 The hands of tender hearted women boiled their own children; these were food for them in the extreme distress of the daughter of my people.
LAM 4:11 The Lord hath executed his wrath; he hath poured out his fierce anger. He hath kindled a fire in Sion, which hath devoured her very foundations.
LAM 4:12 The kings of the earth; all the inhabitants of the world did not believe that an enemy and a destroyer could have entered the gates of Jerusalem.
LAM 4:13 Because of the sins of her prophets; the iniquities of her priests; of them who were shedding innocent blood, in the midst of her,
LAM 4:14 [her watchmen shuddered in the streets, they were polluted with blood, as they could not but have touched their clothes.
LAM 4:15 "Stand off from the unclean." Call to them "Stand off! Stand off! touch not" because they had been touched they shuddered.] Say among the nations, Let them no longer sojourn there.
LAM 4:16 The presence of the Lord was their portion; he will no more look upon them: they paid no respect to the presence of priests; on prophets they had no compassion.
LAM 4:17 While we yet existed our eyes failed looking in vain for our help. when we looked out, we looked to a nation that could not save.
LAM 4:18 We have hunted for our little ones that they might not walk in our streets. Our time is come. Our days are fulfilled. Our time is at hand.
LAM 4:19 They who pursue us are swifter than eagles in the air; they overtook us on the mountains. They lay in wait for us in the desert.
LAM 4:20 In their slaughters is comprehended the breath of our nostrils, our anointed Lord, of whom we said, "Under his shadow we shall live among the nations."
LAM 4:21 Rejoice and be glad, daughter of Idumea who dwellest in the land. To thee however the cup of the Lord will come and thou shalt drink and vomit.
LAM 4:22 O daughter of Sion, thine iniquity is done away. He will no more banish thee. He hath visited thine iniquities, daughter of Edom. He hath exposed thee for thy sins.
LAM 5:1 Remember, Lord, what hath befallen us: look down
LAM 5:2 and behold our reproach. Our inheritance is transferred to strangers; our houses to foreigners.
LAM 5:3 We are become orphans. Our father is no more. Our mothers are like widows.
LAM 5:4 Our water we have drunk for money. Our wood came by barter on our shoulders.
LAM 5:5 We have been persecuted. We have laboured and have had no rest.
LAM 5:6 Egypt laid to a hand; Assyria, till they were satisfied.
LAM 5:7 Our fathers sinned; they are no more. We have borne their transgressions.
LAM 5:8 Slaves have got dominion over us; there is none to deliver us out of their hand.
LAM 5:9 At the peril of our lives we must gather in our corn, because of the sword of the desert.
LAM 5:10 Our skin is black as an oven. They are shrivelled up by storms of famine.
LAM 5:11 Our wives are humbled in Sion; our virgins in the cities of Juda.
LAM 5:12 Our chiefs were hanged up by their hands; our elders were held in no esteem.
LAM 5:13 Our warriors took up a lamentation; and our youths fainted under a club.
LAM 5:14 Our elders have ceased to attend at the gates, and our chosen men have ceased from their songs.
LAM 5:15 The joy of our heart is at an end; our dance is turned into mourning.
LAM 5:16 Our crown is fallen from our head; alas for us! for we have sinned.
LAM 5:17 Because of this, grief is come upon us; our heart is full of sorrow: because of this, our eyes are dim.
LAM 5:18 On mount Sion, because it is desolate, foxes have walked about.
LAM 5:19 But thou, Lord, wilt inhabit it forever: thy throne is for all generations.
LAM 5:20 Why wilt thou utterly forget us? Wilt thou leave1 us for length of days?
LAM 5:21 Turn us to thee, Lord, and we shall be turned and renew our days as heretofore. Because thou wast cast off, thou hast cast us off; thou hast been provoked against us to a high degree.
EZE 1:1 In the thirtieth year, and fourth month, on the fifth day of the month, when I was among the captives by the river Chobar, the heavens were opened and I saw the visions of God.
EZE 1:2 On the fifth of that month [this was the fifth year of the captivity of king Jechonias]
EZE 1:3 the word of the Lord came to Ezekiel son of Buzi the priest, in the land of the Chaldeans, by the river Chobar. And the hand of the Lord was upon me,
EZE 1:4 and I looked, and lo! a whirlwind came from the north, and with it a great cloud surrounded with a splendor of flashing fire; and in the midst thereof, an appearance like that of amber in the middle of the fire,
EZE 1:5 and a splendor in it. And in the middle, a resemblance like that of four living beings. And this was the appearance of them. They had a resemblance of a man in them.
EZE 1:6 And each had four faces, and each had four wings; and their legs were straight
EZE 1:7 and their feet winged and sparking like sparkling brass. And their wings had a quick motion.
EZE 1:8 And underneath their wings on their four sides was a man's hand.
EZE 1:9 And the faces of the four turned not when they went. They marched forward each having a face on every side.
EZE 1:10 And with regard to the similitude of their faces, the four had the face of a man with the face of a lion, on the right; and on the left the four had the face of a bullock, and the four had a face of an eagle.
EZE 1:11 And the wings of the four were expanded upwards, each having a pair expanded adjoining each other and a pair folded on their body.
EZE 1:12 And they moved on, each straight forward, which way soever the wind was moving, they moved on, and turned not.
EZE 1:13 And in the midst of the four living beings, was an appearance like that of glowing coals of fire, resembling lamps whirling round between the
EZE 1:14 living beings with a splendor of fire, and from the fire lightnings flashed.
EZE 1:15 And I beheld and lo! on the ground, close to the four living beings a wheel! one to every of the four.
EZE 1:16 And the appearance of the wheels was like the appearance of a beryl. And the four had one and the same likeness. And their workmanship was as if there was a wheel within a wheel.
EZE 1:17 They ran on their four sections and shifted not their position when they ran,
EZE 1:18 nor did their felloes when they were elevated. And I beheld, and their felloes were full of eyes, all around the four.
EZE 1:19 And when the living beings moved on, the wheels moved on close by them. And when the living beings mounted up from the earth, the wheels mounted up.
EZE 1:20 Wherever the cloud was, there was the wind for their movement; the wheels moved on and were carried aloft with them. Because there was a breath of life in the wheels, when the living beings moved on, the wheels moved on:
EZE 1:21 when those stood still, these stood still: and when those mounted up from the earth, these mounted up with them, because there was a breath of life in the wheels.
EZE 1:22 And over the head of the living beings, there was a likeness resembling a firmament, like the appearance of chrystal over their wings, which were expanded above them.
EZE 1:23 And their wings which were expanded below the firmament, flapped one against another, while every one had a pair that covered their bodies.
EZE 1:24 And when they moved on I heard the sound of their wings like the sound of much water: but when they stopped, their wings were still.
EZE 1:25 And lo! a voice from above the firmament!
EZE 1:26 this being over their heads, there was an appearance like that of a sapphire stone and a resemblance of a throne upon it. And upon the resemblance of the throne a resemblance like the appearance of a man above.
EZE 1:27 And I saw a resemblance of amber from the appearance of the loins and upwards; and from the appearance of the loins and downwards, I saw an appearance of fire: and the splendor thereof round about
EZE 1:28 was like the bow which is in the clouds in a showery day. Such was the state of the splendor round about.
EZE 2:1 This was the vision of the likeness of the glory of the Lord. And when I saw it, I fell on my face and I heard a voice of one speaking and he said to me, Son of man, stand on thy feet and I will speak to thee.
EZE 2:2 Whereupon a blast of wind came upon me and took me and lifted me up and set me on my feet and I heard him speaking to me and he said to me,
EZE 2:3 Son of man, I am about to send thee to the house of Israel, to them who are provoking me; who have provoked me, both they and their fathers even to this day.
EZE 2:4 And thou shalt say unto them, "Thus saith the Lord,
EZE 2:5 "whether they hear or be affrighted; [for they are a provoking house] and let them know that thou art a prophet among them.
EZE 2:6 And thou son of man, be not afraid of them nor daunted at their presence. Because they will sting thee and rise up against thee on all sides and thou dwellest in the midst of scorpions, be not afraid of their words nor terrified at their looks; because they are a provoking house,
EZE 2:7 therefore thou shalt deliver my words to them whether they hear or be affrighted.
EZE 2:8 Because they are a provoking house, thou therefore, son of man, hear him who is speaking to thee and be not thou rebellious like this rebellious house. Open thy mouth and eat what I give thee.
EZE 2:9 Then I looked, and lo! a hand stretched out towards me and in it a roll of a book
EZE 2:10 and he unfolded it before me and there were writings on it on both sides. And the writings were funeral odes and songs of woe.
EZE 3:1 And he said to me, Son of man eat this roll and go and speak to the children of Israel.
EZE 3:2 And when he had opened my mouth and put the roll into it, he said to me, Son of man,
EZE 3:3 Let thy mouth eat and thy belly be filled with this roll which is given thee. So I ate it, and it was in my mouth sweet as honey.
EZE 3:4 Then he said to me, Son of man, go and get thee to the house of Israel and speak to them these words of mine,
EZE 3:5 seeing thou art sent to the house of Israel; not to a people of strange language,
EZE 3:6 nor to many tribes of strange and foreign tongues, nor to them whose pronunciation is harsh and whose words thou canst not understand; though had I sent thee to such they might have hearkened to thee.
EZE 3:7 But the house of Israel will not hearken to thee, since they are not willing to hearken to me. Because all the house of Israel are contentious and stubborn,
EZE 3:8 therefore behold I have made thy face strong against their faces, and I will invigorate thy struggle against their struggling
EZE 3:9 and it shall be on all occasions firmer than a rock. Be not afraid of them nor daunted at their countenance, because they are a provoking house.
EZE 3:10 Then he said to me, Son of man, lay up in thy heart all the words which I have spoken to thee; and
EZE 3:11 having heard with thine ears go get thee to the captivity, to the children of thy people, and thou shalt speak to them and say to them, "Thus saith the Lord," whether they hear or forbear.
EZE 3:12 Then a blast of wind took me up and I heard behind me a sound of a great earthquake, "Blessed be the glory of the Lord from this place of his:"
EZE 3:13 whereupon I looked towards the sound and saw that this sound of an earthquake was that of the wings flapping one against another and that of the wheels near them.
EZE 3:14 Then the blast lifted me up and bore me aloft and I went by the impulse of my own spirit, and the hand of the Lord upon me was strong,
EZE 3:15 and being borne aloft I came to the captivity and went round among them who dwelt by the river Chobar; among them who were there. And I abode there seven days conversing with them.
EZE 3:16 And after these seven days a word of the Lord came to me saying, "Son of man;
EZE 3:17 I have made thee a watchman to the house of Israel; therefore thou shalt hear a word from my mouth and warn them from me.
EZE 3:18 When I say to the unrighteous, Thou shalt surely die, and thou hast not warned the unrighteous to turn from his ways that he may live; that unrighteous man shall die for his iniquity; but his blood I will require at thy hand.
EZE 3:19 But if thou hast warned the unrighteous and he will not turn from his iniquity and from his way; that unrighteous man shall die for his iniquity, and thou shalt deliver thy soul.
EZE 3:20 So when a righteous man turneth from his righteous acts and shall commit transgression though I lay the punishment before him; he shall die. Because thou hast not warned him, though he indeed shall die for his sins [for his righteous acts will not be remembered; yet his blood I will require at thy hand.
EZE 3:21 But if thou hast warned the righteous man not to sin and he sinneth not; the righteous man shall live; and because thou hast warned him, thou shalt deliver thy soul.
EZE 3:22 Then the hand of the Lord was upon me; and he said to me, Arise and go out to the plain and I will there speak to thee.
EZE 3:23 So I arose and went out to the plain; and behold the glory of the Lord stood there like the vision and like the glory of the Lord which I saw by the river Chobar. Whereupon I fell on my face.
EZE 3:24 And a blast of wind came upon me and set me on my feet, and he spoke to me and said to me, Go and shut thyself up in thy house.
EZE 3:25 Now son of man, behold chains are prepared for thee; and thou shalt be bound with them and shalt not get out of them.
EZE 3:26 And I will bind up thy tongue, that thou mayst be dumb and not be to them a reprover, because they are a rebellious house.
EZE 3:27 And when I speak to thee, I will open thy mouth and thou shalt say to them, Thus saith the Lord, whoso heareth let him hear; and let him who is disobedient, be disobedient, since they are a rebellious house.
EZE 4:1 And thou son of man, take thee a tile and set it before thee and portray thereon the city Jerusalem;
EZE 4:2 and thou shalt lay siege to it and build mounts against it and throw up a circumvallation around it and pitch camps against it and arrange the towers for engines round about.
EZE 4:3 Then take thee an iron pan and place it as an iron wall between thee and the city and set thy face against it and it shall be besieged and thou shalt besiege it. This is a sign for the children of Israel.
EZE 4:4 And thou shalt lie on thy left side and lay on it the iniquities of the house of Israel. According to the number of the hundred and fifty days which thou shalt lie upon it thou shalt bear their iniquities.
EZE 4:5 Now I have given thee their iniquities to the number of a hundred and ninety days. So when thou hast taken the iniquities of the house of Israel and finished them,
EZE 4:6 thou shalt lie on thy right side and bear the iniquities of the house of Juda forty days. I have given thee a day for a year.
EZE 4:7 Therefore thou shalt prepare thy face for the siege of Jerusalem and strengthen thine arm and prophesy against it.
EZE 4:8 And behold I have given chains for thee that thou mayst not turn from one of thy sides to the other until the days of thy siege are accomplished.
EZE 4:9 Provide therefore for thyself wheat and barley and beans and lentiles and millet and rye and put them into an earthen vessel and make them into loaves for thyself according to the number of the days which thou liest on thy side, to be eaten in the course of a hundred and ninety days.
EZE 4:10 And thou shalt eat thy bread by weight, twenty shekels a day. From time to time thou shalt eat it:
EZE 4:11 and thou shalt drink water by measure, namely the sixth of an hin to be drunk at stated times.
EZE 4:12 And thou shalt eat the loaves baked like barley cakes on the hearth, and thou shalt bake them in their sight with a fire made of human ordure and
EZE 4:13 shalt say, Thus saith the Lord the God of Israel, So shall the children of Israel eat impure meats among the nations.
EZE 4:14 Upon this I said, Not so: Lord God of Israel, seeing my soul hath not been polluted with impurity. Even from my birth to this day I have not eaten what died of itself, or was torn by wild beasts, nor hath any tainted flesh ever entered my mouth.
EZE 4:15 Thereupon he said to me, Behold I have given thee the dung of cattle instead of human ordure that thou mayst bake thy loaves with it.
EZE 4:16 Moreover he said to me, son of man, Behold I break the staff of bread in Jerusalem and they shall eat bread by weight and with scantiness; and they shall drink water by measure and with faintness;
EZE 4:17 that they may be in want of bread and water and perish, one and all, and be wasted away for their iniquities.
EZE 5:1 And thou son of man, take thee a knife sharper than a barber's razor and having procured such a one thou shalt pass it over thy head and thy beard. Then thou shalt take a pair of scales; and having weighed the hair
EZE 5:2 thou shalt burn the fourth part of it with fire, in the space before the city; during the completion of the days of the siege. And thou shalt take another fourth part and burn it in the midst of the city; and thou shalt hack with the sword another fourth part, around the city; and the other fourth part thou shalt scatter to the wind and I will draw out a sword after them.
EZE 5:3 But of this parcel thou shalt take a few in number and tie them up in thy mantle.
EZE 5:4 Yet even of these thou shalt take some and cast them into the midst of the fire and burn them with fire which shall come out of the city and thou shalt say to all the house of Israel
EZE 5:5 thus saith the Lord, This is Jerusalem. I placed her in the midst of nations and the countries around her,
EZE 5:6 that thou shouldst tell my rules of rectitude to such of the nations as are without law; and that mine ordinances might be the ordinances of the countries around her. Because they rejected my rules of rectitude and did not walk by mine ordinances;
EZE 5:7 therefore thus saith the Lord, Because you have taken your bent from the nations around you, and have not walked in my statutes, nor practised my rules of rectitude, nor acted even conformably to the moral precepts of the nations around you; therefore thus saith the Lord,
EZE 5:8 Behold I am against thee; and in the midst of thee I will execute judgment in the sight of the nations,
EZE 5:9 and do to thee according to all thine abominations, what I have not done, and the like of which I will not do any more.
EZE 5:10 For this cause fathers shall eat children in the midst of thee; and children shall eat fathers. And I will execute judgment upon thee, and scatter all the remnant of thee to every wind.
EZE 5:11 For this cause, as I live saith the Lord, Because thou hast polluted my holy things with all thine abominations; therefore I will cast thee off; mine eye shall not spare nor will I have compassion.
EZE 5:12 The fourth part of thee shall be consumed with pestilence; and the fourth part of thee shall perish by famine in the midst of thee; and the fourth part of thee shall fall by the sword around thee; and I will make bare a sword to pursue them.
EZE 5:13 And my wrath shall be spent, and mine indignation, on them; and thou shalt know why I the Lord have spoken in my zeal, when I have executed mine indignation on them.
EZE 5:14 And I will make thee and thy daughters around thee, a desolation, in the sight of every one who passeth by.
EZE 5:15 And thou shalt be an object of lamentation and horror to the nations around thee, when I have executed judgment on thee with mine avenging wrath: I the lord have spoken.
EZE 5:16 For when I have sent against them my shafts of famine and they shall be for destruction,
EZE 5:17 I will break thy staff of bread and send against thee famine and wild beasts; and punish thee; and death and blood shall pass through upon thee: and I will bring a sword against thee from all around; I the lord have spoken.
EZE 6:1 Again a word of the lord came to me, saying,
EZE 6:2 Son of man set thy face against the mountains of Israel and prophesy against them
EZE 6:3 and thou shalt say, mountains of Israel, hear a word of the lord; Thus saith the lord to the mountains and hills, and to the vales and the forests, Behold I am bringing a sword against you; and your high places shall be destroyed;
EZE 6:4 and your altars and your temples shall be trodden down; and I will cast down your slain before your idols;
EZE 6:5 and scatter your bones around your altars and in all your dwelling places.
EZE 6:6 The cities shall be laid waste and the high places desolated, that your altars may be utterly destroyed: and your idols shall be trampled down, when your Fanes are removed;
EZE 6:7 and your wounded shall fall in the midst of you; and you shall know that I am the lord.
EZE 6:8 When some of you, who have escaped from the sword, are among the nations and in your dispersions through the countries;
EZE 6:9 then shall those of you, who have escaped, remember me among the nations whither they have been carried captives. With their heart which is going a whoring from me, and with their eyes, which are going a whoring after their own devices [I have sworn] they shall bewail themselves for all their abominations
EZE 6:10 and acknowledge that I the lord have spoken.
EZE 6:11 Thus saith the lord, Clap with thy hand, and stamp with thy foot, and say, Ha! ha! to all the abominations of the house of Israel. By sword and by pestilence, and by famine they shall fall.
EZE 6:12 He who is near shall fall by the sword; and he who is far off, shall die by pestilence; and he who is besieged shall be consumed by famine. And I will accomplish my fury on them.
EZE 6:13 And you shall know that I am the Lord, when your slain are in the midst of your idols, around your altars, on every lofty mount, and under every shady tree, where they offered a sweet smelling savour to all their idols.
EZE 6:14 For I will stretch forth my hand against them; and make the land a desolation and a scene of destruction, from the wilderness of Deblatha through all their habitations; and you shall know that I am the Lord.
EZE 7:1 Again a word of the Lord came to me saying, And thou son of man say,
EZE 7:2 "Thus saith the Lord, To the land of Israel an end is coming.
EZE 7:3 [6] The end is come upon the four wings of the land. The end is coming on thee who inhabitest the land. The time is come.
EZE 7:4 [7] The day hath approached, not with commotions nor with pangs.
EZE 7:5 [8] Now near at hand I pour out mine indignation on thee; and upon thee I will spend my wrath; and judge thee for thy ways, and retribute to thee all thine abominations.
EZE 7:6 [9] Mine eye shall not spare, nor will I have compassion. Because I will retribute to thee thy ways, when thine abominations shall be in the midst of thee; therefore thou shalt know that it is I the Lord who smite thee.
EZE 7:7 [3] Now the end is upon thee. I will send it against thee, and punish thee for thy ways and retribute to thee all thine abominations.
EZE 7:8 [4] Mine eye shall not spare, nor will I have compassion. Because I will recompense upon thee thy ways, when thine abominations shall be in the midst of thee; therefore thou shalt acknowledge that I am the Lord.
EZE 7:9 [5]For thus saith the Lord, Lo! the end is coming.
EZE 7:10 Behold it is the day of the Lord. If indeed the rod hath budded,
EZE 7:11 pride hath come to a full growth. Therefore he will break the stay of the unrighteous; but not with commotion nor with perturbation.
EZE 7:12 The end is come. Behold the day! let not him who purchaseth rejoice, nor him who selleth, mourn;
EZE 7:13 since he who purchaseth shall no more return to him who selleth. Nor will any man hold with an eye to life.
EZE 7:14 Sound the trumpet and pass sentence on all together.
EZE 7:15 Abroad let there be battle with the sword, and at home famine and pestilence. Let him who is in the field die by the sword; and them in the city let famine and pestilence destroy.
EZE 7:16 Now shall they escape who escape from among them? When they shall be on the mountains, I will indeed slay all, every one for his iniquities.
EZE 7:17 All hands shall be enfeebled and all thighs stained with filth.
EZE 7:18 And they shall gird on sackcloth; and amazement shall cover them. And shame shall be on all their faces: and on every head, baldness.
EZE 7:19 Their silver shall be thrown in the streets; and their gold shall be disregarded. Their souls shall not be satisfied; nor shall their bellies be filled: because the punishment of their iniquities is come.
EZE 7:20 With their choice apparel which was laid by for ostentation; even with this they adorned the images of their abominations; therefore I have given it to them for defilement;
EZE 7:21 even into the hand of strangers I will deliver it for plunder, and to be a spoil for the ravagers of the earth; and they shall defile it.
EZE 7:22 And I will turn away my face from them; and they shall pollute the places under my peculiar inspection, and come into them unobserved, and profane them
EZE 7:23 and make them an abomination. Because the land is full of peoples, and the city is full of iniquity;
EZE 7:24 therefore I will turn back their tumultuous power, and their holy things shall be polluted.
EZE 7:25 Though an atonement shall come and seek peace, it shall be no more.
EZE 7:26 Woe shall succeed woe; and news be followed by news; and a vision shall be sought from a prophet: and law shall perish from the priest, and counsel from the elders;
EZE 7:27 the chief shall be clothed with darkness; and the hands of the people of the land shall be weakened. According to their ways I will deal with them; and for their crimes I will punish them; and they shall know that I am the Lord.
EZE 8:1 Again in the sixth year in the fifth month, on the fifth of the month as I was sitting at home, and the elders of Juda, were sitting before me, the hand of the Lord came upon me.
EZE 8:2 And I looked and lo! a likeness of a man! From his loins downward was fire, and from his loins upward was an appearance like that of amber.
EZE 8:3 And he stretched forth the similitude of a hand and took hold of me by the crown of the head and a blast of wind lifted me up between heaven and earth, and in a vision of God, brought me to Jerusalem, to the vestibule of the gate facing the north, where was the pillar of the possessor.
EZE 8:4 And behold the glory of the Lord God of Israel was there, such in appearance as I saw in the plain.
EZE 8:5 And he said to me, Son of man, look up with thine eyes towards the north. So I looked up with mine eyes towards the north, and behold from the north to the gate facing the east.
EZE 8:6 And he said to me, Son of man hast thou seen what they are doing, They are committing great iniquities here that they may abstain from my holy things: but thou shalt see still greater iniquities.
EZE 8:7 Then he led me into the vestibule of the court,
EZE 8:8 and said to me, Son of man, dig. So I digged and lo! a door.
EZE 8:9 And he said to me, Go in and see the transgressions which they are committing here.
EZE 8:10 So I went in and beheld, and lo! vain abominations and all the idols of the house of Israel portrayed upon them round about
EZE 8:11 and seventy men of the elders of the house of Israel; and Jechonias the son of Saphan in the midst stood foremost, and every one had a censer in his hand, and the smoke of the incense ascended.
EZE 8:12 And he said to me, Hast thou seen, son of man, what the elders of the house of Israel are doing, every one of them in this hidden apartment of theirs? For they said, The Lord doth not see. The Lord hath forsaken this land.
EZE 8:13 Then he said to me thou shalt see still greater transgressions which they are committing.
EZE 8:14 Then he led me to the vestibule of the gate of the house of the Lord facing the north, and behold here were women seated, singing mournful ditties to Thammuz.
EZE 8:15 And he said to me, Son of man, hast thou seen? Thou shalt see still worse devices than these.
EZE 8:16 Then he led me into the inner court of the house of the Lord; and at the vestibule of the temple of the Lord, between the ailams and the altar, were about twenty men; their backs to the temple of the Lord, and their faces the direct contrary way; and they were worshipping the sun.
EZE 8:17 And he said to me, Hast thou seen? Son of man. Is it a light thing for the house of Juda to commit the transgressions, which they have committed here? Because they have filled the land with iniquity, and lo! they are as it were insulting me to my face.[Note: Here something seems to be wanting. I apprehend; it was the people sacrificing to idols on the house tops.]
EZE 8:18 therefore I will deal with them with wrath. Mine eye shall not spare, nor will I have compassion.
EZE 9:1 Then in my hearing he cried with a loud voice and said, The punishment of this city is at hand, and every one hath in his hand the instruments of the destruction.
EZE 9:2 Thereupon behold there came from the way of the high gate, which faceth the north, six men, every one with his battle axe in his hand; and in the midst of them a man clothed in a long robe and a girdle of sapphire about his loins. And when they came close to the brazen altar,
EZE 9:3 the glory of the God of Israel which was upon the cherubims ascended from them and came to the open part of the house and called the man who was clothed with the long robe and who had a girdle about his loins,
EZE 9:4 and said to him, Go through the midst of Jerusalem and put a mark on the forehead of those men who are sighing and sorrowing for all the transgressions which are committed among them;
EZE 9:5 and to the others he said in my hearing, Go ye after him into the city and smite and spare not with your eyes nor shew compassion.
EZE 9:6 Destroy utterly old men and young, virgins and infants and married women; but go not near any of those who have the mark on them. Begin at my sanctuary. So they began with the men the elders who were in the house.
EZE 9:7 And he said to them, Defile this house and fill the ways with dead as you are going out and continue the slaughter.
EZE 9:8 And while they were slaying them I fell on my face and cried aloud and said, Ah! Lord! art thou utterly destroying the remnant of Israel by pouring out thy wrath on Jerusalem?
EZE 9:9 Whereupon he said to me, The iniquity of the house of Israel and Juda is exceeding great. Because the land is filled with many peoples and the city is filled with iniquity and impurity; and because they said, the Lord hath forsaken this land; the Lord doth not see;
EZE 9:10 therefore mine eye shall not spare nor will I have compassion. I have requited their ways upon their heads.
EZE 9:11 Then, lo! the man who was clothed with the long robe and girded about the loins with the girdle came and made report, saying, I have done as thou orderedst me.
EZE 10:1 Thereupon I looked, and behold above the firmament which was over the head of the cherubims, there was a resemblance of a throne above them like a sapphire stone.
EZE 10:2 And he said to the man who was clothed with the long robe, Go in between the wheels which are under the cherubims and fill thy hands with coals of fire from the midst of the cherubims and scatter them over the city. So in my sight he went in.
EZE 10:3 Now the cherubims stood on the right side of the house as a man goeth in, and the cloud filled the inner court.
EZE 10:4 And the glory of the Lord had removed from the cherubims to the open part of the house and the cloud filled the house and the court was filled with the splendour of the glory of the Lord:
EZE 10:5 and the sound of the wings of the cherubims was heard to the outer court like the voice of God Saddai speaking.
EZE 10:6 And when he had given orders to the man clothed with the holy robe, saying, Take fire from the midst of the wheels from between the cherubims and he had gone in and stood near the wheels,
EZE 10:7 one stretched out his hand into the midst of the fire, which was between the cherubims and took and put it into the hands of him who was clothed with the holy robe and he took it and went out.
EZE 10:8 Now I saw that the cherubims had the likeness of men's hands under their wings.
EZE 10:9 I looked also and lo! four wheels stood close to the cherubims, one wheel close to each cherub; and the appearance of the wheels was like the appearance of a carbuncle stone.
EZE 10:10 And as for their appearance, the four had one and the same likeness, as if there was a wheel within a wheel.
EZE 10:11 When they ran, they ran on their four sections. They altered not their position when they ran, for which way soever the foremost looked, they ran and altered not their position when they ran.
EZE 10:12 Now their backs and their hands and their wings and the wheels were full of eyes all around the four wheels.
EZE 10:13 And in my hearing these wheels were called Gelgel [Note: Chaldean Galgal: wheel or rolling thing; whirlwind].
EZE 10:14 [Omitted]
EZE 10:15 And the cherubims were the same living being which I saw by the river Chobar.
EZE 10:16 And when the cherubims marched on, the wheels ran and kept close to them; and when the cherubims lifted up their wings and were borne aloft from the earth, their wheels altered not their position.
EZE 10:17 When those stood these stood; and when those mounted up; these mounted up with them, for there was a breath of life in them.
EZE 10:18 Then the glory of the Lord went out from the house and mounted up upon the cherubims;
EZE 10:19 and the cherubims raised their wings and mounted up from the earth in my sight. When they went out the wheels were close by them. And they stopped at the vestibule of the gate of the house of the Lord which was over against the house and the glory of the God of Israel was above over them.
EZE 10:20 This was the living being which I saw under the God of Israel at the river Chobar, and I knew that it was the cherubims.
EZE 10:21 Every one had four faces, and every one had eight wings, and the likeness of mens' hands under their wings.
EZE 10:22 And as for the likeness of their faces, these were the same faces which I saw under the glory of the God of Israel at the river Chobar and they marched every one straight forward.

EZE 11:2 And the Lord said to me, son of man, these are the men who devise vanities and who give bad advice in the city,
EZE 11:3 who say, Are not the houses lately rebuilt? This is the cauldron, but we are the flesh.
EZE 11:4 Therefore prophesy against them. Prophesy, Son of man.

EZE 11:9 and drag you out of the midst of it and deliver you into the hands of strangers and execute judgment upon you.
