MAT 3:12 His winnowing instrument is in his hand. He will thoroughly clean his floor, and gather his wheat for the granary; but the chaff he will burn with unquenchable fire."
MAT 3:13 Then cometh Jesus from Galilee, along the Jordan, to John, to be baptized by him:
MAT 3:14 but John earnestly opposed him, saying, "I have need to be baptized by thee. And thou comest to me!"
MAT 3:15 And Jesus in reply said to him, "Permit this at present: for thus it becometh us to confirm all righteousness." Then John permitteth him;
MAT 3:16 and Jesus being baptized was just coming up from the water, when lo! the heavens were opened for him, and John saw the spirit of God descending like a dove and coming upon Jesus;
MAT 3:17 and lo! a voice from heaven said,"This is my son, the Beloved, in whom I am well pleased."
MAT 4:1 Then Jesus was led up by the spirit into the wilderness to be tempted by the devil.
MAT 4:2 And having fasted forty days and forty nights, he was at last hungry.
MAT 4:3 Whereupon the tempter coming to him, said, If thou art Son of God, command these stones to become loaves.
MAT 4:4 In reply to which, Jesus said, It is written, "Man can live not by bread only, but by anything which God is pleased to appoint."
MAT 4:5 Then the devil taketh him along to the holy city and placeth him on the battlement of the temple,
MAT 4:6 and saith to him, If thou art Son of God, cast thyself down; for it is written, "He will give his angels a charge concerning thee, and with their hands they will bear thee up shouldst thou perchance strike thy foot against a stone."
MAT 4:7 Jesus said to him, It is also written, "Thou shall not try the Lord thy God."
MAT 4:8 Again the devil taketh him along with him to a very high mountain and pointeth out to him all the kingdoms of the world and the glory of them,
MAT 4:9 and saith to him, All these I will give thee if thou wilt prostrate thyself and worship me.
MAT 4:10 Whereupon Jesus said to him, "Be gone, Satan: for it is written, "Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God and serve him alone.
MAT 4:11 Then the devil leaveth him, and lo! angels came and ministered to him.
MAT 4:12 Now when Jesus heard that John was committed to prison he withdrew into Galilee;
MAT 4:13 and having left Nazareth he went and dwelt at Capernaum, a sea port at the confines of Zebulon and Nephthaleim;
MAT 4:14 so that there was an accomplishment of what was spoken by the prophet Esaias saying,
MAT 4:15 "The land of Zabulon and the land of Nephthaleim, the sea coast, the banks of the Jordan, Galilee of the nations;
MAT 4:16 the people who sat in darkness saw a great light; and to them who sat in the region and shadow of death, light is sprung up."
MAT 4:17 From that time Jesus began to make proclamation and say, "Reform; for the reign of the heavens is at hand."
MAT 4:18 Now as Jesus was walking along the sea of Galilee, he saw two brothers, Simon called Peter, and Andrew his brother, casting a drag net into the sea; for they were fishermen;
MAT 4:19 and he said to them, Follow me and I will make you fishers of men.
MAT 4:20 Thereupon they immediately left their nets and followed him.
MAT 4:21 And passing on he saw other two brothers, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, in the vessel with their father Zebedee, mending their nets, and he called them.
MAT 4:22 Whereupon they immediately left the vessel and their father, and followed him.
MAT 4:23 Then Jesus went through all Galilee teaching in their synagogues, and proclaiming the good news of the reign and curing every disease, and every malady among the people.
MAT 4:24 And the fame of him spread through all Syria; and they brought to him all their sick, seized and tormented with various distempers"demoniacs, and lunatics and paralytics, and he cured them.
MAT 4:25 And great multitudes followed him from Galilee, and Decapolis and Jerusalem and Judea, and from the banks of the Jordan.
MAT 5:1 On seeing these multitudes he went up to the mount and sat down, and his disciples came to him,
MAT 5:2 and he opened his mouth and taught them, saying,
MAT 5:3 Happy the poor in spirit; for the kingdom of the heavens is theirs.
MAT 5:4 Happy they who mourn; for they shall be comforted.
MAT 5:5 Happy the meek; for they shall inherit the land.
MAT 5:6 Happy they who hunger and thirst for righteousness; for they shall be satisfied.
MAT 5:7 Happy the merciful; for they shall obtain mercy.
MAT 5:8 Happy the pure in heart; for they shall see God.
MAT 5:9 Happy the peace makers; for they shall be called children of God.
MAT 5:10 Happy they who are persecuted for righteousness' sake; for the kingdom of the heavens is theirs.
MAT 5:11 Happy are ye when men will revile and persecute you, and accuse you falsely of every evil thing on my account.
MAT 5:12 Rejoice and exult triumphantly; for great will be your reward in heaven: for thus they persecuted the prophets who were before you.
MAT 5:13 You are the salt of the earth. Now if the salt become insipid, with what can it be made salt? It is no longer fit for any thing, but to be thrown out of doors, and trampled under foot by men.
MAT 5:14 You are the light of the world. A city situate on a mountain cannot be hid.
MAT 5:15 A lamp is not lighted and put under the corn measure, but on the stand, that it may give light to all the family.
MAT 5:16 Thus let your light shine before men, that they may see your good works and glorify your father who is in heaven.
MAT 5:17 Do not imagine that I am come to annul the law and the prophets. I am not come to annul, but to confirm them.
MAT 5:18 For verily I say to you, Until that heaven and this earth shall have passed away, not one jot nor a tittle of the law shall be annulled till all be accomplished.
MAT 5:19 Therefore whosoever shall weaken the force of one of the commandments, were it even the least, and teach men accordingly, he shall be the least esteemed in the reign of the heavens; but whoever shall practise and teach them, he shall be highly esteemed in the reign of the heavens.
MAT 5:20 For I say to you, Unless your righteousness exceed that of the Scribes and Pharisees, you can in no wise enter the kingdom of the heavens.
MAT 5:21 You have heard that it was said to them of old, "Thou shalt not commit murder." And, "Whosoever shall commit murder shall be liable to the sentence of the judges."
MAT 5:22 But I say to you, Whosoever is angry with his brother without cause, shall be liable to the sentence of the judges: and whoever shall say to his brother, Raca, [a contemptuous word] shall be liable to the sentence of the Sanhedrim; and whoever shall say, Moreh, [a reproachful word] shall be liable [to be sentenced] to the vale of fire.
MAT 5:23 If therefore thou bring thy gift to the altar and recollect there that thy brother hath ground of complaint against thee;
MAT 5:24 leave there thy gift before the altar and go away. First of all be reconciled with thy brother, and then come and offer thy gift.
MAT 5:25 Come speedily to a friendly agreement with thine adversary, whilst thou art on the road with him; lest the adversary deliver thee up to the judge; and the judge consign thee to the officer, and thou be thrown into prison.
MAT 5:26 Verily I say to thee, thou shalt not be released until thou hast discharged the last farthing.
MAT 5:27 You have heard that it hath been said to the ancients, "Thou shalt not commit adultery."
MAT 5:28 But I say to you, whoever looketh on a married woman so as to lust after her, hath already committed adultery with her in his heart.
MAT 5:29 Therefore if thy right eye cause thee to stumble, pluck it out and cast it from thee; for it is better for thee to lose one of thy members, than that thy whole body be cast into a vale of fire.
MAT 5:30 And if thy right hand causeth thee to stumble, cut it off and cast it from thee; for it is better for thee to lose one of thy members, than that thy whole body be cast into a vale of fire.
MAT 5:31 It hath also been said, Whosoever would put away his wife, let him give her a bill of divorce.
MAT 5:32 But I say to you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except for whoredom, causeth her to commit adultery: and whoever shall marry her who is put away, committeth adultery.
MAT 5:33 Again you have heard that it hath been said to the ancients, Thou shalt not forswear thyself; but shalt perform thine oaths to the Lord.
MAT 5:34 But I say to you, Swear not at all: neither by heaven, for it is God's throne:
MAT 5:35 nor by the earth, for it is his footstool; nor by Jerusalem; for it is the city of the great king,
MAT 5:36 neither shalt thou swear by thy head; for thou canst not make one hair white or black.
MAT 5:37 But let your word yes, be yes; and your no, no; for whatever exceedeth these, proceedeth from that which is evil.
MAT 5:38 You have heard that it was said, "An eye for an eye: and a tooth for a tooth."
MAT 5:39 But I say to you, Contend not with the injurious: but if one smite thee on the right cheek, turn to him the other also.
MAT 5:40 And if any determine to sue thee at law for thy vest, give it up to him, nay were it even thy mantle.
MAT 5:41 And if one press thee to go one mile, go with him two.
MAT 5:42 Give to him who asketh thee. And from him who would borrow of thee, turn not thou away.
MAT 5:43 You have heard that it was said, "Thou shalt love thy neighbour and hate thine enemy."
MAT 5:44 But I say to you, Love your enemies. Bless them who curse you. Do good to them who hate you: and pray for them who spitefully use you and persecute you;
MAT 5:45 that you may be the children of your Father in heaven: for he causeth the sun to rise on bad and good, and sendeth the rain on just and unjust.
MAT 5:46 For if you love them who love you, what reward have you? Do not even the publicans the same?
MAT 5:47 And if you salute your brethren only, wherein do ye excel? Do not even the publicans do the same?
MAT 5:48 You therefore are to be perfect, as your Father, who is in heaven, is perfect.
MAT 6:1 Take heed not to practise your righteousness before men in order to be observed by them; otherwise you have no reward from your father who is in heaven.
MAT 6:2 Therefore when thou dost an act of charity, sound not a trumpet before thee as the hypocrites do in the synagogues and in the streets that they may be extolled by men. Verily I say to you, they have their reward.
MAT 6:3 But when thou art doing an act of charity, let not thy left hand know what thy right hand is doing;
MAT 6:4 that thine act of charity may be in secret; and thy father who seeth in secret will himself reward thee openly.
MAT 6:5 And when thou prayest, be not like the hypocrites. Because they love to pray standing in the synagogues and at the corners of the streets that men may observe them; verily I say to you, They have their reward.
MAT 6:6 But as for thee, when thou wouldst pray, retire to thy closet, and having shut the door pray to thy father who is in secret, and thy father who seeth in secret will reward thee openly.
MAT 6:7 And when you pray, use not a vain multiplicity of words as the heathen do. For they think they shall be heard for their much speaking.
MAT 6:8 Be not ye therefore like them; for your father knoweth what things you have need of, before you ask him.
MAT 6:9 In this manner therefore pray ye, "Our Father, who art in the heavens, hallowed be thy name;
MAT 6:10 thy reign come; thy will be done on the earth, as it is in heaven;
MAT 6:11 give us to day our daily bread;
MAT 6:12 and forgive us our debts, as we do forgive our debtors;
MAT 6:13 and bring us not into temptation, but deliver us from evil [for thine is the kingdom and the power and the glory for the ages, amen.
MAT 6:14 For if you forgive men their offences, your heavenly father will also forgive you;
MAT 6:15 but if you do not forgive men their offences, neither will your father forgive your offences.
MAT 6:16 And when you fast, be not like the hypocrites, of a dismal countenance; for they disfigure their faces, that men may observe that they are fasting. Verily I say to you, They have their reward.
MAT 6:17 But when thou keepest a fast, anoint thy head and wash thy face,
MAT 6:18 that thy fasting may not appear to men, but to thy father who is in secret, and thy father who seeth in secret will reward thee openly.
MAT 6:19 Lay not up for yourselves treasures on the earth, where moth and rust consume, and where thieves break through and steal;
MAT 6:20 but lay up for yourselves treasures in heaven, where neither moth nor rust consumeth; and where thieves do not break through and steal.
MAT 6:21 For where your treasure is, there will your heart also be.
MAT 6:22 The eye is the lamp of the body. If therefore thine eye be sound thy whole body will be enlightened:
MAT 6:23 but if thine eye be distempered, thy whole body will be dark. If then the light which is in thee be darkness, how great will the darkness be!
MAT 6:24 No man can serve two masters: for he will either hate one and love the other; or he will attend to one and neglect the other. You cannot serve God and a worldly temperent
MAT 6:25 Therefore I say to you, Be not anxious about your life, what you shall eat or what you shall drink; nor about your body, what you shall wear. Is not life a greater gift than food; and the body, than raiment?
MAT 6:26 Observe those birds of the air: they neither sow nor reap, nor lay up in granaries; yet your heavenly father feedeth them. Are not you much more valuable than they?
MAT 6:27 Besides, which of you can by his anxiety prolong his life one hour?
MAT 6:28 And with respect to raiment, why are you anxious? Consider those lilies of the field, how they grow. They neither toil nor spin:
MAT 6:29 yet I affirm, that even Solomon in all his glory was not arrayed like one of these.
MAT 6:30 Now if God thus arrayeth the herbage which is today in the field, and tomorrow to be cast into a furnace, will he not much more clothe you, O ye mistrustful?
MAT 6:31 Therefore be not anxious, saying, What shall we eat; or, what shall we drink; or, with what shall we be clothed?
MAT 6:32 For about all such things the nations are solicitous: for your heavenly father knoweth that you have need of all these things.
MAT 6:33 But seek first the kingdom of God, and the righteousness required by him, and all those things will be superadded to you.
MAT 6:34 Wherefore be not anxious about the morrow; for the morrow will be anxious about its own concerns. Sufficient for every day is its own trouble.
MAT 7:1 Judge not, that you may not be judged;
MAT 7:2 for as you judge, you shall be judged: and the measure which you mete, shall be measured to you again.
MAT 7:3 Now why art thou observant of the mote in thy brother's eye, and insensible to the splinter in thine own eye?
MAT 7:4 Or, how canst thou say to thy brother, Hold! let me take the mote out of thine eye, when lo! there is a splinter in thine own eye?
MAT 7:5 Hypocrite, first take the splinter out of thine own eye; and then thou wilt see clearly to remove the mote out of thy brother's eye.
MAT 7:6 Give not that which is holy to dogs; nor cast your pearls before swine; lest they trample them under foot, and turning tear you.
MAT 7:7 Ask, and ye shall obtain; seek and ye shall find; knock, and the door will be opened to you.
MAT 7:8 For every one who asketh, obtaineth; and he who seeketh, findeth; and to him who knocketh the door will be opened.
MAT 7:9 Is there any man among you, who, when his son asketh bread, will give him a stone;
MAT 7:10 or if he ask for a fish will give him a serpent?
MAT 7:11 If you therefore, bad as you are, know how to give good gifts to your children, how much more will your father who is in heaven give good things to them who ask him?
MAT 7:12 Whatsoever therefore you would that men should do to you, do ye even so to them, for this is the law and the prophets.
MAT 7:13 Enter in at the strait gate. Because the gate is wide and the way broad which leadeth to destruction, therefore many there are who go in through it:
MAT 7:14 because the gate is strait and the way narrow, which leadeth to life, therefore there are few who find it.
MAT 7:15 Now beware of false teachers, who come to you in sheep's clothing, but are inwardly ravenous wolves.
MAT 7:16 By their fruits you may know them. Are grapes gathered from thorns? Or figs from thistles?
MAT 7:17 So every good tree beareth good fruit; and every bad tree beareth bad fruit.
MAT 7:18 A good tree cannot bear bad fruit; nor a bad tree, good fruit.
MAT 7:19 Every tree which beareth not good fruit is cut down and cast into the fire.
MAT 7:20 So then by their fruits you will know them.
MAT 7:21 Not every one who saith to me, Lord, Lord, shall enter into the kingdom of heaven, but he who doeth the will of my father who is in heaven.
MAT 7:22 Many will say to me on that day Lord, Lord, have we not prophesied in thy name and in thy name cast out demons, and in thy name done many miracles,
MAT 7:23 to whom I will then declare, I never acknowledged you; Depart from me ye who work iniquity.
MAT 7:24 Therefore whoever heareth these words of mine and putteth them in practice, him I will compare to a prudent man, who built his house upon the rock.
MAT 7:25 When the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house, it did not fall, because it was founded on the rock.
MAT 7:26 But whoever heareth these words of mine, and doth not put them in practice, may be compared to a foolish man, who built his house on the sand.
MAT 7:27 When the rain descended, and the floods came, and the winds blew, and beat upon that house; it fell, and great was the ruin thereof.
MAT 7:28 When Jesus finished this discourse, the crouds were astonished at his manner of teaching;
MAT 7:29 for in teaching them he was like one having authority, and not like the scribes.
MAT 8:1 And as he was going down from the mount great multitudes followed him.
MAT 8:2 And lo! a leper came and prostrated himself before him, and said, Sir, if thou wilt, thou canst cleanse me.
MAT 8:3 Whereupon Jesus stretched forth his hand and touched him, saying, I will: Be thou cleansed. And immediately he was cured of his leprosy.
MAT 8:4 Then Jesus saith to him, See thou tell no one; but go and shew thyself to the priest, and offer the gift which Moses prescribed, for a testimony to them.
MAT 8:5 And as Jesus was entering Capernaum, a centurion met him and in treated him,
MAT 8:6 saying, Sir, my servant lieth at home struck with a palsy, in great torture.
MAT 8:7 Thereupon Jesus saith to him, I was coming; I will cure him.
MAT 8:8 In reply to which the centurion said, Sir, I am not worthy that thou shouldst come under my roof; but only speak a word and my servant will be cured.
MAT 8:9 For even I, who am myself under command, having soldiers under me, say to one, Go; and he goeth: and to another, Come; and he cometh: and to my slave, Do this; and he doth it.
MAT 8:10 Upon hearing this Jesus expressed admiration, saying to them who followed him, Verily I say to you, I have not found even in Israel such a belief.
MAT 8:11 Now I say to you that many will come from the east and west, and will be placed at table with Abraham and Isaak and Jacob, in the kingdom of the heavens,
MAT 8:12 and the children of the kingdom will be cast out into the outer darkness. Weeping and gnashing of teeth will be there.
MAT 8:13 Then Jesus said to the centurion, Go thy way and be it done for thee as thou hast believed. And that very instant his servant was cured.
MAT 8:14 Jesus also having gone to Peter's house, saw his wife's mother confined to her bed and sick of a fever,
MAT 8:15 and he touched her hand; thereupon the fever left her and she arose and entertained them.
MAT 8:16 And in the evening there were brought to him many demoniacs. And he expelled the spirits with a word, and cured all that were sick
MAT 8:17 so that there was an accomplishment of that which was spoken by the prophet Esaias, saying, "He took our infirmities and bore away our diseases."
MAT 8:18 When Jesus saw great crowds around him, he gave orders to go over to the opposite shore;
MAT 8:19 whereupon a certain scribe accosting him, said, Teacher, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.
MAT 8:20 Jesus saith to him, the foxes have holes and the birds of the air have roosts; but the son of man hath not where to lay his head.
MAT 8:21 Another of his disciples said to him, Master, permit me to go first and bury my father.
MAT 8:22 And to him Jesus said, Follow me, and let the dead bury their own dead.
MAT 8:23 Then having gone aboard the vessel, his disciples followed him.
MAT 8:24 And behold there came on a mighty tempest in the sea, so that the vessel was covered with the waves, and he was asleep.
MAT 8:25 Thereupon his disciples came and awoke him, saying, Master, save us! we are perishing.
MAT 8:26 And he said to them, Why are you fearful, O ye of little faith? Then he arose, and rebuked the winds and the sea, and a great calm ensued.
MAT 8:27 And the men in amaze, said, "What sort of a man is this, that even the winds and the sea obey him?"
MAT 8:28 And when he arrived at the opposite shore in the country of the Gergesenes, there met him two demoniacs coming out of the tombs, so furious that nobody durst pass that way.
MAT 8:29 And instantly they screamed, saying, What hast thou to do with us, Jesus son of God! Art thou come hither before the time to torment us.
MAT 8:30 Now there was at some distance from them a herd of many swine, feeding:
MAT 8:31 and the demons besought him, saying, If thou cast us out, permit us to go into that herd of swine.
MAT 8:32 And he said to them, Go. Thereupon they went out and entered into the herd of swine. And instantly the whole herd ran violently down a precipice into the sea, and perished in the waters.
MAT 8:33 And they who fed them fled; and having gone to the city, they told all the circumstances, including the case of the demoniacs.
MAT 8:34 And presently all the city came out to meet Jesus, and having seen him they intreated him to. withdraw out of their territory.
MAT 9:1 So having gone onboard the vessel, he crossed over, and came to his own city.
MAT 9:2 And lo! they brought to him a paralytic laid on a bed: and Jesus, seeing their faith, said to the paralytic, Take courage, my son; thy sins are forgiven thee.
MAT 9:3 Thereupon some of the Scribes said within themselves, This man blasphemeth.
MAT 9:4 But Jesus knowing their thoughts, said, Why do ye harbour evil thoughts in your hearts?
MAT 9:5 For which is easier? To say, Thy sins are forgiven thee; or to say, Arise and walk?
MAT 9:6 But that you may know that the son of man hath power on earth to forgive sins, Arise [saith he then to the paralytic] take up thy bed and go home.
MAT 9:7 Accordingly he arose and departed to his house.
MAT 9:8 And when the multitude saw this they expressed their admiration and glorified God who had given such power to men.
MAT 9:9 When Jesus was going thence he saw a man, named Matthew, sitting at the custom house; and he saith to him, Follow me. Whereupon he arose and followed him.
MAT 9:10 And when he was at table in the house, behold many publicans and sinners came and placed themselves at the table with Jesus and his disciples.
MAT 9:11 When the Pharisees saw this, they said to his disciples, Why doth your teacher eat with these publicans and sinners?
MAT 9:12 And Jesus hearing this, said to them, They who are well have no need of a physician, but they who are sick.
MAT 9:13 Go then and learn what this meaneth, "I desire mercy rather than sacrifice;" for I did not come to call righteous men, but sinners to reformation.
MAT 9:14 Then John's disciples, accosting him, said, Why do we and the Pharisees fast frequently, but thy disciples never fast?
MAT 9:15 And to them Jesus said, Can bridemen mourn, while the bridegroom is with them? The days indeed will come, when the bridegroom shall be taken away from them and then they will fast.
MAT 9:16 No one mendeth an old garment with a patch of undressed cloth; for such a patch teareth the garment and maketh a greater rent.
MAT 9:17 Neither do men put new wine into old leathern bottles, otherwise the bottles burst, and the wine is spilled, and the bottles are lost. But new wine is put into new bottles, so both are preserved.
MAT 9:18 While he was thus speaking to them, behold a chief came and, making obeisance to him, said, My daughter is at the point of death, but come and lay thy hand on her and she will live.
MAT 9:19 Thereupon Jesus arose and with his disciples followed him.
MAT 9:20 And lo! a woman who had been twelve years afflicted with an efflux of blood, came behind and touched the tuft of his mantle.
MAT 9:21 For she said within herself, If I can only touch his mantle, I shall be cured.
MAT 9:22 And Jesus turned about and when he saw her, said, Daughter, take courage; thy faith hath cured3 thee. And from that instant the woman was cured.
MAT 9:23 And when Jesus came to the house of the chief and saw the minstrels and the crowd in a bustle,
MAT 9:24 he saith to them, withdraw, for the damsel is not dead but asleep, Whereupon they derided him.
MAT 9:25 But when the crowd was turned out, he went in and took her by the hand, and the damsel arose.
MAT 9:26 And the fame of this spread over all that country.
MAT 9:27 As Jesus was departing thence, two blind men followed him, with loud outcries, saying, Son of David, take pity on us.
MAT 9:28 And when he went into the house, the blind men came to him. And Jesus saith to them, Do you believe that I can do this? They say to him, Yes, master.
MAT 9:29 Then he touched their eyes, saying, According to your belief, be it to you.
MAT 9:30 Whereupon their eyes were opened. Then Jesus restrained them, saying, See that none know this.
MAT 9:31 But when they went out, they spread his fame through all that country.
MAT 9:32 At their going out, behold a dumb man, a demoniac, was brought to him;
MAT 9:33 and the demon being expelled, the dumb man spake, and the crowds expressed their amazement, saying, Nothing like this was ever seen in Israel.
MAT 9:34 But the Pharisees said, By the prince of the demons he expelleth the demons.
MAT 9:35 Then Jesus took a circuit through all the cities and villages, teaching in their synagogues and proclaiming the good news of the reign, and healing every disease and every malady among the people.
MAT 9:36 And seeing the multitudes, he had compassion on them because they were fainty and forlorn, like sheep without a shepherd.
MAT 9:37 Then he saith to his disciples, The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the labourers are few.
MAT 9:38 Supplicate therefore the Lord of the harvest to send forth labourers for his harvest.
MAT 10:1 Then having called to him his twelve disciples, he gave them power over unclean spirits, so as to cast them out; and to cure diseases and maladies of every kind.
MAT 10:2 Now the names of the twelve disciples were these. First, Simon, called Peter, and Andrew his brother, James the son of Zebedee, and John his brother,
MAT 10:3 Philip and Bartholomew, Thomas and Matthew the publican, James the son of Alpheus and Lebbeus called Thaddeus,
MAT 10:4 Simon the Chananite and Judas Iscariot, even he who delivered him up.
MAT 10:5 These twelve Jesus sent forth, having given them a charge, saying, Go not away to the Gentiles, nor enter a city of the Samaritans;
MAT 10:6 but go rather to the lost sheep of the house of Israel:
MAT 10:7 and as you go proclaim, saying, The reign of the heavens is at hand.
MAT 10:8 Heal the sick; cleanse lepers; raise the dead; cast out demons; freely you have received; give freely.
MAT 10:9 Provide neither gold, nor silver, nor brass for your purses;
MAT 10:10 nor a scrip for the journey; nor two coats; nor pairs of sandals; nor a staff: for the workman is worthy of his sustenance.
MAT 10:11 Therefore into whatever city or village you enter, inquire who in it is worthy, and continue there till you leave the place.
MAT 10:12 And when you enter the house, salute the family.
MAT 10:13 And if the family be worthy, the peace you wish them will come upon them; but if they be not worthy, the peace you wish will rebound upon your selves.
MAT 10:14 And whosoever will not receive you, nor hear your words, when you leave that house or that city shake off the dust of your feet.
MAT 10:15 Verily I say to you, it will be more tolerable for the land of Sodom and Gomorra in a day of judgment, than for that city.
MAT 10:16 Behold I send you forth like sheep in the midst of wolves; be ye therefore wise as the serpents and harmless as the doves.
MAT 10:17 And be upon your guard against these men, for they will deliver you up to councils and scourge you in their synagogues;
MAT 10:18 and you will be brought before governors and kings for my sake, for a testimony to them and the nations.
MAT 10:19 But when they deliver you up, be not anxious how or what you shall speak: for what you are to speak will be suggested to you at the very instant.
MAT 10:20 For it is not you who speak, but the spirit of your father that speaketh in you.
MAT 10:21 Now brother will deliver up brother to death; and a father, a son; and children will rise up against parents and cause them to be put to death.
MAT 10:22 And you will be hated by all men on the account of my name. But he who persevereth to the end shall be saved.
MAT 10:23 Now when they persecute you in one city, flee to another. For, verily I say to you, before you shall have gone through all the cities of Israel, the son of man will come.
MAT 10:24 The scholar is not greater than the teacher; nor the servant, than the master.
MAT 10:25 It is enough for the scholar to be as his teacher; and the servant, as his master. If they have called the master of the family Beelzebub, how much more, his domestics.
MAT 10:26 Therefore be not afraid of them; for there is nothing hid, which shall not be revealed; nor anything secret, which shall not be known.
MAT 10:27 What I say to you in darkness, speak ye in the light; and what is whispered in your ear, proclaim on the house tops.
MAT 10:28 And be not afraid of them who kill the body, but are not able to kill the soul: but rather fear him, who can destroy both soul and body in hell.
MAT 10:29 Are not two sparrows sold for an assar, yet neither of them falleth to the ground without your father.
MAT 10:30 Nay, the very hairs of your head are all numbered.
MAT 10:31 Fear not therefore; for you are of more value than many sparrows.
MAT 10:32 Whosoever therefore will acknowledge me before men, him I will acknowledge before my father, who is in heaven:
MAT 10:33 but whosoever shall disown me before men, him I will disown before my father who is in heaven.
MAT 10:34 Do not imagine that I am come to send peace on the earth. I am not come to send peace, but a sword.
MAT 10:35 For I am come to set a man at variance with his father; and a daughter with her mother; and a daughter in law with her mother in law.
MAT 10:36 Even the man's own domestics will be his enemies.
MAT 10:37 He who loveth father or mother more than me, is not worthy of me. And he who loveth son or daughter more than me, is not worthy of me.
MAT 10:38 And he who doth not take up his cross and follow me, is not worthy of me.
MAT 10:39 He who hath found his life shall lose it. But he, who shall lose his life for my sake, shall find it.
MAT 10:40 He who receiveth you, receiveth me; and he who receiveth me, receiveth him who sent me.
MAT 10:41 He who receiveth a prophet on the account of his being a prophet, shall receive a prophet's reward. And he who receiveth a righteous man on the account of his being a righteous man, shall receive a righteous man's reward.
MAT 10:42 And whoever shall give any one of these little ones, were it only a cup of cold water to drink, on the account of his being a disciple, verily I say to you, he shall not lose his reward.
MAT 11:1 And when Jesus had finished his instructions to these his twelve disciples, he departed thence to teach and make proclamation Ln their cities.
MAT 11:2 Now John, having heard in prison of the works of the Christ, sent two of his disciples
MAT 11:3 with this message to him; Thou art the one coming; May we expect another? In reply to which,
MAT 11:4 Jesus said to them, Go and tell John what you hear and see.
MAT 11:5 Blind men see, and lame walk. Lepers are cleansed and deaf hear. Dead are raised and poor have glad tidings proclaimed to them.
MAT 11:6 And happy is he to whom I shall not prove a stumbling block.
MAT 11:7 And as they were going away, Jesus began this discourse to the people concerning John, What did you go out to the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
MAT 11:8 But what went ye out to see? A man clothed with soft raiment? Behold they, who wear delicate apparel, frequent the palaces of kings.
MAT 11:9 But what went ye out to see? a prophet? Yes I tell you, and something more than a prophet;
MAT 11:10 for this is he of whom it is written, "Behold I send my messenger before thy face, who shall prepare thy way before thee."
MAT 11:11 Verily I say to you, among them who are born of women, there hath not arisen a greater than John the baptist: but the least in the kingdom  of heaven is a greater than he.
MAT 11:12 Now ever since the days of John the baptist, the kingdom of the heavens is invaded and invaders are forcibly taking possession of it.
MAT 11:13 For till the appearance of John, all the prophets and the law were the public instructors.
MAT 11:14 Indeed, if you will bear to be told it, he is Elias who was to come.
MAT 11:15 Whoever hath ears to hear let him hear.
MAT 11:16 Now to what shall I compare this generation? It is like boys in the market place who call to their playfellows,
MAT 11:17 saying, "We have played to you on the pipe, but you have not danced; We have sung to you songs of woe, and you have not lamented."
MAT 11:18 For John came, abstaining from meat and drink, and they say he hath a demon.
MAT 11:19 The son of man came eating and drinking; and they say, Behold a gluttonous man and a wine drinker; a friend of publicans and sinners. But wisdom is justified by her children.
MAT 11:20 Then he began to upbraid the cities in which the most of his miracles had been done, because they had not reformed.
MAT 11:21 Alas for thee Chorazin! Alas for thee Bethsaida! For had the miracles, which have been performed in you, been done in Tyre and Sidon they would have repented long ago in sack cloth and ashes.
MAT 11:22 But I say to you, the condition of Tyre and Sidon will in a day of judgment, be more tolerable than yours.
MAT 11:23 And thou Capernaum, which hast been exalted to heaven, shalt be brought down to the mansion of the dead; for if the miracles, which have been done in thee, had been done in Sodom, it would have remained to this day.
MAT 11:24 But I say to you, that the condition of the land of Sodom will, in a day of judgment, be more tolerable than thine.
MAT 11:25 At that time Jesus took occasion to say, I thank thee, O father, Lord of heaven and earth; that thou having hid these things from the wise and prudent, hast revealed them to babes.
MAT 11:26 Yes, O father, because it thus seemed good in thy sight.
MAT 11:27 All things are delivered up to me by my father; and none but the father knoweth the son; nor doth any know the father, but only the son, and he to whom the son is pleased to reveal him.
MAT 11:28 Come to me all ye who labour and are heavily burdened and I will give you rest.
MAT 11:29 Take upon you my yoke and learn of me; for I am meek and lowly in heart, and ye shall find rest for your souls.
MAT 11:30 For my yoke is easy and my burden is light.
MAT 12:1 About this time, as Jesus was walking through corn fields on the sabbath days, his disciples were hungry and began to pluck some ears, and eat them.
MAT 12:2 When the Pharisees saw this they said to him, See Thy disciples are doing that which it is not lawful to do on a sabbath.
MAT 12:3 Whereupon he said to them, Have you not read, what David did when he was hungry, and they who were with him?
MAT 12:4 How he went to the house of God and ate the presence loaves, which it was not lawful for him or his company to eat, but only for the priests?
MAT 12:5 Or have you not read in the law, that on the sabbath days the priests in the temple break the sabbath and are blameless?
MAT 12:6 Now I say to you, There is one here greater than the temple.
MAT 12:7 And if you had known the meaning of this,. "I desire mercy rather than sacrifice," you would not have condemned the innocent.
MAT 12:8 For the son of man is lord even of the sabbath.
MAT 12:9 Having departed thence, he went into their synagogue
MAT 12:10 and lo! there was a man there who had his hand withered. And they asked him with a design to accuse him; "Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath days?"
MAT 12:11 And he said to them, What man is there among you, who having one sheep, if it fall into a pit on the sabbath days, will not take hold of it and lift it up?
MAT 12:12 Of how much greater value then is a man than a sheep? Therefore it is lawful to do good on the sabbaths.
MAT 12:13 Then he said to the man, Stretch forth thy hand. And he stretched it out. And his hand was restored sound as the other.
MAT 12:14 Thereupon the Pharisees went out and conspired against him that they might destroy him.
MAT 12:15 But Jesus, knowing this, withdrew from that place; and great multitudes followed him, and he healed them all;
MAT 12:16 and strictly charged them not to make him known;
MAT 12:17 so that there was a full confirmation of what was spoken by the prophet Esaias saying,
MAT 12:18 "Behold my servant whom I have chosen! My beloved in whom my soul is well pleased! I will put my spirit upon him; and he will publish judgment to the nations.
MAT 12:19 He will not contend nor raise a clamour; nor shall any one hear his voice in the streets.
MAT 12:20 A bruised reed he will not break, nor extinguish a dimly burning taper, until he render his judgment victorious.
MAT 12:21 In his name therefore let the nations trust."
MAT 12:22 Then there was brought to him a demoniac, blind and dumb, and he healed him, so that he who was blind and dumb both spake and saw.
MAT 12:23 And all the people were astonished and said, Is this the son of David?
MAT 12:24 But the Pharisees, hearing them said, This man expelleth the demons, only by Beelzebub, the chief of the demons.
MAT 12:25 Thereupon Jesus, knowing their thoughts, said to them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation. And no city or family divided against itself can subsist.
MAT 12:26 Now if Satan expelleth Satan, he is at variance with himself, how then can his kingdom subsist?
MAT 12:27 Besides if I expel demons by Beelzebub, by whom do your sons expel them? Let them therefore be your judges.
MAT 12:28 But if I expel the demons by the Spirit of God, then indeed the reign of God over you is come.
MAT 12:29 How can anyone enter the house of the strong and plunder his goods, unless he first bind the strong one, in which case he may then plunder his house.
MAT 12:30 He who is not for me is against me; and he who gathereth not with me, scattereth.
MAT 12:31 Therefore I say to you, all manner of sin and slander may be forgiven men; but this slanderous speaking against the spirit is not to be forgiven men
MAT 12:32 Even though one speak against the son of man, it may be forgiven him; but whoever shall speak against the holy Spirit is not to be forgiven, either in the present age, or in that to come.
MAT 12:33 Either make the tree good and its fruit good, or make the tree bad, and its fruit bad. For the tree is known by its fruit
MAT 12:34 Brood of vipers! how can you who are evil speak good things? For out of the abundance of the heart the mouth speaketh.
MAT 12:35 The good man out of the good treasure of his heart produceth good things; and the bad man, out of his bad treasure produceth bad things.
MAT 12:36 Now I assure you in respect to every idle word which men shall utter, they shall give an account thereof in a day of judgment.
MAT 12:37 For by thy words thou shalt be justified, and by thy words thou shall be condemned.
MAT 12:38 Then some of the Scribes and Pharisees interposed, saying, Teacher, we desire to see a sign from thee.
MAT 12:39 In reply to which he said to them, an evil, and an adulterous generation demand a sign, but no sign shall be given them, save the sign of the prophet Jonas.
MAT 12:40 For as Jonas was three days and three nights in the belly of the great fish, so the son of man will be three days and three nights in the heart of the earth.
MAT 12:41 The men of Ninive will be raised up at the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it; because they repented at the proclamation of Jonas; and behold something greater than Jonas is here.
MAT 12:42 The queen of the south will be raised up at the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, because she came from the extremities of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon. And behold something greater than Solomon is here,
MAT 12:43 When the unclean spirit hath gone out of the man, it walketh through dry places seeking rest, but doth not find it.
MAT 12:44 Then it saith I will return to my habitation from which I came out. And when it is come, it findeth it unoccupied, swept and furnished.
MAT 12:45 Then it goeth and bringeth with it seven other spirits worse than itself, and they enter and dwell there. So the last state of that man is worse than the first. Thus also will it be with this wicked generation.
MAT 12:46 Now, while he was speaking to the people, lo! His mother and his brethren were standing without, desiring to speak with him.
MAT 12:47 And one said to him, lo! thy mother and thy brethren are standing without, desiring to speak with thee.
MAT 12:48 In reply to which he said to him who told him, who is my mother? And who are my brethren?
MAT 12:49 Then, stretching out his hand towards his disciples, he said, Behold my mother, and my brethren!
MAT 12:50 for whoever will do the will of my father who is in heaven, the same is my brother and sister and mother.
MAT 13:1 And on the same day, Jesus having gone out of the house, sat down by the sea side;
MAT 13:2 but such great multitudes flocked to him that he went on board the vessel and sat down, and all the multitude stood on the shore,
MAT 13:3 and he spake many things to them in parables, saying, Behold the sower went out to sow;
MAT 13:4 and as he was sowing, some grains fell on the highway and the birds came and devoured them.
MAT 13:5 And others fell on rocky ground, where they had little earth; these sprang up immediately, because they had no depth of soil;
MAT 13:6 but soon as the sun arose they were scorched; and for want of root withered away:
MAT 13:7 and some fell among the thorns, and the thorns sprang up and choaked them.
MAT 13:8 And some fell on good ground and yielded increase; some an hundred; some, sixty; and some, thirty fold.
MAT 13:9 Whoever hath ears to hear, let him hear.
MAT 13:10 Then the disciples accosted him, saying, Why speakest thou to them in parables?
MAT 13:11 And he in reply said to them, To you it hath been granted to know the secrets of the reign of the heavens; but to them it hath not been granted.
MAT 13:12 For to him who improveth, more shall be given and he shall abound: but from him who improveth not, even that which he hath shall be taken.
MAT 13:13 To them I speak in parables for this reason, because they overlook what they see, and are inattentive to what they hear; and they do not understand,
MAT 13:14 and in them is fulfilled this prophesy of Esaias, which saith, "Hearing you shall hear, though you may not understand, and seeing you shall see, though you may not perceive;
MAT 13:15 for the heart of this people is callous, and their ears are dull of hearing, and they have shut their eyes, that for a while they may not see with their eyes and hear with their ears, and understand with their heart, and return that I may heal them."
MAT 13:16 But blessed are your eyes, because they see, and your ears, because they hear.
MAT 13:17 For verily I say to you, "Many prophets and righteous men have earnestly desired to see what you see, and have not seen them; and to hear what you hear and have not heard them."
MAT 13:18 Hear then the parable of the sower.
MAT 13:19 When any one heareth the doctrine of the kingdom and doth not mind it, the evil one cometh and snatcheth away what was sown in his heart. This is the meaning of that sown on the highway.
MAT 13:20 And that sown on rocky ground denoteth him, who, upon hearing the word, receiveth it at first with joy,
MAT 13:21 but not having it rooted in him, it is only temporary; and when tribulation and persecution cometh on account of the word, he is immediately stumbled.
MAT 13:22 And that sown among thorns denoteth him, who heareth the word, but worldly care and the delusion of riches choak the word and it becometh unfruitful.
MAT 13:23 But that sown on good ground denoteth him who heareth and mindeth the word, and who beareth fruit and bringeth forth, one a hundred, and another sixty, and another thirty fold.
MAT 13:24 Another parable he stated to them, saying, The reign of the heavens may be compared to a man sowing good seed in his field.
MAT 13:25 But when the men were asleep; his enemy came and sowed darnel among the wheat, and went away.
MAT 13:26 And when the blade sprang up and put forth the ear, then the darnel appeared.
MAT 13:27 Whereupon the servants of the householder came and said to him, Master, didst thou not sow good seed in thy field whence then hath it darnel?
MAT 13:28 And he said to them, An enemy hath done this. Then the servants said to him, Is it thy pleasure then that we go and weed it out?
MAT 13:29 And he said, no. Perhaps in weeding out the darnel you may pull up the wheat with it.
MAT 13:30 Let them both grow together till the harvest. And at the season for reaping I will say to the reapers, Gather the darnel first and bind it in bundles to be burned; then gather the wheat into my barn.
MAT 13:31 Another parable he stated to them, saying, "The reign of the heavens is like a grain of mustard seed which a man took and sowed in his field,
MAT 13:32 which is indeed the smallest of all seeds, but which, when grown, is the largest of the herbs and becometh a tree, so that the birds of the air come and take shelter among the branches."
MAT 13:33 Another parable he stated to them, saying, The reign of the heavens is like leaven which a woman took and covered up in three measures of meal, till the whole was leavened.
MAT 13:34 All these things Jesus spake to them in parables, and did not speak to them without a parable,
MAT 13:35 so that there was a full accomplishment of that which was spoken by the prophet, saying, I will open my mouth with parables, I will utter things kept hid from the foundation of the world.
MAT 13:36 Then Jesus dismissed the multitude and went into the house, and his disciples came to him and said, Explain to us the parable of the darnel in the field.
MAT 13:37 And he answering, said to them, He who soweth the good seed is the son of man.
MAT 13:38 The field is the world. The good seed are the children of the kingdom, and the darnel are the children of the evil one.
MAT 13:39 The enemy who sowed it is the devil. The harvest is the conclusion of the age, and angels are the reapers.
MAT 13:40 As the darnel therefore is gathered and burned with fire, so shall it be at the conclusion of this age.
MAT 13:41 The son of man will send his angels, and they will gather out of his kingdom all the stumbling blocks, and the workers of iniquity,
MAT 13:42 and cast them into the fiery furnace. Weeping and gnashing of teeth will be there.
MAT 13:43 Then shall the righteous shine like the sun in the kingdom of their father. Whoever hath ears to hear, let him hear.
MAT 13:44 Again the kingdom of the heavens is like treasure hid in the field, which, when a man found, he concealed, and for joy thereof goeth away and selleth all that he hath, and purchaseth that field.
MAT 13:45 Again the kingdom of the heavens is like a merchant in quest of fine pearls,
MAT 13:46 who, having met with one of great value, went and sold all that he had and purchased it.
MAT 13:47 Again the kingdom of the heavens is like a sweep net cast into the sea, which enclosed fishes of every kind,
MAT 13:48 which, when it was full, they dragged to the shore; and then sitting down, gathered the good into vessels and threw the bad away.
MAT 13:49 So shall it be at the conclusion of this age. The angels will go forth and sever the wicked from among the righteous
MAT 13:50 and cast them into the fiery furnace. Weeping and gnashing of teeth will be there.
MAT 13:51 Jesus saith to them, Have you understood all these? They  say to him, Yes, Master.
MAT 13:52 Then he said to them, Every Scribe then who is instructed for the kingdom of heaven is like a master of a family who bringeth out of his treasury things new and old.
MAT 13:53 Now when Jesus had finished these parables he departed thence;
MAT 13:54 and being come into his own country, he taught them in their synagogues, so that they were astonished, and said. Whence hath this man this wisdom and these miraculous powers?
MAT 13:55 Is not this the carpenter's son? Is not his mother called Mary and his brethren, James and Joses and Simon and Judas?
MAT 13:56 And his sisters, are they not all among us"? Whence then hath this man all these things?
MAT 13:57 And they were stumbled at him. Thereupon Jesus said to them, A prophet is not without honour save in his own country and in his own family.
MAT 13:58 So he did not perform many miracles there because of their unbelief.
MAT 14:1 At that time Herod the tetrarch hearing of the fame of Jesus,
MAT 14:2 said to his servants, This is John the Baptist. He is raised from the dead, and therefore miracles are performed by him.
MAT 14:3 [For Herod had apprehended John and bound him, and put him in prison on account of Herodias, the wife of his brother Philip:
MAT 14:4 for John had said to him, It is not lawful for thee to have her.
MAT 14:5 Upon which Herod would have put him to death, but he was afraid of the people, because they looked upon him as a prophet.
MAT 14:6 But when Herod's birth day was kept, the daughter of Herodias danced before the company and pleased Herod.
MAT 14:7 Whereupon he promised with an oath to give her whatever she would ask.
MAT 14:8 And she at the instigation of her mother, said, Give me here in a basin the head of John the Baptist.
MAT 14:9 Though the king was sorry, yet from a regard to the oath and the guests, he ordered it to be given her.
MAT 14:10 So he sent and beheaded John in the prison.
MAT 14:11 And his head was brought in a basin and given to the damsel, who carried it to her mother.
MAT 14:12 And his disciples went and took up the body, and buried it, and came and told Jesus.
MAT 14:13 When Jesus heard this he departed thence, in a vessel, privately, to a desert place; and the people, being informed, followed him by land out of the cities.
MAT 14:14 And when Jesus landed he saw a great multitude, and had compassion on them, and healed their sick.
MAT 14:15 And towards evening his disciples accosted him, saying, This is a desert place and the hour is now past, dismiss the multitude that they may go to the villages and buy themselves victuals.
MAT 14:16 And Jesus said to them, They need not go. Give them, ye yourselves, something to eat.
MAT 14:17 And they said, We have here only five loaves and two fishes.
MAT 14:18 Whereupon he said, Bring them hither to me.
MAT 14:19 Then he ordered the multitude to arrange themselves, as at table, on the grass. And having taken the five loaves and the two fishes, he looked up to heaven and pronounced a blessing. Then he brake and gave the loaves to the disciples and the disciples [distributed] them to the multitudes.
MAT 14:20 And they all ate and were satisfied. And there were carried away twelve panniers full of the fragments which remained.
MAT 14:21 Now they who had eaten were about five thousand men, besides women and children.
MAT 14:22 Then Jesus immediately constrained his disciples to embark, and cross over to the other side before him, while he dismissed the multitudes.
MAT 14:23 And when he had dismissed the multitudes he went up, by himself, to the mountain, to pray And in the course of the eve, he was there alone,
MAT 14:24 and the vessel was now in the midst of the sea tossed by the waves, for the wind was contrary.
MAT 14:25 And in the fourth watch of the night, Jesus went to them, walking on the sea.
MAT 14:26 When the disciples saw him walking on the sea, they were terrified, and said it is an apparition, and cried out for fear.
MAT 14:27 Thereupon Jesus immediately spake to them, saying, Take courage: it is I; be not afraid.
MAT 14:28 In reply to which Peter said, Master, if it be them, bid me come to thee on the water.
MAT 14:29 And Jesus said, Come. So Peter having gone down from the vessel, walked on the waves to go to Jesus.
MAT 14:30 But perceiving the wind strong, he was afraid, and, beginning to sink, he cried out, saying, Master, save me.
MAT 14:31 And Jesus immediately stretched forth his hand and took hold of him, saying, Distrustful man, why didst thou doubt?
MAT 14:32 And when they were come into the vessel the wind ceased.
MAT 14:33 And they who were in the vessel came and bowed down to him, saying, Thou art indeed Son of God.
MAT 14:34 And when they had crossed over, they landed in the territory of Gennesaret.
MAT 14:35 And the men of that place, knowing him, sent to all the country around, and they brought to him all that were sick,
MAT 14:36 and intreated him that they might only touch the tuft of his mantle. And as many as touched were perfectly cured.
MAT 15:1 Then some Scribes and Pharisees from Jerusalem accosted Jesus, saying,
MAT 15:2 Why do thy disciples transgress the doctrine of the elders? For they do not wash their hands when they eat bread.
MAT 15:3 In reply to which he said to them, Why do you transgress the commandment of God, from a regard to your doctrines?
MAT 15:4 For God commanded saying, "Honour thy father and thy mother, and whosoever revileth father or mother let him be put to death:
MAT 15:5 but you say, "Whoever shall say to his father or to his mother, Let that by which thou mightest be benefited by me, be dedicated,
MAT 15:6 must not honour either his father or his mother." Thus you have annulled the commandment of God from a regard to your doctrines.
MAT 15:7 Hypocrites! well did Esaias prophesy concerning you, saying,
MAT 15:8 This people draw near to me with their mouth; and with their lips they honour me, but their heart is far from me;
MAT 15:9 and, in vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines, the commands of men.
MAT 15:10 Then having called the multitude to him, he said to them, Hear and understand;
MAT 15:11 It is not that which goeth into the mouth which defileth the man; but it is that which cometh out of the mouth, which defileth the man.
MAT 15:12 Then his disciples coming to him said, Dost thou know that the Pharisees, when they heard that saying, were offended?
MAT 15:13 In reply to which he said, Every plant which my heavenly father hath not planted, is to be rooted up.
MAT 15:14 Let them alone. They are blind leaders of blind. Now if the blind lead the blind, they will both fall into a ditch.
MAT 15:15 Then Peter addressing him said, Explain to us this parable.
MAT 15:16 Whereupon Jesus said, Are you also yet without understanding?
MAT 15:17 Do you not yet perceive, that whatever entereth in at the mouth, goeth into the belly, and is thrown out into the sink?
MAT 15:18 And that what proceed from the mouth come from the heart, and that these defile the man?
MAT 15:19 For out of the heart come malicious surmises, murders, adulteries, fornications, thefts, false testimonies, calumnies.
MAT 15:20 These are the things which defile the man: but to eat with unwashen hands doth not defile the man.
MAT 15:21 Then Jesus having left that place, withdrew into the confines of Tyre and Sidon.
MAT 15:22 And lo! a Chananitish woman from those quarters came out and cried with a loud voice, saying to him, Have pity on me, O my lord, Son of David; my daughter is grievously afflicted by a demon.
MAT 15:23 But he made her no answer. Then his disciples came near and intreated him, saying, Dismiss this woman, for she crieth after us.
MAT 15:24 And he in reply said, My mission is only to the lost sheep of the house of Israel.
MAT 15:25 She nevertheless advanced, and prostrating herself before him, said, O my lord, help me.
MAT 15:26 Whereupon he in reply said, It is not seemly to take the childrens bread and cast it to the dogs.
MAT 15:27 And she said, True, Sir. Yet even the dogs eat of the crumbs which fall from their master's table.
MAT 15:28 Thereupon Jesus in reply said to her, O woman, great is thy faith; Be it to thee as thou desirest. And from that instant her daughter was healed.
MAT 15:29 When Jesus left that place he came nigh to the sea of Galilee, and having ascended the mountain, he sat down there,
MAT 15:30 and great multitudes flocked to him, bringing with them the lame, the blind, the dumb, the cripple and many others, whom they laid at the feet of Jesus, and he healed them;
MAT 15:31 insomuch that the people beheld with amaze the dumb speaking, the cripple sound, the lame walking, and the blind seeing, and they glorified the God of Israel.
MAT 15:32 Then Jesus called his disciples and said, I have compassion on the multitude, because they have attended me now three days, and have nothing to eat. I will not send them away fasting.
MAT 15:33 Perhaps they may faint on the road. Thereupon his disciples say to him, Whence can we get loaves enough, in a wilderness, to satisfy so great a multitude?
MAT 15:34 And Jesus saith to them, How many loaves have you? And they said, Seven, and a few small fishes.
MAT 15:35 Then commanding the multitude to recline on the ground,
MAT 15:36 he took the seven loaves and the fishes, and having given thanks, he broke and gave to his disciples; and the disciples [distributed] to the people.
MAT 15:37 And when they had all eaten and were satisfied, there were carried off seven baskets full of the fragments left.
MAT 15:38 Now they who had eaten were about four thousand men, besides women and children.
MAT 15:39 Then having dismissed the multitude, he embarked and came to the coast of Magdala.
MAT 16:1 And the Pharisees and the Sadducees having come thither with a view to try him, desired that he would show them a sign from heaven.
MAT 16:2 Whereupon he in reply said to them, When it is evening you say, It will be fair weather, for the sky is red:
MAT 16:3 and in the morning, there will be a storm today, for the sky is red and lowering. Hypocrites! you know how to distinguish the appearance of the sky, and can you not discern the signs of the times?
MAT 16:4 An evil and adulterous generation demand a sign, but no sign shall be given them, save that of the prophet Jonas. So leaving them he departed.
MAT 16:5 Now his disciples, going to the other side, had forgotten to bring with them loaves of bread.
MAT 16:6 And Jesus said to them, Take heed and beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the Sadducees.
MAT 16:7 Whereupon they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have not brought loaves with us.
MAT 16:8 And Jesus knowing this, said to them, Why do ye reason among yourselves, O ye of little faith, because you have not brought loaves?
MAT 16:9 Have you yet no reflection? Or do ye not remember the five loaves among the five thousand, and how many panniers you carried off;
MAT 16:10 nor the seven loaves among the four thousand, and how many baskets you carried off?
MAT 16:11 How is it that you do not understand that I did not speak to you of bread, when I cautioned you to beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and the Sadducees?
MAT 16:12 Then they understood that he did not caution them against the leaven of the bread, but against the doctrine of the Pharisees and Sadducees.
MAT 16:13 When Jesus was going to Caesarea Philippi, he asked his disciples, saying, Who do men say that I, the son of man, am?
MAT 16:14 And they said, Some say, John the Baptist; and some, Elias; and some Jeremias, or one of the prophets.
MAT 16:15 He saith to them, And who do ye say that I am?
MAT 16:16 Upon this Peter, in reply, said, Thou art The Christ, the son of the living God.
MAT 16:17 And Jesus answering, said to him, Happy art thou, Simon Barjona; for flesh and blood hath not revealed this to thee, but my father who is in heaven.
MAT 16:18 Now I say to thee, Thou art named Peter, [a rock,] and upon this very rock I will build my church, and the gates of Hades shall not prevail against it.
MAT 16:19 And I will give thee the keys of the kingdom of the heavens; and whatsoever thou shall bind on the earth, will be bound in the heavens; and whatsoever thou shalt loose on the earth, will be loosed in the heavens.
MAT 16:20 Then he charged his disciples not to tell anyone that he, Jesus, is the Christ.
MAT 16:21 From that time Jesus began to point out to his disciples that he must go to Jerusalem, and suffer many things from the elders, and chief priests and scribes, and be put to death, and raised again on the third day.
MAT 16:22 Upon which Peter, taking him aside, began to check him, saying, Mercy on thee, O my Lord! This cannot befal thee.
MAT 16:23 But he, turning, said to Peter, Get thee behind me, Satan. Thou art an obstacle in my way. For thou hast not thy mind bent on the things of God; but on the things of those men.
MAT 16:24 Then Jesus said to his disciples if any one wisheth to follow me, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
MAT 16:25 For whoever wisheth to save his life shall lose it; and whoever shall lose his life for my sake, shall find it.
MAT 16:26 For what will a man be profited, if he should gain the whole world, and be punished with the forfeit of his life? Or, what will not a man give as a ransom for his life?
MAT 16:27 For the son of man will come in the glory of his father, with his angels, and will then render to every one according to his actions.
MAT 16:28 Verily I say to you, there are some of them standing here who shall not taste death until they see the son of man coming in his kingdom.
MAT 17:1 And after six days, Jesus taketh Peter, and James, and John, his brother, and bringeth them up privately to a high mountain,
MAT 17:2 and was transfigured before them. His face shone like the sun: and his raiment became white as the light.
MAT 17:3 And behold there appeared to them Moses and Elias, conversing with him.
MAT 17:4 Whereupon Peter, addressing Jesus, said, Master, it is well that we are here. if thou pleasest let us make here three booths, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
MAT 17:5 While he was yet speaking, behold! a bright cloud overshadowed them; and lo! from the cloud, a voice, saying, This is my Son, the Beloved, in whom I am well pleased. Hear ye him.
MAT 17:6 Upon hearing this the disciples fell on their face and were greatly affrighted.
MAT 17:7 But Jesus came and touched them, and said, Arise, Be not afraid.
MAT 17:8 And having lifted up their eyes they saw none but Jesus only.
MAT 17:9 And as they were coming down from the mountain, Jesus charged them, saying, Tell no one what you have seen, until the son of man shall have risen from the dead.
MAT 17:10 Then his disciples asked him, saying, Why then do the Scribes say, that Elias must come first?
MAT 17:11 In reply to which, Jesus said to them, Elias indeed cometh first and is to finish and begin all anew.
MAT 17:12 Now I say to you, Elias is already come and they did not know him, but have treated him as they pleased. In the same manner also the son of man will soon suffer by them.
MAT 17:13 Then the disciples understood that he spake to them of John the Baptist.
MAT 17:14 And when they were come to the multitude, there came to him a man, who falling on his knees, said,
MAT 17:15 O sir, have pity on my son; for he is afflicted with an epilepsy, and suffereth grievously. For he often falleth into the fire and often into the water.
MAT 17:16 I brought him to thy disciples, but they could not cure him.
MAT 17:17 And Jesus answering, said, O faithless and perverse generation! How long shall I be with you"? How long shall I endure you? Bring him hither to me.
MAT 17:18 Then Jesus rebuked the demon and it went out of him, and from that hour the child was cured.
MAT 17:19 Then the disciples came to Jesus in private, and said, Why could not we cast it out?
MAT 17:20 And Jesus said to them, Because of your unbelief. For verily I say to you, If you have faith as a grain of mustard seed, you might say to that mountain, Remove hence to yonder place; and it would remove; and nothing would be impossible to you:
MAT 17:21 but this kind [of power] goeth not forth, unless by prayer and fasting.
MAT 17:22 Now while they remained in Galilee Jesus said to them, The son of man will soon be delivered into the hands of men,
MAT 17:23 and they will put him to death; and on the third day he will be raised up. And they were exceedingly grieved.
MAT 17:24 And when they were come to Capernaum, the receivers of the assessments for the Temple came to Peter, and said, Doth your teacher pay the didrachm?
MAT 17:25 He saith, Yes. And when he came into the house, before he spake, Jesus said to him, What thinkest thou Simon? Of whom do the kings of the earth receive assessments? Of their own sons or of others?
MAT 17:26 Peter saith to him, Of others. Jesus saith to him, The sons then surely are free.
MAT 17:27 However, that we may not offend them, go to the sea, and throw in a hook, and take the first fish that cometh up; and having opened its mouth thou wilt find a stater: take that and give it to them for me and thee.
MAT 18:1 At that time the disciples came to Jesus, saying, Who is to be greatest in the kingdom of the heavens?
MAT 18:2 Whereupon Jesus, having called to him a little child, placed it in the midst of them
MAT 18:3 and said, Verily I say to you, Unless you be changed, and be like children you shall never enter the kingdom of the heavens.
MAT 18:4 Whosoever therefore shall humble himself as this little child, he is of higher dignity in the kingdom of the heavens.
MAT 18:5 And whoever shall receive one such child in my name, receiveth me.
MAT 18:6 But whoever shall occasion the stumbling of one of such little ones who believe in me, better were it for him that an upper millstone were hanged about his neck and that he were whelmed in the depth of the sea.
MAT 18:7 Alas, for the world because of these stumbling blocks, for these stumbling blocks must needs come: but alas for the man by whom the stumbling block cometh.
MAT 18:8 If then thy hand or thy foot occasioneth thy stumbling, cut them off and cast them from thee. It is better for thee to enter lame or maimed into life, than having two hands or two feet to be cast into the fire which is everlasting.
MAT 18:9 And if thine eye occasioneth thy stumbling, pluck it out and cast it from thee; it is better for thee to enter into life with but one eye, than having two eyes to be cast into the vale of that fire.
MAT 18:10 Take heed that you despise not one of these little ones; for I say to you, Their angels in heaven do continually behold the face of my father who is in heaven.
MAT 18:11 For the son of man is come to save that which was lost.
MAT 18:12 What think you? If any man hath an hundred sheep, and one of them go astray, doth he not leave die ninety nine on the mountains, and go in quest of the stray?
MAT 18:13 And if he happen to find it, verily I say to you, he rejoiceth over it more than over the ninety nine which went not astray.
MAT 18:14 Thus it is not the will of your father who is in heaven that one of these little ones should be lost.
MAT 18:15 Wherefore if thy brother trespass against thee, go and expostulate with him when thou and he are alone. If he hearken to thee thou hast gained thy brother.
MAT 18:16 But if he will not hearken to thee, then take with thee one or two, that by the testimony of two or three witnesses everything may be ascertained;
MAT 18:17 And if he disregard them, tell the congregation; and if he disregard the congregation, let him be to thee as the heathen and the publican.
MAT 18:18 Verily I say to you, whatsoever ye shall bind on the earth will be bound in heaven; and whatsoever ye shall loose on the earth will be loosed in heaven.
MAT 18:19 Again I say to you, If two of you agree on the earth touching any thing which they may ask, it will be done for them by my father who is in heaven.
MAT 18:20 For where two or three are assembled for my name I am there in the midst of them.
MAT 18:21 Then Peter accosting him, said, Master, how often is my brother to trespass against me and I to forgive him? Till seven times?
MAT 18:22 Jesus saith to him, I do not say to thee seven times, but seventy times seven.
MAT 18:23 In this respect the reign of the heavens may be compared to a certain king who determined to settle accounts with his servants.
MAT 18:24 And having begun to settle; there was one brought to him, who owed him ten thousand talents.
MAT 18:25 And as he had not wherewithal to pay; his lord ordered him and his wife and all that he had, to be sold and payment to be made.
MAT 18:26 The servant therefore falling prostrate before him, saith, Have patience with me, my lord, and I will pay thee all.
MAT 18:27 And the lord of that servant, being moved with compassion, dismissed him and forgave him the debt.
MAT 18:28 And as that servant was going out, he met one of his fellow servants who owed him a hundred deniars and seizing him by the throat, he said, Pay me what thou owest.
MAT 18:29 His fellow servant therefore falling at his feet, besought him, saying, Have patience with me and I will pay thee all.
MAT 18:30 And he would not; but went and cast him into prison until he should pay the debt.
MAT 18:31 When his fellow servants saw this they were deeply affected and went and told their lord all that was done.
MAT 18:32 Thereupon his lord having called him in, saith to him, Thou wicked slave, I forgave thee all that debt at thy entreaty;
MAT 18:33 shouldst thou not then have had compassion on thy fellow servant as I had on thee?
MAT 18:34 So his lord, being incensed, delivered him to the executioners of justice until he should pay all that was due to  him,
MAT 18:35 Thus also will my heavenly father deal with you, if you do not from your hearts forgive, everyone the trespasses of his brother.
MAT 19:1 When Jesus had finished these discourses he departed from Galilee and came to the borders of Judea, on the bank of the Jordan.
MAT 19:2 And great multitudes followed him, and he healed them there.
MAT 19:3 And the Pharisees came to him, and trying him said, Is it lawful for a man to put away his wife for every fault?
MAT 19:4 In reply to which he said to them, "Have you not read that the Creator at the beginning made them a male and a female?"
MAT 19:5 Moreover he said, "For this cause a man is to leave his father and his mother, and cleave to his wife, and they two shall be one flesh;
MAT 19:6 so that they are no longer two but one flesh." Therefore what God hath conjoined, let not man separate.
MAT 19:7 They say to him, Why then did Moses command to give a bill of divorce and dismiss her?
MAT 19:8 He saith to them, Because of your intractable disposition Moses permitted you to put away your wives; but it was not so from the beginning.
MAT 19:9 Now I say to you, Whosoever shall put away his wife, except it be for whoredom and shall marry another, committeth adultery: and he who marrieth her who was put away committeth adultery.
MAT 19:10 His disciples say to him, If such be the case between the husband and wife, it is not expedient to marry.
MAT 19:11 Whereupon he said to them, All men cannot admit this inference. But with respect to them to whom it is granted
MAT 19:12 [for there are some who have been eunuchs from their birth, and some have been made eunuchs by men, and there are some who have made themselves eunuchs for the kingdom of heaven] let him admit it, who can admit it.
MAT 19:13 Then children were brought to him that he might lay his hands on them and pray for them; and his disciples rebuked them.
MAT 19:14 Whereupon Jesus said, Let the children alone, and do not hinder them to come to me; for of such is the kingdom of the heavens.
MAT 19:15 And when he had laid his hands on them he departed thence.
MAT 19:16 And behold there came one who said to him, Good teacher, what good thing shall I do, that I may have an everlasting life?
MAT 19:17 In reply to which Jesus said to him, Why callest thou me good? There is none good but God only. But if thou desirest to enter into that life, keep the commandments.
MAT 19:18 He saith to him, Which? And Jesus said, These: Thou shalt not commit murder; Thou shalt not commit adultery; Thou shalt not steal; Thou shall not bear false witness;
MAT 19:19 Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
MAT 19:20 The youth said to him, All these I have kept from my childhood. What do I yet lack?
MAT 19:21 Jesus said to him, If thou wishest to be perfect, go, sell thy estate, and give to the poor; and thou shalt have treasure in heaven. Then come and follow me.
MAT 19:22 Upon hearing this word, the youth went away sorrowful; for he had great possessions.
MAT 19:23 Thereupon Jesus said to his disciples, Verily I say to you, With difficulty will a rich man enter the kingdom of heaven.
MAT 19:24 Again I say to you, It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
MAT 19:25 When his disciples heard this they were greatly astonished and said, Who then can be saved?
MAT 19:26 Thereupon Jesus looking earnestly at them said, With men this is impossible; but with God all things are possible.
MAT 19:27 Then Peter addressing him said, Behold we have left all and followed thee, what then shall we have?
MAT 19:28 Thereupon Jesus said to him, Verily I say to you, With respect to you who have  followed me, at the renovation, when the son of man shall sit on the throne of his glory, you also shall sit on twelve thrones judging the twelve tribes of Israel.
MAT 19:29 And everyone who hath forsaken houses, or brethren, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields for the sake of my name, shall receive an hundred fold compensation. He shall indeed inherit an everlasting life.
MAT 19:30 But many will be first who are last; and last, who are first.
MAT 20:1 For the reign of the heavens is like a householder who went out early in the morning to hire labourers for his vineyard.
MAT 20:2 And having agreed with some labourers for a deniar a day, he sent them to his vineyard.
MAT 20:3 And going out about the third hour he saw some standing in the market place, unemployed,
MAT 20:4 and said to them, Go ye also to the vineyard and I will give you what is reasonable. So they went.
MAT 20:5 Again about the sixth and ninth hour he went out and did the same.
MAT 20:6 And having gone out about the eleventh hour, he found others standing unemployed, and saith to them, Why have you stood here all the day unemployed?
MAT 20:7 They say to him, Because no one hath hired us. He saith to them, Go ye also to the vineyard and you shall receive what is reasonable.
MAT 20:8 And in the evening the owner of the vineyard said to his steward, Call the labourers and pay them their wages, beginning with the last and ending with the first.
MAT 20:9 So they who had been hired at the eleventh hour, came and received even one a deniar.
MAT 20:10 And when the first hired came, they expected to receive more; but they also received everyone a deniar.
MAT 20:11 And when they received it, they murmured against the householder,
MAT 20:12 saying, These last have worked but one hour, and thou hast made them equal to us, who have borne the burden, and the heat of the day.
MAT 20:13 But he in reply said to one of them, Companion! I do thee no wrong. Didst thou not agree with me for a deniar:
MAT 20:14 take what is thine and go thy way. It is my will to give this last as much as to thee.
MAT 20:15 Is it not lawful for me to do what I please with mine own? Is thine eye evil because I am good?
MAT 20:16 So the last shall be first, and the first last. For there are many called, but few chosen.
MAT 20:17 As Jesus was going up to Jerusalem, he took the twelve disciples apart on the road and said to them,
MAT 20:18 Behold we are going up to Jerusalem, and the son of man will be delivered up to the chief priests and Scribes; and they will condemn him to death,
MAT 20:19 and deliver him up to the Gentiles to be mocked, and scourged, and crucified, and on the third day he will rise again.
MAT 20:20 Then the mother of Zebedee's children came to him with her sons, and, prostrating herself, asked a favour of him.
MAT 20:21 Whereupon he said to her, What is thy desire? She said to him, Grant that these two sons of mine may sit, one on thy right hand and the other on thy left in thy kingdom.
MAT 20:22 In reply to which Jesus said, You do not know what you ask. Can you drink the cup which I shall soon drink and be baptized with the baptism, with which I am baptized? They say to him, We can.
MAT 20:23 Then Jesus saith to them, You will indeed drink my cup and be baptized with the baptism with which I am baptized: but to sit on my right hand, and on my left, is not mine to give, unless to them for whom it is prepared by my father.
MAT 20:24 When the ten heard, they were moved with indignation against the two brothers.
MAT 20:25 Whereupon Jesus having called them to him, said, You know that the chiefs of the nations exercise dominion over them; and they who are grandees exercise authority over them:
MAT 20:26 but it shall not be so among you. But whoever among you would wish to be great, let him be your attendant.
MAT 20:27 And whoever among you would wish to be first, let him be your servant;
MAT 20:28 even as the son of man came not to be waited on, but to wait, and to give his life a ransom for many.
MAT 20:29 Now when they were going from Jericho a great multitude followed him.
MAT 20:30 And lo! two blind men who sat by the way side, hearing that Jesus was passing by, cried, saying, Have pity on us, O master, son of David.
MAT 20:31 And when the people reprimanded them that they might hold their peace, they cried the louder, saying, Have pity on us, O master, son of David.
MAT 20:32 Whereupon, Jesus, stopping, called them and said, What do you desire me to do for you?
MAT 20:33 They say to him, Sir! that our eyes may be opened.
MAT 20:34 And Jesus had compassion and touched their eyes; and instantly they received sight. And they followed him.
MAT 21:1 And when they approached Jerusalem and were come to Bethphage, near to the mount of olives, then Jesus sent two disciples,
MAT 21:2 saying to them, Go to that village which is over against you, and straightway you will find an ass tied and a colt with her. Loose her and bring them to me.
MAT 21:3 And if anyone say anything to you; say, The Lord hath need of them and will quickly send them back.
MAT 21:4 Now all this was done, so that there was an accomplishment of what was spoken by the prophet, saying,
MAT 21:5 "Say to the daughter of Sion, Behold thy king cometh to thee, meek and mounted on an ass; even on a young colt the foal of an ass."
MAT 21:6 So the disciples went, and having done as Jesus commanded them,
MAT 21:7 they brought the ass and the colt and threw their mantles on them, and set him thereon.
