MAT 21:8 And the greater part of the multitude threw their mantles on the way, and some cut branches from the trees and strewed them in the way.
MAT 21:9 And the crowds that went before, and they who followed, shouted, saying, Hosannah to the son of David! Blessed he, who is coming in the name of the Lord! Hosannah in the highest!
MAT 21:10 And as he entered Jerusalem, all the city was in commotion, saying, Who is this?
MAT 21:11 And the multitude said, This is Jesus the prophet, who is of Nazareth in Galilee.
MAT 21:12 And Jesus went into the temple of God and drove out all those who were selling and buying in the temple, and overturned the tables of the money changers and the stalls of them who sold doves,
MAT 21:13 and said to them, It is written, "My house shall be called a house of prayer," but you have made it a den of robbers.
MAT 21:14 Then the blind and the lame came to him in the temple and he healed them.
MAT 21:15 When the chief priests and the Scribes saw the wonders which he did, and the children shouting in the temple, and saying, Hosannah to the son of David, they were filled with indignation,
MAT 21:16 and said to him, Hearest thou what these say? Jesus saith to them, Yes. Have you never read, "From the mouth of babes and sucklings thou hast perfected praise."
MAT 21:17 Then leaving them he went out of the city to Bethany and lodged there.
MAT 21:18 In the morning, when he was coming to the city, he was hungry,
MAT 21:19 and seeing a fig tree near the way, he went to it and found nothing thereon but leaves. Whereupon he saith to it, Henceforward let no fruit ever grow on thee. And immediately the fig tree withered.
MAT 21:20 When the disciples saw this they expressed astonishment, saying, How suddenly the fig tree is withered!
MAT 21:21 And Jesus answering, said to them, Verily I say to you, if you have faith, without wavering, you may do not only as much as is done to this fig tree; but if you should even say to that mountain, Be thou lifted up and thrown into the sea, it shall be done.
MAT 21:22 And whatever you ask in prayer, with faith, you shall obtain.
MAT 21:23 And when he was come to the temple, the chief priests and the elders of the people came to him as he was teaching, and said, By what authority dost thou these things? And, Who gave thee this authority?
MAT 21:24 In reply to which, Jesus saith to them, Let me also ask you a question, which if you answer me, I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
MAT 21:25 Whence was the baptism of John? From heaven, or of men? Upon this they reasoned among themselves, saying, if we say, From heaven, he will say, Why then did you not believe him:
MAT 21:26 and if we say, Of men, we fear the people; for they all hold John as a prophet.
MAT 21:27 So in answer to Jesus, they said, We cannot tell. Thereupon Jesus said, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
MAT 21:28 But what think you? A man had two sons. And coming to the first, he said, Son, go work today in my vineyard.
MAT 21:30 And he in reply said, I will not. But afterwards he repented and went. And coming to the second, he ordered him in like manner; and he in reply said, I will, sir; but did not go.
MAT 21:31 Which of the two did the will of his father? They say to him, The first. Jesus saith to them, Verily I say to you, The publicans and the harlots lead the way for you to the kingdom of God.
MAT 21:32 For John came to you in the way of righteousness, and you believed him not: but the publicans and the harlots believed him. And though you saw this, you did not afterwards repent and believe him.
MAT 21:33 Hear another parable. There was a certain landlord who planted a vineyard and hedged it around, and dug therein a wine lake, and built a tower, and let it to tenants and went to a distant country.
MAT 21:34 And when the fruit season approached, he sent his servants to the tenants to receive the fruits of it.
MAT 21:35 But the tenants seizing his servants, beat one and killed another, and stoned another.
MAT 21:36 Again he sent other servants in greater number than the first, and they treated them in the same manner.
MAT 21:37 At last he sent to them his son, saying, They will reverence my son.
MAT 21:38 But when the tenants saw the son, they said among themselves, This is the heir. Come let us kill him and keep possession of his inheritance.
MAT 21:39 So, seizing him, they turned him out of the vineyard and slew him.
MAT 21:40 Now when the lord of the vineyard shall come, what will he do to these tenants?
MAT 21:41 They say to him, "Wretches! he will put them to a wretched death: and his vineyard he will let to others; who will render him the fruits in their seasons."
MAT 21:42 Jesus saith to them, Have you never read in the scriptures, "The stone which the builders rejected was the very one for the head of the corner. This [salvation] was from the Lord, and it is wonderful in our eyes."
MAT 21:43 Therefore I say to you, The kingdom of God shall be taken from you and given to a nation producing the fruits thereof.
MAT 21:44 And he who falleth on that stone will be bruised, but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.
MAT 21:45 Now the chief priests and the Pharisees, when they heard his parables, knew that he spake of them:
MAT 21:46 but when they sought to seize him, they were afraid of the multitude, because they regarded him as a prophet.
MAT 22:1 So Jesus, continuing his discourse, addressed them again in parables, saying,
MAT 22:2 The reign of the heavens may be compared to a temporal king, who made a marriage feast for his son.
MAT 22:3 And he sent his servants to call them who were invited to the wedding, but they would not come.
MAT 22:4 Again he sent other servants, saying, Tell them who have been invited, Behold I have prepared my dinner. My bullocks and my fatlings are killed and all things are ready. Come to the wedding feast.
MAT 22:5 But they turned away with indifference, one to his farm, and another to his merchandise
MAT 22:6 and the rest seized his servants, insulted, and slew them.
MAT 22:7 When the king heard this he was incensed, and sent forth his armies, and destroyed the murderers, and burned their city.
MAT 22:8 Then he saith to his servants, The wedding is indeed ready. but they who have been invited are unworthy;
MAT 22:9 Go ye therefor, to the highways, and invite to the wedding as many as you meet with.
MAT 22:10 Accordingly the servants went out to the highway and assembled all that they met, bad and good. And the wedding was plentifully supplied with guests.
MAT 22:11 And when the king came in to see the guests, he saw there a man who had not on a wedding garment, and saith to him,
MAT 22:12 Companion, how camest thou hither without having on a wedding garment. And he was struck speechless.
MAT 22:13 Then the king said to the attendants, Bind his hands and feet and carry him out and cast him into the outer darkness. Weeping and gnashing of teeth will be there.
MAT 22:14 For there are many called, but few chosen.
MAT 22:15 Then the Pharisees went out and consulted how they might ensnare him by a discourse.
MAT 22:16 So they send to him their disciples with the Herodians, saying, Teacher, We know that thou art true and teachest the way of God truly, and carest for no one. For thou respectest not the persons of men.
MAT 22:17 Tell us therefore what thou thinkest. Is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar, or not?
MAT 22:18 But Jesus, knowing their malice, said, Hypocrites! Why do ye try me?
MAT 22:19 Shew me the tribute money. So they brought him a deniar,
MAT 22:20 then he saith to them, Whose image and inscription is this?
MAT 22:21 They say to him, Caesar's. Then he saith to them, Render then to Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and to God, the things which are God's.
MAT 22:22 Upon hearing this they were struck with surprise, and left him and went away.
MAT 22:23 On the same day there came to him Sadducees, who say, There is no future state. And they asked him,
MAT 22:24 saying, Teacher, Moses said, If a man die, having no children, his brother shall marry his wife, and raise up seed for his brother.
MAT 22:25 Now there were with us seven brothers. And the first married a wife and died; and having no children, he left his wife for his brother.
MAT 22:26 In like manner also the second and the third, even to the seventh.
MAT 22:27 And last of all, the woman also died:
MAT 22:28 in the future state therefore, whose wife shall she be of the seven? For they all married her.
MAT 22:29 In reply to which, Jesus said to them, Ye err, not knowing the scriptures nor the power of God.
MAT 22:30 For in the future state, they neither marry, nor are given in marriage, but are as the angels of God in heaven.
MAT 22:31 But in respect to the revival of the dead. Have you not read what was spoken to you: by God, saying,
MAT 22:32 "I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaak, and the God of Jacob," God is not the God of the dead; but of the living.
MAT 22:33 When the people heard this they were astonished at his manner of teaching.
MAT 22:34 Now when the Pharisees heard that he had silenced the Sadducees, they flocked about him for the same purpose.
MAT 22:35 And one of them, an expounder of the law, with a view to 36 try him, asked him this question,
MAT 22:36 Teacher, which is the great commandment in the law?
MAT 22:37 Thereupon Jesus said to him, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God, with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy mind.
MAT 22:38 This is the first and great commandment.
MAT 22:39 And the second is like it, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
MAT 22:40 On these two commandments hang the whole law and the prophets.
MAT 22:41 Now while the Pharisees were together, Jesus asked them,
MAT 22:42 saying, What think ye concerning the Christ? Whose Son is he? They say to him, David's.
MAT 22:43 He saith to them, How then doth David by the spirit call him Lord; saying,
MAT 22:44 "The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand, until I make thine enemies thy footstool."
MAT 22:45 If then David calleth him Lord: how is he his son?
MAT 22:46 And none could answer him a word. Nor did any one presume from that day forward to ask him any more questions.
MAT 23:1 Then Jesus spake to the multitude and to his disciples,
MAT 23:2 saying, The Scribes and the Pharisees sit in Moses' chair.
MAT 23:3 Observe then and do whatever they enjoin you: but do not act as they do. For they say and do not practise.
MAT 23:4 For they bind up heavy and insupportable burdens and lay them on men's shoulders: but they themselves will not move them with their finger.
MAT 23:5 But all their works they do to be seen by men. For this they make their phylacteries broad, and enlarge the tufts of their mantles,
MAT 23:6 and love the uppermost places at entertainments; and the first seats in the synagogues;
MAT 23:7 and salutations in places of public resort; and to be called by men, Rabbi, Rabbi.
MAT 23:8 But as for you, be ye not called Rabbi; for one is your teacher, namely the Christ. Now as for you all, ye are brethren,
MAT 23:9 and should call no one on earth your father, for one is your father, namely, he who is in heaven.
MAT 23:10 Neither be ye called leaders for one is your leader, namely the Christ.
MAT 23:11 Let then the greatest among you be your attendant.
MAT 23:12 For who soever exalteth himself, shall be humbled, but he who humbleth himself, shall be exalted.
MAT 23:13 Now alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you shut up the kingdom of the heavens against men. For you neither enter in yourselves, nor suffer them who are going in, to enter.
MAT 23:14 Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you devour the houses of the widows; and for a pretext make long prayers. For this you shall be punished with greater severity.
MAT 23:15 Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you traverse sea and land to make one proselyte; and when he is gained, you make him doubly more a child of hell, than yourselves.
MAT 23:16 Alas for you, blind guides, who say, to swear by the temple is not binding; but to swear by the gold of the temple is binding.
MAT 23:17 Foolish and blind! which is greater? The gold? Or the temple which halloweth the gold?
MAT 23:18 And, to swear by the altar doth not bind; but to swear by the gift thereon is binding.
MAT 23:19 Foolish and blind! which is greater? The gift? Or the altar which halloweth the gift?
MAT 23:20 He therefore who sweareth by the altar, sweareth by it and by all on it.
MAT 23:21 And he who sweareth by the temple, sweareth by it and by him who dwelleth therein.
MAT 23:22 And he who sweareth by heaven, sweareth by the throne of God, and by him who sitteth upon it.
MAT 23:23 Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you pay tithe of mint, and dill and cummin, and have neglected the weightier matters of the law; justice, mercy and fidelity. These you ought to have practised without omitting those.
MAT 23:24 Blind guides, you are skimming off the gnat, and swallowing the camel.
MAT 23:25 Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you cleanse the outside of the cup and the plate; but on the inside they are full of rapine, and intemperance.
MAT 23:26 Blind Pharisee, cleanse first what is within the cup, and the plate; so the outside will be clean.
MAT 23:27 Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you are like whitened sepulchres. These indeed appear beautiful on the outside; but within they are full of dead men's bones, and of all Corruption.
MAT 23:28 In like manner you also appear outwardly to men to be righteous; but you are inwardly full of hypocrisy and iniquity.
MAT 23:29 Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you build the sepulchres of the prophets and adorn the monuments of the righteous,
MAT 23:30 and say, If we had been in the days of our fathers we would not have been their accomplices in the blood of the prophets.
MAT 23:31 So you testify against yourselves that you are the sons of them who killed the prophets.
MAT 23:32 As for you then, fill up the measure of your fathers.
MAT 23:33 Serpents! brood of vipers! how can you escape the punishment of hell?
MAT 23:34 For this, behold I am about to send you prophets, wise men and Scribes: and some of them you will kill and crucify; and some of them you will scourge in your synagogues, and persecute from city to city;
MAT 23:35 that upon you may come all the righteous blood shed upon the earth; from the blood of righteous Abel to the blood of Zacharias, son of Barachias, whom ye slew between the temple and the altar.
MAT 23:36 Verily I say to you, All these things will come upon this generation.
MAT 23:37 O Jerusalem! Jerusalem! thou that killest the prophets and stonest them who are sent to thee! how often have I desired to gather thy children even as a hen gathereth her chickens under her wings; but you would not!
MAT 23:38 behold this house of yours is left desolate
MAT 23:39 for you. For I say to you, Henceforth you shall not see me until you say, Blessed is he who is coming in the name of the Lord.
MAT 24:1 Then Jesus went out, and as he was going from the temple, his disciples came to point out to him the buildings of the temple.
MAT 24:2 Whereupon he said to them, See ye not all these? Verily I say to you, There shall not be left here one stone upon another, which shall not be pulled down.
MAT 24:3 And as he was sitting on the mount of olives, his disciples came to him privately and said, Tell us, when will these  Mat 24:things happen; and what will be the sign of thy coming and of the conclusion of this age?
MAT 24:4 Thereupon Jesus answering, said to them, Take heed that no one seduce you.
MAT 24:5 For many will come in my name, saying, I am the Christ and will seduce many.
MAT 24:6 As you will soon hear of wars and rumours of wars, see that you be not troubled. For all these things must happen, but the end is not yet.
MAT 24:7 For nation will rise against nation; and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be famines and pestilences and earthquakes in divers places.
MAT 24:8 Now all these are the beginning of sorrows.
MAT 24:9 Then they will deliver you up to affliction and put you to death; and you will be hated by all nations on the account of my name.
MAT 24:10 And many will then be stumbled and will deliver up one another and hate one another.
MAT 24:11 And many false prophets will rise up and deceive many.
MAT 24:12 And because iniquity will abound, the love of many will grow cold.
MAT 24:13 But he who persevereth to the end shall be saved.
MAT 24:14 The good news of the kingdom shall indeed be proclaimed throughout the whole world for a testimony to all the nations. And then will come the end.
MAT 24:15 Therefore when you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by Daniel the prophet, standing in a holy place, [reader attend!]
MAT 24:16 then let them who are in Judea flee to the mountains:
MAT 24:17 and let not him who is on the house top go down, to carry away any thing out of the house,
MAT 24:18 nor him who is in the field turn back to take up his clothes.
MAT 24:19 But alas for the women with child and for them who give suck in those days.
MAT 24:20 Pray ye therefore that your flight may not be in the winter, nor on a sabbath day.
MAT 24:21 For there will then be great affliction, such as hath not happened from the beginning of the world till now: no, nor ever shall be.
MAT 24:22 Indeed if those days were not shortened, no flesh could escape. But for the sake of the chosen, those days will be shortened.
MAT 24:23 At that time if any say to you, Lo! the Christ is here! or there! believe it not.
MAT 24:24 For false Christs and false prophets will rise up and give out great signs and wonders, so as to deceive, if it were possible, even the chosen.
MAT 24:25 Behold I have forewarned you.
MAT 24:26 Therefore if they say to you, Behold he is in the desert, go not out. Or, behold he is in the secret apartments! do not believe them.
MAT 24:27 For as the lightning, which breaketh forth from the east, shineth even to the west, so will the coming of the son of man be.
MAT 24:28 For wherever the carcass is, there will the eagles be assembled.
MAT 24:29 Now immediately after the tribulation of those days the sun will be darkened and the moon will not give her splendour; and the stars will fall from heaven, and the heavenly powers will be shaken. And then will appear the sign of the son of man in heaven.
MAT 24:30 And then, all the tribes of the land will mourn: and they shall see the son of man coming on the clouds of heaven, with power and great glory.
MAT 24:31 And he will send out his messengers with a loud sounding trumpet, and they will gather his chosen ones from the four winds; from one extremity of heaven to the other.
MAT 24:32 Now learn this parable from that fig tree. When its branches become tender and put forth leaves, you know that the summer is near.
MAT 24:33 So when you see all these things, know assuredly that he is near; at the door.
MAT 24:34 Verily I say to you, This generation shall not pass until all these things shall happen.
MAT 24:35 The heaven and the earth shall fail; but my words shall not fail.
MAT 24:36 But with respect to the day and the season, that none knoweth, not even the angels of the heavens; none but my father only.
MAT 24:37 For as the days of Noe were, so also will this coming of the son of man be.
MAT 24:38 For as in those days, before the deluge, they were eating and drinking, marrying and giving in marriage, till Noe entered the ark;
MAT 24:39 and they did not know till the flood came and swept them all away; so will this coming of the son of man be.
MAT 24:40 Two men will then be in the field; the one is taken and the other left.
MAT 24:41 Two women will be grinding at the mill, the one is taken and the other left.
MAT 24:42 Watch therefore, because you know not at what season your lord cometh.
MAT 24:43 But this you know, that if the master of a family knew at what watch the thief would come, he would be upon guard and not suffer him to break into his house.
MAT 24:44 Be ye therefore ready prepared, because the son of man cometh at an hour you least expect.
MAT 24:45 Who is indeed the faithful and prudent servant, whom his lord hath set over his household to give them their food in due season.
MAT 24:46 Happy that servant, whom his lord when he cometh shall find thus employed.
MAT 24:47 Verily I say to you, he will set him over all his estate.
MAT 24:48 But if that servant being wicked should say in his heart, My lord delayeth his coming;
MAT 24:49 and begin to beat his fellow tenants, and to eat and to drink with drunkards;
MAT 24:50 the lord of that servant will come on a day he least expecteth, and at an hour of which he is not aware
MAT 24:51 and will scourge him in the severest manner and assign him his portion with the hypocrites. Weeping and gnashing of teeth will be there.
MAT 25:1 Now with respect to this, the reign of the heavens may be compared to ten virgins who took their lamps and went out to meet the bridegroom.
MAT 25:2 And five of them were prudent and five foolish.
MAT 25:3 They who were foolish took their lamps, but did not take oil with them.
MAT 25:4 But the prudent took oil in their vessels with their lamps.
MAT 25:5 And while the bridegroom tarried they all became drowsy and fell asleep.
MAT 25:6 And at midnight there was a cry, Behold the bridegroom is coming; Go out and meet him.
MAT 25:7 Then all the virgins arose and trimmed their lamps.
MAT 25:8 And the foolish said to the prudent, Give us some of your oil, for our lamps are going out.
MAT 25:9 In reply to which the prudent said, Perhaps there will not be enough for us and you. Therefore go rather to them who sell, and buy for yourselves.
MAT 25:10 And while they were going to buy, the bridegroom came, and they who were ready went in with him to the wedding, and the door was shut.
MAT 25:11 And after that the other virgins came, saying, Master, master, Open to us.
MAT 25:12 But he in reply, said, Verily I say to you, I do not know you.
MAT 25:13 Watch therefore, because you do not know the day, nor the hour, when the son of man cometh.
MAT 25:14 For he is like a man who, intending to travel, called his servants and committed to them his effects,
MAT 25:15 and to one gave five talents and to another two, and to another one; to every one according to his respective ability, and straightway set out on his journey.
MAT 25:16 Then he who had received the five talents went and traded with them, and made five other talents;
MAT 25:17 and in like manner he who had received the two gained also other two;
MAT 25:18 but he who received the one went and digged a hole in the ground and hid his master's money:
MAT 25:19 and after a long time the master of these servants cometh and reckoneth with them:
MAT 25:20 whereupon he who had received the five talents came and brought other five talents, saying, Sir, thou deliveredst to me five talents, here are besides them five other talents, which I have gained:
MAT 25:21 and his master said to him; "Well done, good and faithful servant, thou hast been faithful in a small trust, I will give thee a much greater; enter into the joy of thy master:"
MAT 25:22 then he who had received the two talents came and said, Sir, thou deliveredst to me two talents, here are, besides them, two other talents, which I have gained:
MAT 25:23 his master said to him, Well done, good and faithful servant, thou hast been faithful in a small trust, I will give thee a much greater, enter thou into the joy of thy master:
MAT 25:24 then he, who had received the one talent, came and said, Sir, I knew that thou art a hard man, reaping where thou hast not sown, and gathering where thou didst not scatter; so,
MAT 25:25 being afraid, I went and hid thy talent in the earth. Here it is. Thou hast what is thine own.
MAT 25:26 Thereupon his master said to him in reply, Malignant and slothful servant! Thou knowest that I reap where I did not sow, and gather where I did not scatter!
MAT 25:27 Thou shouldst therefore have lodged my money with the bankers, that at my return I might have received mine own with interest.
MAT 25:28 Take therefore the talent from him; and give it to him who hath the ten talents.
MAT 25:29 For to every one who improveth more shall be given, and he shall abound; but from him who improveth not, even what he hath shall be taken away:
MAT 25:30 and turn out this unprofitable servant into outer darkness; weeping and gnashing of teeth will be there.
MAT 25:31 So when the son of man shall come in his glory, and all the holy angels with him; he will then sit on the throne of his glory.
MAT 25:32 And before him shall be assembled all the nations. And he will separate them one from another, as a shepherd separateth the sheep from the goats.
MAT 25:33 And he will place the sheep on the right hand and the goats on his left.
MAT 25:34 Then the king will say to them on his right, Come ye blessed of my Father, inherit the kingdom which hath been prepared for you from the formation of the world:
MAT 25:35 for I was hungry, and you gave me food; I was thirsty, and you gave me drink; I was a stranger, and you lodged me;
MAT 25:36 naked, and you clothed me; sick, and you took care of me; I was in prison, and you visited me.
MAT 25:37 Then the righteous will answer him, saying, Lord, when did we see thee hungry, and feed thee; or thirsty, and give thee drink?
MAT 25:38 When saw we thee a stranger, and lodged thee; or naked, and clothed thee?
MAT 25:39 Or when saw we thee sick, or in prison, and came to thee?
MAT 25:40 And the king in reply will say to them, Verily I say to you, Inasmuch as you have done this to one of these my brethren, even the least, you have done it to me.
MAT 25:41 Then he will say to them on his left, Depart from me, ye cursed, into the fire which is everlasting; that prepared for the devil and his angels!
MAT 25:42 For I was hungry, and you gave me no food; I was thirsty, and you gave me no drink;
MAT 25:43 I was a stranger, and you did not lodge me; naked, and you did not clothe me; sick, and in prison, and you did not visit me.
MAT 25:44 Then they also will answer him, saying, Lord, when did we see thee hungry, or thirsty, or a stranger, or naked, or sick, or in prison, and did not minister to thee?
MAT 25:45 And he will answer them, saying, Verily I say to you, Inasmuch as you have not done this to any, the least of these, you have not done it to me.
MAT 25:46 So these shall go to everlasting punishment and the righteous to an everlasting life.
MAT 26:1 When Jesus had finished all these discourses, he said to his disciples,
MAT 26:2 You know that two days hence is the passover, when the son of man is to be delivered up to be crucified.
MAT 26:3 At that time the chief priests, and the Scribes, and the elders of the people, were convened to the court of the high priest, whose name was Caiaphas,
MAT 26:4 and were consulting how they might take Jesus by surprise and kill him.
MAT 26:5 And they said, Not at the festival, that there may not be a tumult among the people.
MAT 26:6 Now when Jesus was at Bethany, in the house of Simon the leper,
MAT 26:7 there came to him a woman, having an alabaster box of precious balsam, which she poured on his head while he was at table.
MAT 26:8 At seeing this, his disciples expressed indignation, saying, Why this profusion!
MAT 26:9 For this balsam might have been sold for a great sum, and given to the poor.
MAT 26:10 Jesus, knowing it, said to them, Why trouble ye the woman? For she hath done a good office for me.
MAT 26:11 For you have the poor always with you; but me you have not always.
MAT 26:12 For in pouring this balsam on my body, she hath done it to embalm me.
MAT 26:13 Verily I say to you, In what part soever of the world these glad tidings shall be proclaimed, mention will also be made of what she hath done, for a memorial of her.
MAT 26:14 Then one of the twelve, named Judas Iscariot, went to the chief priests,
MAT 26:15 and said, What will you give me, and I will deliver him up to you. And they weighed to him thirty shekels of silver:
MAT 26:16 And from that time he watched an opportunity to deliver him up.
MAT 26:17 Now, on the first day of unleavened bread, his disciples came to Jesus, and said to him, Where wilt thou have us make preparation for thee to eat the passover?
MAT 26:18 And he said, Go to the city, to such a person, and say to him, The teacher saith, My time is near. At thy house I am about to celebrate the passover with my disciples.
MAT 26:19 Accordingly the disciples did as Jesus commanded them, and prepared the passover.
MAT 26:20 And when the evening was come he placed himself at the table, with the twelve.
MAT 26:21 And while they were eating, he said, Verily I say to you, One of you is to deliver me up.
MAT 26:22 And they being very sorrowful, began every one of them to say to him, Master, am I?
MAT 26:23 Whereupon he answering, said, One who hath dipped his hand in the dish with me is to deliver me up.
MAT 26:24 The son of man goeth indeed as it is written of him. But alas for that man by whom the son of man is delivered up. Good were it for that man if he had never been born.
MAT 26:25 Even Judas who was about to deliver him up, having taken occasion, said, Am I, Rabbi? He saith to him, As thou hast said.
MAT 26:26 Now as they were eating, Jesus having taken the loaf and pronounced a blessing, broke and gave to the disciples, and said, Take, eat; This is my body.
MAT 26:27 Then having taken the cup and given thanks, he gave it to them, saying, Drink ye all of it.
MAT 26:28 For this is my blood; that of the new covenant; that shed for many, for the remission of sins.
MAT 26:29 Now I say to you, "I will not henceforth drink of the product of the vine; until the day when I shall drink it new with you in my father's kingdom."
MAT 26:30 And after the hymn they went out to the mount of olives.
MAT 26:31 Then Jesus saith to them, You will all be stumbled at me this night; for it is written, I will smite the shepherd and the sheep of the flock will be dispersed!
MAT 26:32 But after I am risen, I will go before you to Galilee.
MAT 26:33 Thereupon Peter addressing him, said, Though all should be stumbled at thee; as for me, I will never be stumbled.
MAT 26:34 Jesus said to him, Verily I say to thee, This very night, before cock crowing, thou wilt three times deny me.
MAT 26:35 Peter saith to him, Though I should die with thee, I will not deny thee. And so said all the disciples.
MAT 26:36 Then Jesus goeth with them to a place called Gethsemane, and saith to the disciples, Stay here while I go yonder to pray.
MAT 26:37 And having taken with him Peter, and the two sons of Zebedee, he began to be in an agony of grief and distress.
MAT 26:38 Whereupon he saith to them, My soul is overwhelmed with anguish 9 even to death. Stay here and watch with me.
MAT 26:39 Then, advancing a little further, he fell prostrate on his face, and prayed, saying, O my father, if it be possible, let this cup be removed from me. Nevertheless not as I would, but as thou wiliest.
MAT 26:40 Then he cometh to the disciples, and finding them asleep, he saith to Peter, So, could you not watch one hour with me?
MAT 26:41 Watch and pray, that you may not come to a trial. The spirit indeed is willing; but the flesh is weak.
MAT 26:42 Again he went away the second time, and prayed, saying, O my father! If this cup cannot be removed from me, without my drinking it; thy will be done.
MAT 26:43 Then coming, he findeth them again sleeping; for their eyes were weighed down.
MAT 26:44 So, leaving them he withdrew again, and prayed a third time, to the same purpose.
MAT 26:45 Then he cometh to these disciples of his, and saith to them, Are you still sleeping and taking repose? Behold the hour is come, and the son of man is delivered up into the hands of sinners.
MAT 26:46 Arise; let us go. Behold he who delivereth me up is at hand.
MAT 26:47 And while he was yet speaking, lo! Judas, one of the twelve, came, and with him a great multitude with swords and clubs, from the chief priests, and the elders of the people.
MAT 26:48 Now his betrayer had given them a sign, saying, The person I shall kiss is he; Secure him.
MAT 26:49 So coming directly up to Jesus, he said, Hail, Rabbi! and kissed him.
MAT 26:50 And Jesus said to him, Companion! for what purpose art thou come? Then others, advancing, laid hands on Jesus, and held him.
MAT 26:51 Upon which one of them who were with Jesus, stretching forth his hand, drew his sword, and smote the servant of the high priest, and cut off his ear.
MAT 26:52 Thereupon Jesus saith to him, Return thy sword to its place. For are all who have taken a sword to perish by a sword?
MAT 26:53 Or dost thou think that I cannot now address ray father, who can send to my assistance, more than twelve legions of angels?
MAT 26:54 How then would the scriptures be fulfilled, that thus it must be?
MAT 26:55 At that instant Jesus was saying to the multitudes, Are you come out as against a rubber with swords and clubs, to take me? Day after day I sat before you teaching in the temple, and you did not lay hold on me.
MAT 26:56 But all this is done that the writings of the prophets may be confirmed. Then all the disciples forsook him and fled.
MAT 26:57 And they who had hold of Jesus led him away to Caiaphas, the high priest, where the Scribes and the elders of the people were assembled.
MAT 26:58 Now Peter followed him at a distance, even to the court of the high priest. And having gone in, he sat down with the attendants, to see the issue.
MAT 26:59 And the chief priests and the elders, even the whole Sanhedrim, sought false testimony against Jesus that they might put him to death,
MAT 26:60 but found it not. Though many false witnesses came forward, they did not find it. At last two false witnesses came,
MAT 26:61 who said, This man said, I can destroy the temple of God and in three days rebuild it.
MAT 26:62 Then the chief priest, standing up, said to him, "Answerest thou nothing to what these testify against thee?"
MAT 26:63 But Jesus was silent. Then the chief priest addressing him, said, I adjure thee by the living God, that thou tell us whether thou art the Christ, the son of God.
MAT 26:64 Jesus saith to him, It is as thou hast spoken. Moreover I say to you, Hereafter you shall see the son of man sitting at the right hand of that Power, and coming on the clouds of heaven.
MAT 26:65 Upon this the high priest rent his clothes, saying, He hath blasphemed. What further need have we of witnesses? Behold you have now heard his blasphemy.
MAT 26:66 What think ye? Thereupon they, answering, said, He is guilty of death.
MAT 26:67 Then they spat in his face and struck him with their fists,68 and smote him with staves, saying,
MAT 26:68 Prophesy to us Christ. Who is he that smote thee?
MAT 26:69 Now when Peter was sitting without, in the court, a servant maid came up to him and said, Thou also wast with Jesus the Galilean.
MAT 26:70 And he denied before them all, saying, I do not know what thou sayest
MAT 26:71 And as he was going out into the porch another maid saw him, and saith to them there, That man also was with Jesus the Nazarene.
MAT 26:72 And he again denied, with an oath, I do not know the man.
MAT 26:73 And a little after, some byestanders came up and said to Peter, Thou also art certainly one of them, for thy speech discovereth thee.
MAT 26:74 Then he began to curse and to swear, I do not know the man. And immediately a cock crowed.
MAT 26:75 Whereupon Peter recollected the word which Jesus said to him, "Before cockcrowing thou wilt three times deny me;" and going out, he wept bitterly.
MAT 27:1 Now early in the morning, all the chief priests and the elders of the people took counsel against Jesus to have him put to death.
MAT 27:2 So, having bound him, they led him away and delivered him up to Pontius Pilate the governor.
MAT 27:3 Then Judas, who had delivered him up, finding that he was condemned, repented and carried back the thirty shekels of silver to the chief priests and the elders,
MAT 27:4 saying, I have sinned in having betrayed innocent blood To which they replied, What is that to us? Look thou to that.
MAT 27:5 Thereupon he threw down the money in the temple, and withdrew, and went and strangled himself.
MAT 27:6 And the chief priests, taking the money, said; It is not lawful to put it into the holy treasury, seeing it is the price of blood.
MAT 27:7 So, having consulted together, they bought with it the pottor's field for the burial of strangers.
MAT 27:8 Therefore that field is ever since called the field of blood.
MAT 27:9 Then was fulfilled that, which was spoken by the prophet Jeremias, saying, "So I took the thirty pieces of silver, as the Lord commanded me. These being the price of him who was valued, whom some of the Israelites valued;
MAT 27:10 these they gave for the potter's field."
MAT 27:11 Now when Jesus stood before the governor, the governor asked him, saying, Thou art the king of the Jews? And Jesus said to him, as thou hast said, [I am.]
MAT 27:12 But when he was accused by the chief priests and the elders, he made no reply.
MAT 27:13 Then Pilate said to him, Dost thou not hear what they testify against thee?
MAT 27:14 But he made no reply to any charge; so that the governor was greatly surprised.
MAT 27:15 Now at a festival it was customary for the governor to release to the people any one prisoner whom they desired.
MAT 27:16 And they had then a noted prisoner named Barabbas.
MAT 27:17 So when they were assembled, Pilate said to them, Whom do you desire me to release to you? Barabbas; or Jesus who is called Christ?
MAT 27:18 For he knew that out of envy they had delivered him up.
MAT 27:19 And while he was sitting on the tribunal, his wife had sent to him, saying, Have nothing to do with that righteous person; for I have this day suffered much in a dream on his account.
MAT 27:20 But the chief priests and the elders had prevailed on the people that they should demand Barabbas, and destroy Jesus.
MAT 27:21 So when the governor, addressing them, said, Which of the two do you desire me to release to you? They said, Barabbas.
MAT 27:22 Pilate saith to them, What then shall I do with Jesus who is called Christ? They all say to him, Let him be crucified.
MAT 27:23 Thereupon the governor said, Why, what evil hath he done? But they with more vehemence cried, Let him be crucified.
MAT 27:24 When Pilate saw that he could not in the least prevail, but that a tumult rather was rising, he took water and washed his hands before the multitude, saying, I am clear from the blood of this innocent person. Look ye to it.
MAT 27:25 Upon which all the people, answering, said, His blood be upon us and upon our children.
MAT 27:26 Then he released to them Barabbas, and having scourged Jesus, delivered him up to be crucified.
MAT 27:27 Then the soldiers of the governor took Jesus to the pretorium, and assembled about him the whole cohort.
MAT 27:28 And having stripped him, they threw around him a scarlet military robe:
MAT 27:29 and having platted a crown of thorns, they put it on his head, and a reed in his right hand; and falling on their knees before him, they mocked him, saying, Hail king of the Jews.
MAT 27:30 Then, having spit in his face, they took the reed and struck him on the head.
MAT 27:31 And when they had mocked him, they took off the robe, and put his own raiment on him, and led him out to be crucified.
MAT 27:32 And as they were going out, they met a man of Cyrene, named Simon, and compelled him to carry the cross.
MAT 27:33 And having come to a place called Golgotha, [the meaning of which is the place of a skull]
MAT 27:34 they gave him to drink vinegar mingled with a bitter drug, which, when he tasted, he would not drink.
MAT 27:35 Then, having crucified him, they parted his garments by lot, thus verifying what was spoken by the prophet, "They parted my garments among them; and for my vesture they cast lots."
MAT 27:36 And, sitting down, they guarded him there.
MAT 27:37 Now over his head they had placed this inscription, denoting the charge against him, This is Jesus the king of the Jews.
MAT 27:38 At the same time two robbers were crucified with him, one on his right hand, and the other on his left.
MAT 27:39 And they who passed by reviled him, shaking their heads,
MAT 27:40 and saying, Thou the demolisher of the temple and the rebuilder of it in three days, save thyself. If thou art the Son of God, come down from the cross.
MAT 27:41 In like manner also the chief priests, and the Scribes, and the elders, deriding him, said,
MAT 27:42 He saved others; cannot he save himself? If he be the king of Israel, let him now come down from the cross, and We will believe him.
MAT 27:43 He trusted in God; let him now deliver him, if he delighteth in him: for, he said, I am the Son of God.
MAT 27:44 Nay, even the robbers, who were crucified with him, upbraided him in the same manner.
MAT 27:45 Now from the sixth hour there was darkness over the whole land till the ninth hour:
MAT 27:46 And about the ninth hour Jesus cried, with a loud voice, saying, Eli, Eli, Lama, Sabachthani, that is, My God, my God, why hast thou forsaken me?
MAT 27:47 Where upon some of them who stood there, hearing this, said, He calleth Elias.
MAT 27:48 And immediately one of them ran, and having taken a spunge, soaked it with vinegar, and having fixed it to a reed, gave him to drink.
MAT 27:49 But the rest said, Forbear, let us see, whether Elias will come to save him.
MAT 27:50 And Jesus, having cried again with a loud voice, expired.
MAT 27:51 And lo! the veil of temple was rent in two from top to bottom; and the earth quaked and the rocks were rent
MAT 27:52 and the tombs were opened. And many bodies of saints, composed to rest, were awakened.
MAT 27:53 And, having come out of their tombs, after his resurrection, they went into the holy city and appeared to many.
MAT 27:54 When the centurion, and they who were with him guarding Jesus, observed the earthquake, and what had happened, they were greatly terrified, and said, This was certainly a son of a God.
MAT 27:55 Now many women were there, looking on at a distance, who had accompanied Jesus from Galilee to wait upon him.
MAT 27:56 Among whom were Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James and Joses, and the mother of the sons of Zebedee.
MAT 27:57 And in the evening there came a rich man of Arimathea, whose name was Joseph, and who himself was a disciple of Jesus.
MAT 27:58 This man having gone to Pilate had begged the body of Jesus; and Pilate had ordered the body to be given to him.
MAT 27:59 So Joseph, having taken the body, wrapped it up in a clean sindon
MAT 27:60 and laid it in his own new tomb, which he had hewn in the rock. And having rolled a great stone to the entrance of the tomb, he went away.
MAT 27:61 But Mary Magdalene and the other Mary continued sitting there over against the tomb.
MAT 27:62 At the close of the day succeeding the preparation, the chief priests and the Pharisees went in a body to Pilate,
MAT 27:63 and said, Sir, we have recollected that this impostor, when alive, said, After three days I shall be raised up.
MAT 27:64 Give orders therefore that the sepulchre be secured till the third day. Perhaps his disciples may come by night, and steal him away, and tell the people, he is risen from the dead. So this last imposture will be worse than the first.
MAT 27:65 Thereupon Pilate said to them, You have a guard. Go and secure it as you can.
MAT 27:66 So they went and secured the sepulchre, sealing the stone and posting the guard.
MAT 28:1 Now the sabbath being over, at the dawn of the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene and the other Mary went to see the sepulchre;
MAT 28:2 and behold there was a great earthquake. For an angel of the Lord, having descended from heaven, came and rolled away the stone from the entrance, and sat upon it.
MAT 28:3 His countenance was like lightning, and his raiment white as snow.
MAT 28:4 And for fear of him the guards trembled, and became as dead men.
MAT 28:5 And the angel accosting the women, said, Be not ye terrified. For I know that you are seeking Jesus who was crucified.
MAT 28:6 He is not here. For he is risen as he said. Come, see the place where the Lord lay.
MAT 28:7 Then go quickly and tell his disciples that he is risen from the dead. And lo he goeth before you to Galilee. There you shall see him. Behold, I have told you.
MAT 28:8 Accordingly, having come out quickly from the tomb, with fear and great joy they ran to tell his disciples.
MAT 28:9 And as they were going to tell his disciples, lo! Jesus met them and said, Peace be to you. Whereupon, they coming near, took hold of his feet and worshipped him.
MAT 28:10 Then Jesus saith to them, Be not afraid: go tell my brethren that they may go to Galilee; there they shall see me.
MAT 28:11 Now while they were going, behold some of the guard, having come to the city, told the chief priests all that had happened.
MAT 28:12 Whereupon they, with the elders, assembled and having held a council, they gave a large sum of money to the soldiers,
MAT 28:13 with this injunction, Say, His disciples came by night and stole him while we were asleep.
MAT 28:14 And if this come to the governor's ears, we will appease him, and secure you.
MAT 28:15 So they took the money, and did as they were taught. And this is the current report among the Jews even at this day.
MAT 28:16 Now the eleven disciples went to Galilee, to the mountain whither Jesus ordered them.
MAT 28:17 And some seeing him prostrated themselves before him, and some doubted.
MAT 28:18 Then Jesus came near and spoke to them, saying, All power in heaven and on earth is given to me.
MAT 28:19 Go therefore and make all the nations disciples, baptizing them to the Name of the Father and the Son and the Holy Spirit,
MAT 28:20 teaching them to observe all that I commanded you. And lo! I am with you all the days to the conclusion of this age. Amen.
MAR 1:1 The beginning of the Gospel of Jesus Christ the Son of God
MAR 1:2 As it is written in the prophets, "Behold I send my messenger before thy face, who shall prepare the way before thee."
MAR 1:3 "A voice of one crying in the wilderness, Prepare the way of the Lord; make the roads for him straight,"
MAR 1:4 John came baptizing in the wilderness, and proclaiming a baptism of reformation, for a remission of sins.
MAR 1:5 And all the country of Judea and the inhabitants of Jerusalem, went out to him, and were all baptized by him in the river Jordan, confessing their sins.
MAR 1:6 Now John's clothing was of camel's hair and he had a leathern girdle about his waist. And his food was locusts and wild honey.
MAR 1:7 And he proclaimed saying, There is one coming after me, who is mightier than I, the latchet of whose sandals I am not worthy to stoop down and untie.
MAR 1:8 I indeed have baptized you in water, but he will baptize you in a holy spirit.
MAR 1:9 And it came to pass in those days, that Jesus came from Nazareth of Galilee, and was baptized in the Jordan, by John,
MAR 1:10 who immediately upon his coming up from the water, saw the heavens parted asunder, and the Spirit like a dove descending upon him.
MAR 1:11 And there came a voice from the heavens, "Thou art my Son, the Beloved, in whom I am well pleased."
MAR 1:12 Presently after this the Spirit sendeth him forth into the wilderness,
MAR 1:13 and he was there in the wilderness forty days, tempted by Satan, and was with the wild beasts; and the angels ministered to him.
MAR 1:14 And after John's imprisonment, Jesus went to Galilee, proclaiming the glad tidings of the reign of God,
MAR 1:15 and saying, The time is accomplished, and the reign of God is at hand. Reform and confide in this good news.
MAR 1:16 And as he was walking along the sea of Galilee, he saw Simon, and Andrew his brother, casting a drag net, into the sea; for they were fishermen;
MAR 1:17 and Jesus said to them, Come with me and I will make you fishers of men.
MAR 1:18 Thereupon they straightway left their nets and followed him.
MAR 1:19 And going thence a little further, he saw James, the son of Zebedee, and John his brother, who were in the vessel, mending the nets.
MAR 1:20 And soon as he called them, they left their father Zebedee in the vessel, with the hired servants, and went after him.
MAR 1:21 And they come to Capernaum; and thenceforward on the sabbath days, he went to the synagogue and taught;
MAR 1:22 and they were astonished at his manner of teaching; for he taught as one having authority and not as the Scribes.
MAR 1:23 Now there was in their synagogue a man with an unclean spirit, and he cried aloud,
MAR 1:24 saying, Forbear! what hast thou to do with us, Jesus of Nazareth? Art thou come to destroy us? I know who thou art; the Holy One of God.
MAR 1:25 Thereupon Jesus rebuked him, saying, Be silent and go out of him.
MAR 1:26 And the unclean spirit, having convulsed the man, and screamed with a loud voice, went out of him.
MAR 1:27 At which all were so amazed, that they asked one another, saying, What is this? What new teaching is this? For with authority he commandeth even the unclean spirits, and they obey him.
MAR 1:28 And thenceforth his fame spread through all the region of Galilee.
MAR 1:29 Immediately on their going out of the synagogue they went to the house of Simon and Andrew, with James and John.
MAR 1:30 And as Simon's mother in law was confined to her bed with a fever, they forthwith spake to him about her;
MAR 1:31 whereupon he went to her, and taking hold of her hand, raised her up, and instantly the fever left her, and she waited on them.
MAR 1:32 And in the evening, when the sun was set, they brought to him all their sick, and those who were possessed by demons.
MAR 1:33 And the whole city was assembled at the door.
MAR 1:34 And he healed many who were sick of various diseases, and cast out many demons; and he permitted not the demons to say they knew him.
MAR 1:35 And in the morning, when the night was far advanced, he arose and went out, and retired to a solitary place, and there prayed;
MAR 1:36 and Simon, and they who were with him, went in quest of him,
MAR 1:37 and having found him they say to him, They are all seeking thee.
MAR 1:38 Whereupon he saith to them, Let us go to the neighbouring villages, that I may there also make proclamation, for I am come forth for that purpose.
MAR 1:39 Accordingly he proceeded, proclaiming the news in their synagogues, through all Galilee, and casting out demons.
MAR 1:40 And there cometh to him a leper, who on his knees intreated him, saying, If thou wilt, thou canst cleanse me.
MAR 1:41 And Jesus had compassion, and stretched forth his hand, and touched him, saying, I will: be thou cleansed.
MAR 1:42 And while he was speaking, the leprosy instantly left the man, and he was cleansed.
MAR 1:43 Then having restrained him, he sent him away immediately,
MAR 1:44 saying to him, See thou say nothing to any one; but go, shew thyself to the priest, and offer for thy purification what Moses hath commanded, for a testimony to them.
MAR 1:45 But when he went out he began to proclaim freely and publish the matter abroad, so that Jesus could no more go openly into a city, but continued without in solitary places, where people resorted to him from all quarters.
MAR 2:1 After some days he again entered Capernaum, and the report spread that he was in a house,
MAR 2:2 and such multitudes presently flocked thither, that even the courts before the door could not contain them. And while he was speaking the word to them,
MAR 2:3 some come to him bringing a paralytic, carried by four men.
MAR 2:4 And not being able to come near to him by reason of the crowd, they drew back the covering over the place where he was, and having opened a passage they lowered down the couch on which the paralytic lay.
MAR 2:5 Upon seeing their faith, Jesus saith to the paralytic, Son, thy sins are forgiven thee.
MAR 2:6 Now there were some of the Scribes sitting there, and they were reasoning in their minds
MAR 2:7 "What! Doth this man thus utter blasphemies! Who can forgive sins but God only."
MAR 2:8 Thereupon Jesus, perceiving immediately by his spirit that they are thus reasoning in themselves, said to them, Why do ye reason thus in your hearts?
MAR 2:9 Which is easier, To say to the paralytic, Thy sins are forgiven thee; or to say, Arise, take up thy couch, and walk?
MAR 2:10 But that you may know that the son of man hath power on the earth to forgive sins, [he saith to the paralytic]
MAR 2:11 I say to thee, Arise, take up thy couch, and go to thy house.
MAR 2:12 Thereupon he arose immediately; and having taken up the couch, went out in the presence of them all. So that they were all amazed, and glorified God, saying, We never saw any thing like this.
MAR 2:13 And he went out again to the sea side, and all the multitude came to him, and he taught them.
MAR 2:14 Now as he passed on he saw Levi, the son of Alpheus, sitting at the custom house, and saith to him, Follow me. Whereupon he arose and followed him.
MAR 2:15 And it came to pass that when Jesus was at table, in this man's house, many publicans and sinners were at table, with Jesus and his disciples; for many of them followed him.
MAR 2:16 When the Scribes and the Pharisees saw him eating with these publicans and sinners, they said to his disciples, What! Doth he eat and drink with these publicans and sinners!
MAR 2:17 This being in the hearing of Jesus, he saith to them, They who are in health have no need of a physician; but they who are sick. I did not come to call righteous men, but sinners, to a reformation.
MAR 2:18 Now it was customary for the disciples of John, and those of the Pharisees, to fast. Therefore they come and say to him, Why do the disciples of John, and those of the Pharisees, fast;19 but thy disciples do not fast?
MAR 2:19 Thereupon Jesus said to them, Can the bridemen fast, while the bridegroom is with them? So long as they have the bridegroom with them, they cannot fast.
MAR 2:20 But the days will come, when the bridegroom will be taken from them, and then they will fast in those days.
MAR 2:21 No one seweth a patch, of undressed cloth on an old garment, else the new patch teareth the old cloth, and the rent is made worse.
MAR 2:22 And no one putteth new wine into old leathern bottles; else the new wine bursteth the bottles. Thus the wine is spilled and the bottles are rendered useless. But new wine is to be put into new bottles.
MAR 2:23 At another time, as he was passing through corn fields, on the sabbath days, it happened that his disciples, as they passed along, began to pluck the ears.
MAR 2:24 Whereupon the Pharisees said to him, See! Why are they doing what is not lawful, on the sabbath days?"
MAR 2:25 And he said to them, Did you never read what David did when he was in a strait; and he and his company were hungry?
MAR 2:26 How he went to the house of God in the days of Abiathar, the high priest, and ate the presence loaves, which it is not lawful for any but the priests to eat, and gave thereof to his attendants?
MAR 2:27 Moreover he said to them, The sabbath was made for man, not man for the sabbath.
MAR 2:28 So that the son of man is lord even of the sabbath.
MAR 3:1 And when he again went to the synagogue, there was a man there who had a withered hand;
MAR 3:2 and they watched him to see whether he would heal on the sabbath, that they might accuse him.
MAR 3:3 Thereupon he saith to the man who had the withered hand. Stand up in the midst.
MAR 3:4 Then he saith to them. Is h lawful to do good on the sabbath days, or to do evil? To save life, or to kill? But they were silent.
MAR 3:5 Then looking round on them with indignation, being grieved for the blindness of their mind, he saith to the man, Stretch forth thy hand. Accordingly he stretched it out, and his hand was restored whole as the other.
MAR 3:6 Upon this the Pharisees went out, and immediately held a consultation with the Herodians against him, how they might destroy him.
MAR 3:7 Again 'Jesus withdrew with his disciples to the sea, and a great multitude followed him from Galilee, and from Judea,
MAR 3:8 and from Jerusalem, and from Idumea, and from the banks of the Jordan. They also around Tyre and Sidon, having heard what he did, flocked to him in crowds.
MAR 3:9 Then he gave orders to his disciples that a boat should attend him, because of the multitude, that they might not throng him.
MAR 3:10 For he healed many; so that they who had maladies, pressed in upon him to touch him.
MAR 3:11 And the unclean spirits; when they saw him, prostrated themselves before him, and cried out, saying, Thou art the Son of God;
MAR 3:12 though he strictly charged them not to make him known.
MAR 3:13 Then he goeth up to the mountain, and calleth to him whom he would, and they went up to him.
MAR 3:14 And he appointed twelve, that they might be with him, and that he might send them to make proclamation;
MAR 3:15 and to have power to cure diseases, and expel demons;
MAR 3:16 namely, Simon, whom he surnamed Peter,
MAR 3:17 and James, the son of Zebedee, and John, the brother of James, [these he surnamed Boanerges, that is, sons of thunder]
MAR 3:18 and Andrew, and Philip, and Bartholomew, and Matthew, and Thomas, and James the son of Alpheus, and Thaddeus, and Simon the Chananite,
MAR 3:19 and Judas Iscariot, who delivered him up. Upon their going into a house,
MAR 3:20 a crowd again assembled, so that they could not so much as eat bread.
MAR 3:21 And when they who were just from it, heard, and were going out to restrain it, [for some said, He is distracted,
MAR 3:22 and the Scribes who had come down from Jerusalem, said, He is possessed by Beelzebub, and by the prince of the demons he expelleth the demons;]
MAR 3:23 Jesus having called them to him, said to them in parables, How can Satan expel Satan?
MAR 3:24 If indeed a kingdom be divided against itself, that kingdom cannot stand;
MAR 3:25 and if a family be divided against itself, that family cannot subsist;
MAR 3:26 and if Satan is risen up against himself, and divided, he cannot subsist; but hath an end.
MAR 3:27 No one can enter the house of the strong, and plunder his goods, unless he first bind the strong one. Then indeed he may rifle his house.
MAR 3:28 Verily I say to you, All transgressions may be forgiven the sons of men, and what slanderous speeches soever they may utter,
MAR 3:29 but whoever shall utter slanders against the Holy Spirit, hath not forgiveness in this age, but is liable to everlasting punishment.
MAR 3:30 Because it was said he hath an unclean spirit,
MAR 3:31 therefore his brethren, and his mother come, and having stood without, sent for him,
MAR 3:32 as the multitude sat around him. And when they said to him, Behold thy mother and thy brethren are Who had just come in from the crowd at the gate, without, inquiring for thee,
MAR 3:33 he answered them, saying, Who is my mother? And who are my brethren?
MAR 3:34 Then looking round on them who sat about him, he saith, Behold my mother and my brethren!
MAR 3:35 For whosoever will do the will of God, the same is my brother, and sister, and mother.
MAR 4:1 And when he began to teach again by the sea side, so great a multitude gathered about him, that he went on board the small vessel, and sat at sea, and all the multitude were on the sea shore.
MAR 4:2 And he taught them many things in parables. and in his manner of teaching, said to them, Hearken!
MAR 4:3 Behold the sower went out to sow!
MAR 4:4 And it happened that as he was sowing, some fell on the highway, and the birds of the air came and devoured it.
MAR 4:5 And some fell on rocky ground, where it had not much depth of soil; and it sprang up immediately, because it had not depth of soil,
MAR 4:6 but when the sun was up, it was scorched, and, for want of root, withered away:
MAR 4:7 and some fell among thorns, and the thorns sprang up and choked it, so that it yielded no fruit:
MAR 4:8 and some fell on good ground, which sprang up and yielded fruit, growing and thriving and bringing forth, some thirty, and some sixty, and some an hundred fold.
MAR 4:9 Then he said to them, Whoever hath ears to hear, let him hear.
MAR 4:10 And when he was in private they who were about him. with the twelve, asked him the meaning of this parable.
MAR 4:11 Whereupon he said to them, To you it is granted to know the secrets of the reign of God; but to those without, all these things are delivered in parables,
MAR 4:12 so that seeing they see, though they may not perceive; and hearing they hear, though they may not understand. Perhaps they may turn, that their sins may be forgiven them.
MAR 4:13 Then he saith to them, Do ye not comprehend this parable? How then will you understand all the parables?
MAR 4:14 The sower soweth the word.
MAR 4:15 Now these are they by the way side, where the word is sown, who have no sooner heard, than Satan cometh, and taketh away the word which was sown in their hearts.
MAR 4:16 And in like manner the rocky ground denoteth those, who, when they hear the word, receive it immediately with joy;
MAR 4:17 but not having it rooted in them, they are but temporary; so that when tribulation, or persecution cometh because of the word, they are instantly stumbled.
MAR 4:18 And these are they sown among thorns, who hear the word,
MAR 4:19 but the cares of this world, and the delusion of riches, and inordinate desires of other things, crowd in and choke the word, so that it becometh unfruitful.
MAR 4:20 And these are they sown on good ground, who hear the word and receive it, and bring forth fruit, some, thirty; and some, sixty; and some, an hundred fold.
MAR 4:21 Then he said to them, Is a lamp brought to be put under the corn measure, or under the bed? Is it not that it may be set on a stand?
MAR 4:22 For there is nothing hidden which shall not be discovered, nor any thing laid up in secret, but that it may be brought to light.
MAR 4:23 If any one hath ears to hear, let him hear.
MAR 4:24 Moreover he said to them, Consider what you hear. With whatever measure you deal out, you shall receive; and to you who are attentive more shall be given.
MAR 4:25 For to him who improveth, more shall be given; but from him who improveth not, even what he hath shall be taken away.
MAR 4:26 Again he said, The reign of God is as when a man soweth seed on the ground.
MAR 4:27 Whether he sleepeth or waketh, night and day, the seed groweth and increaseth, he knoweth not how.
MAR 4:28 For the earth of itself produceth first a blade, then an ear, then full grains in the ear.
MAR 4:29 And when the grain is ripe, he forthwith applieth the sickle, because the harvest is come.
MAR 4:30 Again he said, To what may we compare the reign of God? Or by what similitude may we represent it?
MAR 4:31 It is like a grain of mustard seed, which, when it is sown in the ground, is one of the very smallest seeds there:
MAR 4:32 but, being sown, it springeth up and becometh larger than all plants of the pulse kind, and shooteth out large branches, so that under its shade the birds of the air can find shelter.
MAR 4:33 And with many such parables he spake the word to them as they were able to hear it:
MAR 4:34 but without a parable he did not speak to them. And in private he explained all to his disciples.
MAR 4:35 And the same day, in the evening, he saith to them. Let us cross over to the other side.
MAR 4:36 So, leaving the multitude, they take him along with them as he was on board. And there were some other small vessels with him.
MAR 4:37 And there arose a violent storm of wind, and the waves beat into the vessel, so that it would soon be full.
MAR 4:38 Now he was in the stem, asleep on a pillow. And they awake him, and say, Teacher, carest thou not that we perish?
MAR 4:39 Thereupon he arose and rebuked the wind, and said to the sea, Peace, be still. And the wind ceased, and there was a great calm.
MAR 4:40 Then he said to them, Why are you so much afraid. How is it that you have not faith?
MAR 4:41 And they were exceedingly terrified, and said one to another, Who in reality is this, that even the wind and the sea obey him?
MAR 5:1 And when they arrived at the other side, in the country of the Gaderenes,
MAR 5:2 just as he was stepping out of the vessel, there met him a man coming out from among the tombs, with an unclean spirit,
MAR 5:3 who made his abode in the tombs, and whom no one could confine; no, not even with chains.
MAR 5:4 For he had often been bound with fetters and chains; but he burst the chains and broke in pieces the fetters, so that none could tame him.
MAR 5:5 And he was continually, night and day, on the mountains and in the tombs, screaming, and cutting himself with stones.
MAR 5:6 But upon seeing Jesus at a distance, he ran, and prostrating himself,
MAR 5:7 cried with a loud voice, saying, What hast thou to do with me, Jesus, son of the most high God?" I conjure thee by God not to torment me?
MAR 5:8 For he had said to him, Go out of the man, thou unclean spirit.
MAR 5:9 Then he asked him, What is thy name? And he answered, saying, My name is Legion; for we are many,
MAR 5:10 and earnestly intreated him not to send them out of that country.
MAR 5:11 Now there was there on the mountains, a great herd of swine feeding,
MAR 5:12 and all the demons besought him, saying, Send us to the swine that we may enter into them.
MAR 5:13 And Jesus immediately permitted them. Whereupon the unclean spirits, having gone out, entered into the swine, and the herd rushed down a precipice into the sea, [now they were about two thousand] and were drowned in the sea.
MAR 5:14 And they who fed the swine fled, and told the news in town and country. And the people came out to see what had happened.
MAR 5:15 And when they came to Jesus and saw the demoniac; him who had the legion, sitting, and clothed, and in his right mind, they were terrified.
MAR 5:16 And when the eye witnesses told them what was done to the demoniac, and respecting the swine,
MAR 5:17 they began to intreat him to withdraw from their territories.
MAR 5:18 And as he was going on board the vessel the late demoniac besought him that he might go with him.
MAR 5:19 But Jesus did not permit him, but saith to him, Go home to thy friends, and tell them what the Lord hath done for thee, and hath had compassion on thee.
MAR 5:20 So he departed, and began to proclaim in Decapolis all that Jesus had done for him. And they were all amazed.
MAR 5:21 And when Jesus had repassed in the vessel to the other side, a great multitude gathered about him, and he continued by the sea side.
MAR 5:22 And behold there cometh to him one of the rulers of the synagogue, whose name was Jairus, who, upon seeing him, falleth at his feet
MAR 5:23 and intreateth him earnestly, saying, My little daughter is at the point of death, pray come and lay thy hands on her that she may be cured, and she will live.
MAR 5:24 So Jesus went with him, followed by a great multitude which pressed about him.
MAR 5:25 And a certain woman, who had been twelve years afflicted with an issue of blood,
MAR 5:26 and who had suffered much under many physicians, and spent all that she had, and instead of being any thing the better, rather grew worse,
MAR 5:27 having heard of Jesus, came behind him, in the crowd, and touched his mantle.
MAR 5:28 For she said, If I can but touch his clothes, I shall be cured.
MAR 5:29 And instantly the source of her disorder was dried up, and she felt in her body that she was cured of that disorder.
MAR 5:30 Thereupon Jesus conscious of the power which had gone forth from him, turning about immediately, in the crowd, said, Who touched my clothes?
MAR 5:31 Upon which his disciples said to him, Thou seest how the crowd throng thee, and dost thou say, Who touched me?
MAR 5:32 Still he looked round to see her who had done this,
MAR 5:33 when the woman, knowing what had been done for her, came trembling with fear, and prostrating herself before him, told him the whole truth.
MAR 5:34 Whereupon he said to her, Daughter, thy faith hath cured thee. Go in peace, and continue cured of that disorder of thine.
MAR 5:35 Now while he was speaking, messengers came from the ruler's house, who said, Thy daughter is dead, why troublest thou the teacher any further?
MAR 5:36 Upon hearing this message delivered, Jesus immediately saith to the ruler of the synagogue,57 Be not afraid. Only believe.
MAR 5:37 Then he permitted none to accompany him, but Peter and James, and John the brother of James.
MAR 5:38 And coming to the house of the ruler of the synagogue, and seeing a tumultuous crowd weeping and wailing immoderately,
MAR 5:39 he saith to them, as he was going in, Why make ye this ado, and weep? The child is not dead, but asleep.
MAR 5:40 Upon which they derided him. But he, having put them all out, taketh with him the father and mother of the child, and them who accompanied him, and goeth into the room where the child was laid.
MAR 5:41 And, taking hold of the child's hand, he saith to her, "Talitha cumi," the meaning of which is, damsel, I say to thee, Arise.
MAR 5:42 And immediately the damsel arose and walked about; for she was twelve years old. Upon which they were struck with great astonishment.
MAR 5:43 Then he strictly charged them that none should know this, and ordered something to be given her to eat.
MAR 6:1 Having left that place, he went to his own country, and his disciples accompany him,
MAR 6:2 and on the sabbath day he began to teach in the synagogue. And many who heard were astonished, and said, Whence hath this man these things? And, What wisdom is this which is given him, that such miracles are done by his hands?
MAR 6:3 Is not this the carpenter, the son of Mary, and the brother of James, and Joses, and Judas, and Simon? And are not his sisters here with us? So they were stumbled at him.
MAR 6:4 Upon which Jesus said to them, A prophet is not without honour, save in his own country, and among his kindred, and in his own family.
MAR 6:5 So he could not perform any miracle there, save that he laid his hands on a few sick persons and healed them.
MAR 6:6 And he expressed wonder at their unbelief. When he was going round the neighbouring villages, teaching,
MAR 6:7 he calleth to him the twelve, and began to send them forth, by two and two, and gave them power over the unclean spirits;
MAR 6:8 and ordered them to take nothing for the journey, but only a staff; no scrip, no bread, no money in their purse;
MAR 6:9 but to be shod with sandals; and not to put on two coats.
MAR 6:10 And he said to them, Wherever you enter a house, continue there till you leave that place.
MAR 6:11 And whosoever will not receive you, nor hearken to you, when you depart thence shake off the dirt which is under your feet, as a testimony against them. Verily I say to you, the condition of Sodom and Gomorra will be more tolerable in a day of vengeance, than the condition of that city.
MAR 6:12 So they went forth and proclaimed, that men should reform.
MAR 6:13 And they cast out many demons, and anointed with oil many who were sick, and healed them.
MAR 6:14 Now when king Herod heard of him, [for his name was become famous] he said, John the baptizer is risen from the dead, and therefore these miracles are performed by him.
MAR 6:15 Some said, It is Elias; and others said, It is a prophet, or a person like one of the prophets.
MAR 6:16 But when Herod heard of him, he said, This is John, whom I beheaded. He is risen from the dead.
MAR 6:17 For Herod had sent and apprehended John, and confined him in prison, on account of Herodias, his brother Philip's wife, whom he had married.
MAR 6:18 For John had said to Herod, It is not lawful for thee to have thy brother's wife.
MAR 6:19 Therefore Herodias was enraged at him, and wished to kill him, but could not;
MAR 6:20 for Herod revered John, knowing him to be a righteous and holy man; and he protected him, and did many things by his advice, and heard him with pleasure:
MAR 6:21 At length a favourable opportunity occurred. When Herod, on his birth day, made an entertainment for the great officers of his court and army, and the chiefs of Galilee,
MAR 6:22 and the daughter of this same Herodias came in and danced, and pleased Herod and his guests, the king said to the damsel, Ask of me what thou wilt, and I will give it thee:
MAR 6:23 nay, he swore to her, Whatever thou shalt ask of me, I will give, even to the half of my kingdom.
MAR 6:24 Upon this she went out and said to her mother, What shall I ask? And she said, The head of John the baptist.
MAR 6:25 So coming in immediately with all haste to the king, she made her request, saying, I desire thee to give me forthwith, in a basin, the head of John the baptist.
MAR 6:26 Though the king was much grieved, yet from a regard to his oaths, and his guests, he would not refuse her.
MAR 6:27 So the king immediately despatched a sentinel with orders to bring the head of the baptist. And he went and beheaded him in the prison,
MAR 6:28 and brought his head in a basin, and gave it to the damsel: and the damsel gave it to her mother.
MAR 6:29 And when his disciples heard this, they went and took up his body, and laid it in a sepulchre.
MAR 6:30 Now the apostles come together again to Jesus, and when they had given him a full account both of what they had done, and what they had taught,
MAR 6:31 he said to them, Come by yourselves privately, to a solitary place, and rest yourselves a little while. For there were so many coming and going that they had not leisure even to eat.
MAR 6:32 So they went away by themselves, in the vessel, to a solitary place.
MAR 6:33 And the multitudes saw them going, and many knew the place, and ran thither by land, in. crowds, from all the cities, and got there before them, and assembled to meet him.
MAR 6:34 When Jesus landed and saw a great multitude, he had compassion on them, because they were like sheep which have no shepherd; and he began to teach them many things.
MAR 6:35 And the day being now far spent, his disciples came to him and said, This is a desert place, and the day is now far spent,
MAR 6:36 Dismiss them, that they may go to the neighbouring farms and villages, and buy themselves bread, for they have nothing to eat.
MAR 6:37 And he in reply, said to them, Supply them ye yourselves. Thereupon they say to him, Must we go and buy bread to the amount of two hundred deniars for them to eat.
MAR 6:38 He saith to them, How many loaves have you? Go and see. And having examined, they say, Five, and two fishes.
MAR 6:39 Then he ordered them to make all the people place themselves as at table on the grass, in several companies.
MAR 6:40 Accordingly they arranged themselves in rows, by hundreds and by fifties.
MAR 6:41 Then he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and having looked up to heaven, he pronounced a blessing. Then he broke the loaves, and gave to his disciples to set before them, and distributed the two fishes among them all.
MAR 6:42 And when they had all eaten, and were satisfied,
MAR 6:43 there were carried away twelve panniers full of the fragments, and the remains of the fishes.
MAR 6:44 Now they who had eaten of the loaves were about five thousand men.
MAR 6:45 Immediately after this, he constrained his disciples to embark, and go before him to the other side, to Bethsaida; while he dismissed the people.
MAR 6:46 And when he had sent them away, he retired to the mountain to pray.
MAR 6:47 And in the course of the evening the vessel was in the midst of the sea, and he all alone on the land.
MAR 6:48 And he saw them toiling at the oar; for the  wind was contrary. And about the fourth watch of the night, he goeth to them, walking on the sea, and seemed inclined to pass them.
MAR 6:49 But they, seeing him walking on the sea, thought it was an apparition, and uttered a loud scream.
MAR 6:50 For they all saw him, and were terrified. Whereupon he immediately spoke to them, saying, Take courage: it is I; be not afraid;
MAR 6:51 and went on board to them. And the wind ceased. At which they were still more excessively astonished and expressed admiration.
MAR 6:52 For they had not come to a right understanding by the loaves. For their understanding was callous.
MAR 6:53 And having crossed over, they came to the region of Genesaret, and put into port.
MAR 6:54 And on their going out of the vessel the people knew him.
MAR 6:55 And, running through the whole country around, they began to bring the sick on beds, to every place where they heard he was.
MAR 6:56 And wherever he entered towns, or cities, or villages, they laid the sick in the streets, and begged that they might but touch the tuft of his mantle. And as many as touched were cured.
MAR 7:1 Then the Pharisees, and some of the Scribes who had come from Jerusalem,
MAR 7:2 resort to him in a body, and seeing some of his disciples eating bread with unclean, that is with unwashen hands, they found fault.
MAR 7:3 For the Pharisees, and all the Jews, holding the doctrine of the elders, do not eat with out washing the hands with the doubled fist:
MAR 7:4 and if they come from the market they do not eat without dipping them. And there are many other usages which they have adopted, such as the dipping of cups, and pots, and brass vessels, and couches.
MAR 7:5 Therefore the Pharisees and the Scribes ask him, Why do not thy disciples walk according to the doctrines of the elders, but eat bread with unwashen hands?
MAR 7:6 In reply to which he said to them, Well did Esaias prophesy concerning you, hypocrites; as it is written, "This people honour me with their lips, but their heart is far from me.
MAR 7:7 And in vain do they worship me, teaching doctrines, the commands of men.
MAR 7:8 For laying aside the commandment of God, you adhere to the doctrine of men; the dipping of cups, and drinking vessels, and many other things, of the like nature.
MAR 7:9 Indeed said he to them, You fairly annul the commandment of God to make room for this doctrine of yours.
MAR 7:10 For Moses said, "Honour thy father and thy mother; and, Let him who curseth father or mother be put to death."
MAR 7:11 But you say, "If a man say to his father, or to his mother, Let that be Corban, [that is to say dedicated,] by which thou mightest be benefitted by me;"
MAR 7:12 do not then permit him any more to do any thing for his father or his mother;"
MAR 7:13 thus annulling the word of God, by this doctrine of yours, which you have handed down. And thus you act in many other instances.
MAR 7:14 Then having called to him the whole multitude he said to them, Hearken to me, all of you, and understand.
MAR 7:15 There is nothing from without, which by entering into a man can defile him; but the things which proceed from within him, are those which defile a man.
MAR 7:16 If any one hath ears to hear, let him hear.
MAR 7:17 And when he withdrew from the multitude into a house, his disciples asked him concerning this parable.
MAR 7:18 Whereupon he saith to them, Are you also so void of understanding? Do you not perceive that nothing which entereth into a man from without can defile him;
MAR 7:19 because it doth not enter into the heart; but into the belly, and the of scouring of all meats passeth out into the sink?
MAR 7:20 But, said he, it is that which cometh out of a man, which defileth him.
MAR 7:21 For from within, out of the heart of man, proceed those evil surmises, adulteries, fornications, murders,
MAR 7:22 thefts, inordinate desires, malice, fraud, sensuality, envy, detraction, pride, foolishness.
MAR 7:23 All these are the evil things which come from within, and defile the man.
