MAR 7:24 Then he arose and went from that place to the confines of Tyre and Sidon. And having entered the house he desired that none should know. But he could not be concealed.
MAR 7:25 For a woman, whose little daughter had an unclean spirit, having heard of him, came and fell at his feet
MAR 7:26 [now the woman was a Greek, a native of Syrophoenicia] and intreated him to expel the demon out of her daughter.
MAR 7:27 But Jesus said to her, Let the children first be satisfied; for it is not seemly to take the children's bread and cast it to the dogs.
MAR 7:28 To which she, in reply, said to him, True, sir; but still the dogs under the table eat the children's crumbs.
MAR 7:29 Thereupon he said to her, For this saying, Go home. The demon is gone out of thy daughter.
MAR 7:30 So, going home, she found the demon was gone out, and her daughter lying on the bed.
MAR 7:31 Then, quitting the confines of Tyre and Sidon, he came again to the sea of Galilee, along the borders of Decapolis.
MAR 7:32 And they bring to him a man who was deaf, and had an impediment in his speech, and beseech him to lay his hands on him.
MAR 7:33 Whereupon he taketh him apart from the multitude, and put his fingers in his ears, and he spat, and touched his tongue;
MAR 7:34 Then, looking up to heaven, he sighed, and said, Ephphatha, that is, Be opened.
MAR 7:35 And immediately his ears were opened, and his tongue loosed, and he spake distinctly.
MAR 7:36 Though he commanded them not to tell any one, yet the more he enjoined them the more abundantly they proclaimed .his miracles.
MAR 7:37 And being struck with inexpressible amazement, said, He hath done all things well, he maketh the deaf hear, and the dumb speak.
MAR 8:1 In those days the multitude being very great, and having nothing to eat, Jesus called his disciples to him, and saith to them,
MAR 8:2 I have compassion on the multitude, because they have continued with me now three days and have nothing to eat;
MAR 8:3 and if I send them home fasting, they will faint by the way, for some of them have come from afar.
MAR 8:4 Thereupon his disciples answered, Whence can they be supplied with bread here in the wilderness?
MAR 8:5 And he asked them, How many loaves have you? And they said, Seven.
MAR 8:6 Then he ordered the multitude to place themselves on the ground. And having taken the seven loaves, and given thanks, he brake, and gave to his disciples to distribute, and they distributed to the multitude.
MAR 8:7 And they had a few small fishes. So, when he had pronounced a blessing, he ordered these also to be served up.
MAR 8:8 And when they had eaten, and were satisfied, the fragments which remained were carried off in seven baskets.
MAR 8:9 Now they who had eaten were about four thousand.0 And when he had dismissed them
MAR 8:10 he straightway embarked with his disciples, and went to the district of Dalmanutha.
MAR 8:11 And the Pharisees came out and began to dispute with him; and, in order to try him, desired of him a sign from heaven.
MAR 8:12 Whereupon with a deep sigh, he saith, "Why doth this generation demand a sign? Verily I say to you, There shall be no sign given to this generation."
MAR 8:13 So, leaving them, he embarked again, and went to the other side.
MAR 8:14 Now his disciples had forgotten to take in bread, and they had only one loaf with them in the vessel.
MAR 8:15 And he gave them a charge, saying, Take heed; beware of the leaven of the Pharisees and of the leaven of Herod.
MAR 8:16 Thereupon they reasoned among themselves, saying, It is because we have not bread.
MAR 8:17 Jesus, perceiving this, saith to them, Why do you imagine that it is because you have not bread? Are you yet so void of sense and understanding? Have you hearts still callous?
MAR 8:18 Having eyes do you not see? And having ears do you not hear? And have you no memory?
MAR 8:19 When I brake the five loaves for the five thousand, how many panniers full of fragments did you carry off? They say to him, Twelve.
MAR 8:20 And when I brake the seven loaves for the four thousand, how many baskets full of fragments did you carry off? They said, Seven.
MAR 8:21 Then he said to them, How is it that you do not understand?
MAR 8:22 Then he cometh to Bethsaida, and they bring a blind man to him, and intreat him to touch him.
MAR 8:23 Thereupon taking the blind man by the hand, he led him out of the village; and after spitting on his eyes, he laid his hands on him, and asked him if he seeth any thing?
MAR 8:24 And he looking up, said, I see the men like trees; walking about.
MAR 8:25 Then he laid his hands on his eyes again, and made him look up. And his sight was restored, and he saw them all clearly.
MAR 8:26 Then he sent him to his house, saying, Neither go to the village, nor tell any one in the village.
MAR 8:27 Then Jesus went forth, with his disciples, to the villages of Caesarea-philippi. And by the way he asked his disciples, saying, who do men say that I am?
MAR 8:28 And they answered, John the Baptist: but some say, Elias; and others say, One of the prophets.
MAR 8:29 Then he saith to them, And who do you say that I am? Peter answering, saith to him, Thou art the Christ.
MAR 8:30 Then he charged them to tell no one this concerning him,
MAR 8:31 and began to inform them that the son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, and chief priests, and scribes, and put to death, and after three days rise again.
MAR 8:32 And he spake this so plainly, that Peter, taking him aside, began to rebuke him.
MAR 8:33 Whereupon, turning about and looking on his disciples, he rebuked Peter, saying, Get thee behind me, Satan! For thou hast thy mind bent, not on the things of God, but on the things of men.
MAR 8:34 Then, having called to him the multitude, with his disciples, he said to them, Whosoever hath a mind to come under my guidance, let him deny himself, and take up his cross, and follow me.
MAR 8:35 For whosoever would save his life, shall lose it; but whoever shall lose his life for the sake of me, and the glad tidings, he shall save it.
MAR 8:36 For what will it profit a man, if he should gain the whole world, and forfeit his life?
MAR 8:37 Or what will not a man give as a ransom for his life?
MAR 8:38 For whoever shall be ashamed of me and of my words, in this adulterous and sinful generation, of him the son of man will be ashamed, when he cometh in the glory of his father, with his holy angels.
MAR 9:1 Then he said to them, Verily I say to you, There are some of those standing here, who shall not taste death till they see the reign of God come with power.
MAR 9:2 Six days after this, Jesus taketh Peter, and James, and John, and leadeth them up, privately by themselves, to a high mountain, and was transfigured in their presence.
MAR 9:3 And his raiment became glittering white like snow, to such a degree as no fuller on earth could whiten.
MAR 9:4 And there appeared to them Elias with Moses, who were conversing with Jesus.
MAR 9:5 Whereupon Peter, addressing Jesus, said, Rabbi, It is well that we are here. Let us make three booths, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias.
MAR 9:6 For he did not know what to say; for they were terrified.
MAR 9:7 Then there came a cloud which overshadowed them, and from the cloud came a voice, saying, This is my Son, the Beloved; hearken to him.
MAR 9:8 And instantly looking about, they saw no one anymore, but only Jesus with them.
MAR 9:9 And as they were coming down from the mountain, he strictly charged them not to tell anyone what they had seen, until the son of man is risen from the dead.
MAR 9:10 This expression they laid hold on, questioning among themselves what this rising from the dead could mean.
MAR 9:11 Then they asked him, saying, Why do the Scribes say that Elias must first come?
MAR 9:12 In reply to which, he said to them, Elias indeed having come first, finisheth and beginneth all anew, in a manner conformable to what is written of the son of man, that he may suffer many things, and be treated with contempt.
MAR 9:13 But I say to you, that Elias hath actually come; and they have done to him what they pleased, as it is written of him.
MAR 9:14 And as he was coming to his disciples, he saw a great crowd about them, and the Scribes disputing with them.
MAR 9:15 And all the people when they saw him, were instantly struck with awe, and ran to salute him.
MAR 9:16 Then he asked the Scribes, About what are you disputing with them?
MAR 9:17 And one of the multitude answering, said, O! Teacher, I brought to thee this my son, who hath a dumb spirit.
MAR 9:18 And whenever it seizeth him, it convulseth him; and he foameth, and grindeth his teeth, and is shrivelled up. I spoke indeed to thy disciples to cast it out, but they could not.
MAR 9:19 Thereupon Jesus, in reply to him, saith, O faithless generation! How long shall I be with you? How long am I to endure you! Bring him to me.
MAR 9:20 So he was brought to him. And soon as he saw Jesus, the spirit threw him into convulsions; and, falling on the ground, he rolled about and foamed.
MAR 9:21 And Jesus asked his father, How long since this befel him? And he said, From his childhood.
MAR 9:22 And oft times it hath cast him into fire, and into waters to destroy him. But if thou canst do anything, have compassion on us and help us.
MAR 9:23 Thereupon Jesus said to him, With regard to this canst thou believe? All things are possible for him who believeth.
MAR 9:24 Upon which the father of the child immediately cried out, and with tears said, I do believe: Help, O sir, my unbelief.
MAR 9:25 And when Jesus saw that the people were crowding upon him, he rebuked the unclean spirit, saying to it, Thou dumb and deaf spirit, I command thee; Go out of him; and enter no more into him;
MAR 9:26 and the demon having screamed, and severely convulsed him, went out. And he was like one dead. So that many said, He is dead.
MAR 9:27 But Jesus, taking him by the hand, raised him, and he stood up.
MAR 9:28 And when he went into a house, his disciples asked him privately, Why could not we cast it out?
MAR 9:29 And he said to them, This kind [of power*] can go forth by nothing but by prayer and fasting,
MAR 9:30 Having left that place, they travelled through Galilee, and he did not desire that any should know;
MAR 9:31 for he was teaching  his disciples. And he said to them, The son of man is about to be delivered up into the hands of men, and they will put him to death. And being put to death, he will rise again on the third day.
MAR 9:32 But they did not comprehend the meaning of this, and were afraid to ask him.
MAR 9:33 And when he came to Capernaum, and was in the house, he asked them. What was that, about which you were debating among yourselves on the road.
MAR 9:34 And they were silent. For on the road they had debated among themselves, Who should be greatest.
MAR 9:35 Then sitting down, he called the twelve, and saith to them, If any one desireth to be first, let him be last of all, and servant of all.
MAR 9:36 Then having taken a child, he placed it in the midst of them; and taking it in his arms, he said to them,
MAR 9:37 Whosoever shall receive one of such children on my account, receiveth me; and whoever shall receive me, receiveth him who sent me.
MAR 9:38 Then John addressed him, saying, Teacher, we saw one who doth not accompany us, casting out demons in thy name, and we forbade him, because he doth not accompany us.
MAR 9:39 Whereupon Jesus said, Forbid him not, for there is no one who will do a miracle in my name, and be readily able to speak evil of me.
MAR 9:40 For whoever is not against us is for us.
MAR 9:41 For whosoever shall give you a cup of water to drink on my account, because you belong to Christ, verily I say to you, He shall not lose his reward.
MAR 9:42 And whoever shall cause one of these little ones, who believe in me, to stumble, better were it for him, that a millstone were hanged about his neck, and he cast into the sea.
MAR 9:43 Therefore, if thy hand cause thee to fall, cut it off. It is better for thee to enter maimed into life, than having two hands, to go into hell, into the fire which is unextinguishable;
MAR 9:44 "Where their worm dieth not; and the fire is not extinguished!
MAR 9:45 And if thy foot cause thee to fall, cut it off, it b better for thee to enter lame into life, than, having two feet, to be cast into hell, into the fire which is unextinguishable;
MAR 9:46 where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not extinguished.
MAR 9:47 And if thine eye causeth thee to fall, pluck it out; it is better for thee to enter one eyed into the kingdom of God, than having two eyes, to be cast into the hell of that fire;
MAR 9:48 where their worm dieth not, and the fire is not extinguished.
MAR 9:49 For every one is to be salted for fire, as every sacrifice is to be salted with salt.
MAR 9:50 Salt is good; but if the salt become saltless, with what can you season it? Have salt in yourselves, and maintain peace with one another.
MAR 10:1 Having departed thence, he cometh to the borders of Judea, through the plain of the Jordan. And multitudes again resort to him, and he, as usual, again taught them.
MAR 10:2 And the Pharisees came, and with a view to try him, asked him, is it lawful for a man to put away his wife.
MAR 10:3 Whereupon he, in reply, said to them, What hath Moses commanded you?
MAR 10:4 And they said, Moses permitted to write a bill of divorce and to put away.
MAR 10:5 In answer to this, Jesus said to them, Because of your intractable disposition, Moses wrote this precept for you.
MAR 10:6 But from the beginning of the creation God made them a male and a female.
MAR 10:7 For this cause a man is to leave his father and mother and cleave to his wife.
MAR 10:8 And they two shall be one flesh. So that they are no longer two, but one flesh.
MAR 10:9 Therefore what God hath conjoined, let not man separate.
MAR 10:10 And when he was in the house, his disciples asked him again concerning this matter.
MAR 10:11 Whereupon he saith to them, Whosoever shall put away his wife, and marry another, committeth adultery against her.
MAR 10:12 And if a woman put away her husband, and marry another, she committeth adultery.
MAR 10:13 Then children were brought to him, that he might touch them; and his disciples rebuked those who brought them.
MAR 10:14 But Jesus, observing this, expressed displeasure, and said to them, Suffer the children to come to me, and do not hinder the; for of such is the kingdom of God.
MAR 10:15 Verily I say to you, Whosoever will not, like a child, receive the kingdom of God, he shall in no wise enter it.
MAR 10:16 Then, having taken them in his arms, he laid his hands on them, and blessed them.
MAR 10:17 And as he was setting out on his journey, one came running, and kneeling down before him, asked him, Good teacher, what shall I do that I may inherit an everlasting life?
MAR 10:18 Thereupon Jesus said to him, Why callest thou me good? There is none good but God only.
MAR 10:19 Thou knowest the commandments; thou shall not commit adultery, thou shalt not commit murder, thou shalt not steal, thou shalt not bear false testimony, thou shalt not defraud, honour thy father and thy mother.
MAR 10:20 He answering, said to him, Teacher, All these I have observed from my childhood.
MAR 10:21 Then Jesus, looking stedfastly on him, loved him, and said to him, One thing is wanting to thee. Go sell what thou hast, and give to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven. Then come, and having taken up the cross, follow me.
MAR 10:22 At this word, he was grieved and went away sorrowful, for he had great possessions.
MAR 10:23 Thereupon Jesus, looking round, saith to his disciples, How difficult it is for them who have riches to enter into the kingdom of God!
MAR 10:24 At these words of his, his disciples being astonished, Jesus, addressing them again, saith, Children, How difficult a thing it is for them who trust in riches to enter into the kingdom of God.
MAR 10:25 It is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
MAR 10:26 At this they were still more astonished, and said among themselves, Who then can be saved?
MAR 10:27 Whereupon Jesus, looking stedfastly on them, saith, With men it is impossible, but not with God. For with God all things are possible.
MAR 10:28 Upon this Peter took occasion to say to him, Behold we have forsaken all and followed thee.
MAR 10:29 In reply to this, Jesus said, Verily I say to you, There is none who hath left house, or brothers, or sisters, or father, or mother, or wife, or children, or fields, for the sake of me and the glad tidings,
MAR 10:30 who shall not now, even in the present time, receive an hundred fold compensation for houses, and brothers, and sisters, and mothers, and children, and fields, as well as for persecutions and in the age to come, everlasting life.
MAR 10:31 But many who are first, shall be last, and the last, first.
MAR 10:32 When they were on the way up to Jerusalem, and Jesus was walking before them, they were seized with a horror, and followed him with fear. Whereupon1 Jesus, again taking the twelve aside, took occasion to tell them what would soon befal him.
MAR 10:33 Behold, said he, we are going up to Jerusalem, and the son of man will be delivered up to the chief priests, and the Scribes; and they will condemn him to death, and deliver him up to the Gentiles,
MAR 10:34 who will insult him, and scourge him, and spit upon him, and put him to death; and on the third day he will rise again.
MAR 10:35 When James 'and John, the sons of Zebedee, accosted him, saying, Teacher, we desire that thou wouldst do for us what we are going to ask;
MAR 10:36 thereupon he said to them, What do you desire me to do for you?
MAR 10:37 And they said to him, Grant us, that one of us may sit on thy right hand, and the other on thy left, in thy glory.
MAR 10:38 Thereupon Jesus said to them, You do not know what you are asking. Can you drink the cup which I am about to drink, and be baptized with the baptism with which I am about to be baptized?
MAR 10:39 They said to him, we can. Then Jesus said to them, you shall indeed drink the cup which I am about to drink, and be baptized with the baptism, with which I am about to be baptized;
MAR 10:40 but to sit on my right hand and on my left, is not mine to give, except to those for whom his prepared.
MAR 10:41 Now the ten, when they heard this, began to express indignation in respect to James and John;
MAR 10:42 but Jesus, having called them to him, said to them, You know that the rulers of the nations exercise lordship over them; and their grandees exercise authority over them;
MAR 10:43 but it shall not be so among you. But whoever would be great among you, let him be your attendant:
MAR 10:44 and whoever of you would be first, let him be the servant of all.
MAR 10:45 For the son of man did not come to be waited on, but to serve; and to give his life as a ransom for many,
MAR 10:46 Then they proceeded on to Jericho, and as he was going out of Jericho, with his disciples and a great multitude, blind Bartimeus, son of Timeus, was sitting by the way side, begging.
MAR 10:47 And when he heard that it is Jesus, the Nazarene, he began to cry aloud, and say, Jesus, son of David, have pity on me.
MAR 10:48 And many rebuked him, that he should hold his peace; but he cried the louder, Son of David, have pity on me.
MAR 10:49 There upon Jesus, stopping, ordered him to be called. So they call the blind man, Saying to him, Take courage; arise; he calleth thee.
MAR 10:50 Upon which, throwing aside his mantle, he sprang up and came to Jesus.
MAR 10:51 And Jesus, addressing him, said, What dost thou desire me to do for thee? And the blind man said to him, Rabboni, that I may again receive sight:
MAR 10:52 Thereupon Jesus said to him, Go thy way. Thy faith hath cured thee. And instantly he recovered his sight, and followed Jesus in the way.
MAR 11:1 And when they approach Jerusalem, being come as far as Bethphage and Bethany, near the mount of olives, he sendeth two of his disciples,
MAR 11:2 and saith to them, Go to that village over against you, and just as you enter it, you will find a colt tied, on which no man ever rode. Loose it, and bring it.
MAR 11:3 And if any one say, Why do ye this? Say, The master hath need of it, and will quickly send it back hither.
MAR 11:4 So they went, and found the colt tied before the door, at a place where two ways met. And as they were loosing it,
MAR 11:5 some of the people standing there, said to them, What do you mean by untying the colt?
MAR 11:6 And they answered them as Jesus had ordered; upon which they let them go.
MAR 11:7 So they brought the colt to Jesus; and when they had laid their mantles thereon, he sat upon it.
MAR 11:8 And many spread their mantles on the way; 'and others cut sprigs from the trees, and strewed them in the way.
MAR 11:9 And they who went before, and they who followed, cried, saying, Hosanna! Blessed he who is coming in the name of the Lord!
MAR 11:10 Blessed the approaching reign of our father David! that coming in the name of the Lord, Hosanna, in the highest!
MAR 11:11 So Jesus entered Jerusalem, and into the temple, and when he had taken a survey of all, as it was now evening, he went out to Bethany with the twelve.
MAR 11:12 And on the morrow, as they were coming out from Bethany, he was hungry,
MAR 11:13 and seeing a fig tree at a distance, full of leaves, he went to see if he could find any fruit on it [for the time to gather figs was not come] but going to it he found nothing but leaves.
MAR 11:14 Thereupon Jesus said to it, Henceforth let no one ever eat fruit of thee. And his disciples heard.
MAR 11:15 Then they came to Jerusalem, and Jesus, having entered the temple, began with turning out them who were buying and selling in the temple. And he overturned the tables of the money changers, and the stalls of them who sold doves,
MAR 11:16 and suffered no one to carry a vessel through the temple.
MAR 11:17 And he taught, saying, Is it not written, "My house shall be called a house of prayer for all the nations;" but you have made it a den of robbers.
MAR 11:18 When the Scribes, and the chief priests heard this, they sought how to destroy him, for they were afraid of him, because all the people were astonished at his doctrine.
MAR 11:19 Now, when evening was come, he went out of the city.
MAR 11:20 And next morning, as they were passing by; they saw the fig tree dried up from the roots.
MAR 11:21 Whereupon Peter, recollecting, saith to him, Rabbi, Behold the fig tree which thou cursedst, is quite dried up.
MAR 11:22 In reply to which, Jesus saith to them, Have faith in God.
MAR 11:23 For verily I say to you, If one should say to that mountain, Be thou lifted up and cast into the sea; and have no doubt in his mind, but believe that what he saith cometh to pass; whatever he may command shall be done for him.
MAR 11:24 Therefore I say to you, What things soever you ask when you pray, believe that you will receive, and you shall have them.
MAR 11:25 But when you stand praying, if you have any ground of complaint against any one, forgive him; that your father who is in heaven may forgive you your trespasses.
MAR 11:26 For if you do not forgive, neither will your father, who is in heaven, forgive you your trespasses.
MAR 11:27 Then they come again to Jerusalem; and as he was walking in the temple, the chief priests, and the Scribes, and the elders, come to him,
MAR 11:28 and say to him, By what authority doest thou these things? And, Who hath given thee authority that thou shouldst do such things?
MAR 11:29 And Jesus, answering, said to them, I also will ask you one question. Answer me; and I will tell you by what authority I do these things.
MAR 11:30 Was the baptism of John from heaven or of men? Answer me.
MAR 11:31 Upon this they reasoned among themselves, saying, If we say, From heaven; he will say, Why then did you not believe him?
MAR 11:32 But if we say, From men; they feared the people; for all held John to be really a prophet.
MAR 11:33 So they in reply; say to Jesus, We cannot tell. There upon Jesus answering, saith to them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
MAR 12:1 Then he addressed them in parables, saying, A man planted a vineyard, and hedged it about, and dug a wine lake, and built a tower, and let it to tenants, and went to a distant country.
MAR 12:2 And at the vintage season he sent a servant to the tenants, that he might receive from them some of the fruit of the vineyard.
MAR 12:3 But they, having seized him, beat him, and sent him away empty.
MAR 12:4 Again he sent to them another servant; and him they attacked with stones, and wounded on the head, and sent back with disgrace.
MAR 12:5 Again he sent another, whom they killed; and many others, some of whom they beat, and some they killed.
MAR 12:6 Therefore, at last, having an only son, his beloved, he sent him also to them, saying, They will reverence mv son.
MAR 12:7 But the tenants said among themselves, This is the heir. Come; let us kill him; and the inheritance will be our own.
MAR 12:8 So having seized him, they killed him, and threw him out of the vineyard.
MAR 12:9 What therefore will the owner of the vineyard do? He will come and destroy these tenants, and give the vineyard to others.
MAR 12:10 Have you never read this portion of scripture, "The stone which the builders rejected, was the very one for the head of the corner.
MAR 12:11 This [salvation] was from the Lord, and is wonderful in our eyes."
MAR 12:12 Upon this they sought to lay hold of him, but were afraid of the people. For they knew that he had spoken the parable against them. So they left him and went away,
MAR 12:13 and send to him some of the Pharisees, and the Herodians, to entrap him with a speech.
MAR 12:14 And when they came, they say to him, Teacher, we know that thou art true, and carest for no man. For thou respectest not the person of men, but teachest the way of God with truth. Is it lawful to pay tribute to Caesar? Or is it not?
MAR 12:15 Should we give? Or should we not give? But he, knowing their hypocrisy, said to them, Why do ye try me? Bring me a deniar, that I may see it.
MAR 12:16 So they brought him one. Then he saith to them, Whose image and inscription is this? And they said, Caesar"s.
MAR 12:17 Then Jesus, answering, said to them, Render to Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and to God, the things which are God's. And they expressed admiration at him.
MAR 12:18 Then came to him the Sadducees, who say there is no revival of the dead. And they asked him, saying,
MAR 12:19 Teacher, Moses hath written for us, that if any one's brother die, and leave a wife without leaving children, his brother should take his wife and raise up a seed for his brother.
MAR 12:20 Now there were seven brothers, and the first took a wife, and died without leaving issue.
MAR 12:21 Then the second took her, and died, and he left no issue. And the same was the case with the third.
MAR 12:22 Indeed the seven married her, but left no issue. Last of all, the woman also died.
MAR 12:23 At the revival of the dead, therefore, when they rise again, whose wife will she be? for she hath been wife to the seven.
MAR 12:24 In reply to which, Jesus said to them, Are you not led into error because of your not knowing the scriptures, nor the power of God?
MAR 12:25 For when the dead rise again, they neither marry nor are given in marriage; but are as the angels in heaven.
MAR 12:26 Now with respect to the dead, that they are raised, have you not read in the book of Moses, how God spake in the bush to him, saying, "I am the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaak, and the God of Jacob.
MAR 12:27 He is not the God of the dead; but the God of the living. You are therefore led much astray.
MAR 12:28 Then one of the Scribes who had heard them disputing, and knew that he had answered them properly, coming up, asked him, Which is the chief commandment of all?
MAR 12:29 Whereupon Jesus answered, This is the chief of all the commandments: "Hear, O Israel, The Lord is our God:
MAR 12:30 the Lord is one: and thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thine understanding, and with all thy strength." This is the first commandment.
MAR 12:31 And the second, resembling it, is this, "Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself". There is no other commandment greater than these.
MAR 12:32 Upon this the Scribe said to him, right! Teacher! thou hast said truly that there is one God; and there is no other besides him:
MAR 12:33 and to love him with the whole heart, and with the whole understanding, and with the whole soul, and with the whole strength; and to love one's neighbour as himself, is more than all the burnt offerings and the sacrifices.
MAR 12:34 Whereupon Jesus observing that he had answered discreetly, said to him, Thou art not far from the kingdom of God. And, after that, no one ventured to ask him any questions.
MAR 12:35 Then Jesus, in the course of his teaching in the temple, said, How do the Scribes say, That the Christ is the son of David?
MAR 12:36 For David himself, by the Holy Spirit, said, "The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand until I make thine enemies thy footstool."
MAR 12:37 If David then calleth him Lord, how is he his son? As the great multitude heard him with pleasure,
MAR 12:38 he said to them in his manner of teaching, Beware of the Scribes, who are fond of walking in long robes, and of salutations in public places of resort,
MAR 12:39 and of the principal seats in the synagogues, and the uppermost places at entertainments
MAR 12:40 who devour the families of widows, and make long prayers for a disguise. Such shall receive greater condemnation.
MAR 12:41 As Jesus was sitting over against the treasury, he observed in what manner the multitude throw money into the treasury. And many being rich, threw in a great deal.
MAR 12:42 At length a poor widow came, and threw in two mites, which make a farthing.
MAR 12:43 Thereupon Jesus, having called his disciples to him, saith to them, Verily I say to you, This poor widow hath thrown in more than all those who have thrown into the treasury.
MAR 12:44 For they have all contributed out of their superfluous store; but she, out of what she wanted for herself, hath thrown in all that she had"her whole living.
MAR 13:1 And as he was going out of the temple, one of his disciples saith to him, Teacher, see! what huge stones and stately buildings!
MAR 13:2 Whereupon Jesus answering, saith to him, Thou seest these great buildings? There shall not be left one stone on another which shall not be demolished.
MAR 13:3 And as he was sitting on the mount of olives, over against the temple, Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, asked him privately,
MAR 13:4 Tell us, when will these things happen? And what will be the sign of the impending accomplishment of all these things.
MAR 13:5 Thereupon Jesus, in answer to them, took occasion to say, Take heed that none seduce you:
MAR 13:6 for many will come in my name, saying, I am he; and will seduce many.
MAR 13:7 Now when you shall hear of wars and rumours of wars, be not alarmed; for this must happen; but the end is not yet.
MAR 13:8 For nation will rise against nation; and kingdom against kingdom. And there will be earthquakes in divers places. And there will be famines and commotions. These are the beginnings of sorrows.
MAR 13:9 Now look to yourselves. For they will deliver you up to councils and synagogues. You will be scourged and brought before governors and kings, for my sake, to bear testimony to them.
MAR 13:10 For the glad tidings must be first proclaimed to all the nations.
MAR 13:11 But when they bring you to deliver you up, be not solicitous beforehand what to say; nor premeditate; but whatever shall be suggested to you on the occasion, speak that: for it is not you, who speak; but the Holy Spirit.
MAR 13:12 Now brother will deliver up brother to death: and a father, a son: and children will rise up against parents, and cause them to be put to death:
MAR 13:13 and you will be hated by all men on account of my name. But he who persevereth to the end shall be saved.
MAR 13:14 Now when you see the abomination of desolation, which was spoken of by the prophet Daniel, erected where it ought not [ Reader attend!] then let them who are in Judea flee to the mountains;
MAR 13:15 and let not him who is on the house top go down into the house, nor enter it to carry away any thing out of his house.
MAR 13:16 And let not him who is in the field turn back to take up his mantle.
MAR 13:17 But alas! for the women who are with child; and for them who give suck in those days.
MAR 13:18 Pray therefore that your flight may not be in winter.
MAR 13:19 For in those days there will be such distress as hath not happened from the beginning of the creation, which God created, till now; nor ever shall be.
MAR 13:20 And had not the Lord shortened those days, no flesh could escape. But for the sake of the chosen, whom he hath made choice of, he hath shortened those days.
MAR 13:21 Now, if at that time, anyone say to you, Lo! the Christ is here! or, Lo! he is there! believe it not.
MAR 13:22 For false Christs and false prophets will rise up and give out signs and wonders to seduce, if possible, even the chosen ones.
MAR 13:23 But be upon your guard. Lo! I have foretold you all things.
MAR 13:24 But in those days, after that distress, the sun will be darkened, and the moon will withhold her splendour,
MAR 13:25 and the stars of heaven will continue falling, and the powers which are in the heavens will be shaken.
MAR 13:26 And then they shall see the son of man coming in clouds with great power and glory.
MAR 13:27 And then he will send his messengers and gather his chosen ones from the four winds from the remotest part of the earth to the remotest part of heaven.
MAR 13:28 Now learn this parable from that fig tree: when its branch becometh tender and putteth forth leaves, you know that the summer is near.
MAR 13:29 So when you see these things happen, know that he is near, at the door.
MAR 13:30 Verily I say to you, This generation shall not pass away until all these things are accomplished.
MAR 13:31 The heaven and the earth will fail, but my words shall not fail.
MAR 13:32 But with respect to the day, and the season, that none knoweth; neither the angels who are in heaven, nor the son none but the father.
MAR 13:33 Look, watch and pray; for you do not know when the time is.
MAR 13:34 As when a man was going to travel, on leaving his family and assigning to his servants their charge, even to even' one his work, he commanded the porter to watch;
MAR 13:35 watch ye therefore; for you do not know when the master of the family cometh; whether in the evening, or at midnight, or at cockcrowing, or in the morning,
MAR 13:36 lest coming unexpectedly, he find you asleep.
MAR 13:37 Now what I say to you, I say to all, Watch.
MAR 14:1 Now after two days was the passover, and the festival of unleavened bread. And the chief priests, and the Scribes were contriving how they might seize him by surprise, and put him to death.
MAR 14:2 And they said, Not at the festival; lest there be a tumult among the people.
MAR 14:3 And he being at Bethany in the house of Simon the leper, while he was at table a woman came with an alabaster phial of balsam; of pure unadulterated spikenard, which is very costly, and shaking the phial, she poured out of it on his head.
MAR 14:4 At which some expressed indignation, saying, Why is this waste of the balsam?
MAR 14:5 For it might have been sold for more than three hundred deniars, and given to the poor. And as they were restraining her,
MAR 14:6 Jesus said, Let her alone. Why do ye trouble her? She hath done a good work for me.
MAR 14:7 For you have the poor always with you and can, when you please, do them good; but me you have not always.
MAR 14:8 She hath done what she could. She hath come beforehand to anoint my body for its embalment.
MAR 14:9 Verily I say to you, In whatever quarter of the world these glad tidings are proclaimed, what this woman hath done will be mentioned to her honour.
MAR 14:10 Upon this, Judas Iscariot, one of the twelve, went to the chief priests, in order to deliver him up to them.
MAR 14:11 And when they heard, they rejoiced exceedingly, and promised to give him money. So he sought a favourable opportunity to deliver him up.
MAR 14:12 And on the first day of the festival of unleavened bread, the day when the paschal lamb was to be killed, his disciples said to him, Where wouldst thou have us go and prepare for thine eating the paschal lamb.
MAR 14:13 Thereupon he despatched two of his disciples, saying to them, Go to the city, and you will meet a man carrying a pitcher of water; follow him.
MAR 14:14 And wherever he shall enter, say to the master of the house, The teacher saith, Where is the dining room in which I may eat the passover with my disciples?
MAR 14:15 And he will shew you a large upper room, ready furnished. Make preparation for us there.
MAR 14:16 So the disciples went, and came to the city, and found as he had told them, and prepared the passover.
MAR 14:17 And in the evening he cometh with the twelve.
MAR 14:18 And as they were at table, and eating, Jesus said, Verily I say to you, One of you, who is eating with me, is to deliver me up.
MAR 14:19 At this they began to be sorrowful, and to say severally; one, Am I? And another, Am I?
MAR 14:20 And he answering, said to them, It is one of the twelve who is dipping with me in the dish.
MAR 14:21 The son of man departeth indeed as it is written of him, but alas for that man.by whom the son of man is delivered up. Good were it for that man, if he had never been born.
MAR 14:22 And, as they were eating, Jesus having taken a loaf and pronounced a blessing, broke and gave to his disciples, and said, Take; eat; this is my body.
MAR 14:23 Then having taken the cup, and given thanks, he gave to them  and they all drank of it.
MAR 14:24 Then he said to them, This is my blood; that of the new covenant; that shed for many.
MAR 14:25 Verily I say to you, I will no more drink of the product of the vine, until the day when I shall drink it new in the kingdom of God.
MAR 14:26 And when they had sung a hymn, they went out to the mount of olives.
MAR 14:27 And Jesus saith to them, This night you will all be stumbled at me. For it is written, "will smite the shepherd and the sheep will be scattered."
MAR 14:28 But after I am risen, I will go before you to Galilee.
MAR 14:29 Hereupon Peter said to him, Though all should be stumbled, I will not.
MAR 14:30 Jesus saith to him, Verily I say to thee, This very night before a cock crow twice, thou wilt three times deny me.
MAR 14:31 But he with more vehemence said, Though I should die with thee, I will not deny thee. And all the rest said the same.
MAR 14:32 Then they come to a place called Gethsemane, and he saith to his disciples, Stay here, till I pray.
MAR 14:33 Then he taketh with him Peter, and James and John, and being seized with agonizing horror and distress of mind,
MAR 14:34 he saith to them, My soul is exceeding sorrowful even to death. Stay here and watch.
MAR 14:35 Then having advanced a little further, he prostrated himself on the ground, and prayed, that if it were possible this hour might pass from him.
MAR 14:36 And he said, Abba, father, all things are possible to thee. Take away this cup from me. Nevertheless not my will, but thine be done.
MAR 14:37 Then he cometh and findeth them asleep, and saith to Peter, Simon, art thou asleep? Couldst thou not watch one hour?
MAR 14:38 Watch and pray, that you may not come to a trial. The spirit is indeed willing; but the flesh is weak.
MAR 14:39 Then going away again, he prayed, using the same words.
MAR 14:40 And on returning, he found them again asleep. For their eyes were weighed down, and they did not know what to answer him.
MAR 14:41 Then he cometh the third time, and saith to them, Are you still asleep and taking rest? It is over. The hour is come. Behold the son of man is delivered into the hands of sinners.
MAR 14:42 Arise and let us go. Lo! he who delivereth me up is at hand.
MAR 14:43 And immediately, while he was still speaking, Judas, one of the twelve, cometh, and with him a great multitude, with swords and clubs, from the chief priests, and the scribes, and the elders.
MAR 14:44 Now he, who delivered him up, had given them a signal, saying, The person whom I will kiss, is he: seize him and carry him away securely.
MAR 14:45 So, when he came, having advanced directly up to Jesus, he saith, Rabbi, Rabbi, and kissed him.
MAR 14:46 Whereupon they laid their hands on him and held him.
MAR 14:47 Then one of them who stood by, having drawn his sword, smote the servant of the chief priest, and cut off his ear.
MAR 14:48 And Jesus addressing them, said, Are you come out as against a robber, with swords and clubs, to take me?
MAR 14:49 I was daily amongst you in the temple, teaching you, and you did not arrest me. But the scriptures must be fulfilled.
MAR 14:50 Then all forsook him, and fled.
MAR 14:51 But a certain youth followed him, having only a sindon wrapped about his naked body; and the young men laid hold on him.
MAR 14:52 Whereupon he let go the Sindon and fled from them naked.
MAR 14:53 And when they brought Jesus to the chief priest; all the chief priests, and the elders, and the Scribes, assembled with him.
MAR 14:54 Now Peter had followed him, at a distance, quite into the court of the chief priest, and sat there with the attendants, warming himself at the fire.
MAR 14:55 And the chief priests and the whole Sanhedrim sought for evidence against Jesus, to put him to death, but found it not.
MAR 14:56 For many bore false witness against him, but their testimonies did not agree.
MAR 14:57 Then there arose some who falsely testified against him, saying,
MAR 14:58 We heard him say, I will destroy this temple made with hands, and in three days build another not made with hands.
MAR 14:59 But neither in this did their testimony agree.
MAR 14:60 Then the chief priest, standing up in the midst, asked Jesus, saying, Answerest thou nothing? What sayest thou to what these testify against thee?
MAR 14:61 But Jesus was silent, and made no reply. Then the chief priest interrogated him, and saith to him, Art thou the Christ, the son of the Blessed?
MAR 14:62 Thereupon Jesus said, I am. And you shall see the son of man seated on the right hand of that power, and coming with the clouds of heaven.
MAR 14:63 Upon this, the chief priest rent his clothes, and said, What farther need have we of witnesses?"
MAR 14:64 You have heard this blasphemy. What think ye? And they all adjudged him to be liable to death.
MAR 14:65 Then some began to spit upon him, and to cover his face, and buffet him, and say to him, Prophesy: when the attendants smote him on the cheek with their open hands.
MAR 14:66 Now, Peter being in the court below, one of the maid servants of the chief priest cometh,
MAR 14:67 and seeing Peter warming himself, having viewed him narrowly, she saith, Thou also wast with Jesus, the Nazarene.
MAR 14:68 Whereupon he denied, saying, I do not know, nor do I understand what thou sayest. Then he went out into the portico, and a cock crowed.
MAR 14:69 And the girl, seeing him again, began to say to the bye standers, that man is one of them.
MAR 14:70 Hereupon he denied again. And a little while after, they who stood by, said to Peter, Thou art certainly one of them; for thou art a Galilean, and thy speech sheweth it.
MAR 14:71 Upon this, he began with imprecations and oaths to say, I do not know the man of whom you speak.
MAR 14:72 And a cock crowed a second time. Then Peter recollected what Jesus said to him, Before a cock crow twice, thou wilt three times deny me; and covering his head, he wept.
MAR 15:1 And early in the morning, the chief priests, with the elders, and the Scribes, even the whole Sanhedrim, having consulted together, bound Jesus, and led him away, and delivered him up to Pilate.
MAR 15:2 And Pilate asked him, Thou art the king of the Jews? And he in reply, said to him, It is as thou sayst.
MAR 15:3 Then the chief priests accused him of many things; but he made no answer.
MAR 15:4 Then Pilate asked him again, saying, Answerest thou nothing? Observe how many things they testify against thee.
MAR 15:5 But Jesus still made no reply, so that Pilate was astonished.
MAR 15:6 Now at every festival he released to them any one prisoner whom they desired.
MAR 15:7 And there was one Barabbas confined with his fellow insurgents, who in their insurrection had committed murder.
MAR 15:8 So when the people with a loud clamour, began to demand what was usually granted to them,
MAR 15:9 Pilate addressing them, said, Is it your pleasure that I release to you the king of the Jews?
MAR 15:10 For he knew that out of envy the chief priests had delivered him up.
MAR 15:11 But the chief priests instigated the populace to desire that he would rather release to them Barabbas.
MAR 15:12 And when Pilate addressing them again, said, What then do you wish me to do with him whom you call king of the Jews?
MAR 15:13 They again cried, Crucify him.
MAR 15:14 Then Pilate said to them, Why? What evil hath he done? But they cried more vehemently, Crucify him.
MAR 15:15 Thereupon Pilate willing to satisfy the populace, released Barabbas to them, and having scourged Jesus, delivered him up to be crucified.
MAR 15:16 Then the soldiers led him away to the court called the praetorium, and having assembled the whole cohort,
MAR 15:17 they arrayed him in purple, and platting a crown of thorns, they put it on his head,
MAR 15:18 and began with saluting him, "Hail, king of the Jews."
MAR 15:19 Then they smote him on the head with a reed, and spat upon him, and bowing their knees, made obeisance to him.
MAR 15:20 And when they had mocked him they stripped him of the purple, and put his own clothes on him, and led him out to crucify him.
MAR 15:21 And they compel one Simon, a Cyrenian, who was coming from the country, the father of Alexander and Rufus, to carry his cross.
MAR 15:22 So they bring him to Golgotha [the meaning of which is, The place of a scull]
MAR 15:23 and offered him myrrhed wine to drink. But he did not take it.
MAR 15:24 And when they had crucified him, they divided his garments into parcels, casting lots on them, to decide what each should take.
MAR 15:25 Now it was the third hour when they nailed him to the cross:
MAR 15:26 and the inscription of the charge against him, which was written over him, was, The king of the Jews.
MAR 15:27 And together with him they crucify two robbers, one on his right hand and the other on his left.
MAR 15:28 Thus was the scripture fulfilled which saith, "And he was numbered with transgressors."
MAR 15:29 And they who passed by kept reviling him, shaking their heads, and saying, Ah! thou destroyer of the temple; and rebuilder of it in three days,
MAR 15:30 save thyself, and come down from the cross.
MAR 15:31 And in like manner the chief priests, and the Scribes, jesting with one another, said, He saved others, Cannot he save himself?
MAR 15:32 Let this Christ, this king of Israel, now come down from the cross that we may see and believe. Even they who were crucified with him, reviled him.
MAR 15:33 But when the sixth hour was come, there was darkness over the whole land, until the ninth hour.
MAR 15:34 And at the ninth hour, Jesus cried with aloud voice, saying, "Eloi, Eloi, Lama sabachthani" which is, being interpreted, My God, my God, Why hast thou forsaken me?
MAR 15:35 Which, when some of the bystanders heard, they said, Hark! he is calling Elias.
MAR 15:36 Then one ran, and having filled a spunge with vinegar, and put it on a reed, offered him drink, saying, Let alone; let us see whether Elias cometh to take him down.
MAR 15:37 Then Jesus, having uttered a loud cry, expired.
MAR 15:38 Upon which the veil of the temple was rent in two, from top to bottom.
MAR 15:39 And when the centurion who stood opposite to him, saw that he cried thus, and expired, he said, This man was certainly a son of a God.
MAR 15:40 Now there were women looking on at a distance, among whom was Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of James the younger, and of Joses, and Salome;
MAR 15:41 [these had attended him when he was in Galilee, and ministered to him] and many others who had come up with him to Jerusalem.
MAR 15:42 And in the course of the evening, during preparation time [that is, the cessation from labour which is usual before the sabbath,]
MAR 15:43 came Joseph of Arimathea, an honourable senator, who himself also was expecting the reign of God; he had taken courage, and gone in to Pilate and begged the body of Jesus:
MAR 15:44 upon which Pilate expressed wonder if he could be dead, and calling for the centurion, asked him, If he had been dead any time.
MAR 15:45 And being informed by the centurion, he had granted the body to Joseph;
MAR 15:46 and he, having bought a sindon, and taken Jesus down, wrapped him in the sindon and laid him in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock, and rolled a stone on the door of the sepulchre.
MAR 15:47 Now Mary Magdalene, and Mary the mother of Joses, saw where he was laid.
MAR 16:1 So when the sabbath was over, Mary Magdalene and Mary the mother of James, and Salome, bought spices, that they might go and embalm him.
MAR 16:2 And very early in the morning of the first day of the week, they come to the sepulchre. When the sun was rising;
MAR 16:3 and just as they were saying to one another, Who will roll away the stone for us from the door of the sepulchre,
MAR 16:4 [for it was very large] upon looking up, they see that the stone hath been rolled away.
MAR 16:5 And going into the sepulchre, they saw a youth sitting on the right side, clothed with a white robe, and they were terrified.
MAR 16:6 Whereupon he said to them, Be not terrified. You are seeking Jesus, the Nazarene, who was crucified. He is risen. He is not here. Behold the place where they laid him.
MAR 16:7 But go, tell his disciples, Peter in particular, that he goeth before you to Galilee. There you shall see him, as he said to you.
MAR 16:8 Thereupon, having come out in haste, they ran from the sepulchre; but they were seized with such terror and consternation that they said nothing to any one, they were so frightened.
MAR 16:9 Now Jesus, having risen very early in the morning of the first day of the week, appeared first to Mary Magdalene, out of whom he had cast seven demons.
MAR 16:10 She went and told his attendants who were mourning and weeping;
MAR 16:11 but when they heard that he is alive, and was seen by her, they did not believe.
MAR 16:12 After that, he appeared in another form, to two of them as they were walking into the country.
MAR 16:13 Whereupon these came and told the rest; but they did not believe them.
MAR 16:14 At length he appeared to the eleven, when they were at table, and upbraided them for their incredulity and obstinacy, because they did not believe them who had seen him after his resurrection.
MAR 16:15 Then he said to them, Go to all the world, and proclaim the glad tidings to all mankind.
MAR 16:16 He who believeth, and is baptized, shall be saved; but he who disbelieveth shall be condemned.
MAR 16:17 Now these signs shall accompany them who believe; by my name they will expel demons; they will speak with new tongues:
MAR 16:18 they will take up serpents: though they drink deadly poison, it shall not hurt them: upon sick persons they will lay their hands, and they shall recover.
MAR 16:19 So after the Lord had spoken to them, he was taken up to heaven, and sat at the right hand of God;
MAR 16:20 and they went forth and proclaimed the tidings every where, the Lord co-operating with them, and confirming the word with those concomitant signs.
LUK 1:1 Whereas many have undertaken to compose a history of those things which have been accomplished among us,
LUK 1:2 as they who were from the beginning eye witnesses, and are ministers of the word, have delivered them to us;
LUK 1:3 it seemed good to me. also, when I had accurately traced every thing from the very first, immediately afterwards to write to thee, most excellent Theophilus,
LUK 1:4 that thou mayst know the certainty of those doctrines in which thou hast been instructed.
LUK 1:5 In the days of Herod, the king of Judea, there was a certain priest named Zacharias, of the course of Abia; and his wife, whose name was Elizabeth, was of the race of Aaron.
LUK 1:6 They were both righteous in the sight of God, walking in all the commandments and precepts of the Lord, without blame.
LUK 1:7 Now they had no child, as Elizabeth was barren. And they were both advanced in years.
LUK 1:8 And it came to pass that when he was performing the priest's office before God, in the order of his course,
LUK 1:9 it fell to his lot, according to the order of the priesthood, to go into the temple of the Lord, to burn incense,
LUK 1:10 while the whole multitude of the people were praying without, at the time of the  incense offering.
LUK 1:11 And an angel of the Lord appeared to him, standing on the right side of the altar of incense,
LUK 1:12 at the sight of whom Zacharias was greatly discomposed and terrified.
LUK 1:13 Whereupon the angel said to him, Fear not, Zacharias; for thy prayer is heard; and thy wife, Elizabeth, will bear thee a son, and thou shalt call his name John.
LUK 1:14 He will indeed be to thee matter of joy and exultation; and many will rejoice at his birth.
LUK 1:15 For he will be great in the sight of the Lord. He must not drink wine, nor any fermented liquor. With a holy spirit he will be filled, even from his mother's womb.
LUK 1:16 And he will turn many of the children of Israel to the Lord their God.
LUK 1:17 He will go before in his presence, with the spirit and power of Elias, to turn the hearts of fathers to their children, and prepare disobedient persons, by a deep sense of righteous things, to be for the Lord a well disposed people.
LUK 1:18 Thereupon Zacharias said to the angel, How can I know this? for I am an old man, and my wife is far advanced in years.
LUK 1:19 In reply to which, the angel said to him, I am Gabriel, who attend in the presence of God: and I am sent to speak to thee, and to tell thee these glad tidings.
LUK 1:20 Now, behold, thou shalt be dumb and unable to speak, until the day when these tidings shall be accomplished; because thou hast not believed my words, which shall be confirmed in their season.
LUK 1:21 Now the people were waiting for Zacharias, and wondered at his tarrying so long in the temple.
LUK 1:22 And when he came out, he could not speak to them. So they perceived that he had seen a vision in the temple: for he made signs to them and continued deaf and dumb.
LUK 1:23 And when the days of his ministration were accomplished, he departed to his own house.
LUK 1:24 And after these days, his wife Elizabeth conceived; and kept herself retired five months, saying,
LUK 1:25 The Lord hath dealt thus with me in the days in which he looked on me to take away my reproach among men.
LUK 1:26 Arid in the sixth month, God sent the angel Gabriel to a city of Galilee, named Nazareth,
LUK 1:27 to a virgin contracted to a man, whose name was Joseph, of the house of David. And the virgin's name was Mary.
LUK 1:28 And when the angel entered, he said to her, Hail, favourite of heaven! The Lord is with thee! Blessed thou among women!
LUK 1:29 Upon seeing him she was greatly discomposed at his speech, and revolved in her mind what sort of a salutation this might be.
LUK 1:30 Whereupon the angel said to her, Fear not, Mary. For thou hast found favour with God.
LUK 1:31 Now behold thou shall conceive, and bear a son, and shalt call his name Jesus.
LUK 1:32 He will be great and will be called the son of the Most High. And the Lord God will give him the throne of his father David.
LUK 1:33 And he will reign over the house of Jacob forever. And of his kingdom there shall be no end.
LUK 1:34 Then Mary said to the angel, How can this be, since I know  not man.
LUK 1:35 And the angel answering, said to her, A holy spirit will come upon thee, and the power of the Most High will overshadow thee, therefore the holy offspring will be called the son of God.
LUK 1:36 Now behold Elizabeth thy cousin, even she hath conceived a son in her old age. And this is the sixth month with her, who hath been called barren.
LUK 1:37 For with God nothing is impossible.
LUK 1:38 Thereupon Mary said, Behold the handmaid of the Lord. Be it to me according to thy word.
LUK 1:39 And the angel left her. And in those days Mary set out and travelled with speed to the hill country, to a city of Juda,
LUK 1:40 and went to the house of Zacharias and saluted Elizabeth.
LUK 1:41 And soon as Elizabeth heard the salutation of Mary, the infant leaped in her womb: and Elizabeth was filled with a holy spirit,
LUK 1:42 and with a loud acclamation said, Blessed thou among women! and blessed the fruit of thy womb.
LUK 1:43 How have I this honour, that the mother of my Lord should come to me!
LUK 1:44 For behold! soon as the sound of thy salutation reached mine ear, the babe within me leaped for joy.
LUK 1:45 Happy indeed is she who believed that there shall be an accomplishment of the things spoken to her from the Lord.
LUK 1:46 Then Mary said, My soul doth magnify the Lord:
LUK 1:47 and my spirit exulteth in God, my Saviour:
LUK 1:48 because he hath regarded the low condition of his handmaid. For behold! henceforth all generations will call me happy.
LUK 1:49 Because the Mighty One hath done great things for me; therefore hallowed be his name.
LUK 1:50 Indeed his mercy on them who fear him, extendeth to generations of generations.
LUK 1:51 With his arm he hath displayed strength. He hath scattered them who were elated with the imagination of their heart.
LUK 1:52 From thrones he hath hurled potentates, and exalted them of low degree.
LUK 1:53 He hath filled the hungry with good things; and sent away the rich empty.
LUK 1:54 He hath supported his servant Israel, remembering [as he spoke to our fathers] mercy
LUK 1:55 for Abraham and his seed forever.
LUK 1:56 And Mary abode with her about three months, and then returned home.
LUK 1:57 Now when the time for Elizabeth's delivery was come, she8 brought forth a son.
LUK 1:58 And her neighbours and her relations, hearing that the Lord had magnified his mercy to her, rejoiced with her.
LUK 1:59 And on the eighth day they came to circumcise the child, and called him Zacharias, after the name of his father.
LUK 1:60 But his mother interposing, said, No. He shall be called John.
LUK 1:61 And they said to her, There is none among thy kindred who is called by that name.
LUK 1:62 Then they made signs to his father to know what he would have him called.
LUK 1:63 And he, having demanded a table book, wrote, saying, His name is John. At which they were all surprised.
LUK 1:64 And his mouth was immediately opened, and his tongue loosed, and he spake, praising God.
LUK 1:65 And all in the neighbourhood were struck with awe. And the fame of all these things spread through the whole hill country of Judea.
LUK 1:66 And all who heard laid them up in their mind, saying, What will this child be? And the hand of the Lord was with him.
LUK 1:67 And Zacharias his father was filled with a holy spirit, and he prophesied, saying,
LUK 1:68 Blessed be the Lord, the God of Israel; because he hath visited and delivered his people.
LUK 1:69 He indeed hath raised up for us a horn of salvation in the house of his servant David
LUK 1:70 [as he spake by the mouth of his holy prophets of old]
LUK 1:71 a deliverance from our enemies, and out of the hand of all who hate us
LUK 1:72 in kindness to our fathers, and in remembrance of his holy covenant
LUK 1:73 [as he sware to our father Abraham]
LUK 1:74 that he would grant us, that we, being delivered out of the hands of our enemies, may serve him without fear,
LUK 1:75 in holiness and righteousness before him, all the days of our life.
LUK 1:76 Now as for thee, child, thou shalt be called a prophet of the Most High; for thou shall go before in the presence of the Lord, to prepare his ways;
LUK 1:77 to give his people a knowledge of salvation, by a remission of their sins,
LUK 1:78 through the tender mercy of our God, by which the Anatole [the day spring] from on high hath visited us
LUK 1:79 to give light to them who are sitting in darkness and the shadow of death, to guide our feet to the way of peace."
LUK 1:80 And the child grew, and became strong in spirit, and was in the deserts till the day of the manifestation of him to Israel.
LUK 2:1 Now it happened in those days, that an edict came forth from Caesar Augustus, that this whole inhabited land should be enrolled.
LUK 2:2 This was the first enrolment; it was made when Cyrenius was a governor of Syria;
LUK 2:3 and all went to be enrolled, every one to his own city,
LUK 2:4 and accordingly Joseph went up from Galilee, from the city of Nazareth to Judea, to the city of David, which is called Bethlehem, because he was of the house and patriarchal family of David,
LUK 2:5 to be enrolled with Mary his espoused wife, who was then great with child.
LUK 2:6 And while they were there, the time came that she should be delivered;
LUK 2:7 and she brought forth her son, the first born, and swathed him, and laid him in a manger; because there was no room for them in the house appropriate to lodging.
LUK 2:8 Now in that country there were shepherds in the open fields tending their flocks by turns, during the night watches.
LUK 2:9 And lo! an angel of the Lord stood by them; and a glory of  the Lord shone around them; at which they were greatly affrighted.
LUK 2:10 Whereupon the angel said to them, Be not afraid; for lo! I bring you glad tidings; matter of great joy, which it will be to all the people
LUK 2:11 That to you there is born this day in the city of David, a Saviour, who is Christ the Lord.
LUK 2:12 And this will be the sign for you. You will find a babe swathed, lying in the manger.
LUK 2:13 Then suddenly there was with the angel a multitude of the heavenly host, praising God, and saying,
LUK 2:14 Glory to God in the highest [heaven!] And on earth, peace! good will among men!
LUK 2:15 And as soon as the angels withdrew from them to heaven; the men; the shepherds said one to another, "come, let us go to Bethlehem and see this which is come to pass, which the Lord hath made known to us."
LUK 2:16 So they went with all speed, and found Mary and Joseph, and the babe that lay in the manger;
LUK 2:17 and, having seen, they divulged what had been told them concerning this child.
LUK 2:18 And all that heard were amazed at the things which were told them by the shepherds.

LUK 4:1 Now Jesus being full of a holy spirit, returned from the Jordan, and was led by the spirit into the wilderness;
LUK 4:2 and being forty days tempted by the devil, he ate nothing during those days. And when they were ended, he at length was hungry.
LUK 4:3 Whereupon the devil said to him, If thou art Son of God, command that stone to become a loaf of bread.
LUK 4:4 And Jesus answered him, saying, It is written, that man can live, not by bread only, but by whatever God appointeth.
LUK 4:5 Now the devil having taken him up to a high mountain, had shewed him all the kingdoms of the inhabited land, in a moment of time,

LUK 4:7 If thou therefore wilt worship me, all shall be thine.
LUK 4:8 Thereupon Jesus, answering him, said, Get thee behind me, Satan, for it is written, "Thou shalt worship the Lord thy God, and him only thou shalt serve."
LUK 4:9 He had also brought him to Jerusalem and placed him on the battlement of the temple, and said to him, If thou art the son of God, throw thyself down from this;
LUK 4:10 for it is written, that He will give his angels a charge concerning thee to preserve thee;
LUK 4:11 and that With their hands they will bear thee up, shouldst thou peradventure dash thy foot against a stone.
LUK 4:12 In reply to which, Jesus said to him, It is said," Thou shalt not try the Lord thy God."

LUK 4:30 But he, having passed through the midst of them, went away.

LUK 5:35 The days indeed will come when the bridegroom shall be taken from them, then will they fast in those days.

LUK 5:37 Neither doth any one put new wine into old leathern bottles: if any doth, the new wine will burst the bottles, and thus the wine will be spilled, and the bottles rendered useless.
LUK 5:38 But new wine must be put in new bottles, so both will be preserved.
