LUK 7:18 When John was informed by his disciples of all these things,
LUK 7:19 he called two of them and sent them to Jesus, saying, Thou art the one coming: may we expect another?
LUK 7:20 And when the men came to him, they said, John the baptist hath sent us to thee saying, Thou art the one coming: may we expect another?
LUK 7:21 Now at that very time he was curing many of diseases, and maladies, and evil spirits, and graciously bestowing sight to many who were blind.
LUK 7:22 And Jesus answering, said to them, Go and tell John what you have seen and heard; that the blind see; the lame walk; lepers are cleansed; deaf hear; dead are raised to life, and the poor have glad tidings proclaimed to them.
LUK 7:23 And happy is he who shall not be stumbled at me.
LUK 7:24 And when John's messengers were gone, he took occasion to say to the people respecting John, What went ye out to the wilderness to see? A reed shaken by the wind?
LUK 7:25 But what went ye out to see? A man clothed with soft raiment? Behold they who are splendidly dressed, and who live luxuriously, are to be found in royal palaces.
LUK 7:26 But what went ye out to see? A prophet? Yes, I tell you, and something more than a prophet.
LUK 7:27 This is he, of whom it is written, "Behold I send my messenger before thee, who shall prepare thy way for thee."
LUK 7:28 For I say to you, Among those who are born of women, there is not a greater prophet than John the baptist, but the least in the kingdom of God is a greater than he.
LUK 7:29 All the people indeed, even the publicans, when they heard, justified God by submitting to the baptism of John;
LUK 7:30 but the Pharisees and the teachers of the law made null, with regard to themselves, the counsel of God, by not submitting to be baptized by him;
LUK 7:31 therefore the Lord said, To what shall I compare the men of this generation, and to what are they like?
LUK 7:32 They are like children who sit in the market place and call to one another, and say, We have played on the pipe for you, and you have not danced: we have sung for you songs of woe, and you have not wept.
LUK 7:33 For John the baptist came neither eating bread nor drinking wine, and you say, He hath a demon.
LUK 7:34 The son of man came eating and drinking; and you say, Behold a gluttonous man and a wine bibber; a friend of publicans and sinners.
LUK 7:35 But wisdom is justified by all her children.
LUK 7:36 When one of the Pharisees asked him to eat with him, and he had gone to the Pharisee's house and placed himself at table,
LUK 7:37 behold a woman in the city who was a sinner, when she knew that he was at table in the Pharisee's house, took an alabaster bottle of myrrh,
LUK 7:38 and standing behind, at his feet, weeping, she first bathed his feet with her tears, and wiped them with the tresses of her hair. Then she kissed his feet and anointed them with the myrrh.
LUK 7:39 When the Pharisee who had invited him saw this, he said within himself, if this man were a prophet, he would know what sort of a woman this is, who toucheth him; that she is a sinner.
LUK 7:40 Thereupon Jesus addressing him, said; Simon, I have something to say to thee. And he saith, Teacher, say it.
LUK 7:41 A certain creditor had two debtors. The one owed him five hundred deniars; and the other fifty.
LUK 7:42 And as they had not wherewithal to pay, he forgave them both. Which of them, therefore, said he, will love him most?
LUK 7:43 To which Simon replied, He, I suppose, to whom he forgave most. Jesus said to him, Thou hast judged rightly.
LUK 7:44 Then turning towards the woman, he said to Simon, Thou seest this woman? I came to thy house: Thou gavest me no water for my feet; but she with her tears hath washed my feet, and wiped them with the hairs of her head:
LUK 7:45 Thou gavest me no kiss: but she, since I came in, hath not ceased kissing my feet.
LUK 7:46 My head thou didst not anoint with oil: but she hath anointed my feet with myrrh.
LUK 7:47 For what reason? I tell thee. Her sins which are many, are forgiven her; therefore her love is great. But he to whom little is forgiven, hath little love.
LUK 7:48 Then he said to her, Thy sins are forgiven.
LUK 7:49 Upon this, they who were at table with him began to say within themselves, Who is this that forgiveth sins?
LUK 7:50 Thereupon he said to the woman, Thy faith hath saved thee, Go in peace.
LUK 8:1 Immediately after this he travelled through cities and villages, publishing and proclaiming the glad tidings of the reign of God, accompanied by the twelve,
LUK 8:2 and by certain women who had been delivered from evil spirits and diseases, particularly Mary, called Magdalene, Out of whom had gone seven demons;
LUK 8:3 and Joanna the wife of Chusa, Herod's steward, and Susanna, and many others, who ministered to him out of their possessions.
LUK 8:4 And as a great multitude were coming together, and those in every city were flocking to him, he said  by way of parable,
LUK 8:5 The sower went out to sow his seed. And as he was sowing, some fell on the highway and was trampled under foot, and the birds of the air devoured it.
LUK 8:6 And some fell on rocky ground, and having sprung up, it withered for want of moisture.
LUK 8:7 And some fell among thorns, and the thorns springing up with it, choaked it.
LUK 8:8 And some fell on good ground, and sprang up and yielded increase an hundred fold. Having said this, he cried with a loud voice, Whosoever hath ears to hear, let him hear.
LUK 8:9 And when his disciples asked him, saying, What is the meaning of this parable,
LUK 8:10 he said, To you it is granted to know the mysteries of the kingdom of God, which to others are couched under parables, so that they see and do not see, and they hear and do not understand.
LUK 8:11 Now this is the meaning of the parable. The seed is the word of God.
LUK 8:12 By the highway, are meant those hearers out of whose hearts the devil coming, taketh away the word, that they may not believe and be saved.
LUK 8:13 By the rocky ground are meant those who, when they hear the word, receive it with joy; but not having it rooted in them, they are but temporary believers, and in time of trial apostatise.
LUK 8:14 The ground overrun with thorns denoteth them who hear, and who going away are choaked with cares and riches and the pleasurable enjoyments of life, so that they do not bring fruit to perfection.
LUK 8:15 But by the good ground are meant they, who with an honest and good heart, having heard the word, retain it, and perseveringly bring forth fruit.
LUK 8:16 Now no one having lighted a lamp covereth it with a vessel or putteth it under a couch; but setteth it on a stand that they who come in may see the light.
LUK 8:17 For there is nothing obscure which shall not be made clear; nor any thing concealed which shall not be made known and come to light.
LUK 8:18 Take heed therefore how you hear; for to him who improveth, more shall be given; but from him who improveth not, even what he thinketh he hath, will be taken away.
LUK 8:19 When his mother and his brethren came to him, and could not get near him by reason of the crowd,
LUK 8:20 and some informed him, saying, Thy mother and thy brethren are standing without, and desire to see thee;
LUK 8:21 he in reply, said to them, My mother and mv brethren are they who hear the word of God and do it.
LUK 8:22 One day Jesus having gone on board a vessel with his disciples, said to them, Let us cross over to the other side of the lake. So they set sail.
LUK 8:23 And as they were sailing he fell asleep; and a storm of wind came down on the lake, and they were filled, and in danger;
LUK 8:24 Whereupon they went near and awoke him, saying, Master, master, we are lost. Upon which he arose and rebuked the wind, and the raging of the water, and they were still; and there was a calm.
LUK 8:25 And he said, to them, Where is your faith? And they being terrified, expressed admiration, saying one to another, Who in reality is this, that he commandeth even the winds and the water, and they obey him!
LUK 8:26 And when they arrived at the country of the Gadarenes, which is over against Galilee;
LUK 8:27 just as he was landing he was met by a man of the city who had been long possessed by demons, and who wore no clothes, nor abode in any house, but in the tombs;
LUK 8:28 who upon seeing Jesus, screamed and fell down before him, and said with a loud voice, What hast thou to do with me, Jesus son of the Most High God. I beseech thee, torment me not.
LUK 8:29 For he had commanded the unclean spirit to go out of the man. For it had often seized him. And when he was bound with chains and fastened with fetters, bursting the bonds, he was driven by the demon into the wilderness.
LUK 8:30 Then Jesus asked him, saying, What is thy name? And he said, Legion. [For many demons had entered into him]
LUK 8:31 and entreated him that he would not command them to go into the abyss.
LUK 8:32 Now there was a herd of many swine there, feeding on the mountain, so they besought him to permit them to enter into the swine. And when he permitted them,
LUK 8:33 the demons quitting the man, entered into the swine, and the herd rushed down a precipice into the lake, and were drowned.
LUK 8:34 When the swine herds saw what had happened, they fled, and running away, spread the news through the city and the country
LUK 8:35 Upon which the people came out to see what was done. And when they came to Jesus and found the man, out of whom the demons were gone, sitting at the feet of Jesus, clothed and in his right senses, they were terrified.
LUK 8:36 And upon being informed by the spectators how the demoniac had been cured,
LUK 8:37 all the people of the neighbouring country of the Gadarenes entreated him to depart from them. Because they were struck with great terror, he therefore going on board the vessel, set out on his return.
LUK 8:38 Now the man, out of whom the demons had gone, begged to be with him. But Jesus dismissed him, saying,
LUK 8:39 Return to thy house, and tell what God hath done for thee. So he returned, and published through the whole city all that Jesus had done for him.
LUK 8:40 And when Jesus returned, the multitude welcomed him, for they were all waiting for him.
LUK 8:41 And behold there came a man named Jairus, who was a ruler of the synagogue, who prostrating himself at the feet of Jesus, besought him to go to his house;
LUK 8:42 because he had a daughter, an only child, about twelve years of age, and she was dying. And as he was going, the people crowded him;
LUK 8:43 and a woman, who had been twelve years afflicted with an issue of blood, and who had spent all her living on physicians, none of whom could cure her,
LUK 8:44 came behind and touched the tuft of his mantle; and instantly her issue of blood was staunched.
LUK 8:45 Thereupon Jesus said, Who touched me? And when all denied, Peter and they who were with him, said; Master, the crowds are thronging and pressing thee, and dost thou say, Who touched me?
LUK 8:46 But Jesus said, Some one hath touched me, for I perceived a power going forth from me.
LUK 8:47 And when the woman saw that she had not escaped notice, she came trembling, and prostrating herself before him, told him in the presence of all the people, for what cause she had touched him, and how she was cured instantly.
LUK 8:48 Whereupon he said to her, Daughter, take courage; thy faith hath cured thee. Go in peace.
LUK 8:49 And while he was yet speaking, there cometh one from the ruler of the synagogue's house, and saith to him, Thy daughter is dead. Trouble not the teacher.
LUK 8:50 Upon hearing this, Jesus, addressed him, saying, Be not afraid. Only believe; and she will recover.
LUK 8:51 And when he entered the house, he permitted none to go .in, but Peter and James and John, and the father and the mother of the child.
LUK 8:52 Now all were weeping and lamenting her. But he said, Weep not. She is not dead; but asleep.
LUK 8:53 Upon which they derided him, knowing that she was dead.
LUK 8:54 And when he had put them all out, and taken her by the hand, he called, saying, Maiden, arise.
LUK 8:55 Whereupon her breath returned, and she arose immediately. And he ordered some food to be given her.
LUK 8:56 And her parents were astonished. And he charged them to tell no one what was done.
LUK 9:1 When he, having called together the twelve disciples, gave them power and authority over all the demons, and to cure diseases;
LUK 9:2 and was sending them to proclaim the reign of God, and to heal the sick;
LUK 9:3 he said to them, Take nothing for the journey; neither staves, nor scrip, nor bread, nor money, nor two coats apiece.
LUK 9:4 And into whatever house you enter, abide there till you leave the place.
LUK 9:5 And wherever they will not receive you, when you are leaving that city, shake off the dust from your feet, for a testimony against them.
LUK 9:6 Accordingly, they departed and went through the villages, proclaiming the glad tidings, and performing cures every where.
LUK 9:7 When Herod, the tetrarch, heard of all that was done by him, he was perplexed; because it was said by some, that John was raised from the dead;
LUK 9:8 and by others, that Elias is plainly come; and by others, that one of the ancient prophets is risen up.
LUK 9:9 And Herod said, John I beheaded: but who is this of whom I hear such things? And he desired to see him.
LUK 9:10 Therefore, when the apostles returned, and told Jesus all that they had done, he took them apart, and withdrew to a solitary place, belonging to a city called Bethsaida.
LUK 9:11 And as the people knew it, they followed him, and he received them, and spoke to them concerning the kingdom of God, and healed them who had need of healing.
LUK 9:12 And when the day began to decline, the twelve came, and said to him, Dismiss the multitude, that they may go to the neighbouring towns and farms, for lodging and provisions; for we are here in a desert place.
LUK 9:13 But he said to them, Do you, yourselves, give them something to eat. Thereupon they said to him, We have not more than five loaves and two fishes. Must we then go and buy food for all this people?
LUK 9:14 For they were about five thousand men. Then he said to his disciples, Range them as at table, in companies, fifty in a company.
LUK 9:15 And they did so. And when they were all ranged,
LUK 9:16 he took the five loaves and the two fishes, and looking up to heaven, pronounced a blessing, and broke them and gave to the disciples to set before the multitude.
LUK 9:17 And when they had all eaten, and were satisfied, there was taken up a surplusage of fragments which filled twelve panniers.
LUK 9:18 After that, when he was praying in a retired place, his disciples were with him, and he asked them, saying, Who do the people say that I am?
LUK 9:19 And they in reply, said, John the Baptist; but others say, Elias; and others, that one of the ancient prophets is risen up.
LUK 9:20 Then he said to them, And who do you say that I am? In answer to this, Peter said, The Christ of God.
LUK 9:21 Thereupon he checked them, and ordered them to tell no one this;
LUK 9:22 adding, that the son of man must suffer many things, and be rejected by the elders, and chief priests, and Scribes, and be put to death, and raised on the third day.
LUK 9:23 Moreover he said to all, if any one desireth to come under my guidance, let him deny himself, and take up his cross daily, and follow me.
LUK 9:24 For whoever would save his life shall lose it. But whosoever shall lose his life for my sake, he shall save it.
LUK 9:25 For what advantage is it to a man to have gained the whole world and destroyed himself, or be punished with the loss of life.
LUK 9:26 For whoever shall be ashamed of me, or of my words, of him the son of man will be ashamed when he shall come in his own glory, and in that of the father, and the holy angels.
LUK 9:27 Now I tell you of a truth, there are some of those standing here, who shall not taste death until they see the reign of God.
LUK 9:28 About eight days after these discourses, he took Peter, and John, and James, and went up to the mountain to pray.
LUK 9:29 And while he was praying, the form of his countenance was changed, and his raiment was dazzling white.
LUK 9:30 And behold two men conversed with him. These were Moses and Elias,
LUK 9:31 who appeared in glory, and spoke of that departure of his which he was soon to accomplish at Jerusalem.
LUK 9:32 Now Peter, and they who were with him, had been overpowered with sleep; but awaking thoroughly, they saw his glory, and the two men who were standing with him.
LUK 9:33 And as they were withdrawing from him, Peter said to Jesus, Master, it is well that we are here. Let us make three booths, one for thee, and one for Moses, and one for Elias, not knowing what he said.
LUK 9:34 And while he was thus speaking, a cloud came and overshadowed them. And at entering the cloud, they were terrified.
LUK 9:35 And there came a voice from the cloud, saying, This is my son, the Beloved; hearken to him.
LUK 9:36 Now at the time of the voice, Jesus was alone. And they were silent and told no one in those days aught of what they had seen.
LUK 9:37 And on the following day, when they were coming down from the mountain, a great multitude met him.
LUK 9:38 And behold a man from the crowd cried out, saying, Teacher, I beseech thee, look upon my son; for he is mine only child.
LUK 9:39 And behold a spirit seizeth him, and instantly he screameth; and it convulseth him with foam, and hardly departeth from him, when it hath bruised him.
LUK 9:40 I indeed besought thy disciples to cast it out, but they could not.
LUK 9:41 In reply to this, Jesus said, O faithless and perverse generation, how long shall I be with you! how long shall I endure you!
LUK 9:42 Bring thy son hither. And as he was coming, the .demon dashed him on the ground and threw him into convulsions. But Jesus rebuked the unclean spirit, and cured the child, and delivered him to his father.
LUK 9:43 And all were astonished at the mighty power of God. And while they were expressing admiration at all that Jesus had done, he said to his disciples,
LUK 9:44 Give diligent attention to these words; for the son of man will soon be delivered up into the hands of men.
LUK 9:45 But they did not know the meaning of this. It was hid from them so that they did not understand it; and they were afraid to ask him the meaning of that expression.
LUK 9:46 Now a surmise had crept in among them, which of them should be greatest.
LUK 9:47 And as Jesus perceived the ill grounded reasoning of their heart, he took a child, and placed it by him,
LUK 9:48 and said to them, Whoever will receive this child for my name, receiveth me; and whoever receiveth me, receiveth him who sent me. For he who is least among you all, even he shall be great.
LUK 9:49 Then John addressing him, said, Master, we saw one casting out the demons in thy name, and we forbade him because he doth not follow [thee] with us.
LUK 9:50 Thereupon Jesus said to him, Forbid not; for he who is not against us is for us.
LUK 9:51 Now when the days of his being received up were about to be completed, he resolutely set his face to go to Jerusalem,
LUK 9:52 and sent messengers before him, who set out and came to a town of Samaritans to make preparation for him.
LUK 9:53 But they would not receive him, because they perceived that he was going to Jerusalem.
LUK 9:54 Upon seeing this, his disciples, James and John, said, Master, Is it thy pleasure that we command fire to come down from heaven and consume them, as Elias did?
LUK 9:55 Whereupon, turning about, he rebuked them, and said, You do not know what spirit you are of.
LUK 9:56 For the son of man did not come to destroy men's lives, but to save them. So they went to another village.
LUK 9:57 It happened also in the course of their travels, that on the way one said to him, Master, I will follow thee whithersoever thou goest.
LUK 9:58 Whereupon Jesus said to him, The foxes have holes, and the birds of the air have roosts; but the son of man hath not where to lay his head.
LUK 9:59 And to another he said, Follow me. And when he said, Master, suffer me first to go and bury my father;
LUK 9:60 Jesus said to him, Let the dead bury their own dead; but go thou, and proclaim the reign of God.
LUK 9:61 And when another said, Master I will follow thee; but let me first go and bid them farewell, who are at my house;
LUK 9:62 Jesus said to him, No man, who hath put his hand to the plough and looketh back, is fit for the kingdom of God.
LUK 10:1 After these things, the Lord appointed seventy others, and sent them, two and two; before him, to every city and village whither he himself was soon to go;
LUK 10:2 and he said to them, The harvest indeed is plentiful, but the labourers are few. Entreat therefore the Lord of the harvest to send forth labourers for his harvest.
LUK 10:3 Go ye. Behold I send you forth like lambs among wolves.
LUK 10:4 Carry neither purse, nor scrip, nor sandals. And salute no one by the way.
LUK 10:5 And into whatever house you enter, first say, Peace be to this house.
LUK 10:6 And if the son of peace be there, your peace will rest upon it; but if not, it will return to you. And
LUK 10:7 continue in the same family, eating and drinking such things as they have. For the labourer is worthy of his wages. Go not from one family to another.
LUK 10:8 And into whatever city you enter, when they entertain you eat such things as are set before you.
LUK 10:9 And heal the sick therein, and say to them, The reign of God is come near to you.
LUK 10:10 But whatever city you enter, when they do not receive you, go out into the streets thereof and say,
LUK 10:11 The very dust of this city of yours which cleaveth to us, we wipe off for you: nevertheless, know this, that the reign of God hath come nigh unto you.
LUK 10:12 Now I say to you, the condition of Sodom will be more tolerable on that day than the condition of that city.
LUK 10:13 Alas for thee, Chorazin! Alas for thee, Bethsaida! for if the miracles which have been performed in you, had been done in Tyre and Sidon, they would have repented long ago, sitting in sackcloth and ashes.
LUK 10:14 But it will be more tolerable for Tyre and Sidon at the judgment, than for you.
LUK 10:15 And thou, Capernaum, which art exalted to the skies, shall be thrust down to Hades.
LUK 10:16 He who hearkeneth to you, hearkeneth to me: and he who rejecteth you, rejecteth me; and he who rejecteth me, rejecteth him who sent me.
LUK 10:17 And when the seventy returned with joy, saying, Master, even the demons are subject to us through thy name;
LUK 10:18 he said to them, I beheld Satan falling like lightning from heaven:
LUK 10:19 behold I give you power to tread upon serpents and scorpions, and upon all the power of the enemy, and nothing shall in anywise hurt you.
LUK 10:20 Nevertheless, rejoice not at this, that spirits are subject to you; but rather rejoice that your names are enrolled in heaven.
LUK 10:21 At that same time Jesus rejoiced in spirit, and said, I thank thee, O Father, Lord of heaven and earth, that thou, having hid these things from the wise and learned, hast revealed them to babes; Yes, O father, that it thus seemed good in thy sight.
LUK 10:22 All things are delivered up to me by my Father; and none knoweth who the Son is, except the Father; nor who the Father is, except the Son, and he to whom the Son will please to reveal him.
LUK 10:23 Then turning to the disciples apart, he said, Happy the eyes, which see what you see!
LUK 10:24 for I say to you, that many prophets and kings have desired to see what you see, and have not seen them; and to hear what you hear, and have not heard them.
LUK 10:25 Then a certain teacher of the law stood up, and with a view to try him, said, Teacher, what must I do to inherit everlasting life?
LUK 10:26 Whereupon Jesus said to him, What is written in the law? How readest thou?
LUK 10:27 And he in reply, said, Thou shalt love the Lord thy God with all thy heart, and with all thy soul, and with all thy strength, even with thy whole mind; and thy neighbour as thyself.
LUK 10:28 Upon this Jesus said to him, Thou hast answered right. Do this and thou shall live.
LUK 10:29 But he, wishing to justify himself, said, And who is my neighbour?
LUK 10:30 In answer to which Jesus said, A certain man from Jerusalem was going down to Jericho, and fell among robbers, who having stripped him, and wounded him, went off, leaving him half dead.
LUK 10:31 And accidentally a certain priest went down that way, who saw him and passed on over against him.
LUK 10:32 And in like manner, a Levite coming to the place, when he came and saw him, passed him by.
LUK 10:33 But a certain Samaritan, who was on a journey, came where he was; and when he saw him, he had compassion
LUK 10:34 and went up to him, and bound up his wounds, pouring thereon oil and wine. Then having set him on his own beast, he brought him to an inn, and took care of him.
LUK 10:35 And the next morning, when he was departing, he took out two deniars, and gave them to the innkeeper, and said to him, Take care of this man: and whatever thou expendest more, I will pay thee when I return.
LUK 10:36 Now, which of these three, thinkest thou, was neighbour to him who fell among the robbers?
LUK 10:37 The expounder of the law said, He who did him the act of kindness. Thereupon Jesus said to him, Go thou, and do in like manner.
LUK 10:38 And as they were travelling, he came to a certain village, and a woman whose name was Martha, received him into her house.
LUK 10:39 Now she had a sister called Mary, who sat down at the feet of Jesus and heard his discourse.
LUK 10:40 But Martha was cumbered about dispensing amply for the entertainment. So coming in, she said, Master, Carest thou not that my sister hath left me to serve alone? Speak to her therefore that she may assist me.
LUK 10:41 In reply to which, Jesus saith to her, Martha, Martha, thou art anxious and troubling thyself about many things.
LUK 10:42 But there is one thing necessary. As for Mary, she hath chosen that good portion which shall not be taken from her.
LUK 11:1 It came to pass also when he was at a certain place, praying, that soon as he had done, one of his disciples said to him, Master, teach us to pray, as John taught his disciples.
LUK 11:2 Whereupon he said to them, When you pray, say, Our Father, who art in heaven; hallowed be thy name; thy reign come; thy will be done on earth, as it is in heaven;
LUK 11:3 give us day by day our daily bread,
LUK 11:4 and forgive us our sins, for we indeed do forgive every one who offendeth us: and bring us not into temptation; but deliver us from the evil one.
LUK 11:5 Then he said to them, Should any of you have a friend, and go to him at midnight, and say to him, Friend, lend me three loaves of bread;
LUK 11:6 for a friend of mine is come off his road to me, and I have nothing to set before him:
LUK 11:7 and he from within should say in reply, Do not trouble me now: the door is shut, and my children as well as I are in bed: I cannot rise and give thee:
LUK 11:8 I say to you, though he will not rise and give him on account of being his friend; yet on account of his importunity he will rise and give him what he wanteth.
LUK 11:9 Now I say to you, Ask, and you shall obtain: seek, and you shall find: knock, and the door will be opened to you.
LUK 11:10 For every one who asketh obtaineth: and he who seeketh, findeth: and to him who knocketh, the door will be opened.
LUK 11:11 What father among you would give his son a stone, when he asketh for bread? Or, if he asketh for a fish, would, instead of a fish, give him a serpent?
LUK 11:12 Or, if he asked for an egg, would give him a scorpion?
LUK 11:13 If you, then, bad as you are, know how to give good gifts to your children; how much more will your heavenly father give a holy spirit to them who ask him?
LUK 11:14 Again, when he was expelling a demon, which was dumb, and as soon as the demon went out the dumb man spoke, and the people expressed admiration,
LUK 11:15 but some of them said, By Beelzebub, the prince of the demons, he expelleth the demons;
LUK 11:16 and others, to try him, demanded of him a sign from heaven;
LUK 11:17 he, knowing their thoughts, said to them, Every kingdom divided against itself is brought to desolation, and house after house falleth.
LUK 11:18 Now if Satan be divided against himself, how can his kingdom subsist? Because you say that I expel the demons by Beelzebub;
LUK 11:19 therefore if I expel the demons by Beelzebub, by whom do your sons expel them? Let them therefore be your judges.
LUK 11:20 But if I, with the finger of God, expel the demons, then indeed the kingdom of God hath reached you.
LUK 11:21 While the strong one armed guardeth his court, his goods are safe.
LUK 11:22 But when one stronger than he attacketh and overcometh him, he taketh from him his armour on which he relied. Then he divideth his spoils.
LUK 11:23 He who is not with me is against me. And he who doth not gather with me scattered!
LUK 11:24 When the unclean spirit hath gone out of the man; it walketh about through dry places, seeking rest: and finding none, it saith, I will return to my house from which I came out.
LUK 11:25 And when it is come, it findeth the house swept and garnished.
LUK 11:26 Then it goeth and taketh along seven other spirits worse than itself; and they having entered in, dwell there. So the last state of that man is worse than the first,
LUK 11:27 As he was thus speaking, it happened that a woman among the crowd, raising her voice, said to him, Happy the womb which bore thee and the breasts which thou hast sucked!
LUK 11:28 Whereupon he said, Nay, rather happy they who hear the word of God and keep it.
LUK 11:29 Now the crowds being collected in a body, he took occasion to say, This is a wicked generation. It seeketh a sign; but to it no sign shall be given, save the sign of the prophet Jonas.
LUK 11:30 For as Jonas was a sign to the Ninevites, so will the son of man be to this generation.
LUK 11:31 The queen of the south will be raised up at the judgment with the men of this generation, and will condemn them; because she came from the extreme parts of the earth to hear the wisdom of Solomon, and behold something greater than Solomon is here.
LUK 11:32 The men of Nineve will stand up at the judgment with this generation, and will condemn it, because they repented at the proclamation of Jonas, and behold something greater than Jonas is here.
LUK 11:33 No one having lighted a lamp putteth it in a secret place, or under the corn measure, but on a stand, that they who come in may see the light.
LUK 11:34 The eye is the lamp of the body; therefore when the eye is clear, the whole body is enlightened; but when it is distempered, the whole body is dark.
LUK 11:35 See therefore that the light which is in thee be not darkness.
LUK 11:36 Is then thy whole body enlightened? To one who hath no part dark, the whole, being enlightened.
LUK 11:37 After he had spoken, a certain Pharisee invited him to dine with him, so he went and placed himself at table.
LUK 11:38 And when the Pharisee who saw this expressed surprise that he had not first washed before dinner,
LUK 11:39 the Lord said to him, Now as for you Pharisees, yon cleanse the outside of the cup and plate; but as to the inside, it is full of your rapacity and wickedness.
LUK 11:40 Unthinking men! Did not he who made the outside make the inside also?
LUK 11:41 But with respect to the things in it, give alms, and behold they are all clean to you.
LUK 11:42 But alas for you, Pharisees! because you pay tithe of mint, and rue, and of all kinds of pulse, and neglect justice and the love of God. These you ought to have practised, without, however, neglecting the other.
LUK 11:43 Alas for you, Pharisees! because you love the uppermost seats in the synagogues, and salutations in public places.
LUK 11:44 Alas for you, Scribes and Pharisees, hypocrites! because you are like concealed graves, over which men walk without perceiving them.
LUK 11:45 Upon this, one of the teachers of the law, interposing, saith to him, Teacher, by speaking thus dost thou reproach us also?
LUK 11:46 Thereupon he said, Alas for you also, ye teachers of the law, because you load men with heavy burdens hard to be borne, and will not yourselves touch these burdens with one of your fingers.
LUK 11:47 Alas for you; because you build the monuments of the prophets, and your fathers slew them.
LUK 11:48 You therefore bear testimony, and approve the works of your fathers. Because they slew them, you, therefore, build their monuments;
LUK 11:49 on this account indeed said the wisdom of God, I will send them prophets and apostles, some of whom they will kill, and others they will persecute,
LUK 11:50 that the blood of all the prophets, which hath been shed from the foundation of the world, may be required of this generation.
LUK 11:51 from the blood of Abel to the blood of Zacharias who was slain between the altar and the temple: Verily I say to you, it will be required of this very generation.
LUK 11:52 Alas for you, teachers of the law! because you have taken away the key of knowledge. You entered not in yourselves; and them who were entering you hindered.
LUK 11:53 Now while he was saying these things to them, the Scribes and the Pharisees took occasion to urge him vehemently, and provoke him to speak of many things,
LUK 11:54 laying snares for him, and seeking to catch something from his mouth, that they might accuse him;
LUK 12:1 by which myriads of the people being drawn together, so as to trample upon one another, he took occasion to say to his disciples, Above all, things beware of the leaven of the Pharisees, which is hypocrisy;
LUK 12:2 for there is nothing concealed which shall not be disclosed; nor any thing hid, which shall not be known.
LUK 12:3 Because what you have said in the dark, will be heard in the light; and what you have whispered in closets will be proclaimed on the house tops;
LUK 12:4 therefore I say to you, my friends; Be not afraid of them who kill the body, and after that can do no more:
LUK 12:5 but I will point out to you whom you should fear; Fear him, who after he hath killed, hath power to cast into hell. I repeat it to you, Fear him.
LUK 12:6 Are not five sparrows sold for two assars? Yet not one of them is forgotten before God.
LUK 12:7 Nay, the very hairs of your head are all numbered. Fear not therefore; you are of more value than many sparrows.
LUK 12:8 Now I say to you, Whosoever will acknowledge me before men, him the son of man will acknowledge before the angels of God:
LUK 12:9 but he who hath denied me before men shall be disowned before the angels of God.
LUK 12:10 And with respect to every one who shall speak a word against the son of man, it is to be forgiven him, but he who shall speak slanderously against the holy spirit shall not be forgiven.
LUK 12:11 Now when they bring you before their synagogues, and magistrates, and rulers, be not anxious how or what defence you shall make, or what you shall say:
LUK 12:12 for the holy spirit will teach you that very instant, what you ought to say.
LUK 12:13 When one in the crowd said to him, Teacher, order my brother to divide the inheritance with me;
LUK 12:14 thereupon he said. to him, Man, who made me a judge or a divider over you?
LUK 12:15 Then he said to them, Take heed and be upon your guard against covetousness. For in what affluence soever a man may be, his life doth not depend on his possessions.
LUK 12:16 Then he spoke a parable to them saying, There was a certain rich man, whose ground produced plenteously.
LUK 12:17 Whereupon he reasoned within himself, saying, What shall I do; for I have not room to store my crops.
LUK 12:18 Then he said, I will do this. I will pull down my store houses and build larger, and there lay up all my produce and my good things.
LUK 12:19 And I will say to my soul; Soul, thou hast many good things laid up in store for many years: take thine ease; eat; drink; and be joyful.
LUK 12:20 Whereupon God said to him; Fool, this very night this soul of thine will be demanded of thee. Whose then will those things be which thou hast provided?
LUK 12:21 Thus let every one [say] to himself who is heaping up treasure and is not rich for God.
LUK 12:22 Then he said to his disciples, For this cause I say to you, be not anxious about your life, what you shall eat; nor for your body, what you shall wear.
LUK 12:23 Life is a greater gift than food, and the body than raiment.
LUK 12:24 Observe those ravens! they neither sow nor reap; nor have they cellar or barn; yet God feedeth them. Of how much greater value are you than these birds?
LUK 12:25 Now which of you can, with all his solicitude, add a moment to his life?
LUK 12:26 If therefore, you cannot make the smallest addition to it, why are you anxious about the rest?
LUK 12:27 Observe those lilies how they grow! They neither toil nor spin; yet I say to you, Even Solomon in all his glory, was not arrayed like one of these.
LUK 12:28 Now if God doth thus clothe the herbage, which is in the field today, and tomorrow is cast into a furnace, how much more will he clothe you, O distrustful men?
LUK 12:29 As for you, therefore, be not inquisitive about what you shall eat, or what you shall drink, nor agitated with restless thoughts.
LUK 12:30 For about all these things the nations of the world are inquisitive: but your Father knoweth that you have need of all these things.
LUK 12:31 But seek the kingdom of God, and all these things will be superadded to you.
LUK 12:32 Fear not, little flock. Because it hath pleased your Father to give you that kingdom,
LUK 12:33 sell your possessions and give alms: provide for yourselves purses which do not wear out; a treasure in the heavens, which will never fail; where no thief approacheth, nor moth spoileth:
LUK 12:34 for where your treasure is, there will your heart be also.
LUK 12:35 Let your loins be girded, and your lamps burning;
LUK 12:36 and be like men who are waiting their master's return from a wedding; that when he cometh and knocketh, they may instantly open for him.
LUK 12:37 Happy those servants, whom the master, when he cometh, shall find watching. Verily I say to you, he will gird himself, and having placed them at table, will come and wait upon them.
LUK 12:38 And whether he come in the second watch, or come in the third watch, and find them in such a state, happy are those servants.
LUK 12:39 Now this you know, that if the master of a family knew at what hour a thief would come, he would watch, and not suffer him to break into his house.
LUK 12:40 Be ye therefore also prepared, because at the hour of which you are not aware, the Son of man cometh,
LUK 12:41 Then Peter said to him, Master, dost thou speak this parable to us, or to all in general?
LUK 12:42 Thereupon the Lord said, Who is indeed the faithful and prudent steward, whom his master shall have set over his family to dispense regularly the stated allowance of food?
LUK 12:43 Happy is that servant, whom his master, when he cometh, shall find thus employed.
LUK 12:44 Verily I say to you, he will appoint him overseer of all his estate.
LUK 12:45 But should that servant say in his heart, My master delayeth his coming, and begin to beat the men servants, and maid servants, and to eat and drink and carouse;
LUK 12:46 the master of that servant will come on a day when he doth not expect him, and in an hour he is not aware of, and will scourge him in the severest manner, and assign him his portion with the unfaithful.
LUK 12:47 Now that servant who knew his master's will, and did not keep himself ready, nor act agreeably to his will, shall be beaten with many stripes;
LUK 12:48 but he who did not know it, and did things deserving chastisement, shall be beaten with few. For to whom much is given, of him much will be required. And the more a man is entrusted with, the more will be demanded from him.
LUK 12:49 I came to put fire on the earth; and what would I but that it were now kindled!
LUK 12:50 I have also a baptism to be baptized with, and how am I straightened until it be accomplished.
LUK 12:51 Do you imagine that I am come to give peace on the earth? I tell you, No; but rather division.
LUK 12:52 For henceforth five in one house will be divided; three against two and two against three.
LUK 12:53 Father will be divided against son, and son against father; mother against daughter, and daughter against mother; mother in law against daughter in law, and daughter in law against mother in law.
LUK 12:54 Then addressing the multitudes, he said, When you see the cloud rising from the west, presently, say you, there is a shower coming. And so it happeneth.
LUK 12:55 And when the south wind bloweth, you say, It will be hot. And so it happeneth.
LUK 12:56 Hypocrites! you have knowledge to discern the face of the earth and the sky; how is it then that you do not discern this time?
LUK 12:57 And why do ye not, even for your own sakes, judge aright?
LUK 12:58 For when thou art going with thine adversary to a magistrate, endeavour to come to an agreement with him on the way, lest he bring thee before the judge; and the judge deliver thee up to the officer, and the officer commit thee to prison:
LUK 12:59 I tell thee thou canst not get out of that, till thou hast paid the last farthing.
LUK 13:1 Now there were some present who, on that occasion told him of the Galileans, whose blood Pilate had mingled with their sacrifices:
LUK 13:2 whereupon Jesus, in reply, said to them, Do you imagine that those Galileans were the greatest sinners in all Galilee, because they suffered these things?
LUK 13:3 I tell you, No. But, unless you reform, you shall all perish in like manner.
LUK 13:4 Or those eighteen men, upon whom the tower of Silo- am fell, and killed them, do you think that they were the greatest offenders of all the men who dwelt in Jerusalem?
LUK 13:5 I tell you, No; but unless you reform, you shall all perish in like manner.
LUK 13:6 Then he spake this parable. A certain man had a fig tree planted in his vineyard, and he went seeking fruit on it, but found none.
LUK 13:7 Whereupon he said to the vine dresser, Behold this is the third year that I have come, seeking fruit on this fig tree, without finding any. Cut it down. Why doth it cumber the ground?
LUK 13:8 To which he replied, Master, let it alone one year longer, until I dig about it and dung it.
LUK 13:9 Perhaps it may bear fruit: if not; then cut it down.
LUK 13:10 When he was teaching in one of the synagogues on the sabbath day,
LUK 13:11 behold there was a woman there, who for eighteen years had a spirit of infirmity, and was so bowed down that she could in no wise look up.
LUK 13:12 And when Jesus saw her he called her to him, and said to her, Woman, thou art loosed from this thine infirmity,
LUK 13:13 and laid his hands on her. And instantly she stood upright and glorified God.
LUK 13:14 Upon which the ruler of the synagogue, to express his indignation because Jesus cured on the sabbath day, addressed the people and said, There are six days on which work should be done: come therefore on those days and be cured, and not on the sabbath day.
LUK 13:15 Thereupon the Lord answered him, and said, Hypocrite! Doth not every one of you, on the sabbath day, loose his ox or his ass from the stall, and lead it to water?
LUK 13:16 And ought not this woman, a daughter of Abraham, whom Satan hath bound, lo! these eighteen years, to be loosed from this bond on the sabbath day?
LUK 13:17 And upon his saying this, all his opposers were ashamed, and the whole multitude expressed joy for all the glorious things which were done by him.
LUK 13:18 Then he said, To what is the kingdom of God like? and to what shall I compare it?
LUK 13:19 It is like a grain of mustard seed, which a man took and threw in his garden, and it grew and became a great tree, and the birds of the air lodged among its branches.
LUK 13:20 Again he said, To what shall I compare the reign of God?
LUK 13:21 It is like leaven, which a woman took and mixed up with three measures of meal till the whole was leavened.
LUK 13:22 When he was passing through cities and towns, teaching, and continuing his journey to Jerusalem,
LUK 13:23 and one said to him, Master, are there few who are saved? He said to them;
LUK 13:24 Strive with all your might to enter in through the narrow gate; for many, I assure you, will seek to enter, who will not be able.
LUK 13:25 When the master of the house is raised up, and shall have shut the door and you begin to stand without and knock at the door, saying, Lord, Lord, open to us, he will Answer and say to you, I do not know you, whence you are.
LUK 13:26 Then you will begin to say, We have eaten and drunk in thy presence, and thou hast taught in our streets.
LUK 13:27 But he will say, I tell you I do not know you whence you are. Depart from me all you workers of iniquity.
LUK 13:28 Weeping and gnashing of teeth will be there, when you shall see Abraham, and Isaak, and Jacob, and all the prophets, in the kingdom of God, and you yourselves cast out.
LUK 13:29 People indeed will come from the east and west, and from the north and south, and be entertained in the kingdom of God.
LUK 13:30 And behold there are last, who shall be first; and there are first, who shall be last.
LUK 13:31 On that same day, some Pharisees came and said to him, Get away and depart hence; for Herod intendeth to kill thee.
LUK 13:32 Whereupon he said to them, Go and tell that fox, Behold I cast out demons, and perform cures to day and to morrow, and on the third day I am perfected.
LUK 13:33 But I must continue my course to day and to morrow, and the day following; for it is not to be supposed that a prophet will be destroyed any where but in Jerusalem.
LUK 13:34 O Jerusalem! Jerusalem! thou that killest the prophets and stonest them who are sent to thee! How often would I have gathered thy children, as a hen doth her brood under her wings; and ye would not.
LUK 13:35 Behold your house is left for you a desolation. And verily I say to you, You shall not see me until the time come when you will say, Blessed he, who is coming in the name of the Lord!
LUK 14:1 It happened also on a sabbath day, when he went to eat at the house of one of the chiefs who were Pharisees, and they were watching him,
LUK 14:2 behold there was before him a man, who had a dropsy;
LUK 14:3 thereupon Jesus, addressing the teachers of the law, and the Pharisees, said, Is it lawful to heal on the sabbath day?
LUK 14:4 But they were silent. Then taking the man by the hand, he healed him. And having dismissed him,
LUK 14:5 he continued his discourse to them, and said, Who amongst you, if his ass or his ox fall into a pit, will not instantly pull it out on the sabbath day?
LUK 14:6 And to this they could not make reply.
LUK 14:7 Then observing how eager the guests were for the first places at table, he addressed them in a parable, and said,
LUK 14:8 When thou art invited by any one to a wedding, do not take the uppermost place, lest a person of greater distinction than thou be invited by him.
LUK 14:9 In which case he who invited thee and him will come and say to thee, Give place to this man. Then thou, with confusion, must take the lower place.
LUK 14:10 But when thou art invited, go and take the lowest place, that when he who invited thee cometh, he may say to thee, Friend, go up higher. Then thou wilt have honour in the sight of them who are at table with thee.
LUK 14:11 For whoever exalteth himself, shall be humbled, and he who humbleth. himself, shall be exalted.
LUK 14:12 Then he said to him who had invited him; When thou makest a dinner or a supper, invite not thy friends, nor thy brethren, nor thy relations, nor thy rich neighbours, lest they also invite thee in their turn, and a recompense be made thee.
LUK 14:13 But when thou makest an entertainment, invite the poor, the maimed, the lame and the blind,
LUK 14:14 and thou shall be happy. For as they are not of ability to requite thee, a requital will be made to thee at the resurrection of the righteous.
LUK 14:15 Upon hearing this, one of the guests said to him, Happy is he who eateth bread in the kingdom of God.
LUK 14:16 Whereupon he said to him, A certain man made a great supper, and invited many.
LUK 14:17 But when he sent out his servants at supper time, to say to them who were invited; Come, for all things are now ready;
LUK 14:18 they all, from one [motive] began to make excuses. The first said to him, I have bought a field, and I must go and see it. I pray thee make my excuse.
LUK 14:19 And another said, I have bought five yoke of oxen, and I am going to try them: I pray thee make my excuse.
LUK 14:20 And another said, I have married a wife, and therefore I cannot go.
LUK 14:21 So the servant came and told his master these things. And the master of the family, being incensed, said to his servant, Go out quickly to the streets and lanes of the city, and bring in hither the poor and the maimed, and the lame, and the blind.
LUK 14:22 And when the servant said, Master, I have done as thou didst command, and still there is room;
LUK 14:23 the master said to the servant, Go out to the highways and hedges, and press people to come that my house may be full.
LUK 14:24 For I say to you, None of the men who have been invited shall taste of my supper.
LUK 14:25 As great multitudes were travelling with him, he turned to them and said,
LUK 14:26 If any one cometh to me, and slighteth not his father, and mother, and wife, and children, and brothers, and sisters, nay, and even his own life, he cannot be my disciple.
LUK 14:27 And whosoever doth not take up his cross and follow me, he cannot be my disciple.
LUK 14:28 Which of you, intending to build a tower, doth not first sit down and calculate the cost, to know whether he hath sufficient to finish it?
LUK 14:29 Lest, having laid the foundation, and not being able to complete the work; he become the scoff of all who see it,
LUK 14:30 who will say, This man began to build, but was not able to finish.
LUK 14:31 Or, what king marching out to encounter another in battle, doth not first sit down and consult, whether he with ten thousand men, is able to meet him who is coming against him with twenty thousand?
LUK 14:32 And if not: doth he not, while the other is yet at a great distance, send an embassy, and sue for peace?
LUK 14:33 In like manner, therefore, let every one of you do. He who doth not give up all his possessions, cannot be my disciple.
LUK 14:34 Salt is good; but if the salt become insipid, with what can it be recovered?
LUK 14:35 It is neither fit for the land, nor the dunghill. It is thrown away. Whoever hath ears to hear, let him hear.
LUK 15:1 As the publicans and sinners were all continually resorting to him to hear him,

LUK 15:3 he then spake this parable to them, saying,
LUK 15:4 What man among you having a hundred sheep, doth not, upon losing one of them, leave the ninety nine in the wilderness and go in search of that which is lost until he find it?
LUK 15:5 And having found it, doth he not joyfully lay it on his shoulders;
LUK 15:6 and upon coming home call together his friends, and neighbours, saying to them, Rejoice with me, because I have found the sheep which was lost?
LUK 15:7 Thus, I assure you, there will be greater joy in heaven for one reforming sinner, than for ninety nine righteous persons who have no need of reformation.
LUK 15:8 Or what woman having ten drachmas doth not, if she lose one of them, light a lamp, and sweep the house, and search diligently until she find it?
LUK 15:9 And having found it, doth she not assemble her female friends and neighbours, saying, Rejoice with me, because I have found the drachma which was lost?
LUK 15:10 Thus, I assure you, there is joy in the presence of the angels of God for one reforming sinner.

LUK 15:15 So he went and connected himself with one of the citizens of that country who sent him to his farm to feed swine,

LUK 15:18 I will rise and go to my father, and say to him, Father, I have sinned against heaven and in thy sight,
LUK 15:19 and am no more worthy to be called thy son: make me as one of thy hired servants.

LUK 15:21 Whereupon the son said to him, Father, I have sinned against heaven and in thy sight, and am no more worthy to be called thy son.

LUK 15:32 But we ought to feast and rejoice because this thy brother was dead and is come to life. He was indeed lost and is now found.
LUK 16:1 Then he said to his disciples, There was a certain rich man who had a steward. And this steward was accused of having wasted his substance.
LUK 16:2 So having called him, he said to him, What is this that I hear of thee? Give an account of thy stewardship; for thou canst no longer be steward.
LUK 16:3 Thereupon the steward said within himself, What am I to do, since my lord taketh from me the stewardship; I am not able to dig: to beg I am ashamed.
LUK 16:4 I am resolved what to do, that when I am removed from the stewardship, I may be received into their houses.
LUK 16:5 So having sent severally for every of his lord's tenants, he said to the first, How much art thou to pay to my lord?
LUK 16:6 And he said, A hundred baths of oil. Thereupon he said to him, Take thy lease, and sit down quickly, and write Fifty.
LUK 16:7 Then he said to another, And how much art thou to pay? And he said, a hundred cores of wheat. Whereupon he saith to him, Take thy lease and write eighty.
LUK 16:8 And the master commended the unjust steward, because he had acted prudently. Because the children of this world are more prudent for their generation, than the children of the light, are for theirs;
LUK 16:9 therefore I say to you, From the worldly prudence of this unrighteousness, make ye friends for yourselves, that when you fail, ye may be received into the everlasting abodes.
LUK 16:10 He who is faithful in very little, is faithful also in much; and he who is unjust in very little, is unjust also in much.
LUK 16:11 If you then were not faithful with this unjust worldly prudence who will entrust to you the true?
LUK 16:12 And if you were not faithful with that which is another's, will any one give you that to be your own?
LUK 16:13 No servant can serve two masters; for he will either hate one, and love the other; or he will attach himself to one, and despise the other: you cannot serve God and worldly prudence.

LUK 16:17 But sooner shall the heaven and the earth perish, than one tittle of the law fail.

LUK 16:20 And there was a certain poor man, named Lazarus, who was laid at his gate, full of sores,
LUK 16:21 desirous indeed to be fed with the crumbs which fell from his table: and moreover the dogs came and licked his sores.
LUK 16:22 At length this poor man died, and was carried by angels to Abraham's bosom. And the rich man died also, and was buried.
LUK 16:23 And in the mansion of the dead having lifted up his eyes, being in torment, he seeth Abraham far off and Lazarus in his bosom.
LUK 16:24 Whereupon he cried and said, Father, Abraham, have pity on me and send Lazarus, that he may dip the tip of his finger in water and cool my tongue; for I am tormented in this flame.
LUK 16:25 And Abraham said, Son, remember that thou receivedst thy good things in thy life time; and Lazarus in like manner, his evil things. But now he is comforted, and thou art tormented.
LUK 16:26 But besides all this, there is betwixt us and you, a huge gulf fixed; so that they, who would go hence to you, cannot. Neither can they who are there, cross over to us.
LUK 16:27 Then he said, I intreat thee therefore, Father, to send him to my father's house;
LUK 16:28 for I have five brothers, that he may testify to them, that they also may not come to this place of torment.

LUK 17:1 Then he said to his disciples, It is not to be supposed that offences will not come; but alas for him, by whom they come.
LUK 17:2 It would be better for him to have a millstone hanged about his neck and to be thrown into the sea, than to cause one of these little ones to stumble.
LUK 17:3 Take heed to yourselves. And if thy brother trespass against thee, rebuke him: and if he repent, forgive him.
LUK 17:4 And if he trespass against thee seven times a day, and seven times a day return to thee, saying, I repent; thou shall forgive him.
LUK 17:5 Upon this the disciples said to the Lord, Increase our faith.
LUK 17:6 Whereupon the Lord said to them, If you had faith like a grain of mustard seed, you might say to that sycamine tree, Be thou rooted up and planted in the sea. And it would obey you.
LUK 17:7 Now would any of you, having a servant ploughing, or feeding cattle, say to him immediately on his coming from the field, Come in and sit down to table:
LUK 17:8 would he not rather say to him, Get ready my supper, and gird thyself and wait upon me, until I have done eating and drinking; and afterwards thou mayst eat and drink?
LUK 17:9 Doth he think himself obliged to that servant for obeying his orders? I think not.
LUK 17:10 So when you have done all that you are commanded to do, say, We are servants who have conferred no favour; for we have only done what we were bound to do.

LUK 17:14 And upon seeing them, he said to them, Go and show yourselves to the priests. And it came to pass that as they were going they were cleansed.
LUK 17:15 Whereupon one of them perceiving that he was healed, returned glorifying God with a loud voice;
LUK 17:16 and prostrating himself at the feet of Jesus, gave him thanks. Now he was a Samaritan.
LUK 17:17 Upon this, Jesus addressing him, said, Were not the ten cleansed? Where then are the nine?
LUK 17:18 Have none returned to give glory to God, but only this alien?
LUK 17:19 Then he said to him, Rise and go thy way. Thy faith hath cured thee.
LUK 17:20 Being asked by the Pharisees when the reign of God would commence, he answered and said to them, The reign of God doth not commence with parade;
LUK 17:21 nor shall they say, Lo, here! or Lo, there! For behold the reign of God is within you.
LUK 17:22 Then he said to his disciples, The days will come, when you will earnestly desire to see one of the days of the son of man, and will not see it.
LUK 17:23 When they say to you, Lo, here! or Lo, yonder! Go not out, nor follow them.

LUK 17:25 But he must first suffer many things and be rejected by this generation.
LUK 17:26 And as it was in the days of Noe, so will it be in the days of the son of man.
LUK 17:27 They ate; they drank; they married, and were given in marriage, until the day that Noe entered the ark; and the flood came and destroyed them all.
LUK 17:28 Just so it was also in the days of Lot. They ate; they drank; they bought; they sold; they planted; they built:
LUK 17:29 but on the day that Lot went out of Sodom, it rained fire and brimstone from heaven and destroyed them all.
LUK 17:30 Even so will it be on the day when the son of man will be revealed.
LUK 17:31 On that day, whoever shall be on the house top, and his goods in the house, let him not come down to carry them away. And in like manner let not him who shall be in the field turn back to what is behind him.

LUK 17:33 One, though he may seek to save his life, shall lose it. And another, though he may expose his life, shall save it.

LUK 17:35 Two women will be grinding together; the one will be taken and the other left.
LUK 17:36 Two men will be in the field, the one will be taken and the other left.

LUK 18:1 Then he addressed them with a parable, to shew them that they ought to persevere in prayer, and not be discouraged;
LUK 18:2 saying, There was in a certain city a judge, who neither feared God, nor regarded man.
LUK 18:3 And there was in that city a widow, who went to him, saying, Do me justice on mine adversary.
LUK 18:4 And for a while he would not. But afterwards he said within himself, Though I neither fear God, nor regard man,
LUK 18:5 yet because this widow giveth me trouble, I will do her justice, that she may not, by coming perpetually, torment me.
LUK 18:6 And the Lord said, Hear what this unjust judge saith!
LUK 18:7 And will not God vindicate the cause of his chosen, who are crying to him day and night"? Will he linger in their cause?
LUK 18:8 He will, I assure you, vindicate their cause speedily. But will the son of man, when he cometh, find this belief in this land"?
LUK 18:9 Then with a view to some who had a confidence in themselves that they were righteous, and who despised others, he spake this parable,
LUK 18:10 Two men went up to the temple to pray; the one, a Pharisee; and the other, a publican.
LUK 18:11 The Pharisee, standing by himself, prayed thus, O God, I thank thee that I am not as the rest of men, extortioners, unjust, adulterers; nor even as that publican.
LUK 18:12 I fast twice a week. I pay tithes of all that I possess.
LUK 18:13 But the publican, who stood at a distance, did not presume so much as to lift up his eyes to heaven, but smote upon his breast, saying; God, be merciful to me a sinner.
LUK 18:14 I tell you, this man went down to his house acquitted, and not the other. For whosoever exalteth himself shall be humbled, but he who humbleth himself shall be exalted.
LUK 18:15 When they brought even little children to him that he might touch them, and his disciples observing it, rebuked them;
LUK 18:16 Jesus thereupon having called the children to him, said, Suffer the children to come to me, and do not hinder them, for of such is the kingdom of God.
LUK 18:17 Verily I say to you, Whosoever will not as a child receive the kingdom of God, he shall in no wise enter it.

LUK 18:20 Thou knowest the commandments; thou shall not commit adultery; thou shalt not commit murder; thou shalt not steal; thou shalt not bear false witness; honour thy father and thy mother.
LUK 18:21 And he said, all these I have kept from my youth.
LUK 18:22 Upon hearing this, Jesus said to him, There is still one thing wanting to thee. Sell all that thou hast and distribute to the poor, and thou shalt have treasure in heaven. Then come and follow me.
LUK 18:23 At hearing this he was very sorrowful; for he was very rich.
LUK 18:24 When Jesus saw that he was very sorrowful, he said, With what difficulty will men who have these things, enter into the kingdom of God!
LUK 18:25 for it is easier for a camel to pass through the eye of a needle, than for a rich man to enter the kingdom of God.
LUK 18:26 And when they who heard this said, Who then can be saved?
LUK 18:27 He said, Things, which are impossible to men, are possible to God.
LUK 18:28 Then Peter said, Behold we have forsaken all and followed thee.
LUK 18:29 Whereupon Jesus said to them, Verily I say to you, There is none who hath left house or parents, or brothers, or wife, or children for the sake of the kingdom of God,
LUK 18:30 who shall not receive manifold more in return in this present time, and in the age to come everlasting life.

LUK 18:33 And when they have scourged him, they will put him to death. And on the third day he will rise again.
LUK 18:34 But they understood nothing of these things. This matter indeed was hid from them, so that they did not comprehend the meaning of what was spoken.

LUK 19:13 So having called ten servants of his, he delivered to them ten pounds weight of money, and said to them, Trade with this till I return.
LUK 19:14 Now his citizens hated him, and sent an embassy after him, saying, We do not wish this man to reign over us.
LUK 19:15 And when he had obtained the regal government and was come back, he ordered those servants, to whom he had given the money, to be called to him, that he might know what each had gained.
LUK 19:16 And the first came and said, My lord, that pound of thine, hath gained ten pounds.
LUK 19:17 Whereupon he said to him, Well done, good servant! because thou hast been faithful in a very small trust, be thou the governor of ten cities.
LUK 19:18 Then the second came and said, My lord, that pound of thine hath gained five pounds.
LUK 19:19 Whereupon he said to him, Be thou also governor of five cities.
LUK 19:20 Then another came and said, My lord, here is that pound of thine, which I have kept laid up in a napkin.
LUK 19:21 For I was afraid of thee, because thou art an austere man. Thou takest up what thou laidst not down, and reapest what thou didst not sow.
LUK 19:22 Whereupon he Saith to him, Out of thine own mouth I will condemn thee, thou malignant slave. Thou knowest that I am an austere man, taking up what I laid not down, and reaping what I did not sow!
LUK 19:23 Why then didst thou not put my money in the bank, that at my return I might have received it with interest?

LUK 19:25 [and upon their saying to him, My lord he hath ten pounds]

LUK 20:1 Soon one of those days when he was teaching the people in the temple, and proclaiming the glad tidings, the chief priests, and the Scribes, and the elders, came up to him and accosted him,
LUK 20:2 saying, Tell us, by what authority thou dost these things? Or who hath given thee this authority?
LUK 20:3 In answer to which, he said to them, Let me also ask you one question, and do you tell me.
LUK 20:4 Was the baptism of John from heaven, or of men?
LUK 20:5 Upon this they reasoned among themselves, saying, If we say from heaven, he will say, Why then did you not believe him?
LUK 20:6 And if we say, Of men; all the people will stone us; for they are all firmly persuaded that John was a prophet.
LUK 20:7 So they answered that they did not know whence it was.
LUK 20:8 Thereupon Jesus said to them, Neither do I tell you by what authority I do these things.
LUK 20:9 Then he addressed to the people this parable. A certain man planted a vineyard and let it to husbandmen, and went abroad for many seasons.
LUK 20:10 And at one season he sent a servant to the husbandmen that they might give him some of the product of the vineyard. But the husbandmen beat him and sent him away empty.
LUK 20:11 Again he sent another servant; and him also they beat, and abused shamefully, and sent away empty.
LUK 20:12 Again he sent a third, and this one they wounded and cast out.
LUK 20:13 Then the owner of the vineyard said, What shall I do? I will send my son, the Beloved. Perhaps they will reverence him, when they see him.
LUK 20:14 But when the husbandmen saw him, they reasoned among themselves, saying, This is the heir. Come, let us kill him, that the inheritance may be our own.
LUK 20:15 So having, cast him out of the vineyard they slew him. What then will the owner of the vineyard do to them?
LUK 20:16 He will come and destroy those husbandmen and give the vineyard to others. Upon hearing this, they said, God forbid.
LUK 20:17 But he looking earnestly at them, said, "What then is the meaning of this passage of scripture, The stone which the builders rejected was the very one for the head of the corner!
LUK 20:18 Whosoever falleth on this stone will be bruised; but on whomsoever it shall fall, it will grind him to powder.
LUK 20:19 Upon this the chief priests and the Scribes sought to lay hands on him that very hour, [but they were afraid of the people,] for they knew that he had spoken this parable with a view to them.
LUK 20:20 Therefore, having watched him diligently, they sent to him spies who should feign themselves to be righteous men, that they might lay hold of some word of his, in order to deliver him up to the jurisdiction and authority of the governor.
LUK 20:21 So they asked him, saying, Teacher, we know that thou speakest and teachest uprightly, and that thou art not a respecter of persons, but teachest the way of God with truth.
LUK 20:22 Is it lawful for us to pay tribute to Caesar, or is it not?
LUK 20:23 But he, knowing their craftiness, said to them, Why are you trying me?
LUK 20:24 Shew me a deniar. Whose image and inscription hath it? When they in reply, said, Caesar's;
LUK 20:25 then he said to them, Render then to Caesar the things which are Caesar's; and to God, the things which are God's.
LUK 20:26 So they were not able to take advantage of his decision before the people. Therefore, having expressed admiration at his answer, they held their peace.
LUK 20:27 Then some of the Sadducees, who deny a future state, came and asked him,
LUK 20:28 saying, Teacher, Moses hath written for us, If a man's brother, having a wife, die; when he dieth childless, his brother must take his wife and raise up a seed for his brother,
LUK 20:29 Now there were seven brothers. And the first, having taken a wife, died childless.
LUK 20:30 Then the second took the wife, and he died childless:
LUK 20:31 then the third took her, and so all the seven, and died without issue.
LUK 20:32 And last of all the woman also died.
LUK 20:33 In the future state, therefore, whose wife of them is she, as she hath been married to all the seven?
LUK 20:34 In reply to this, Jesus said to them, The children of this world marry and are given in marriage;
LUK 20:35 but they who shall be accounted worthy to obtain that state, and the resurrection from the dead, neither marry nor are given in marriage,
LUK 20:36 For they can die no more. For angel-like they are indeed children of God, being children of the resurrection.
LUK 20:37 Now that the dead are raised up, even Moses hath plainly shewn; as at the bush he stileth the Lord, the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaak, and the God of Jacob.
LUK 20:38 For he is not the God of the dead, but of the living. For to him they are all alive.
LUK 20:39 Upon this, some of the scribes addressing him, said, Teacher, thou hast spoken well.
LUK 20:40 And after that they did not presume to ask him another question.
LUK 20:41 Then he said to them, How do they say that the Christ is the son of David,
LUK 20:42 when David himself saith in the book of Psalms, The Lord said to my Lord, Sit at my right hand
LUK 20:43 until I make thine enemies thy footstool,
LUK 20:44 David therefore calleth him Lord, how then is he his son?

LUK 20:47 who devour the families of widows, and for a disguise make long prayers. They shall receive a severer sentence of judgment.

LUK 22:32 and I have prayed for thee that thy faith may not quite fail. When thou therefore hast recovered thyself, strengthen thou thy brethren.
LUK 22:33 Upon this Peter said to him, "Master, I am ready to go with thee to prison and to death."
LUK 22:34 Whereupon he said, I tell thee, Peter, a cock will not crow this day before thou wilt thrice deny that thou knowest me.
LUK 22:35 Then he said to them, When I sent you without purse and scrip and sandals, did you want any thing? And when they said No;
LUK 22:36 then he said to them, But now let him who hath a purse take it, and likewise a scrip. And let him who hath not a sword sell his mantle and buy one.
LUK 22:37 For I say to you, this portion of scripture" And he was ranked with malefactors," must yet be accomplished in me. For the things concerning me are coming to a close.
LUK 22:38 Then they said, Master, here are two swords. And he said, it is enough.
LUK 22:39 Then he went out and retired as usual to the mount of olives; and his disciples followed him.
LUK 22:40 And when he came to the place, he said to them, Pray, that you may not come to trial.
LUK 22:41 Then having withdrawn about a stone's throw from them, he kneeled down and prayed,
LUK 22:42 saying, O Father, if thou wilt remove this cup from me; but not my will, but thine be done.
LUK 22:43 Then an angel from heaven appeared to him, strengthening him.
LUK 22:44 And being in an agony, he prayed more earnestly. And his sweat was like great drops of blood falling on the ground.
LUK 22:45 Then he arose from prayer, and went to his disciples, and found them asleep, oppressed with grief.
LUK 22:46 And he said to them, What! Are you asleep! Rise and pray that you may not come to trial.
LUK 22:47 And while he was yet speaking, Lo! a crowd! And he who is called Judas, one of the twelve, came on before them and went up to Jesus to kiss him.
LUK 22:48 Whereupon Jesus said to him, Judas, dost thou deliver up the son of man with a kiss?
LUK 22:49 Then they who were about him seeing what would happen, said to him, Master, shall we smite with the sword?
LUK 22:50 And one of them smote the servant of the high priest, and cut off his right ear.
LUK 22:51 Thereupon Jesus interposing, said, Permit thus long; and having touched his ear, healed him.
LUK 22:52 Then Jesus said to the chief priests, and the officers of the temple guard, and the elders who were come against him, Are you come out as against a robber with swords and clubs?
LUK 22:53 When I was daily with you in the temple, you did not stretch forth your hands against me. But this is your hour, and the power of darkness.
LUK 22:54 Then they who had seized him led him away. And when they were bringing him to the house of the chief priest, Peter followed at a distance.
LUK 22:55 And as they had kindled a fire in the middle of the court, and were sitting around it, Peter sat down in the midst of them.
LUK 22:56 And a maid servant having seen him sitting opposite to the light, and viewed him attentively, said, That man was also with him.
LUK 22:57 Upon which Peter denied him, saying, Woman, I do not know him.
LUK 22:58 And a little while after, another seeing him, said, Thou also art one of them. whereupon Peter said, Man, I am not.
LUK 22:59 And about the space of an hour after, another confidently affirmed, saying, This man was certainly with him; for he is a Galilean.
LUK 22:60 Thereupon Peter said, Man, I do not know what thou sayest. And instantly, while he was yet speaking, the cock crowed.
LUK 22:61 Upon which the Lord, turning about, looked upon Peter. And Peter recollected the word of the Lord, how he said to him, Before cock crowing thou wilt three times deny me.
LUK 22:62 And Peter went out and wept bitterly.
LUK 22:63 Now the men, who had Jesus in custody, insulted him while they smote him.
LUK 22:64 Having covered his eyes they struck him on the face, and asked him, saying, Prophesy. Who is he who smote thee?
LUK 22:65 And uttered many other invectives against him.
LUK 22:66 And soon as it was day, the national senate, with the chief priests, and the Scribes, convened. And having caused him to be brought up before their Sanhedrim, they said,
LUK 22:67 Art thou the Christ? Tell us. Whereupon he said to them, If I tell you, you will not believe me.
LUK 22:68 And if I ask you a question, you will not answer me, nor dismiss me.
LUK 22:69 From this time the son of man will be seated on the right hand of the power of God.
LUK 22:70 Thereupon they all said, Thou then art the son of God? And he said to them, It is as you say.
LUK 22:71 Then they said, what farther need have we of testimony? For we ourselves have heard from his own mouth.
LUK 23:1 Then the whole assembly arose and led him away to Pilate,
LUK 23:2 and began to accuse him, saying, We found this man perverting the nation, and forbidding to pay tribute to Caesar, saying that he himself is Christ, a king.
LUK 23:3 Thereupon Pilate asked him, saying, Thou art the king of the Jews? And he, in reply, said to him, It is as thou sayest.
LUK 23:4 Then Pilate said to the chief priests, and the people, I find nothing criminal in this man.
LUK 23:5 But they were the more vehement, saying, He raiseth sedition among the people, teaching through all Judea, from Galilee, where he began, even to this place.
LUK 23:6 When Pilate heard them mention Galilee, he asked, Is the man a Galilean?"
LUK 23:7 And finding that he was of Herod's jurisdiction, he sent him to Herod, who was also at Jerusalem in those days.
LUK 23:8 And when Herod saw Jesus he was very glad; for he had long desired to see him. Because he had heard much of him, therefore he hoped to see some miracle done by him,
LUK 23:9 and questioned him about many things. But Jesus made him no answer.
LUK 23:10 So when the chief priests, and the Scribes had stood up, urging their accusations against him with much vehemence;
LUK 23:11 and Herod with his soldiers had treated him with contempt and mockery, having arrayed him with a splendid robe, he sent him back to Pilate.
LUK 23:12 And on that day Pilate and Herod became friends; for they had been before at enmity one with the other.
LUK 23:13 Then Pilate, having called together the chief priests and the rulers of the people,
LUK 23:14 said to them, You have brought this man to me as one who perverteth the people. And behold, on examining him before you, I have found nothing criminal in this man, touching those things which you lay to his charge.
LUK 23:15 Neither indeed hath Herod: for I referred you to him. Now as it appears that nothing deserving death hath been done by him:
LUK 23:16 shall I therefore, when I have chastised him, let him go?
LUK 23:17 Now he was under a necessity of releasing one to them at every festival,
LUK 23:18 so they with one consent cried out, saying, Away with this man and release to us Barabbas.
LUK 23:19 This was a person who on account of an insurrection in the city, and for murder, had been committed to prison.
LUK 23:20 Pilate therefore addressed them again, being desirous to release Jesus.
LUK 23:21 But they  exclaimed, saying, Crucify him; Crucify him.
LUK 23:22 But he said to them a third time, Why, what evil hath he done? I have found nothing in him deserving death. I will therefore chastise him and let him go.
LUK 23:23 But they with loud clamours persisted in their demands that he should be crucified. So the clamours of them and of the chief priests prevailed,
LUK 23:24 and Pilate pronounced sentence that what they requested should be done,
LUK 23:25 and released to them the man who for sedition and murder had been thrown into prison, whom they demanded, and gave up Jesus to their will.
LUK 23:26 And as they were leading him away, they laid hold on one Simon, a Cyrenian, who was coming from the country, and laid the cross on him, that he might carry it after Jesus.
LUK 23:27 And a great multitude of the people followed him, among whom were many women, who beat their breasts, and bewailed him.
LUK 23:28 Whereupon, Jesus turning to them, said, Daughters of Jerusalem, weep not for me; but weep for yourselves and for your children;
LUK 23:29 for lo! days are coming in which they will say, Happy the barren, and the wombs which never bare, and the breasts which never gave suck.
LUK 23:30 Then will they begin to say to the mountains, Fall upon us: and to the hills, Cover us.
LUK 23:31 For if such things be done with green wood; how must it be with dry!
LUK 23:32 Now there were two other persons, who were malefactors, led along with him to be crucified.
LUK 23:33 And when they came to the place called Calvary, they there crucified him and the two malefactors, one on his right hand and the other on his left.
LUK 23:34 Whereupon Jesus said, Father, forgive them, for they know not what they are doing. Then dividing his garments in shares they cast lots.
LUK 23:35 And the people stood looking on; and both they and the rulers mocked him, saying, He saved others; let him save himself, if he be the Christ, the chosen of God.
LUK 23:36 And the soldiers also, coming and offering him vinegar, insulted him,
LUK 23:37 saying, If thou art the king of the Jews, save thyself.
LUK 23:38 For over him there was an inscription, written in Greek, and Latin, and Hebrew. This is The King Of The Jews.
LUK 23:39 Even one of the malefactors who were on crosses, reviled him, saying, If thou art the Christ, save thyself and us.
LUK 23:40 Upon which the other, in reply, rebuked him, saying, Hast thou no fear of God even when thou art suffering the same punishment?
LUK 23:41 We indeed justly; for we are receiving the due reward of our crimes. But this man hath done nothing amiss.
LUK 23:42 Then he said to Jesus, Lord, remember me when thou comest to thy kingdom.
