LUK 23:43 Whereupon Jesus said to him, Verily I say to thee, Today thou shalt be with me in paradise.
LUK 23:44 It was now about the sixth hour, and there came darkness over the whole land until the ninth,
LUK 23:45 when the sun was darkened, and the veil of the temple was rent down the middle;
LUK 23:46 and Jesus crying with a loud voice, said, Father, into thy hands I commit my spirit. And having said this he expired.
LUK 23:47 Now when the centurion saw what had happened, he glorified God, saying, Certainly this was a righteous man.
LUK 23:48 And all the multitudes who had crowded to the spectacle, seeing what had happened, beat their breasts and returned home.
LUK 23:49 Now all his male acquaintance had stood at a distance, while the women, who had accompanied him from Galilee, were viewing these things.
LUK 23:50 And lo! a man named Joseph, who was a senator, a good and righteous man,
LUK 23:51 and who had not concurred with the rest in their counsel and proceedings; he was of Arimathea, a city of the Jews, and was one who was expecting the reign of God.
LUK 23:52 This man went to Pilate and begged the body of Jesus;
LUK 23:53 and having taken it down, he wrapped it in a sindon, and laid it in a sepulchre which was hewn out of a rock, and in which nobody had ever been laid.
LUK 23:54 As it was now preparation time, and the sabbath was55 clearing up;
LUK 23:55 When the women who had come with Jesus from Galilee, had followed him down and seen the sepulchre, and how the body was laid,
LUK 23:56 they returned and provided spices and ointments of myrrh, and had rested the sabbath, according to. the commandment,
LUK 24:1 And on the first day of the week, they went very early in the morning to the sepulchre, carrying the spices which they had provided. And there were some others with them.
LUK 24:2 And they found the stone rolled away from the sepulchre,
LUK 24:3 but on going in did not find the body of the Lord Jesus.
LUK 24:4 And while they were in perplexity on this account, lo! two men stood by them in glistening robes;
LUK 24:5 at which they being terrified, and inclining their face to the ground, the men said to them, Why seek ye the living among the dead?"
LUK 24:6 He is not here; but is risen. Remember how he spake to you, while he was yet in Galilee,
LUK 24:7 saying, The son of man must be delivered into the hands of sinful men, and be crucified, and on the third day rise again.
LUK 24:8 Then they remembered his words,
LUK 24:9 and having returned from the sepulchre, they told all these things to the eleven, and to all the rest.
LUK 24:10 Now it was Mary Magdalene, and Joanna, and Mary the mother of James, and the rest with them, who told these things to the apostles.
LUK 24:11 But their words appeared to them like an idle tale, and they did not believe them.
LUK 24:12 Peter indeed, starting up, ran to the sepulchre, and having stooped down, saw nothing but the linens lying there. Upon which he went away home, musing with astonishment on what had happened.
LUK 24:13 And behold, on that same day, two of them were travelling to a village called Emmaus, which was sixty furlongs from Jerusalem;
LUK 24:14 and they conversed with each other on all these occurrences.
LUK 24:15 And while they were conversing and reasoning together, Jesus himself drew near and travelled along with them.
LUK 24:16 But their eyes were withheld from knowing him.
LUK 24:17 And he said to them, What matters are these about which you are conferring with one another on the road, and are sad?
LUK 24:18 Thereupon one of them, whose name was Cleopas, answering, said to him, Art thou such a stranger in Jerusalem as not to know the things which have happened there in these days?
LUK 24:19 And he said, What things? They answered him, Those respecting Jesus, the Nazarene, who was a great prophet, mighty in miracles and doctrine before God and all the people
LUK 24:20 how our chief priests and our rulers delivered him up to be condemned to death, and they have crucified him.
LUK 24:21 Now we were hoping that he is the person who would soon deliver Israel. But indeed with all this, it is now the third day since these things happened.
LUK 24:22 But again some women of our company have astonished us; having been at the sepulchre very early in the morning,
LUK 24:23 and not finding his body, they came and told us that they had seen a vision of angels, who say that he is alive.
LUK 24:24 Whereupon some of the men who were with us went to the sepulchre, and found matters just as the women said: but him they did not see.
LUK 24:25 Then he said to them, O thoughtless, and slow of heart to believe all that the prophets have spoken!
LUK 24:26 Was it not necessary that the Christ should suffer these things and enter into his glory?
LUK 24:27 Then beginning with Moses and proceeding through all the prophets, he explained to them, by all those writings, the things concerning himself.
LUK 24:28 And when they drew near to the village to which they were going, he seemed as intending to go farther.
LUK 24:29 But they pressed him, saying, Stay with us; for it is towards evening. The day is far spent. So he went in to stay with them.
LUK 24:30 And when he was at table with them, he took the loaf, and blessed, and brake, and distributed to them.
LUK 24:31 Whereupon their eyes were opened, and they knew him, and he disappeared from them.
LUK 24:32 Then they said to one another, Did not our hearts burn within us while he talked with us on the road, and while he expounded the scriptures to us?
LUK 24:33 Then rising up immediately, they returned to Jerusalem, and found the eleven and those with them in a throng,
LUK 24:34 affirming that the Lord is indeed risen and hath appeared to Simon.
LUK 24:35 And they told the occurrences on the road, and how he became known to them by his breaking the loaf.
LUK 24:36 And while they were thus speaking, Jesus himself stood in the midst of them; and saith to them, Peace be to you.
LUK 24:37 At which they were affrighted, and, being in terror, thought they saw a spirit;
LUK 24:38 he said to them, Why are you alarmed? And why do groundless surmises arise in your hearts?
LUK 24:39 View my hands and my feet; that it is I myself; handle me and see, for a spirit hath not flesh and bones as you see me have.
LUK 24:40 While saying this, he shewed them his hands and his feet.
LUK 24:41 And as they were still diffident on account of their joy, and in amaze, he said to them, Have you any food here?
LUK 24:42 Thereupon they gave him a piece of broiled fish and part of a honey comb,
LUK 24:43 which he took and ate before them.
LUK 24:44 Then he said to them, This is what I told you while I was yet with you, That all the things written concerning me in the law of Moses, and in the prophets, and in the Psalms, must needs be accomplished.
LUK 24:45 Then he opened their minds that they might understand the scriptures,
LUK 24:46 and he said to them, Thus it is written, and thus it behoved the Christ to suffer and rise from the dead on the third day;
LUK 24:47 and that for his name reformation and remission of sins should be proclaimed to all the nations, beginning at Jerusalem.
LUK 24:48 Now you are witnesses of these things.
LUK 24:49 And behold I will send upon you what my father promised. And as for you, reside ye in the city of Jerusalem until you are indued with power from on high.
LUK 24:50 After that he led them out to Bethany, and having lifted up his hands, he blessed them;
LUK 24:51 and while he was blessing them, he was parted from them and carried up into heaven;
LUK 24:52 and they, having worshipped him, returned to Jerusalem with great joy,
LUK 24:53 and were continually in the temple, praising and blessing God. Amen.
JOH 1:1 In the beginning was the Word; and the Word was with God; and the Word was God.
JOH 1:2 He was in the beginning with God.
JOH 1:3 By him all things were made, and without him there was not made one single thing.
JOH 1:4 What was in him was life, and this life was the light of men,
JOH 1:5 and this light shineth in the darkness, and the darkness did not reach it.
JOH 1:6 There was a man sent from God: his name was John.
JOH 1:7 This man came as a witness to bear witness concerning this light, that by means of him all might believe.
JOH 1:8 He was not the light, but was to bear witness concerning the light.
JOH 1:9 The light [the true light which enlighteneth every man] coming into the world
JOH 1:10 was in the world, and the world was made by him, and the world knew him not.
JOH 1:11 He came to his own peculiar territories, and his own peculiar people did not receive him.
JOH 1:12 But to as many as received him he granted the privilege of becoming children of God, even to them who believe in his name,
JOH 1:13 who were born, not of bloods, nor of the will of the flesh, nor of the will of man, but of God.
JOH 1:14 Now the Word became incarnate, and dwelt as in a tent among us, and we beheld his glory; a glory as of an only begotten from the father. He was full of grace and truth.
JOH 1:15 Of him John testifieth when he cried, saying, "This is he of whom I said, He who is coming after me is preferred before me, for he was before me."
JOH 1:16 And of his fulness we have all received even grace for grace.
JOH 1:17 Because the law was given by Moses grace and truth came by Jesus Christ.
JOH 1:18 No one hath ever seen God. This only begotten son, who is in the bosom of the father, even he hath made him known.
JOH 1:19 Now this is the testimony of John: when the Jews of Jerusalem sent priests and Levites to ask him, Who art thou?
JOH 1:20 He frankly declared and did not deny, but frankly declared, I am not the Christ.
JOH 1:21 Then they asked him, What then? Art thou Elias? And he said, I am not: art thou the prophet And he answered, No.
JOH 1:22 Then they said to him, Who art thou? That we may give an answer to them who sent us: What sayest thou of thyself?
JOH 1:23 He said, I am "The voice of one crying in the wilderness, Make straight the way of the Lord," as the prophet Esaias said.
JOH 1:24 Now they who were sent were of the Pharisees.
JOH 1:25 Then they asked him and said to him, Why then dost thou baptize, if thou art not the Christ, nor Elias, nor the prophet?
JOH 1:26 John answered them saying, I baptize in water; but there is one in the midst of you, whom you know not.
JOH 1:27 He is the person who is coming after me; who is preferred to me, the latchet of whose sandal I am not worthy to untie.
JOH 1:28 These things passed at Bethabara on the bank of the Jordan, where John was baptizing.
JOH 1:29 The next day John seeth Jesus coming towards him, and saith, Behold the lamb of God, which taketh away the sin of the world!
JOH 1:30 this is he of whom I said, After me cometh a man who hath been before me; for he existed before me.
JOH 1:31 As for me, I did not know him; but to the end that he might be made manifest to Israel; for this purpose I came baptizing in water.
JOH 1:32 Moreover John testified saying, I beheld the Spirit descending like a dove from heaven, and it remained upon him.
JOH 1:33 Now for my part I did not know him; but he who sent me to baptize in water, even he said to me, On whomsoever thou shalt see the spirit descending and remaining on him, the same is he who baptizeth in a holy spirit.
JOH 1:34 Now I have Seen and testified that this is The Son Of God.
JOH 1:35 Again, on the next day, John was standing with two of his disciples,
JOH 1:36 and having fixed his eyes intently on Jesus as he was walking, he saith, Behold the lamb of God!
JOH 1:37 and the two disciples heard him speaking, and followed Jesus.
JOH 1:38 When Jesus turned and saw them following him, he saith to them, What seek ye? And they said to him, Rabbi, [the meaning of which, when interpreted, is Teacher] where dost thou make thine abode?
JOH 1:39 He saith to them, Come and see. They went and saw where he made his abode, and staid with him that day; for it was about the tenth hour.
JOH 1:40 Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, was one of the two who heard John and followed Jesus.
JOH 1:41 He first findeth his brother Simon, and saith to him, We have found the Messias, [the meaning of which is the Christ] [the anointed]
JOH 1:42 and brought him to Jesus. And Jesus, having looked earnestly on him, said, Thou art Simon the son of Jonas. Thou shalt be called Cephas [the meaning of which is the same as that of Peter] [a rock.]
JOH 1:43 On the day following Jesus determined to set out for Galilee, and finding Philip, he saith to him, Come with me.
JOH 1:44 Now Philip was of Bethsaida, the city of Andrew and Peter.
JOH 1:45 Philip finding Nathaniel, saith to him, We have found him of whom Moses in the law, and the prophets have written, Jesus of Nazareth, the son of Joseph.
JOH 1:46 Upon which Nathaniel saith to him, Of Nazareth can there be any thing good! Philip saith to him, Come and see.
JOH 1:47 Jesus saw Nathaniel coming to him and saith respecting him, Behold an Israelite indeed, in whom there is no guile!
JOH 1:48 Nathaniel saith to him, Whence knowest thou me? Jesus in reply said to him, Before Philip called thee, when thou wast under the fig tree, I saw thee.
JOH 1:49 In answer to this, Nathaniel said to him, Rabbi, thou art the son of God. Thou art the king of Israel.
JOH 1:50 Jesus answered and said to him, Because I told thee, I saw thee under the fig tree, dost thou believe? Thou shalt see greater things than these.
JOH 1:51 Then he saith to him, Verily, verily I say to you, Hereafter you shall see the heaven opened, and the angels of God ascending and descending on the son of man.
JOH 2:1 Now on the third day there was a wedding at Cana of Galilee, and the mother of Jesus was there;
JOH 2:2 and Jesus and his disciples were invited to the wedding.
JOH 2:3 And the wine having fallen short, the mother of Jesus saith to him, They have no wine.
JOH 2:4 Jesus saith to her, Woman, what hast thou to do with me? My hour is not yet come.
JOH 2:5 His mother saith to the waiters, Do whatever he shall bid you.
JOH 2:6 Now there were six water pots of stone, containing two or three measures apiece, placed there for the Jewish rites of purifying.
JOH 2:7 Jesus saith to the waiters, Fill those water pots with water. And when they had filled them to the brim,
JOH 2:8 then he saith to them, Draw out now and carry some to the master of the feast. And when they had carried,
JOH 2:9 and the master of the feast had tasted the water which was made wine [now he did not know whence it was, but the waiters who had drawn off the water knew] the master of the feast calleth the bridegroom,
JOH 2:10 and saith to him, Every man serveth up the good wine first, and when the guests have drunk plentifully, then that which is worse. Thou hast kept the good wine till now.
JOH 2:11 This at Cana, in Galilee, Jesus made the beginning of his miracles and manifested his glory, and his disciples believed on him.
JOH 2:12 After this, he and his mother, and his brethren, and his disciples went down to Capernaum, but they did not stay there many days.
JOH 2:13 For the passover of the Jews was nigh, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem
JOH 2:14 and found in the temple them who sold cattle, and sheep, and doves, and the changers of money seated;
JOH 2:15 and having made a whip of bulrushes, he drove them all out of the temple, with the sheep and cattle, and poured out the money of the changers, and overturned their tables,
JOH 2:16 and said to them who sold doves, Take these things hence. Make not the house of my father a house of merchandize.
JOH 2:17 Then did his disciples remember that it was written, "My zeal for thy house hath consumed me."
JOH 2:18 Hereupon the Jews addressed him, and said, What sign dost thou shew us to justify thy doing these things?
JOH 2:19 In reply to which Jesus said to them, Destroy this temple, and in three days I will raise it up.
JOH 2:20 Thereupon the Jews said, This temple was forty six years a building, and wilt thou raise it up in three days?
JOH 2:21 But he spake of the temple of his body:
JOH 2:22 therefore, when he was risen from the dead, his disciples remembered that he had said this to them; and they believed the scriptures, and the word which Jesus had spoken.
JOH 2:23 Now while he was in Jerusalem at the passover, during the festival, many believed in his name when they saw the miracles which he did.
JOH 2:24 But Jesus did not trust himself to them, because he knew all men.
JOH 2:25 And because he had no need that any one should testify of man, for he himself knew what was in man;
JOH 3:1 there being a man of the sect of the Pharisees, named Nicodemus, a ruler of the Jews;
JOH 3:2 when this man came to Jesus by night, and said to him, Rabbi, We know that thou art a teacher come from God; for no one can do the miracles which thou dost, unless God be with him,
JOH 3:3 Jesus answered and said to him, Verily, verily I say to thee, unless a man be born again, he cannot discern the reign of God.
JOH 3:4 Nicodemus saith to him, How can a man be born, when he is old? Can he enter a second time into his mother's womb and be born?
JOH 3:5 Jesus answered, Verily, verily I say to thee, unless a man be born of water and spirit, he cannot enter the kingdom of God.
JOH 3:6 That which is born of the flesh, is flesh; and that which is born of the spirit, is spirit.
JOH 3:7 Wonder not at my telling thee, You must be born again.
JOH 3:8 That blast of wind bloweth where it pleaseth, and thou hearest the sound of it, but dost not know whence it cometh and whither it goeth. So is every one who is born of the spirit.
JOH 3:9 Nicodemus answered, and said to him, How can these things be?
JOH 3:10 In reply to which, Jesus said to him, Art thou the teacher of Israel, and knowest not these things?
JOH 3:11 Verily, verily I say to thee, We speak what we know, and testify what we have seen; yet you do not receive our testimony.
JOH 3:12 If I have told you earthly things and you do not believe; how will you believe if I tell you heavenly things?
JOH 3:13 No one indeed hath ascended up into heaven, but he who came down from heaven, namely, the son of man who is in heaven.
JOH 3:14 But as Moses lifted up the serpent in the wilderness, so must the son of man be lifted up,
JOH 3:15 that whosoever believeth in him may not perish; but have everlasting life.
JOH 3:16 For God so loved the world that he gave his only begotten son, that whosoever believeth in him may not perish, but have everlasting life.
JOH 3:17 For God did not send his son into the world to condemn the world; but that the world may be saved by him.
JOH 3:18 He who believeth in him will not be condemned; but he who believeth not, is condemned already; because he hath not believed in the name of the only begotten son of God.
JOH 3:19 And this is the condemnation, that light is come into the world, and men loved darkness more than light, because their works were evil.
JOH 3:20 For whosoever doeth evil hateth the light, and doth not come to the light, that his deeds may not be detected.
JOH 3:21 But he who practiseth truth cometh to the light, that his works may be open to view, because they are the operations of God."
JOH 3:22 After this, Jesus went with his disciples into the country of Judea, and spent some time with them there, and baptized.
JOH 3:23 And John also was baptizing at Enon, near Saleim, because there was much water there, and people used to come there and be baptized;
JOH 3:24 for John was not yet thrown into prison.
JOH 3:25 There was therefore a dispute between some of the disciples of John, and the Jews, respecting purification,
JOH 3:26 and they went to John, and said to him, Rabbi, he who was with thee on the bank of the Jordan, to whom thou didst bear testimony, behold he is baptizing, and all are flocking to him.
JOH 3:27 In reply to which, John said, A man can receive nothing from heaven, unless it be given him.
JOH 3:28 You yourselves are witnesses for me that I said, "I am not the Christ; but that I am sent before him.
JOH 3:29 He is the bridegroom, who hath the bride. But the friend of the bridegroom, who standeth and heareth him, rejoiceth exceedingly on the account of the bridegroom's voice. This joy of mine therefore, is complete.
JOH 3:30 He must increase, but I must decrease.
JOH 3:31 The one coming from above, is above all. He who is of the earth is earthly, and speaketh of the earth. The one coming from heaven is above all,
JOH 3:32 and what he hath seen and heard, that he testifieth, yet none receiveth his testimony.
JOH 3:33 He who hath received his testimony, hath set his seal to this, That God is true.
JOH 3:34 For he whom God hath sent, speaketh the words of God; for God giveth him not the spirit by measure.
JOH 3:35 The father loveth the son, and hath given all things into his hand.
JOH 3:36 He who believeth in the son, hath an everlasting life; but he who disbelieveth the son, shall not see life; but the wrath of God will abide on him.
JOH 4:1 When the Lord, therefore, knew that the Pharisees had heard that Jesus is making and baptizing more disciples than John,
JOH 4:2 [though it was not indeed Jesus himself, but his disciples who baptized]
JOH 4:3 he left Judea and went again into Galilee:
JOH 4:4 and as he must needs pass through Samaria,
JOH 4:5 therefore he cometh to a city of Samaria, called Sichar, near the piece of ground which Jacob gave to his son Joseph.
JOH 4:6 Now Jacob's well was there. And as Jesus, wearied as he was with the journey, was sitting by the well, [it was about the sixth hour]
JOH 4:7 a woman of Samaria came out to draw water. Jesus saith to her, Give me to drink;
JOH 4:8 [for his disciples were gone to the city to buy food;]
JOH 4:9 thereupon the woman of Samaria saith to him, How is it that thou, being a Jew, askest drink of me, who am a woman of Samaria? [For the Jews have no friendly intercourse with the Samaritans.]
JOH 4:10 Jesus answered and said to her, If thou hadst known the bounty of God, and who it is who saith to thee, Give me to drink, thou wouldst have asked of him, and he would have given thee living water.
JOH 4:11 The woman saith to him, Sir, thou hast nothing to draw with, and the well is deep; whence then hast thou this living water?
JOH 4:12 Art thou greater than our father Jacob, who gave us this well, and drank thereof, himself, and his children, and his cattle?
JOH 4:13 In reply to which, Jesus said to her, every one who drinketh of this water will thirst again;
JOH 4:14 but whosoever shall drink of the water which I will give him, will never thirst. But the water which I will give him, will be in him a fountain of water springing up for an everlasting life.
JOH 4:15 The woman saith to him, O, sir, give me that water, that I may not thirst, nor come hither to draw.
JOH 4:16 Jesus saith to her, Go, call thy husband and come hither.
JOH 4:17 The woman in reply said, I have no husband. Jesus saith to her, Thou art right in saying, I have no husband:
JOH 4:18 for thou hast had five husbands; and he whom thou now hast, is not thy husband. In this thou hast spoken truth.
JOH 4:19 The woman saith to him, Sir, I perceive that thou art a prophet.
JOH 4:20 Our fathers have usually worshipped on this mountain; but you say, that at Jerusalem is the place where worship ought to be performed.
JOH 4:21 Jesus saith to her, Woman, believe me, the hour is coming when you will worship the Father, neither on this mountain, nor at Jerusalem.
JOH 4:22 You worship what you do not know. We worship what we do know: for salvation is of the Jews.
JOH 4:23 But the hour is coming; indeed is now come, when the true worshippers will worship the Father in spirit and truth. For such worshippers of him the Father seeketh.
JOH 4:24 God is Spirit; and they who worship him ought to worship him in spirit and truth.
JOH 4:25 The woman saith to him, I know that the Messias [he who is called the Christ] is coming. When he is come he will tell us all things.
JOH 4:26 Jesus saith to her, I who am speaking to thee am he.
JOH 4:27 [Now at that instant his disciples came and wondered at his talking with the woman, yet none of them said, What seekest thou? Or why talkest thou with her?]
JOH 4:28 Thereupon the woman left her pitcher, and went to the city, and saith to the men,
JOH 4:29 Come, see a man who told me all that I ever did. Is this the Christ?
JOH 4:30 Therefore they of the city set out and were coming to him.
JOH 4:31 Now in the mean while his disciples entreated him, saying, Rabbi, eat.
JOH 4:32 But he said to them; I have meat to eat which you do not know.
JOH 4:33 His disciples therefore said to one another, Hath any one brought him food?
JOH 4:34 Jesus saith to them, It is my food to do the will of him who sent me, and to finish his work.
JOH 4:35 Do you not say, Yet four months, and the harvest cometh. Behold I say to you, Lift up your eyes and view the fields; for they are already white for harvest.
JOH 4:36 And he who reapeth receiveth wages, and gathereth fruit for an everlasting life, that he who soweth, and he who reapeth, may rejoice together.
JOH 4:37 For herein is that saying verified, that one soweth, and another reapeth.
JOH 4:38 I have sent you to reap that on which you bestowed no labour. Others have laboured and you have entered on their labours.
JOH 4:39 Now many of the Samaritans of that city believed in him, on the testimony of the woman who said, He told me all that I ever did.
JOH 4:40 Therefore, when these Samaritans came, they intreated him to tarry with them. So he stayed there two days.
JOH 4:41 And many more believed, because of what he himself spake,
JOH 4:42 and they said to the woman, It is not now on account of thy talk that we believe; for we ourselves have heard and we know that he is indeed the Saviour of the world, the Christ.
JOH 4:43 Now after the two days he departed thence, and went to Galilee, [but not directly to Nazareth]
JOH 4:44 for Jesus himself had testified that a prophet is not honoured in his native place.
JOH 4:45 Therefore when he came to Galilee, the Galileans received him, having seen all that he had done at Jerusalem, during the festival. For they also went up to the festival.
JOH 4:46 Jesus therefore went again to Cana of Galilee, where he had made the water wine. And there was a certain officer of the king, whose son was sick at Capernaum.
JOH 4:47 This person, upon hearing that Jesus was come from Judea to Galilee, went to him and intreated him to go down and cure his son; for he was at the point of death.
JOH 4:48 Jesus therefore said to him, Unless you see signs and wonders, can you not believe?
JOH 4:49 The officer saith to him, Sir, Come down before my child die.
JOH 4:50 Jesus saith to him, Go home: thy son liveth. And the man believed the word which Jesus spake to him, and went away.
JOH 4:51 And as he was going down, his servants met him and told him, saying, Thy son liveth.
JOH 4:52 Whereupon he inquired of them at what hour he began to mend. And they told him, that yesterday, at seven o'clock, the fever left him.
JOH 4:53 So the father knew that it was the very time when Jesus said to him, Thy son liveth, and he and his whole family believed.
JOH 4:54 This second miracle Jesus performed on his second coming from Judea to Galilee.
JOH 5:1 After this there was a festival of the Jews, and Jesus went up to Jerusalem.
JOH 5:2 Now there is in Jerusalem at the sheep gate, a pool, which is called in Hebrew Bethesda, having five porticos,
JOH 5:3 in which lay a great multitude of infirm persons, blind, lame, and withered, waiting for the moving of the water.
JOH 5:4 For from time to time an angel came down into the pool and moved the water. He therefore, who went in first after this movement of the water, was cured of whatever disease he had.
JOH 5:5 Now there was a certain man there who had been in his infirmity thirty eight years.
JOH 5:6 Jesus seeing him lying there, and knowing that he had been in that condition now a long time, saith to him, Hast thou a desire to be healed?
JOH 5:7 The infirm man answered him, Sir, I have no one to put me in the pool when the water is moved. And while I am going another steppeth down before me.
JOH 5:8 Jesus saith to him, Rise; take up thy couch and walk about.
JOH 5:9 Upon which the man was instantly well, and took up his couch and walked about. Now there was a sabbath on that day;
JOH 5:10 therefore the Jews said to him who was cured, It is a sabbath: It is not lawful for thee to carry the couch.
JOH 5:11 He answered them, He who made me well, even he said to me, Take up thy couch and walk about.
JOH 5:12 Thereupon they asked him, Who is the man who said to thee, take up thy couch and walk about?
JOH 5:13 But he who was cured did not know who it was; for as there was a crowd in the place, Jesus had glided away.
JOH 5:14 After this Jesus findeth him in the temple, and said to him, Behold thou art made well. Sin no more, lest something worse befall thee.
JOH 5:15 The man went and told the Jews that it was Jesus who had cured him.
JOH 5:16 And for this cause the Jews persecuted Jesus and sought to kill him, because he did these things on a sabbath.
JOH 5:17 Thereupon Jesus answered them, My Father worketh even now, and I also work.
JOH 5:18 For this therefore the Jews sought the more to kill him, because he not only broke the sabbath, but called God peculiarly his father, likening himself to God.
JOH 5:19 Upon which Jesus addressed them, and said, Verily, verily I say to you, The son can of himself do nothing, unless indeed he see the Father doing it; for whatever things He doth, these the Son doth likewise.
JOH 5:20 For the Father loveth the Son, and sheweth him all that he himself doth. And he will shew him greater works than these, that you may wonder.
JOH 5:21 For as the Father raiseth the dead and restoreth to life, so the Son restoreth to life, whom he pleaseth.
JOH 5:22 For the Father judgeth no one, but hath committed the whole act of judging to his Son,
JOH 5:23 that all may honour the Son, as they honour the Father. He who honoureth not the Son, doth not honour the Father, who sent him.
JOH 5:24 Verily, verily I say to you, He who heareth my word, and believeth on him who sent me, hath an everlasting life, and doth not incur condemnation, but hath passed from death to that life.
JOH 5:25 Verily, verily I say to you, a time is coming, nay is now come, when the dead will hearken to the voice of the son of God, and they who hearken shall live.
JOH 5:26 For as the Father hath life in himself, so he hath granted to the son to have life also in himself,
JOH 5:27 and hath also given him authority to execute judgment, because he is a son of man.
JOH 5:28 Wonder not at this; for a time is coming when all that are in the graves shall hearken to his voice,
JOH 5:29 and come forth; they who have done good, to a resurrection of life, and they who have done evil, to a resurrection of condemnation.
JOH 5:30 I can do nothing of myself. As I hear, I judge. And my judgment is just; for I do not seek mine own will, but the will of the Father who sent me.
JOH 5:31 If I testify of myself my testimony is not true.
JOH 5:32 There is another who testifieth concerning me; and I know that the testimony which he giveth concerning me is true.
JOH 5:33 You sent to John, and he gave a testimony to the truth.
JOH 5:34 But as for me, I do not receive human testimony, but mention this that you may be saved.
JOH 5:35 He was the lighted and shining lamp; and for a while you were disposed to exult with joy at his light.
JOH 5:36 But I have a greater testimony than John's. For the works which my father hath given me to perform; these very works, which I do, testify concerning me, that the father hath sent me.
JOH 5:37 Indeed the father who hath sent me hath himself given a testimony concerning me. You have neither heard his voice at any time, nor seen a visible appearance of him
JOH 5:38 Indeed you have not his word abiding in you, because you do not believe him whom he hath sent.
JOH 5:39 You search the scriptures because you think you have by means of them everlasting life!  Now these are the very writings which testify concerning me;
JOH 5:40 yet you will not come to me that you may have life.
JOH 5:41 I do not receive glory from men.
JOH 5:42 But I know you that you have not the love of God in you.
JOH 5:43 I have come in my father's name and you do not receive me; if another come in his own name, him you will receive.
JOH 5:44 How can you believe while you court honour one from another, and do not seek the glory which is from God alone?
JOH 5:45 Do not imagine that I will accuse you to the father. There is one who is your accuser, namely, Moses, in whom you have trusted.
JOH 5:46 For if you had believed Moses, you would believe me; for he hath written concerning me.
JOH 5:47 Now if you have not believed his writings, how will you believe my words?
JOH 6:1 After these things Jesus went away. On the coast of the sea, that of Galilee, that of Tiberias,
JOH 6:2 he was also followed by a great multitude, because they saw the miracles which he performed on the diseased.
JOH 6:3 And Jesus went up to the mountain, and sat down there with his disciples.
JOH 6:4 Now the passover, the festival of the Jews, was nigh.
JOH 6:5 Jesus therefore lifting up his eyes, and seeing a great multitude coming to him, saith to Philip, Whence can we buy bread to feed these people.
JOH 6:6 Now this he said to try him, for he himself knew what he was going to do.
JOH 6:7 Philip answered him, Two hundred deniars would not purchase bread enough for every one of them to take a morsel.
JOH 6:8 One of his disciples, namely Andrew, the brother of Simon Peter, saith to him,
JOH 6:9 There is a lad here who hath five barley loaves, and two small fishes; but what are they among so many?
JOH 6:10 Then Jesus said, Cause the men to arrange themselves on the ground. Now there was much grass in the place. The men therefore, to the number of about five thousand, arranged themselves on the ground.
JOH 6:11 Then Jesus took the loaves and having given thanks, distributed to the disciples; and the disciples distributed to them who were on the ground; and in like manner of the fishes, as much as they chose.
JOH 6:12 And when they were satisfied, he saith to his disciples, Gather up the fragments which remain, that nothing may be lost.
JOH 6:13 So they gathered, and with the fragments, which the people after eating had left of the five barley loaves, they filled twelve panniers.
JOH 6:14 When these men saw the miracle which Jesus had done, they said, This is certainly the prophet"He who is coming into the world.
JOH 6:15 Jesus therefore knowing that they were about to come and take him by force to make him king, withdrew again to the mountain himself alone.
JOH 6:16 And as the evening was coming on, his disciples went down to the sea,
JOH 6:17 and having gone on board the vessel, they coasted along towards Capernaum. Darkness had now come on and Jesus had not come to them,
JOH 6:18 and the sea ran high by reason of the wind, which blew hard.
JOH 6:19 So when they had rowed about twenty five or thirty furlongs, they saw Jesus walking on the sea, and approaching the vessel; and they were terrified.
JOH 6:20 Whereupon he said to them, It is I; be not afraid.
JOH 6:21 They wished therefore to take him into the vessel; and immediately the vessel was at the land to which they were going.
JOH 6:22 On the day following the people who continued on the sea side, having seen that there was no vessel there besides that one in which his disciples had embarked, and that Jesus did not go on board the vessel with his disciples, but that his disciples had gone away alone.
JOH 6:23 Other vessels however came from Tiberias, nigh to the place where they had eaten bread after the Lord gave thanks
JOH 6:24 when the people therefore saw that neither Jesus nor his disciples were there, they went on board these vessels and came to Capernaum, seeking Jesus;
JOH 6:25 and having found him on that coast of the sea, they said to him Rabbi, when didst thou come hither?
JOH 6:26 Jesus in reply said to them, Verily, verily I say to you, You seek me; not because you have seen miracles; but because you have eaten of the loaves and were satisfied.
JOH 6:27 Labour not to procure the food which perisheth, but the food which endureth for an everlasting life, which the son of man will give you; for him the Father, namely God, hath sealed.
JOH 6:28 Thereupon they said to him, What must we do that we may work the works of God?
JOH 6:29 Jesus answered and said to them, This is the work of God that you believe in him whom he hath sent.
JOH 6:30 Then they said to him, What miracle dost thou perform that we may see and believe in thee? What workest thou?
JOH 6:31 Our fathers ate manna in the wilderness, as it is written, "He gave them bread from heaven to eat."
JOH 6:32 Upon this Jesus said to them, Verily, verily I say to you, Moses did not give you the bread from heaven; but my Father giveth you the true bread of heaven:
JOH 6:33 for the bread of God is that which cometh down from heaven and giveth life to the world.
JOH 6:34 Thereupon they said to him, Master, give us evermore that bread.
JOH 6:35 Then Jesus said to them, I am the bread of that life. He who cometh to me, shall never hunger; and he who believeth in me, shall never thirst.
JOH 6:36 But I have told you that though you have seen me, you do not believe.
JOH 6:37 All that the Father giveth me, will come to me. And him who cometh to me I will not reject.
JOH 6:38 For I am come down from heaven not to do mine own will, but the will of him who sent me.
JOH 6:39 And this is the will of the Father, who sent me that of all which he hath given me, I should lose nothing, but raise it up at the last day.
JOH 6:40 And this is the will of him who sent me, that every one who seeth the son, and believeth in him, may have an everlasting life, and that I raise him up at the last day.
JOH 6:41 The Jews then murmured at him, because he said, I am the bread which came down from heaven,
JOH 6:42 and they said, Is not this Jesus, the son of Joseph, whose father and mother we know? How then doth he say, I came down from heaven?
JOH 6:43 Therefore Jesus answered and said to them, Murmur not among yourselves.
JOH 6:44 No one can come to me, unless the Father, who hath sent me, draw him. And as for me, I will raise him up at the last day.
JOH 6:45 It is written in the prophets, They shall be all taught of God. Every one therefore who hath heard and learned from the Father, cometh to me.
JOH 6:46 Not that any one hath seen the Father, save he only who is from God. He hath seen the Father.
JOH 6:47 Verily, verily, I say to you, He who believeth in me, hath an everlasting life.
JOH 6:48 I am the bread of that life.
JOH 6:49 Your fathers ate the manna in the wilderness, and died.
JOH 6:50 Such is the bread which cometh down from heaven, that whoever shall eat of it shall not die.
JOH 6:51 I am that living bread which came down from heaven. If any one eat of this bread he shall live forever. Now the bread which I will give is this flesh of mine, which I will give for the life of the world.
JOH 6:52 Upon this the Jews debated among themselves, saying, How can this man give us his flesh to eat?
JOH 6:53 Therefore Jesus said to them, Verily, verily, I say to you, Unless you eat the flesh of the son of man, and drink his blood, you have no life in you.
JOH 6:54 He who eateth my flesh and drinketh my blood, hath an everlasting life, and I will raise him up at the last day.
JOH 6:55 For this flesh of mine is food indeed; and this blood of mine is indeed drink.
JOH 6:56 He who eateth my flesh, and drinketh my blood, abideth in me and I in him.
JOH 6:57 As the living Father hath sent me, and I live by the Father; so he. who eateth me, even he will live by me.
JOH 6:58 This is the bread which is come down from heaven. Not as your fathers ate the manna and died. He who eateth this bread shall live forever.
JOH 6:59 These things he said in a public assembly, as he was teaching at Capernaum.
JOH 6:60 Many of his disciples, therefore, when they heard them, said, This is harsh doctrine, who can hearken to it?
JOH 6:61 Thereupon Jesus knowing in himself that his disciples were murmuring at this, he said to them, Doth this offend you?
JOH 6:62 What if you see the son of man ascending up where he was before.
JOH 6:63 It is the spirit which giveth life, the flesh profiteth nothing. The words which I speak to you are spirit, they are life.
JOH 6:64 But there are some of you who do not believe; [for Jesus knew from the beginning who they are who do not believe, and who it is that will deliver him up]
JOH 6:65 and [said he] for this cause I said to you, that none can come to me unless it be given him by my Father.
JOH 6:66 From this time many of his disciples withdrew and walked no more with him,
JOH 6:67 therefore Jesus said to the twelve, Have you also a mind to go away?
JOH 6:68 Whereupon Simon Peter answered him, Master, to whom shall we go? Thou hast the words of an everlasting life,
JOH 6:69 and we believe and know that thou art the Christ, the Son of the living God.
JOH 6:70 Jesus answered them, Have I not chosen you twelve? Yet one of you is a spy.
JOH 6:71 Now he spake of Judas Iscariot, son of Simon; for he thought of delivering him up though he was one of the twelve.
JOH 7:1 After this Jesus travelled about in Galilee, for he did not chuse to walk in Judea, because the Jews sought to kill him.
JOH 7:2 Now the Jews festival of tabernacles was near,
JOH 7:3 therefore his brethren said to him, Depart hence and go to Judea that thy disciples may see the works which thou dost.
JOH 7:4 For one who seeketh to be known publicly, doth any thing in secret. Since thou dost these things, shew thyself to the world.
JOH 7:5 [For even his brethren did not believe in him.]
JOH 7:6 Thereupon Jesus saith to them, My time is not yet come; but your time is always ready.
JOH 7:7 The world cannot hate you: but it hateth me, because I testify concerning it that its works are evil.
JOH 7:8 Go ye up to this festival. I am not yet going up to this festival, because my time is not yet fully come.
JOH 7:9 And having said this, he continued in Galilee.
JOH 7:10 But when his brethren were gone up, then he also went up to the festival, not publicly, but in a private manner.
JOH 7:11 The Jews therefore sought him at the festival, and said, Where is he?
JOH 7:12 And there was much private dispute concerning him, among the people; for some said he is a good man; and others said, No; but he seduceth the people.
JOH 7:13 No one, however, spoke openly of him, for fear of the Jews.
JOH 7:14 But about the middle of the festival Jesus went up to the temple and taught.
JOH 7:15 And the Jews expressed astonishment, saying, How came this man acquainted with letters, having never had an education?
JOH 7:16 Jesus addressing them, said, This doctrine of mine is not mine, but his, who sent me.
JOH 7:17 If any man is disposed to do his will, he will know in respect to this doctrine, whether it is of God, or whether I speak from myself.
JOH 7:18 He who speaketh from himself, seeketh his own glory; but he who seeketh the glory of him who sent him, is true, and in him there is no falsehood.
JOH 7:19 Did not Moses give you the law? Yet none of you observeth the law. Why do you seek to kill me?
JOH 7:20 The people answered and said, Thou art possessed by a demon; Who seeketh to kill thee?
JOH 7:21 In reply to which Jesus said to them, I did one work and you all express wonder at it.
JOH 7:22 Moses gave you the law of circumcision [not that it is from Moses, but from the patriarchs,] and you circumcise a man on a sabbath.
JOH 7:23 If a person receiveth circumcision on a sabbath, that the law of Moses may not be broken, are you angry with me because on a sabbath I cured a man whose whole body was diseased.
JOH 7:24 Judge not according to appearance, but judge righteous judgment.
JOH 7:25 Upon this some of the inhabitants of Jerusalem said, Is not this he whom they seek to kill?
JOH 7:26 Yet behold he speaketh boldly, and they say nothing to him. Perhaps the rulers know indeed that he is really the Christ!
JOH 7:27 But we know whence this man is; but as for the Christ, when he cometh, no one knoweth whence he is.
JOH 7:28 Hereupon, Jesus, as he was teaching in the temple, cried and said, Do you indeed both know me, and know whence I am? I have not come of myself. But he who hath sent me is true, Him you do not know;
JOH 7:29 but I know him, because I am immediately from him, and he sent me.
JOH 7:30 Upon this they sought to seize him, but no one laid his hand on him, because his hour was not yet come.
JOH 7:31 Many of the people, however, believed in him and said, Will the Christ, when he cometh, do greater miracles than those which this man hath done?
JOH 7:32 The Pharisees heard of the people's whispering such things concerning him; and the Pharisees and the chief priests sent officers to apprehend him.
JOH 7:33 Jesus therefore said to them, Yet a little while I am with you. When I go away to him who sent me,
JOH 7:34 you will seek me but will not find me; and where I am you cannot come.
JOH 7:35 Upon this the Jews said among themselves, Whither is he going, that we shall not find him? Is he going to the dispersed among the Greeks, to teach the Greeks?
JOH 7:36 What is the meaning of this saying of his, "You will seek me and will not find me, and where I am going you cannot come?"
JOH 7:37 It being now the last the great day of the festival, Jesus stood and cried, saying, If any one thirst, let him come to me and drink.
JOH 7:38 He who believeth in me; as the scripture hath said, Out of his belly will flow streams of living water.
JOH 7:39 Now this he said in reference to the spirit which they who believed in him were to receive; for a holy spirit was not yet received, because Jesus was not yet glorified.
JOH 7:40 Hereupon many of the people, when they heard this saying, said, This is certainly the prophet,
JOH 7:41 Others said, This is the Christ. But others said', Doth the Christ come out of Galilee?
JOH 7:42 Hath not the scripture said that the Christ cometh of the seed of David and from Bethlehem, the town whence David was?
JOH 7:43 So there was a division among the people on his account.
JOH 7:44 And some of them had a mind to seize him, but no one laid hands on him.
JOH 7:45 The officers therefore went to the chief priests and the Pharisees, who said to them, Why have you not brought him?
JOH 7:46 The officers replied, Never did a man speak like this man.
JOH 7:47 Thereupon the Pharisees answered them, Are you also seduced?
JOH 7:48 Hath any of the chief priests believed in him, or any of the Pharisees?
JOH 7:49 But this multitude, which know not the law, are accursed.
JOH 7:50 Nicodemus, he who came to Jesus by night, and who was one of them, said to them,
JOH 7:51 Doth our law condemn the man without hearing him, and knowing what he hath done?
JOH 7:52 In reply to which, they said to him, Art thou also of Galilee? Search and see that a prophet of Galilee hath not been raised up.
JOH 7:53 Then every one went to his own home.
JOH 8:1 As for Jesus, he went to the mount of olives,
JOH 8:2 and early in the morning he came, again to the temple, and all the people came to him. And when he had taken a seat, and was teaching them,
JOH 8:3 the Scribes and the Pharisees bring to him a woman caught in adultery; and, having set her in the midst,
JOH 8:4 they say to him, Teacher, this woman was caught in the very act of adultery.
JOH 8:5 Now Moses in the law hath commanded us that such be stoned. What therefore .dost thou say?
JOH 8:6 This they said to try him, that they might have matter for accusing him. Thereupon Jesus stooped down and wrote with his finger on the ground.
JOH 8:7 And as they continued asking him, he raised himself up, and said to them, Let him among you who is without sin throw the first stone at her.
JOH 8:8 Then he stooped down again and wrote on the ground.
JOH 8:9 But they who heard, being convicted by their own conscience, went out, one by one, the eldest first, even to the last, and Jesus was left alone, and the woman standing in the midst.
JOH 8:10 When Jesus raised himself up, and saw none but the woman, he said to her, Woman, where are thine accusers? Hath no one passed sentence on thee?
JOH 8:11 And she said, No one, Sir. Then Jesus said to her, Neither do I pass sentence on thee. Go and sin no more.
JOH 8:12 Then Jesus spake to them again, saying, I am the light of the world. He who floweth me will not walk in darkness, but shall have the light of life.
JOH 8:13 Hereupon the Pharisees said to him, Thou testifiest concerning thyself. This testimony of thine is not to be regarded.
JOH 8:14 Jesus answered and said to them, Though I testify concerning myself, my testimony is to be regarded, because I know whence I came, and whither I am going. But as for you, you do not know whence I come, nor whither I am going.
JOH 8:15 You judge according to the flesh, I judge no one.
JOH 8:16 Yet if I judge, my judgment is true, because I am not alone, but I and the Father who sent me.
JOH 8:17 Now it is written in your law, that the testimony of two men is true.
JOH 8:18 I am one testifying concerning myself, and the Father who sent me testifieth concerning me.
JOH 8:19 Thereupon they said, Where is thy Father? Jesus replied, You neither know me nor my Father. If you had known me, you would have known my Father also.
JOH 8:20 These things Jesus spake in the treasury, as he was teaching in the temple; yet no one laid hands on him. Because his hour was not yet come;
JOH 8:21 therefore Jesus said to them again, I am. going away, and you will seek me and die in your sins. Whither I go you cannot come.
JOH 8:22 Upon this, the Jews said, Will he kill himself, that he saith, Whither I go you cannot come?
JOH 8:23 Then he said to them, You are from below; I am from above. You are of this world; I am not of this world;
JOH 8:24 therefore I said to you, You will die in your sins: for if you do not believe that I am, you will die in your sins.
JOH 8:25 Upon this they said to him, Who art thou? And Jesus said to them, I am what I told you at the beginning,
JOH 8:26 and am now telling you. I have many things to speak and to judge respecting you. He indeed who sent me is true, and I speak to the world what I have heard from him.
JOH 8:27 They did not know that he was speaking to them of the Father;
JOH 8:28 therefore Jesus said to them, When you have lifted up the son of man, then you will know who I am; and that I do nothing of myself; but speak these things as my Father taught me.
JOH 8:29 He indeed who sent me is with me. The Father hath not left me alone, because I do always the things which are pleasing to him.
JOH 8:30 While he was thus speaking many believed in him,
JOH 8:31 therefore to the Jews who believed in him Jesus said, If you continue steadily in this doctrine of mine, you are my disciples indeed;
JOH 8:32 and you will know the truth, and the truth will make you free.
JOH 8:33 Some answered him, We are the seed of Abraham, and have never been in bondage to any one: how then dost thou say, Ye shall be made free.
JOH 8:34 To them Jesus replied, Verily, verily, I say to you, Whosoever committeth sin is the slave of sin.
JOH 8:35 Now the slave abideth not in the family forever; but the son abideth forever.
JOH 8:36 If therefore the son shall make you free, you will be free indeed.
JOH 8:37 I know that you are Abraham's seed; but you seek to kill me, because my word continueth not in you.
JOH 8:38 What I have seen with my Father, I speak; and what you have seen with your father you do.
JOH 8:39 They answered and said to him, Abraham is our father. Jesus saith to them, If ye were the children of Abraham, you would do the works of Abraham.
JOH 8:40 But now you seek to kill me, a man who told you the truth which I heard from God. Abraham did not do this.
JOH 8:41 You do the works of your father. Hereupon they said to him, We were not born of fornication; we have one father, namely, God.
JOH 8:42 Then Jesus said to them, If God were your father, you would love me; for I proceed and do come from God. For I have not come of myself, but he sent me.
JOH 8:43 Why do ye not understand what I say? It is because you cannot bear this doctrine of mine.
JOH 8:44 You are of your father the devil, and bent upon executing the desires of your father. He was a manslayer from the beginning, and did .not abide in the truth. Because there is no truth in him, when he speaketh falsehood he speaketh what is. natural to him, for he is a liar, and the father  of it.
JOH 8:45 But as for me, because I speak the truth, you do not believe me.
JOH 8:46 Which of you convicteth me of sin? Now, if I speak truth, why do you not believe me?
JOH 8:47 He who is of God doth, for this cause, hear the words of God: you do not hearken, because you are not of God.
JOH 8:48 Thereupon the Jews answered, and said to him, Are we not right in saying, Thou art a Samaritan, and possessed by a demon?
JOH 8:49 Jesus replied, I am not possessed by a demon, but I honour my Father, and you dishonour me.
JOH 8:50 As for me, I seek not mine own glory. There is one who seeketh [it] and judgeth.
JOH 8:51 Verily, verily, I say to you, If any one will keep this doctrine of mine, he shall never see death.
JOH 8:52 Thereupon the Jews said to him, Now we know that thou art possessed by a demon. Abraham is dead and the prophets; yet thou sayest, I any one keep this doctrine of mine, he shall never taste death.
JOH 8:53 Art thou greater than our father Abraham who died? The prophets also died. Whom dost thou make thyself?
JOH 8:54 Jesus answered, If I glorify myself, this glory of mine is nothing. It is the Father who glorifieth me, of whom you say that he is your God.
JOH 8:55 Now you do not know him, but I know him; and if I should say, I do not know him, I would speak falsely like you. But I know him and keep his word.
JOH 8:56 Your father Abraham was transported with a desire to see this day of mine, and he saw it, and was made glad.
JOH 8:57 Upon this the Jews said to him, Thou art not yet fifty years old, and hast thou seen Abraham?
JOH 8:58 Jesus said to them, Verily, verily, I say to you, Before Abraham was, I am.
JOH 8:59 Upon this they took up stones to throw at him. But Jesus concealed himself and went out of the temple, passing through the midst of them, and thus withdrew.
JOH 9:1 And as he was passing along he saw a man who was blind from his birth,
JOH 9:2 whereupon his disciples asked him, saying, Rabbi, who sinned this man, or his parents, that he should be born blind?
JOH 9:3 Jesus answered, It was neither for any sin of this man, nor of his parents: but that the works of God may be manifested in him;
JOH 9:4 I must work the works of him who sent me, while it is day. Night is coming, when no one can work.
JOH 9:5 While I am in the world, I am the light of the world.
JOH 9:6 Having said this he spat on the ground, and made some clay with the spittle, and spread the clay on the blind man's eyes,
JOH 9:7 and said to him, Go, wash them at the pool of Siloam [the meaning, of which is Sent.] So he went and washed them and returned seeing.
JOH 9:8 Thereupon the neighbours, and they who had seen him before, when he was blind, said, Is not this he who used to sit begging?
JOH 9:9 Some said, It is he: and others said it is like him. He said, I am [the man.]
JOH 9:10 Then they said to him, How were thine eyes opened?
JOH 9:11 In reply to which he said, A man called Jesus made clay and anointed mine eyes, and said to me, Go to the pool of Siloam and wash them. So I went and washed them and got sight.
JOH 9:12 Then they said to him, Where is he? He saith, I do not know.
JOH 9:13 They brought to the Pharisees him who was formerly blind.
JOH 9:14 Now it was a sabbath when Jesus made the clay and opened his eyes.
JOH 9:15 Therefore the Pharisees asked him again, how he got sight. And he said to them, He put clay on mine eyes, and I washed them and see.
JOH 9:16 Thereupon some of the Pharisees said; That man is not from God, because he doth not keep the sabbath. Others said, How can a sinful man do such miracles? So there was a dissention among them.
JOH 9:17 They say to the blind man again, What sayest thou of him for opening thine eyes? He said, He is a prophet.
JOH 9:18 The Jews therefore did not believe in respect to him, that he had been blind and got sight, until they called the parents of him who had obtained sight,
JOH 9:19 and asked them saying, Is this your son who you say was born blind? How then doth he now see?
JOH 9:20 In answer to which his parents said, We know that this is our son, and that he was born blind.
JOH 9:21 But how he now seeth, we do not know: nor do we know who hath opened his eyes. He is of age; ask him; let him speak for himself.
JOH 9:22 This his parents said, because they were afraid of the Jews; for the Jews had now agreed that if any one acknowledged Jesus to be the Christ, he should be excommunicated.
JOH 9:23 For this cause his parents said, He is of age; ask him.
JOH 9:24 Then they called a second time the man who had been blind, and said to him, Give glory to God. We know that this man is a sinner.
JOH 9:25 Upon this he answered and said, If he be a sinner, I know not. One thing I know, that I was blind, and now I see.
JOH 9:26 Then they said to him again, What did he do to thee? How did he open thine eyes?
JOH 9:27 He answered them, I have told you already. Did you not hear? Why do you desire to hear it again? Have you indeed a mind to be his disciples?
JOH 9:28 Upon this they reviled him and said, Thou art a disciple of his; but as for us, we are disciples of Moses.
JOH 9:29 We know that God spake to Moses; but as for this man, we know not whence he is.
JOH 9:30 In reply to this the man said to them, Why; in this there is something marvellous, that you do not know whence he is, though he hath opened mine eyes.
JOH 9:31 Now we know that God hearkeneth not to sinners; but if any one be a worshipper of God, and do his will, to him he hearkeneth.
JOH 9:32 From the beginning of the world it was never heard that any one opened the eyes of one born blind.
JOH 9:33 If this man were not from God he could do nothing.
JOH 9:34 They answered and said to him, Thou wast altogether born in sin, and dost thou teach us? And they excommunicated him.
JOH 9:35 Jesus heard that they had excommunicated him; and having met with him he said to him, Dost thou believe in the son of God?
JOH 9:36 He answered and said, Who is he, Sir, that I may believe in him.
JOH 9:37 Jesus said to him, Thou indeed seest him, and it is he who is talking with thee.
JOH 9:38 Whereupon he said, Lord, I believe, and worshipped him.
JOH 9:39 Then Jesus said, I am come into this world for judgment that they who do not see may see, and that they who see may become blind;
JOH 9:40 and some of the Pharisees who were with him, when they heard this, said, Are we blind?
JOH 9:41 Jesus said to them, If you were blind, you would not have had sin; but now you say, We see; therefore your sin remaineth.
JOH 10:1 Verily, verily, I say to you, He who entereth not by the door into the fold of the sheep, but climbeth over some other way, is a thief and a robber:
JOH 10:2 but he who goeth in by the door is the shepherd of the sheep.
JOH 10:3 To him the doorkeeper openeth and the sheep hearken to his voice; and he calleth his own sheep by name, and leadeth them out.
JOH 10:4 And when he hath brought out his own sheep, he goeth before them and his sheep follow him because they know his voice.
JOH 10:5 They will not follow a stranger, but will flee from him, because they do not know the voice of strangers.
JOH 10:6 This parable Jesus spake to them, but they did not comprehend the meaning of what he said to them,
JOH 10:7 therefore Jesus said to them again, Verily, verily I say to you, I am the door of the sheep.
JOH 10:8 All that have come in my stead, are thieves and robbers: but the sheep did not hearken to them.
JOH 10:9 I am the door. If any enter in by me, it shall be safe, and shall go in and out, and find pasture.
JOH 10:10 The thief cometh only to steal and to kill and to destroy. I am come that the sheep may have life and that they may have it superabundantly.
JOH 10:11 I am the good shepherd. The good shepherd exposeth his life for the sheep.
JOH 10:12 But the hireling, who is not the shepherd, and to whom the sheep do not belong, when he seeth the wolf coming leaveth the sheep and fleeth; and the wolf seizeth some and scattereth the sheep.
JOH 10:13 The hireling fleeth because he is a hireling and careth not for the sheep.
JOH 10:14 I am the good shepherd and I know mine own sheep, and am known by them who are mine,
JOH 10:15 even as the father knoweth me, and I know the father; and I lay down my life for the sheep.
JOH 10:16 Now I have other sheep which are not of this fold. These also I must lead; they will hearken to my voice, and there shall be one flock and one shepherd.
JOH 10:17 On this account the father loveth me, because I lay down my life so that I may take it again.
JOH 10:18 No one forceth it from me; but I lay it down of myself. I have power to lay it down, and I have power to take it again. This commission I have received from my father.
JOH 10:19 Upon this there was another division among the Jews, on account of these sayings.
JOH 10:20 And many of them said, He is possessed by a demon, and is mad, Why do you. hearken to him?
JOH 10:21 Others said, These are not the words of a demoniac. Can a demon open the eyes of the blind?
JOH 10:22 When they were celebrating the dedication festival at Jerusalem, and it was stormy weather;
JOH 10:23 and Jesus was walking in the temple in Solomon's portico;
JOH 10:24 the Jews again came around him, and said to him, How long dost thou keep us in suspense? If thou art the Christ, tell us plainly:
JOH 10:25 Jesus answered them, I told you but you do not believe. The works which I do in my father's name these testify concerning me.
JOH 10:26 But you do not believe, for you are not of my sheep.
JOH 10:27 My sheep, as I told you, hearken to my voice and I know them, and they follow me:
JOH 10:28 and I give them everlasting life; and they shall never perish, nor shall any one wrest them out of my hand.
JOH 10:29 My father who gave them to me, is greater than all, and none is able to wrest them out of my father's hand.
JOH 10:30 I and my father are one.
JOH 10:31 Hereupon the Jews again took up stones to stone him.
JOH 10:32 Jesus addressed them, I have shewn you many good works from my father, for which of those works would you stone me?"
JOH 10:33 The Jews answered him saying, For a good work we are not about to stone thee, but for blasphemy, even because thou, being a man, makest thyself God.
JOH 10:34 Jesus answered them, Is it not written in your law "I said you are Gods."
JOH 10:35 If it stileth them gods to whom the word of God was addressed, [now the scripture cannot be set aside]
JOH 10:36 do you say of me, whom the father hath consecrated and sent into the world, "Thou blasphemest," because I said, I am the son of God?
JOH 10:37 If I do not the works of my father, believe me not.
JOH 10:38 But if I do; though you do not believe me, believe the works; that you may know and believe that the father is in me, and I in him.
JOH 10:39 Upon this they again sought to seize him. But he withdrew out of their hands,
JOH 10:40 and went again to the bank of the Jordan; to the place where John baptized at first, and abode there.
JOH 10:41 And many resorted to him and said, John indeed wrought no miracle; but all that John said respecting this man is true.
JOH 10:42 And many there believed in him.
JOH 11:1 Now one Lazarus, an inhabitant of Bethany, the town of Mary and her sister Martha, was sick.
JOH 11:2 It was this Mary who anointed the Lord with balsam, after wiping his feet with her hair, whose brother Lazarus was sick.
JOH 11:3 The sisters, therefore sent to Jesus, saying, Sir, He whom thou lovest is sick.
JOH 11:4 Upon hearing this, Jesus said, This sickness is not unto death, but for the glory of God, that by it the son of God may be glorified.
JOH 11:5 Therefore though Jesus loved Martha and her sister, and Lazarus,
JOH 11:6 yet when he heard that he was, sick, he then stayed two days in the place where he was.
JOH 11:7 And after that he saith to his disciples, Let us go again to Judea.
JOH 11:8 The disciples say to him, Rabbi, very lately the Jews sought to stone thee, and art thou going thither again?
JOH 11:9 Jesus answered, Are there not twelve hours in the day? If any one walketh in the day he stumbleth not, because he seeth the light of this world:
JOH 11:10 but if any one walk in the night he stumbleth because there is no light in him.
JOH 11:11 Thus he spake, and after that he saith to them, Our friend Lazarus is composed to rest; but I am going to wake him.
JOH 11:12 Thereupon his disciples said, Master, if he is composed to rest, he will recover.
JOH 11:13 Now Jesus spoke of his death; but they thought that he spoke of taking rest in sleep.
JOH 11:14 Therefore Jesus then told them plainly, Lazarus is dead.
JOH 11:15 And on your account that you may believe, I am glad that I was not there. But let us go to him.
JOH 11:16 Upon this Thomas, who is called Didymus, said to his fellow disciples, Let us also go that we may die with him.
JOH 11:17 So when Jesus came, he found that he had now been four days in the tomb.
JOH 11:18 Now Bethany was near Jerusalem, about fifteen furlongs off.
JOH 11:19 And many of the Jews had come to Martha and Mary, to comfort them on the death of their brother.
JOH 11:20 Therefore soon as Martha heard that Jesus is coming she went out to meet him; but Mary remained in the house.
JOH 11:21 Martha therefore said to Jesus, Master, if thou hadst been here my brother would not have died;
JOH 11:22 but still I know that whatever thou wilt ask of God, God will grant thee.
JOH 11:23 Jesus saith to her, Thy brother shall rise again.
JOH 11:24 Martha said to him, I know that he will rise again at the resurrection, at the last day.
JOH 11:25 Jesus said to her, I am the resurrection and the life; he who believeth in me, though he may die, shall live.
JOH 11:26 And none who liveth and believeth in me shall ever die. Believest thou this?
JOH 11:27 She saith to him, Yes, Lord, I believe that thou art the Christ, the Son of God, the one coming into the world.
JOH 11:28 And having said this, she went and called her sister Mary privately, saying, The teacher is come and calleth for thee.
JOH 11:29 As soon as she heard, she riseth instantly and goeth to him.
JOH 11:30 Now Jesus had not yet entered the village, but was at the place where Martha met him.
JOH 11:31 When the Jews therefore who were in the house, and comforting her, saw that Mary arose hastily and went out, they followed her, saying, She is going to the tomb to weep there.
JOH 11:32 When Mary then was come to the place where Jesus was, upon seeing him she fell at his feet, saying to him, Lord, if thou hadst been here my brother would not have died.
JOH 11:33 Therefore when Jesus saw her weeping, and the Jews also weeping who came with her, he restrained his spirit, and was troubled,
JOH 11:34 and said, Where have you laid him? They say to him, Master, Come and see.
JOH 11:35 Jesus wept.
JOH 11:36 Upon this the Jews said, Behold! how he loved him!
JOH 11:37 And some of them said, Could not this man who opened the eyes of the blind have prevented his death?
JOH 11:38 Then Jesus, again restraining himself, cometh to the tomb. Now it was a cave and a stone lay upon it.
JOH 11:39 Jesus saith, Remove the stone. Martha, the sister of him who was dead, saith to him, Master, by this time the smell is offensive; for this is the fourth day.
JOH 11:40 Jesus saith to her, Did I not tell thee, if thou wouldst believe thou shouldst see the glory of God?
JOH 11:41 Then they removed the stone from where the deceased lay. And Jesus lifted up his eyes and said, Father, I thank thee that thou hast heard me.
JOH 11:42 Now I know that thou hearest me always; but I have said this for the sake of the people standing around, that they may believe that thou hast sent me.
JOH 11:43 And having said this, he cried with a loud voice, Lazarus, Come forth.
JOH 11:44 Whereupon he who had been dead came forth, bound hand and foot with grave clothes, and his face was wrapped in a napkin. Jesus saith to them, Loose him and let him go.
JOH 11:45 Upon this many of the Jews who had come to Mary, when they saw what Jesus had done, believed in him.
JOH 11:46 But some of them went to the Pharisees and told them what Jesus had done.
JOH 11:47 Whereupon the chief priests and the Pharisees assembled the Sanhedrim, and said, What are we doing? Because this man doth many miracles,
JOH 11:48 if we let him go on thus, all will believe in him, and the Romans will come and destroy both this place and this nation of ours.
JOH 11:49 And one of them, namely, Caiaphas, being chief priest that year, said to them, Are you totally ignorant,
JOH 11:50 and do you not consider that it is better for us that one man die for the people than that the whole nation should perish.
JOH 11:51 Now this he said not merely of himself, but being high priest that year, he prophesied that Jesus was soon to die for that nation,
JOH 11:52 and not for that nation only, but that he might gather into one body the children of God who were scattered abroad.
JOH 11:53 From that day therefore they consulted together that they might put him to death.
JOH 11:54 For this reason Jesus walked no more publicly among the Jews, but went thence to the country near the wilderness, to a city called Ephraim, and continued there with his disciples.
JOH 11:55 Now the passover of the Jews was near, and many came up to Jerusalem from the country, before the passover, to purify themselves.
JOH 11:56 They therefore sought Jesus, and said to one another as they were standing in the temple, What think ye? Will he not come to this festival?
JOH 11:57 Now the chief priests and the Pharisees had issued an order, that if any one knew where he is, he should give information, that they might apprehend him.
JOH 12:1 Jesus therefore, six days before the passover, went to Bethany were Lazarus was, who had been dead, and whom he had raised from the dead.
JOH 12:2 And a supper was made for him there; and Martha waited, and Lazarus was one of them who were at table with him.
JOH 12:3 Mary then having taken a pound of the balsam of spikenard, unadulterated, very costly, anointed the feet of Jesus when she had wiped his feet with her hair. And the house was filled with the odour of the balsam.
JOH 12:4 Upon which one of the disciples, namely Judas Iscariot, son of Simon, who was about to deliver him up,
JOH 12:5 said, Why was not this balsam sold for three hundred deniars, and given to the poor?"
JOH 12:6 Now this he said, not because he cared for the poor, but because he was a thief and had the purse and carried off what was put into it.
JOH 12:7 Therefore Jesus said, Let her alone. She hath kept this for the day of preparing my body for burial,
JOH 12:8 for you have the poor always with you; but me you have not always.
JOH 12:9 Now a great number of the Jews knew that he was there, and had come, not on the account of Jesus only; but to see Lazarus, whom he had raised from the dead;
JOH 12:10 the chief priests therefore determined to put Lazarus also to death,
JOH 12:11 because on his account many of the Jews withdrew and believed in Jesus.
JOH 12:12 On the next day a great multitude who had come to the festival, hearing that Jesus is coming to Jerusalem,
JOH 12:13 took branches of palm trees and went out to meet him, and cried, Hosanna! Blessed he, who is coming in the name of the Lord! The king of Israel!
JOH 12:14 Now Jesus having found a young ass, was riding thereon, agreeably to what is written,
JOH 12:15 "Fear not, daughter, of Sion! behold thy king cometh mounted on an ass's colt."
JOH 12:16 These things his disciples did not understand at the time; but when Jesus was glorified, then they remembered that these things were written concerning him; and that they had done them for him.
JOH 12:17 Now because the multitude who were with him testified that he had called Lazarus from the tomb, and raised him, from the dead;
JOH 12:18 and on this account the multitude met him, because they heard that he had done this miracle,
JOH 12:19 therefore the Pharisees said among themselves, You see that you gain no advantage. Behold the world is gone after him.
JOH 12:20 Now among them who came up to worship at the festival, there were some Greeks.
JOH 12:21 These therefore came to Philip, who was of Bethsaida of Galilee, and asked him, saying, Sir, We wish to see Jesus.
JOH 12:22 Philip cometh and telleth Andrew. And Andrew and Philip tell Jesus.
JOH 12:23 Whereupon Jesus answered them, saying, The hour is come that the Son of man should be glorified.
JOH 12:24 Verily, verily I say to you, If the grain of wheat which falleth on the ground dieth not, it remaineth a single grain. But if it die, it bringeth forth much fruit.
JOH 12:25 He who loveth his life, will lose it: but he who slighteth his life in this world, shall keep it for an everlasting life.
JOH 12:26 If any one would wait upon me, let him follow me; and where I am, there shall this attendant of mine also be. And if any one wait upon me my Father will reward him.
JOH 12:27 Now is my soul troubled. What then? Shall I say, Father save me from this hour? But for this cause I came to this hour.
JOH 12:28 Father, glorify thy name. Thereupon a voice came from heaven, "I have glorified it, and I will glorify it again."
JOH 12:29 The multitude therefore who were standing by, when they heard it, said, it thundered. Others said, An angel hath spoken to him,
JOH 12:30 Jesus answered and said, This voice hath not come for my sake, but for yours.
JOH 12:31 Now is the judgment of this world. Now will the chieftain of this world be cast out.
JOH 12:32 As for me, when I am lifted up from the ground, I will draw all men to me.
JOH 12:33 [Now this he said, signifying the death he should soon die.]
JOH 12:34 The multitude answered him, We have heard out of the law that "The Christ remaineth forever." How then dost thou say, That the son of man must be lifted up? Who is this son of man?
JOH 12:35 Jesus therefore said to them, Yet a little while the light is with you. Walk while you have the light that the darkness may not overtake you; for he who walketh in darkness knoweth not where he is going.
JOH 12:36 while you have the light, believe in the light, that you may be children of light. Having said this, Jesus withdrew, and was concealed from them.
JOH 12:37 Now though he had performed so many miracles before them, they did not believe in him,
JOH 12:38 so that the word of the prophet Esaias was confirmed, which he spoke, Lord who hath believed our report, and to whom hath the arm of the Lord been revealed?
JOH 12:39 It was because they were not enabled to believe that in another place Esaias said,
JOH 12:40 He hath blinded their eyes, and stupified their hearts, so that they saw not with their eyes, nor understood with their heart, nor turned that I might heal them.
JOH 12:41 This Esaias said when he saw his glory and spake concerning him.
JOH 12:42 Nevertheless when several of the chief's believed in him, but on account of the Pharisees did not acknowledge it, that they might not be excommunicated,
JOH 12:43 [for they loved the praise of men, more than the praise of God]
JOH 12:44 therefore Jesus raised his voice and said, He who believeth in me, believeth not merely in me, but in him who sent me.
JOH 12:45 And he who beholdeth me, beholdeth him who sent me.
JOH 12:46 I being light am come into the world, that whoever believeth in me may not remain in darkness.
JOH 12:47 Now if any one hear my words and believe not; it is not I who condemn him; for I did not come to condemn the world, but to save the world.
JOH 12:48 He who slighteth me and receiveth not my words, hath that which condemneth him; the word which I have spoken, that will condemn him at the last day.
JOH 12:49 Because I have not spoken from myself, but the father who sent me hath himself given me a command what I should enjoin, and what I should speak,
JOH 12:50 and I know that his commandment is everlasting life, therefore what I speak, I speak just as the father directed me.
JOH 13:1 . Now before this festival of the passover, as Jesus knew that his time was come that he should remove from this world to the father, having loved his own who were in the world, he loved them to the last.
JOH 13:2 When they were at supper [the devil having already put it into the heart of Judas Iscariot son of Simon to deliver him up,]
JOH 13:3 Jesus knowing that the father hath given all things into his hands, and that he had come forth from God, and is going to God,
JOH 13:4 riseth from the supper and layeth aside his upper garments, and having taken a towel and girded himself,
JOH 13:5 he then poureth water into the basin and began to wash the feet of the disciples and wipe them with the towel, with which he was girded.
JOH 13:6 He cometh therefore to Simon Peter. Whereupon Peter saith to him, "Master, thou wash my feet?"!
JOH 13:7 Jesus answered and said to him, What I am doing thou dost not comprehend at present, but thou shalt know hereafter.
JOH 13:8 Peter saith to him, Thou shalt never wash my feet. Jesus answered him, Unless I wash thee thou hast no portion with me.
JOH 13:9 Simon Peter saith to him; Master, not my feet only, but also the hands and the head.
JOH 13:10 Jesus saith to him, He who hath bathed needeth only to wash the feet, the rest of the body being clean. Now you are clean, but not all,
JOH 13:11 [For he knew him who was delivering him up, therefore he said, You are not all clean.]
JOH 13:12 So when he had washed their feet and put on his garments, having again taken his place at table, he said to them, Consider what I have done to you.
JOH 13:13 You call me The teacher and the master; and you say right, for so I am.
JOH 13:14 If I then, the master and the teacher, have washed your feet, you ought to wash one another's feet;
JOH 13:15 for I have set you an example, that you may do as I have done to you.
JOH 13:16 Verily, verily I say to you, The servant is not greater than his master; nor is a missionary greater than he who sent him.
JOH 13:17 If you know these things, happy are you if you practise them.
JOH 13:18 I do not speak of you all. I know whom I have chosen. But that the scripture may be fulfilled, He Who is eating bread with me hath lifted up his heel against me.
JOH 13:19 This I tell you now before it happeneth, that when it cometh to pass you may believe me to be what I am.
JOH 13:20 Verily, verily I say to you, He who receiveth whomsoever I shall send, receiveth me; and he who receiveth me receiveth him who sent me.
JOH 13:21 Having said this, Jesus was troubled in spirit and testified and said, Verily, verily I say to you, that one of you is to deliver me up.
JOH 13:22 Upon this his disciples looked at one another, doubting of whom he spake.
JOH 13:23 Now one of the disciples, whom Jesus loved, was reclined at table next to Jesus.
JOH 13:24 Simon Peter therefore beckoned to him to ask who it might be of whom he spake.
JOH 13:25 Thereupon he, bending back his head to Jesus breast, saith to him, Master, who is it?
JOH 13:26 Jesus answereth, It is he to whom I will give this morsel after I have dipped it. Then, having dipped the morsel, he giveth it to Judas Iscariot, the son of Simon.
