JOH 13:27 And, after the morsel, Satan then entered into him. Therefore Jesus said to him, What thou dost, do quickly.
JOH 13:28 Now none of them at table knew for what purpose he said this to him.
JOH 13:29 For some thought, as Judas had the purse, that Jesus is saying to him, Buy what we have need of for the festival, or that he should give something to the poor.
JOH 13:30 He therefore, having received the morsel, went out immediately. Now it was night.
JOH 13:31 When he therefore was gone, Jesus saith, Now is the son of man glorified; and God is glorified by him.
JOH 13:32 If God be glorified by him, God will also glorify him in himself. Indeed without delay he will glorify him.
JOH 13:33 Children, yet a little while I am with you. You will seek me, and as I said to the Jews, whither I am going yon cannot come, so I now say to you.
JOH 13:34 A new commandment I give you, that you love one another. As I have loved you, that you also love one another.
JOH 13:35 By this all men will know that you are my disciples, if you exercise mutual love.
JOH 13:36 Simon Peter saith to him, Master, whither art thou going? Jesus answered him, Whither I am going thou canst not follow me now; but here after thou wilt follow me.
JOH 13:37 Peter saith to him, Master, Why can not I follow thee now? I will lay down my life for thee.
JOH 13:38 Jesus answered him, Thou wilt lay down thy life for me! Verily, verily, I say to thee, A cock will not crow till thou hast thrice denied me.
JOH 14:1 Let not your hearts be troubled. Trust in God: trust also in me.
JOH 14:2 In my Father's house there are many mansions. If there were not, would I have said to you, I am going to prepare a place for you?
JOH 14:3 Now when I have gone and prepared a place for you, I will come again and take you to myself, that where I am you may be also.
JOH 14:4 Now you know whither I am going and you know the way;
JOH 14:5 Thomas saith to him, Master, We do not know whither thou art going, how then can we know the way?
JOH 14:6 Jesus saith to him, I am the way and the truth and the life. No one cometh to the father but by me.
JOH 14:7 Had you known me, you would have known my Father also. But hence forth you know him and have seen him.
JOH 14:8 Philip saith to him, Master shew us the Father, and it sufficeth.
JOH 14:9 Jesus saith to him, Am I so long a time with you, and hast thou not known me, Philip? He who hath seen me hath seen the Father: how then sayest thou, Shew us the Father?
JOH 14:10 Dost thou not believe that I am in the Father, and the Father in me? The words which I speak to you, I do not speak from myself. And it is the Father himself abiding in me who doth the works.
JOH 14:11 Believe me that I am in the Father and that the Father is in me. At least believe me on account of the works themselves.
JOH 14:12 Verily, verily, I say to you, He who believeth in me, even he shall do the works which I do; nay, works greater than these he shall do, because I am going to my Father,
JOH 14:13 and whatever you ask in my name, that I will do. That the Father may be glorified in the Son,
JOH 14:14 if you ask any thing in my name, I will do it.
JOH 14:15 If you love me keep my commandments,
JOH 14:16 and I will ask the Father and he will give you another monitor, that he may continue with you forever,
JOH 14:17 even the spirit of truth which the world cannot receive because it neither seeth him nor knoweth him. But you know him, because he abideth with you and will be in you.
JOH 14:18 I will not leave you orphans. I am coming to you.
JOH 14:19 Yet a little while and the world seeth me no more; but you see me. Because I live therefore you shall live.
JOH 14:20 In that day you will know that I am in my Father, and you in me, and I in you.
JOH 14:21 He who hath my commandments and keepeth them; he. it is who loveth me. And he who loveth me will be loved by my Father, and I will love him and manifest myself to him.
JOH 14:22 Judas [not the Iscariot] saith to him, Master, How is it that thou wilt manifest thyself to us, and not to the world?"
JOH 14:23 Jesus in reply, said to him, If any one love me, he will keep my word and my Father will love him; and we will come to him and make an abode with him.
JOH 14:24 He who doth not love me, doth not keep my words. Now the word which you hear is not mine only, but the Fathers who sent me.
JOH 14:25 These things I have spoken to you, while I remain with you.
JOH 14:26 But the Monitor the Holy Spirit which the Father will send in my name, he will teach you all things and bring to your remembrance all that I have said to you.
JOH 14:27 Peace I leave with you. This peace of mine I give you. It is not as the world giveth that I give to you. Let not your heart be troubled nor dismayed.
JOH 14:28 You have heard me say to you, I am going away and I am coming to you. If you love me, you would rejoice because I said, I am going to the Father: for my Father is greater than I.
JOH 14:29 Now I have told you before it come to pass, that when it is come to pass you may believe.
JOH 14:30 I will not discourse much more with you, for the; chieftain of this world is coming, and hath nothing to do with me;
JOH 14:31 save only that the world may know that I love the Father and do as he commanded me. Arise; let us go hence.
JOH 15:1 I am the true vine, and my Father is the vine dresser.
JOH 15:2 Every branch in me which beareth not fruit, he loppeth off; and every branch which beareth fruit he cleaneth to make it more fruitful.
JOH 15:3 Now you are clean through the word which I have spoken to you.
JOH 15:4 Abide in me, and I [will abide] in you. As the branch cannot bear fruit of itself unless it abide in the vine; so neither can you unless you continue in me.
JOH 15:5 I am the vine; you are the branches. He who continueth in me and I in him he it is who beareth much fruit. Because, separated from me, you can bear nothing:
JOH 15:6 if any one continueth not in me he is thrown away as the branch is when it is withered. Such indeed are gathered and thrown into the fire and burned.
JOH 15:7 If you continue in me, and my words continue in you, ask what you will and it will be done for you:
JOH 15:8 by this my Father is glorified. That you may bear much fruit, you must be my disciples.
JOH 15:9 As the Father hath loved me, so I have loved you. Continue ye in my love.
JOH 15:10 If you keep my commandments, you shall continue in my love; as I have kept my Father's commandments and continue in his love.
JOH 15:11 These things I have spoken to you that my joy may continue, and that your joy may be complete.
JOH 15:12 This is my commandment, that you love one another as I have loved you.
JOH 15:13 No one hath greater love than this, that he would lay down his life for his friends.
JOH 15:14 You are my friends, if you do what I command you.
JOH 15:15 I no longer call you servants; because the servant doth not know what his master doth. But I have called you friends, because I have made known to you all that I heard from my Father.
JOH 15:16 It was not you who chose me; but it was I who chose you, and placed you that you may go forth bearing fruit, and that your fruit may continue, that the Father may give you whatever you ask of him in my name.
JOH 15:17 These things I command you that you may love one another.
JOH 15:18 If the world hate you, consider that it hated me before you.
JOH 15:19 If ye were of the world, the world would love its own. Now because you are not of the world, but I have chosen you out of the world, therefore the world hateth you.
JOH 15:20 Remember the word which I spake to you. The servant is not greater than his master. If they persecuted me, they will also persecute you. If they have kept my word, they will also keep yours.
JOH 15:21 But all these things they will do to you on account of my name, because they do not know him who sent me.
JOH 15:22 If I had not come and spoken to them, they would not have had sin; but now they have no excuse for their sin.
JOH 15:23 He who hateth me, hateth my Father also.
JOH 15:24 If I had not done among them works which no other did, they would not have had sin: but now, though they have seen, they have hated both me and my Father.
JOH 15:25 But by this is fulfilled the word which is written in their law, They hated me without cause.
JOH 15:26 Now when the monitor whom I Will send to you from the Father, is come; the spirit of truth who proceedeth from the Father, he will testify concerning me.
JOH 15:27 And as for you, bear ye witness also, because you have been with me from the beginning.
JOH 16:1 These things I have spoken to you that you may not be stumbled.
JOH 16:2 They will excommunicate you. Indeed a time is coming, when whosoever killeth you will think he doth an act of religious worship to God.
JOH 16:3 And these things they will do to you because they know neither the Father nor me.
JOH 16:4 But I have spoken these things to you, that, when that time cometh, you may remember that I mentioned them to you. I did not tell you them from the beginning, because I was with you.
JOH 16:5 But now I am going to him who sent me, and none of you asketh me, Whither art thou going.
JOH 16:6 But because I have told you these things, sorrow hath filled your hearts.
JOH 16:7 But, I tell you this truth, it is to your advantage that I go away: for if I do not go, the monitor will not come to you; but when I go I will send him to you.
JOH 16:8 And when he is come, he will convince the world in respect to sin, and in respect to righteousness, and in respect to judgment
JOH 16:9 in respect to sin, because they do not believe in me;
JOH 16:10 and in respect to righteousness because I go to my Father and you see me no more;
JOH 16:11 and in respect to judgment, because the prince of this world is judged.
JOH 16:12 I have still many things to say to you, but you cannot bear them now.
JOH 16:13 But when he the spirit of truth, is come, he will lead you into all the truth; for he will not speak from himself, but will speak whatsoever he shall have heard, and will explain to you the train of events.
JOH 16:14 He will glorify me, for he will receive of mine, and communicate to you.
JOH 16:15 All that the Father hath is mine; therefore I said, He will receive of mine, and communicate to you.
JOH 16:16 Yet a little while and you do not see me; and again a little while and you shall see me, because I am going to the Father.
JOH 16:17 Upon this some of his disciples said to one another, What is this which he saith to us, "A little while and you do not see me; and again a little while and you shall see me;" and, "because I am going to the Father."
JOH 16:18 They said therefore, What is this little while of which he speaketh? We do not comprehend what he saith.
JOH 16:19 As Jesus knew that they were desirous to ask him, therefore he said to them, Do ye inquire among yourselves concerning this, because I said, A little while, and you do not see me; and again a little while and you shall see me?
JOH 16:20 Verily, verily, I say to you, "You will weep and mourn; but the world will rejoice. You will be sorrowful; but your sorrow will be turned into joy.
JOH 16:21 A woman in travail hath sorrow, because her time is come; but when the child is born, she no more remembereth her anguish, for joy that a man is born into the world.
JOH 16:22 So you at present are in grief; but I will see you again and your heart will be made joyful; and that joy of yours no one shall take from you.
JOH 16:23 Now in that day you will not ask me any thing. Verily, verily, I say to you, whatever you shall ask of the Father in my name, he will give you.
JOH 16:24 Hitherto you have asked nothing in my name. Ask and ye shall receive, that your joy may be complete.
JOH 16:25 These things I have spoken to you in parables. But a time is coming when I will no more speak to you in parables, but with plainness of speech tell you respecting the Father.
JOH 16:26 In that day you will ask in my name, and I do not say to you that I will ask the Father for you;
JOH 16:27 for the Father himself loveth you, because you have loved me and have believed that I came from God.
JOH 16:28 I came forth from the Father and am come into the world. Again I leave the world and am going to the Father.
JOH 16:29 His disciples say to him, Behold now thou speakest plainly and usest no parable.
JOH 16:30 Now we know that thou knowest all things, and hast no need that any should ask thee questions. By this we believe that thou camest forth from God.
JOH 16:31 Jesus answered them, Do you now believe?
JOH 16:32 Behold the time is coming, indeed is now come, when you will be scattered every one to his own, and you will leave me alone; yet I am not alone, because the Father is with me.
JOH 16:33 These things I have spoken to you, that you may have peace in me. In this world you will have trouble; but take courage: I have overcome the world.
JOH 17:1 Having spoken this, Jesus raised his eyes to heaven, and said, Father the hour is come. Glorify thy son, that thy son may glorify thee;
JOH 17:2 that, as thou hast given him power over all flesh, he may, according to all that thou hast given him, give to these everlasting life.
JOH 17:3 Now this is the life everlasting that they may know thee the only true God, and Jesus Christ whom thou hast sent.
JOH 17:4 I have glorified thee on the earth; I have finished the work which thou gavest me to do.
JOH 17:5 Now therefore, O Father, glorify thou me, with thyself, with that glory which I had in thy presence before the world was.
JOH 17:6 I have made known thy name to the men whom thou gavest me out of the world. They were thine, and thou gavest them to me, and they have kept thy word.
JOH 17:7 They now know that all those things which thou gavest me, come from thee.
JOH 17:8 Because I have given them the doctrines which thou gavest me, therefore they have received them, and know certainly that I came forth from thee; and believe that thou didst send me.
JOH 17:9 I pray for them. I am not praying for the world, but for them whom thou gavest me. Because they are thine,
JOH 17:10 and all things that are mine are thine, and thine are mine, and I am glorified by them,
JOH 17:11 and am no longer in this world, but these are in this world, and I am coming to thee: Holy Father, keep in thy name them whom thou gavest me that they may be one as we are.
JOH 17:12 While I was with them in the world, I kept them in thy name. Them whom thou gavest to me I have guarded, and none of them is lost, unless it be the son of perdition, so that the scripture is fulfilled;
JOH 17:13 but I am now coming to thee, and I speak these things in this world, that they may have their joy in me completed in them.
JOH 17:14 I have given them thy word, and the world hath hated them, because they are not of the world as I am not of the world.
JOH 17:15 I do not ask thee to remove them out of the world, but to preserve them from the evil one.
JOH 17:16 They are not of the world, as I am not of the world.
JOH 17:17 Consecrate them for thy truth. The Word which is thine, is truth.
JOH 17:18 As thou hast sent me into the world, so I have sent them into the world.
JOH 17:19 And for them I consecrate myself, that they may be consecrated for truth.
JOH 17:20 Now I do not pray for these only, but for those also who shall by means of their word believe in me,
JOH 17:21 that all may be one as thou, Father, art in me and I in thee, that they also may be one in us that the world may believe that thou hast sent me,
JOH 17:22 and that I have given them the glory which thou gavest me, that they may be one as we are one
JOH 17:23 I in them and thou in me, that they may be taken into union, and that the world may know that thou hast sent me, and hast loved them as thou hast loved me.
JOH 17:24 O Father, with respect to them whom thou hast given me, my desire is that where I am, they may be with me, that they may behold my glory which thou hast given me, because thou lovedst me before the foundation of the world.
JOH 17:25 Righteous Father, though the world did not know thee, I knew thee, and these have known that thou didst send me.
JOH 17:26 I have made known thy name to them, and I will make it known, that the love with which thou hast loved me may be in them and I in them.
JOH 18:1 When Jesus had thus spoken, he went out with his disciples to the bank of the brook Kedron, where there was a garden into which he went with his disciples.
JOH 18:2 Now Judas who delivered him up knew the place, because Jesus had often resorted thither with his disciples.
JOH 18:3 Judas, therefore, having got the band of soldiers and under officers from the chief priests, and Pharisees, cometh thither with lanterns and torches and weapons.
JOH 18:4 Thereupon Jesus, knowing all that were coming upon him, went forth and said to them, Whom do ye seek?
JOH 18:5 They answered him, Jesus the Nazarene. Jesus saith to them, I am he. Now Judas, who delivered him up, was with them.
JOH 18:6 As soon then as he said to them, I am he, they drew back and fell on the ground.
JOH 18:7 He therefore asked them again, Whom do you seek? And when they answered, Jesus the Nazarene;
JOH 18:8 Jesus replied, I have told you that I am he. If therefore you seek me, let these go their way;
JOH 18:9 that the word might be fulfilled which he spake, saying, "Of them whom thou gavest me I have lost none."
JOH 18:10 Upon this Simon Peter, having a sword, drew it and smote the servant of the chief priest, and cut oft" his right ear. Now the servant's name was. Malchus.
JOH 18:11 Thereupon Jesus said to Peter, Put up thy sword into the sheath. Must I not drink the cup which my Father hath given me?
JOH 18:12 Then the band of soldiers, and the commander and the under officers of the Jews, took Jesus and bound him,
JOH 18:13 and led him away, first to Annas, for he was the father in law of Caiaphas, who was chief priest that year.
JOH 18:14 Now it was Caiaphas who in council said to the Jews, It was expedient that one man die for the people.
JOH 18:15 Now Simon Peter, and another, disciple, followed Jesus. The other disciple was known to the chief priest, and went in with Jesus into the court of the chief priest,
JOH 18:16 but Peter stood at the gate without. The other disciple, therefore, who was known to the chief priest, went out and spoke to the portress, and brought in Peter.
JOH 18:17 Whereupon the girl, the portress, saith to Peter, Art not thou one of the disciples of that man? He saith, I am not.
JOH 18:18 Now the servants and the under officers stood by a fire which they had made, because it was cold, and were warming themselves; and Peter stood with them and was warming himself.
JOH 18:19 Meanwhile the chief priest asked Jesus concerning his disciples, and concerning his doctrine.
JOH 18:20 Jesus answered him, I spake openly to the world, I taught always in the synagogues and in the temple, to which the Jews always resort. And I have spoken nothing in secret.
JOH 18:21 Why askest thou me? Ask them who heard what I spoke to them. Behold they know what I have said.
JOH 18:22 Upon his saying this, one of the under officers who stood by, gave Jesus a slap on the cheek, saying, Answerest thou the high priest so?
JOH 18:23 Jesus answered him, If I have spoken disrespectfully, testify concerning the disrespect: but if properly; why smitest thou me?
JOH 18:24 Now Annas had sent him bound to Caiaphas the chief priest.
JOH 18:25 Still Simon Peter was standing warming himself; they therefore said to him, Art not thou also one of his disciples? He denied and said, I am not.
JOH 18:26 One of the servants of the chief priest, a kinsman of him whose ear Peter had cut off, said, Did I not see thee in the garden with him?
JOH 18:27 Thereupon Peter again denied, and immediately a cock crowed.
JOH 18:28 From Caiaphas they led Jesus away to the judgment hall of the Roman governor. Now it was early in the morning and they themselves did not go into the hall that they might not be polluted, but that they might eat the passover.
JOH 18:29 Pilate therefore came out to them and said, What accusation do you bring against this man?
JOH 18:30 They in reply, said to him, If he were not a malefactor we would not have delivered him over to thee.
JOH 18:31 Then Pilate said to them; Take him yourselves and judge him according to your law. Upon this the Jews said to him, It is not lawful for us to put any man to death,
JOH 18:32 so that the word was fulfilled which Jesus had spoken, signifying by what kind of death he was to die.
JOH 18:33 Then Pilate went again into the hall, and called Jesus and  said to him, Thou art the king of the Jews?
JOH 18:34 Jesus answered him, Dost thou say this from thyself? Or have others told it thee concerning me?
JOH 18:35 Pilate answered him, Am I a Jew? Thine own nation, even the chief priests, have delivered thee up to me. What hast thou done?
JOH 18:36 Jesus answered, My kingdom is not of this world. If my kingdom were of this world, my attendants would have fought to prevent my being delivered up to the Jews. But now my kingdom is not of this world.
JOH 18:37 Thereupon Pilate said to him, Thou art a king then? Jesus answered, It is as thou sayest, I am a king. For this I was born, and for this I came into the world, to bear testimony for the truth. Every one who is of the truth hearkeneth to my voice.
JOH 18:38 Pilate saith to him, What is truth? And having said this, he went out again to the Jews, and saith to them, I find no fault in him.
JOH 18:39 Now you have a custom that I should release one to you at the passover. Is it your will therefore that I release to you the king of the Jews?
JOH 18:40 Upon this they all cried out again, saying, Not this man, but Barabbas. Now this Barabbas was a robber.
JOH 19:1 Then Pilate took Jesus and scourged him,
JOH 19:2 and the soldiers having platted a crown of thorns, put it on his head and threw around him a purple robe,
JOH 19:3 and said, Hail! king of the Jews! When they gave him slaps on the cheek.
JOH 19:4 Then Pilate went out again and saith to them, Behold I bring him out to you that you may know that I find no fault in him.
JOH 19:5 So Jesus came out wearing the crown of thorns and the purple robe. And Pilate saith to them, Behold the man.
JOH 19:6 Upon which when the chief priests, and the officers saw him, they cried, saying, Crucify him; crucify him. Pilate saith to them, Take him yourselves and crucify him; for I find no fault in him.
JOH 19:7 The Jews answered, We have a law; and by that law of ours he ought to die, because he hath pretended to be the son of God.
JOH 19:8 Now when Pilate heard this expression he was more alarmed
JOH 19:9 and went again into the judgment hall, and saith to Jesus, Whence art thou? But Jesus made him no answer.
JOH 19:10 Then Pilate saith to him, Dost thou not speak to me? Knowest thou not, that I have power to crucify thee; and that I have power to release thee?
JOH 19:11 Jesus answered, Thou couldst have no power at all against me, if it were not given thee from above; therefore he who delivered me up to thee hath the greater sin.
JOH 19:12 From this [time] Pilate sought to release him; but the Jews cried out, saying, If thou let this man go, thou art not Caesar's friend. Whoever maketh himself a king speaketh against Caesar.
JOH 19:13 When Pilate therefore heard this speech, he brought out Jesus and sat down on the tribunal in a place called the pavement [in Hebrew Gabbatha.]
JOH 19:14 [It was now the paschal preparation day, and the sixth hour was drawing on,] and he saith to the Jews, Behold your king!
JOH 19:15 Whereupon they cried out, Away, away with him; crucify him. Pilate saith to them, Shall I crucify your king? The chief priests answered, We have no king but Caesar.
JOH 19:16 Then he delivered him up to them to be crucified. So they took Jesus and led him away,
JOH 19:17 and he went out, carrying his cross, to the place called Sculls, [in Hebrew, Golgotha,]
JOH 19:18 where they crucified him, and two others with him; one on one side and the other on the other side, and Jesus in the middle.
JOH 19:19 Now Pilate had written a label and put it on the cross, and the writing was this, Jesus The Nazarine, The King Of The Jews.
JOH 19:20 This label therefore many of the Jews read; for the place where Jesus was crucified was near the city; and the inscription was in Hebrew and Greek and Latin.
JOH 19:21 Wherefore the chief priests of the Jews said to Pilate, Write not The king of the Jews, but, that he said, I am the king of the Jews.
JOH 19:22 Pilate answered, What I have written, I have written.
JOH 19:23 Now when the soldiers had nailed Jesus to the cross, they took his garments and divided them into four parts, to every soldier a part. But as for the vest, as it was without seam, being woven from the top throughout,
JOH 19:24 they said to one another, Let us not tear it, but cast lots for it, whose it shall be, so that the scripture was fulfilled which saith, "They parted my garments among them; and for my vesture they cast lots." These things the soldiers actually did.
JOH 19:25 Now there stood by the cross of Jesus, his mother, and his mother's sister, Mary the wife of Cleophas, and Mary Magdalene.
JOH 19:26 Jesus therefore seeing his mother, and the disciple whom he loved standing near, saith to his, "mother, Woman, behold thy son!
JOH 19:27 Then he saith to the disciple, Behold thy mother!" And from that hour the disciple took her to his own home.
JOH 19:28 After this, Jesus, knowing that all things were now accomplished, that the scripture might be fulfilled, saith, "I thirst".
JOH 19:29 Upon which, as there was a vessel set full of vinegar, some having filled a sponge with vinegar put it on a stalk of hyssop and put it to his mouth.
JOH 19:30 When Jesus had received the vinegar, he said, It is finished, and bowing his head, he expired.
JOH 19:31 Now that the bodies might not remain on the cross during the sabbath, therefore when it was preparation time [for that sabbath was a great day] the Jews besought Pilate that their legs might be broken and the bodies removed.
JOH 19:32 The soldiers therefore came and broke the legs of the first and also of the other who had been crucified with him.
JOH 19:33 But when they came to Jesus, as they saw that he was already dead, they did not break his legs.
JOH 19:34 But one of the soldiers with his spear pierced his side, and blood and water issued forth immediately.
JOH 19:35 Now he who was an eye witness hath testified this. And his testimony is true, and [Jesus] himself knoweth that he speaketh the truth that you may believe.
JOH 19:36 For these things were done that the scripture might be fulfilled, "A bone of him shall not be broken."
JOH 19:37 And again another scripture saith, "They will look on him whom they have pierced."
JOH 19:38 After this, Joseph of Arimathea, who was a disciple of Jesus, but for fear of the Jews, a concealed one, asked leave of Pilate to take away the body of Jesus, and Pilate granted it. He therefore came and took away the body of Jesus.
JOH 19:39 And Nicodemus, he who formerly came to Jesus by night, came also with a mixture of myrrh and aloes, weighing about a hundred pounds.
JOH 19:40 So they took the body of Jesus and wrapped it up in linen swathings with the spices, according to the Jewish custom of embalming.
JOH 19:41 Now at the place where he was crucified there was a garden, and in the garden a new tomb, in which no one had ever been laid.
JOH 19:42 Therefore on account of the preparation of the Jews, they laid Jesus there, because the tomb was nigh at hand.
JOH 20:1 Now on the first day of the week, Mary Magdalene cometh to the tomb early in the morning, while there was still darkness, and she seeth the stone was taken away from the tomb.
JOH 20:2 Upon which she runneth and cometh to Simon Peter and the other disciple, whom Jesus loved, and saith to them, They have taken the master out of the tomb and we do not know where they have laid him.
JOH 20:3 Thereupon Peter set out with the other disciple, and they went to the tomb.
JOH 20:4 Now they both ran together, but the other disciple out ran Peter and came first to the tomb.
JOH 20:5 And having stooped down he seeth the linen swathings laid by; but did not go in.
JOH 20:6 Then cometh Simon Peter following him, and he went into the tomb and seeth the linen swathings laid by,
JOH 20:7 and the napkin, which was on his head, not laid with the linen swathings, but folded up in a place by itself.
JOH 20:8 Then the other disciple, who came first to the tomb, went in also and saw and believed.
JOH 20:9 For they did not yet know the scripture, that he was to rise from the dead.
JOH 20:10 Therefore these disciples went their way home again.
JOH 20:11 But Mary stood without, before the tomb, weeping. And as she wept, she stooped down to look into the tomb,
JOH 20:12 and seeth two angels robed in white, sitting one at the head and the other at the feet, where the body of Jesus had lain:
JOH 20:13 and they say to her, Woman why weepest thou? She saith to them, Because they have taken away my lord, and I know not where they have4 laid him.
JOH 20:14 And, having said this, she turneth about and seeth Jesus standing, but did not know that it is Jesus.
JOH 20:15 Jesus saith to her, Woman, why weepest thou? Whom art thou seeking? She, supposing him to be the gardener, saith to him, Sir, if thou hast taken him up; tell me where thou hast laid him, and I will take him away.
JOH 20:16 Jesus saith to her, Mary! She turning saith to him, Rabboni, that is to say, Teacher.
JOH 20:17 Jesus saith to her, Cling not to me, for I have not yet ascended to my Father: But go to my brethren and tell them, I am about to ascend to my Father and to your Father, and to my God and your God.
JOH 20:18 Mary Magdalene cometh and telleth the disciples that she hath seen the Lord, and that he spoke these things to her.
JOH 20:19 In the evening, on that same day, the first day of the week, the doors where the disciples assembled being shut for fear of the Jews, Jesus came and stood in the midst, and saith to them, "Peace be to you."
JOH 20:20 And having said this, he shewed them his hands and his side, and the disciples were rejoiced at seeing the Lord.
JOH 20:21 Then Jesus said to them again, Peace be to you. As the Father sent me so I send you.
JOH 20:22 And having said this he breathed on them, and saith to them, Receive a holy spirit.
JOH 20:23 Whose sins soever you forgive, they are forgiven them, and whose sins soever you retain, they are retained.
JOH 20:24 Now Thomas, one of the twelve, he who is called Didymus, was not with them when Jesus came.
JOH 20:25 The other disciples therefore said to him, We have seen the Lord. But he said to them, Unless I see in his hands the print of the nails; and put my finger into the print of the nails; and put this hand of mine into his side, I will not believe.
JOH 20:26 And after eight days, his disciples were again within, and Thomas with them. Jesus cometh, the doors being shut, and stood in the midst and said, Peace be to you.
JOH 20:27 Then he saith to Thomas, Reach hither thy finger and behold my hands! and reach thy hand and put it in to my side; and be not an unbeliever, but a believer.
JOH 20:28 And Thomas answered and said to him, My Lord and my God.
JOH 20:29 Jesus saith to him, Thomas, Because thou hast seen me, thou hast believed? Happy they who have not seen me and yet believe.
JOH 20:30 Now Jesus performed many other miracles in the presence of his disciples, which are not written in this book.
JOH 20:31 But these are written that you may believe that Jesus is the Christ, the Son of God, and that believing, you may have life by his name.
JOH 21:1 After this Jesus shewed himself again to his disciples, by the sea of Tiberias, and in this manner he shewed himself.
JOH 21:2 Simon Peter, and Thomas called Didymus, and Nathaniel, who was of Cana in Galilee, and the sons of Zebedee, and two other of his disciples, were together.
JOH 21:3 Simon Peter saith to them, I am going a fishing. They say to him, We will go with thee. They went and presently got aboard the vessel, and that  night caught nothing.
JOH 21:4 And when it was morning Jesus stood on the shore, but the disciples did not know that it was Jesus.
JOH 21:5 Then Jesus saith to them, Lads, have you any thing to eat? They answered him, No.
JOH 21:6 Then he said to them, Cast the net on the right side of the vessel and you will find. So they cast, and now they were not able to draw it up, by reason of the multitude of fishes.
JOH 21:7 Upon this that disciple whom Jesus loved saith to Peter, It is the Lord. Simon Peter therefore, upon hearing that it is the Lord, girded on his vest, for he was stript, and threw himself into the sea.
JOH 21:8 But the other disciples came in the boat, [for they were not far from land, only about two hundred cubits] dragging the net with the fishes.
JOH 21:9 As soon then as they came ashore, they see a fire of coals ready and a little fish on it, and a loaf of bread.
JOH 21:10 Jesus saith to them, Bring some of the fish you have now caught.
JOH 21:11 Simon Peter went and drew the net ashore full of large fishes, a hundred and fifty three. And though they were so many, the net was not torn.
JOH 21:12 Jesus saith to them, Come to breakfast. Now none of the disciples ventured to ask him, Who art thou? knowing that it was the Lord.
JOH 21:13 Then Jesus cometh and taketh the loaf and giveth to them, and the small fish likewise.
JOH 21:14 This was now the third time that Jesus appeared to these his disciples, after he was risen from the dead.
JOH 21:15 So when they had breakfasted, Jesus saith to Simon Peter, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me more than these? He saith to him, Yes, Lord, Thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith to him, Feed my lambs.
JOH 21:16 Again he saith to him a second time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? He saith to him, Yes, Lord, thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith to him, Tend my sheep.
JOH 21:17 He saith to him the third time, Simon, son of Jonas, lovest thou me? Peter was grieved that he said to him, the third time, "Lovest thou me," and he said to him, Lord thou knowest all things. Thou knowest that I love thee. Jesus saith to him, Feed my sheep.
JOH 21:18 Verily, verily I say to thee, When thou wast young, thou didst gird thyself and walk where thou wouldst; but when thou shalt be old, thou shalt stretch forth thy hands, and another will gird thee and carry thee whither thou wouldst not.
JOH 21:19 Now this he said to him, signifying by what sort of a death he should glorify God. And having said this, Jesus saith to him, Follow me.
JOH 21:20 Now when Peter turned about and saw the disciple whom Jesus loved following, [even him who at the supper reclined on his breast and said, Master, who is he that is about to deliver thee up]
JOH 21:21 Peter seeing him, saith to Jesus, Lord, and this one, what in respect to him?
JOH 21:22 Jesus saith to him, If I will that he stay till I come, what is that to thee?
JOH 21:23 Follow thou me. This saying therefore went abroad among the brethren, that this disciple should not die. But Jesus did not say to him, he should not die; but, If I will that he stay till I come, what is that to thee?
JOH 21:24 This is the disciple who testifieth concerning these things and hath written these things. And we know that his testimony is true.
JOH 21:25 There are indeed many other things which Jesus did. With respect to them, if they were all committed to writing, one by one, even then I do not think that the world would cordially receive the books written. Amen.
ACT 1:1 Composed, O Theophilus, the former treatise concerning all that Jesus took occasion both to do and teach
ACT 1:2 till the day when he was taken up, after giving a charge by the Holy Spirit to the apostles whom he had chosen,
ACT 1:3 and to whom he had, after his suffering, shewn himself to be alive, by many proofs, during forty days appearing to them, and speaking of what concerned the kingdom of God.
ACT 1:4 Then assembling them together, he ordered them not to depart from Jerusalem, but to wait for the promise of the Father, which you have heard from me.
ACT 1:5 For John indeed baptized in water, but you shall be baptized in a Holy Spirit not many days hence.
ACT 1:6 When they therefore were come together they asked him, saying, Lord, art thou at this time about to restore the kingdom to Israel?
ACT 1:7 Whereupon he said to them, It is not for you to know times and seasons which the Father hath reserved in his own disposal.
ACT 1:8 But you shall receive power when the Holy Spirit is come upon you; and you shall be witnesses for me in Jerusalem, and in all Judea, and Samaria, and to the remotest part of the earth.
ACT 1:9 And having said this, while they were beholding [him] he was taken up, and a cloud received him out of their sight.
ACT 1:10 And as they continued looking stedfastly up to heaven, while he was going, behold! two men stood near them, robed in white,
ACT 1:11 who addressed them, saying, Men of Galilee, why stand ye gazing up to heaven? This same Jesus who is taken up from you into heaven, will come in the same manner as you have seen him going to heaven.
ACT 1:12 Then they returned to Jerusalem from the mount called Olivet, which is near Jerusalem, a sabbath day's journey from it.
ACT 1:13 And when they came in, they went up into the upper room, where Peter, and James, and John, and Andrew, Philip and Thomas, Bartholomew and Matthew, James, son of Alpheus, and Simon Zelotes, and Judas the brother of James, usually made their abode.
ACT 1:14 These all continued with one mind in prayer and supplication, with the women, particularly Mary the mother of Jesus, and with his brethren.
ACT 1:15 And in those days Peter rising up in the midst of the disciples, [the number of persons assembled being about one hundred and twenty]
ACT 1:16 said, Men, brethren, It was necessary that this scripture should be fulfilled, which the Holy Spirit predicted, by the mouth of David, concerning Judas who was guide to them who laid hold on Jesus;
ACT 1:17 because he was numbered with us, and had a part of this service allotted him
ACT 1:18 [Now this man indeed had purchased! a field with the reward of his iniquity, and, falling on his face, had burst asunder, and all his bowels gushed out;
ACT 1:19 and this was so generally known to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, that the field is called in their language, Akeldama, that is field of blood]
ACT 1:20 for it is written in the book of Psalms, "Let his fold be desolate, and let there be no inhabitant therein. And, His office let another take;"
ACT 1:21 It is necessary therefore, that one of these men who have accompanied us, during all the time that the Lord Jesus came in and went out over us,
ACT 1:22 beginning from the baptism of John to the day on which he was taken up from us, should be a witness with us of his resurrection.
ACT 1:23 So they set up two, Joseph called Barsabas, who was surnamed Justus, and Matthias.
ACT 1:24 And having prayed, saying, "Thou, O Lord, who knowest the hearts of all men, shew which of these two thou hast chosen
ACT 1:25 to take the share of this ministration and apostleship which Judas abandoned to go to his own place,"
ACT 1:26 they cast lots; and the lot fell on Matthias; and he was numbered with the eleven apostles.
ACT 2:1 Now when the day of pentecost was fully come, they were all with one accord in the same place.
ACT 2:2 And suddenly there came from heaven a sound as of a mighty rushing wind, which filled the whole house where they were sitting.
ACT 2:3 And there appeared to them separate tongues, as of fire, and it settled on each of them.
ACT 2:4 And they were all filled with a holy spirit and began to speak in different languages, as the spirit gave them to make solemn addresses.
ACT 2:5 Now there were residing at Jerusalem Jews, devout men from every nation under heaven.
ACT 2:6 So when this report spread, the multitude came together and were confounded. Because every one heard them speaking in his own peculiar dialect;
ACT 2:7 therefore they were astonished and expressed their amazement, saying one to another, Behold! are not all these men who speak, Galileans?"
ACT 2:8 How then do we hear, every one in his own native tongue!
ACT 2:9 Parthians and Medes and Elamites and the inhabitants of Mesopotamia and Judea, and Capadocia, Pontus and Asia,
ACT 2:10 Phrygia and Pamphilia, Egypt and the parts of Lybia about Gyrene, the Roman strangers also both Jews and Proselytes,
ACT 2:11 Cretans and Arabs, we hear them speaking, in our own tongues, the wonderful dispensations of God.
ACT 2:12 So they were all amazed and in suspense, saying to one another, What can be the meaning of this?
ACT 2:13 But others scoffingly said, They are filled with sweet wine.
ACT 2:14 Whereupon Peter, as he was standing with the eleven, raised his voice and thus solemnly addressed them, "Men of Judea and all ye inhabitants of Jerusalem, let this be made known to you; and listen attentively to my words:
ACT 2:15 for these men are not drunk as you suppose; for it is but the third hour of the day.
ACT 2:16 But this is what was spoken by the prophet Joel,
ACT 2:17 "And it shall come to pass in the last days, saith God, that I will pour out a portion of my spirit upon all flesh; and your sons and your daughters shall prophesy; and your young men shall see visions; and your old men shall dream dreams;
ACT 2:18 and upon my servants, and upon my handmaids, in those days I will pour out a portion of my spirit, and they shall prophesy:
ACT 2:19 and I will exhibit wonders in the heaven above, and signs on the earth beneath; blood and fire and smoky vapour.
ACT 2:20 The sun shall be turned into darkness, and the moon into blood, before the coming of the great and illustrious day of the Lord.
ACT 2:21 And it shall come to pass, that whoever will call on the name of the Lord shall be saved.
ACT 2:22 "Men of Israel hear these words Jesus the Nazarene, a man from God, pointed out to you by miracles and wonders and signs, which God performed by him among you, as you yourselves know.
ACT 2:23 Him, being surrendered up by the determinate counsel and foreknowledge of God, you have taken; and by the hands of wicked men have crucified and slain.
ACT 2:24 Him God hath raised up, having loosed the bonds of death, as it was not possible that he could be holden by it:
ACT 2:25 for concerning him David saith, I saw the Lord continually before me: because he is at my right hand that I may not be moved;
ACT 2:26 therefore my heart was gladdened, and my tongue exulted with joy; and moreover my flesh also will dwell in hope,
ACT 2:27 that thou wilt not leave my soul in the mansion of the dead, nor suffer thy Holy One to see corruption.
ACT 2:28 Thou hast made known to me the ways of life. Thou with thy presence wilt fill me with joy."
ACT 2:29 Men, brethren, permit me to speak freely to you concerning the patriarch David, that he is both dead and buried; and his sepulchre is among us to this day.
ACT 2:30 Being therefore a prophet, and knowing that God had sworn to him with an oath, that from the fruit of his loins he would, as far as regardeth the flesh, raise up the Christ to sit on his throne,
ACT 2:31 he spoke prophetically of the resurrection of the Christ, that his soul was not left in the mansion of the dead, nor did his flesh see corruption.
ACT 2:32 This very Jesus God hath raised up, of which we all are witnesses.
ACT 2:33 Being therefore exalted at the right hand of God, and having received the promise of the Holy Spirit from the Father, he hath poured out this which you now see and hear.
ACT 2:34 For David did not ascend into the heavens; yet he saith, "The Lord said to my lord, Sit at my right hand,
ACT 2:35 until I make thine enemies thy footstool."
ACT 2:36 Therefore let all the house of Israel know assuredly, that God hath made the same Jesus whom ye have crucified, Lord and Christ.
ACT 2:37 Upon hearing this, they were pierced to the heart and said to Peter and the rest of the apostles, Men, brethren, What shall we do?
ACT 2:38 Thereupon Peter said to them, Repent and let every one of you be baptized to the remission of sins for the name of Jesus Christ, and you will receive the gift of the Holy Spirit.
ACT 2:39 For the promise is to you and to your children, and to all them afar off, whomsoever the Lord our God may invite."
ACT 2:40 And with many other words he obtested and exhorted them, saying, "Save yourselves from this depraved generation."
ACT 2:41 Then they who gladly received his word were baptized, and about three thousand souls were that day added;
ACT 2:42 and continued stedfast in the doctrine of the apostles and in the community, and in the breaking of the loaf, and in prayers,
ACT 2:43 and there was fear on every soul; and many wonders and signs were done by the apostles.
ACT 2:44 Now all they who believed were together, and had all things in common;
ACT 2:45 and they sold their possessions and goods and distributed them to all, as any had need.
ACT 2:46 And continuing daily with one accord in the temple, and breaking bread at home, they partook of food with joy and singleness of heart,
ACT 2:47 praising God and having favour with all the people. And the Lord added daily to the congregation them who were cured.
ACT 3:1 Now at the same time that Peter and John were going up2 to the temple at the hour of prayer, namely, at the ninth hour,
ACT 3:2 there was a certain man carried up who had been lame from his birth, whom they laid daily at the gate of the temple, called Beauty-Gate, to ask alms of them who were going into the temple;
ACT 3:3 who seeing Peter and John just about to enter the temple, begged to receive an alms.
ACT 3:4 Whereupon Peter and John having fixed their eyes on him, Peter said, Look on us.
ACT 3:5 Upon which he looked earnestly at them, expecting to receive something from them.
ACT 3:6 Then Peter said, Silver and gold I have none. But what I have, that I give thee. In the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, rise up and walk.
ACT 3:7 Then having taken him by the right hand he raised him up. And instantly his feet and ankle bones were strengthened;
ACT 3:8 and leaping up, he stood; then walked and entered the temple with them, walking and leaping and praising God.
ACT 3:9 When all the people saw him walking and praising God,
ACT 3:10 and recollected that he was the man who used to sit begging at the Beauty-gate of the temple, they were filled with wonder and astonishment at what had happened to him.
ACT 3:11 And while the lame man who was cured, kept hold of Peter and John, all the people in amaze crowded to them in the portico called Solomon's.
ACT 3:12 Now when Peter saw this he thus addressed the people. "Men of Israel, why wonder ye at this? Or why do ye fix your eyes on us, as if we by our own power or piety had made this man walk?
ACT 3:13 The God of Abraham, and Isaak, and Jacob; the God of our fathers hath glorified his servant Jesus whom ye delivered up. Yes, you renounced him in the presence of Pilate, when he had determined to release him:
ACT 3:14 you indeed renounced the Holy One and the Just, and desired a murderer to be granted to you.
ACT 3:15 You indeed killed him who is the conductor to life, whom God hath raised from the dead, of which we are witnesses.
ACT 3:16 Now for the belief in his name, his name hath strengthened this man whom you see and know. Yes, the belief which is by him hath given this man this perfect soundness in the presence of you all.
ACT 3:17 And now brethren, I know that it was through ignorance that both' you and your rulers acted thus;
ACT 3:18 and that what God foretold by the mouth of all his prophets; That The Christ Should Suffer, he hath thus accomplished.
ACT 3:19 Repent therefore and return, that your sins may be blotted out, that seasons of refreshment may come from the presence of the Lord;
ACT 3:20 and that he may send him who hath been before hand proclaimed to you; namely, Jesus Christ,
ACT 3:21 whom the heaven must receive till the time of the consummation of all which God hath spoken by the mouth of all his holy prophets of old:
ACT 3:22 for Moses indeed said to the fathers, "The Lord your God will raise up for you from among your brethren a prophet like me. To him you must hearken according to all that he shall speak to you;
ACT 3:23 and whoever the person be who will not hearken to that prophet, he shall be cut off front among the people.
ACT 3:24 All the prophets also from Samuel, even as many of the following ones as have spoken, have likewise foretold these days.
ACT 3:25 You are the children of the prophets and of the covenant which God made with our fathers, saying to Abraham "And by thy seed all the families of the earth shall be blessed."
ACT 3:26 It is to you first that God, having raised up his son Jesus, hath sent him, blessing you, when you turn every one from his iniquities.
ACT 4:1 Now while they were speaking to the people; the priests, and the captain of the temple, and the Sadducees,
ACT 4:2 displeased at their teaching the people and promulgating by Jesus the resurrection from the dead, came on them,
ACT 4:3 and laid hands on them, and put them in prison till the next day. For it was now evening.
ACT 4:4 But many of those who heard the word believed. And the number of the men became about five thousand.
ACT 4:5 And on the morrow their rulers, and elders, and Scribes at Jerusalem assembled,
ACT 4:6 with Annas the chief priest, and Caiaphas, and John, and Alexander, and as many as were of the pontifical family;
ACT 4:7 and having set them in the midst, they asked by what power, or by what name, have you done this?
ACT 4:8 Then Peter being filled with a holy spirit, said to them, "Rulers of the people and elders of Israel,
ACT 4:9 if we are this day examined for a good deed done to an infirm man, by what means he hath been healed,
ACT 4:10 be it known to you all, and to all the people of Israel, that by the name of Jesus Christ the Nazarene, whom ye crucified; whom God raised from the dead by him this man standeth before you, perfectly cured.
ACT 4:11 This is the stone that was rejected by you the builders, which was for the head of the corner.
ACT 4:12 This cure indeed is by no other, nor is there any other name under heaven given among men by which we can be saved."
ACT 4:13 Now when they saw the boldness of Peter and John, and found that they were illiterate men, and in private stations of life, they wondered; and recollected their having been with Jesus.
ACT 4:14 And seeing the man who was cured standing with them, they could make no reply.
ACT 4:15 So, having ordered them to withdraw from the Sanhedrim, they conferred among themselves,
ACT 4:16 saying, What can we do with these men? For that a signal miracle hath indeed been done by them, is manifest to all the inhabitants of Jerusalem, and we cannot deny it.
ACT 4:17 But that it may not spread farther among the people, let us severely threaten them not to speak any more for this name to any man.
ACT 4:18 So having called them in, they gave them this general charge, not to make solemn addresses, nor teach, for the name of that Jesus.
ACT 4:19 But Peter and John in reply to them, said, Whether it be right in the sight of God to hearken to you rather than to God, judge ye.
ACT 4:20 For we cannot but speak the things which we have seen and heard.
ACT 4:21 So, having further threatened them, they dismissed them, not finding how to punish them, because of the people who all glorified God for that which was done.
ACT 4:22 For the man, upon whom this miracle of healing was performed, was above forty years old.
ACT 4:23 So, being discharged, they went to their brethren and told them all that the chief priests and the elders had said to them;
ACT 4:24 which when they heard, they with one accord raised their voice to God and said, O Lord, thou art the God, who madest the heaven and the earth and the sea, and all that are therein,
ACT 4:25 who by the mouth of thy servant David hast said, "Why did nations rage, and tribes meditate vain things?"
ACT 4:26 The kings of the earth combined, and the chiefs assembled together against the Lord and against his Anointed."
ACT 4:27 For indeed against thy holy Child Jesus whom thou hast anointed, both Herod and Pontius Pilate, with nations and the tribes of Israel, were gathered together,
ACT 4:28 to do what thy hand and thy council had determinately marked out beforehand to be brought to pass.
ACT 4:29 Now with regard to present occurrences, look down, O Lord, on their threatenings, and enable thy servants to speak thy word with all freedom
ACT 4:30 when thou stretchest forth thy hand for healing; and signs and. wonders are done by the name of thy holy child, Jesus.
ACT 4:31 And while they were praying, the place in which they were assembled was shaken. And they were all filled with a Holy Spirit and spoke the word of God with boldness.
ACT 4:32 Now the whole body of the believers were of one heart and one soul. And no one said that any of his goods were his own; but all things were common among them.
ACT 4:33 And the apostles delivered with great power the testimony of the resurrection of the Lord Jesus. And there was great thankfulness among them all;
ACT 4:34 for there was not one indigent person among them: for as many as were proprietors of lands or houses sold them and brought the prices of the things sold,
ACT 4:35 which being laid at the apostles feet, distribution was made to every one according as any had need.
ACT 4:36 In particular Joses, who by the apostles was surnamed Barnabas, the signification of which is Son of Consolation, a Levite, and by birth a Cyprian,
ACT 4:37 having an estate, sold it and brought the money and laid it at the apostles feet.
ACT 5:1 But there was a certain man named Ananias, who with his wife Sapphira sold an estate
ACT 5:2 and kept back a part of the price, his wife also being privy to it. And having brought a certain part he laid it at the feet of the apostles.
ACT 5:3 Upon which Peter said, Ananias, Why hath Satan filled thy heart that thou shouldst lie to the Holy Spirit, and keep back a part of the price of the land?
ACT 5:4 While it remained, did it not remain thine? And when sold it was still at thine own disposal. Why then hast thou determined this thing in thy heart? Thou hast not lied to men, but to God.
ACT 5:5 Upon hearing these words Ananias fell down and expired. And great fear came upon all who heard these things.
ACT 5:6 Then the young men arose and having swathed him, they carried him out and buried him.
ACT 5:7 And about the space of three hours after, his wife, not knowing what had happened, came in.
ACT 5:8 And Peter said to her, Tell me; did you sell the land for such a price? And she said, Yes, for so much.
ACT 5:9 Thereupon Peter said to her, How is it that you have agreed to try the spirit of the Lord? Behold the feet of them, who have buried thy husband are at the door, and they will carry thee out.
ACT 5:10 At that instant she fell at his feet and expired. And the young men coming in found her dead. So they carried her out and buried her by her husband.
ACT 5:11 And great fear came upon all the congregation, and upon all that heard these things;
ACT 5:12 and by the hands of the apostles many signs and wonders were done among the people: Now they were all with one accord in Solomon's porch,
ACT 5:13 and of the rest no one presumed to join himself to them, but the people magnified them,
ACT 5:14 and believers in the Lord, multitudes both of men and women were more and more added
ACT 5:15 so that in every street they brought out the sick and laid them on beds and couches, that the shadow of Peter as he went along might overshadow some of them.
ACT 5:16 But when the multitude also of the cities around flocked to Jerusalem, bringing the sick and those who were tormented with unclean spirits, who were all cured;
ACT 5:17 the chief priest rising up, and all his party; the sect of the Sadducees, they were filled with zeal,
ACT 5:18 and laid their hands on the apostles and put them in the common prison.
ACT 5:19 But during the night an angel of the Lord opened the doors of the prison; and having brought them out said,
ACT 5:20 Go, and having taken your station in the temple, speak to the people all the words of this life.
ACT 5:21 Upon hearing this they went into the temple about break of day, and taught. Now when the chief priest was come with his party and had convened the Sanhedrim and all the elders of the children of Israel, they sent to the prison to have them brought up.
ACT 5:22 But when the officers went and did not find them in the prison; they returned and made report,
ACT 5:23 saying, We found indeed the prison shut with all safety, and the guards without standing before the door; but on opening we found no one within.
ACT 5:24 And while the priest and the captain of the temple and the chief priests, upon hearing these words, were doubting how this could be,
ACT 5:25 there came one who told them, saying, Behold! the men whom you put in prison, are standing in the temple and teaching the people.
ACT 5:26 Then the captain went with the under officers and brought them, but without violence; for they were afraid of being stoned by the people.
ACT 5:27 And when they had brought them, and set them before the Sanhedrim, the chief priest asked them,
ACT 5:28 saying, Did we not strictly charge you not to teach for this name"? Yet behold you have filled Jerusalem with this doctrine of yours and wish to bring that man's blood upon us.
ACT 5:29 In reply to which Peter and the apostles said, We must obey God rather than men.
ACT 5:30 The God of our fathers hath raised up Jesus, whom ye slew, having caused him to be suspended on a cross
ACT 5:31 even him, a chief leader and a Saviour, God hath exalted at his right hand to give repentance to Israel and a remission of sins.
ACT 5:32 And we are his witnesses of these things, as is also the Holy Spirit which God hath granted to them who obey him.
ACT 5:33 At hearing this they were cut to the heart, and consulted to put them to death.
ACT 5:34 But there stood up a man in the Sanhedrim; a Pharisee named Gamaliel, a teacher of the law, in great esteem among all the people; and having moved that the apostles withdraw for a little while,
ACT 5:35 he said to them, "Men of Israel, take heed to yourselves how you proceed in regard to these men.
ACT 5:36 For some time ago Theudas started up, saying that he was an. extraordinary person, to whom a number of men, about four hundred, joined themselves. He was destroyed, and all that put confidence in him were broken up and came to nothing.
ACT 5:37 After him started up Judas, the Galilean, in the days of the enrolment, and drew a great many people after him. He also perished, and all that put confidence in him were dispersed.
ACT 5:38 Now therefore on this occasion I say to you, Forbear from meddling with these men, and let them alone: for if this counsel or this work be of men; it will moulder away.
ACT 5:39 But if it be of God you cannot annul it. Peradventure you may be found even fighting against God."
ACT 5:40 So to him they agreed: and having called in the apostles and scourged them, they charged them not to speak about the name of Jesus and dismissed them.
ACT 5:41 Thereupon they went from the presence of the Sanhedrim, rejoicing that they were counted worthy to suffer shame for his name.
ACT 5:42 And every day, both in the temple and at home, they ceased not to teach and publish the glad tidings, That Jesus is the Christ.
ACT 6:1 Now in those days, the number of the disciples being multiplied, there was a murmuring of the Hellenists against the Hebrews that their widows were neglected in the daily distribution.
ACT 6:2 Wherefore the twelve having called together the multitude of the disciples said, It is not proper that we should leave the word of God to attend tables:
ACT 6:3 look out therefore, brethren, from among yourselves seven men of good reputation, full of a holy spirit and wisdom, whom we may appoint to this office.
ACT 6:4 And as for us, we will continue in the constant exercise of prayer, and in the ministration of the word.
ACT 6:5 And this speech pleased the whole multitude. So they chose Stephen, a man full of faith and a holy spirit, and Philip and Prochorus and Nicanor and Timon and Parmenias and Nicholas a proselyte of Antioch,
ACT 6:6 whom they set before the apostles, who having prayed, laid their hands on them.
ACT 6:7 So the word of God spread, and the number of disciples was greatly multiplied in Jerusalem, and a great multitude of the priests became obedient to the faith.
ACT 6:8 Now Stephen being full of faith and power performed miracles and great signs among the people,
ACT 6:9 and there arose some of the synagogue of the Libertini, as it was called, and of the Cyrenians and Alexandrians, and of those of Cilicia and Asia, who disputed with Stephen;
ACT 6:10 but not being able to withstand the wisdom and spirit with which he spoke,
ACT 6:11 they suborned men to say, We heard him speak blasphemous words against Moses, and against God.
ACT 6:12 And having stirred up the people and the elders and the Scribes, they came upon him and seized him, and brought him to the Sanhedrim,
ACT 6:13 and set up false witnesses, who said, This man is incessantly speaking blasphemous words against this holy place and the law;
ACT 6:14 for we heard him saying that Jesus the Nazarene will destroy this place and change the customs which Moses delivered to us.
ACT 6:15 And all who sat in the Sanhedrim, looking stedfastly at him, beheld his countenance, like the countenance of an angel.
ACT 7:1 Then the chief priest said, Are these things so?
ACT 7:2 Upon which he said, Men, brethren and fathers hearken. The God of the glory appeared to our father Abraham, when he was in Mesopotamia, before he dwelt in Charran,
ACT 7:3 and said to him, Depart from this country of thine, and from thy kindred, and come to the land which I will shew thee.
ACT 7:4 Thereupon he went from the land of the Chaldees, and dwelt in Charran; and thence after his father died, God removed him to this land in which you now dwell,
ACT 7:5 but gave him no inheritance in it; not even a foot of land. He indeed promised that he would give it to him for a possession, even to his seed after him, though he then had no child.
ACT 7:6 And God spake thus; That his seed should sojourn in a strange land and be enslaved and afflicted: four hundred years:
ACT 7:7 and the nation which they shall serve I will judge, said God, and after that they shall come out and serve me in this place.
ACT 7:8 Then he gave him the covenant of circumcision. So Abraham begat Isaak, and circumcised him on the eighth day, and Isaak begat Jacob; and Jacob, the twelve patriarchs.
ACT 7:9 And the patriarchs, being moved with envy, sold Joseph into Egypt. But God was with him,
ACT 7:10 and delivered him out of all his afflictions, and gave him favour and wisdom in the sight of Pharao king of Egypt, who appointed him ruler over Egypt, and all his household.
ACT 7:11 And there came a famine over all the land of Egypt and Chanaan. It was indeed a great affliction and our fathers found no sustenance.
ACT 7:12 So when Jacob heard that there was corn in Egypt, he sent our fathers the first time;
ACT 7:13 and on their second going down Joseph made himself known to his brothers; and Joseph's kindred was made known to Pharao.
ACT 7:14 Then Joseph sent for his father Jacob and all his kindred, amounting to threescore and fifteen souls.
ACT 7:15 So Jacob went down to Egypt and died, he and our fathers,
ACT 7:16 and were conveyed to Sychem, and deposited in the sepulchre which Abraham bought for a sum of money of the sons of Emmer the Sychemite.
ACT 7:17 And as the time approached for accomplishing the promise which God had made with an oath to Abraham, the people increased and multiplied in Egypt,
ACT 7:18 until another king arose, who knew not Joseph.
ACT 7:19 This king, mischievously politic against our family, ill treated our fathers, causing their children to be ex posed that they might not be preserved alive.
ACT 7:20 At this time Moses was born, who was exceeding beautiful, and was nursed up three months in his father's house.
ACT 7:21 Being then exposed, Pharao's daughter took him up and had him nursed for her own son.
ACT 7:22 So Moses was instructed in all the wisdom .of the Egyptians, and became mighty in council and in actions.
ACT 7:23 And when he was forty years old it came into his mind to visit his brethren, the children of Israel.
ACT 7:24 And seeing one of them injured, he defended him and avenged the injury by killing the Egyptian.
ACT 7:25 Now he supposed that his brethren would understand that by his hand God was about to give them deliverance. But they understood not,
ACT 7:26 and on the next day when he shewed himself to them who were quarrelling and persuaded them to peace, saying, Men, you are brethren, Why do ye injure one another?
ACT 7:27 He who was doing his neighbour the injury thrust him away, saying, Who made thee a chief and a judge over us?
ACT 7:28 Dost thou mean to kill me as thou didst the Egyptian yesterday?
ACT 7:29 At this speech Moses fled and became a sojourner in the land of Madiam, where he became the father of two sons.
ACT 7:30 And when forty years were completed, an angel of the Lord appeared to him in the wilderness at mount Sinai, in a flame of fire in a bush,
ACT 7:31 which when Moses saw, he was astonished at the vision. And as he was going near to view it, there came a voice of the Lord to him,
ACT 7:32 "I am the God of thy fathers; the God of Abraham, and the God of Isaak, and the God of Jacob." Upon which Moses trembled and durst not view it.
ACT 7:33 Then the Lord said to him, Loose the sandals from thy feet, for the place where thou standest is holy ground.
ACT 7:34 I have indeed seen the affliction of my people in Egypt, and have heard their groaning and am come down to deliver them. Now therefore come, I will send thee to Egypt.
ACT 7:35 This Moses whom they rejected, saying, Who made thee a chief and a judge? this very person God sent as a chief and a deliverer by the hand of an angel who appeared to him in the bush
ACT 7:36 This person brought them out by performing wonders and signs in Egypt and at the Red sea, and in the wilderness, forty years.
ACT 7:37 This is the very Moses who said to the children of Israel, The Lord your God will raise up for you, from among your brethren, a prophet like me, to him you are to hearken.
ACT 7:38 This is the person who was in the congregation in the wilderness, with the angel who spake to him at mount Sinai, and with our fathers; who received living oracles to give to us;
ACT 7:39 to whom our fathers would not be obedient, but rejected him, when with their hearts they turned towards Egypt,
ACT 7:40 saying to Aaron, Make gods for us to go before us; for as for this Moses who brought us out of the land of Egypt, we do not know what is become of him.
ACT 7:41 So they made a calf in those days and brought a sacrifice for the idol, and rejoiced in the works of their own hands.
ACT 7:42 Therefore God turned and gave them up to worship the host of heaven. As it is written in the book of the Prophets, "Have you, O house of Israel, offered to me burnt offerings and sacrifices, forty years in the wilderness?
ACT 7:43 You have indeed taken up the tabernacle of Moloch and the star of your God Remphan; those types which you have made to worship them; therefore I will transport you beyond Babylon.
ACT 7:44 The tabernacle of the testimony was among our fathers in the wilderness, as he who spoke to Moses had ordered it to be made according to the pattern which he had seen.
ACT 7:45 This tabernacle, which our fathers with Joshua received and brought into the territory of the nations which God drove out from before our fathers, continued till the days of David;
ACT 7:46 who found favour in the sight of God, and made it his petition to find a habitation for the God of Jacob.
ACT 7:47 But it was Solomon who built a house for him.
ACT 7:48 But the Most High dwelleth not in temples made with hands. As the prophet saith,
ACT 7:49 "The heaven is my throne, and the earth, my footstool. What sort of a house will you build for me? saith the Lord. And of what sort shall be the place of my rest?
ACT 7:50 Did not my hands make all these things?"
ACT 7:51 O stiff necked and uncircumcised in heart and ears Ye do always resist the Holy Spirit. As your fathers did, so do ye.
ACT 7:52 Which of the prophets have not your fathers persecuted? Indeed they have slain them who prophesied concerning the coming of that Righteous one, of whom you have now become the betrayers and murderers:
ACT 7:53 you who have received the law through ranks of angels, but have not kept it.
ACT 7:54 At hearing this they were cut to the heart and gnashed their teeth at him.
ACT 7:55 But he being full of a holy spirit, having his eyes fixed towards heaven, beheld the glory of God and Jesus standing at the right hand of God:
ACT 7:56 whereupon he said, Behold! I see the heavens opened and the Son of man standing at the right hand of God.
ACT 7:57 At which they screamed aloud, and stopped their ears and rushed upon him with one accord.
ACT 7:58 And having driven him out of the city they stoned him. And the witnesses laid their mantles at the feet of a young man named Saul,
ACT 7:59 and stoned Stephen, invoking and saying, Lord Jesus, receive my spirit.
ACT 7:60 Then he kneeled down and cried out with a loud voice, O! Lord, charge not this sin to their account; and having said this he fell asleep.
ACT 8:1 Now Saul continued to express satisfaction at his death: and there was at that time a great persecution against the congregation which was at Jerusalem; and all, except the apostles, were scattered through the regions of Judea and Samaria.
ACT 8:2 While devout men were carrying Stephen to the grave and making great lamentation for him,
ACT 8:3 Saul was making havock of the congregation. Entering into houses and dragging out men and women, he committed them to prison.
ACT 8:4 They, however, who were dispersed, went about proclaiming the glad tidings of the word;
ACT 8:5 and Philip having come to a city of Samaria, proclaimed to them the Christ.
ACT 8:6 And the crowds with one accord attended to what were spoken by Philip, when they heard and saw the signal miracles which he performed.
ACT 8:7 For unclean spirits, with which many were possessed, went out of them with loud outcries: and many paralytic and lame persons were cured.
ACT 8:8 And there was great joy in that city.
ACT 8:9 Now there was a certain man, named Simon, who had heretofore practised magical arts in that city and astonished the nation of Samaria, pretending that he was an extraordinary person,
ACT 8:10 to whom all paid regard, from the least to the greatest, saying, This man is the great power of God. 11 To him indeed they paid regard because for a long time he had astonished them with his magical arts
ACT 8:12 But when they believed Philip's proclamation of the glad tidings concerning the kingdom of God and the name of Jesus Christ, they were baptized, both men and women.
ACT 8:13 And even Simon himself believed, and being baptized, he continued steadily with Philip. And seeing signs and great miracles done, he was astonished.
ACT 8:14 Now when the apostles who were at Jerusalem heard that Samaria had received the word of God, they sent to them Peter and John,
ACT 8:15 who having gone down, prayed for them that they might receive a holy spirit.
ACT 8:16 For it had not yet fallen on any of them, and they were only baptized to the name of the Lord Jesus.
ACT 8:17 Then they laid their hands on them and they received a holy spirit.
ACT 8:18 When Simon saw that by the laying on of the hands of the apostles the holy spirit was given, he offered them money,
ACT 8:19 saying, Give me also this power, that on whomsoever I lay my hands he may receive a holy spirit.
ACT 8:20 Whereupon Peter said to him, let thy money with thee be for destruction! Because thou hast thought that this free gift of God may be purchased with money,
ACT 8:21 thou hast no portion nor share in this matter, for thy heart is not right in the sight of God.
ACT 8:22 Repent therefore of this wickedness of thine; and beseech God, if indeed this thought of thy heart can be forgiven thee.
ACT 8:23 For I perceive that thou art for bitter gall and for a bond of iniquity.
ACT 8:24 In reply to which Simon said, Pray ye to the Lord for me that none of these things which you have mentioned may come upon me.
ACT 8:25 Now when they had testified and spoken the word of the Lord, they set out on their return to Jerusalem, and communicated the glad tidings to many villages of the Samaritans.
ACT 8:26 In the mean while an angel of the Lord spoke to Philip, saying, Arise and go southward on the road which leadeth down from Jerusalem to Gaza, namely, the desert road.
ACT 8:27 So he arose and went. And lo! a man of Ethiopia, an eunuch, a grandee of Candace, the queen of the Ethiopians, who was her high treasurer, who had come to Jerusalem to worship,
ACT 8:28 and was on his return, was sitting in a chariot and reading the prophet Esaias.
ACT 8:29 And the Spirit said to Philip, Go near and keep close to that chariot.
ACT 8:30 So Philip ran close up and heard him reading the prophet Esaias. Whereupon he said, Dost thou understand what thou art reading?
ACT 8:31 To which he replied, How can I unless some one guide me? Then he invited Philip to come up and take a seat with him.
ACT 8:32 Now the passage of scripture which he was reading was this, "He was led as a sheep to slaughter; and as a lamb before its shearer is dumb, so he openeth not his mouth.
ACT 8:33 In his humiliation his legal trial is taken away. Who will declare his manner of life? Because his life is taken from the earth.
ACT 8:34 And the eunuch addressing Philip, said, Of whom, I pray thee, doth the prophet say this? Of himself or of some other person?
ACT 8:35 Then Philip opened His mouth, and beginning with this scripture, told him the glad tidings of Jesus.
ACT 8:36 And as they continued the journey, they came to a certain water. Whereupon the eunuch said, Behold! here is water. What hindereth my being baptized?
ACT 8:37 And Philip said, If thou believest with thy whole heart, it may be done. To which he replied, I believe that Jesus Christ is the son of God.
ACT 8:38 Then he ordered the chariot to stop. And they both went down into the water, both Philip and the eunuch; and he baptized him.
ACT 8:39 And when they came up out of the water, the spirit of the Lord conveyed Philip away. And the eunuch saw him no more. For he proceeded on in his journey rejoicing,
ACT 8:40 and Philip was found at Azotus. And passing on he proclaimed the glad tidings in all the cities, till he came to Caesarea.
ACT 9:1 As for Saul he was still breathing out threatening and slaughter against the disciples of the Lord. Having gone to the chief priest,
ACT 9:2 he asked letters from him to the synagogues at Damascus, that if he should find any of this way, whether men or women, he might bring them bound to Jerusalem.
ACT 9:3 But when he was on the road and drawing near to Damascus, suddenly a light from heaven shone around him.
ACT 9:4 And having fallen on the ground, he heard a voice saying to him, "Saul, Saul, Why persecutes! thou me?"
ACT 9:5 And he said, Who art thou, Lord? And the Lord said, "I am Jesus, whom thou art persecuting. It is hurting thyself to kick against sharp pointed goads."
ACT 9:6 Whereupon he trembling and in amaze, said, Lord, What wouldst thou have me do?  And the Lord said to him, Arise and go to the city and it will be told thee what thou must do."
ACT 9:7 Now the men who accompanied him were amazed, hearing indeed the sound, but seeing no one.
ACT 9:8 Then Saul arose from the earth. But as upon opening his eyes he saw nobody, they led him by the hand and brought him to Damascus.
ACT 9:9 And he was three days without sight, and neither ate nor drank.
ACT 9:10 Now there was in Damascus a certain disciple named Ananias, And to him the Lord said in a vision, Ananias! And he said, Lord, here I am.
ACT 9:11 Then the Lord said to him, Arise and go to the street, which is called Straight street, and inquire at the house of Judas for Saul of Tarsus; for behold he is praying,
ACT 9:12 and hath seen in a vision a man named Ananias, coming in and laying a hand on him that he may recover sight.
ACT 9:13 Upon which Ananias answered, Lord, I have heard from many concerning this man, how much evil he hath done to thy saints in Jerusalem;
ACT 9:14 and he is here with authority from the chief priests to bind all who invoke thy name.
ACT 9:15 And the Lord said to him, Go: for this person is a vessel which I have chosen to bear my name before nations and kings and the children of Israel. For
ACT 9:16 I will shew him what he must suffer for my name.
ACT 9:17 So Ananias went and entered the house, and having laid his hands on him, said, Brother Saul, The Lord, even Jesus who appeared to thee on the road as thou camest, hath sent me that thou mayst recover sight and be filled with a holy spirit.
ACT 9:18 Upon this there fell immediately from his eyes something like scales, and instantly he recovered sight. Then he arose and was baptized;
ACT 9:19 and having taken some food, he was strengthened. And Saul was some days with the brethren in Damascus,
ACT 9:20 and forthwith, in the synagogues proclaimed Jesus that he is the son of God.
ACT 9:21 At which all that heard were surprised, and said, Is not this he who made havoc of them at Jerusalem, who invoked that name, and came hither on purpose to carry such bound to the chief priests?
ACT 9:22 But Saul was strengthened more and more, and confounded the Jews who dwelt at Damascus, proving that this person is the C H R I S T .
ACT 9:23 Now when many days were fulfilled, the Jews conspired to kill him;
ACT 9:24 and Saul was apprized of their plot. As they were watching the gates day and night to murder him,
ACT 9:25 the disciples took him by night and let him down over the wall, lowering him in a basket.
ACT 9:26 And when Saul came to Jerusalem and tried to associate with the disciples, they were all afraid of him, not believing that he was a disciple.
ACT 9:27 But Barnabas took him and brought him to the apostles, and told them, how he had on the road seen the Lord, who had spoken to him; and how he had spoken boldly in Damascus in the name of Jesus.
ACT 9:28 So he was with them coming in and going out at Jerusalem,
ACT 9:29 and speaking boldly in the name of the Lord Jesus. He spoke also and disputed with the Hellenists, and they attempted to kill him.
ACT 9:30 But when the brethren knew this they brought him down to Caesarea, and sent him on to Tarsus.
ACT 9:31 Now then the congregations throughout all Judea and Galilee, and Samaria, were enjoying peace. Being built up and walking in the fear of the Lord, and the consolation of the holy spirit, they were multiplied.
ACT 9:32 And it came to pass that as Peter was passing through all, he came down also to the saints who dwelt at Lydda
ACT 9:33 and found there a man, named .Aeneas, who was paralytic, and had been confined to his bed eight years.
ACT 9:34 And Peter said to him, "Aeneas, Jesus, The Christ, cureth thee. Arise and make thy bed." And he arose immediately.
ACT 9:35 And all the inhabitants of Lydda and Sarona saw him, and turned to the Lord.
ACT 9:36 Now there was at Joppa a certain disciple named Tabitha [the signification of which in Greek, is Dorcas [a Roe.]] This woman abounded in good works and in acts of charity.
