ACT 9:37 And at this time she fell sick and died. And when they had washed her, they laid her out in an upper room.
ACT 9:38 And as Lydda was near Joppa, the disciples, hearing that Peter was there, sent two men to him, intreating him to come to them without delay.
ACT 9:39 Accordingly Peter arose and went with them. And when he came they took him up to the upper room. And all the widows stood by him, weeping and shewing the tunicks and mantles which Dorcas had made while she was with them.
ACT 9:40 Then Peter, having put them all out, kneeled down and prayed, and turning to the body, he said, Tabitha, arise. Upon which she opened her eyes, and seeing Peter, sat up.
ACT 9:41 Then Peter giving her his hand, helped her up, and having called the saints and the widows, presented her alive.
ACT 9:42 And this was known throughout all Joppa, and many believed in the Lord.
ACT 9:43 And after this he continued many days at Joppa with one Simon, a tanner.
ACT 10:1 Now there was at Caesarea a certain man named Cornelius, a centurion of that called the Italian cohort.
ACT 10:2 He was pious, and feared God with all his household, and did many acts of benevolence to the people, and prayed to God continually.
ACT 10:3 About the ninth hour of the day, he saw plainly in a vision, an angel of God coming in to him and saying to him, Cornelius!
ACT 10:4 Upon which he having fixed his eyes on him, and being terrified, said, Lord! what is it? Then the angel said to him, Thy prayers and thine acts of benevolence have ascended for a memorial before God.
ACT 10:5 Now therefore send men to Joppa and call for Simon who is surnamed Peter.
ACT 10:6 He lodgeth with one Simon, a tanner, whose house is by the sea side. He will tell thee what thou must do.
ACT 10:7 So when the angel who spoke to him was gone, Cornelius called two of his household servants and a devout soldier of them who waited on him continually,
ACT 10:8 and having related to them the whole affair, he sent them to Joppa.
ACT 10:9 And on the next day while they were on their journey and approaching towards the city, Peter went up on the house top to pray, about the sixth hour.
ACT 10:10 Now he had become hungry and wished to take some refreshment; and while it was preparing he fell into a trance,
ACT 10:11 and saw the heaven opened, and a kind of vessel coming down to him, like a great sheet tied by the four corners, and let down to the earth,
ACT 10:12 in which were all sorts of four footed beasts of the earth, namely, the wild beasts and the reptiles, and the birds of the air.
ACT 10:13 And there came a voice to him, Rise Peter; Kill And Eat.
ACT 10:14 Whereupon Peter said, By no means, Lord. For I have never eaten any thing common or unclean.
ACT 10:15 And a voice said to him a second time, What God hath cleansed call not thou that common.
ACT 10:16 And this was done thrice, and then the vessel was again taken up into heaven.
ACT 10:17 And while Peter was in great doubt, what this vision which he had seen could mean, behold the men who were sent by Cornelius, having inquired out Simon's house, stood at the gate,
ACT 10:18 and calling, asked, Doth Simon who is surnamed Peter, lodge here?
ACT 10:19 And while Peter was pondering on the vision, the spirit said to him, Behold there are three men inquiring for thee.
ACT 10:20 Arise therefore, get thee down and go with them, without any cavilling, for I have sent them.
ACT 10:21 So Peter went down to the men who were sent to him from Cornelius, and said, Behold I am he for whom you are inquiring. What is the cause of your coming?
ACT 10:22 They said, Cornelius, a centurion, a righteous man, and one who feareth God, and is approved by the testimony of the whole Jewish nation, hath been divinely warned by a holy angel to send for thee to his house and receive instruction from thee.
ACT 10:23 Peter therefore, having invited them in, entertained them hospitably, and on the morrow he set out with them. And some of the brethren who were of Joppa accompanied him.
ACT 10:24 And on the day following they arrived at Caesarea, Now Cornelius was waiting for them, having called together his kinsmen and intimate friends.
ACT 10:25 And as Peter was coming in, Cornelius met him, and prostrating himself at his feet, made obeisance.
ACT 10:26 But Peter raised him up, saying, Rise up: I am but a man.
ACT 10:27 Then conversing with him he went in, and finding many assembled
ACT 10:28 he said to them, You know unlawful it is for a man who is a Jew, to associate with or go to one of another nation: but God hath shewn me, that I am not to call any man common or unclean.
ACT 10:29 For this cause, when I was sent for, I came without any hesitation. I ask therefore on what account you have sent for me?
ACT 10:30 Thereupon Cornelius said, Four days ago I was fasting till this hour, and at the ninth hour praying in my house. And lo! a man stood before me in splendid attire,
ACT 10:31 and said, Cornelius, thy prayer is heard, and thine acts of benevolence are remembered before God;
ACT 10:32 send therefore to Joppa for Simon who is surnamed Peter. He lodgeth at the house of Simon, a tanner, by the sea side. He will come and speak to thee.
ACT 10:33 Therefore I sent to thee immediately and thou hast done well in coming. Now therefore we are all here in the presence of God, to hear all that God hath given thee in charge.
ACT 10:34 Then Peter opened his mouth and said, Of a truth I perceive that God is not a respecter of persons;
ACT 10:35 but in every nation he who feareth him and worketh righteousness is acceptable to him.
ACT 10:36 According to the word which he sent to the children of Israel, when he published the glad tidings of peace by Jesus Christ, He is Lord of all.
ACT 10:37 You know the affair which is spread through all Judea, taking its rise from Galilee after the baptism which John proclaimed respecting Jesus; him from Nazareth
ACT 10:38 how God anointed him with a holy spirit and power. Him who went about doing good, and healing all who were oppressed by the devil; for God was with him,
ACT 10:39 and we are witnesses of all that he did both in the country of the Jews, and in Jerusalem; Him, whom they slew, suspending him on a cross
ACT 10:40 even him God raised up the third day, and granted him to become manifest,
ACT 10:41 not to all the people, but to witnesses who were preappointed by God; to us who have eaten, and drunk with him after he arose from the dead.
ACT 10:42 And he commanded us to proclaim to the people and testify that he is the one determinately pointed out by God to be the judge of the living and the dead.
ACT 10:43 To him all the prophets bear witness, that every one who believeth in him, shall receive remission of sins by his name.
ACT 10:44 While Peter was yet speaking these words the holy spirit fell on all them who heard this word.
ACT 10:45 Whereupon all the circumcised believers who had come with Peter were astonished that the gift of the holy spirit was poured out upon the Gentiles also.
ACT 10:46 For they heard them speaking in divers languages and magnifying God.
ACT 10:47 Then Peter addressed them saying, Can any one on any account forbid water, that these should not be baptized who have received the holy spirit in the same manner as even we did?
ACT 10:48 So he ordered them to be baptized in the name of the Lord. Then they intreated him to stay some days.
ACT 11:1 Now the apostles and the brethren who were in Judea heard that the Gentiles also had received the word of God.
ACT 11:2 So when Peter went up to Jerusalem, they of the circumcision cavilled at him,
ACT 11:3 saying, Thou hast gone to men who are uncircumcised, and hast eaten with them.
ACT 11:4 Thereupon Peter stated to them the whole affair in order from the beginning, saying,
ACT 11:5 I was praying in the city Joppa, and in a trance I saw a vision, a kind of vessel coming down, like a great sheet let down by the four corners, out of heaven, and it came close to me.
ACT 11:6 On which when I fixed mine eyes, I observed and saw the four footed beasts of the earth, namely the wild beasts and the reptiles, and the birds of the air;
ACT 11:7 and I heard a voice saying to me, Rise, Peter; kill and eat.
ACT 11:8 But I said, By no means, Lord; For nothing common or unclean hath ever entered my mouth.
ACT 11:9 Thereupon a voice from heaven addressed me a second time, saying, What God hath cleansed, call not thou that common.
ACT 11:10 Now this was done three times, then all were drawn up again into heaven.
ACT 11:11 And lo! at that instant three men arrived at the house where I was, who were sent to me from Caesarea.
ACT 11:12 And the spirit commanded me to go with them without any scruple. Now there went with me these six brethren. And when we came to the house of the man,
ACT 11:13 he told us how he had seen in his house, the angel standing and saying to him, Send men to Joppa for Simon, surnamed Peter,
ACT 11:14 who will dictate to the matters by which thou and all thy household shall be saved.
ACT 11:15 And when I had begun to speak, the holy spirit fell upon them as it did upon us at the beginning.
ACT 11:16 Then I remembered the word of the Lord how he said, John indeed baptized in water, but ye shall be baptized in a holy spirit.
ACT 11:17 If then God granted the same free gift to them as to us, who believed in the Lord Jesus Christ, who was I, that I should obstruct God?
ACT 11:18 Having heard this they acquiesced and glorified God, saying, God hath then indeed granted to the Gentiles repentance unto life.
ACT 11:19 Now they who had been dispersed by reason of the distress which arose about Stephen, had travelled as far as Phoenicia and Cyprus and Antioch, speaking the word to none but Jews only.
ACT 11:20 But there were some of them, men of Cyprus and Cyrene, who went into Antioch and spoke to the Greeks, proclaiming the glad tidings of the Lord Jesus.
ACT 11:21 And the hand of the Lord was with them, and a great number believed and turned to the Lord.
ACT 11:22 When the report of this reached the ears of the congregation which was at Jerusalem, they sent forth Barnabas to go as far as Antioch.
ACT 11:23 And when he came and saw the grace of God, he was filled with joy and exhorted them all to adhere to the Lord with a firm determination of heart.
ACT 11:24 Because he was a good man and full of a holy spirit and faith, therefore a considerable multitude was added to the Lord.
ACT 11:25 Upon which Barnabas went to Tarsus to seek. Saul.
ACT 11:26 And having found him he brought him to Antioch. And for a whole year they assembled with this congregation, and taught a considerable multitude. And the disciples at Antioch first got the name of Christians.
ACT 11:27 And in those days there came down prophets from Jerusalem to Antioch.
ACT 11:28 And one of them named Agabus rising up signified by the spirit that there would very soon be a great famine throughout the whole inhabited land, which accordingly came to pass in the days of Claudius Caesar.
ACT 11:29 Whereupon the disciples determined, every one according to his ability to send relief to the brethren who dwelt in Judea.
ACT 11:30 And. this they did, sending it to the elders by the hands of Barnabas and Saul.
ACT 12:1 Now about that time Herod the king stretched forth his hands to afflict some of the congregation,
ACT 12:2 and slew with the sword James the brother of John.
ACT 12:3 And as he saw that this pleased the Jews, he proceeded to apprehend Peter also.
ACT 12:4 But as this was during the days of unleavened bread, when he had apprehended him he put him in prison, committing him to the custody of four quaternions of soldiers, intending to bring him out to the people after the passover.
ACT 12:5 So Peter was kept in prison; and there was earnest prayer to God made for him by the congregation.
ACT 12:6 And when Herod was about to bring him forth, on that very night, as Peter was sleeping between two soldiers, being bound with two chains; and the guards before the door were keeping watch,
ACT 12:7 behold an angel of the Lord suddenly appeared, and a light shone in the prison. And touching Peter's side he roused him up, saying, Arise quickly. Upon which his chains dropped from his hands.
ACT 12:8 Then the angel said to him, Gird thyself and put on thy sandals; and when he had done so, then he saith to him, Throw thy mantle around thee and follow me.
ACT 12:9 So going out, he followed him, but did not know that what was done by the angel was real, but thought he saw a vision.
ACT 12:10 And having passed the first and second guard, they came to the iron gate leading into the city, which opened to them of its own accord. So, going out, they proceeded on through one street, and suddenly the angel left him.
ACT 12:11 Then Peter coming to himself, said, Now I know certainly that the Lord hath sent his angel and delivered me out of the hand of Herod, and from all the expectation of the Jews.
ACT 12:12 Then, upon recollection, he went to the house of Mary the mother of John, surnamed Mark, where many were assembled and praying.
ACT 12:13 And when Peter knocked at the door of the gateway, a servant maid named Rhoda, went to inquire who was there.
ACT 12:14 But knowing Peter's voice, she, for joy, did not open the gate, but ran and told that Peter was at the gate.
ACT 12:15 Upon which they said to her, Thou art mad. But she confidently affirmed that it was certainly so: then they said, It is his angel.
ACT 12:16 As Peter continued knocking, they opened the gate, and upon seeing him, were extremely surprised.
ACT 12:17 But he having beckoned to them with his hand to be silent, related to them how the Lord had brought him out of prison, and said, Tell this to James and the brethren. Then departing, he went to another place.
ACT 12:18 Now as soon as it was day there was no small disturbance among the soldiers, What was become of Peter.
ACT 12:19 And Herod  having caused search to be made for him, and not finding him, after examining the guards, he ordered them to be led away to execution. Then departing from Judea, he went down to Caesarea and resided there.
ACT 12:20 Now Herod was meditating a war against the Tyrians and Sidonians; but they with one accord waited on him, and having made Blastus the king's chamberlain their friend, they sued for peace, because their country was subsisted by that of the king.
ACT 12:21 And on a set day Herod arrayed in robes of state and seated on the throne, made a speech to them,
ACT 12:22 upon which the people shouted, It is the voice of a god and not of a man!
ACT 12:23 And instantly an angel of the Lord smote him, because he gave not God the glory. And being gnawed by worms he died.
ACT 12:24 Still the word of God increased and was multiplied;
ACT 12:25 and Barnabas and Saul, having fully performed their service, had returned from Jerusalem, taking with them John who was surnamed Mark.
ACT 13:1 Now there was in the congregation at Antioch, certain prophets and teachers, namely, Barnabas and Symeon called Niger, and Lucius the Cyrenian, and Manaem, who had been brought up with Herod the tetrarch, and Saul.
ACT 13:2 And whilst they were ministering to the Lord, and fasting, the holy spirit said, Set apart for me Barnabas and Saul, for the work to which I have called them.
ACT 13:3 So having fasted and prayed, and laid their hands on them, they dismissed them.
ACT 13:4 They then being sent forth by the holy spirit, went down to Seleucia, and thence sailed to Cyprus.
ACT 13:5 And arriving at Salamis, they proclaimed the word of God in the synagogues of the Jews. And they had John for their attendant.
ACT 13:6 And having traversed the island till they came to Paphos, they found there a magian, a false prophet, a Jew whose name was Barjesus.
ACT 13:7 He was with the proconsul Sergius Paulus, a man of understanding, who had sent for Barnabas and Saul, and desired to hear the word of God.
ACT 13:8 But Elymas the Magian, [for thus his name is translated] set himself against them, endeavouring to divert the proconsul from the belief.
ACT 13:9 Upon which Saul, who is also called Paul, being filled with a holy spirit, and having his eyes fixed upon him,
ACT 13:10 said, O! full of all deceit and of all wickedness, son of the devil, enemy of all righteousness; wilt thou not cease to pervert the right ways of the Lord!
ACT 13:11 Now therefore behold the hand of the Lord is upon thee, and thou shall be blind and shall not see the sun for a season. And instantly there fell upon him a mist and darkness. And groping about he sought some to lead him by the hand.
ACT 13:12 Then the proconsul, upon seeing what was done, believed, being struck with awe at the doctrine concerning the Lord.
ACT 13:13 Now Paul and his company, having taken their departure from Paphos, came to Perga in Pamphylia; but John having withdrawn from them, returned to Jerusalem.
ACT 13:14 They, however, went on from Perga and came to Antioch, in Pisidia, and going into the synagogue on the sabbath day, they sat down.
ACT 13:15 And after the reading of the law and the prophets, the rulers of the synagogue sent to them, saying, Men, brethren, if you have any word of consolation to the people, deliver it.
ACT 13:16 Whereupon Paul stood up and beckoning with his hand for attention, said, Men of Israel and ye who fear God, hearken!
ACT 13:17 The God of the people Israel chose our fathers and exalted the people when they sojourned in the land of Egypt, and with an uplifted arm brought them out of it;
ACT 13:18 and for the space of about forty years bore with their behaviour in the wilderness.
ACT 13:19 And having destroyed seven nations in the land of Chanaan, he distributed their land among them.
ACT 13:20 And after these things, which took up about four hundred and fifty years, he gave them judges till Samuel the prophet.
ACT 13:21 But from that time they desired a king, and God gave them Saul, the son of Kis, a man of the tribe of Benjamin, Forty years.
ACT 13:22 Then having removed him, he raised up for them David to be king, to whom he gave this testimony, "I have found David the son of Jesse, a man according to my heart, who will execute all my orders."
ACT 13:23 Of his seed God hath, according to promise, raised up for Israel a saviour, namely Jesus,
ACT 13:24 before whose appearance John proclaimed a baptism of reformation to all the people of Israel.
ACT 13:25 And as John was fulfilling his course, he said, I am not he whom you suppose me to be; but behold he is coming after me, the latchet of whose shoe I am not worthy to untie.
ACT 13:26 Men, brethren, children of the race of Abraham, and those among you, who fear God, to you the word of this salvation is sent.
ACT 13:27 For the inhabitants of Jerusalem and their chiefs, not knowing him, have indeed by condemning him fulfilled the words of the prophets which are read every sabbath day.
ACT 13:28 Though they found no cause of death, they demanded of Pilate that he should be executed.
ACT 13:29 And when they had accomplished all that was written concerning him, he was taken down from the cross and laid in a tomb.
ACT 13:30 But God raised him from the dead,
ACT 13:31 and for many days he appeared to them who came up with him from Galilee to Jerusalem. They are his witnesses to the people.
ACT 13:32 And we proclaim to you the glad tidings with respect to the promise made to the fathers,
ACT 13:33 That God hath fulfilled it to us their children by raising up Jesus, even as it is written in the second psalm, "Thou art my son, this day I have begotten thee"
ACT 13:34 and that he hath raised him from the dead never more to return to corruption, as he said, "I will give you the gracious promises to David which are faithful:
ACT 13:35 and therefore, in another place, he saith, "Thou wilt not suffer thy holy one to see corruption!"
ACT 13:36 For David indeed, having in his generation answered the purpose of God, went to rest and was laid with his fathers, and saw corruption;
ACT 13:37 but he whom God raised up did not see corruption.
ACT 13:38 Be it known therefore to you, Men, brethren, that by this person remission of sins is proclaimed to you;
ACT 13:39 and that by him every one who believeth is acquitted from all those sins, from which you Could not be acquitted by the law of Moses.
ACT 13:40 Take heed therefore that what is said in the prophets may not come upon you
ACT 13:41 "Behold ye despisers, and express your amaze and vanish. For I am working a work in your days, which you will not believe, though one tell you."
ACT 13:42 And on their going out of the synagogue of the Jews, the Gentiles intreated that these things might be spoken to them, in the interim till the next sabbath.
ACT 13:43 And when the synagogue broke up, many of the Jews and of the devout proselytes followed Paul and Barnabas, who spoke to them and exhorted them to persevere in the grace of God.
ACT 13:44 And on the next sabbath almost the whole city was assembled to hear the word of God.
ACT 13:45 But when the Jews saw the crowds they were filled with zeal and contradicted what was spoken by Paul; contradicting and reviling.
ACT 13:46 Whereupon Paul and Barnabas with great freedom of speech said, It was necessary that the word of God should be first spoken to you. But since you reject it, and judge yourselves unworthy of this everlasting life, behold we turn to the Gentiles
ACT 13:47 for thus the Lord hath commanded us, "I have set thee for the light of nations, that thou mayst be for salvation to the remotest parts of the earth."
ACT 13:48 Upon hearing this, the Gentiles rejoiced and glorified the word of the Lord; and as many as were fitly disposed for everlasting life, believed.
ACT 13:49 And the word of the Lord spread through that whole region.
ACT 13:50 But the Jews stirred up the devout women, even such as were women of rank, and the leading men of the city, and raised a persecution against Paul and Barnabas, and expelled them out of their territories.
ACT 13:51 Upon which they having shaken off the dust of their feet against them, went to Iconium.
ACT 13:52 Now the disciples were filled with joy and a holy spirit,
ACT 14:1 and at Iconium they went in the same manner to the synagogue of the Jews, and spoke so that a great number both of Jews and Greeks believed.
ACT 14:2 But the disbelieving Jews stirred up and disaffected the minds of the Gentiles against the brethren.
ACT 14:3 They, however, staid there a considerable time, speaking boldly for the Lord who gave attestation to the word of his grace, and granted signs and miracles to be done by their hands.
ACT 14:4 So the multitude of the city were divided, some siding with the Jews, and some with the apostles.
ACT 14:5 But as a violent attempt was going to be made, both by the Gentiles and Jews, with their chiefs, to assault and stone them,
ACT 14:6 they having intelligence of it, fled to the cities of Lycaonia; to Lystra and Derbe, and the region around;
ACT 14:7 and proclaimed the glad tidings there.
ACT 14:8 Now at Lystra there sat a man who had no use of his feet, being a cripple from his birth, who had never walked.
ACT 14:9 This man was listening to Paul speaking, who fixing his eyes upon him, and perceiving that he had faith to be healed,
ACT 14:10 said with a loud voice, Stand upright on thy feet. Upon which he leaped up and walked.
ACT 14:11 When the people saw what Paul had done, they lifted up their voice, and, in the Lycaonian dialect, said, "The Gods are come down to us in the likeness of men."
ACT 14:12 And they called Barnabas, Jupiter: and Paul, Mercury; because he was the chief speaker.
ACT 14:13 And the priests of Jupiter's temple which was before their city, brought bulls with garlands to the gates, and together with the multitude, desired to offer a sacrifice.
ACT 14:14 But the apostles Barnabas and Paul, hearing of this, rent their clothes and ran in among the crowd, crying out
ACT 14:15 and saying, Men, why do ye these things? We are only frail mortals like yourselves, proclaiming to you to turn from these vanities to the living God, who made the heaven and the earth, and the sea, and all the things which are therein;
ACT 14:16 who in the ages past suffered all the nations to walk in their own ways,
ACT 14:17 though at the same time he did not fail to give an evidence of himself, by conferring favours, giving us rain from heaven and fruitful seasons, filling our hearts with food and gladness.
ACT 14:18 And with such speeches as these, they, with difficulty, restrained the people from offering them a sacrifice.
ACT 14:19 But there came thither some Jews from Antioch and Iconium, who, having gained over the populace and stoned Paul, dragged him out of the city, supposing him dead.
ACT 14:20 But while the disciples were around him, he arose and went into the city. And on the morrow he departed with Barnabas to Derbe.
ACT 14:21 And when they had proclaimed the glad tidings in that city, and made a considerable number of disciples, they returned to Lystra, and Iconium, and Antioch,
ACT 14:22 establishing and confirming the souls of the disciples, and exhorting them to continue in the faith. And because we must enter into the kingdom of God through many afflictions;
ACT 14:23 they therefore appointed elders for them in every congregation, and having fasted and prayed, they recommended them to the Lord in whom they believed.
ACT 14:24 Then passing through Pisidia, they came to Pamphilia.
ACT 14:25 And having spoken the word in Perga, they went down to Attalia,
ACT 14:26 and thence sailed to Antioch, from which place they had been delivered up to the grace of God, for the work which they had now accomplished.
ACT 14:27 And on their arrival they assembled the congregation and told them all that God had done with them; and that he had opened the door of faith for the Gentiles.
ACT 14:28 Now when they had continued there a considerable time with the disciples,
ACT 15:1 there came down from Judea some persons who taught the brethren, "Unless you be circumcised after the manner of Moses, you cannot be saved."
ACT 15:2 Whereupon, as there arose a dissention, and Paul and Barnabas had no small debate with them, they determined that Paul and Barnabas, and some from among themselves, should go up to the apostles and elders at Jerusalem, about this question.
ACT 15:3 They therefore, being forwarded on their journey by the congregation, passed through Phoenicia and Samaria; and by declaring fully the conversion of the Gentiles, they gave great joy to all the brethren.
ACT 15:4 And when they arrived at Jerusalem they were well received by the congregation, particularly by the apostles and elders, and they gave an account of all that God had done by them.
ACT 15:5 Thereupon some of the sect of the Pharisees who believed, rose up and said, that it was necessary to circumcise those, and order them to keep the law of Moses.
ACT 15:6 And the apostles and elders were convened to deliberate on this matter.
ACT 15:7 And after much debate, Peter arose, and said to them, Men, brethren, you know that a good while ago, God made choice among us that by my mouth the Gentiles should hear the word of these glad tidings and believe.
ACT 15:8 And God who knoweth the heart, bare witness for them, giving them the holy spirit in the same manner as he did to us;
ACT 15:9 and made no distinction between us and them, purifying their hearts by belief.
ACT 15:10 Now therefore why do ye try God, to put upon the neck of the disciples, a yoke which neither our fathers nor we are able to bear?
ACT 15:11 but we trust that we shall be saved by the favour of the Lord Jesus Christ, in the same manner as they do.
ACT 15:12 Upon this the multitude were silent and heard Barnabas and Paul, relating all the signs and wonders which God hath done among the Gentiles by them.
ACT 15:13 And when they had done speaking, James answered and said, Men, brethren, hearken to me,
ACT 15:14 Simeon hath related how God first looked down on the Gentiles, to take from among them a people for his name.
ACT 15:15 And with this the words of the prophets agree, as it is written.
ACT 15:16 "After this I will return and rebuild the tabernacle of David which hath fallen. I will rebuild those parts of it which have fallen to decay, and those parts of it which have been demolished, and raise it up again,
ACT 15:17 that the rest of mankind may seek the Lord; even all the nations who are called by my name, saith the Lord who doth all these things."
ACT 15:18 To God all his works are known from eternity;
ACT 15:19 therefore it is my judgement not to disquiet those of the Gentiles who turn to God;
ACT 15:20 but to enjoin them to abstain from the pollutions of idols, and fornication, and what is strangled, and blood,
ACT 15:21 because from generations of old Moses hath in every city them who preach him, being read in the synagogue every sabbath.
ACT 15:22 It was then determined by the apostles and elders, when they with the whole congregation had chosen chief men from among them, to send with Paul and Barnabas to Antioch, Judas, who is surnamed Barsabas, and Silas, leading men among the brethren,
ACT 15:23 by whom they wrote the following letter. "The apostles and the elders and the brethren, to the brethren from among the Gentiles in Antioch, and Syria and Cilicia,
ACT 15:24 greeting. As we have heard that some who went out from among us have troubled you with discourses, unsettling your minds, saying, You must be circumcised and keep the law, though we gave them no such injunction,
ACT 15:25 we being all of one mind determined that after making a choice, we would send men to you with our beloved Barnabas and Paul,
ACT 15:26 men who have hazarded their lives for the name of our Lord Jesus Christ:
ACT 15:27 we have therefore sent Judas and Silas, who by word of mouth will tell you the same things.
ACT 15:28 For it hath seemed good to the holy spirit and to us to lay upon you, over and above the things absolutely necessary, no more burden than these.
ACT 15:29 To abstain from things offered to idols, and blood, and what is strangled, and fornication, from which you will do well to keep yourselves. Farewell."
ACT 15:30 So they being despatched came to Antioch and assembling the multitude, delivered the letter,
ACT 15:31 and when they had read it, they rejoiced for the consolation.
ACT 15:32 And as Judas and Silas were themselves also teachers, they with many discourses exhorted the brethren, and established them.
ACT 15:33 And having tarried some time they had leave to depart with peace from the brethren to the apostles.
ACT 15:34 But Silas thought proper to continue there.
ACT 15:35 Paul also, and Barnabas, continued at Antioch, teaching and publishing with many others the glad tidings of the word of the Lord.
ACT 15:36 And after some days Paul said to Barnabas, Let us, I pray thee, return and visit our brethren in every city where we have published the word of the Lord, to see how they do.
ACT 15:37 And Barnabas advised to take along with them, John surnamed Mark.
ACT 15:38 But Paul did not think it proper to take along with them one who had quitted them in Pamphylia, and had not gone with them to the work.
ACT 15:39 There was therefore a sharp dispute, so that they separated one from the other. And Barnabas took Mark and sailed to Cyprus.
ACT 15:40 As for Paul, having chosen Silas and being commended by the brethren to the favour of God,
ACT 15:41 he set out and passed through Syria and Cilicia, establishing the congregations
ACT 16:1 and then went down to Derbe and Lystra. And behold there was there a certain disciple, named Timothy, whose mother was a believing Jewess, but his father was a Greek.
ACT 16:2 He was well spoken of by the brethren in Lystra and Iconium.
ACT 16:3 This man Paul wished to go with him. So he took and circumcised him because of the Jews who were in those places, for they all knew that his father was a Greek.
ACT 16:4 And as they passed through the cities they "delivered to their keeping the determinations of the apostles and elders who were at Jerusalem.
ACT 16:5 So the congregations were established in the faith, and grew daily more and more numerous.
ACT 16:6 Now when they had passed through Phrygia and Galatia, [having been restrained by the holy spirit from speaking the word in Asia proper]
ACT 16:7 coming towards Mysia, they attempted to go to Bithynia, but the spirit did not permit them.
ACT 16:8 So passing by Mysia, they went down to Troas.
ACT 16:9 And a vision appeared to Paul in the night; it was a certain man, a Macedonian, standing and intreating him, and saying, Cross over to Macedonia and help us.
ACT 16:10 Therefore as he saw this vision, we immediately endeavoured to go to Macedonia, concluding from it, that the Lord called us to publish the glad tidings to them.
ACT 16:11 So, embarking at Troas, we sailed directly to Samothracia, and the next day to Neapolis,
ACT 16:12 and thence to Philippi, which is a city of the first district of Macedonia, a Roman colony. And in this city we continued several days,
ACT 16:13 and on the sabbath day we went out of the city to the river side, where there was an established place of prayer, and sat down and spoke to the women who had assembled.
ACT 16:14 And a certain woman, named Lydia, a dealer in purple, of the city of Thyatira, a worshipper of God, was listening. The Lord had opened her heart to attend to the things which were spoken by Paul.
ACT 16:15 And when she and her household were baptized, she intreated us saying, If you have judged me to be faithful to the Lord come and lodge at my house. So she prevailed upon us.
ACT 16:16 And it came to pass, as we were going to the oratory, we were met by a certain female slave who had a spirit of Python, and who brought her masters much gain by divining.
ACT 16:17 This girl, following Paul and us, cried, saying, These men are the servants of the most high God. They are telling us the way of salvation.
ACT 16:18 And this she did for many days. At length Paul, being troubled, turned and said to the spirit, I command thee, in the name of Jesus Christ, to go out of her. And at that instant it went out.
ACT 16:19 When her masters saw that the hope of their gain was gone, they laid hold of Paul and Silas and dragged them to the forum, before the magistrates.
ACT 16:20 And having set them before the generals of the army, they said, These men, being Jews, trouble this city of ours exceedingly,
ACT 16:21 and teach customs which it is not lawful for us, who are Romans to receive or practise.
ACT 16:22 Upon this the populace rose up together against them; and the generals ordered them to be stript and beaten with rods.
ACT 16:23 And having inflicted on them many stripe's, they committed them to prison, charging the jailor to keep them safely.
ACT 16:24 He having received such a charge, thrust them into the inner prison, and secured their feet in the stocks.
ACT 16:25 And about midnight Paul and Silas, having prayed, sung a hymn to God; and the prisoners heard them.
ACT 16:26 And suddenly there was a great earthquake, so that the foundations of the prison were shaken, and all the doors were instantly opened,
ACT 16:27 and the fetters of all dropped off. Upon which the jailor awaking, and seeing the doors of the prison open, drew his sword and was just going to kill himself, thinking that the prisoners had escaped.
ACT 16:28 But Paul cried with a loud voice, saying, Do thyself no harm, for we are all here.
ACT 16:29 Thereupon, calling for lights, he ran in, and being in a tremour, prostrated himself before Paul and Silas,
ACT 16:30 and having brought them out, said, O sirs, What must I do to be saved?
ACT 16:31 And they said, Believe in the Lord Jesus Christ, and thou shalt be saved, thou and thy household.
ACT 16:32 Then they spoke the word of the Lord to him, and to all that were in his house.
ACT 16:33 And he taking them that very hour of the night, washed their stripes; and he and all his family were immediately baptized.
ACT 16:34 Then conducting them up to his house, he spread a table and rejoiced with all his family for having believed in God.
ACT 16:35 And in the course of the day the generals sent the lictors, saying, Dismiss those men,
ACT 16:36 When the jailor made this report to Paul, The generals have sent that you may be discharged; now, therefore, depart and go in peace;
ACT 16:37 Paul said to them, Having scourged us publicly without a trial, men who are Roman citizens, they have cast us into prison, and now discharge us privately!
ACT 16:38 No. Let them come themselves and take us out. When the lictors reported these words to the generals, they were terrified, hearing that they are Romans. So
ACT 16:39 they came and comforted them, and having taken them out, intreated them to leave the city.
ACT 16:40 Now when they came out of prison, they went to Lydia's where seeing the brethren, they comforted them and departed;
ACT 17:1 and passing through Amphipolis and Apollonia, they came to Thessalonica, where there was a synagogue of the Jews.
ACT 17:2 And according to his custom, Paul went in among them; and for three sabbaths discoursed to them from the scriptures,
ACT 17:3 opening and stating that the Christ was to suffer .and rise from the dead, and that this Jesus whom I announce to you is The Christ.
ACT 17:4 And some of them were convinced, and associated with Paul and Silas; and a great multitude of the devout Greeks; and of women of distinction not a few.
ACT 17:5 But the disbelieving Jews, affecting zeal, and collecting some ill disposed men of the lowest class, raised a mob and set the city in an uproar; and besetting Jason's house sought to bring them out to the people;
ACT 17:6 but not finding them, they dragged Jason and some brethren before the magistrates of the city, crying out, Those men who have turned the world upside down, are come here also;
ACT 17:7 and Jason hath harboured them, though they all act contrary to the decrees of Caesar, saying, There is another king, one Jesus.
ACT 17:8 So they alarmed the multitude and the magistrates, who heard these things;
ACT 17:9 and these having taken security of Jason and the rest, dismissed them.
ACT 17:10 Now the brethren had immediately sent away Paul and Silas by night to Berea, where being arrived, they went into the synagogue of the Jews.
ACT 17:11 Now these were of a more generous disposition than those of Thessalonica. They received the word with all readiness, daily examining the scriptures whether these things were so,
ACT 17:12 and accordingly many of them believed, and of the Grecian women of rank, and of the men not a few.
ACT 17:13 But when the Jews of Thessalonica knew that the word of God was proclaimed by Paul at Berea, they came thither also and set the populace in a ferment;
ACT 17:14 upon which the brethren immediately sent away Paul towards the sea. But Silas and Timothy continued there.
ACT 17:15 Now they who attended Paul conducted him to Athens, and having received his orders for Silas and Timothy to come to him with all speed, they departed.
ACT 17:16 And while Paul was waiting for them at Athens, his spirit within him was greatly troubled, when he saw the city overspread with idols.
ACT 17:17 Therefore he discoursed in the synagogue to the Jews and proselytes, and in the forum daily to them who met him.
ACT 17:18 And while some of the epicurean and stoic philosophers were conferring with him, some said, "What would this retailer of scraps say?" And others, "He appeareth to be a proclaimer of strange deities." Because he proclaimed the glad tidings of Jesus and the resurrection,
ACT 17:19 therefore they took hold of him and brought him to the Areopagus, saying, May we know what this new doctrine is which is spoken by thee.
ACT 17:20 For thou bringest some strange things to our ears. .We wish therefore to know what these things mean.
ACT 17:21 Now all the Athenians, and the foreigners who reside among them, spent their leisure time in nothing else but in telling and hearing news.
ACT 17:22 Paul then being placed in the midst of the Areopagus, said, Men of Athens, I perceive from every thing I see, that you are exceedingly addicted to the worship of demons.
ACT 17:23 For as I passed along and beheld the objects and instruments of your devotion, I found an altar with this inscription, To The Unknown God. Him, therefore whom you worship without knowing him, I announce to you.
ACT 17:24 He is the God who made the world and all the things which are therein. He is the Lord of heaven and earth. He dwelleth not in temples made with hands;
ACT 17:25 nor is he served by the hands of men, as needing any thing. He is the giver of life and breath, and of all things, to all,
ACT 17:26 and hath made of one blood the whole nation of men to inhabit the whole face of the earth, having marked out times previously arranged in order, and the boundaries of their habitation,
ACT 17:27 for them to seek the Lord if haply they might feel, and find him, though he indeed is not far from any one of us.
ACT 17:28 For in him we live and are moved and exist; as some also of your own poets have said, "For we his offspring are."
ACT 17:29 Being therefore the offspring of God, we ought not to imagine the Deity to be like gold, or silver, or stone, wrought by the art and contrivance of man.
ACT 17:30 God indeed having overlooked the ages of this ignorance; now maketh proclamation to all men every where to reform,
ACT 17:31 because he hath appointed a day in which he will judge the world righteously, by a man whom he hath pointed out: of which he hath given assurance to all men, by raising him. from the dead.
ACT 17:32 When they heard of the resurrection of the dead, some made a jest of it; and some said we will hear thee again on this subject.
ACT 17:33 On which Paul went out from among them.
ACT 17:34 But some men of rank adhered to him and believed, among whom was Dionysius, a member of the Areopagus; also a woman of rank, named Damaris, and others with them.
ACT 18:1 After this Paul departed from Athens and went to Corinth,
ACT 18:2 where finding a certain Jew, named Aquilas, a native of Pontus, who had lately come from Italy with his wife Priscilla, because Claudius had commanded all the Jews to depart out of Rome, he went to them;
ACT 18:3 and being of the same trade, lived and wrought with them; for they were tentmakers.
ACT 18:4 And every sabbath day he discoursed in the synagogue, and conciliated the affections both of Jews and Greeks.
ACT 18:5 But when Silas and Timothy were arrived from Macedonia, Paul was enrapt by the spirit, testifying to the Jews that Jesus is The Christ.
ACT 18:6 And upon their setting themselves against this, and using abusive language, he shook his garments, and said to them, Your blood is on your own head. I am clear. Henceforth I will go to the Gentiles.
ACT 18:7 So having left them, he went to the house of a certain person named Justus, a worshipper of God, whose house was adjoining to the synagogue.
ACT 18:8 Now Crispus, the ruler of the synagogue, with all his household, believed in the Lord: and many of the Corinthians, when they heard, believed and were baptized.
ACT 18:9 And in a vision by night, the Lord said to Paul, Be not afraid, but speak, and keep not silence;
ACT 18:10 for I am with thee; and no one shall set upon thee to hurt thee: for I have much people in this city.
ACT 18:11 So he continued there a year and six months, teaching among them the word of God.
ACT 18:12 Now when Gallio was proconsul of Achaia, the Jews with one accord rose against Paul and brought him to the tribunal,
ACT 18:13 saying, This person persuadeth men to worship God, contrary to the law.
ACT 18:14 And when Paul was about to open his mouth, Gallio said to the Jews, If it were indeed some act of injustice or malicious villainy, I could with reason, O Jews, bear with you.
ACT 18:15 But if it is a question about a word, or names, or your law, you may look to it yourselves; for I will not be a judge of such matters.
ACT 18:16 So he drove them from the tribunal.
ACT 18:17 Then all the Greeks took Sosthenes the ruler of the synagogue, and beat him before the tribunal. But Gallio did not concern himself in the affair.
ACT 18:18 After this Paul having continued there a considerable time longer, took leave of the brethren and sailed to Syria, and with him Priscilla and Aquilas, having shaved his head at Cenchrea, for he had a vow:
ACT 18:19 and touching at Ephesus he left them there. He indeed having gone to the synagogue discoursed to the Jews;
ACT 18:20 but though they requested him to tarry longer with them he would not consent,
ACT 18:21 but took his leave of them, saying, I must by all means keep the ensuing festival at Jerusalem. But I will come back to you again, if God permit. So, sailing from Ephesus
ACT 18:22 he arrived at Casarea; and having gone up and saluted the congregation,
ACT 18:23 he went down to Antioch where he spent some time, and then departed and passed successively through Galatia and Phrygia, establishing all the disciples.
ACT 18:24 In the mean while a certain Jew named Apollos, born at Alexandria, an eloquent man, had come to Ephesus.
ACT 18:25 This man being well versed in the scriptures, had been instructed in the way of the Lord, and being fervent in spirit, he spoke and expounded accurately the passages concerning the Lord, being acquainted only with the baptism of John.
ACT 18:26 And when he began to speak boldly in the synagogue, Aquilas and Priscilla, having heard him, took him home and explained to him more accurately the way of God.
ACT 18:27 And as he was desirous to go to Achaia, the brethren encouraged him and wrote to the disciples to receive him. And being arrived there he by his gift greatly assisted them who had believed,
ACT 18:28 for he strenuously confuted the Jews in public, shewing by the scriptures that Jesus is The Christ.
ACT 19:1 Now while Apollos was at Corinth, Paul having passed through the upper provinces came to Ephesus, where finding2 certain disciples
ACT 19:2 he said to them, Did you receive a holy spirit when you believed? Upon which they said to him, We have not so much as heard that a holy spirit is [received.]
ACT 19:3 There upon he said to them, To what then were ye baptized? And they said, To the baptism of John.
ACT 19:4 Then Paul said, John indeed baptized the baptism of reformation, telling the people that they should believe in one coming after him, namely in Jesus The Christ.
ACT 19:5 Upon hearing this they were baptized to the name of the Lord Jesus;
ACT 19:6 and Paul having laid his hands on them, the holy spirit came upon them and they spoke with tongues and prophesied.
ACT 19:7 Now they were in all about twelve men.
ACT 19:8 Now having gone to the synagogue he spoke boldly for three months, reasoning and recommending the things concerning the kingdom of God.
ACT 19:9 But as some were stubborn disbelievers and continued to revile the way before the multitude, he withdrew from them and separated the disciples, discoursing daily in the school of one Tyrannus.
ACT 19:10 And this he continued to do for the space of two years, so that all the inhabitants of Asia, both Jews and Greeks, heard the word of the Lord Jesus.
ACT 19:11 And God wrought extraordinary miracles by the hands of Paul,
ACT 19:12 so that handkerchiefs and aprons were carried from his body to them who were sick, and the diseases were removed from them, and evil spirits went out of them.
ACT 19:13 Upon this some of the strolling Jewish exorcists attempted to name the name of the Lord Jesus, over them who had these evil spirits, saying, "We adjure you by that Jesus whom Paul proclaimeth"
ACT 19:14 Now there were seven sons of one Sceva, a Jewish chief priest, who did this.
ACT 19:15 Upon which the evil spirit in reply said, Jesus I know, and I have some knowledge of Paul: but who are ye?
ACT 19:16 Then the man, in whom was the evil spirit, springing upon them, and getting a mastery over them, prevailed against them so that they fled out of his house naked and wounded.
ACT 19:17 And this was known to all, both Jews and Greeks, who dwelt at Ephesus; and fear fell upon them all. And the name of the Lord Jesus was magnified.
ACT 19:18 And many of them who believed came and confessed, and made a public acknowledgment of their deeds.
ACT 19:19 And several of them having practised magical arts, brought their books and burned them publicly, the value of them by computation amounting to fifty thousand pieces of silver.
ACT 19:20 So powerfully did the word of the Lord increase and prevail.
ACT 19:21 Now when these things were accomplished, Paul resolved in his mind, after passing through Macedonia and Achaia to go to Jerusalem, saying, after I have been there, I must also see Rome.
ACT 19:22 So having sent forward two of them who attended him, namely Timothy and Erastus, into Macedonia, he himself tarried some time in Asia.
ACT 19:23 And during that time there was a considerable disturbance about this way.
ACT 19:24 For one Demetrius, a silversmith, a maker of silver shrines of Diana, kept in employ a great number of artists;
ACT 19:25 and having assembled these and the workmen of like occupation, he said, "Men, you know that on this manufacture dependeth our maintenance.
ACT 19:26 And you see and hear that not only in Ephesus, but almost throughout all Asia, this Paul by his persuasion hath perverted a vast multitude, saying that they which are made with hands, are not gods.
ACT 19:27 So that not only this occupation of ours is in danger of being brought into disrepute; but the temple also of the great goddess Diana, of .being set at naught; and her majesty destroyed, whom all Asia and the world worshippeth."
ACT 19:28 Upon hearing this and being full of rage they shouted, saying, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
ACT 19:29 And the whole city was filled with confusion. And they rushed with one accord into the theatre, dragging along with them Gaius and Aristarchus, men of Macedonia, Paul's fellow travellers.
ACT 19:30 Upon this Paul had a mind to go to the people, but the disciples did not permit him.
ACT 19:31 And some of the chiefs of Asia also, who were his friends, sent to him and advised him not to venture into the theatre.
ACT 19:32 Now some cried one thing; and some, another. For the congregation was in the utmost confusion, and the greater part did not know for what particular purpose they had convened.
ACT 19:33 But when they had thrust Alexander out of the crowd, the Jews pushing him forward, and Alexander waving his hand wished to make a defence to the people,
ACT 19:34 they knowing that he was a Jew, there was, for about two hours, one continued shout from all, crying out, Great is Diana of the Ephesians.
ACT 19:35 At length the recorder having stilled the crowd, said, Men of Ephesus, who is there who doth not know that the city of the Ephesians is a humble devotee of the great goddess Diana, and of the image which fell from Jupiter?
ACT 19:36 Since these things are incontestable you ought to be quiet, and to do nothing rashly.
ACT 19:37 For you have brought hither these men, who have neither violated things sacred, nor reviled your goddess.
ACT 19:38 If now Demetrius and his fellow craftsmen have an action against any one, the courts are open and there are proconsuls to judge: let them bring their suits.
ACT 19:39 And if you seek any thing in respect to other matters, let it be discussed in a legal assembly of the people.
ACT 19:40 For we indeed are in danger of being called in question for this day's riot, there being no cause which we can assign for this tumultuous concourse. 41 Having said this, he dismissed the assembly.
ACT 20:1 Now this tumult being over, Paul sent for the disciples, and having embraced them, he set out to go to Macedonia.
ACT 20:2 And when he had gone through those parts, and comforted them with many a discourse, he came to Greece,
ACT 20:3 where having spent three months, as an ambush was laid for him by the Jews just as he was on the point of embarking for Syria, he thought it advisable to return through Macedonia.
ACT 20:4 And there accompanied him to Asia, Sopater the Berean; and of the Thessalonians, Aristarchus and Secundus; and Gains, of Derbe; and Timothy; and the Asiatics, Tychicus, and Trophimus.
ACT 20:5 These having gone before, waited for us at Troas;
ACT 20:6 And we, after the days of unleavened bread, set sail from Philippi, and in five days came to them at Troas, where we staid seven days.
ACT 20:7 And on the first day of the week when the disciples assembled to break bread, Paul, being about to depart on the morrow, discoursed with them, and lengthened out the discourse till midnight.
ACT 20:8 Now in the upper room where they were assembled, there were many lamps.
ACT 20:9 And a certain young man named Eutychus, who was sitting in an open window, bending backwards in a deep sleep, was, while Paul was continuing his discourse, bent quite back with the sleep, and fell from the third story, and was taken up dead.
ACT 20:10 But Paul going down, threw himself upon him, and taking him in his arms, said, Be not troubled, for his life is in him.
ACT 20:11 Then going up again, and having broken bread and eaten, he conversed with them a considerable time, even till break of day, and so departed.
ACT 20:12 Now when they brought up the lad alive and were not a little comforted,
ACT 20:13 we went before to the ship and sailed to Assos where we were to take in Paul. For so he had ordered, intending himself to go by land.
ACT 20:14 And when he met us at Assos we took him in and came to Mitylene.
ACT 20:15 And sailing thence we came the next day over against Chios, and on the day following reached Samos. And after stopping at Trogyllium, we came the next day to Miletus.
ACT 20:16 For Paul had determined to sail by Ephesus, that he might not spend time in Asia, for he was earnestly desirous, if it were possible for him, to be at Jerusalem on the day of Pentecost.
ACT 20:17 So from Miletus he sent to Ephesus, and called hither the elders of the congregation.
ACT 20:18 And when they came to him, he said to them, You know how from my first coming into Asia, I have been with you all the time,
ACT 20:19 serving the Lord with all humility, and with many tears and trials which befel me by the insidious practices of the Jews;
ACT 20:20 how I have never shrunk from those things which are advantageous; from announcing to you and teaching you publicly and privately,
ACT 20:21 attesting both to Jews and Greeks the turning of the mind to God, and the belief in our Lord Jesus Christ.
ACT 20:22 Now behold I am going up to Jerusalem, bound by the spirit, not knowing the things which shall befal me there,
ACT 20:23 save only that the Holy spirit testifieth in every city, saying, That bonds and afflictions await me.
ACT 20:24 But I make no account of any of these, nor is this life of mine so much my concern as to finish with joy my course; even the office which I have received from the Lord Jesus, to testify the glad tidings of the favour of God.
ACT 20:25 And now behold I know that all you among whom I have gone proclaiming the reign of God, shall no more see my face;
ACT 20:26 therefore I testify to you this day that I am clear from the blood of all men.
ACT 20:27 For I have not shrunk from declaring to you the whole counsel of God.
ACT 20:28 Take heed therefore to yourselves and to the whole flock among which the holy spirit hath made you overseers to tend the congregation of God which he hath purchased with his own blood.
ACT 20:29 For this I know, that after my departure there will enter in among you grievous wolves, not sparing the flock.
ACT 20:30 Yes, even from among yourselves men will start up, speaking perverse things to draw the disciples after them.
ACT 20:31 Watch therefore, remembering that for the space of three years I did not cease, night nor day, with tears to warn every one.
ACT 20:32 And now with regard to these things I recommend you, brethren, to God and to the word of his grace, who is able to build you up and to give you an inheritance among all who are sanctified.
ACT 20:33 I have coveted no man's silver or gold, or raiment.
ACT 20:34 Even you yourselves know that these very hands have ministered to my wants, and to the supply of them who were with me.
ACT 20:35 On all occasions I have suggested to you that you ought thus to labour, and support the indigent, and to remember the words of the Lord Jesus, that he said, "It is a greater happiness to give, than to receive."
ACT 20:36 And when he had thus spoken, he kneeled down with them all and prayed.
ACT 20:37 And there was great weeping among them all; and they fell upon Paul's neck and kissed him,
ACT 20:38 being more particularly afflicted at his having said, that they should see his face no more.
ACT 21:1 Then they conducted him to the ship; and soon as we were parted from them and clear of the land, keeping a straight course we came to Coos, and the next day to Rhodes, and thence to Patara;
ACT 21:2 where finding a vessel bound to Phoenicia, we went aboard and set sail.
ACT 21:3 And coming in sight of Cyprus, and leaving it on the left, we sailed for Syria and arrived at Tyre; for the ship was to land her cargo there.
ACT 21:4 And having by diligent inquiry found out the disciples, we staid there seven days. Some of these told Paul by the spirit not to go up to Jerusalem.
ACT 21:5 But when these days were ended, we set out on our departure, they, with women and children, all attending us out of the city, and kneeling down on the sea shore, we prayed;
ACT 21:6 then having saluted each other, we embarked, and they returned home.
ACT 21:7 And when we had finished the voyage from Tyre, we landed at Ptolemais, and having saluted the brethren, staid with them one day.
ACT 21:8 And on the morrow we who were Paul's company, departed and came to Caesarea, and going to the house of Philip the evangelist, who was one of the seven, we abode with him.
ACT 21:9 Now he had four virgin daughters who were prophetesses.
ACT 21:10 And after we had been there several days, there came down from Judea a prophet named Agabus,
ACT 21:11 who coming to us and taking Paul's girdle, bound his own hands and feet and said, Thus saith the holy spirit, So will the Jews at Jerusalem bind the man, whose girdle this is, and deliver him into the hands of the Gentiles.
ACT 21:12 Upon hearing this both we and they of that place in treated him not to go up to Jerusalem.
ACT 21:13 But Paul answered, Why make ye this ado, weeping and breaking my heart? As for me, I am ready, not only to be bound, but even to die at Jerusalem for the name of the Lord Jesus.
ACT 21:14 So, as he could not be prevailed on, we acquiesced, saying, "The will of the Lord be done."
ACT 21:15 And after those days we got ready and went up to Jerusalem.
ACT 21:16 And some of the disciples came with us from Csesarea and brought us to one Mnason, a Cyprian, an old disciple, with whom we were to lodge.
ACT 21:17 Now when we arrived at Jerusalem, the brethren received us with joy.
ACT 21:18 And on the day following Paul went with us to James. And when all the elders were come,
ACT 21:19 he saluted them and gave them a particular account of all that God had done among the Gentiles by his ministry;
ACT 21:20 which when they heard, they glorified the Lord, and said to him, Thou seest, brother, how many myriads there are of believing Jews, and they are all zealous observers of the law.
ACT 21:21 Now they have been informed concerning thee, that thou teachest all the Jews who are among the Gentiles to abandon Moses, telling them not to circumcise their children, nor walk in the established rites.
ACT 21:22 What then is to be done? At all events the multitude must needs assemble; for they will hear that thou art come.
ACT 21:23 Do this then which we tell thee: there are four men with us who have a vow upon them.
ACT 21:24 Take these and purify thyself with them, and be at charges for them that they may shave their heads; and that all may know that there is nothing in those things of which they have been told concerning thee; but that thou thyself walkest regularly, keeping the law.
ACT 21:25 Now with respect to the Gentiles who have believed, we have sent them our decision; that they are not to observe such things, but only to abstain from what is offered to idols, and from blood, and from what is strangled, and from fornication.
ACT 21:26 So Paul took the men, and the next day being purified with them he went into the temple, announcing the full term of the days of the purification, even to the time when the offering for each of them was to be made;
ACT 21:27 but as the seven days were to be completed, the Jews from Asia, having seen him in the temple, threw all the multitude into confusion, and laid hands on him,
ACT 21:28 crying out, Men of Israel help; This is the man who is continually teaching all men every where against the people and the law and this very place; and moreover he hath brought Greeks into the temple and defiled this holy place.
ACT 21:29 [For they had before seen Trophimus, the Ephesian, in the city with him, and imagined that Paul had brought him into the temple.]
ACT 21:30 Upon this the whole city was moved, and there was a concourse of the people; and laying hold on Paul they dragged him out of the temple, and immediately the gates were shut.
ACT 21:31 And while they were seeking to kill him, a report came to the commander of the cohort that all Jerusalem Was in commotion.
ACT 21:32 Upon which he instantly took soldiers and centurions and ran in among them. And when they saw the commander and the soldiers, they left off beating Paul.
ACT 21:33 Then the commander drew near and arrested him, and ordered him to be bound with two chains, and demanded who he was and what he had done.
ACT 21:34 And as some in the crowd cried one thing, and some another, and he could not know the certainty by reason of the tumult, he ordered him to be brought into the castle.
ACT 21:35 And when he was on the stairs it happened that Paul was carried up by the soldiers, on account of the violence of the crowd.
ACT 21:36 For the multitude of the people followed, crying, Away with him.
ACT 21:37 So, when Paul was just about to enter the castle, he said to the commander, May I be favoured with a word to thee? Upon which he said, Canst thou speak Greek?
ACT 21:38 Art thou not the Egyptian who some time ago raised an insurrection, and led out into the wilderness four thousand of the assassins?
ACT 21:39 Thereupon Paul said, I am indeed a Jew of Tarsus, in Cilicia, a citizen of no inconsiderable city, I intreat thee therefore, permit me to speak to the people.
ACT 21:40 And on his giving permission, Paul standing on the stairs waved his hand to the people; and a great silence taking place, he addressed them in the Hebrew dialect, saying,
ACT 22:1 brethren and fathers, hear my defence which I now make to you.
ACT 22:2 [And when they heard that he spoke to them in the Hebrew dialect, they were the more silent, whereupon he said,]
ACT 22:3 I indeed am a Jew, born at Tarsus, in Cilicia, but brought up in this city, instructed accurately at the feet of Gamaliel in the law of our fathers, being a zealous worshipper of God as you all are at this day;
ACT 22:4 one who persecuted this sect to death, binding and delivering into custody both men and women,
ACT 22:5 as even the chief priest and the whole Sanhedrim can witness for me; from whom when I had received letters to the brethren at Damascus, I went with a design to bring those also who were there, in chains to Jerusalem, that they might be punished.
ACT 22:6 But it came to pass that when I was on the journey and drawing near to Damascus, about mid-day, a great light from heaven suddenly flashed around me.
ACT 22:7 Upon which I fell to the ground, and I heard a voice saving to me, Saul, Saul, Why persecutest thou me?
ACT 22:8 And I answered, Lord, who art thou? And he said to me, I am Jesus the Nazarene, whom thou art persecuting.
ACT 22:9 Now they who were with me saw indeed the light and were terrified, but did not hear the voice of him who spake to me.
ACT 22:10 Then I said, Lord, what am I to do? And the Lord said to me, Arise and go to Damascus, and there thou shall be told of all that is appointed for thee to do.
ACT 22:11 But as I could not see, by reason of the glory of that light, being led by them who were with me, I went to Damascus,
ACT 22:12 where one Ananias, a devout man according to the law, in high repute with all the Jewish inhabitants,
ACT 22:13 came to me, and standing near me, said, Brother Saul, look up. And that instant I looked up upon him.
ACT 22:14 Then he said, The God of our fathers hath prepared thee to know his will and to see the righteous one, and to hear a voice from his mouth,
ACT 22:15 that thou mayst be a witness for him to all men of what thou hast seen and heard.
ACT 22:16 Now therefore why delayest thou? Arise, baptize and wash thee from thy sins, calling upon the name of the Lord.
ACT 22:17 And it came to pass when I returned to Jerusalem and was praying in the temple, that I fell into a trance
ACT 22:18 and saw him saying to me, Make haste and depart speedily out of Jerusalem; for they will not receive thy testimony concerning me.
ACT 22:19 Whereupon I said, Lord, they know that I am one who imprisoned and scourged in the synagogues them who believed in thee
ACT 22:20 and when the blood of thy witness Stephen was shed, I was standing by and gladly consenting to the slaughter of him, and watching the clothes of them who were killing him.
ACT 22:21 And he said to me, Depart, for I will send thee to far distant nations.
ACT 22:22 Now till that Word they had continued listening to him; then they raised their voice saying, Away with such a one from the earth, for it is not fit that he should live.
ACT 22:23 And as they continued to cry aloud and were casting off their mantles and throwing dust in the air,
ACT 22:24 the commander ordered him to be brought into the castle and examined by scourging that he might know for what cause they raised such an outcry against him.
ACT 22:25 But while they were straining him with thongs, Paul said to the centurion who stood by, Is it lawful for you to scourge a man who is a Roman, and hath not had a trial.
ACT 22:26 Upon hearing this the centurion went to the commander and told him, saying, Consider what thou art about to do; for this man is a Roman.
ACT 22:27 Thereupon the commander came and said to him, Tell me. Art thou a Roman? And he said, Yes.
ACT 22:28 The commander replied, I bought that right of citizenship with a large sum. And Paul said, I had it by birth.
ACT 22:29 They therefore who were going to put him to the question, departed from him immediately. And the commander was afraid, knowing that he was a Roman, and that he had been tying him up.
ACT 22:30 And on the next morning, as he was desirous to know certainly what it was of which he was accused by the Jews, he loosed him from the chains and ordered the chief priests and their whole Sanhedrim to meet; and having brought Paul down he set him before them.
ACT 23:1 Then Paul having fixed his eyes on the Sanhedrim said, Men, brethren, I have conducted myself with an entire good conscience as a subject of God even to this day.
ACT 23:2 Upon which the chief priest Ananias ordered them who stood by him to smite him on the mouth.
ACT 23:3 Whereupon Paul said to him, God is about to smite thee, thou whited wall! Dost thou sit to judge according to the law, and in defiance of the law order me to be smitten?
ACT 23:4 Upon this the bystanders said. Dost thou revile the chief priest of God?
ACT 23:5 And Paul said. Brethren, I was not aware that he is chief priest: for it is written, Thou shalt not speak evil of the ruler of thy people.
ACT 23:6 Paul then perceiving that the one part were Sadducees; and the other Pharisees, cried aloud in the Sanhedrim, Men, brethren, I am a Pharisee, a son of a Pharisee. For a hope even of a resurrection of the dead I am now to be judged.
ACT 23:7 And on his saying this there arose a dissention between the Pharisees and the Sadducees, and the multitude was divided.
ACT 23:8 For the Sadducees say, There is no resurrection nor any angel nor spirit; but the Pharisees acknowledge both.
ACT 23:9 And there was a great clamour. And the Scribes, siding with the Pharisees, arose and contended, saying, We find nothing amiss in this man. If a spirit or an angel hath spoken to him, let us not fight against God.
ACT 23:10 And as the tumult increased, the commander, apprehensive that Paul might be torn in pieces by them, ordered the army to march down and take him from among them and bring him into the castle.
ACT 23:11 Now the night following, the Lord standing by him said, "Paul be of good courage; for as thou hast testified concerning me at Jerusalem, so thou must bear witness at Rome also."
ACT 23:12 And in the course of the day some of the Jews, having entered into a conspiracy, bound themselves by the solemn Anathema, saying they would neither eat nor drink till they had killed Paul.
ACT 23:13 And there were more than forty who took this oath,
ACT 23:14 and who went to the chief priests and elders and said, We have bound ourselves by the solemn Anathema not to taste any thing till we have slain Paul.
ACT 23:15 Now therefore do you with the Sanhedrim make application to the commander that he may bring him down to you to morrow, as being about to examine his affair more minutely. And as for us, before he come near, we are prepared to kill him.
ACT 23:16 But Paul's sister's son hearing of the plot, went to the castle and being admitted told Paul.
ACT 23:17 Whereupon Paul called one of the centurions and said, Introduce this young man to the commander, for he hath something to tell him.
ACT 23:18 He therefore took him along and conducting him to the commander said, Paul the prisoner called me to him, and desired me to introduce to thee this young man who hath something to tell thee.
ACT 23:19 Thereupon the commander took him by the hand, and retiring to a private place asked, What is it that thou hast to tell me?
ACT 23:20 And he said, The Jews have agreed to request thee to bring down Paul to morrow to the Sanhedrim, under a pretence of making some more minute inquiry concerning him;
ACT 23:21 but be not prevailed on by them; for there are more than forty men of them in ambush, who have bound themselves by a solemn anathema not to eat nor drink, till they have killed him, and they are now ready, expecting this promise from thee.
ACT 23:22 Upon this the commander dismissed the young man with this charge, Tell no one that thou hast given me this information.
ACT 23:23 Then calling two of the centurions he said, Get ready two hundred soldiers to go to Caesarea, and seventy horsemen, and two hundred spearmen, by the third hour of the night
ACT 23:24 and provide beasts that they may mount Paul and conduct him safe to Felix the general.
ACT 23:25 Then he wrote a letter of which this is a copy.
ACT 23:26 Claudius Lysias to his excellency general Felix, health and happiness.
ACT 23:27 This man was seized by the Jews and just upon the point of being slain by them, when I came with the army and rescued him. Having learned that he is a Roman
ACT 23:28 and being desirous to know the crime of which they accused him, I took him down to their Sanhedrim,
ACT 23:29 and found that he was accused of matters touching questions of their law, but had done nothing that deserved death or imprisonment.
ACT 23:30 But receiving intelligence of a plot against the man, which the Jews were in act to execute, I have sent him to thee and directed his accusers to lay before thee their charges against him. Farewell.
ACT 23:31 The soldiers therefore, pursuant to their orders, took Paul and conducted him that night to Antipatris
ACT 23:32 and on the morrow returned to the castle leaving the horse to go on with him.
ACT 23:33 These on their arrival at Caesarea delivered the letter to the general and presented Paul to him.
ACT 23:34 And when the general had read the letter, he asked him of what province he was. And being informed that he was of Cilicia,
ACT 23:35 I will hear thee, said he, when thy accusers are also come. And he ordered him to be kept in Herod's praetorium.
ACT 24:1 And after five days the chief priest, Ananias, came down with the elders and one Tertullus, an orator, and laid before the general an accusation against Paul.
ACT 24:2 And he being called up, Tertullus began the accusation, saying, As we enjoy great peace by thy means, and from thy prudent administration great benefits result to this nation,
ACT 24:3 we on all occasions and every where acknowledge this, most excellent Felix, with all gratitude.
ACT 24:4 But that I may not further trouble thee, I beseech thee to hear us in brief with thy usual indulgence.
ACT 24:5 For having found this man to be a pest and a mover of sedition, among all the Jews, through the whole empire, and a ringleader of the sect of the Nazarenes,
ACT 24:6 and who attempted to profane even the temple, we apprehended him, and would have judged him according to our law;
ACT 24:7 but Lysias the commander coming with a strong force, took him out of our hands
ACT 24:8 and ordered his accusers to come to thee. By examining the man himself thou canst gain a full knowledge of all these things of which we accuse him.
ACT 24:9 And the Jews gave assent, affirming that these things were so.
ACT 24:10 In answer to this, when the general beckoned to him to speak, Paul replied. Knowing that thou hast been for many years a judge to this nation, I enter upon my defence with the more cheerfulness,
ACT 24:11 as thou canst know that it is not more than twelve days since I went up to worship at Jerusalem.
ACT 24:12 And they neither found me disputing with any man in the temple; nor raising sedition among the people, either in the synagogues or in the city:
ACT 24:13 nor can they prove any of the things which they now lay to my charge.
ACT 24:14 But this I confess to thee, that after the way which they call a sect, I worship the God of our fathers, believing all the institutes of the law and the writings of the prophets;
ACT 24:15 having a confidence in God, which they themselves also entertain, that there will be a resurrection of the dead, both of the just and the unjust;
ACT 24:16 and with this I exercise myself to have a conscience void of offence before God and men continually.
ACT 24:17 Now after many years I went to bring contributions for my nation and religious offerings;
ACT 24:18 in which [services] some Jews from Asia found me purified in the temple, without crowd or tumult.
ACT 24:19 Those ought to have been present before thee, and to bring their accusation, if they had, any against me.
ACT 24:20 Or let these men themselves say whether, when I stood before the Sanhedrim, they found any crime in me;
ACT 24:21 unless it be for this single expression which I uttered while standing among them, "That for the resurrection of the dead I am this day to be judged by you."
ACT 24:22 When Felix heard these things he put them off, saying, Having gained a more accurate knowledge of the things respecting this way when Lysias the commander comes down, I will inquire fully into your business.
ACT 24:23 And he gave orders to the centurion that Paul be kept in custody, not closely confined; and that none of his friends be hindered from assisting him or coming to him.
ACT 24:24 And after some days Felix came with his wife Drusilla, who was a Jewess, and sent for Paul and heard him concerning the faith in Christ.
ACT 24:25 And while Paul was discoursing concerning justice and temperance, and the judgment to come, Felix, being terrified, said, Go thy way for the present, and when I find a convenient time I will send for thee:
ACT 24:26 hoping withal that money would be given him by Paul that he might discharge him, and for this cause he sent for him the oftener, and conversed with him.
ACT 24:27 After two years however Felix was succeeded by Portius Festus, and being desirous to ingratiate himself with the Jews, Felix left Paul bound.
ACT 25:1 Therefore when Festus came to the government and three days after went up from Caesarea to Jerusalem,
ACT 25:2 the chief priests and the principal men of the Jews laid before him an information against Paul
ACT 25:3 and earnestly intreated him to favour them so far as to send for him to Jerusalem; [they having laid an ambush to kill him on the road.]
ACT 25:4 Whereupon Festus replied, that Paul was in custody at Caesarea and that he himself would shortly set out thither.
ACT 25:5 Therefore, said he, Let the chief men among you go down with me; and if there be any thing criminal in the man, let them accuse him.
ACT 25:6 So when he had tarried among them more than ten days he went down to Caesarea, and on the morrow taking his seat on the tribunal he ordered Paul to be brought.
ACT 25:7 And when he appeared, the Jews who had come down from Jerusalem stood around and brought many heavy accusations against Paul, which they could not prove.
ACT 25:8 To which when Paul replied, Neither against the law of the Jews, nor against the temple, nor against Caesar, have I committed any offence,
ACT 25:9 Festus willing to gratify the Jews addressed Paul saying, Wilt thou go up to Jerusalem, and be judged there before me concerning these things?
ACT 25:10 Upon which Paul said, I stand at Caesar's judgment seat, where I ought to be judged. To the Jews I have done no wrong, as thou thyself well knowest.
ACT 25:11 If indeed I am guilty, or have committed any capital crime, I do not deprecate death: but if the charges which they bring against me be groundless, no man can give me up to gratify them. I appeal to Caesar.
ACT 25:12 Then Festus, having conferred with his council, replied, Thou hast appealed to Caesar. To Caesar thou shall go.
ACT 25:13 Some days after, king Agrippa and Bernice came down to Caesarea to pay their respects to Festus,
ACT 25:14 and as they spent many days there Festus stated Paul's case to the king, saying, There is a man who was left a prisoner by Felix,
ACT 25:15 concerning whom, when I was at Jerusalem, the chief priests and the elders of the Jews laid an information, soliciting judgment against him.
ACT 25:16 To whom I made answer that it is not customary with the Romans to give up any man to destruction, till he who is accused is confronted with his accusers, and hath an opportunity to make a defence respecting the charge:
ACT 25:17 therefore when they came hither, I without any delay ascended the tribunal the next day, and ordered the man to be brought up.
ACT 25:18 Against whom, when the accusers stood up, they advanced no charge of such things as I expected,
ACT 25:19 but objected against him some disputed points relative to their peculiar mode of worship, and respecting one Jesus who had died, whom Paul affirmed to be alive.
ACT 25:20 And as I was at a loss how to decide in such a case, I asked him, if he would go to Jerusalem and be tried there respecting these matters.
ACT 25:21 But Paul having appealed that his cause should be referred to the cognisance of the Emperor, I ordered him to be kept in custody, till I can send him to Caesar.
ACT 25:22 Upon which Agrippa said to Festus, I could wish myself to hear the man. Tomorrow then, said he, thou shalt hear him.
ACT 25:23 On the morrow therefore, when Agrippa and Bernice were come with a numerous splendid retinue and had entered the hall of audience, with the commanders of cohorts and the principal men of the city, at the command of Festus, Paul was brought.
