ACT 25:24 And Festus said, King Agrippa, and all you who are here present with us, You see this man, about whom the whole body of the Jews have made application to me, both at Jerusalem and in this place, crying out that he ought not to live any longer.
ACT 25:25 But as for me, finding that he had done nothing which deserved death, and he himself having appealed to the Emperor, I have determined to send him.
ACT 25:26 Now as I have nothing certain to write to my master concerning him; I have therefore brought him out before you and especially before thee, king Agrippa, that after this examination, I may have something to write.
ACT 25:27 For to me it seemeth absurd to send a prisoner without specifying the charge against him.
ACT 26:1 Then Agrippa said to Paul, Thou art permitted to speak for thyself. Upon which Paul stretched forth his hand and made this defence.
ACT 26:2 Touching all the things of which I am accused by the Jews, I think myself happy, O king Agrippa, that I am this day to make my defence before thee,
ACT 26:3 specially skilled as thou art in all the Jewish customs and controversies; therefore I beseech thee to hear me patiently.
ACT 26:4 My course of life; that from my youth; that which from the beginning was led among my own nation at Jerusalem, is known to all the Jews.
ACT 26:5 They have a prior knowledge of me from an early period, if they would testify, that according to the strictest sect of our religion I lived a Pharisee.
ACT 26:6 And now I stand arraigned for a hope of the promise which God made to our fathers,
ACT 26:7 and which our twelve tribes, by their continual services night and day, hope to obtain: for which hope, O king Agrippa, I am accused by the Jews.
ACT 26:8 It is deemed among you somewhat incredible that God raiseth the dead;
ACT 26:9 as for me I indeed myself thought that I ought to do many things in opposition to the name of Jesus the Nazarene.
ACT 26:10 And this I did at Jerusalem: and many of the saints I shut up in prison, having received this authority from the chief priests. And when they were put to death, I gave assent.
ACT 26:11 And in all the synagogues many a time did I, by torments, urge them to blaspheme. And being transported to madness against them, I pursued them even to foreign cities.
ACT 26:12 With which views when I was going to Damascus, with authority, and a commission which I had from the chief priests,
ACT 26:13 in the middle of the day, on the road, I saw, O king, a light from heaven, exceeding the brightness of the sun, flashing around me and them who were accompanying me.
ACT 26:14 And when we had all fallen to the ground, I heard a voice speaking to me and in the Hebrew dialect, saying, Saul, Saul, why persecutes thou me? It is hurting thyself to kick against sharp pointed goads.
ACT 26:15 And I said, Lord, who art thou? And he said, I am Jesus, whom thou art persecuting.
ACT 26:16 But arise, and stand on thy feet; for I have appeared to thee for this purpose, to appoint thee a minister and a witness of the things which thou hast seen, and of the things for which I will appear to thee,
ACT 26:17 delivering thee from the people and the nations to which I now send thee
ACT 26:18 to open their eyes, that they may turn from darkness to light and from the power of satan to God, that they may receive a remission of sins and an inheritance among them who are sanctified by the belief in me.
ACT 26:19 From that time, O king Agrippa, I was not disobedient to the heavenly vision,
ACT 26:20 but made proclamation first to them at Damascus, then at Jerusalem and throughout all the country of Judea, and to the nations, to reform and turn to God, performing works worthy of the change of mind.
ACT 26:21 For these things the Jews seized me in the temple, and attempted to kill me.
ACT 26:22 Having therefore obtained help from God, I have continued to this day, testifying both to small and great, saying nothing but what the prophets have said were to come to pass; particularly Moses,
ACT 26:23 that the Christ should suffer, that he the first of a resurrection from the dead is to proclaim light to the people and the nations.
ACT 26:24 While Paul was thus making his defence, Festus said with a loud voice, Paul thou art distracted. Those many writings whirl thee to madness.
ACT 26:25 To which he replied, I am not mad, most noble Festus; but am speaking the words of truth and soberness.
ACT 26:26 For the king is acquainted with these things, to whom therefore I speak with freedom. For I am persuaded that none of these things have escaped his notice. For this hath not been done in a corner.
ACT 26:27 Thou, O king Agrippa, believest the prophets? I know that thou believest.
ACT 26:28 Upon this Agrippa said to Paul, Thou almost persuadest me to become a Christian.
ACT 26:29 And Paul said, I would to God, that not only thou, but also all who hear me this day, were both almost and altogether such as I am, except these chains.
ACT 26:30 And as he was saying this, the king rose up, and the general and Bernice and they who sat with them.
ACT 26:31 And as they were withdrawing, they conferred with each other, saying, This man hath done nothing that deserveth death or chains.
ACT 26:32 And Agrippa said to Festus, This man might have been set at liberty if he had not appealed to Caesar.
ACT 27:1 So, as it was determined that we should sail to Italy, they delivered Paul and some other prisoners, to a certain centurion, named Julius, of the Augustan cohort.
ACT 27:2 And having embarked in a vessel of Adramyttium, we set sail, intending to coast along the shores of Asia, Aristarchus a Macedonian of Thessalonica being with us.
ACT 27:3 And on the next day we touched at Sidon, where Julius, who treated Paul with great humanity, suffered him to go to his friends and enjoy the benefit of their care.
ACT 27:4 Having taken our departure from this place we sailed close under Cyprus, because the winds were contrary.
ACT 27:5 And traversing the sea over against Cilicia and Pamphylia, we came to Myra of Lycia,
ACT 27:6 where the centurion met with a ship of Alexandria, bound for Italy, and put us on board it.
ACT 27:7 And sailing slowly for several days and having hardly got over against Cnidus, the wind not favouring us, we sailed close under Crete over against Salmone;
ACT 27:8 and weathering this with much ado came to a place called Fair-haven, near to which is the city Lasea.
ACT 27:9 Much time being spent and the navigation now dangerous [for it was now after the fast,] Paul gave them warning,
ACT 27:10 saying to them, Sirs, I perceive that this voyage will be attended with damage and no small risk, not only of the vessel and cargo, but also of our lives.
ACT 27:11 But the centurion paid greater regard to the pilot and the master of the vessel than to what Paul said.
ACT 27:12 And as the harbour was not convenient for a winter station, the greater part advised to depart thence and try to reach Phenice; a port in Crete looking south west and north west, to winter there.
ACT 27:13 So a gentle breeze springing up from the south. they, confident of gaining their point, weighed anchor and sailed close along Crete.
ACT 27:14 But not long after there arose against it a tempestuous wind, which is called Euroclydon,
ACT 27:15 and the vessel being hurried away and not able to look up to the wind, we were forced to let her drive.
ACT 27:16 And running close under a little island called Clauda, we had much ado to secure the boat:
ACT 27:17 Having hoisted this in they used helps, undergirding the ship. And fearing lest they should run on the quicksands, they lowered the sail and so were driven.
ACT 27:18 But as we were exceedingly tossed by the tempest, they on the next day threw overboard some of the cargo.
ACT 27:19 And on the third day we with our own hands threw overboard the tackling of the ship.
ACT 27:20 Now as neither sun nor stars appeared for several days, and the tempest still bore hard upon us, all hopes of escaping were at last taken away.
ACT 27:21 And there being then a great abstinence from food, Paul standing in the midst of them said, Sirs, you ought to have hearkened to me and not sailed from Crete and incurred this damage and risk.
ACT 27:22 However, for the present, I exhort you to be of good courage, for there will be no loss of any life among you, but of the ship only.
ACT 27:23 For an angel of God, whose I am, and whom I serve, stood by me last night,
ACT 27:24 and said, Fear not, Paul. Thou must appear before Caesar; and lo! God hath given thee all them who are sailing with thee.
ACT 27:25 Therefore take courage, sirs: for I have a confidence in God that the result will be just as it hath been told me.
ACT 27:26 But we must be shipwrecked on some island.
ACT 27:27 So when the fourteenth night was come, while we were driving about in the Adriatic sea, about midnight, the sailors suspected that they were approaching some land.
ACT 27:28 And upon sounding they found twenty fathoms. And proceeding a little further they sounded again, and found fifteen fathoms.
ACT 27:29 So fearing lest they should run ashore among rocks, they dropped four anchors from the stern and wished for day.
ACT 27:30 But the sailors seeking to flee from the ship, and having hoisted out the boat under a pretence of carrying out anchors from the bow,
ACT 27:31 Paul said to the centurion and the soldiers, Unless those continue  in the ship, you cannot be saved.
ACT 27:32 Upon this the soldiers cut the ropes of the boat and let it go adrift.
ACT 27:33 And while day was coming on, Paul advised them all to take some refreshment, saying, Longing for this fourteenth day you continue fasting, having taken nothing.
ACT 27:34 Therefore I intreat you to take refreshment, for this is conducive to your safety: for not a hair shall fall from the head of any of you.
ACT 27:35 And having said this he took bread, and gave thanks to God in the presence of them all, and having broken it began to eat.
ACT 27:36 And they all became cheerful and also took nourishment.
ACT 27:37 Now we in the ship were in all two hundred and seventy six souls.
ACT 27:38 And when they had satisfied themselves with food, they lightened the vessel, throwing out the corn into the sea.
ACT 27:39 And when it was day they did not know the land; but they observed a creek convenient for landing, into which they determined, if possible, to force the ship.
ACT 27:40 So having got rid of the anchors, leaving them in the sea, and at the same time loosing the bands of the rudder and hoisting the mainsail to the wind, they pressed towards the shore.
ACT 27:41 And coming to a place where two currents met, they ran the ship aground. And the prow stuck fast and remained immoveable; but the stern was broken to pieces by the force of the waves.
ACT 27:42 It was now the counsel of the soldiers to kill the prisoners, lest any should swim away and escape.
ACT 27:43 But the centurion desirous to save Paul prevented their design and ordered those who could swim to throw themselves out first and get to land;
ACT 27:44 and the rest, some on planks, and some on pieces of the vessel: and so it came to pass that all got safe to land.
ACT 28:1 And having escaped, they then knew that the island was called Melita.
ACT 28:2 Now the barbarians treated us with uncommon humanity; for having kindled a fire they took us all to it, because of the3 present rain, and because of the cold.
ACT 28:3 And as Paul having gathered a bundle of sticks was laying them on the fire, a viper coming out from the heat, fastened on his hand.
ACT 28:4 When the barbarians saw the venomous creature hanging to his hand they said to one another, This man is certainly a murderer whom vengeance suffereth not to live, though he hath escaped from the sea.
ACT 28:5 He indeed shaked off the venomous creature into the fire, and suffered no harm;
ACT 28:6 but they expected that he would swell or fall dead suddenly. But when they had waited a considerable time and saw no mishap befal him, they changed their minds and said, He is a god.
ACT 28:7 Now in the neighbourhood of that place lay the estate of the chief man of the island, whose name was Publius, who took us to his house and entertained us kindly three days.
ACT 28:8 And it happened that the father of Publius being seized with a fever and a dysentery, was confined to his bed, to whom Paul went in and having prayed, laid his hands on him, and cured him.
ACT 28:9 This therefore being done, the rest in the island who had diseases came and were cured.
ACT 28:10 Therefore they honoured us with many honours and at our departure put on board such things as were necessary.
ACT 28:11 Now after three months we embarked on board a ship of Alexandria which had for its ensign Castor and Pollux, and which had wintered in that island.
ACT 28:12 And being conveyed to Syracuse we staid there three days.
ACT 28:13 Thence we came round and touched at Regium; and after one day, the south wind springing up, we on the second day arrived at Puteoli,
ACT 28:14 where we met with brethren and were intreated to stay with them seven days and then set out for Rome,
ACT 28:15 from which place the brethren, having heard of us, came, some to Appii-forum and some to Tres-tabernae to meet us. And when Paul saw them he gave thanks to God and took courage.
ACT 28:16 And when we arrived at Rome the centurion delivered the prisoners to the prefect. But Paul was permitted to be at a private lodging, with the soldier who guarded him.
ACT 28:17 And it came to pass after three days that Paul sent for them who were the chief men of the Jews, and when assembled he said to them, Men, brethren, though I have done nothing against the people, or the customs of our fathers, I was delivered up a prisoner from Jerusalem into the hands of the Romans.
ACT 28:18 These when they examined me, would have set me at liberty, because I had done nothing that deserved death.
ACT 28:19 But the Jews opposing this, I was forced to appeal to Caesar, not that I have any thing to lay to the charge of my nation.
ACT 28:20 For this cause, therefore, I have sent for you that I might see you and speak with you. For on account of the hope of Israel, I am bound with this chain.
ACT 28:21 To this they replied, We have neither received any letters concerning thee from Judea, nor hath any of the brethren who have arrived, related or spoken any harm of thee.
ACT 28:22 But we should be glad to hear what thou thinkest; for with respect to this sect we know that it is every where spoken against.
ACT 28:23 So having set him a day, they came to him at his lodging, in greater numbers; to whom he explained the kingdom of God, testifying and endeavouring to reconcile them to the things concerning Jesus, from the law of Moses and the prophets, from morning till evening.
ACT 28:24 And some indeed were reconciled by what were spoken, and some disbelieved.
ACT 28:25 And being at variance among themselves they broke up, upon Paul's saying one word, that the holy spirit had spoken well to our fathers by the prophet Esaias,
ACT 28:26 saying, "Go and say to the people, Hearing you shall hear, though you may not understand; and seeing you shall see, though you may not perceive;
ACT 28:27 for the heart of this people is callous, and their ears are dull of hearing, and they have shut their eyes, that for a while they may not see with their eyes, and hear with their ears, and understand with their hearts, and turn that I may heal them."
ACT 28:28 Be it known therefore to you, that this salvation of God is sent to the Gentiles, and they will hearken to it.
ACT 28:29 And when he had said this the Jews departed, debating warmly among themselves.
ACT 28:30 And Paul continued two whole years in his own hired house, and received all that came to him,
ACT 28:31 proclaiming the reign of God, and teaching the things concerning the Lord Jesus Christ with all freedom and without restraint.
ROM 1:1 Paul, a servant of Jesus Christ, a called apostle, set apart for the gospel of God,
ROM 1:2 which he promised heretofore by his prophets in the Holy Scriptures
ROM 1:3 concerning his son, [him who was of a seed of David with respect to flesh
ROM 1:4 him who was determinately marked out as son of God by a power, according to a spirit of holiness, of rising up from the dead,]
ROM 1:5 [namely]] Jesus Christ, our Lord, by whom we have received favour and an apostolical mission, that for his name there may be an obedience of faith among all the nations,
ROM 1:6 among which you indeed are called ones of Jesus Christ
ROM 1:7 to all who are at Rome, beloved of God, called and consecrated; favour be to you, and peace from God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM 1:8 In the first place, I thank my God through Jesus Christ for you all, that your belief is celebrated throughout the whole world.
ROM 1:9 For God, whom I serve with my spirit in the gospel of his son, is my witness how incessantly I make mention of you, intreating always in my prayers
ROM 1:10 that by the will of God I may at length have some how a favourable opportunity to come to you.
ROM 1:11 For I long to see you that I may impart to you some spiritual gift for your establishment,
ROM 1:12 that is, to partake of consolation among you by the faith which is mutually in us, both yours and my own.
ROM 1:13 Now, brethren, I would not have you ignorant that I have hitherto been hindered, though I have often heretofore purposed to come to you, that I might have some fruit among you even as among the other nations.
ROM 1:14 I am a debtor both to Greeks and barbarians, to both the learned and the unlearned,
ROM 1:15 so that as far as it rests with me, I am ready to publish the glad tidings to you also who are at Rome.
ROM 1:16 For I am not ashamed of the gospel of the Christ; for it is the power of God for salvation to every one who believeth, to the Jew in the first place, and also to the Greek.
ROM 1:17 For by it there is revealed a justification of God's appointment because of belief, that we may believe. As it is written, "But the just shall live because of belief:
ROM 1:18 for the wrath of God is revealed from heaven against all ungodliness and unrighteousness of the men, who by unrighteousness repress truth.
ROM 1:19 Because that which is to be known of God is manifest among them, for God hath manifested it to them;
ROM 1:20 for his invisible attributes, both his eternal power and divine majesty, being thought upon, are from the creation of the world clearly discoverable by the things made, so that they are without excuse
ROM 1:21 because when they knew God, they did not glorify him as God, nor give him thanks, but became vain by their ill- grounded reasonings, and their foolish heart was darkened;
ROM 1:22 pretending to be wise, they became fools,
ROM 1:23 and changed the glory of the incorruptible God for an image representing coruptible man, and birds, and four footed beasts, and reptiles;
ROM 1:24 therefore God delivered them up, by the desires of their own hearts, to impurity, that by themselves their own bodies might be dishonoured.
ROM 1:25 They changed the truth of God for a falsity, and worshipped and served the creature, and not the creator who is blessed forever, Amen:
ROM 1:26 therefore God gave them up to infamous passions; for even their women perverted the instinct of nature;
ROM 1:27 and in like manner the males also leaving the sex, were inflamed with desires towards each other, which they most shamefully indulged, men with men, and received in themselves the retribution which was justly due to their error.
ROM 1:28 And as they did not search out God to have constantly a due sense of him, God gave them up to an undiscerning mind to do things unseemly,
ROM 1:29 filled as they were with all manner of injustice, lewdness, maliciousness, covetousness, mischief, being full of envy, murder, contention, fraud, evil habits; being whisperers,
ROM 1:30 backbiters, haters of God, insulters of men, insolent, boastful, inventors of evils, disobedient to parents,
ROM 1:31 without understanding, covenant breakers, void of natural affection, implacable, unmerciful.
ROM 1:32 Some having recognised God's law, That they who do such things deserve death, not only do the same things themselves, but have even a complacency in them who commit them;
ROM 2:1 therefore thou art inexcusable, O man, whosoever thou art, who judgest another: for in the act of judging another thou condemnest thyself. For thou the judger dost the same things.
ROM 2:2 Now we know .that the judgment of God is according to truth against them who commit such things.
ROM 2:3 And dost thou imagine, O man, who judgest them who commit such things and dost the same thyself, that thou shall escape the judgment of God?
ROM 2:4 Or dost thou contemn the riches of his gentleness and forbearance and long suffering, not considering that the gentleness of God is leading thee to a reformation?
ROM 2:5 Indeed according to this obduracy, and impenitent heart of thine thou art treasuring up for thyself wrath against a day of the wrath and of the revelation of the righteous judgment of God,
ROM 2:6 who will render to every one according to his works
ROM 2:7 to them who by perseverance in well-doing, seek for glory and honour, and incorruption [he will grant] everlasting life;
ROM 2:8 but for them who are contentious and disobedient to the truth and in subjection to unrighteousness, there will be indignation and wrath,
ROM 2:9 tribulation and anguish, upon every soul of man who doth evil, of the Jew first, and also of the Greek;
ROM 2:10 but glory and honour and peace, for every one who doth good; for the Jew first, and also for the Greek.
ROM 2:11 For with God there is no respect of persons.
ROM 2:12 For as many as have sinned without law, shall without law perish, and as many as have sinned, being under law shall be judged by law, on the day when, according to my gospel, God will judge the secrets of men by Jesus Christ.
ROM 2:13 For it is not the hearers of the law who are righteous in the sight of God, but the doers of the law will be justified;
ROM 2:14 for when the Gentiles who have not law do by nature the duties required by the law, these not having law are a law to themselves.
ROM 2:15 By the joint testimony of their conscience, and by their debates one with another, whether accusing or defending, they shew the matter of the law written in their hearts.
ROM 2:16 [See verse 12]
ROM 2:17 Behold thou art called a Jew, and thou restest on the law and gloriest in God,
ROM 2:18 and knowest his will, and triest things which differ, being instructed out of the law,
ROM 2:19 and hast a confidence that thou thyself art a guide of the blind, a light to them who are in darkness,
ROM 2:20 an instructor of the ignorant, a teacher of babes, having the form of the knowledge and of the truth in the law.
ROM 2:21 Thou therefore who teachest another, dost thou not teach thyself? Thou who proclaimest not to steal, dost thou steal?
ROM 2:22 Thou who sayest, Commit not adultery', dost thou commit adultery? Thou who abominatest idols, dost thou violate things sacred?
ROM 2:23 Thou who gloriest in a law, dost thou by the breach of that law dishonour God?
ROM 2:24 For as it is written, "On your account the name of God is blasphemed among the nations."
ROM 2:25 For circumcision is indeed profitable if thou performest the law. But if thou art a transgressor of the law thy circumcision is become uncircumcision.
ROM 2:26 If then the uncircumcision keep the moral precepts of the law, shall not such a one's uncircumcision be accounted circumcision?
ROM 2:27 And may not the uncircumcision which in a state of nature performeth the law, judge thee who being under a written law and circumcision art a transgressor of law?
ROM 2:28 For he is not a Jew, who is one outwardly; nor is that circumcision, which is barely in the flesh:
ROM 2:29 but he, who is a Jew inwardly, whose circumcision is that of the heart"spiritually not literally, whose praise is not from men, but from God.
ROM 3:1 What then is the superior privilege of the Jew, or what the advantage of circumcision?
ROM 3:2 Much every way. First indeed that they were intrusted with the oracles of God.
ROM 3:3 Well! what if some have been unfaithful? Shall their unfaithfulness make void the faithfulness of God?
ROM 3:4 No, by no means. Yea, let God be true, though every man be a liar, as it is written, " So that thou must be justified in thy acts and must overcome when thou art judged."
ROM 3:5 If then our unrighteousness established the righteousness of God, what shall we say, Is not God unjust who taketh vengeance? I speak as a man.
ROM 3:6 No, by no means. In that case, how shall God judge the world?
ROM 3:7 For if by my falsehood the truth of God hath abounded to his glory, why am I yet condemned as a sinner?
ROM 3:8 And will you, [as we are calumniated and as some affirm that we] say, that we should do evil that good may come, you whose condemnation is just?
ROM 3:9 What preference then have we? None at all. For we have before charged both Jews and Greeks with being all under sin;
ROM 3:10 as it is written, "There is none righteous, no, not one.
ROM 3:11 There is none who hath understanding. There is none who seeketh God.
ROM 3:12 They are all gone aside; They are all together become vile; There is none who doth good; no, not one.
ROM 3:13 Their throat is an open sepulchre. With their tongues they practised deceit. The poison of asps is under the lips of them,
ROM 3:14 Whose mouth is full of cursing and bitterness.
ROM 3:15 Their feet are swift to shed blood.
ROM 3:16 Destruction and misery are in their ways.
ROM 3:17 And the way of peace they did not know.
ROM 3:18 There is no fear of God before their eyes".
ROM 3:19 Now we know that what things soever the law saith, it saith to them who are under the law, that every mouth may be stopped, and the whole world stand convicted before God.
ROM 3:20 Because no flesh can be justified before him by works of law; for by law there is a knowledge of sin,
ROM 3:21 now therefore, independency of law, there is made manifest a justification of God's appointment, attested by the law and the prophets
ROM 3:22 even a justification, of God's appointment, by faith in Jesus Christ, for all and upon all who believe; for there is no distinction;
ROM 3:23 for all have sinned and come short of the glory of God.
ROM 3:24 They are justified freely by his grace through the redemption which is by Christ Jesus,
ROM 3:25 whom God heretofore exhibited as a mercy seat by faith in his blood, that, on account of the remission of past sins, during the forbearance of God,
ROM 3:26 it might be an indication of this justification of his, pointing to a display of this justification of his at this time, in order to shew this, That he is just and the justifier of him who is a believer in Jesus.
ROM 3:27 Where then is this boasting? It is excluded. By what law? By that of works? No; but by a law of belief.
ROM 3:28 We conclude therefore that man is justified by belief independent of works of law.
ROM 3:29 Is God the God of Jews only? Is he not also [the God] of the Gentiles? Yes, of Gentiles also:
ROM 3:30 since it is one and the same God who will justify circumcision because of belief and uncircumcision by the same belief.
ROM 3:31 Do we then by this belief make law void? No, by no means: on the contrary we establish law.
ROM 4:1 What then shall we say that our father Abraham obtained in regard to the flesh?
ROM 4:2 for if Abraham was justified because of works he hath matter of boasting. But he hath not before God.
ROM 4:3 For what saith the scripture, "And Abraham believed God and it was reckoned to him for righteousness."
ROM 4:4 Now to him who worketh the reward is not reckoned a favour, but a debt.
ROM 4:5 But to him who doth not work, but believeth in him who acquitteth the ungodly, his belief is placed to account for righteousness.
ROM 4:6 As David also saith in respect to the happiness of the man to whose account God placeth righteousness without works,
ROM 4:7 "Happy they whose iniquities are forgiven; And whose sins are covered:
ROM 4:8 Happy the man to whose account the Lord will not charge sin."
ROM 4:9 Now with respect to this happiness, doth it come upon the circumcision only, or upon the uncircumcision also? For we say that the believing was reckoned to Abraham for righteousness.
ROM 4:10 How then was it reckoned to him? When he was in circumcision, or in uncircumcision? Not when in circumcision; but when in uncircumcision;
ROM 4:11 and he received the sign of circumcision as a seal of the righteousness of that belief, which he had in uncircumcision, that he might be a father of all who believe when in a state of uncircumcision, in order that this righteousness may be reckoned to them also
ROM 4:12 and a father of circumcision to them who are not only circumcised, but who also walk in the footsteps of that belief of our father Abraham, which he had during uncircumcision.
ROM 4:13 For the promise that he should be heir of the world was not made to Abraham or his seed, during law, but during the righteousness of belief.
ROM 4:14 For if they who are under law are heirs, the believing is made void, and the promise rendered of no effect.
ROM 4:15 For the law operateth to produce wrath; for where there is no law, there is no transgression.
ROM 4:16 Therefore the promise is because of faith, that it may be matter of favour to this extent, that it may be firm to the whole seed"not only to that under the law, but to that of the faith of Abraham,
ROM 4:17 who; as it is written, " I have made thee a father of many nations" is the father of us all in the sight of him in whom he believed; namely God who reanimateth the dead, and calleth up things not yet in existence as if actually existing.
ROM 4:18 Against hope he believed with a hope that he should become father of many nations according to what was said, "So shall thy seed be"
ROM 4:19 and far from being weak in faith, he did not consider his own body now become dead, he being then in his hundredth year; nor the deadness of Sarah's womb.
ROM 4:20 He disputed not against the promise of God by unbelief; but was strong in faith, giving glory to God,
ROM 4:21 and being fully persuaded that he was able to perform what he had promised.
ROM 4:22 Therefore it was reckoned to him for righteousness.
ROM 4:23 Now it was not written merely for his sake, that it was reckoned to him,
ROM 4:24 but for our sakes also to whom it will now be reckoned, namely to such as believe in him who hath raised from the dead Jesus our Lord,
ROM 4:25 who was delivered up for our offences and raised again for our justification.
ROM 5:1 Therefore being justified because of belief, we have peace with God through our Lord Jesus Christ,
ROM 5:2 through whom we have, by this belief, obtained access to this favour in which we stand and boast in a hope of the glory of God.
ROM 5:3 And not only so, but we boast also in our tribulations, as we know that tribulation operateth to produce patience;
ROM 5:4 and patience, a proof; and proof, a hope;
ROM 5:5 and this hope will not shame us, because the love of God is diffused through our hearts by a Holy Spirit, which is given us.
ROM 5:6 For while we were yet without strength, Christ In due time died for the ungodly:
ROM 5:7 for scarcely will any one die for a just man; though perhaps for the good some one may even flare to die:
ROM 5:8 but God confirmeth his love for us, because while we were yet sinners, Christ died for us.
ROM 5:9 Much more therefore shall we, being now acquitted by his blood, be saved by him from the wrath;
ROM 5:10 For if we, when enemies, were reconciled to God by the death of his son, much more shall we, being reconciled, be saved by his life.
ROM 5:11 And not only so. but we also boast in God. through out Lord Jesus Christ, by whom we have now obtained this reconciliation,
ROM 5:12 on this account; as sin entered into this world by one man, and death by sin, and so death for which all sinned passed through unto all men:
ROM 5:13 for there was sin in the world until the law: now sin is not placed to account where there is no law;
ROM 5:14 but death reigned from Adam to Moses, even over them who had not sinned after the likeness of the transgression of Adam, who is a type of him who was to come:
ROM 5:15 but the free gift is not as the transgression; for if for the transgression of the one, the many died; much more hath the favour of God, and the free gift by the favour of the other man, Jesus Christ, superabounded to the many:
ROM 5:16 nor is this free gift as in the case when one sinned" for the sentence was a condemnation for one offence, but the
ROM 5:17 free gift is an acquittal from many transgressions. For if for the offence of the one, death reigned by that one; much more shall they who receive the superabundance of this favour and of the free gift of this acquittal, reign in life by the other, namely Jesus Christ.
ROM 5:18 Therefore as by one transgression there was a sentence of condemnation for all men; so by one acquittal there is an adjudication of life for all men.
ROM 5:19 For as by the disobedience of the one man, the many were ranked as sinners, so also by the obedience of the other man, the many will be ranked as righteous.
ROM 5:20 Now the law came in a little way, so that transgression abounded, but where sin abounded, favour superabounded,
ROM 5:21 that as sin had reigned by death, so favour might reign by means' of a justification for everlasting life, through Jesus Christ our Lord.
ROM 6:1 What shall we say then? Shall we continue in sin that favour may abound?
ROM 6:2 No, by no means. With respect to us who have died to sin, how can we any more live therein?
ROM 6:3 Do you not know that as many of us as have been baptized to Christ Jesus, have been baptized to his death?
ROM 6:4 We have therefore been buried with him by that baptism to his death, that as Christ was raised from the dead by the glory of the Father, so we also may walk in newness of life.
ROM 6:5 For if we are grafts, we are made so by the similitude of his death, but by that of his resurrection we shall actually be so.
ROM 6:6 This we know, that our old man was crucified with him that the body of sin may be stopped from operating, in order that we may no longer be slaves to sin.
ROM 6:7 For he who is dead, is delivered from sin.
ROM 6:8 Now if we have died with Christ, we believe that we shall live with him,
ROM 6:9 as we know that Christ, being raised from the dead, dieth no more. Death hath no more a mastery over him.
ROM 6:10 For inasmuch as he died for sin, he died once for all; but as he liveth, he liveth for God.
ROM 6:11 So likewise reckon ye yourselves to be dead to sin, but alive for God in Christ Jesus our Lord.
ROM 6:12 Therefore let not sin reign in your mortal body, so as by the appetites thereof to serve sin;
ROM 6:13 nor deliver up your members to sin as instruments of unrighteousness; but deliver yourselves up to God, as brought to life from the dead, and your members as instruments of righteousness for God.
ROM 6:14 For sin is not to have dominion over you, as you are not under the law, but under favour.
ROM 6:15 What then: shall we sin because we are not under law, but under favour? No, by no means.
ROM 6:16 Do you not know that to whatsoever you deliver yourselves up as servants at command, you are the slaves of that which you obey, whether it be of sin for death; or of obedience for righteousness.
ROM 6:17 But thanks be to God, that though you were slaves of sin, yet from the heart you have conformed to the mould of doctrine in which you were cast,
ROM 6:18 and being freed from sin, have become servants of righteousness.
ROM 6:19 [I speak in the language of human affairs because of the weakness of your flesh,] for as you yielded up your members to iniquity, as slavish instruments of uncleanness and all manner of iniquity, so now yield up your members as servants to righteousness for sanctification.
ROM 6:20 For when you were servants of sin"when you were at a loose from righteousness,
ROM 6:21 what fruit therefore had you then from those things of which you are now ashamed? For the end of them is death.
ROM 6:22 But being now set free from sin and become servants of God, you have your fruit to holiness, and in the end, everlasting life.
ROM 6:23 For die wages of sin is death; but the free gift of God is everlasting life by Christ Jesus our Lord.
ROM 7:1 Or do not you, brethren, know [for I now speak to them who know law] that the law hath dominion over man as long as it liveth?
ROM 7:2 For the married woman is by law bound to her husband while he is alive. But if the husband die, a stop is put to the operation of the law of the husband.
ROM 7:3 Therefore if she marry another man while her husband is alive, she will get the name of an adulteress; but if her husband die, she is free from the law so as not to be an adulteress by becoming another man's wife.
ROM 7:4 So you also, my brethren, are become dead to the law by means of the body of the Christ, that you may be for another, who is raised from the dead, that we may bring forth fruit to God.
ROM 7:5 For when we were in the flesh, the sinful passions, which subsisted under the law, exerted their energy in our members to bring forth fruit to death:
ROM 7:6 but we are now set free from the law by the death of that by which we were holden, so that we may serve with a new spirit, and not by the old letter.
ROM 7:7 What shall we say then? Is the law sin? No, by no means. Indeed I should not have known sin, had it not been for the law. For I should not have known covetousness, had not the law said, "Thou shall not covet"
ROM 7:8 But sin having got an advantage by the commandment, wrought in me all manner of desire. For without law sin is dead.
ROM 7:9 Now as for me, I for a while was alive without law, but when the commandment came, sin revived and I died.
ROM 7:10 So I found the commandment which was for life, to be for death.
ROM 7:11 For sin having got an advantage by the commandment, seduced me, and by it slew me.
ROM 7:12 So that the law is indeed holy, and the commandment is holy, just and good.
ROM 7:13 Hath that then which is good been death to me?  No, by no means. But sin, so that it appeared to be sin, continued working death for me by that which is good, so that sin appeared to be sin in the highest degree by the commandment.
ROM 7:14 For we know that the law is spiritual, but as for me, I being carnal, am sold to sin.
ROM 7:15 For what I am doing I do not allow; for that which I approve, I do not perform; but what I hate, that I do.
ROM 7:16 Now if I do that which I do not approve, I assent to the law that it is good:
ROM 7:17 and it is now not I myself, who do this, but sin which dwelleth in me.
ROM 7:18 For I know that in me, that is, in my flesh, good doth not dwell. For to will is present with me, but the performance of what is good, I do not find.
ROM 7:19 For the good which I approve, I do not perform; but evil which I disapprove, this I do.
ROM 7:20 Now if I do that which I myself disapprove; it is no more I myself who do it; but sin which dwelleth in me.
ROM 7:21 I find then this law for me, that when I would do good, evil is close to me.
ROM 7:22 For in the inner man I am delighted with the law of God;
ROM 7:23 but I perceive another law in my members warring against the law of my mind and making me a captive to the law of sin which is in my members.
ROM 7:24 Wretched man that I am! who will deliver me from this deathful body?
ROM 7:25 I thank God that through Jesus Christ our Lord, [do I then myself with the mind serve the law of God, but with the flesh the law of sin?
ROM 8:1 There is then no condemnation now to them who are in Christ Jesus and who walk not after the flesh, but after the spirit.
ROM 8:2 For the law of the spirit of the life in Christ Jesus hath freed me from the law of sin and death;
ROM 8:3 for as it was out of the power of the law to do this, inasmuch as it was weak through the flesh, God having sent his own son in a likeness of sinful flesh, and to be a sin offering, hath condemned this sin in the flesh,
ROM 8:4 that the morality of the law might be confirmed by us who walk not after flesh, but after spirit:
ROM 8:5 for they who are followers of flesh have their minds bent on the things of the flesh; but the followers of spirit, on the things of the spirit.
ROM 8:6 For the bent of the flesh is death; but the bent of the spirit is life and peace.
ROM 8:7 Because the bent of the flesh is enmity to God, [for it is not in subjection to the law of God, nor indeed can be,]
ROM 8:8 they therefore who are in a carnal state cannot please God.
ROM 8:9 But you are not in a carnal state, but in a spiritual state, if indeed the spirit of God dwelleth in you. But if any one hath not the spirit of Christ, he is none of his.
ROM 8:10 But if Christ be in you, the body indeed is dead because of sin, but the spirit is alive, because of a justification;
ROM 8:11 and if the spirit of him who raised up Jesus from the dead dwelleth in you, he who hath raised up the Christ from the dead will quicken even those dead bodies of yours by his spirit which dwelleth in you.
ROM 8:12 Therefore we, brethren, are not debtors to the flesh, that we should live according to the flesh;
ROM 8:13 for if you live according to the flesh, you are dying; but if you by the spirit mortify the deeds of the body, you shall live.
ROM 8:14 For as many as are led by the spirit of God, are sons of God.
ROM 8:15 For you have not received a spirit of bondage again to fear; but you have received a spirit of adoption, by which we cry, Abba, Father.
ROM 8:16 This very spirit beareth joint witness with our spirit that we are children of God;
ROM 8:17 and if children, then heirs; heirs indeed of God, and joint heirs with Christ if we suffer with him so that with him we may also be glorified.
ROM 8:18 For I reckon that the sufferings of this present time are not worthy to be set against that glory which is about to be revealed for us.
ROM 8:19 For the earnest expectation of mankind is waiting for the manifestation of the children of God.
ROM 8:20 For to vanity this creation was subjected, not as a voluntary agent, but by him who subjected it to a hope
ROM 8:21 that this very creation shall be freed from the slavery of this corruption, that it may enjoy the glorious liberty of the children of God.
ROM 8:22 For we know that this whole creation are groaning together, and even till now are all in pain as a woman in travail.
ROM 8:23 Nay, even they who have the first fruits of the spirit, even we ourselves are groaning within ourselves, waiting for an adoption the redemption of this body of ours.
ROM 8:24 For to this hope we have escaped. Now hope which is attained, is not hope; for why should one hope for that which he enjoyeth. 25 But if we hope for what we do not enjoy, we wait for it with patience,
ROM 8:26 and in such a manner as the spirit joineth in helping our infirmities: for we do not know what we should pray for as we ought, but the spirit itself intercedeth for us with groans which cannot be expressed in words.
ROM 8:27 And he who searcheth the hearts knoweth the bent of the spirit, that it pleadeth for saints according to the will of God.
ROM 8:28 And we know that all things are working together for good to them who love God"to them who according to a previous purpose are now actually called.
ROM 8:29 For those whom he foreknew, even these he marked out beforehand to be of a form the same as that of the image of his son, that he might be a first born among many brethren.
ROM 8:30 And those whom he marked out beforehand he actually called, and those whom he called, even these he acquitted, and those whom he acquitted even these he glorified.
ROM 8:31 What then shall we say to these things? If God is for us, who can be against us?
ROM 8:32 He who spared not his own son but delivered him up for us all, how will he not also with him freely grant us all things?
ROM 8:33 Who shall lodge an accusation against them whom God hath chosen? God who acquitteth?
ROM 8:34 who is he who shall condemn? Christ who died? Rather indeed who is raised up, who is actually at the right hand of God, and who maketh intercession for us?
ROM 8:35 Who shall separate us from the love of the Christ? Shall tribulation or distress, or persecution, or famine, or nakedness, or peril, or sword?
ROM 8:36 [As it is written, "For thy sake we are killed all the day long, And accounted as sheep for slaughter"
ROM 8:37 We indeed in all these things are more than conquerors by means of him who hath loved us.
ROM 8:38 For I am persuaded that neither death, nor life, nor angels, nor principalities, nor powers, nor things present, nor things to come,
ROM 8:39 nor height, nor depth, nor any other created being shall be able to separate us from the love of God which is in Christ Jesus our Lord.
ROM 9:1 I speak the truth in Christ, I lie not, my conscience, with a holy spirit, bearing joint witness for me
ROM 9:2 that I have great grief and incessant sorrow in my heart
ROM 9:3 [for I even I myself wished the followers of Christ to be devoted to destruction,] for my brethren, my kinsmen according to the flesh,
ROM 9:4 who are Israelites, to whom belonged the adoption and the glory, and the covenants, and the civil government, and the religious service, and the promises;
ROM 9:5 whose ancestors were the patriarchs, and from whom, with regard to flesh, the Christ is [descended] who is over all, God blessed forever. Amen.
ROM 9:6 It is not however to be supposed that the word of God hath failed. For with regard to all the descendants of Israel, they are not Israel;
ROM 9:7 nor are they all children, because they are of the race of Abraham; but in Isaak a seed shall be called for thee.
ROM 9:8 That is to say, It is not the children of the flesh who are the children of God; but the children of the promise are reckoned for seed.
ROM 9:9 For this is the word of the promise. "About this time twelve month I will come and Sarah shall have a son."
ROM 9:10 And not only so but the same was the case with Rebecca, when she was with child of twins by one man, namely, our father Isaak.
ROM 9:11 For the children being not yet born, nor having done any thing good or evil that the purpose might rest on the choice of God, not in consideration of works, but of his call,
ROM 9:12 it was said to her, "The elder shall serve the younger."
ROM 9:13 As it is written "Jacob I have loved and Esau I have slighted."
ROM 9:14 What then shall we say"? Is there injustice with God? No by no means.
ROM 9:15 For to Moses he saith, "I will have mercy on whomsoever I please to have mercy'? and I will have compassion on whomsoever I please to compassionate.
ROM 9:16 Therefore it is not of him who willeth, nor of him who runneth, but of God, who sheweth mercy.
ROM 9:17 For the scripture saith to Pharaoh, "I have raised thee up for this purpose that by thee I may display my power; and that my name may be celebrated throughout all the earth."
ROM 9:18 Well then, he sheweth mercy to whom he pleaseth, and hardeneth whom he pleaseth,
ROM 9:19 wilt thou then say to me, Why doth he yet find fault, for who hath resisted his will?
ROM 9:20 But who art thou, O man, who enterest into a dispute with God? Shall the thing formed say to him who formed it, Why hast thou made me thus?
ROM 9:21 Hath not the potter power over the clay to make, out of the same lump, one vessel for honour, and another for dishonour?
ROM 9:22 What if God willing to manifest his wrath and make known his power, did with much long suffering, bear with the vessels of wrath fitted for destruction,
ROM 9:23 to the end that he might make known the riches of his glory on the vessels of mercy which he had previously prepared for glory
ROM 9:24 even us whom he hath called not only from among the Jews, but also from among the Gentiles.
ROM 9:25 As he actually saith by Hosea, "I will call them my people who are not my people; and I will call her beloved, who was not beloved."
ROM 9:26 And it shall come to pass that in the place where it was said to them, You are not my people, they shall there be called children of the7 living God."
ROM 9:27 Esaias also crieth concerning Israel, "Though the number of the children of Israel be as the sand of the sea, this remnant shall be saved."
ROM 9:28 For he is closing an account and making a deduction with saving goodness. Because the Lord will make with the land a reckoning from which a deduction is made,
ROM 9:29 therefore as Esaias said. "Had not the Lord of hosts left us a seed, we must have been like Sodom and become like Gomorrah."
ROM 9:30 What then are we to infer? That the Gentiles who did not pursue righteousness, attained righteousness, but it was a righteousness because of belief;
ROM 9:31 but Israel pursuing a law of righteousness did not come up to the law of righteousness.
ROM 9:32 Why?] Because they sought it not from belief; but as if attainable by works of law. For they stumbled at the stumbling stone.
ROM 9:33 As it is written, "Behold I lay in Sion a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence. "And "whosoever believeth in him shall not be shamed."
ROM 10:1 Brethren, the earnest desire of my heart and my supplication to God for Israel is, that they may be saved.
ROM 10:2 For I bear them witness that they have a zeal for God, but not according to knowledge.
ROM 10:3 For being ignorant of the righteousness of God's appointment, and seeking to establish a righteousness of their own, they did not submit themselves to God's righteousness.
ROM 10:4 For Christ is the end of the law for righteousness to every one who believeth:
ROM 10:5 For Moses describeth the righteousness which is from the law, thus; "The man who doth these things shall live thereby;"
ROM 10:6 but the righteousness because of believing speaketh in this manner: Say not in thy heart, Who will ascend up to heaven [that is to bring Christ down];
ROM 10:7 or who will go down to the abyss [that is to bring up Christ from the dead]
ROM 10:8 But what doth it say? The matter is near thee, in thy mouth and in thy heart. That is, the matter of this belief, which we proclaim,
ROM 10:9 That if thou wilt acknowledge with thy mouth the Lord Jesus, and believe with thy heart that God hath raised him from the dead, thou shalt be saved.
ROM 10:10 For with the heart man believeth for righteousness, and with the mouth acknowledgment is made for salvation.
ROM 10:11 For the scripture saith, "Whosoever believeth in him shall not be shamed."
ROM 10:12 For there is no distinction of Jew and Greek; for he is Lord of all, abounding in riches for all who call upon him;
ROM 10:13 "For whosoever will call on the name of the Lord shall be saved."
ROM 10:14 How then shall they call on him in whom they have not believed? And how shall they believe in him, of whom they have not heard? And how shall they hear without a proclaimer?
ROM 10:15 and how shall they proclaim, unless they be sent? As it is written, "How beautiful are the feet of them who proclaim the joyful message of peace"who proclaim the glad tidings of good things."
ROM 10:16 But all have not duly hearkened to the good news, for Esaias saith, "Lord, who hath believed this report of ours."
ROM 10:17 The believing is indeed because of hearing, and what they heard is by the order of God.
ROM 10:18 But I say, Have they not heard? What! Is their sound then gone forth to every land; and their doctrines to the limits of the world?
ROM 10:19 But I say, Hath not Israel known? First Moses saith, "I will provoke you by what is not a nation, By a foolish nation I will vex you."
ROM 10:20 But Esaias is more explicit, and saith, "I was found by them who sought me not, I became manifest to them who inquired not for me."
ROM 10:21 But concerning Israel he saith, "I have stretched out my hands all the day long to a disobedient and gainsaying people."
ROM 11:1 I say then, Hath God utterly rejected his people?  No, by no means. For even I myself am an Israelite, of the seed of Abraham, of the tribe of Benjamin.
ROM 11:2 God hath not utterly rejected his people whom he heretofore acknowledged. Do you not know by Elias what the scripture saith? When he is pleading with God against Israel, saying,
ROM 11:3 "Lord, they have slain thy prophets and demolished thine altars; and I alone am left, and they seek my life."
ROM 11:4 What doth the divine oracle say to him? "I have reserved for myself seven thousand men who have not bowed a knee to Baal."
ROM 11:5 In like manner, therefore, at this present time there is a remnant according to a choice of favour.
ROM 11:6 Now if it be by favour, it is no more in consideration of works, since in this case the favour be no favour: but if it be in consideration of works it is no more of favour, otherwise the work is no work.
ROM 11:7 What is the inference?  That which Israel sought he did not obtain; but the chosen obtained it and the rest were blinded.
ROM 11:8 As it is written, "God hath given them a spirit of stupefaction, eyes not to see and ears not to hear even to this day."
ROM 11:9 And David saith, "Let their table be for a snare and for a trap, and for a stumbling block, and for a retribution to them.
ROM 11:10 Let their eyes be darkened that they may not see, And bow down their neck continually."
ROM 11:11 I say then, Did they stumble that they might fall?  No, by no means. But on this lapse of theirs the Gentiles have this salvation to provoke them to emulation.
ROM 11:12 Now if this lapse of theirs is the riches of the world and the diminution of them is the riches of the Gentiles, how much more will their fulness be!
ROM 11:13 [For I tell you, Gentiles, inasmuch as I am the apostle of the Gentiles, I honour my office,
ROM 11:14 if I can any how excite to emulation them who are my flesh and save some of them].
ROM 11:15 For if the casting of them off is the reconcilement of the world, what must the taking of them back be, but life from the dead?
ROM 11:16 Now if that portion which is set apart from an offering is holy, so will the mass be. And if the root is holy, so are the branches:
ROM 11:17 And if some of the branches are broken off, and thou being a wild olive art ingrafted among them and become a partaker of the root and fatness of the olive tree,
ROM 11:18 boast not against the branches. But if thou boast [remember that] thou dost not support the root, but the root supporteth thee.
ROM 11:19 Thou wilt say then, The branches were broken off, that I might be ingraffed.
ROM 11:20 Well! They were broken off for their disbelief, and thou standest for thy belief. Be not high minded; but fear;
ROM 11:21 For if God spared not the natural branches, perhaps he may not spare thee.
ROM 11:22 Behold then the kindness and the severity of God: severity against them indeed who have fallen, and kindness to thee if thou continue in that kindness, otherwise thou also wilt be cut off.
ROM 11:23 And with respect to them, if they continue not in their disbelief, they shall be ingraffed. For God is able to ingraff them again.
ROM 11:24 For if thou hast been cut from a natural wild olive tree, and contrary to nature graffed on a good olive tree; how much more shall they that are natural branches be graffed on their own olive tree.
ROM 11:25 For, that you, brethren, may not have too high an opinion of your selves, I would not have you ignorant of this secret, That a partial blindness hath come upon Israel until the fulness of the Gentiles shall have come in,
ROM 11:26 and then at length all Israel shall be saved. As it is written "For the sake of Sion the Deliverer will come And turn away ungodliness from Jacob:
ROM 11:27 And this shall be my covenant with them When I take away their sins.
ROM 11:28 With respect to these glad tidings, they are enemies on your account; but with respect to the choice, they are beloved on account of the fathers.
ROM 11:29 For the favours and choice of God are not reversed.
ROM 11:30 For as you for a while rebelled against God, but have now obtained mercy at their rebellion;
ROM 11:31 so they also have now rebelled at the mercy shewn to you, that they also may be objects of mercy.
ROM 11:32 For God hath shut all up for disobedience that he may have mercy on all.
ROM 11:33 O the depth of the riches, and of the wisdom, and of the knowledge of God! How unsearchable are his judgments, and his ways not to be traced out!
ROM 11:34 For who hath known the mind of the Lord"? Or who hath been his counsellor?
ROM 11:35 Or who hath first given to him, that in return he may receive a recompense?
ROM 11:36 Because of him, and by him, and for him are all things; to him be the glory forever, Amen;
ROM 12:1 therefore I exhort you, brethren, by the mercies of God, to present your bodies a living, holy, acceptable sacrifice to God as your rational, religious service;
ROM 12:2 and be not conformed to this world; but transformed by the renewal of your mind, that you may know experimentally what the will of God is, which is good and acceptable and perfect.
ROM 12:3 For by virtue of the favour which is granted to me, I charge every one who is among you not to have an overweening opinion of himself, but to bend his thoughts to the attaining of a sober and modest demeanour, as God hath distributed a portion of faith to every one.
ROM 12:4 For as we have many members in one body, and all the members have not the same office;
ROM 12:5 so we being many are one body in Christ, but individually members of one another,
ROM 12:6 and employed in exercising free gifts, according to the favour conferred on us, different as they are, if prophesy, in conformity to that belief;
ROM 12:7 if a ministerial office, in that office; and if one is a teacher, in teaching;
ROM 12:8 and the exhorter in exhortation; let him who giveth [do it] with sincerity; him who superintendeth, with assiduity; him who sheweth mercy, with cheerfulness.
ROM 12:9 Let love be unfeigned: abhor what is evil; adhere closely to what is good;
ROM 12:10 in brotherly love be tenderly affectionate one to another: in honour prefer one another;
ROM 12:11 in business be not slothful: Be fervent in spirit; constant in serving the Lord;
ROM 12:12 joyful in hope; patient in tribulation; stedfastly persevering in prayer;
ROM 12:13 administering to the wants of the saints; cultivating hospitality:
ROM 12:14 Bless them who persecute you"bless and curse not.
ROM 12:15 Set your hearts on this with respect to each other"to rejoice with them who rejoice, and to weep with them who weep.
ROM 12:16 Set not your minds on high things, but accommodate yourselves to things which are low. Be not wise in your own conceits.
ROM 12:17 Render to none evil for evil. Be provident in regard to things good in the sight of all men.
ROM 12:18 If possible, that is, as far as in your power, be at peace with all men.
ROM 12:19 Beloved, avenge not yourselves, but give place to the wrath; for it is written, "Vengeance is mine; I will requite, saith the Lord."
ROM 12:20 Therefore if thine enemy hunger feed him; if he be thirsty, give him drink; for by doing so thou wilt use the means to melt him.
ROM 12:21 Be not overcome by evil; but overcome evil with good.
ROM 13:1 Let every soul be subject to the ruling powers; for there is no power but from God. The powers in being are arranged by God;
ROM 13:2 so that he who setteth himself against the power resisteth the arrangement of God; and they who resist shall receive for themselves condemnation.
ROM 13:3 For the rulers are not a terror to good works but to evil. Dost thou then wish not to dread the power? Do that which is good and thou shall have praise from it.
ROM 13:4 For it is a minister of God for good to thee. But if thou dost evil, be in dread; for it wieldeth not the sword in vain. For it is a minister of God, an avenger to execute wrath on him who doth evil.
ROM 13:5 Therefore it is necessary to submit to government, not only on account of punishment, but also for conscience's sake.
ROM 13:6 Indeed on this account you pay taxes, because there are ministers of God continually employed for this very purpose.
ROM 13:7 Render therefore to all their dues; tribute to whom tribute; custom to whom custom; reverence to whom reverence; honour to whom honour is due.
ROM 13:8 Owe no one any thing, save this, to love one another: for he who loveth others hath fulfilled the law:
ROM 13:9 for this: Thou shalt not commit adultery; Thou shall not murder; Thou shalt not steal; Thou shalt not bear false witness; Thou shall not covet; and whatever other commandment there be, is summed up in this commandment, Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself.
ROM 13:10 This love worketh no evil to one's neighbour: This love therefore is the fulfilling of the law.
ROM 13:11 Furthermore, as we know the season, that it is now high time for us to rouse from sleep, for our deliverance is nearer now than when we first believed:
ROM 13:12 The night is far spent; the day is drawing on; let us therefore put off the works of darkness, and put on the armour of light;
ROM 13:13 and let us walk as in day light, in a becoming manner; not in revels and drunken debauches; not in dalliance and wantonness; not in strife and envy;
ROM 13:14 but put on the Lord Jesus Christ, and make not provision for the flesh to fulfil its desires.
ROM 14:1 Receive into fellowship him who is weak in the faith, without regard to differences of opinions.
ROM 14:2 One indeed believeth that he may eat all things; another who is weak eateth vegetables.
ROM 14:3 Let not him, who eateth despise him who doth not eat. And let not him who doth not eat, judge him who eateth. For God hath taken him into his family,
ROM 14:4 who art thou who judgest another's servant. To his own master he standeth or falleth. But he shall stand, for God is able to establish him.
ROM 14:5 One indeed judgeth one day above another; another esteemeth every day alike. Let every one be fully persuaded in his own mind.
ROM 14:6 He who regardeth the day, regardeth it for the Lord; and he who regardeth not the day, refraineth from regarding it, for the Lord. He who eateth, eateth for the Lord, for he giveth God thanks; and he who eateth not, refraineth from eating, for the Lord, and he giveth God thanks.
ROM 14:7 For none of us liveth to himself, nor doth any die to himself.
ROM 14:8 For whether we live, we live to the Lord; and if we die, we die to the Lord; so that whether we live or die, we are the Lord's.
ROM 14:9 For to this end Christ died and rose and lived again, that he might be Lord both of the dead and the living.
ROM 14:10 Why then judgest thou thy brother, or why despisest thou thy brother? For we shall all stand before the judgment seat of the Christ;
ROM 14:11 For it is written, "As I live, saith the Lord, to me every knee shall bow, and every tongue shall give praise to God."
ROM 14:12 Since every one of us then shall give an account of himself to God,
ROM 14:13 let us therefore no more judge one another, but rather come to this determination, not to lay a stumbling block in the way of a brother, nor give any occasion of offence.
ROM 14:14 I know and am fully assured by the Lord Jesus; that nothing is of itself unclean. But to him who thinketh any thing unclean, to him it is unclean.
ROM 14:15 Now if on account of thy food thy brother is grieved, thou no longer walkest According to love. Destroy not by thy food him for whom Christ died.
ROM 14:16 Let not therefore the good which you enjoy be ill spoken of.
ROM 14:17 For the reign of God is not eating and drinking, but righteousness and peace and joy in a holy spirit.
ROM 14:18 For he who serveth the Christ in these things is acceptable to God and approved by men.
ROM 14:19 Let us then pursue those things which tend to peace and mutual edification.
ROM 14:20 Do not for the sake of food destroy the work of God. All things indeed are pure; but they are an evil to a man who eateth for a stumbling block.
ROM 14:21 It is good not to eat flesh, nor drink wine, nor any thing by which thy brother falleth, or stumbleth, or is made weak.
ROM 14:22 Thou hast a belief; exercise it at home by thyself before God. Happy he who upon a strict examination doth not condemn himself.
ROM 14:23 Now he who maketh distinctions is condemned if he eateth, because he eateth not with belief; and every thing which is not according to belief is a sin.
ROM 15:1 We then who are strong ought to bear the infirmities of the weak, and not to please ourselves.
ROM 15:2 Let every one of us please his neighbour as far as is good for edification.
ROM 15:3 For even the Christ did not consult his own gratification, but as it is written, "The reproaches of them who reproached thee fell upon me."
ROM 15:4 For whatever was written heretofore, was written for our instruction, that we by patience and the consolation of the scripture may have hope.
ROM 15:5 Now may the God of this patience and of this consolation grant you to have your minds mutually bent on this very thing after the example of Christ Jesus,
ROM 15:6 that you may unanimously, with one voice, glorify the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ.
ROM 15:7 Therefore receive one another into fellowship, even as the Christ received us into his family, for the glory of God.
ROM 15:8 Now I say that, for the truth of God, Jesus Christ became the minister of circumcision, to confirm the promises made to the fathers;
ROM 15:9 and that the Gentiles are to glorify God for his mercy. As it is written, "For this cause I will praise thee among the nations and sing to thy name."
ROM 15:10 And again it is said, "Rejoice, O nations, with his people."
ROM 15:11 And again, Praise the Lord, all ye nations: Praise him, all ye people,
ROM 15:12 also, And again Esaias saith, "There shall be the root of Jesse, even he who riseth up to rule nations; in him nations will put their trust.
ROM 15:13 Now may the God of this trust fill you with all joy and peace in believing, that you may abound in this trust by virtue of a holy spirit.
ROM 15:14 Now as for me, I am persuaded, my brethren, with respect to you, that you yourselves are full of goodness, filled with all knowledge and able to instruct one another;
ROM 15:15 nevertheless I have written to you, brethren, with more boldness, partly as your remembrancer, because of the favour which God hath granted me,
ROM 15:16 that I should be a ministering servant of Jesus Christ to the Gentiles, and employed in the holy service of dispensing the glad tidings of God, that the offering of the Gentiles may be accepted, being hallowed by a holy spirit.
ROM 15:17 Therefore I have matter of boasting in Christ Jesus with respect to the things pertaining to God.
ROM 15:18 For I will not presume to mention any thing, save what Christ hath wrought by me for the obedience of the Gentiles, both in profession and practice,
ROM 15:19 by virtue of signs and wonders, by the power of the spirit of God; so that from Jerusalem and the country around even to Illyricum, I have confirmed the glad tidings of the Christ,
ROM 15:20 [yet when thus ambitious to publish the glad tidings] not where Christ was named, that I might not build on another's foundation;
ROM 15:21 but as it is written, "They to whom no publication was made concerning him, shall see, and they who have not heard, will attentively consider."
ROM 15:22 Therefore, though I have been many times hindered from coming to you,
ROM 15:23 yet having now no further scope in these parts, and having had, for many years, a strong desire to visit you,
ROM 15:24 I will, when I take a journey to Spain, come to you. For I hope to see you on my way, and to be forwarded thither by you, when I shall have first been in some degree satisfied with your company.
ROM 15:25 But now I am going to Jerusalem as an almoner to the saints.
ROM 15:26 For Macedonia and Achaia have been pleased to make a contribution for the poor saints in Jerusalem.
ROM 15:27 For they have been pleased! Indeed they are their debtors. For if the Gentiles have partaken of their spiritual things, they ought to minister to them with temporal things.
ROM 15:28 Having therefore performed this business, and secured to them this contribution, I will come to you in my way to Spain.
ROM 15:29 And I know that when I come to you, I shall come with a fulness of the blessing of the glad tidings of the Christ.
ROM 15:30 Now I beseech you, brethren, by our Lord Jesus Christ and by the love of the spirit, to join with me in earnest supplications to God, for me;
ROM 15:31 that I may be delivered from the unbelievers in Judea; and that this service of mine, which carrieth me to Jerusalem, may be acceptable to the saints,
ROM 15:32 that I may come to you with joy, by the will of God, and refresh myself with you.
ROM 15:33 Now the God of peace be with you all. Amen.
ROM 16:1 I recommend to you Phebe our sister, who is an almoner of the congregation at Cenchrea,
ROM 16:2 that you may receive her in the Lord in a manner becoming the saints, and afford her such assistance as her business may require: for she indeed hath assisted many, particularly myself.
ROM 16:3 Salute Priscilla and Aquilas my fellow labourers in Christ Jesus,
ROM 16:4 who for my life exposed their own; to whom not only I, but all the Gentile congregations also, owe thanks.
ROM 16:5 Salute also the congregation at their house. Salute my beloved Epenetus, who is the first fruits of Achaia for Christ.
ROM 16:6 Salute Mary, who hath taken a great deal of pains on our account.
ROM 16:7 Salute Andronicus and Junias, my kinsmen and my fellow prisoners. They are in high repute among the apostles, and were in Christ before me.
ROM 16:8 Salute Amplias, who is my beloved in the Lord.
ROM 16:9 Salute Urbanus, our fellow labourer in Christ, and Stachys, who is my beloved.
ROM 16:10 Salute Appelles, who is approved in Christ. Salute those who are of the household of Aristobulus.
ROM 16:11 Salute Herodian, my kinsman. Salute those of the household of Narcissus, who are in the Lord.
ROM 16:12 Salute Tryphena and Tryphosa, who have laboured in the Lord. Salute the beloved Persis, who hath laboured much in the Lord.
ROM 16:13 Salute Rufus, the chosen in the Lord, and his mother and mine.
ROM 16:14 Salute Asyncritus, Phlegon, Ermas, Patrobas, Herme, and the brethren with them.
ROM 16:15 Salute Philologus, and Julias, and Nereus, and his sister, and Olympus, and all the saints with them.
ROM 16:16 Salute one another with a holy kiss. The congregation of Christ salute you.
ROM 16:17 Now I exhort you, brethren, to mark them who make the divisions and the stumbling blocks contrary to the doctrine which you have learned; and avoid them.
ROM 16:18 For such men do not serve our Lord Jesus Christ, but their own belly. And by their fawning speeches and flattering forms of address, they deceive the hearts of the innocent.
ROM 16:19 For your obedience is come abroad to all; I therefore rejoice on your account, and wish you to be indeed wise for good, and without any mixture of evil.
ROM 16:20 And the God of peace will soon bruise satan under your feet. The favour of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
ROM 16:21 Timothy, my fellow labourer, and Lucius, and Jason, and Sosipater, my kinsmen, salute you.
ROM 16:22 I, Tertius, the writer of this letter, salute you in the Lord.
ROM 16:23 Gaius, who entertaineth me and the whole congregation, saluteth you. Erastus, the chamberlain of the city, saluteth you: so doth Quartus the brother.
ROM 16:24 The favour of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
ROM 16:25 Now to him who is able to establish you according to my glad tidings and the proclamation of Jesus Christ; according to the disclosure of a secret which was concealed in times of old,
ROM 16:26 but which is now laid open, and by prophetic writings made known to all the nations, according to an order of the everlasting God, for the obedience of belief
ROM 16:27 to the only wise God be the glory forever, through Jesus Christ. Amen.
1CO 1:1 Paul, called to be an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, and Sosthenes the brother,
1CO 1:2 to the congregation of God which is at Corinth; to them who are hallowed by Christ Jesus; called to be holy, together with all those in every place who invoke the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, both their Lord and ours:
1CO 1:3 favour be to you, and peace from God our father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
1CO 1:4 I thank my God always with respect to you, for the favour of God which is granted you by Christ Jesus,
1CO 1:5 that in every thing you have been enriched by him with all doctrine and with all knowledge,
1CO 1:6 in the same manner as the testimony of Christ was confirmed among you;
1CO 1:7 so that you are not deficient in any gift during your waiting for the full manifestation of our Lord Jesus Christ,
1CO 1:8 who will confirm you to the end, exempt from accusation in the day of our Lord Jesus Christ.
1CO 1:9 God is faithful by whom you have been called to a fellowship in his son, Jesus Christ our Lord.
1CO 1:10 And I intreat you, brethren, by the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, that you all speak the same thing, and that there be no divisions among you, but that you be perfectly united in the same mind and in the same sentiment.
1CO 1:11 For I am informed respecting you, my brethren, by some of Chloe's family, that there are contentions among you;
1CO 1:12 I mean this, that every one of you saith, I am for Paul; and I am for Apollos; and I for Cephas; and I for Christ.
1CO 1:13 Is the Christ divided"? Was Paul crucified for you? Or were you baptized to the name of Paul?
1CO 1:14 I thank God that I baptized none of you, except Crispus and Gaius,
1CO 1:15 that none might say that I baptized to my own name.
1CO 1:16 I baptized also the household of Stephanas. I do not recollect that I baptized any other.
1CO 1:17 For Christ did not send me to baptize, but to proclaim the glad tidings, not with wisdom of speech, that the cross of the Christ might not be rendered useless.
1CO 1:18 For this doctrine [the doctrine of the cross] is foolishness to them who perish; but to us who are saved it is the power of God.
1CO 1:19 For it is written, "I will destroy the wisdom of the wise and abolish the understanding of the prudent."
1CO 1:20 Where is the wise? Where the scribe? Where the disputer of this age? Hath not God shewn the wisdom of this world to be folly?
1CO 1:21 For when, amidst the wisdom of God, the world did not, by means of that wisdom, know God; it pleased God by the foolishness of this proclamation to save them who believe;
1CO 1:22 so when the Jews demand a sign and the Greeks seek wisdom,
1CO 1:23 as for us, we proclaim a crucified Christ; to the Jews indeed a stumbling block, and to the Greeks foolishness;
1CO 1:24 but to them who are called, both Jews and Greeks, Christ the power of God and the wisdom of God;
1CO 1:25 because this foolish thing of God is wiser than men, and this weak thing of God is stronger than men.
1CO 1:26 For observe, brethren, this call of you, that there are not many wise after the flesh, not many mighty, not many of illustrious birth;
1CO 1:27 but God hath chosen the foolish things of the world to put to shame the wise; and the weak things of the world God hath made choice of to put to shame the strong
1CO 1:28 and the ignoble of this world, and those of no account, God hath chosen; nay, the very nothings, to put a stop to the operation of the things which are,
1CO 1:29 that no flesh might boast in his presence.
1CO 1:30 And it is owing to him that you are in Christ Jesus, who hath been made to us wisdom from God, namely, righteousness, and sanctification, and redemption,
1CO 1:31 so that as it is written, Let him who boasteth boast in the Lord."
1CO 2:1 Now as for me, brethren, when I came to you, I did not come with a pomp of language or of wisdom, announcing to you the testimony of God;
1CO 2:2 for I determined to know nothing among you but Jesus Christ, even that crucified person; and
1CO 2:3 with regard to myself, I was among you in weakness and in fear, and in great trembling;
1CO 2:4 and my discourse and my proclamation was not with persuasive words of human wisdom, but with a demonstration of spirit and power,
1CO 2:5 that your belief might not be by the wisdom of men, but by the power of God.
1CO 2:6 We, however, speak wisdom among them who are perfect, but a wisdom not of this age, nor of the chiefs of this age to whose operations a stop is put;
1CO 2:7 but we speak a mysterious wisdom of God that hidden [wisdom] which God determinately marked out for the benefit of the ages, to our glory
1CO 2:8 which none of the chiefs of this age knew [for had they known it they would not have crucified the Lord of the glory]
1CO 2:9 things indeed, which as it is written, "Eye hath not seen, nor ear heard, nor the heart of man conceived; " which God hath prepared for them who love him;
1CO 2:10 and which God hath revealed to us by his spirit. For this spirit searcheth all things, even the depths of God.
1CO 2:11 For who of mankind knoweth the things of a man, but only the spirit of the man which is in him? So no one knoweth the things of God, but the spirit of God only.
1CO 2:12 Now we have not received the spirit of this world, but the spirit which is from God, that we may know the things which God hath freely granted to us;
1CO 2:13 which things we indeed speak, not in set words of human wisdom, but in the dictated words of a holy spirit, explaining spiritual things by spiritual words.
1CO 2:14 Now an animal man receiveth not those dictates of the spirit of God; for they are foolishness to him, and he cannot know them, because they are to be spiritually examined;
1CO 2:15 but the spiritual man examineth all things, and is himself examined by no man.
1CO 2:16 For who hath known the mind of the Lord? Who can instruct him? As for us we have the mind of Christ.
1CO 3:1 Now with regard to myself, I could not, brethren, speak to you as spiritual, but as carnal men, as babes in Christ.
1CO 3:2 I fed you with milk, and not with strong food, because you were not arrived at strength; nor are you indeed yet strong, even now.
1CO 3:3 For you are yet carnal; for while there is among you envy and strife and divisions, are you not carnal and walking in the ways of man?
1CO 3:4 For when one saith, I am for Paul; and another, I am for Apollos, are you not carnal?
1CO 3:5 Who then is Paul? And who is Apollos? Are they any thing but mere dispensers of another's bounty, by whose means you have believed? Even as the Lord hath given to each,
1CO 3:6 I planted, Apollos watered; but God gave the increase.
1CO 3:7 So that neither the planter nor the waterer is any thing; it is God only who giveth growth.
1CO 3:8 Now he who planteth and he who watereth are all one; and each shall receive his peculiar reward according to his peculiar labour.
1CO 3:9 For we are fellow labourers belonging to God; you are God's field; you are his building.
1CO 3:10 According to the favour of God granted to me, I, like a skilful architect, have laid a foundation, and another buildeth upon it. But let every one take heed how he buildeth thereon.
1CO 3:11 For no one can lay any other foundation than that which is laid, which is Jesus The Christ.
1CO 3:12 Now if upon this foundation any one buildeth gold, silver, precious stones, wood, hay, stubble;
1CO 3:13 the work of every one will be made manifest; for the day will shew it: Because it is revealed with fire, therefore the fire will prove every one's work of what sort it is.
1CO 3:14 If any one's work which he hath built upon it, shall stand the test, he will receive a reward.
1CO 3:15 If any one's work be consumed he will lose that; but he shall himself be saved but so as through fire.
