1CO 3:16 Do you not know that you are a temple of God, and that the spirit of God dwelleth in you?
1CO 3:17 If any one corrupt the temple of God, him God will destroy; for the temple of God is holy.
1CO 3:18 Whosoever you are, let no one deceive himself. If am one among you seemeth to be wise in this age, let him become a fool that he may become wise.
1CO 3:19 For the wisdom of this world is foolishness with God: for it is written, He entangleth the wise in their craft."
1CO 3:20 And again, "The Lord knoweth the thoughts of the wise that they are vain."
1CO 3:21 So let no one boast in men; for all things .are yours:
1CO 3:22 whether Paul. or Apollos, or Cephas, or the world, or life, or death, or things present, or things to come, all are yours,
1CO 3:23 and you are Christ's and Christ is God's.
1CO 4:1 In this manner let a man reckon us, as servants of Christ and stewards of divine mysteries.
1CO 4:2 Now that, which is principally required in a steward, is, that he be found faithful.
1CO 4:3 To me indeed it is a matter of very small concern, to be tried by you or by human process; nay, I will not be my own judge.
1CO 4:4 For though I am not conscious to myself of an' thing amiss, yet even in that case I am not justified; but he who trieth me is the Lord.
1CO 4:5 So pass no judgment prematurely, until the Lord come, who will bring to light the hidden things of darkness, and expose to view the counsels of the hearts, and then the praise for every one will be from God.
1CO 4:6 Now, brethren, I have transferred these things by a figure to myself and Apollos, for your sakes, that by us you may learn not to have your minds bent upon any thing above what is written; that you may not any of you be puffed up
1CO 4:7 for one [teacher] against another. For who distinguisheth thee? Or what hast thou, which thou didst not receive? Now if thou hast received, why boastest thou as if thou hadst not received?
1CO 4:8 You are now full! you are now rich! you have now reigned without us. I wish indeed that you did reign, that we also might reign with you.
1CO 4:9 For it seems as if God had exhibited us, the apostles, last on the stage as devoted to death since we are made a spectacle to the world, both to angels and men.
1CO 4:10 We are fools on the account of Christ; but you are prudent in Christ: We are weak; but you are strong: you are honourable; but we are despised:
1CO 4:11 Even at this very moment we are hungry and thirsty and naked and buffeted, and are wandering about and weary,
1CO 4:12 working with our own hands. Being reviled we give good words; being persecuted we suffer patiently;
1CO 4:13 being defamed we exhort. We are become as it were the expiatory sacrifices of the world; the refuse of all things until now.
1CO 4:14 I do not write these things to shame you, but am admonishing you as my beloved children.
1CO 4:15 For though you may have ten thousand guides in Christ, yet you have not many fathers; for by means of the glad tidings I am your father in Christ Jesus.
1CO 4:16 Therefore I intreat you to be imitators of me.
1CO 4:17 For this cause I have sent to you Timothy, who is my beloved son, and faithful in the Lord, who will remind you of my ways; those in Christ, as I am every where teaching in every congregation.
1CO 4:18 Now some are puffed up as if I would not come to you;
1CO 4:19 but I will come to you quickly, if it be the Lord's will, and I will know not the word, but the power of them who are puffed up.
1CO 4:20 For the reign of God is not in word but in power.
1CO 4:21 What do you chuse? that I should come to you with a rod, or with love and a spirit of meekness?
1CO 5:1 It is currently reported that there is among you an act of lewdness, and of such a sort as is not named among the nations, so that one hath his father's wife:
1CO 5:2 And you are puffed up! Why did you not rather mourn, in order that he who hath done such a deed might be removed from among you?
1CO 5:3 For I indeed, absent as I am in the body, but present in the spirit, have already determined as if I were present, with regard to him who hath done this,
1CO 5:4 in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ, when you and my spirit are assembled with the power of the Lord Jesus Christ,
1CO 5:5 to deliver such a one over to satan for the destruction of the flesh, that the spirit may be saved in the day of the Lord Jesus.
1CO 5:6 This boasting of yours is unbecoming. Do you not know that a little leaven leaveneth the whole mixture?
1CO 5:7 Purge out therefore the old leaven that you may be a new mass as you are unleavened. For Christ our Paschal lamb is indeed slain for us,
1CO 5:8 so that we should keep the festival, not with old leaven, nor with the leaven of wickedness and malignity; but with the unleavened bread of sincerity and truth.
1CO 5:9 I wrote to you in that letter not to associate with fornicators,
1CO 5:10 not including in general the fornicators of this world, nor those who are immoderate in their desires, or rapacious, or idolaters; since in that case you must needs have gone out of the world.
1CO 5:11 But this is what I now write to you, that if any one named a brother, be a fornicator, or one who gratifieth immoderate desires, or an idolater, or a railer, or a drunkard, you are not to associate; no, nor eat with such a one.
1CO 5:12 For what have I to do with passing sentence on those who are without? Is not this the case? On those within you are to pass sentence,
1CO 5:13 and God will pass sentence on those without. Therefore remove the wicked person from among yourselves.
1CO 6:1 Dare any of you having a controversy with another submit it to a trial before the unrighteous, and not before the saints?
1CO 6:2 Do you not know that the saints are to judge the world? If then the world is to be judged by you, are you unworthy to judge petty causes?
1CO 6:3 Do you not know that we shall judge angels? Can we not then things which concern this life?
1CO 6:4 If you therefore have controversies relating to affairs of this life, do you appoint those to be judges who are held in no esteem by the congregation?
1CO 6:5 To your shame I say, is it so that there is not among you a wise man; not so much as one who can determine a cause between brethren;
1CO 6:6 but brother goeth to law with brother and that before unbelievers?
1CO 6:7 Now, then, it is indeed a disparagement to you that you have law suits among yourselves. Why do you not rather suffer wrong? Why do you not rather suffer loss?
1CO 6:8 Instead of this you yourselves do wrong, and defraud even your brethren.
1CO 6:9 Do you not know that the unjust shall not inherit the kingdom of God? Be not deceived; neither fornicators, nor idolaters, nor adulterers, nor the voluptuous, nor sodomites,
1CO 6:10 nor thieves, nor such as indulge inordinate desires, nor drunkards, nor railers, nor extortioners, shall inherit the kingdom of God.
1CO 6:11 Now such some of you were; but, you have washed yourselves; but you are hallowed, but you are acquitted by the name of the Lord Jesus and by the spirit of our God.
1CO 6:12 Are all things lawful for me! All things however are not expedient. Are all things lawful for me! I however will not be a slave to any thing.
1CO 6:13 Meats are for the belly, and the belly for meats! But God will put a stop to the operation of both; But as for the body, it is not for fornication, but for the Lord; and the Lord for the body:
1CO 6:14 And as God hath raised up the Lord, he will by his power raise up you also.
1CO 6:15 Do you not know that your bodies are members 'of Christ? Shall I then take the members of the Christ, and make them members of a harlot? Surely no.
1CO 6:16 Do you not know that he who is joined to the harlot is one body with her? For the scripture saith, "They two shall be one flesh."
1CO 6:17 Now he who is joined to the Lord is one spirit with him.
1CO 6:18 Flee fornication. Every other sin, which a man committeth, is without the body; but he who committeth whoredom sinneth against his own body.
1CO 6:19 Do you not know that your body is a temple of a holy spirit in you, which you have from God? Indeed you are not your own;
1CO 6:20 for you have been bought with a price. Therefore glorify God with your body and with your spirit which are his.
1CO 7:1 Now with respect to those matters about which you wrote to me, it is well for a man not to marry:
1CO 7:2 but to avoid fornication let every man have his own wife; and every woman her own husband.
1CO 7:3 Let the husband render due benevolence to the wife; and in like manner the wife to the husband.
1CO 7:4 The wife hath not the power over her own body; but the husband: And in like manner the husband hath not the power over his own body; but the wife.
1CO 7:5 Withdraw not from each other, unless by mutual consent for a time, that you may devote yourselves to fasting and prayer. Then come together again that satan may not tempt you through your incontinence.
1CO 7:6 Now this I say by way of counsel, not of command;
1CO 7:7 for I wish all men to be as I myself am. But every one hath his peculiar gift from God, some of one kind; and some, of another.
1CO 7:8 I say then to unmarried men and to widows, it is well for them if they continue as I do.
1CO 7:9 But if they have not the gift of continency, let them marry; for it is better to marry than to burn.
1CO 7:10 And to them who are married I give this injunction; not I but the Lord: That a wife separate not herself from her husband;
1CO 7:11 but if she hath actually separated, let her continue unmarried, or be reconciled to her husband; and that a husband put not away a wife.
1CO 7:12 And to the rest I say, not the Lord; if any brother hath an unbelieving wife, and she is well satisfied to live with him, let him not divorce her:
1CO 7:13 and if any woman hath an unbelieving husband, and he is well satisfied to live with her, let her not divorce him.
1CO 7:14 For the unbelieving husband is hallowed by the wife, and the unbelieving wife is hallowed by the husband; else your children would be unclean; whereas they are now holy.
1CO 7:15 But if the unbelieving withdraw; let him or her withdraw, the brother or the sister is not in such cases enslaved: But God hath called us to peace.
1CO 7:16 For how knowest thou, O wife, but thou mayst save thy husband? Or how knowest thou, O husband, but thou mayst save thy wife?
1CO 7:17 But as God hath distributed to every one; as the Lord hath called every one, so let him walk. And thus I enjoin in all the congregations.
1CO 7:18 Hath any one been called, being circumcised, let him not become uncircumcised. Hath any been called in a state of uncircumcision, let him not be circumcised.
1CO 7:19 The circumcision is nothing, and the uncircumcision is nothing, in comparison with keeping the commandments of God.
1CO 7:20 In whatever state any one hath been called, in that let him abide.
1CO 7:21 Hast thou been called being a slave, let it not give thee concern. But if thou canst be made free, chuse that rather.
1CO 7:22 For he who is called by the Lord, being a slave, is the Lord's freedman; and in like manner he who is called being free, is the vassal of Christ.
1CO 7:23 You have been bought with a price, become not slaves of men.
1CO 7:24 Brethren, in whatever state any one hath been called, in that let him continue with God.
1CO 7:25 Now with respect to the virgins, I have no commandment of the Lord; but I give an opinion as one who hath obtained mercy of the Lord to be faithful.
1CO 7:26 I think then this to be good on account of the impending distress; that it is well for a man to be as he is.
1CO 7:27 Art thou bound to a wife? seek not to be disengaged: Art thou disengaged from a wife, seek not a wife.
1CO 7:28 But if thou shouldst actually marry, thou hast not sinned; and if the virgin marry she hath not sinned. But such will have affliction in the flesh: But I spare you
1CO 7:29 and say this, brethren, that the time with regard to what remaineth, is shortened, so that they who have wives should be as if they had them not;
1CO 7:30 and they who weep, as if they wept not; and they who rejoice, as if they rejoiced not; and they who buy, as not possessing; and they
1CO 7:31 who use this world, as not using it immoderately. For the scenery of this world is shifting;
1CO 7:32 and I wish you to be free from anxious cares. He who is unmarried careth for the things of the Lord how he may please the Lord;
1CO 7:33 but he who is married careth for the things of the world, how he may please his wife.
1CO 7:34 There is the like difference between the wife and the virgin. The unmarried careth for the things of the Lord, that she may be holy both in body and spirit; but she who is married careth for the things of the world, how she may please her husband.
1CO 7:35 Now this I say for your own benefit, not with a view to lay a snare for you; but for that which is becoming and best adapted to a steady, uninterrupted adherence to the Lord.
1CO 7:36 But if any man thinketh that he bringeth reproach on his virgin; if she be past the prime, this then should be the rule, What she willeth, let him do, he doth not sin; let them marry:
1CO 7:37 but whoever hath come to a. fixed determination in his heart, using no constraint, but hath power with respect to his own will and hath determined in his heart to keep his virgin, he doth well.
1CO 7:38 So that he who giveth in marriage doth well, but he who giveth not in marriage doth better.
1CO 7:39 A wife is bound by law as long as her husband liveth; but if her husband die; she is at liberty to many whom she will; only in the Lord.
1CO 7:40 But she is happier, if she continue as she is. This is my opinion, and I think I have a spirit of God.
1CO 8:1 Now with regard to the things offered to idols, we know that we all have knowledge. [This knowledge puffeth up; but love edifieth.
1CO 8:2 If then any one thinketh that he knoweth any thing, he knoweth nothing yet as he ought to know.
1CO 8:3 But if any one loveth God by him he is acknowledged.]
1CO 8:4 Therefore in respect to the eating of things offered to idols, we know that an idol is nothing in the world: and that there is no other God but one.
1CO 8:5 for though there are nominal gods both in heaven and on earth, as there are many gods and many lords;
1CO 8:6 yet to us there is out one God, the father of all, of whom are all things and we for him; and one Lord Jesus Christ, by whom are all things and we by him.
1CO 8:7 But all have not this knowledge; and some, with the consciousness of regard for the idol, even to this time eat meat as sacrificed to an idol; and their conscience being weak is defiled.
1CO 8:8 Now food doth not recommend us to God. For if we eat we are not the better; nor are we the worse if we do not eat.
1CO 8:9 But take heed that this liberty of yours do not prove a stumbling block to the weak.
1CO 8:10 For if one seeth thee who hast knowledge seated at table in an idol temple, will not the conscience of him who is weak be emboldened to eat the idol sacrifice?
1CO 8:11 And shall the weak brother, for whom Christ died, be destroyed for thy knowledge?
1CO 8:12 When you sin thus against the brethren and wound their weak conscience, you sin against Christ.
1CO 8:13 Wherefore if meat cause my brother to stumble, I will never eat flesh that I may not cause my brother to stumble.
1CO 9:1 Am not I an apostle? Am not I free? Have not I seen Jesus Christ our Lord? Are not you my work in the Lord?
1CO 9:2 If to others I am not an apostle, yet surely I am to you. For your being in the Lord is the seal of my apostleship.
1CO 9:3 My answer to them who examine me is this
1CO 9:4 Have we not a power to eat and drink?
1CO 9:5 Have we not a power to take along with us a sister, wife as well as the other apostles, and the brethren of the Lord, and Cephas?
1CO 9:6 Or are I only and Barnabas excluded from the privilege of not working?
1CO 9:7 Who goeth to war any time at his own expenses? Who planteth a vineyard and eateth not of the fruit thereof? Who feedeth a flock and doth not eat of the milk of that flock?
1CO 9:8 Do I say these things according to the custom of human affairs? Doth not the law say the same?
1CO 9:9 For in the law of Moses it is written, "Thou shalt not muzzle an ox treading out corn": Is God solicitous for oxen?
1CO 9:10 Or doth he not unquestionably say this for our sake? For us indeed it was written, because he who plougheth ought to plough in hope; and he who thresheth in hope ought to partake of his hope.
1CO 9:11 If we have sown for you spiritual things is it a great matter if we reap your carnal things?
1CO 9:12 If others exercise this power over you, may not we rather? But we have not made use of this power; but endure all things that we may not give any obstruction to the glad tidings of the Christ.
1CO 9:13 Do you not know that they who prepare the sacrifice eat of the sacrifice? They who attend on the altar partake with the altar.
1CO 9:14 So also the Lord hath ordered for them who proclaim the glad tidings, that they should live by the glad tidings
1CO 9:15 But as for me I have not made use of any of these privileges nor have I written these things that they should be a rule for me. For it were better for me to die than that any should deprive me of what is my boast.
1CO 9:16 For though I publish the glad tidings I have no cause of boasting; for I am under an obligation and woe is for me if I do not publish the glad tiding
1CO 9:17 for if I do this willingly, I have a reward; but if against my will I have been intrusted with an office, what then is the reward for me?
1CO 9:18 In this case, when proclaiming the glad tiding I will make the glad tidings of the Christ so far unexpensive, not to use to the utmost the privilege which I have by the glad tidings.
1CO 9:19 For being free from all men, I have made myself a slave to all that I may gain the more.
1CO 9:20 To the Jews I became as a Jew that I might gain the Jews: to them under law, as if I were under law, that I might gain those under law:
1CO 9:21 to them without law, as if I were without law [not as without law to God, but under a law to Christ] that I might gain those with out law:
1CO 9:22 To the weak I became as weak, that I might gain the weak; to all those I have become all this that I may save all.
1CO 9:23 And this I do in consequence of the glad tidings that I may be a joint sharer thereof.
1CO 9:24 Do you not know that they who run a race, all run; but one only rcceiveth the prize? In this manner run ye, that you may obtain.
1CO 9:25 Now, every one who is to contend in the public games is temperate in all things. They indeed do this that they may obtain a corruptible crown. But we [to obtain] one that is incorruptible.
1CO 9:26 For my part, therefore, I run in this manner, not as if I were running unseen: I fight, not as if I were beating the air;
1CO 9:27 but I buffet my body and subdue it, lest having proclaimed the glad tidings to others I myself should be disapproved.
1CO 10:1 Moreover, I would not, brethren, have you ignorant that our fathers were all under the cloud, and that they all passed through the sea,
1CO 10:2 and were all baptized to Moses in the cloud and in the sea;
1CO 10:3 and did all eat the same spiritual food;
1CO 10:4 and did all drink of the same spiritual drink, for they drank from a spiritual rock accompanying them; now that rock was the Christ.
1CO 10:5 But with the greater part of them God was not well pleased; for they were overthrown in the wilderness.
1CO 10:6 Now these things were examples for us, that we may not lust after evil things as they did.
1CO 10:7 Be not ye then idolaters as some of them were; as it is written, "The people sat down to eat and drink and rose up to play:"
1CO 10:8 Nor let us commit fornication as some of them did, and there fell in one day twenty three thousand:
1CO 10:9 nor let us try the Christ as some indeed of them did, and were destroyed by serpents:
1CO 10:10 nor murmur ye, as some of them murmured and were destroyed by the destroyer.
1CO 10:11 Now all these things came upon them for examples, and were written for the instruction of us on whom the ends of the ages have met.
1CO 10:12 So let him who thinketh that he standeth, take heed that he do not fall.
1CO 10:13 No trial hath come upon you but such as is common to man; and God is faithful, and will not suffer you to be tried above your strength, but will with the trial make a way to escape, that you may be able to bear it.
1CO 10:14 Therefore, my beloved, flee from idolatry.
1CO 10:15 I speak to you as men of understanding; judge ye what I say
1CO 10:16 The cup of blessing which we bless, is it not a fellowship in the blood of the Christ? The loaf which we break, is it not a Fellowship in the body of the Christ?
1CO 10:17 Because it is one loaf, we being many are one body, for we ail partake of this one loaf.
1CO 10:18 Consider Israel according to the flesh; are not they who eat the sacrifices, partakers in common of the altar.
1CO 10:19 What then, do I say that an idol is any thing? or that what is sacrificed to an idol is any thing?
1CO 10:20 No. I only say, that what the nations sacrifice, they sacrifice to demons and not to God. Now, I would not have you to be partakers in the worship of the demons.
1CO 10:21 You cannot drink the cup of the Lord and the cup of demons. You cannot partake of the table of the Lord and of the table of demons.
1CO 10:22 Are we provoking the Lord to jealousy? Are we stronger than he?
1CO 10:23 All things are lawful for me. All things however are not expedient, All things are lawful for me." All things however do not edify.
1CO 10:24 Let none seek barely his own interest, but every one that of his neighbour.
1CO 10:25 Eat whatever is sold in the shambles, asking no questions for conscience sake;
1CO 10:26 for the earth is the Lord's and the fulness thereof.
1CO 10:27 And if any of the disbelievers invite you to an entertainment, and you chuse to go, eat whatever is set before you, asking no questions for conscience sake.
1CO 10:28 But if any one say to you, This was sacrificed to an idol, eat not of it for the sake of him who gave the information; and for conscience sake; for the earth is the Lord's and the fulness thereof.
1CO 10:29 When I say conscience I do not mean one's own, but the conscience of the other.
1CO 10:30 But why is my liberty to be judged by another's conscience? And if I partake with thankfulness, why am I ill spoken of for what I give thanks?
1CO 10:31 Whether then you eat or drink, or whatever you do, do all to the glory of God.
1CO 10:32 Conduct yourselves so as to give no offence to Jews or Greeks, or the congregation of God,
1CO 10:33 even as I do. In all things I please all men, not studying barely my own interest, but that of the many, that they may be saved.
1CO 11:1 Be ye imitators of me as I am of Christ.
1CO 11:2 Now, I praise you, brethren, that in all things you are mindful of me and hold fast the doctrines as I delivered them to you;
1CO 11:3 and I wish you to know that the Christ is the head of every man; and that the head of woman is the man; and the head of Christ is God.
1CO 11:4 Every man praying or prophesying with his head covered dishonoureth his head;
1CO 11:5 and every woman praying or prophesying with the head uncovered dishonoureth her head; for it is the same as if she were shaven.
1CO 11:6 For if a woman is not veiled, let her be shorn. But if it be shameful for a woman to be shorn or shaved, let her be veiled.
1CO 11:7 For man indeed ought not to have his head covered, he being an image and a glory of God; but woman is a glory of man;
1CO 11:8 for man was not made of woman; but woman of man.
1CO 11:9 Nor was man created for the woman; but woman for the man.
1CO 11:10 The woman, therefore, ought to have a covering on the head, because of the messengers.
1CO 11:11 Nevertheless, man is not without woman, nor woman without man in the Lord.
1CO 11:12 For as the woman was of the man, so also the man is by the woman; and all things are of God.
1CO 11:13 Judge for yourselves. Is it becoming for a woman unveiled to pray to God?
1CO 11:14 Doth not nature itself teach you that if a man hath long hair, it is a shame to him;
1CO 11:15 but if a woman hath long hair it is a glory to her; because the hair is given her for a veil.
1CO 11:16 If any one, however, is disposed to be contentious, neither we nor the congregations have any such custom.
1CO 11:17 But in regard to this which I am about to mention I do not commend you, because you meet together not for the better but for the worse.
1CO 11:18 For in the first place, on your assembling together in the congregation, I hear that there are divisions among you; and I partly believe it:
1CO 11:19 for there must be sects among you, that the approved among you may become manifest.
1CO 11:20 When you therefore assemble together, it is not to eat the Lord's supper;
1CO 11:21 for every one at eating taketh first his own supper, so one indeed is hungry and another is plentifully fed.
1CO 11:22 What? have you not houses for eating and drinking? Or do you despise the congregation of God, and expose to shame them who have not? What must I say to you? Shall I commend you for this? I do not commend you.
1CO 11:23 For I received from the Lord this which I delivered to you, that the Lord Jesus on the night in which he was delivered up, took a loaf,
1CO 11:24 and having given thanks, broke it, and said, "Take, eat; this is my body which is broken for you. Do this in commemoration of me."
1CO 11:25 And in like manner, the cup also, after supper, saying, "This cup is the new covenant by my blood. Do this, as often as you drink it, in commemoration of me.
1CO 11:26 For as often as you eat this loaf, and drink this cup, you proclaim the death of the Lord, until he come.
1CO 11:27 So that whosoever shall eat this loaf or drink this cup of the Lord in an unworthy manner, he will be guilty of the body and blood of the Lord.
1CO 11:28 Now, let a man examine himself, and in this manner eat of that loaf and drink of that cup;
1CO 11:29 for he who eateth and drinketh in an unworthy manner, eateth and drinketh a judgment for himself, not distinguishing the body of the Lord.
1CO 11:30 For this cause many among you are weakly and sick, and many are falling asleep.
1CO 11:31 For if we distinguish ourselves, should we not be judged?
1CO 11:32 And being judged, we are corrected by the Lord, that we may not be condemned with the world.
1CO 11:33 Wherefore, my brethren, when you assemble to eat, wait for one another;
1CO 11:34 and if any one is hungry let him eat at home, that you may not come together for judgment. And the rest I will set in order when I come.
1CO 12:1 Now, brethren, I would not have you ignorant with respect to the spiritual gifts.
1CO 12:2 You know that you were Gentiles carried away to dumb idols just as you were led.
1CO 12:3 Therefore I certify to you that none speaking by a spirit of God saith that Jesus is an Anathema; and that none can say that Jesus is the Lord, but by a holy spirit.
1CO 12:4 Now, there are diversities of gifts, but the same spirit;
1CO 12:5 and there are diversities of offices, but the same Lord;
1CO 12:6 and there are diversities of energies, but it is the same God who by his inward operation worketh all these effects in all.
1CO 12:7 Now, this manifestation of the spirit is given to every one for that which is profitable.
1CO 12:8 For to one is given, by the spirit, a word of wisdom; and to another, a word of knowledge according to the same spirit;
1CO 12:9 and to another, faith, by the same spirit; and to another, gifts of healing, by the same spirit;
1CO 12:10 and to another, mighty powers of working miracles; and to another, the gift of prophecy; and to another, that of discerning spirits; and to another, divers languages; and to another, the interpretation of languages.
1CO 12:11 Now, it is one and the same spirit who effecteth all these, distributing his own as he pleaseth, to every one.
1CO 12:12 For as the body is one, and hath many members, and all the members of that one body, being many, are one body; so also is the Christ.
1CO 12:13 For by one spirit we are all baptized to one body, whether we were Jews or Greeks, slaves, or freemen; and have all been made to drink to one spirit.
1CO 12:14 For the body is not one member, but many.
1CO 12:15 If the foot should say, "Because I am not a hand, I am not of the body," is it therefore not of the body?
1CO 12:16 And if the ear should say, "Because I am not an eye, I am not of the body," is it therefore not of the body?"
1CO 12:17 If the whole body were eye, where would, be the hearing? If the whole were hearing, where would be the smelling?
1CO 12:18 But now God hath placed the members, every one of them, in the body, as it hath pleased him.
1CO 12:19 But if they were all one member, where would be the body?
1CO 12:20 Now they indeed are many members, yet one body:
1CO 12:21 and the eye cannot say to the hand, I have no need of thee: nor can the head say to the feet, I have no need of you.
1CO 12:22 On the contrary, those members of the body which seem to be the weakest are more especially necessary;
1CO 12:23 and on those which we think the more dishonourable parts of the body we bestow the more abundant honour: and the uncomely parts of us have more abundant finery,
1CO 12:24 of which the comely parts have no need. God indeed hath formed the symmetry of the body, giving more abundant honour to the part which wanteth it,
1CO 12:25 that there may be no schisms in the body, but that the members may have mutual concern for one another;
1CO 12:26 so that if one member suffereth, all the rest suffer with it; and if one member is honoured, all the rest rejoice with it.
1CO 12:27 Now with regard to you, ye are a body of Christ, even individual members,
1CO 12:28 whom God hath placed in the congregation; first, apostles, secondly, prophets, thirdly, teachers, then miraculous powers, then gifts of healing, helps, governments, different languages.
1CO 12:29 Are all apostles? Are all prophets? Are all teachers? Have all miraculous powers?
1CO 12:30 Have all the gifts of healing? Do all speak divers languages? Are all interpreters?
1CO 12:31 But you are ambitious of those gifts which are of superior excellence. Well, I am going to point out to you a way still more excellent.
1CO 13:1 Though I speak with the tongues of men and of angels, if I have not love, I am but a sounding brass or a tinkling cymbal;
1CO 13:2 and though I have a gift of prophesy and understand all the mysteries and all this knowledge; and though I have all that faith, so as to remove mountains; if I have not love, I am nothing.
1CO 13:3 And though I distribute all my substance to feed the poor, and deliver up my body to be burned, if I have not love, it profiteth me nothing.
1CO 13:4 Love is long suffering; it aboundeth in kindness. Love is not envious. Love is not insolent: it is not puffed up.
1CO 13:5 It doth not behave itself unbecomingly. It is not self interested. It is not easily provoked. It placeth not the evil to account.
1CO 13:6 It rejoiceth not in iniquity, but shareth in the joys of truth.
1CO 13:7 It beareth all things. It believeth all things. It hopeth all things. It endureth all things patiently.
1CO 13:8 Love never faileth. But as for prophecies, they will be out of use. As for languages, they will cease: As for science, it will be done away.
1CO 13:9 For we now know in part and prophesy in part,
1CO 13:10 but when perfection is come, there will a stop be put to that which is in part.
1CO 13:11 When I was a child, I spake as a child, I thought as a child, I reasoned as a child; but when I became a man, I put a stop to childish things.
1CO 13:12 For we now by means of a mirrour see a representation of things; but we shall then see face to face. I now know in part; but I shall then know as I am known.
1CO 13:13 Now then these three, faith, hope and love, will remain; but love is the greatest of the three.
1CO 14:1 Be zealous then in the pursuit of this love, and aspire after spiritual gifts, but chiefly that you may prophesy.
1CO 14:2 For he who speaketh in a strange language, speaketh not to men but to God: for none understandeth; and with a spirit he speaketh mysteries.
1CO 14:3 But he who prophesieth, speaketh to men edification, and exhortation, and consolation.
1CO 14:4 He who speaketh in an unknown tongue edifieth himself; but he who prophesieth, edifieth a congregation.
1CO 14:5 Now I wish you all to speak with tongues; but much rather that you should prophesy: For he who prophesieth is greater than he who speaketh with tongues, unless some one interpret, that the congregation may be edified.
1CO 14:6 For instance, should I, brethren, come to you, speaking with tongues, what shall I profit you, unless I explain to you what I say, be it either a revelation, or science, or a prophecy, or a doctrine.
1CO 14:7 In like manner with regard to inanimate things which give a sound, whether pipe or kithara, unless they produce distinct notes, how can it be known what that is, which is played on the pipe or kithara.
1CO 14:8 For if even a trumpet give an undistinguishable sound who will prepare himself for battle?
1CO 14:9 So also with regard to you, unless you utter with the tongue a discourse of a clear signification, how can that which is spoken be known? You will be indeed talking to the air.
1CO 14:10 Let there be ever so many kinds of sounds in the world, and none of them without signification,
1CO 14:11 if I do not know the meaning of the sound I shall be to the speaker a barbarian, and he who speaketh will be the same to me.
1CO 14:12 Such also is the case with you. Since you then are ambitious of spiritual gifts, seek to abound in such as tend to the improvement of the congregation.
1CO 14:13 Let him therefore who speaketh in an unknown tongue, pray that he may interpret.
1CO 14:14 For if I pray in an unknown tongue, my spirit prayeth, but my understanding is unfruitful.
1CO 14:15 What then is to be done? I am to pray with the spirit and to pray with the understanding also. I am to sing with the spirit, and to sing with the understanding also.
1CO 14:16 Otherwise if thou bless with the spirit, how can he who occupieth the place of the unlearned say Amen at thy giving thanks, when he knoweth not what thou sayest?
1CO 14:17 Thou indeed givest thanks well, but the other is not edified.
1CO 14:18 I thank my God, I speak with tongues more than you all;
1CO 14:19 but in a congregation I would rather speak five words with my understanding that I may instruct others, than ten thousand words in an unknown tongue.
1CO 14:20 Brethren, be not children in your understandings; but be infants in malice; and in your understandings full grown men.
1CO 14:21 It is written in the law, "By men of strange tongues and with strange lips I will speak to this people; yet for all this they will not hearken to me, saith the Lord."
1CO 14:22 So that these strange tongues are for a sign, not for them who believe; but for unbelievers. But prophesying is not for unbelievers, but for them who believe.
1CO 14:23 If therefore the whole congregation assemble and all speak with unknown tongues, and there should come in any uninstructed persons or unbelievers, would they not say that you are raving?
1CO 14:24 But if all prophesy, and any unbeliever or uninstructed person come in, he is convicted by all; examined by all;
1CO 14:25 and thus the secrets of his heart are laid open, and so, falling on his face, he will worship God, declaring that God is indeed among you.
1CO 14:26 What then, brethren, is to be done? When you come together every one of you hath a psalm; hath a doctrine; hath a strange tongue; hath a revelation; hath an interpretation; let all be for edification;
1CO 14:27 and if any one speak in an unknown tongue, let him speak as by two, or at the most three; and in parts, and let one interpret:
1CO 14:28 but if there be no interpreter, let him be silent in a congregation, and speak to himself and to God.
1CO 14:29 And let two or three prophets speak, and let the rest deliberate.
1CO 14:30 And if a revelation be made to another who is sitting, let the first have become silent.
1CO 14:31 For you can all prophesy, one by one, that all may learn, and all be comforted,
1CO 14:32 And the spirits of prophets are subject to prophets.
1CO 14:33 For God is not a God of confusion, but of peace, As in all the congregations of the saints
1CO 14:34 let your women be silent in these congregations: for they are not permitted to talk, but to be in subjection, as the law also saith:
1CO 14:35 And if they wish to learn any thing let them ask their husbands at home. For it is shameful for women to talk in a congregation.
1CO 14:36 Did the word of God go forth from you? or did it come to you only?
1CO 14:37 If any one be, in reality, a prophet, or a spiritual man, let him acknowledge that what I write to you are the commandments of the Lord.
1CO 14:38 But if any one doth not know this, let him continue ignorant.
1CO 14:39 So then, brethren, be ambitious of prophesying, and prohibit not the speaking with tongues.
1CO 14:40 Let all things be done in a becoming and orderly manner.
1CO 15:1 I now, brethren, remind you in what terms I proclaimed the gospel which I proclaimed to you, and which you received, and in which you have continued,
1CO 15:2 and by which also you are saved, if you strictly adhere to it, unless indeed you believed in vain.
1CO 15:3 For I delivered to you, as one of the principal things, that which I actually received, that Christ died for our sins, according to the scriptures;
1CO 15:4 and that he was buried; and that he was raised up the third day according to the scriptures;
1CO 15:5 and that he was seen by Cephas, then, by the twelve;
1CO 15:6 after that he was seen by above five hundred brethren at once, of whom the greater number are even now alive, but some indeed are composed to rest;
1CO 15:7 after that he was seen by James, then by all the apostles;
1CO 15:8 and, last of all, he was seen also by me, who am as it were one born out of due time;
1CO 15:9 for I am the very least of the apostles, and am not worthy to be called an apostle, because I persecuted the congregation of God.
1CO 15:10 But by the favour of God I am what I am; and this favour of his which reached me was not fruitless; but I have laboured more than they all; yet not I, but the grace of God which was with me.
1CO 15:11 Whether therefore I or they laboured, thus do we proclaim, and thus you have believed.
1CO 15:12 Now, if Christ be proclaimed, that he hath been raised from the dead, how do some among you say that there is no resurrection of the dead?
1CO 15:13 If there is indeed no resurrection of the dead, then Christ is not raised.
1CO 15:14 And if Christ hath not been raised, our proclamation is vain, and your belief is also vain.
1CO 15:15 And we are found to be actually false witnesses of God; because we have testified concerning God, that he hath raised the Christ, whom he hath not raised, if indeed the dead are not raised.
1CO 15:16 For if the dead are not raised, then Christ was not raised.
1CO 15:17 And if Christ hath not been raised, your belief is vain; you are still in your sins;
1CO 15:18 and consequently they, who have been composed to rest in Christ, have perished.
1CO 15:19 If we have hope in Christ in this life only, we, of all men, are most to be pitied.
1CO 15:20 But now Christ hath been raised from the dead. He was the first fruits of them who have been composed to rest.
1CO 15:21 For since by man came death, by man also cometh a resurrection of the dead.
1CO 15:22 For as by Adam all die, so by the Christ all shall be brought to life:
1CO 15:23 but every one in his proper order; Christ the first fruits; then they who belong to Christ, at his coming:
1CO 15:24 then the end, when he shall deliver up the kingdom to God the father, when he shall have put a stop to all empire and all authority, and all power.
1CO 15:25 For he must reign until he hath put all the enemies under his feet.
1CO 15:26 The last enemy, death, is to be destroyed:
1CO 15:27 for he hath put all under his feet. "But when it is said, That all are subjected; it is evident that there is an exception of him who subjected the all to him;
1CO 15:28 and when the all are subjected to him, then will the Son himself also be subjected to him who subjected the all to him that God may be the all in all.
1CO 15:29 This being the case what will they do who are baptized for the dead? If they who are altogether dead are not raised up, why are they then baptized for the dead?
1CO 15:30 and why are we every hour incurring danger
1CO 15:31 I dying daily? I swear by that boasting of yours" [meaning that which I have in Christ Jesus our Lord]
1CO 15:32 "if I as a man had fought with beasts at Ephesus, what advantage is that to me if the dead are not raised up? Let us eat and drink, for to morrow we die."
1CO 15:33 Be not led astray; "good morals are debauched by talk profane."
1CO 15:34 Be righteously sober and sin not. For some have not a knowledge of God. I say this to your shame.
1CO 15:35 But a certain person will say, How are the dead raised, and with what sort of a body do they come?
1CO 15:36 Simpleton! that which thou thyself sowest is not quickened unless it dieth.
1CO 15:37 And as to what thou sowest, thou sowest not the body which is to be, but a bare grain, for instance, of wheat, or of any other seeds:
1CO 15:38 and God giveth it a body as it hath pleased him, and to every of the seeds its own peculiar body.
1CO 15:39 All flesh is not of the same sort; but there is one sort of flesh peculiar to men; another to beasts, and another to fishes, and another to birds.
1CO 15:40 There are also celestial bodies, and terrestrial bodies. But the glory of the celestial is of one sort, and the glory of the terrestrial, of another.
1CO 15:41 The glory of the sun is of one kind; and the glory of the moon, of another; and the glory of the stars is different: One star differeth from another in glory.
1CO 15:42 Thus it is also with respect to the resurrection of the dead. That which is sown, is sown in corruption; it is raised in incorruption;
1CO 15:43 it is sown in dishonour; it is raised in glory: it is sown in weakness; it is raised in power:
1CO 15:44 it is sown an animal body; it is raised a spiritual body. There is an animal body; and there is a spiritual body.
1CO 15:45 Thus also it is written, "The first man Adam was made a living soul." The latter Adam is a quickening spirit.
1CO 15:46 The spiritual was not first, but the animal; then the spiritual.
1CO 15:47 The first man from the earth was earthy; the second man is the Lord from heaven.
1CO 15:48 As the earthy was, such also are they who are earthy. And as the heavenly is, such shall they be who are heavenly.
1CO 15:49 And as we have borne the image of the earthy, we shall also bear the image of the heavenly.
1CO 15:50 Now this I say, brethren, that flesh and blood cannot inherit the kingdom of God; nor can corruption inherit incorruption.
1CO 15:51 Behold I tell you a secret: We shall not all be composed to rest; but we shall all be changed
1CO 15:52 in a moment in the twinkling of an eye, at the last trumpet, for it will sound, and the dead will be raised incorruptible, and we shall be changed.
1CO 15:53 For this corruptible must put on incorruptibility; and this mortal must put on immortality.
1CO 15:54 Now when this corruptible shall have put on incorruptibility; and this mortal shall have put on immortality, then will be brought to pass the word which is written, "Death is completely swallowed up."
1CO 15:55 O death where is thy sting? Where thy victory, O grave?
1CO 15:56 Sin is indeed the sting of death; And the law is the strength of sin:
1CO 15:57 But thanks be to God who gives us the victory Through our Lord Jesus Christ.
1CO 15:58 So then, my beloved brethren, be ye stedfast, immoveable, abounding always in the work of the Lord, for as much as you know that your labour in the Lord is not in vain.
1CO 16:1 Now, with respect to the collection which is for the saints, as I have directed in the congregations of Galatia, so do ye also.
1CO 16:2 Every first day of the week, let every one of you lay by him, and put into a common treasury, what he can conveniently; that when I come there may be no collection then made.
1CO 16:3 And when I come, whomsoever you approve, them I will despatch with letters to carry your bounty to Jerusalem.
1CO 16:4 And if it be thought proper that I myself should go, they shall go with me.
1CO 16:5 Now I will come to you when I have passed through Macedonia, [for I am going through Macedonia]
1CO 16:6 and perhaps I may continue with you some time, or even spend the winter, that you may forward me on in whatever journey I may take.
1CO 16:7 For I do not wish to see you now on my way, but hope to spend some time with you, if the Lord permit.
1CO 16:8 But I will stay at Ephesus until the pentecost,
1CO 16:9 for a great and effectual door is opened for me, though there are many opposers.
1CO 16:10 Now when Timothy comes to you, see that he be with you without fear; for he worketh the work of the Lord, as I myself do.
1CO 16:11 Therefore let none despise him; but forward him on in peace, that he may come to me; for I wait for him with the brethren.
1CO 16:12 Now with respect to Apollos the brother, I importuned him much to go to you with the brethren. Though upon the whole it was not his will to go now, yet he will go when there shall be a favourable opportunity.
1CO 16:13 Watch; stand firm in the faith; acquit yourselves like men; be strong;
1CO 16:14 let all your affairs be transacted with love.
1CO 16:15 And I intreat you, brethren, [you know the household of Stephanas, that it is the first fruits of Achaia, and that they have addicted themselves to the service of the saints;]
1CO 16:16 that you submit yourselves to such, and to every fellow worker and labourer.
1CO 16:17 Now I rejoice at the coming of Stephanas, and Fortunatus, and Achaicus, because they have supplied to the full what was wanting on your part.
1CO 16:18 For they have quieted my spirit as well as yours. Have regard therefore to such as these.
1CO 16:19 The congregations of Asia salute you. Aquilas, and Priscilla; and the congregation at their house, salute you with much affection in the Lord.
1CO 16:20 All the brethren salute you. Salute ye one another with a holy kiss.
1CO 16:21 The salutation of me Paul with my own hand
1CO 16:22 If any one loveth not the Lord Jesus Christ, let him be an Anathema. Maranatha.
1CO 16:23 The favour of the Lord Jesus Christ be with you.
1CO 16:24 My love be with you all in Christ Jesus. Amen.
2CO 1:1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, and Timothy the brother, to the congregation of God which is at Corinth, together with all the saints who are in all Achaia.
2CO 1:2 Favour be to you and peace from God our Father, and the Lord Jesus Christ.
2CO 1:3 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, the Father of mercies and the God of all consolation,
2CO 1:4 who comforteth us in all our affliction, to the end that we may be able to comfort them who are in any affliction, with the comfort with which we ourselves have been comforted by God.
2CO 1:5 Because in proportion as the sufferings of the Christ abound towards us, so by means of Christ our consolation also aboundeth;
2CO 1:6 and whether we are afflicted, it is for your consolation and salvation, which is effectually wrought out by a patient enduring of the same sufferings which we suffer; or if we are comforted, it is for your consolation and salvation;
2CO 1:7 therefore our hope of you is stedfast, as we know, that as you are partakers of the sufferings, so will you be also of the consolation.
2CO 1:8 For we do not, brethren, wish you to be ignorant with respect to that affliction of ours which befel us in Asia; that we were exceedingly pressed beyond our strength, so that we had indeed no hopes of life;
2CO 1:9 but had in ourselves the sentence of death, that we might not trust in ourselves, but in God who raiseth the dead,
2CO 1:10 who delivered us from so great a death, and doth deliver: in whom we trust that he will still deliver us,
2CO 1:11 you joining the assistance of your prayers for us, that the favour granted to us for the sake of many may be acknowledged by many with thanksgiving on our behalf.
2CO 1:12 For this is the matter of our boasting; the testimony of our conscience, that with simplicity and godly sincerity, not with carnal wisdom, but by the grace of God, we have conducted ourselves in the world, and more especially towards you.
2CO 1:13 For we write nothing to you but what you clearly understand or have acknowledged, and will, I hope, even to the end acknowledge,
2CO 1:14 as some of you have acknowledged us, that we are your boast, as you indeed will be ours, in the day of the Lord Jesus.
2CO 1:15 And in this confidence I purposed to come to you first, that you might have a second benefit;
2CO 1:16 and through you to proceed on to Macedonia, and from Macedonia to come to you again, and be by you forwarded on to Judea.
2CO 1:17 Did I then, in purposing this, use fickleness? Or what I purpose do I purpose according to the flesh, so that with me there may be the yes, yes; and the no, no?
2CO 1:18 Now as God is faithful, our word to you was not yes and no.
2CO 1:19 For the Son of God, [namely] Jesus Christ, who was proclaimed among you by us namely by me, and Silvanus, and Timothy, was not yes and no; but by him hath been made yes.
2CO 1:20 For all the promises of God are in him yes, and in him Amen, for glory to God through us.
2CO 1:21 Now, he who keepeth us together with you firm for Christ, and anointed us, is God,
2CO 1:22 who hath sealed us, and given us the earnest of the spirit in our hearts;
2CO 1:23 and I appeal to God, as a witness on my life, that with a view to spare you I have not yet come to Corinth:
2CO 1:24 not that we have dominion over your faith; but are joint promoters of your joy; for in this faith you have continued;
2CO 2:1 but I determined this with myself, that my coming again should not be the occasion of grief to you.
2CO 2:2 For if I grieve you, who is there to gladden me? None, but he whom I have made sorrowful:
2CO 2:3 and I wrote to you for this 'very purpose, that, when I come, I may not have grief on account of them for whom I ought to rejoice; as I have a confidence in you all, that my joy is the joy of you all.
2CO 2:4 For in great affliction and anguish of heart I wrote to you, with many tears"not that you should be grieved, but that you might know that overflowing love which I have for you.
2CO 2:5 Now if any one hath occasioned grief, he hath grieved me only as a partner in it; that I may not continue a burden on you all;
2CO 2:6 sufficient for such a one is the censure which hath been passed by the majority;
2CO 2:7 so that, on the contrary, I rather wish you to forgive and comfort him, that such a one may not be overwhelmed with an excess of sorrow.
2CO 2:8 Therefore I intreat you to authorise love for him.
2CO 2:9 For this was one purpose of my writing, that  I might have this proof of you, whether you are obedient in all things.
2CO 2:10 And to whomsoever you forgive any thing, I do so too. For with regard to myself, if I have forgiven any one whatever any thing, I have forgiven him for your sakes, in the presence of Christ,
2CO 2:11 that Satan may not get an advantage over us, for we are not ignorant of his devices.
2CO 2:12 Now when I came to Troas for the purpose of proclaiming the glad tidings of the Christ, though the Lord opened a door for me,
2CO 2:13 I had no rest in my spirit, because I did not find my brother Titus; but taking leave of them, I set out for Macedonia.
2CO 2:14 But thanks be to God who causeth us always to triumph in the Christ, and who manifesteth by us, in every place, the odour of the knowledge of him.
2CO 2:15 Because we are for God a strong odour of the Christ among them who are saved, and among them who perish
2CO 2:16 [to these indeed an odour of death for death, but to those an odour of life for life] who therefore is sufficient for this?
2CO 2:17 For we do not like the many, adulterate the word of God, but as men of sincerity, but as men of God, in the presence of God in Christ we speak.
2CO 3:1 "Are we beginning again to commend ourselves to you? Do we only want, like certain persons, commendatory letters to you, or letters of recommendation from you?
2CO 3:2 You yourselves are our letter. It hath been written in our hearts; it is known and read by all men.
2CO 3:3 You are shewn publickly because you are the letter of Christ which we make use of. It is written, not with ink, but with the spirit of the living God; not on tables of stone, but on fleshly tables of the heart.
2CO 3:4 Such is the confidence which we have through Christ in regard to God;
2CO 3:5 not that we are of ourselves sufficient to reckon any thing as proceeding from ourselves; but our sufficiency is from God,
2CO 3:6 who hath qualified us to be ministers of a new covenant; not of letter but of spirit; for the letter killeth, but the spirit giveth life.
2CO 3:7 [Now if the ministration of death engraven in letters, on stones, was attended with such glory, that the children of Israel could not look steadily on the face of Moses, because of the temporary glory of his countenance;
2CO 3:8 shall not the ministration of the spirit be much more attended with glory?
2CO 3:9 For if that ministration of condemnation was attended with glory, much more doth this ministration of justification abound in glory.
2CO 3:10 For that indeed which was glorious, is in this respect not glorious because of this super-excellent glory.
2CO 3:11 For if that which was temporary was with glory, much more shall this which is permanent be attended with glory.
2CO 3:12 Having therefore such a hope, we use great plainness of speech,
2CO 3:13 and do not [act] as Moses. He put a veil on his face, that the children of Israel might not look stedfastly to the end of that which is abolished.
2CO 3:14 Their minds were indeed blinded, for even to this day that very veil at the reading of the old covenant remaineth. That which is abolished by Christ is not unveiled,
2CO 3:15 but even at this day when Moses is read there is a veil upon their heart,
2CO 3:16 but when ever it shall turn to the Lord that veil will be taken away.
2CO 3:17 Now the Lord is the spirit? And where the spirit of the Lord, is, there is liberty; and we all with an unveiled face viewing, as in a mirrour, the glory of the Lord, are transformed into the same image from glory to glory, as from the Lord of spirit.
2CO 4:1 Having therefore this ministration, as we have obtained mercy, we do not falter,
2CO 4:2 but have renounced the secrets of shame, not walking in craftiness, nor dealing deceitfully with the word of God, but by the clear manifestation of the truth recommending ourselves to every man's conscience in the sight of God.
2CO 4:3 If then these glad tidings of ours are veiled, they are veiled by those perishing things,
2CO 4:4 with which the god of this world hath blinded the minds of the disbelieving, that the splendour of the glad tidings of the glory of the Christ, who is an image of God, may not shine upon them.
2CO 4:5 For we do not proclaim ourselves, but Christ Jesus the Lord; and ourselves your servants for Jesus sake.
2CO 4:6 Because it is God, who commanded light to shine out of darkness, who hath shined in our hearts, to give a lustre of the knowledge of the glory of God in the person of Jesus Christ;
2CO 4:7 and we have this treasure in earthen vessels, that the excellence of the power may belong to God and not be from, us;
2CO 4:8 we are pressed on every side, but not utterly crushed; perplexed, but not in despair;
2CO 4:9 persecuted, but not quite forsaken; cast down, but not destroyed;
2CO 4:10 always carrying about in the body the dying of the Lord Jesus, that the life of Jesus may be manifested in this body of ours.
2CO 4:11 For we, who are living, are continually delivered up to death on the account of Jesus, that the life of Jesus may be manifested in this frail flesh of ours.
2CO 4:12 So that death is operative in us, and life in you.
2CO 4:13 But having the same spirit of belief as is mentioned in this portion of scripture, "I believed, therefore I spake," we also believe and therefore we speak,
2CO 4:14 knowing that he who raised the Lord Jesus will raise us also by Jesus and present us with you.
2CO 4:15 For all this is for your sakes that the superabounding favour may make thanksgiving by many redound the more to the glory of God.
2CO 4:16 For this cause we do not faint: nay though this outer man of ours is wasted, yet the inner is renewed day by day.
2CO 4:17 For this momentary and light affliction of ours is working out for us an eternal weight of glory, great beyond expression,
2CO 4:18 while we are aiming not at things seen, but at things unseen; for the things seen are temporary, but the things unseen are eternal.
2CO 5:1 For we know that when the earthly house of this dwelling of ours is dissolved, we have a building of God, a house not made with hands, everlasting in the heavens.
2CO 5:2 For in this we groan, wishing earnestly to clothe ourselves with that house of ours; that heavenly habitation;
2CO 5:3 for having indeed that on, we shall not be found naked.
2CO 5:4 For truly we who are in this dwelling do groan, being loaded with a burden, for which we do not wish to unclothe ourselves, but to clothe ourselves, so that what is mortal may be swallowed up by life.
2CO 5:5 Now it is God who hath worked us up to this, and who hath indeed given us the earnest of the spirit.
2CO 5:6 Therefore we are always undaunted, [as we know that while we are dwelling in this body we are sojourning abroad from the Lord;
2CO 5:7 [for we walk by faith and not by sight;]
2CO 5:8 and go on undaunted [as we think it better for us to be abroad from the body and at home with the Lord;]
2CO 5:9 and therefore make it the height of our ambition, whether staying or going, to be well pleasing to him.
2CO 5:10 For we must all appear before the judgment seat of the Christ, that every one may receive according to what he hath done in this bodily state, whether good or evil.
2CO 5:11 Knowing therefore the terror of the Lord we persuade men, and are open to the view of God, and I hope that we have been open also to your conscience.
2CO 5:12 For we are not "commending ourselves again to you" but are giving you an occasion of boasting on our behalf, that you may make use of it before those who boast in outward appearance and not in heart.
2CO 5:13 For if we have been transported beyond ourselves it is to God; and if we are sober, it is for you.
2CO 5:14 For the love of the Christ urgeth us on, judging this, that if one died for all then indeed were they all dying,
2CO 5:15 and that he died for all to the end that they who live might no longer live for themselves, but for him who died and was raised up for them.
2CO 5:16 So that henceforth we know no one after the flesh. Nay though we indeed knew Christ after the flesh, yet we now know him so no more.
2CO 5:17 So that if any one is in Christ, he is a new creation. The old things are passed away, behold! all those things are made new.
2CO 5:18 And all this is of God, who hath reconciled us to himself by Jesus Christ, and hath given us the ministry of this reconciliation.
2CO 5:19 So because God was in Christ reconciling a world to himself, not reckoning to them their transgressions, and hath committed to us the word of this reconciliation,
2CO 5:20 we therefore as ambassadors for Christ; as if God were exhorting by us, we, in behalf of Christ, intreat, "Be reconciled to God;
2CO 5:21 for he hath made him who knew no sin, a sin offering for us, that by him we may be made the righteousness of God;
2CO 6:1 and cooperating with him, we also exhort you that it may not be in vain that you have received this favour of God.
2CO 6:2 For he saith, "In an acceptable time I have hearkened to thee, And in a day of salvation helped thee. "Behold now is an acceptable time! Behold now is a day of salvation; [and this we do]
2CO 6:3 giving no offence in any thing that the office may not be blamed;
2CO 6:4 but approving ourselves in every respect as ministers of God, by great constancy in afflictions, in distresses, in straits,
2CO 6:5 in stripes, in imprisonments, in tumults, in labours, in watchings, in fastings,
2CO 6:6 in purity, in knowledge, in long suffering, in gentleness, in a holy spirit, in undissembled love,
2CO 6:7 in the word of truth, in the power of God, with the armour of righteousness on the right and left,
2CO 6:8 in honour and dishonour, in evil report and good report, as deceivers, though we are true;
2CO 6:9 as unknown, though well known; as dying, though behold we live; as chastened, yet not put to death;
2CO 6:10 as sorrowful, yet still rejoicing; as poor, yet enriching many; as having nothing, yet possessing all things.
2CO 6:11 O Corinthians! Our mouth is opened to you; our heart is enlarged.
2CO 6:12 You are not straightened by us, but you are straightened by your own affections.
2CO 6:13 Now in return, I speak as to children, Be ye also enlarged.
2CO 6:14 Form no associations with unbelievers; for what fellowship is there between righteousness and unrighteousness? What communion hath light with darkness?
2CO 6:15 What concord hath Christ with Belial? or what portion hath a believer with an unbeliever?
2CO 6:16 And what agreement hath the temple of God with idols? For you are the temple of the living God. As God hath said, "Because I will dwell among them and walk about among them, and will be their God, and they shall be my people;
2CO 6:17 therefore come out from among them and separate yourselves, saith the Lord, and touch no unclean thing, and I will receive you,
2CO 6:18 and be to you a father, and you shall be my sons and daughters, saith the Lord Almighty."
2CO 7:1 Having therefore, beloved, these promises, let us purify ourselves from all defilement of flesh and spirit, perfecting holiness in the fear of God.
2CO 7:2 Receive us cordially. We have injured no one; we have corrupted no one; we have defrauded no one.
2CO 7:3 I do not speak to condemn you; for I have said before that you are in our hearts, to die together, and to live together.
2CO 7:4 I use great freedom of speech to you. I have great boasting with regard to you. I am filled with comfort. I superabound with joy in all our affliction.
2CO 7:5 For when we arrived in Macedonia our flesh had no rest, but we were afflicted every way. Without were fightings; within, fears.
2CO 7:6 But God who comforteth them who are cast down, comforted us by the coming of Titus;
2CO 7:7 not barely however by his coming, but by the consolation with which he was comforted on your account, when he informed us of your longing desire, your bitter sorrow, your zeal for me; so that I was the more rejoiced;
2CO 7:8 because if I grieved you by that letter, I have no cause to regret, though I did regret; for I find that that letter, though suitable to the occasion, made you sorry.
2CO 7:9 Now I rejoice, not that you were made sorrowful, but that you were affected with a sorrow which led to a reformation. For you were affected with a godly sorrow, that you might in no wise receive damage from us.
2CO 7:10 For godly sorrow operateth to produce a reformation for salvation, never to be repented of; but the sorrow of this world worketh death.
2CO 7:11 For behold! this very thing; your being affected with a godly sorrow, what solicitude it hath wrought in you! nay, what apologies! what indignation! what fear! what longing desire! what zeal! what avengement! By your whole conduct you have shewn yourselves to be clear in this matter.
2CO 7:12 Now though I indeed wrote to you, it was not on the account of him who had done the injury, nor of him who was injured, but that our solicitude, which we have for you, might be made manifest to you in the presence of God.
2CO 7:13 We were therefore comforted for your comfort, and rejoiced the more exceedingly at the joy of Titus; because his spirit was refreshed by you all;
2CO 7:14 so that if I boasted of you to him, I was not shamed; but as we spake all things to you with truth, so also our boast which we made to Titus hath been verified;
2CO 7:15 and his affection for you increaseth more abundantly on recollecting the obedience of you all, how you received him with fear and trembling.
2CO 7:16 I rejoice therefore that I can wholly confide in you.
2CO 8:1 We now, brethren, make known to you, the bounty of God which hath been granted by the congregations of Macedonia,
2CO 8:2 that in a great trial of affliction, the abundance of their joy, though their poverty was very great, abounded for the richness of their liberality
2CO 8:3 that to the utmost of their ability, I bear them witness, nay, beyond their ability, they were of themselves forward,
2CO 8:4 beseeching us with much intreaty to receive this bounty, and take a share with others in the office of distributing it to the saints,
2CO 8:5 not indeed as if we had expected this; but they gave themselves first to the Lord, then to us by the will of God,
2CO 8:6 so as to induce us to exhort Titus, as he had begun, to continue on and complete this bounty among you;
2CO 8:7 that, as you abound in every thing; in belief, and doctrine, and knowledge, and in all earnestness even in your love for us, you might abound also in this bounty.
2CO 8:8 I do not say this by way of command, but am, during the exertion of others, proving the genuineness of your love.
2CO 8:9 For you know the bounty of our Lord Jesus Christ, that rich as he was, he for your sakes became poor, that through his poverty you might become rich.
2CO 8:10 And I give you my opinion on this occasion, for this is becoming of you who took the lead, not only in doing, but even in forming the design above a year ago.
2CO 8:11 Now therefore compleat the doing, that the performance with what you have, may be answerable to the readiness with which you undertook it.
2CO 8:12 For if there be a willingness, a person is accepted according to what he hath; not according to what he hath not.
2CO 8:13 For it is not the design that others should be eased, and you burdened;
2CO 8:14 but for the sake of equality your abundance at this time should supply their want; in order that their abundance may supply your want, so that there may be an equality.
2CO 8:15 As it is written, He Who gathered much had nothing over, and he who gathered little did not fall short."
2CO 8:16 Now thanks be to God, who putteth the same earnestness for you in the heart of Titus.
2CO 8:17 For he indeed received an exhortation, but from an extraordinary earnestness he was going to you of his own accord.
2CO 8:18 Now with him we have sent the brother whose praise is by the gospel throughout all the congregations.
2CO 8:19 And not only so, but he hath been chosen by the congregations to accompany us with this bounty; the distribution of which we have undertaken for the glory of the Lord and your readiness,
2CO 8:20 using this precaution that none may blame us in the distribution of this large sum;
2CO 8:21 being careful to conduct ourselves well, not only in the sight of the Lord, but also in the sight of men.
2CO 8:22 And with them we have sent that brother of ours whose diligence in many affairs we have many a time experienced, and who is now more than ordinarily intent on this from the great confidence which he hath in you.
2CO 8:23 Now with regard to Titus, he is my partner and fellow labourer for you; and as for our brethren, they are messengers of congregations, a glory of Christ.
2CO 8:24 Display therefore for them, and for the view of these congregations, the demonstration of your love, and of our boasting on your behalf.
2CO 9:1 For with regard to the contribution itself, which is for the saints, it is superfluous for me to write to you.
2CO 9:2 For I know the forwardness of your minds, and boast of it on your behalf to the Macedonians, that Achaia was ready a year ago. And this zeal of yours hath been a spur to the multitude.
2CO 9:3 Now I have sent these brethren, that this boast of ours on your behalf may not, in this instance, be vain; that, as I said, you may be ready prepared;
2CO 9:4 lest if some Macedonians should come with me and find you unprepared, we, not to say you, may be put to the blush for this confident boasting.
2CO 9:5 Therefore I thought it necessary to exhort these brethren to go before to you, and to get your bounty, of which you had given previous notice, completed before hand, that so it may be ready as a bounty, not as an extorted gift.
2CO 9:6 Now considering this, that he who soweth sparingly shall reap sparingly, and that he who soweth bountifully will reap bountifully,
2CO 9:7 let every one give as he is predisposed in his heart, not with regret, nor reluctance; for God loveth a cheerful giver:
2CO 9:8 and God is able to make every bounty redound to your advantage. That you having always a sufficiency in every thing, may abound to every good work,
2CO 9:9 [as it is written, "He hath dispersed, he hath given to the poor, his righteousness shall endure for ever;"
2CO 9:10 and may He who furnisheth abundantly seed for the sower and bread for food, supply and multiply your seed, and increase the products of your righteousness!]
2CO 9:11 you are enriched in every thing for every act of bounty, which operateth through us to produce thanksgiving to God.
2CO 9:12 Because the distribution of this religious offering not only supplieth the wants of the saints, but also superaboundeth with many thanksgivings to God;
2CO 9:13 [by the experience of this distribution they glorify God for your avowed subjection to the glad tidings of the Christ;] therefore, for the liberality of this contribution for them and for all;
2CO 9:14 and for the supplication which is made for you by them who love you on account of the supereminent favour of God for you,
2CO 9:15 thanks be to God for this his unspeakable gift.
2CO 10:1 Now I Paul myself exhort you by the meekness and gentleness of the Christ, [I who when present am indeed lowly among you, but being absent am bold towards you]
2CO 10:2 and I pray this; that I may not when I am present presume upon that confidence, with which I lay my account to act boldly against some who reckon us as walking after the flesh.
2CO 10:3 For walking in flesh, not after the flesh, we are carrying on a war
2CO 10:4 [the weapons of our warfare being indeed not carnal but mighty through God for the demolition of fortifications]
2CO 10:5 demolishing surmises and every mount raised against the knowledge of God, and bringing every sentiment captive to the obedience of the Christ;
2CO 10:6 and being in a state of readiness to punish every act of disobedience, when your obedience is complete.
2CO 10:7 Consider what is before you. If any one is confident in himself that he is Christ's; let him again reckon this from himself, that as he himself is Christ's, so we also belong to Christ.
2CO 10:8 For though I should boast even somewhat more of this power of ours, which the Lord hath given us for edification, and not for your destruction, I shall not be put to shame.
2CO 10:9 In order that I may not seem as if I would terrify you by my letters,
2CO 10:10 ["For his letters, saith one, are indeed weighty and strong; but his bodily presence is weak, and his words contemptible,"]
2CO 10:11 let such a one reckon upon this, that such as we are in word by letters when we are absent, such we will actually be in deed when we are present.
2CO 10:12 For we do not presume to rank or compare ourselves with some of them who commend themselves, but are not aware that they are measuring themselves by themselves, and comparing themselves with themselves.
2CO 10:13 As for us we will not boast of things not measured out to us; but according to the measure of the rule of measure which God measured out to us to have come even to you;
2CO 10:14 for we did not stretch ourselves out beyond bounds as not reaching yon; for even to you we came the first with the glad tidings of the Christ;
2CO 10:15 not into what were not measured out to us, boasting in other men's labours; but having a hope, on your faith being increased, to be by you farther enlarged, according to our .allotment
2CO 10:16 to publish the good tidings in the regions beyond you; not in another's allotment; in places ready prepared, for the sake of boasting.
2CO 10:17 But let him who boasteth, boast in the Lord.
2CO 10:18 For it is not he who commendeth himself, who is approved, but he whom the Lord commendeth.
2CO 11:1 I wish you would bear with me a little in this folly. Do but bear with me;
2CO 11:2 for I am jealous of you with a godly jealousy. For I fitted you for one husband only, that I might present you as a chaste virgin to the Christ;
2CO 11:3 but I am afraid lest by some means as the serpent by his subtilty deceived Eve, so your affections should be corrupted from their singleness for the Christ.
2CO 11:4 For if indeed he who cometh, proclaimeth another Jesus, whom we have not proclaimed; or if you receive another spirit which you have not received, or other glad tidings than what you have accepted, you did well in bearing.
2CO 11:5 For I reckon that I am not a whit behind the chiefest apostles;
2CO 11:6 and though I am but rude in speech, yet I am not in knowledge: but in every respect we have been manifested to you in all things.
2CO 11:7 Did I commit a fault in abasing myself that you might be exalted, because I proclaimed the glad tidings of God to you gratis?
2CO 11:8 I took spoil of other congregations, having received Wages for my attendance on you.
2CO 11:9 Even when present with you, and in want, I was burthensome to no one; for the brethren who came from Macedonia supplied my want, so that I kept myself from being in any wise burthensome to you, and I will continue to do so.
2CO 11:10 It is a truth of Christ in me that this boasting shall not be stopped against me in the regions of Achaia.
2CO 11:11 Why? Because I do not love you? God knoweth
2CO 11:12 that what I do and will do is that I may cut off the advantage of those who are wishing for an advantage; that in what they boast, they may be found acting as we do:
2CO 11:13 For such as they are false apostles, deceitful workers, transforming themselves into apostles of Christ.
2CO 11:14 Nor is this to be wondered at; for Satan himself putteth on the appearance of an angel of light:
2CO 11:15 No wonder, then, if his ministers transform themselves to appear like ministers of righteousness. But their end will be according to their works.
2CO 11:16 Again, I say, let not, a certain person think me a fool; but if he should, bear ye however with me as a fool, that I also may boast a little.
2CO 11:17 What I am going to say, I do not say according to the Lord, but as with folly on the subject of this boasting.
2CO 11:18 Since many boast after the flesh, let me also boast.
2CO 11:19 For wise as you are, you easily bear with fools;
2CO 11:20 for you bear, if one enslaveth you; if one devoureth; if one receiveth; if one exalteth himself; if one openly insulteth you.
2CO 11:21 In regard to reproach; as, "That we are weak"; I say that on whatever any one can presume [I speak foolishly] I can do the same.
2CO 11:22 Are they Hebrews? So am I. Are they Israelites? So am I. Are they of the seed of Abraham? So am I.
2CO 11:23 Are they ministers of Christ? [I speak with an excess of folly] I am more so; more abundant in labours; far surpassing in stripes; more frequent in imprisonments, often in deaths.
2CO 11:24 Of the Jews I five times received forty stripes save one.
2CO 11:25 Thrice I was beaten with rods. Once I was stoned. Thrice I have been shipwrecked. In the deep I spent a whole night and day.
2CO 11:26 On journeys I have been frequently in dangers from rivers; in dangers from robbers; in dangers from my country men; in dangers from foreign nations; in dangers in cities; in dangers in a wilderness; in dangers at sea; in dangers among false brethren:
2CO 11:27 In toil and fatigue, in watchings many a time, with hunger and thirst; in fastings many a time, with cold and nakedness.
2CO 11:28 Beside these things from without, I have this disturbance daily crowding upon me; the anxious care of all the congregations.
2CO 11:29 Who is weak and I not weak? Who is offended and I not inflamed?
2CO 11:30 If I must boast, let me boast of things regarding my weakness.
2CO 11:31 The God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ; the self-existent, ever blessed being knoweth that I do not lie.
2CO 11:32 At Damascus the governor under king Aretas posted guards in the city of the Damascenes, with a design to seize me,
2CO 11:33 whereupon I was let down in a basket, through a window in the wall, and escaped his hands.
2CO 12:1 To me indeed it is of no advantage to boast; for I will come to visions and revelations of the Lord.
2CO 12:2 I know a man in Christ, that fourteen years ago such a one was suddenly conveyed to the third heaven, [whether in the body I do not know or out of the body I do not know, God knoweth]
2CO 12:3 and I know that such a man was suddenly conveyed to paradise [whether in the body or out of the body I do not know; God knoweth]
2CO 12:4 and he heard unutterable things which it is out of the power of man to express.
2CO 12:5 For such a one I may boast, but for my self; I will not boast, except of my infirmities.
2CO 12:6 Though should I indeed have a mind to boast, I shall not be a fool; for I will speak truth. But I forbear, lest any should7 ascribe to me beyond what he seeth me, or heareth of me.
2CO 12:7 Indeed that I might not be too much elated by the astonishing greatness of these revelations, there was given me a thorn for the flesh, a messenger of satan to buffet me, that I might not be too much elated.
2CO 12:8 For this I besought the Lord thrice, that it might depart from me.
2CO 12:9 Whereupon he said to me, My grace is sufficient for thee; for my strength is perfected in weakness. Therefore I will with the greatest pleasure, rather boast of my weaknesses, that the power of the Christ may shelter me.
2CO 12:10 I feel therefore a complacency in weaknesses, in reproaches, in difficulties, in persecutions, in distresses for Christ; for when I am weak, then am I strong.
2CO 12:11 I am become a foolish boaster! you have compelled me. For I ought to have been commended by you. For I am not a whit behind the chiefest apostles, although I am nothing.
2CO 12:12 The signs indeed of the apostle have been wrought among you with all patience, with signs and wonders and miracles.
2CO 12:13 For what instance is there of your being inferior to other congregations, unless it be this; that I have not been burthensome to you? Forgive me this injury.
2CO 12:14 Behold I am in preparation to come to you a third time, and I will not be burthensome to you. For I seek not your possessions, but yourselves. For children are not bound to lay up treasures for the parents, but the parents for the children.
2CO 12:15 And as for me, I will, with the greatest pleasure, spend and be spent for your sakes, though the more I love you, the less I be beloved.
2CO 12:16 Now be it so that I did not burthen you, but being crafty I took you in by artifice.
2CO 12:17 Did I take an undue advantage of you by any of them whom I sent to you?
2CO 12:18 I entreated Titus to go, and with him I sent the brother. Did Titus take any undue advantage of you? Did we not walk in the same spirit? Did we not in the same steps?
