2TH 3:3 But the Lord is faithful, and will establish you, and guard you from the wicked one:
2TH 3:4 and we have this hope in the Lord with regard to you, that you both do, and will do, what we tell you.
2TH 3:5 And may the Lord direct your hearts to the love of God and to the perseverance of the Christ.
2TH 3:6 Now we charge you, brethren, in the name of our Lord Jesus Christ to withdraw yourselves from every brother who walketh disorderly and not according to the doctrine which he received from us.
2TH 3:7 For you yourselves know how you ought to imitate us: that we did not behave ourselves irregularly among you,
2TH 3:8 nor eat any man's bread for nothing; but with labour and toil worked night and day, that we might not be burthensome to any of you;
2TH 3:9 not because we are destitute of authority, but that we might exhibit ourselves as a pattern for you to imitate.
2TH 3:10 For when we were with you we gave you this charge, that he who would not work should not eat.
2TH 3:11 For we hear that there are some among you who walk disorderly, doing no work, but busying themselves impertinently.
2TH 3:12 Now we charge such, and intreat them by the Lord Jesus Christ, to work quietly, and eat their own bread.
2TH 3:13 And as for you, brethren, be not weary in well doing.
2TH 3:14 And if any one doth not obey this injunction of ours by this letter, mark that man, and have no intimate connection with him, that he may be ashamed.
2TH 3:15 Yet count him not an enemy, but admonish him as a brother.
2TH 3:16 And may the Lord of peace himself grant you peace continually in every respect. The Lord be with you all.
2TH 3:17 The salutation of me Paul, with my own hand, which is a mark in every letter. Thus I write
2TH 3:18 The favour of our Lord Jesus Christ be with you all. Amen.
1TI 1:1 Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, according to the appointment of God our Saviour, and the Lord Jesus Christ our hope;  Paul, an apostle of Jesus Christ, by the will of God, according to the promise of life which is by Christ Jesus;
1TI 1:2 to Timothy, my genuine son by belief, be favour, mercy, peace from God our father and Christ Jesus our Lord.
1TI 1:3 As I entreated thee, when I was going to Macedonia, to continue at Ephesus; that thou mightest charge certain persons not to teach a different doctrine,
1TI 1:4 nor pay attention to fables and endless genealogies, which rather promote disputes than the godly edification, which is by faith:
1TI 1:5 Now the end of that charge is love, from a pure heart, and good conscience, and an unfeigned belief;
1TI 1:6 from which some having swerved, have turned aside to vain discourse,
1TI 1:7 desiring to be teachers of the law. not understanding what they say, nor about what they are so positive.
1TI 1:8 We know indeed that the law is good, if one use it as a law,
1TI 1:9 considering this, that law is not enacted for a righteous man, but for the lawless and refractory; for the impious and sinful; for the immoral and profane; for murderers of fathers and murderers of mothers; for homicides,
1TI 1:10 fornicators, sodomites, enslavers of men, liars, perjured persons, and whatever else is contrary to the wholesome doctrine
1TI 1:11 according to the glorious glad tidings of the blessed God with which I have been intrusted,
1TI 1:12 and am thankful to Christ Jesus our Lord who qualified me; for his counting me faithful, putting into office me
1TI 1:13 who was before a reviler, and a persecutor, and an outrageous offender: but I obtained mercy because I acted ignorantly, in unbelief.
1TI 1:14 And this favour of our Lord superabounded with faith and love which is by Christ Jesus.
1TI 1:15 This is a faithful word and worthy of all acceptation, That Christ Jesus came into the world to save sinners of whom I am a chief;
1TI 1:16 but I obtained mercy for this purpose, that Jesus Christ might display the utmost forbearance in me, a chief, for an example to them who should afterwards trust in him for everlasting life.
1TI 1:17 Now to the king of the ages; the incorruptible, invisible, only wise God, be honour and glory, for the ages of the ages. Amen.
1TI 1:18 This charge I commit to thee, son Timothy, according to the preceding gifts of prophesying conferred on thee, that by them thou mayst carry on this good warfare,
1TI 1:19 having faith and a good conscience, which last some having discarded, they have, in respect to the faith, suffered shipwreck,
1TI 1:20 of which number are Hymeneus and Alexander, whom I have delivered over to satan, that they may learn not to blaspheme.
1TI 2:1 I therefore exhort thee first of all, that supplications, prayers, intercessions, thanksgivings, be made for all men;
1TI 2:2 for kings and all who are in authority, that we may lead a quiet and peaceable life with all piety and honesty;
1TI 2:3 for this is good and acceptable in the sight of God our saviour,
1TI 2:4 who willeth all men to be saved, and to come to an acknowledgment of truth.
1TI 2:5 For there is one God, and one mediator between God and men, the man Christ Jesus,
1TI 2:6 who gave himself as a ransom for all; as the testimony for his own times;
1TI 2:7 for which I have been appointed a herald and an apostle, [I speak the truth in Christ, I do not lie] a teacher of nations in belief and truth.
1TI 2:8 I therefore give it in charge that the men pray in every place, lifting up holy hands, without wrath and surmise:
1TI 2:9 in like manner also, that the women adorn themselves in comely apparel, with bashful modesty; not with curls, or gold, or pearls, or costly array;
1TI 2:10 but with good works, as it becometh women who profess a reverence for God.
1TI 2:11 Let women learn in quietness with all submission.
1TI 2:12 For I do not allow a woman to teach or to usurp authority over man, but to be in quietness.
1TI 2:13 For Adam was formed first, then Eve;
1TI 2:14 and Adam was not deceived: but the woman being deceived was in transgression,
1TI 2:15 but to be saved by the child birth, if they continue in faith and love and sanctification, with a sober mind.
1TI 3:1 This is a faithful word. If any one desireth the office of an overseer, he desireth a good work.
1TI 3:2 The overseer therefore ought to be blameless, the husband of one wife, sober, discreet, well behaved, hospitable, qualified to teach,
1TI 3:3 not addicted to wine, no striker, not attached to sordid gain, but of a gentle disposition, not quarrelsome, not a lover of money,
1TI 3:4 one who presideth well over his own household, having his children in due subordination, with all gravity,
1TI 3:5 [for if one doth not know how to preside over his own household, how can he take care of the congregation of God;]
1TI 3:6 not one newly converted, lest, being lifted up with pride, he fall into the condemnation of the devil.
1TI 3:7 He ought also to have a good character from those without, that he may not fall into reproach and the snare of the devil.
1TI 3:8 Almoners in like manner should be grave, not double tongued, not addicted to much wine, not attached to sordid gain,
1TI 3:9 holding the mystery of the faith with a pure conscience;
1TI 3:10 and let even such be first tried, then, if found blameless, let them exercise the office of almoners.
1TI 3:11 Women in like manner should be grave, not addicted to slander, sober, faithful in all things.
1TI 3:12 Let almoners be the husbands of one wife, presiding well over their children and their own households;
1TI 3:13 for they who discharge the office of an almoner well, acquire for themselves an honourable rank, and much freedom of speech in the faith which is in Christ Jesus.
1TI 3:14 These things I write to thee, hoping to come to thee in a little time;
1TI 3:15 but if I be delayed, that thou mayest know how thou oughtest to conduct thyself in the house of God, that is in the congregation of the living God. The pillar and firm support of the truth is
1TI 3:16 [and unquestionably great is the mystery of this religion,] God hath been manifested in flesh, justified by spirit, hath appeared to messengers, been proclaimed among nations, believed on in the world, taken up in glory.
1TI 4:1 But the spirit saith expressly that in latter times some will apostatise from this belief, giving heed to seducing spirits, and doctrines concerning demons,
1TI 4:2 through the hypocrisy of liars, who have their own conscience seared,
1TI 4:3 forbidding marriage, and enjoining an abstinence from meats which God hath created to be partaken of with thankfulness by the faithful, and by them who are convinced of this truth,
1TI 4:4 that every thing which God created is good, and nothing to be rejected; for when taken with thankfulness
1TI 4:5 it is sanctified by the permission of God and prayer.
1TI 4:6 By suggesting these things to the brethren thou wilt be a good minister of Jesus Christ, nourished by the words of this belief, and this good doctrine, which thou hast followed.
1TI 4:7 But as for vain and groundless fables, reject them, and exercise thyself for godliness.
1TI 4:8 For bodily exercise is of little service, but this godliness is profitable for all things, having a promise of the present life and of that to come.
1TI 4:9 This is a faithful word and worthy of all acceptation;
1TI 4:10 for it is for this that we both labour and suffer reproach, because we have trusted in the living God, who is the saviour of all men, especially of the faithful.
1TI 4:11 Announce these things and teach them.
1TI 4:12 Let none despise thy youth; but be thou a pattern to the faithful in doctrine, in behaviour, in love, in spirit, in fidelity, in purity.
1TI 4:13 Until I come apply thyself to reading, to exhortation, to teaching.
1TI 4:14 Neglect not the gift which is in thee, which was given thee by prophesy with the laying on of the hands of the assembled elders.
1TI 4:15 Meditate on these things; be intent upon them. That thy improvement in all things may be manifest,
1TI 4:16 take heed to thyself and to thy doctrine; continue in them: for by doing this thou wilt save thyself and them who hearken to thee.
1TI 5:1 Rebuke not an aged man with sharpness; but admonish him as a father; young men, as brothers;
1TI 5:2 aged women, as Mothers; young women, as sisters, with all purity.
1TI 5:3 Honour widows who are widows indeed.
1TI 5:4 But if any widow hath children, or grand children; let these first learn to respect their own household, and to make suitable returns to their parents; for this is good and acceptable in the sight of the Lord.
1TI 5:5 Now she, who being really a widow and desolate, hath trusted in God, will continue in her supplications and prayers night and day;
1TI 5:6 but she, who indulgeth herself in sensuality, is dead, though she liveth.
1TI 5:7 Announce these things, that they may be irreprehensible.
1TI 5:8 Now if any one doth not provide for his own, and especially for those of his family, he hath renounced his belief, and is worse than an infidel.
1TI 5:9 Let no widow under sixty years old be put on the list, Having been the wife of one man,
1TI 5:10 is she eminent for good works? Hath she brought up children? Hath she exercised hospitality? Hath she washed the feet of the saints? Hath she assisted the afflicted? Hath she been assiduous to perform every good work?
1TI 5:11 As for young widows, reject them; for when they become impatient of the restraints of the Christ, they will wish to marry,
1TI 5:12 incurring blame for having violated their former engagement.
1TI 5:13 Add to this, that, being idle, they learn to ramble from house to house, and are not only idle, but are indeed tatlers, and intermedlers, speaking tilings which are unbecoming.
1TI 5:14 My decision therefore is, that the younger widows marry, bear children, govern their families, give no advantage, no occasion of reproach to the adversary.
1TI 5:15 For some have already turned aside after satan.
1TI 5:16 If any believer of either sex hath widows, let him or her relieve them, and let not the congregation be burdened, that they may relieve them who are really widows.
1TI 5:17 Let the elders who preside well be accounted worthy of double honour, especially they who labour in word and doctrine;
1TI 5:18 for the scripture saith, "Thou shalt not muzzle an ox treading out corn," and, "The labourer is worthy of wages."
1TI 5:19 Receive not an accusation against an elder, but on the testimony of two or three witnesses.
1TI 5:20 Them, who sin, rebuke before all, that others may fear.
1TI 5:21 I charge thee before the God and Lord Jesus Christ, and the chosen angels, to observe these things without prejudging, and to do nothing by partiality.
1TI 5:22 Lay hands upon no one hastily, nor be a partaker in the sins of others. Keep thyself pure.
1TI 5:23 Discontinue the drinking of water, and take a little wine on account of thy stomach, and thy frequent indisposition.
1TI 5:24 The sins of some are so notorious that they go before them to judgment. Some indeed they follow.
1TI 5:25 In like manner also the good works of some are open and manifest; and such as are otherwise cannot be hid.
1TI 6:1 Let as many as are under a yoke of bondage account their masters worthy of all honour, that the name of God, and this doctrine, may not be reviled.
1TI 6:2 And let not those who have believing masters disregard them because they are brethren, but serve them the more, because they who receive the good service are believers, and beloved. Teach these things, and enforce them by exhortation.
1TI 6:3 If any one teacheth otherwise, and doth not attend to the wholesome words of our Lord Jesus Christ, and to the doctrine according to godliness,
1TI 6:4 he is puffed up, knowing nothing, but raving upon questions and debates about words, from which proceed envy, contention, abusive language, evil suspicions,
1TI 6:5 preposterous studies of men whose minds are corrupt and devoid of truth, who suppose this religion to be a matter of gain. From such withdraw thyself.
1TI 6:6 Now this religion, with contentment, is a great gain.
1TI 6:7 For we brought nothing into this world; and it is evident that we can carry nothing out of it.
1TI 6:8 Having then food and raiment let us be content with these.
1TI 6:9 But they who determine to be rich, fall headlong into temptation, and a snare, and into many foolish and hurtful desires, which plunge men into ruin and destruction.
1TI 6:10 For the love of money is the root of all evil; to gratify which, some have wandered from the faith, and pierced themselves through with many sorrows.
1TI 6:11 But thou, man of God, shun these things and pursue righteousness, godliness, faith, love, patience, gentleness.
1TI 6:12 Maintain the good combat of faith. Lay hold on the life everlasting to which thou hast been invited, and of which thou hast made a good profession before many witnesses.
1TI 6:13 I charge thee in the presence of God, who giveth life to all, and of Christ Jesus who witnessed before Pontius Pilate the good confession,
1TI 6:14 to keep thyself, in respect to this command, unspotted, irreprehensible, until the appearance of our Lord Jesus Christ,
1TI 6:15 which, in his own proper times will be displayed by him, who is the blessed and only potentate, the king of kings and the lord of lords,
1TI 6:16 who alone hath immortality, who inhabiteth light inaccessible, whom no man hath seen, or can see, to whom be honour and everlasting dominion. Amen.
1TI 6:17 Charge them who are rich in this present state not to be high minded; not to trust in uncertain riches, but in the living God who imparteth to us richly all things for enjoyment;
1TI 6:18 to be beneficent; to be rich in good works, ready to distribute; willing to communicate,
1TI 6:19 laying up for themselves a good deposit for the time to come, that they may obtain the life everlasting.
1TI 6:20 O Timothy keep this deposit, avoiding the profane empty declamations, and the antitheses of that falsely called science,
1TI 6:21 which some making a profession of, have, in respect to this belief, wandered from the mark. The favor be with thee. Amen.
2TI 1:2 to Timothy, a beloved son, be favour, mercy, peace from God our Father, and Christ Jesus our Lord.
2TI 1:3 I thank God, whom I serve from my forefathers with a pure conscience, that I have so uninterruptedly the remembrance of thee in my prayers, night and day,
2TI 1:4 earnestly desiring [when I call to mind thy tears] to see thee that I may be filled with joy,
2TI 1:5 recollecting that unfeigned belief in thee, which dwelt first in thy grand mother Lois and thy mother Eunice, and I am persuaded is in thee also:
2TI 1:6 for which cause I remind thee to kindle up that gift of God which is in thee by the laying on of my hands.
2TI 1:7 For God hath not given us a spirit of cowardice, but of power, and love, and a sound mind.
2TI 1:8 Be not therefore ashamed of the testimony of our Lord, nor of me who am a prisoner on his account; but share with me in affliction for the glad tidings, according to the power of God,
2TI 1:9 who hath saved us, and called us with a holy invitation, not according to our works, but according to his own purpose, and the favour which was granted to us in Christ Jesus, before the times composed of ages,
2TI 1:10 and which hath now been manifested by the appearance of our Saviour Jesus Christ, who hath put a stop to the operations of death, and hath brought life and incorruption to light by the glad tidings,
2TI 1:11 for which I have been appointed a herald, and an apostle, and a teacher of nations.
2TI 1:12 For which cause also I suffer these things, but am not ashamed; for I know in whom I have trusted, and am persuaded, that he is able to keep that which I have deposited with him till that day.
2TI 1:13 Use the form of sound words, which thou hast heard from me, with faith and the love in Christ Jesus.
2TI 1:14 Keep that good deposit by means of a holy spirit which dwelleth in us. This thou knowest,
2TI 1:15 that all the Asiatics have withdrawn from me, of whom are Phygellus and Hermogenes'
2TI 1:16 The Lord grant mercy to the household of Onesiphorus, because he often refreshed me and was not ashamed of this chain of mine;
2TI 1:17 but when he was at Rome, sought me out diligently and found me.
2TI 1:18 The Lord grant him to find mercy from the Lord in that day! Indeed, on how many occasions he ministered to me at Ephesus, thou thyself knowest very well.
2TI 2:1 Do thou, therefore, my son, strengthen thyself with the favour which is in Christ Jesus;
2TI 2:2 and what thou hast heard from me, in the presence of many witnesses, commit thou to faithful men, who will be able to teach others.
2TI 2:3 Do thou therefore endure hardships as a good soldier of Jesus Christ.
2TI 2:4 No one going to war entangleth himself with worldly affairs, that he may please him who hath inlisted him.
2TI 2:5 And if a man combateth in the public games, he is not crowned, unless he combat according' to the rules prescribed.
2TI 2:6 The husbandman must labour before he partaketh of the fruits. 7 Consider what I say, and may the
2TI 2:8 Lord grant thee understanding in all things.  Remember Jesus Christ, of the seed of David, raised from the dead according to these glad tidings of mine
2TI 2:9 for which I suffer even to bonds, as a malefactor; but the word of God is not bound.
2TI 2:10 For this Cause I bear all things patiently for the sake of the chosen, that they also may obtain that salvation which is by Christ Jesus, with everlasting glory.
2TI 2:11 This is a faithful word. For if we have died with him, we shall also live with him.
2TI 2:12 If we suffer, we shall indeed reign with him. If we deny him, he will deny us.
2TI 2:13 If we are unfaithful, he will continue faithful; he cannot deny himself.
2TI 2:14 Bring these things to remembrance, giving a solemn charge in the presence of the Lord not to dispute about words. It answereth no useful purpose. It tendeth to the subversion of the hearers.
2TI 2:15 Study diligently to present thyself approved before God, a workman that needeth not to be ashamed; handling rightly the word of truth.
2TI 2:16 And repress those profane empty declamations; for they will proceed on to farther impiety;
2TI 2:17 and like a gangrene the word of these men will spread, of whom are Hymeneus and Philetus,
2TI 2:18 who have swerved from the truth, saying that the resurrection is already past; and subvert the belief of some.
2TI 2:19 Nevertheless the foundation of God standeth firm, having this inscription""The Lord knoweth them who are his;" and "Let every one who nameth the name of Christ depart from iniquity."
2TI 2:20 Now, in a great house there are not only vessels of gold and silver, but also of wood and potter's clay; and some indeed for honourable uses and some for meaner purposes.
2TI 2:21 If any one therefore purify himself from these he will be a vessel for honour, set apart and suitable for the master, ready prepared for every good work.
2TI 2:22 Fly then the passions of youth and pursue righteousness, fidelity, love, peace with them who invoke the Lord with a pure heart.
2TI 2:23 And avoid foolish and ignorant debates, knowing that they generate strifes.
2TI 2:24 Now, the servant of the Lord ought not to be at strife; but ought to be gentle towards all, ready to teach, patient of ills,
2TI 2:25 with meekness instructing opposers: perhaps God may grant them a change of mind so as to acknowledge the truth,
2TI 2:26 and they who have been captivated by the devil for his pleasure, may rouse and escape from his snare.
2TI 3:1 But know this, that in the last days there will be grievous times.
2TI 3:2 For the men will be selfish, avaricious, vain, haughty, addicted to slander, disobedient to parents, ungrateful, unholy,
2TI 3:3 void of natural affection, perfidious, false accusers, intemperate, fierce, destitute of love for goodness,
2TI 3:4 betrayers, headstrong, puffed up with conceit, lovers of pleasure rather than lovers of God,
2TI 3:5 having a form of religion but denying the power of it. From such turn away;
2TI 3:6 for of such sort are they who insinuate themselves into families, and lead captive weak women laden with sin, led aside by various lusts,
2TI 3:7 always learning, but never able to come to a knowledge of truth.
2TI 3:8 Now as Jannes and Jambres withstood Moses, so do these men withstand the truth, having their minds corrupted, being, with respect to this belief, such as cannot stand the test
2TI 3:9 But they shall not advance much further; for the folly of these shall be exposed to the world, as that of those was.
2TI 3:10 Now as for thee, thou hast traced accurately my doctrine, my manner of life, my purpose, my belief, my long suffering, my love, my patience,
2TI 3:11 my persecutions, my sufferings, what befell me at Antioch, at Iconium, at Lystra; what persecutions I endured: but out of them all the Lord delivered me.
2TI 3:12 Indeed all who wish to live holy in Christ Jesus will be persecuted,
2TI 3:13 and wicked men and impostors will grow worse and worse, deceiving and being deceived.
2TI 3:14 But as for thee, continue thou in what thou hast learned; and in the belief of which thou hast been confirmed, knowing from whom thou hast learned them;
2TI 3:15 and that, from thy childhood, thou hast known the holy scriptures, which are able to make thee wise for salvation by trusting in Christ Jesus.
2TI 3:16 All scripture, given by divine inspiration, is indeed profitable for doctrine, for conviction, for reformation, for instruction in righteousness,
2TI 3:17 that the man of God may be complete, thoroughly fitted for every good work.
2TI 4:1 I therefore charge thee in the presence of the God, and the Lord Jesus Christ, who is about to judge living and dead at his glorious appearance and reign,
2TI 4:2 proclaim the word; be intent thereon, in season and out of season; convince, rebuke, exhort with all long suffering and doctrine.
2TI 4:3 For a time will come when they will not endure sound doctrine: But when they have an itch of hearing they will, according to their own desires, heap up for themselves teachers,
2TI 4:4 who will turn their attention from the truth, and they will be turned aside to fables.
2TI 4:5 Be thou therefore watchful on all occasions. Endure hardships: perform the work of a publisher of the glad tidings. Discharge thy ministerial office completely.
2TI 4:6 For I am now about to be poured out as a libation; and the time of my departure is at hand.
2TI 4:7 I have maintained the good combat. I have finished the course; I have kept the faith.
2TI 4:8 As to what remaineth, there is laid up for me the crown of righteousness, which the Lord, the righteous judge, will give me on that day, not only to me, but to all who have loved his glorious appearance.
2TI 4:9 Use all diligence to come to me quickly.
2TI 4:10 For Demas, from a love for this world, hath forsaken me, and is gone to Thessalonica; Crescens, to Galatia; Titus, to Dalmatia.
2TI 4:11 Luke alone is with me. Take Mark and bring him with thee; for he is useful to me for attendance,
2TI 4:12 as I have sent Tychicus to Ephesus.
2TI 4:13 When thou comest, bring the cloak which I left with Carpus at Troas, and the books, especially the parchments.
2TI 4:14 Alexander the coppersmith hath lodged many false accusations against me. Let the Lord reward him according to his works:
2TI 4:15 Be thou on thy guard against him, for he greatly withstood our words.
2TI 4:16 At my first defence no one attended; but all forsook me. May this not be charged to their account!
2TI 4:17 But the Lord stood by me and strengthened me, that the proclamation might be made completely by me, and that all the nations might hear it. And I was delivered out of the mouth of a lion.
2TI 4:18 And the Lord will deliver me from every evil work, and save me for his heavenly kingdom. To him be the glory, for the ages of the ages. Amen.
2TI 4:19 Salute Priscas and Aquilas, and the household of Onesiphorus.
2TI 4:20 Erastus staid at Corinth; and I left Trophimus sick at Miletus.
2TI 4:21 Endeavour to come to me before winter. Eubulus, and Pudens, and Linus, and Claudia, and all the brethren, salute thee.
2TI 4:22 The Lord Jesus Christ be with thy spirit. The favour be with you. Amen.
TIT 1:1 Paul, a servant of God, and apostle of Jesus Christ, for the faith of God's chosen people, and the acknowledgment of a truth which promoteth piety
TIT 1:2 in hope of an everlasting life, which the God of truth promised before the times consisting of ages,
TIT 1:3 and in his own times promulgated as his word, by a proclamation with which I am entrusted, according to the appointment of the saviour our God;
TIT 1:4 to Titus, a genuine son according to the common faith, be favour, mercy, peace from God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ our Saviour.
TIT 1:5 I left thee in Crete for this purpose that thou mightest regulate what were wanting, and appoint elders in every city as I ordered thee.
TIT 1:6 If there be any one blameless, the husband of one wife, having faithful children, who are not accused of riot, nor ungovernable.
TIT 1:7 For the overseer ought to be blameless as God's steward, not self willed, not passionate, not addicted to wine, not quarrelsome, not greedy of sordid gain;
TIT 1:8 but a lover of hospitality, a lover of goodness, sober, just, holy, temperate,
TIT 1:9 adhering to the faithful word, as he hath been taught, that he may be able to exhort with sound doctrine, and convince them who oppose it.
TIT 1:10 For there are many who are disorderly, vain talkers and deceivers, especially they of the circumcision,
TIT 1:11 who ought to be curbed, who subvert whole houses teaching what they ought not, for the sake of sordid gain.
TIT 1:12 One of themselves, a prophet of their own hath said, "False Cretans! savage beasts! to gluttony and sloth devote!"
TIT 1:13 This is a true testimony; on this account rebuke them sharply, that they may be sound in the faith,
TIT 1:14 not giving heed to Jewish fables and commands of men who pervert the truth.
TIT 1:15 To the pure, all things are indeed pure but to the polluted and unbelieving, nothing is pure. Their mind and conscience are polluted:
TIT 1:16 they make a profession of knowing God, but with their works they deny him; being abominable, and disobedient, and lost to every good work.
TIT 2:1 But as for thee speak thou what is consistent with sound doctrine
TIT 2:2 that aged men be sober, grave, discreet, sound in their belief, their love, their patience;
TIT 2:3 that aged women, in like manner, be in behaviour as becometh saints, not addicted to slander, not enslaved to wine, good instructors, that they may
TIT 2:4 teach the young women to be discreet, to love their husbands, to love their children,
TIT 2:5 to be modest, chaste, attentive to domestic affairs, good, submissive to their husbands; that the word of God may not be ill spoken of.
TIT 2:6 In like manner exhort young men to be sober minded,
TIT 2:7 shewing thyself in all things a pattern of good works; in thy doctrine displaying integrity, gravity, incorruptness,
TIT 2:8 sound discourse which cannot be condemned, that he who is of an opposite party may be ashamed, having nothing bad to say of you.
TIT 2:9 Exhort servants to be obedient to their masters; to be in all things studious to please; not answering again,
TIT 2:10 not embezzling, but shewing all good fidelity, that they may in all things adorn the doctrine of our saviour God.
TIT 2:11 For the favour of God which is for salvation hath been brightly displayed for all men
TIT 2:12 teaching us in order that we, renouncing impiety and worldly lusts, may live soberly and righteously and piously in this present world,
TIT 2:13 waiting for the blessed hope and the bright display of the glory of the great God, and saviour of us Jesus Christ,
TIT 2:14 who gave himself for us, that he might redeem us from all iniquity and purify for himself a peculiar people, zealous of good works.
TIT 2:15 Speak these things, and exhort and rebuke with all authority. Let no one despise thee.
TIT 3:1 Put them in mind to be subject to governments and authorities; to pay prompt obedience; to be ready for every good work;
TIT 3:2 to revile no one; not to be quarrelsome; to be gentle, shewing all meekness to all men.
TIT 3:3 For we, even we ourselves were formerly foolish, disobedient, led astray, slaves to divers lusts and pleasures living in malice and envy, objects of hatred, hating one another;
TIT 3:4 but when the kindness and love of God our saviour for man was brightly displayed,
TIT 3:5 not for works of righteousness which we had done, but according to his own mercy; he saved us by a bath of regeneration, and a renewal of a holy spirit,
TIT 3:6 which he poured out on us abundantly through Jesus Christ our saviour,
TIT 3:7 in order that we, being pardoned by his favour, might become expectant heirs of everlasting life.
TIT 3:8 This is a faithful word; and in respect to these things I charge thee to exert thy utmost influence in order that they who believe in God, may study to be foremost in good works. These are the things which are comely, and profitable for men.
TIT 3:9 But discountenance foolish questions, and genealogies, and strifes, and debates about law: for they are unprofitable and vain.
TIT 3:10 With regard to a factious man, after a first and second admonition, avoid him;
TIT 3:11 knowing that such a one is wholly turned aside, and sinneth self condemned.
TIT 3:12 When I send Artemas to thee, or Tychicus, come to me with all speed to Nicopolis; for I have determined to winter there.
TIT 3:13 Forward on their journey Zenas the lawyer, and Apollos, with all diligence, so that nothing may be wanting to them.
TIT 3:14 And let our brethren learn to be foremost in good works on all needful occasions, that they may not be unfruitful.
TIT 3:15 All that are with me salute thee. Salute them who love us in the faith. The favour be with you all. Amen.
PHM 1:1 Paul, a prisoner for the sake of Jesus Christ, and Timothy, the brother, to Philemon our beloved, and fellow labourer,
PHM 1:2 and to Apphia the beloved, and to Archippus our fellow soldier and to the congregation in thy house;
PHM 1:3 favour be to you, and peace from God our father and the Lord Jesus Christ.
PHM 1:4 I thank my God, making mention of thee always in my prayers,
PHM 1:5 hearing of the faith which thou hast in the Lord Jesus, of thy love for all the saints,
PHM 1:6 so that every good man among you must acknowledge that thy participation of the faith is operative for Christ Jesus. [Or literally, "that thy participation of the faith may, in the acknowledgment of every good man among you, be operative for Christ Jesus."]
PHM 1:7 For we have great joy and comfort for this love of thine, because the bowels of the saints are refreshed by thee, brother.
PHM 1:8 Wherefore though I have much boldness in Christ to enjoin thee what is fit;
PHM 1:9 yet on account of this love I rather use entreaty. Being such as I am, Paul an old man, and now indeed a prisoner on account of Jesus Christ,
PHM 1:10 I entreat thee in respect to this son of mine whom I have begotten in my bonds; namely, Onesimus,
PHM 1:11 who was formerly unprofitable to thee; but is now profitable both to thee and me
PHM 1:12 whom I have sent back; do thou then receive him kindly, that is, as one whom I tenderly love,
PHM 1:13 whom I was determining to keep with me that for thee he might wait on me during my being in bonds for the glad tidings;
PHM 1:14 but I would not do any thing without thy consent, that the benefit derived from thee might not be as it were forced, but of free will.
PHM 1:15 For perhaps he was separated from thee for a short time for this very purpose, that thou mightest have him ever after,
PHM 1:16 not as a slave, but above a slave, as a brother beloved in a special manner by me, [and how much more ought he to be by thee] both in flesh, and in the Lord.
PHM 1:17 If therefore thou esteemest me as a companion, receive him as thou wouldst myself.
PHM 1:18 And if he hath wronged thee, or oweth thee any thing, place it to my account.
PHM 1:19 I Paul myself have written with my own hand. I will make compensation. Not to mention to thee that thou owest me even thine own self.
PHM 1:20 I beseech thee, brother, let me have joy of thee in the Lord: gratify my tender affections in the Lord.
PHM 1:21 I have written to thee in a confidence of thy compliance, knowing that thou wilt do even more than I express.
PHM 1:22 In the mean while prepare a lodging for me, for I hope that, by means of your prayers, I shall be granted to you.
PHM 1:23 Epaphras my fellow prisoner in Christ Jesus,
PHM 1:24 Marcus, Aristarchus, Demas and Luke, my fellow labourers, salute thee.
PHM 1:25 The favour of our Lord Jesus Christ be with your spirit. Amen.
HEB 1:1 GOD, who in sundry parcels and in divers manners spake in time past to the fathers by the prophets,
HEB 1:2 hath in these last days spoken to us by a son whom he hath constituted heir of all things, by whom also he made the ages;
HEB 1:3 who being an effulgence of the glory, and an impress of his substance, and upholding all things by the word of his power, having by himself made a purification of our sins, sat down on the right hand of the majesty on high,
HEB 1:4 being made as much superior to the heavenly messengers as the name he hath inherited is more excellent than theirs:
HEB 1:5 for to which of those messengers did he ever say, "Thou art my son, this day I have begotten thee. "And again, "I will be to him a father, and he shall be to me a son?"
HEB 1:6 And again when he would bring the first born into the world, he saith, "And let all God's messengers worship him.
HEB 1:7 Now in respect to the messengers it is said, "Who maketh winds his messengers, and flaming fire his ministers:
HEB 1:8 but with respect to the son, "Thy throne, O God, is forever and ever: The sceptre of thy kingdom is a sceptre of rectitude:
HEB 1:9 Thou didst love righteousness and hate iniquity, Therefore God, thy God anointed thee With the oil of joy above thy associates!"
HEB 1:10 Again, "Thou, Lord, in the beginning didst lay the foundation of the earth, And the heavens are the work of thy hand.
HEB 1:11 They shall perish, but thou wilt endure. They shall all wax old like a garment,
HEB 1:12 And like a mantle thou wilt fold them up and they shall be changed :But as for thee, thou art the same And thy years shall have no end".
HEB 1:13 And to which of these messengers did he ever say, "Sit at my right hand till I make thine enemies thy footstool."
HEB 1:14 Are they not all ministering spirits sent forth on service on the account of them who are to be heirs of salvation?
HEB 2:1 For this cause we ought to give the more earnest heed to the things which we have heard, lest we, through negligence, let them slip.
HEB 2:2 For if the word spoken by messengers was firm, and every transgression and disobedience received as its reward a correspondent requital,
HEB 2:3 how shall we escape, if we neglect so great a salvation, which was first published by the Lord, and confirmed for us by them who heard him,
HEB 2:4 God giving a joint testimony, by signs, and wonders, and divers miracles, and distributions of a holy spirit, according to his own will.
HEB 2:5 For he did not subject to angels the dispensation to come, of which we are speaking;
HEB 2:6 but one in a certain place hath testified, saying, "What is man, that thou shouldst be mindful of him! Or a son of man, that thou shouldst visit him!
HEB 2:7 Thou madest him a little lower than angels; With glory and honour thou hast crowned him,
HEB 2:8 And set him over the works of thy hands. Thou hast put all things under his feet." For when he put all things under his feet, he left nothing which was not put in subjection to him.  But now we do not yet see all things subjected to him.
HEB 2:9 But we see him who was made a little lower than angels [namely] Jesus, on account of suffering death crowned with glory and honour, that so he by the favour of God might taste death for every man.
HEB 2:10 For it became him for whom are all things, and by whom are all things, when bringing many sons to glory to make the leader of their salvation perfect by sufferings.
HEB 2:11 For both he who sanctifieth and they who are sanctified are all of one; for which cause he is not ashamed to call them brethren,
HEB 2:12 saying, "I will declare thy name to my brethren, In the midst of a congregation I will praise thee."
HEB 2:13 And, again: "I will trust in him;" and, again: "Here am I and the children whom God hath given me."
HEB 2:14 As the children therefore were partakers of flesh and blood, he himself likewise partook of the same in order that he might, by his death, put a stop to the operation of him who hath the power of death, that is the devil;
HEB 2:15 and deliver from bondage them who were all their lives liable to the fear of death.
HEB 2:16 For he indeed doth not take hold of angels, but taketh hold of the seed of Abraham,
HEB 2:17 whence it behoved him to be made like his brethren in all things; that he might be a merciful and faithful chief priest in things pertaining to God, to make atonement for the sins of the people.
HEB 2:18 For by what he himself suffered when he was tried he can help them who are tried.
HEB 3:1 Wherefore, holy brethren, partakers of a heavenly invitation, consider attentively this apostle and chief priest of our profession, [namely] Christ Jesus
HEB 3:2 who was faithful to him who appointed him, even as Moses was, in his whole house.
HEB 3:3 For he hath been counted worthy of as much greater honour than Moses, as he who hath builded a house hath more honour than the house.
HEB 3:4 For every house hath some builder, but he who builded all things is God.
HEB 3:5 Now Moses was faithful in this whole house of his as a servant for a testimony of those things to be spoken;
HEB 3:6 but Christ as a son over his own house, whose house we are, if we stedfastly maintain this confidence, and the boast of this hope, firm to the end.
HEB 3:7 Wherefore as the Holy Spirit saith, "Today since you have heard his voice,
HEB 3:8 Let not your hearts be refractory as at Bitterness as in the day of the temptation in the wilderness;
HEB 3:9 Where your fathers tried me; they proved me, though they saw my works. Forty years.
HEB 3:10 For which cause I was incensed with that generation; And said, They do always err with the heart, And have not known my ways:
HEB 3:11 So in mine indignation I solemnly said, "They shall not enter into my rest."
HEB 3:12 Take heed, brethren, that there be not in any of you an evil heart of unbelief in departing from the living God;
HEB 3:13 but while this today is proclaimed, that none of you may be rendered obstinate by the deceitfulness of sin
HEB 3:14 [for we are made associates of the Christ if we retain the beginning of this confidence firm to the end]
HEB 3:15 exhort one another daily by its being said, "Today since you have heard his voice let not your hearts be refractory as at Bitterness."
HEB 3:16 For some hearers provoked him; but did they not all come out of Egypt by Moses?
HEB 3:17 Now, against whom was he incensed forty years? Was it not against them who sinned, whose carcasses fell in the wilderness?
HEB 3:18 And to whom did he solemnly say that they should not enter into his rest, but to them who were disobedient.
HEB 3:19 So we see that they could not enter in because of unbelief.
HEB 4:1 Let us therefore be afraid, lest having a promise left of entering into His Rest any of us should fall short of it.
HEB 4:2 For we have had the glad tidings proclaimed to us, as they also had; but the word which they heard did not profit them; as it was not mixed up with belief by the hearers.
HEB 4:3 For we who have believed enter into that rest spoken of in this passage, "So in my indignation I said they shall not enter into My Rest; "namely, That from the works done at the foundation of the, world.
HEB 4:4 For where speaking of the seventh day the scripture said thus, "And on the seventh day God rested from all His works.
HEB 4:5 And again in this place: "They shall not enter into My rest."
HEB 4:6 Therefore since it is left for some to enter into it, and they who had the glad tidings first proclaimed to them did not enter in because of unbelief,
HEB 4:7 He again determinately apointeth out a day, namely Today, saying by David after so long a time, as it hath been mentioned, "Today since you have heard his voice let not your hearts be refractory."
HEB 4:8 For if Joshua had given them rest, the scripture would not after that have spoken of another day.
HEB 4:9 There is then a Sabbath rest left for the people of God.
HEB 4:10 For he who entereth into That Rest Of His hath desisted from his works, as God did from his.
HEB 4:11 Let us therefore use all diligence to enter into This Rest, that none may fall short by a like example of disobedience.
HEB 4:12 For the word of God is living, and active, and sharper than any two-edged sword, and penetrateth even to the separation of animal life and spirit, and of joints and marrow, and is capable of discerning the desires and thoughts of the heart.
HEB 4:13 There is indeed no creature concealed from his sight. All things are naked and exposed to the eyes of him with whom we have to do.
HEB 4:14 Having therefore a great chief priest who hath passed through the heavens, namely Jesus the son of God, let us hold fast our profession. 15 For we have not a chief priest incapable of sympathizing in our infirmities; but one who hath been tried in all respects like ourselves, but without sin.
HEB 4:16 Let us therefore come with confidence to the throne of grace, that we may obtain mercy and find favour for seasonable assistance.
HEB 5:1 For every chief priest, taken from among men, is constituted for men over things pertaining to God, that he may offer both gifts and sacrifices for sins,
HEB 5:2 being able to treat the ignorant and wandering with moderation and compassion, encompassed as he himself is with infirmity;
HEB 5:3 and for this reason it is his duty to offer sacrifices for sins, as well for himself as for the people.
HEB 5:4 Now no one assumeth to himself this honour, but he who is called of God as Aaron was.
HEB 5:5 Thus also the Christ did not dignify himself with the office of chief priest, but was dignified with it by him who said to him, "Thou art my son; this day I have begotten the
HEB 5:6 Just as he saith also in another psalm, "Thou art a priest forever after the order of Melchisedek."
HEB 5:7 He, [who in the days of his flesh, having, with a strong cry and tears, offered up prayers and supplications to him who was able to save him from death, and being hearkened to, did, from a reverential awe notwithstanding his being a son, learn obedience from what he suffered;
HEB 5:9 and being consecrated became the author of everlasting salvation to all who obey him,]
HEB 5:10 was proclaimed by God a chief priest after the order of Melchisedek,
HEB 5:11 concerning whom we have much to say, but not easy to be explained as you are slow of apprehension.
HEB 5:12 For though by this time you ought to be teachers, you have need of some one to teach you over again the first elements of the oracles of God, and have need of milk and not strong food: 13 for every one who useth milk is unskilled in the doctrine of justification, for he is a babe,
HEB 5:14 and this strong food is for full grown men, who by long practice and exercise have their senses improved for the discernment of both good and evil.
HEB 6:1 Therefore dropping the discourse of the government of the Christ, let us, without laying again a foundation of reformation from dead works, and of faith in God,
HEB 6:2 of the doctrine concerning baptism, and the laying on of hands, and the resurrection of the dead, and eternal judgment, proceed to the consecration.
HEB 6:3 And this we will do if God permit:
HEB 6:4 for with regard to them who have been once enlightened, and have tasted this free, this heavenly gift, and have been made partakers of a holy spirit,
HEB 6:5 and tasted the good word of God, and the miraculous powers of the age about to come,
HEB 6:6 and have fallen off; it is impossible to renew them again for a reformation, since they are crucifying for themselves afresh the son of God and exposing him to open shame.
HEB 6:7 For ground which drinketh up the rain that frequently falleth on it, and produceth plants fit for the use of them for whom it is cultivated, receiveth a blessing from God;
HEB 6:8 but that which produceth briars and thorns is rejected, and near a curse, the end of which is for burning.
HEB 6:9 But respecting you, beloved, we are persuaded better things, even things which accompany salvation; though we speak thus.
HEB 6:10 For God is not unjust to forget your work, and the labour of that love which you have shewn for his name, by the assistance which you have given and continue to give to the saints.
HEB 6:11 Now we earnestly desire that every one of you would shew the same diligent concern for the full assurance of this hope to the end:
HEB 6:12 that you may not become languid, but imitators of them who through faith and long suffering inherit the promises.
HEB 6:13 For when God made a promise to Abraham, as he had none greater to swear by, he swore by himself,
HEB 6:14 saying, "Surely blessing I will bless thee, and multiplying I will multiply thee."
HEB 6:15 And so he, having waited with patience, obtained the promise.
HEB 6:16 For men indeed swear by a greater, and an oath for confirmation being to them an end of strife,
HEB 6:17 God, willing on this occasion to shew more fully to the heirs of this promise the immutability of his determination, interposed an oath,
HEB 6:18 that by two immutable things, in which it was impossible for God to deceive, there might be strong consolation for us who have fled to take hold of this proffered hope,
HEB 6:19 which we have as an anchor of the soul, both sure and stedfast; and which entereth within the veil,
HEB 6:20 whither a forerunner hath entered for us, namely Jesus, made a chief priest forever, after the order of Melchisedek.
HEB 7:1 For this Melchisedek, king of Salem, priest of the most high God, who met Abraham on his return from the slaughter of the kings, and blessed him,
HEB 7:2 and to whom Abraham gave a tenth of all, was in the first place, by the interpretation of his name, king of righteousness, and in the, next place he was actually king of Salem, that is, king of peace;
HEB 7:3 of whose father and mother there is no mention, no account of descent, nor of the beginning of his days, nor of the end of his life, but likened to the son of God he abideth a priest continually.
HEB 7:4 Now consider what a great personage he was to whom even the patriarch Abraham gave a tenth of the spoils.
HEB 7:5 The Levites indeed who receive the priesthood have according to law a commandment to tithe the people, that is their own brethren descended from the loins of Abraham;
HEB 7:6 but he who was not of their pedigree received tithes of Abraham, and blessed him who had the promises.
HEB 7:7 Now, beyond all dispute, the inferior is blessed by the superior.
HEB 7:8 Again, here indeed men who die receive tithes; but there HE received them of whom it is testified that he liveth.
HEB 7:9 Indeed, as one may say, even Levi who receiveth tithes, was tithed in the person of Abraham;
HEB 7:10 for he was yet in the loins of his father, when Melchisedek met him.
HEB 7:11 Again, if perfectness had been by the Levitical priesthood [for it was for this that the people received the law] what further need was there of saying that another priest should be raised up after the order of Melchisedek, and not after the order of Aaron?
HEB 7:12 For the priesthood being changed there is of necessity a change of the law.
HEB 7:13 For he in respect to whom these things are said belonged to another tribe, none of whom gave attendance at the altar.
HEB 7:14 For it is evident that our Lord sprang from Judah, in respect to which tribe Moses spake nothing of a priesthood.
HEB 7:15 And this is still more clear, if after the likeness of Melchisedek another priest is raised up,
HEB 7:16 who is made not according to the law of a commandment concerning flesh, but according to the power of an endless life.
HEB 7:17 For he testifieth, saying, "Thou art a priest forever after the order of Melchisedek."
HEB 7:18 Here then is a disannulment of a preceding commandment on account of its weakness and inutility,
HEB 7:19 [for the law made nothing perfect] and an introduction of a better hope by which we draw near to God.
HEB 7:20 And inasmuch as this was not without an oath, 21 [for with regard to them, they indeed were made priests without an oath, but he was made with an oath, by him who said to him, "The Lord hath sworn and will not change, thou art a priest forever after the order of 'Melchisedek"",
HEB 7:22 by so much Jesus is made the surety of a better covenant.
HEB 7:23 Again, with regard to them, many were made priests, because death prevented a continuance: 24 but He, because of his continuing forever, hath a priesthood which doth not pass from one to another.
HEB 7:25 So that he is completely able to save them, who come to God by him, as he is ever alive to intercede for them.
HEB 7:26 For it suited us to have such a chief priest"one holy, innocent, undefined, separate from sinners, and made higher than the heavens,
HEB 7:27 who is not under a daily necessity [as the chief priests are,] of offering sacrifices first for his own sins, and then for those of the people; for this he did once for all when he offered up himself.
HEB 7:28 For the law constituteth men chief priests who have infirmities; but the word of the oath which succeedeth the law [constituted] the Son, who is consecrated forever.
HEB 8:1 Now the sum of what I have said is this, Such a chief priest we have who hath taken a seat at the right hand of the throne of the majesty in the heavens:
HEB 8:2 he is a minister of the holies, and of the true tabernacle, which the Lord pitched, and not man.
HEB 8:3 For every chief priest is appointed to offer gifts and sacrifices; hence it is necessary that H E should have something to offer;
HEB 8:4 for if he were on earth he could not be a priest, as there are priests who offer the gifts according to the law.
HEB 8:5 These perform divine service for a sample and shadow of the heavenly things, as Moses was divinely admonished, when he was about to make the tabernacle, for it is said, "see that thou make all things according to the model shewn thee on this mountain."
HEB 8:6 Now then He hath more noble services allotted to him, in as much as he is the mediator of a better covenant, which is established on better promises.
HEB 8:7 For if the first covenant had been faultless there would have been no occasion for a second
HEB 8:8 for finding fault with them he saith, "Behold days are coming, saith the Lord, when I will make a new covenant with the house of Israel, and the house of Judah.
HEB 8:9 not such a covenant as I made with their fathers, on the day when I took them by the hand to lead them out of Egypt; because they did not abide by that covenant of mine, therefore I took no care of them, saith the Lord.
HEB 8:10 This is the covenant which I will make with the house of Israel, After these days, saith the Lord, adapting my laws to their understanding I will write them on their hearts: and I will be their God, and they shall be my people.
HEB 8:11 And they shall no more teach, every one his neighbour, and every one his brother, saying, Know the Lord; for all shall know me from the least to the greatest of them;
HEB 8:12 for I will be merciful to their iniquities, and no more remember their sins and their transgressions."
HEB 8:13 By calling this a new covenant he hath antiquated the first. Now that which is antiquated, and grown old, is near being abolished.
HEB 9:1 Now then the first covenant had the ordinances of divine service and the worldly sanctuary;
HEB 9:2 for a tabernacle was prepared; the first compartment, in which are the candlestick, and the table, and the presentment of the loaves; this is called the Holy.
HEB 9:3 And beyond the second veil is a compartment which is called, The Holy of Holies,
HEB 9:4 containing a golden altar and the ark of the covenant, all overlaid with gold, in which was the golden urn containing the manna, and the staff of Aaron which budded, and the tables of the covenant,
HEB 9:5 and above it the cherubim of glory overshadowing the mercy-seat, concerning which we are not at this time to speak particularly.
HEB 9:6 These things being thus prepared, the priests, performing the divine services, go on all occasions into the first compartment;
HEB 9:7 but into the second the chief priest only, and but once a year, not without blood, which he offereth for himself and for the errors of the people,
HEB 9:8 the Holy Spirit plainly shewing this, that the way into the holies was not yet manifested while that tabernacle hath a standing.
HEB 9:9 This figurative representation was for the time being, according to which gifts and sacrifices were offered, which cannot make him who performeth service, perfect with regard to the conscience,
HEB 9:10 they being things imposed barely for meats, and drinks, and divers baptisms, and rules of conduct respecting flesh, until the time of reformation:
HEB 9:11 But Christ being come, a chief priest of the future good things, hath entered into the holies by the greater and more perfect tabernacle; not by one made with hands, that is, not of this creation;
HEB 9:12 nor with the blood of goats and young bulls, but with his own blood, once for all, having procured everlasting redemption.
HEB 9:13 For if the blood of bulls and goats, and the ashes of a heifer, sprinkling the unclean sanctify, to the cleansing of the flesh;
HEB 9:14 how much more will the' blood of the Christ, who by an eternal spirit hath offered himself without blemish to God, purify your conscience from dead works that you may serve the living God.
HEB 9:15 Indeed on the account of this he is the mediator of a New Covenant, that [there having been death for a pardon of the transgressions under the first covenant they who have been called may receive the promise of the everlasting inheritance.
HEB 9:16 For where there is a covenant it necessarily infers the death of that by which it is established.
HEB 9:17 For a covenant is ratified over the dead, and it hath no validity at all while that by which it is established liveth.
HEB 9:18 Whence even the first covenant was not ratified without blood;
HEB 9:19 for when every precept according to law was rehearsed by Moses to all the people, he took the blood of the calves and goats, with water, and scarlet wool, and hyssop, and the Book, and he sprinkled it on all the people
HEB 9:20 saying, This is the blood of the covenant which God hath enjoined on you.
HEB 9:21 And in like manner he sprinkled the tabernacle and all the utensils for the holy service with blood.
HEB 9:22 And according to the law almost all things are purified with blood. Indeed without a shedding of blood there was no remission.
HEB 9:23 There was therefore a necessity that the things which were symbols of those in heaven, should be purified with these, but the heavenly things themselves, with sacrifices better than these.
HEB 9:24 For the Christ did not enter into holies made with hands, the symbols of the true; but into heaven itself; now to appear in the presence of God on our behalf:
HEB 9:25 not that he may many a time offer himself [us the chief priest goeth every year into the holies with blood not his own]
HEB 9:26 else he then must have suffered many a time from the foundation of the world; but now once for all, at the end of the ages, he hath been manifested for the purpose of abolishing sin offerings by the sacrifice of himself.
HEB 9:27 And as it is appointed for men to die once, and after that there is a judgment;
HEB 9:28 so also the Christ, being once offered up to bear the sins of many, will appear a second time, without a sin offering, for the salvation of them who wait for him.
HEB 10:1 For the law having a shadow of the good things to come and not the very image of those things, can by no means make them who present themselves, perfect for ever by those sacrifices which they offer year after year.
HEB 10:2 Otherwise would they not have ceased to be offered? Since they who performed the service, being once purified, would no more have a consciousness of sins.
HEB 10:3 But by these there is an annual remembrance of sins.
HEB 10:4 For it is impossible for the blood of bulls and goats to take away sins.
HEB 10:5 Therefore when coming into the world he saith, "Sacrifices and offering? thou didst not desire, but preparedst for me a body.
HEB 10:6 In whole burnt offerings and offerings for sin thou hadst no pleasure;
HEB 10:7 then I said, Behold I come [in the volume of a book it is written of me] to perform, O God, thy will."
HEB 10:8 Having first said, "Sacrifice and offering and whole burnt offerings, and offerings for sins thou didst not desire, nor take pleasure in them," [These were offered according to the law]
HEB 10:9 He then said, "Behold I come to perform, O God, thy will" [he taketh away the first that he may establish the second].
HEB 10:10 by which will we are sanctified by the offering of the body of Jesus Christ once only.
HEB 10:11 Though every priest hath indeed stood performing daily service, and frequently offering the same sacrifices, these can by no means take away sins;
HEB 10:12 but he having offered for sins one sacrifice, to last for ever, sat down at the right hand of God,
HEB 10:13 thenceforth waiting till his enemies are made his footstool.
HEB 10:14 For by one offering he hath made perfect for ever them who are sanctified.
HEB 10:15 And this indeed the holy spirit testified! to us; for after saying,
HEB 10:16 This is the covenant which I will make with Them "After these days, saith the Lord, having adapted my laws to their understandings, I will write them on their minds,
HEB 10:17 and their sins and iniquities I will remember no more."
HEB 10:18 Now, where there is a remission of these, there is no more an offering for sin.
HEB 10:19 As we, therefore, brethren, have, by virtue of the blood of Jesus, free access to the holies 20 by a new and living way, which He hath consecrated for us, through the veil, that is, his flesh;
HEB 10:21 and a great high priest over the house of God,
HEB 10:22 let us come with a true heart in the full assurance of faith, having our hearts sprinkled from an evil conscience and the body washed with pure water.
HEB 10:23 Let us hold fast the profession of this hope without wavering; for he who hath promised is faithful;
HEB 10:24 and let us observe one another, in order to excite love and good works,
HEB 10:25 not forsaking the assembling of ourselves together, as is the custom of some, but comforting one another; and so much the more as you see the day approaching.
HEB 10:26 For if we sin wilfully, after we have received the knowledge of the truth, there remaineth no more any sacrifice for sins,
HEB 10:27 but a certain dreadful expectation of judgment, and fiery indignation which will devour the adversaries.
HEB 10:28 Whoever hath set at naught the law of Moses dieth without mercy, on the evidence of two or three witnesses.
HEB 10:29 Of how much greater punishment, think ye, will he be thought worthy, who hath trampled upon the Son of God, and accounted the blood of the covenant, by which he was sanctified, a common thing, and treated contemptuously the spirit of grace?
HEB 10:30 For we know him who said, "Vengeance is mine, I will requite, saith the Lord;" and, again, "The Lord will judge his people."
HEB 10:31 It is a dreadful thing to fall into the hands of the living God.
HEB 10:32 But call to remembrance the former days, in which, after you were enlightened, you endured a great conflict of sufferings,
HEB 10:33 being publicly exposed to reproaches and afflictions, and at the same time sympathizing with them who were thus treated:
HEB 10:34 For you sympathized with me in my bonds, and waited with joy the seizure of your goods, knowing that you had in yourselves a better,"even an ever-during substance in heaven.
HEB 10:35 Therefore cast not away that confidence of yours which hath a great recompense of reward.
HEB 10:36 For you must persevere, that when you have performed the will of God, you may receive the promised reward.
HEB 10:37 "For yet a little while, and he who is coming will come, and will not delay;
HEB 10:38 now the just shall live because of faith; but if he, through fear, draw back; my soul hath no pleasure in him."
HEB 10:39 But we are not of them who draw back for perdition; but of them who believe for the attainment of life.
HEB 11:1 Now, faith is a confident expectation of things hoped for; a convincement of the mind with respect to the reality of things not seen.
HEB 11:2 By this therefore the ancients obtained reputation.
HEB 11:3 By faith we understand that the ages were arranged by a word of God, that the things seen should not at all be out of things which appear.
HEB 11:4 By faith Abel offered to God a more excellent sacrifice than Cain; by means of which he received a testimonial of being righteous, God himself giving a testimony in favour of his gifts; and by it he, though dead, still speaketh.
HEB 11:5 By faith Enoch was translated that he should not see death; and he was not found, because God translated him; for before his translation he received this testimonial that he was well pleasing to God.
HEB 11:6 Now without faith it is impossible to be well pleasing; for he who cometh to God must believe that he existeth, and that he is the rewarder of them who diligently seek him.
HEB 11:7 By faith Noah, when warned of unforeseen events, with a religious concern prepared an ark for the saving of his household; by which he condemned the world, and became heir of that righteousness which is by faith.
HEB 11:8 By faith Abraham, when called, shewed obedience by going to the place which he was to receive for an inheritance, and set out on his journey not knowing whither he was going.
HEB 11:9 By faith he sojourned in the land of promise as in a strange land, and dwelt in tents with Isaak and Jacob, who were coheirs with him of the same promise.
HEB 11:10 For he expected that city which hath foundations, whose architect and founder is God.
HEB 11:11 By faith Sarah also received strength for conception, and was delivered of a son when she was past age, because she judged him faithful who had promised.
HEB 11:12 Therefore there sprang even from one, and him dead as to these things, a posterity like the stars of heaven for multitude, and like the sand on the sea shore which is innumerable.
HEB 11:13 These all died in faith without receiving the things promised, but they viewed them at a distance, and were persuaded of, and embraced them, and acknowledged that they were strangers and sojourners in the land.
HEB 11:14 For they who speak thus shew plainly that they are seeking their father's country:
HEB 11:15 Now had these been mindful of that from which they came out, they might have had an opportunity of returning thither:
HEB 11:16 but now they desire a better; that is a heavenly country; therefore God is not ashamed of them; to be invoked as their God: for he prepared a city for them.
HEB 11:17 By faith Abraham, when he was put to the trial, offered up Isaak. Though he had received the promises he offered up his only begotten son,
HEB 11:18 in respect to whom it had been said, that "in Isaak a seed shall be called for thee,"
HEB 11:19 reckoning that God was able to raise him up, even from the dead, from which in a figurative sense, he had received him.
HEB 11:20 By faith respecting things to come Isaak blessed Jacob and Esau.
HEB 11:21 By faith Jacob, when a dying, blessed each of Joseph's sons and worshipped, bowing upon the head of his staff.
HEB 11:22 By faith Joseph, at the close of his life, made mention of the departure of the Israelites, and gave a charge concerning his bones.
HEB 11:23 By faith Moses, when he was born was concealed three months by his parents, because they saw that he was a comely child, and they were not terrified by the king's edict.
HEB 11:24 By faith Moses, when he was become great, refused to be called the son of Pharaoh's daughter,
HEB 11:25 chusing rather to suffer afflictions with the people of God, than to enjoy the pleasures of sin for a season;
HEB 11:26 accounting the reproach of the Christ greater riches than the treasures of Egypt; for he had an eye to the reward.
HEB 11:27 By faith he left Egypt in defiance of the king's wrath; for he persevered as seeing Him who is invisible.
HEB 11:28 By faith he celebrated the passover, and the pouring out of the blood, that the destroyer of the first born might not touch them.
HEB 11:29 By faith they passed through the red sea as on dry ground, which the Egyptians attempting to do were swallowed up.
HEB 11:30 By faith the walls of Jericho fell down, when processions had been made around them, for seven days.
HEB 11:31 By faith Rahab the harlot did not perish with the unbelievers, she having received the spies with peace.
HEB 11:32 And what shall I say more? For the time would fail me to speak of Gideon, and Barak, and Sampson, and Jephthae of David and Samuel, and the prophets,
HEB 11:33 who by faith subdued kingdoms, wrought righteousness, obtained promises, stopped the mouths of lions,
HEB 11:34 quenched the violence of fire, escaped the edge of the sword, were strengthened from weakness, became mighty in battle, repelled armies of aliens.
HEB 11:35 Women received their dead children, by a restoration of them to life. As for others, some were tortured, not expecting deliverance, that they might obtain a better resurrection;
HEB 11:36 and others received the trial of mockings, and scourgings, besides bonds and imprisonments.
HEB 11:37 They were stoned; they were sawn asunder; they were tempted; they were slain with the sword; they wandered about in sheep skins, in goats skins, destitute, afflicted, tormented,
HEB 11:38 [of whom the world was not worthy] wandering in deserts, and mountains, and dens, and caves of the earth.
HEB 11:39 Though these all received a testimonial by means of their belief, they did not obtain the promise,
HEB 11:40 God having provided something better for us, that without us they should not be made perfect.
HEB 12:1 As we therefore are encompassed with such a cloud of witnesses, let us lay aside every weight, and the sin which easily entangleth us, and let us run without intermission the race set before us,
HEB 12:2 looking forward to Jesus, the leader and perfecter of this faith, who for the joy that was set before him endured a cross, despising shame, and hath taken a seat at the right hand of the throne of God.
HEB 12:3 Consider him who bore such contradiction of sinners against himself, that you may not grow weary, nor faint in your minds.
HEB 12:4 You have not yet in your contest with sin resisted to blood.
HEB 12:5 And have you forgotten this exhortation which speaketh to us as to children, "My son slight not the correction of the Lord, Nor faint when reproved by him;
HEB 12:6 For whom the Lord loveth he reproveth, And chastiseth every son whom he receiveth.
HEB 12:7 If you endure correction God dealeth with you as sons. For what son is there whom a father doth not correct?
HEB 12:8 Now if you are without correction, of which all are partakers, you are indeed bastards and not sons.
HEB 12:9 Well then: we have had fathers of our flesh who have corrected us, and we have reverenced them; shall we not much more submit ourselves to the father of our spirits, and live?
HEB 12:10 For they indeed for a few days corrected us as they thought fit; but he for our advantage, that we may partake of his holiness.
HEB 12:11 Now all correction seemeth, for the present, not to be matter of joy, but of grief; yet afterwards it produceth the peaceful fruit of righteousness to them who are exercised therewith.
HEB 12:12 Therefore lift up the hands which hang down, and the knees which are feeble,
HEB 12:13 and make straight tracks with your feet, that that which is lame may not be sprained, but rather healed.
HEB 12:14 Follow peace with all men, and that holiness without which none shall see the Lord,
HEB 12:15 watching diligently that none fall short of the favour of God"that no root of bitterness spring up and occasion trouble, and many be defiled by it
HEB 12:16 that there be no fornicator, nor profane person like Esau, who for a single meal sold his birth right;
HEB 12:17 for you know that afterwards when he wished to inherit the blessing, he was rejected; for he found no way to change his father's mind, though he earnestly sought it with tears.
HEB 12:18 For you are not come to a mountain which might be touched, and to blazing fire, and to gloom, and darkness, and a turbid tempest,
HEB 12:19 and to the sound of a trumpet, and a sound of words, the hearers of which entreated that the discourse might not be continued to them;
HEB 12:20 for they could not bear this threat, "And if even a beast touch the mountain, it shall be stoned or pierced through with a dart."
HEB 12:21 And so awful was the appearance, that Moses said, "I am exceedingly terrified and tremble:"
HEB 12:22 but you are come to mount Sion, and to the city of the living God, to the heavenly Jerusalem, and to myriads of angels
HEB 12:23 to the general assembly and congregation of first born, enrolled in heaven, and to God the judge of all, and to the spirits of just men made perfect,
HEB 12:24 and to Jesus the mediator of a new covenant, and to the blood of sprinkling which speaketh better things than that of Abel.
HEB 12:25 See that you do not reject him who speaketh. For if they did not escape who rejected him who gave forth oracles on earth, how much less shall we who reject him who is from heaven,
HEB 12:26 whose voice then shook the earth, but he hath now announced, saying, "Yet once more I shake not only the earth but the heaven also."
HEB 12:27 Now this expression, "Yet once more" signifieth the removal of the things shaken, as having been made, that the things which are immoveable may remain.
HEB 12:28 As we have therefore received a kingdom which cannot be shaken, let us have gratitude by which we may serve God acceptably, with reverence and holy awe:
HEB 12:29 for our God is a consuming fire.
HEB 13:1 Let brotherly love continue.
HEB 13:2 Be not unmindful of hospitality; for by this some have unknowingly entertained angels.
HEB 13:3 Remember them who are in bonds, as if you were bound with them; them who suffer ill treatment, as being yourselves in the body.
HEB 13:4 Let marriage be held in esteem by all, and its bed be undefiled: for whoremongers and adulterers God will judge.
HEB 13:5 Let your conduct be free from avarice. Be content with what you have; for he hath said, "I will never leave thee, nor will I ever forsake thee."
HEB 13:6 So that we may say with confidence, "The Lord is my helper, I will not fear what man can to do me."
HEB 13:7 Remember your leaders, who spake to you the word of God. Observing carefully the issue of their conduct, imitate their faith. Jesus Christ is the same yesterday, today, and forever.
HEB 13:8 Be not led away by various and strange doctrines, for it is better to have the heart strengthened with favour than with meats which have not profited those versed in them.
HEB 13:10 We have an altar from which they who serve in the tabernacle have no right to eat.
HEB 13:11 For the bodies of those animals, the blood of which is carried by the chief priest into the holies for a sin offering, are burned without the camp.
HEB 13:12 And therefore Jesus, that he might by his own blood sanctify the people, suffered without the gate.
HEB 13:13 Let us then go out to him, without the camp, bearing his reproach.
HEB 13:14 For we have no abiding city here, but are seeking one to come.
HEB 13:15 By him therefore let us offer up continually to God a sacrifice of praise, that is, the fruit of our lips, praising his name;
HEB 13:16 and forget not beneficence and contribution: for with such sacrifices God is well pleased.
HEB 13:17 Obey your leaders and yield to them [for they are watching over your souls,[as they who must give an account] that they may do it with joy and not with grief; for this would be unprofitable for you.
HEB 13:18 Pray for us; for we are confident that we have a good conscience, being desirous of conducting ourselves honourably in all things, 19 and I exhort you to this with the more earnestness, that I may be restored to you the sooner.
HEB 13:20 Now may the God of this peace, who raised from the dead the shepherd of the flock, who is great by the blood of an everlasting covenant, namely, our Lord Jesus,
HEB 13:21 perfect you in every good work, that you may do his will, working in you what is well pleasing in his sight through Jesus Christ: to whom be the glory for the ages of the ages. Amen.
HEB 13:22 Now I beseech you, brethren, bear with this word of exhortation, for I have sent it to you in brief.
HEB 13:23 You know that our brother Timothy is set at liberty, with whom, if he come soon, I will see you.
HEB 13:24 Salute all your leaders and all the saints. They of Italy salute you.
HEB 13:25 The favour be with you all. Amen.
JAM 1:1 James, "a servant of God and of the Lord Jesus Christ, to the twelve tribes who are dispersed abroad, Greeting.
JAM 1:2 Count it, my brethren, all joy when you fall into divers trials,
JAM 1:3 knowing that the trial of your faith operateth to produce patience.
JAM 1:4 Let patience then have a full effect, that you may be perfect and complete, deficient in nothing.
JAM 1:5 And if any of you wanteth wisdom, let him ask it of God, who giveth to all liberally and upbraideth not; and it will be given him.
JAM 1:6 But let him ask with faith, without wavering, for he who wavereth is like a wave of the sea, raised by the wind and tossed about.
JAM 1:7 Let not therefore such a man think that he shall receive any thing from the Lord.
JAM 1:8 A man unsteady in his mind, is unstable in all his ways.
JAM 1:9 Let the brother who is in low circumstances glory in his exaltation;
JAM 1:10 and him who is rich, in his humiliation, because he shall pass away like a flower of the grass.
JAM 1:11 For the sun riseth with its scorching heat, and withereth the blade, and the flower thereof failleth, and its beautiful appearance is gone. Just so will the rich man be blasted in his pursuits.
JAM 1:12 Happy the man, who endureth a trial! because having stood the test, he will  Jas 1:receive the crown of life, which the Lord hath promised to them who love him.
JAM 1:13 Let no one when tempted say, I am tempted of God. For God cannot be tempted by evil, neither doth he tempt any one.
JAM 1:14 But every one is tempted by his own desire, when allured and ensnared.
JAM 1:15 In that case desire having conceived, bringeth forth sin, and sin, when grown up, produceth death.
JAM 1:16 Be not led astray, my beloved brethren:
JAM 1:17 Every good donation, and every perfect gift, is from above, and cometh down from the father of lights, with whom there is no change, nor shadow of turning. 18 Of his own will he hath impregnated us with a word of truth, that we may be a kind of first fruits of his creatures.
JAM 1:19 Therefore, my beloved brethren, let every man be swift to hear, slow to speak, slow to wrath:
JAM 1:20 for the wrath of man worketh not the righteousness of God.
JAM 1:21 Therefore having thrown off all the filth and scum of wickedness, receive with meekness the implanted word which is able to save your souls;
JAM 1:22 and be doers of the word, and not hearers only, deceiving yourselves.
JAM 1:23 For if any one is a hearer of the word and not a doer, he is like a man viewing his natural face in a glass.
JAM 1:24 For having viewed himself, and gone away, he instantly forgot what manner of person he was.
JAM 1:25 But whosoever hath looked carefully into the perfect law of this liberty, and continued therein; he being not a forgetful hearer, but a doer of work, shall by his doing be happy.
JAM 1:26 If any one among you thinketh to be religious without bridling his tongue, he is but deceiving his heart. Such a one's religion is vain.
JAM 1:27 Pure and undefiled religion in the sight of our God and father is this, to take the oversight and care of orphans and widows in their distress, and to keep one's self unspotted from the world.
JAM 2:1 Do not, my brethren, exercise this belief of our glorious Lord Jesus Christ in partial regards for persons.
JAM 2:2 For if there should come into your assembly a man in splendid dress, having his fingers adorned with gold rings; and there should come in also a poor man in mean apparel;
JAM 2:3 and you should pay respect to the man in the splendid dress, and say to him, sit thou here in an honourable place; and say to the poor man, stand thou there; or, sit here below my footstool:
JAM 2:4 have you not actually made distinctions among yourselves, and become ill principled judges?
JAM 2:5 Hearken, my beloved brethren, hath not God chosen the poor of this world to be rich in faith, and heirs of the kingdom, which he hath promised to them who love him?
JAM 2:6 But you have treated the poor with disdain. Do not the rich domineer over you? Do they not drag you to tribunals?
JAM 2:7 Do they not revile that honourable name by which you are called?
JAM 2:8 If you fulfil a law which, according to the scripture, is indeed a royal one, namely, "Thou shalt love thy neighbour as thyself," you do well:
JAM 2:9 but if you have respect of persons, you commit sin, and are by that law convicted as transgressors.
