JAM 2:10 For whosoever is to keep the whole law and shall fail in one point, is guilty of all.
JAM 2:11 For it having said, "Thou shalt not commit adultery," hath also said, "Thou shalt not murder" Now, if thou shall not commit adultery, but shalt commit murder, thou art become a transgressor of law.
JAM 2:12 Thus speak and act thus, as you are to be judged by a law of liberty;
JAM 2:13 for the sentence of judgment shall be without mercy for him who hath not exercised mercy, though mercy glorieth over a sentence of judgment.
JAM 2:14 What is the advantage, my brethren, though one should say he hath belief, when he hath not works? Can that belief save him?
JAM 2:15 Suppose a brother or a sister be naked, or in want of daily food,
JAM 2:16 and one of you should say to them, go in peace: be warmed, and be fed to the full; and you do not give them the things necessary for the body, is this any advantage?
JAM 2:17 Just so it is in respect to this belief, if it hath not works; being by itself it is dead.
JAM 2:18 One indeed may say, thou hast belief, and I have works. Shew me thy belief by thy works. As for me, I will shew thee my belief by my works.
JAM 2:19 Thou believest that there is one God. Thou dost well. The demons also believe and tremble.
JAM 2:20 But wouldst thou, vain man, know that belief without works is dead?
JAM 2:21 Was not Abraham, our father, justified by works when he offered up his son Isaak on the altar?
JAM 2:22 Thou seest that his belief co-operated with his works, and by his works his belief was perfected.
JAM 2:23 And the scripture was fulfilled, which saith, "Abraham believed God and it was reckoned to him for righteousness;" and he was called the friend of God.
JAM 2:24 You see then that a man is justified by works, and not by belief only.
JAM 2:25 In like manner also, was not Rahab the harlot justified by works, having secreted the messengers, and sent them out another way?
JAM 2:26 For as the body without spirit is dead, so belief without works is dead also.
JAM 3:1 Be not, my brethren, many teachers; as you know that we shall receive a severer sentence;
JAM 3:2 for in many instances we all offend. If any one offend not in discourse he is a perfect man, and able to bridle in the whole body.
JAM 3:3 Behold we put bits in the mouths of horses to make them obey us, and we manage their whole body.
JAM 3:4 Behold ships also, how large soever they be, though driven by hard gales are managed by a very small helm, and kept to the course which the pilot in tendeth.
JAM 3:5 So also the tongue is a very small member, yet it boasteth great things. See what a great pile of wood a little fire kindleth to a flame!
JAM 3:6 Now, the tongue is a fire, the leader of iniquity; the tongue is set among the members, staining the whole body, and setting the wheel of nature in a blaze, when it is itself set in a blaze by hell.
JAM 3:7 For all kinds of beasts, and birds, and reptiles, and fishes, are subdued and have been subdued by man;
JAM 3:8 But the tongue of man none can subdue. It is an ungovernable monster: it is full of deadly poison.
JAM 3:9 With it we bless our God and father; and with it we curse men, who are made after the image of God.
JAM 3:10 Out of the same mouth proceed blessing and cursing. These things, my brethren, ought not to be so.
JAM 3:11 Doth the fountain send forth sweet water and bitter out of the same opening? 12 Can a fig-tree, my brethren, produce olives? Or the vine, figs? So no fountain can yield salt Water and fresh.
JAM 3:13 Whoever among you is a man of wisdom and knowledge, let him, by a virtuous course of life, shew his works with the meekness of wisdom.
JAM 3:14 But if you have bitter zeal, and strife in your heart, do not boast and lie against the truth.
JAM 3:15 This is not the wisdom which cometh down from above; but that which is of an earthly, sensual, and devilish nature.
JAM 3:16 For where there is a zeal with strife, there will be confusion, and every thing which is bad.
JAM 3:17 Now the wisdom which cometh from above, is first pure, then peaceable, gentle, easily to be entreated, full of mercy and good fruits, without partiality, and without hypocrisy.
JAM 3:18 And the fruit of this righteousness is peaceably sown by them who cultivate peace.
JAM 4:1 Whence come wars and fightings among you? Is it not from this"from those sensual appetites of yours which are at war in your members?
JAM 4:2 You covet and use not. You kill, and envy, and cannot enjoy. You fight, and wage war, and do not possess, because you do not ask.
JAM 4:3 You ask and do not receive, because you ask amiss, that you may lavish on your sensual appetites.
JAM 4:4 Ye adulterers and adulteresses! do you not know that the friendship of this world is enmity against God? Whoever therefore wisheth to be a friend of the world is adjudged an enemy of God.
JAM 4:5 Do you think that the scripture speaketh in vain? Doth the spirit which dwelt in us excite desire to envy?
JAM 4:6 It granteth indeed a greater favour, therefore it saith, "God resisteth the proud, and granteth favour to the humble."
JAM 4:7 Submit yourselves therefore to God. Resist the devil and he will flee from you.
JAM 4:8 Draw near to God and he will draw near to you. Cleanse your hands, ye sinners; and purify your hearts, ye double minded.
JAM 4:9 Be afflicted and mourn and weep. Let your laughter be turned into grief; and your joy into con fusion of face.
JAM 4:10 Humble yourselves in the sight of the Lord and he will exalt you. Speak not, brethren, against one another. He who speaketh against a brother, and judgeth his brother, speaketh against law, and judgeth law. Now if thou judgest law, thou art not a doer of law, but a judge.
JAM 4:12 There is but one [judge]: the lawgiver, who is able to save and destroy; who art thou who judgest another?
JAM 4:13 Come, now, ye who say, Today or tomorrow we will go to this or that city, and spend a year there, and traffic, and get gain,
JAM 4:14 when you do not know what will be the result of tomorrow. For what is your life? For it is a vapour which appeareth for a little while and then vanisheth.
JAM 4:15 Instead of your saying, If it be the Lord's will, and we shall live, we will do this or that,
JAM 4:16 you now boast of your arrogant projects. All such boasting is evil. Therefore to know what is good and not do it, is a sin.
JAM 5:1 Come, now, ye rich; weep, and raise a mournful cry for the miseries which are coming upon you.
JAM 5:2 Your riches are corrupted, and your garments are moth eaten.
JAM 5:3 Your gold and your silver are covered with rust; and the rust of them will be a witness against you, and corrode your flesh like fire. You have heaped up treasure in the last days.
JAM 5:4 Behold the wages of the labourers who have reaped your fields, which you have withholden, raise a cry; and the outcries of these reapers have reached the ears of the Lord of Sabaoth.
JAM 5:5 You have lived luxuriously on the earth. You have indulged voluptuousness. You have pampered your hearts, as on a day of public feasting.
JAM 5:6 You have condemned you have murdered the just one. Is he not setting himself in array against you?
JAM 5:7 Wherefore be ye, brethren, patient till the coming of the Lord. Behold the husbandman expecteth the precious fruits of the earth, waiting for them with patience, until it hath received the former and the latter rain.
JAM 5:8 Wait ye also with patience. Strengthen your hearts, because the coming of the Lord is near.
JAM 5:9 Repine not, brethren, against one another, that you may not be condemned. Behold the judge is at the door.
JAM 5:10 For an example of enduring adversity, and of long suffering, take, my brethren, the prophets who have spoken in the name of the Lord.
JAM 5:11 Behold we call those sufferers happy. You have heard of the patience of Job, and have seen the Lord's termination" that the Lord is full of compassion and tender mercy.
JAM 5:12 Now above all things, my brethren, swear not, either by heaven, or by the earth, or by any other oath; but let your yes, be yes; and your no, no; that you may not fall under condemnation.
JAM 5:13 Is any one among you afflicted, let him pray. Is any one cheerful, let him sing praises.
JAM 5:14 Is any among you sick, let him send for the elders of the congregation, and let them pray over him, having anointed him with oil in the name of the Lord.
JAM 5:15 And the prayer of this faith will cure the sick, and the Lord will raise him up. And though he may have committed sin, he will be forgiven.
JAM 5:16 Confess your faults to one another, and pray for one another, that you may be healed. The prayer of a righteous man under the divine impulse is very powerful.
JAM 5:17 Elias was a man frail and mortal like ourselves. In one prayer he prayed that it might not rain, and it did not rain on the land during three years and six months.
JAM 5:18 And he prayed again, and the heaven gave rain, and the land bloomed with its productions.
JAM 5:19 Brethren, if any among you hath wandered from the truth and another hath brought him back,
JAM 5:20 let him know that he who hath brought back a sinner from the error of his way, shall save a soul from death, and cover a multitude of sins.
1PE 1:1 Peter, an apostle of Jesus Christ, to the sojourners of the dispersion in Pontus, Galatia, Cappadocia, Asia and Bithynia,
1PE 1:2 whom God the Father, according to his predetermination hath chosen, that by a sanctification of spirit they may obey, and be sprinkled with the blood of Jesus Christ; favour be to you, and may peace be multiplied.
1PE 1:3 Blessed be the God and Father of our Lord Jesus Christ, who, according to his abundant mercy, hath regenerated us to a lively hope by the resurrection of Jesus Christ from the dead
1PE 1:4 for an inheritance incorruptible, incapable of defilement or decay, reserved in heaven for us
1PE 1:5 who are, during belief, kept safely by the power of God, for a deliverance prepared to be revealed in the last time;
1PE 1:6 in whom you exult with joy though you are now for a little while, if it be necessary, distressed with divers trials;
1PE 1:7 in order that your faith, which hath stood the test and is much more precious than gold which is of a perishable nature though tried by fire, may be found praise worthy, and honourable, and glorious, at the manifestation of Jesus Christ,
1PE 1:8 whom without knowing him personally you love; in whom though you do not now see him, yet you believe, and rejoice with an inexpressible and glorified joy,
1PE 1:9 receiving as the completion of your faith the salvation of your souls:
1PE 1:10 about which salvation the prophets, who prophesied concerning this favour for you, made diligent inquiry
1PE 1:11 and search, trying to find to what time, and what manner of time, the spirit of Christ within them pointed, when it testified before hand the sufferings which were for Christ, and the glories which should succeed them:
1PE 1:12 to whom it was revealed that it was not for themselves, but for us, that they dispensed those things which have now been announced to you by them who proclaimed to you the glad tidings with a holy spirit sent from heaven; into which things angels have an earnest desire to look narrowly.
1PE 1:13 Wherefore having girded up the loins of your understanding, being perfectly sober, keep your hope fixed on the favour to be conferred on you at the manifestation of Jesus Christ;
1PE 1:14 as obedient children, not fashioning yourselves in conformity to your former desires during your ignorance;
1PE 1:15 but as he who hath called you is holy, be ye also holy in the whole course of your life;
1PE 1:16 for it is written, "Be ye holy, because I am holy."
1PE 1:17 And since you invoke, as father, him who without respect of persons judgeth every one according to his work, pass the time of your sojourning in fear;
1PE 1:18 knowing that from that vain course of life, handed down to you from your fathers, you have been redeemed not with perishable things such as silver and gold,
1PE 1:19 but with the precious blood of Christ, as of a lamb without blemish and without spot,
1PE 1:20 fore-ordained indeed before the foundation of the world, and manifested in these last times, for the sake of you
1PE 1:21 who by him believe in God, who hath raised him from the dead, and hath given him glory, so that you may have faith and hope in God.
1PE 1:22 Having, in obedience to the truth, purified your souls by the spirit for an unfeigned brotherly affection, love one another fervently with a pure heart,
1PE 1:23 as you have been born again not of corruptible but of incorruptible seed, by the word of God, which liveth and endureth forever.
1PE 1:24 Because "all flesh is as grass, and all the glory of man as a flower of grass. the grass withereth, and the flower thereof falleth,
1PE 1:25 but the decree of the Lord endureth forever", and this is the decree which hath been proclaimed as glad tidings for you;
1PE 2:1 Therefore laying aside all malice, and all deceit, and every kind of hypocrisy, envy and slander,
1PE 2:2 like newborn babes desire the pure milk of the word that by it you may thrive.
1PE 2:3 Since you have tasted that the Lord is gracious,
1PE 2:4 to whom you are come as to a living stone, by men indeed rejected, but with God chosen and precious,
1PE 2:5 and you yourselves as living stones are built up a spiritual house, a holy priesthood to offer up spiritual sacrifices acceptable to God through Jesus Christ;
1PE 2:6 on which account also there is in the scripture this passage, "Behold I lay in Sion a chosen, precious, chief corner stone, and he who confideth in it, shall not be ashamed,"
1PE 2:7 this honour then being for you who believe: but to the disbelieving, "the stone, which the builders rejected that which was for the head of the corner,"
1PE 2:8 is indeed a stone of stumbling and a rock of offence. They disbelieving the word stumble at the thing for which they were laid:
1PE 2:9 but you being a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people peculiarly set apart that you may publish the praises of him who called you out of darkness into his marvellous light
1PE 2:10 you who formerly were not a people but are now the people of God who were uncompassionated, but are now compassionated
1PE 2:11 beloved; I beseech you as strangers and sojourners to abstain from carnal lusts, which war against the soul:
1PE 2:12 let your behaviour among the nations be virtuous, that when they speak against you as evil doers, they who have been eye witnesses may from your good works glorify God in the day of visitation.
1PE 2:13 Be subject therefore to every human establishment for the Lord's sake, whether to a king as supreme,
1PE 2:14 or to governor as persons sent by him for the punishment of evil doers, and for the praise of them who do well.
1PE 2:15 For it is the will of God that you should by such good behaviour curb the ignorance of foolish men.
1PE 2:16 As freemen, but not like those who use their freedom as a cover for wickedness, but as servants of God
1PE 2:17 honour all men, love the brotherhood; fear God; honour the king.
1PE 2:18 You who are servants, be subject to your masters with reverence, not only to the good and gentle, but also to the morose.
1PE 2:19 For this is pleasing, if from a conscientious regard to God one endureth grief suffering wrongfully.
1PE 2:20 For what glory is it, if when you commit a fault and are beaten, you suffer patiently? But if when acting well you meet with ill usage, and bear it, this is well pleasing in the sight of God.
1PE 2:21 For to this you have been called, because Christ himself suffered for you, leaving you an example that you should follow in his footsteps,
1PE 2:22 "Who committed no sin, nor was guile found in his mouth";
1PE 2:23 who when he was reviled, did not revile again, when he suffered, did not threaten; but committed himself to him who judgeth righteously;
1PE 2:24 who himself offered up our sins in his own body on the cross, that we, being freed from those sins, might live for righteousness; "by whose stripes you have been healed."
1PE 2:25 For you were like sheep going astray, but are now brought back to the shepherd and overseer of your souls.
1PE 3:1 In like manner ye wives, be subject to your own husbands, that if any of them disbelieve the word they may by the deportment of their wives, without a word, be won over,
1PE 3:2 when they see your reverential, chaste behaviour.
1PE 3:3 And let your adorning be, not that which is external by plaiting the hair with appendages of gold, nor finery of dress;
1PE 3:4 but the hidden man of the heart, with the incorruptible ornament of a meek and quiet spirit, which is highly precious in the sight of God.
1PE 3:5 For thus, in former times, the holy women who trusted in God adorned themselves, submitting to their husbands,
1PE 3:6 [as Sarah, whose daughters you are, obeyed Abraham, calling him lord] doing what was right, and alarmed by no terror.
1PE 3:7 Likewise ye husbands cohabit with your wives, paying respect to them as the weaker sex, and moreover as co-heirs with you of the grant of life, that there may be no impediment to your prayers.
1PE 3:8 Finally, be all of one mind, sympathising with one another, full of brotherly love, compassionate, courteous
1PE 3:9 not rendering evil for evil, revile for revile; but on the contrary, blessing; knowing that you have been called for this, that you may inherit a blessing.
1PE 3:10 For "whoever desireth life; and loveth to see good days; Let him keep his tongue from evil, And his lips from speaking guile;
1PE 3:11 Let him depart from evil and do good; Let him seek peace and pursue it.
1PE 3:12 Because the eyes of the Lord are upon the righteous, And his ears are open to their prayers: But the face of the Lord is against them who do evil."
1PE 3:13 Who then will hurt you if you be imitators of him who is good?
1PE 3:14 But if you should even suffer on the account of righteousness, you are happy. Be not terrified with the fear of them, nor dismayed;
1PE 3:15 but sanctify the Lord in your hearts" and be always prepared, in answer to every one who demandeth of you a reason for the hope which is in you, to make a defence with meekness and fear,
1PE 3:16 having a good conscience, that when they speak against you as evil doers, they who calumniate your good conversation in Christ may be put to shame.
1PE 3:17 For if it be the will of God that you should suffer, it is better that you should suffer as well doers than as evil doers.
1PE 3:18 Because Christ himself suffered once for sins, the just for the unjust, that he might bring us to God: being indeed put to death in flesh, but brought to life by that spirit
1PE 3:19 with which he went, and to the spirits which are [now] in prison
1PE 3:20 made proclamation at the time they were disobedient when the long suffering of God was waiting once for all in the day of Noe, while the ark was a building, in which a few, that be eight souls, made their escape during the flood;
1PE 3:21 an antitype to which, namely baptism, [not a removal of the filth of the flesh, but an earnest conscientious application to God] doth now save us also, by means of the resurrection of Jesus Christ,
1PE 3:22 who, having gone to heaven, is at the right hand of God, angels and authorities and powers being made subject to him.
1PE 4:1 Christ therefore having suffered in flesh for us, arm ye yourselves with this reflection, that he who hath suffered in flesh hath been stopped from sin,
1PE 4:2 to the end that he may no longer live the rest of his time in flesh for the lusts of men; but for the will of God.
1PE 4:3 For the past time of this life sufficeth to have wrought the will of the Gentiles, walking in lasciviousness, inordinate desires, excess of wine, revels, carouses, and abominable idolatries;
1PE 4:4 at this they are surprized; and when you do not run with them into the same sink of debauchery, they rail.
1PE 4:5 They shall give an account to him who is prepared to judge living and dead.
1PE 4:6 For to this end also the gospel was proclaimed to the dead, that judged as they might be according to men in flesh, they might live according to God in spirit.
1PE 4:7 Now the end of all things is at hand, therefore be sober, and watch unto prayer,
1PE 4:8 and above all things have fervent love for one another: for this "love will cover a multitude of sins."
1PE 4:9 Be hospitable to one another without grudging.
1PE 4:10 According as every one hath received a free gift continue dispensing it to each other as good stewards of the manifold grace of God
1PE 4:11 if any one speaketh, as speaking the oracles of God; if any one dispenseth, as dispensing out of a stock which God supplieth; that in all things God may be gloried through Jesus Christ, to whom belongeth the glory and the power, for the ages of the ages. Amen.
1PE 4:12 Beloved, be not surprized at the fiery trial among you, which is come upon you to try you, as if some strange thing had befallen you:
1PE 4:13 but inasmuch as you partake of the sufferings of the Christ, rejoice; that at the manifestation of his glory you may indeed rejoice with exceeding great joy. 14 If you are reproached for the name of Christ you are happy; because the spirit of the glory, even the spirit of God resteth on you. On their part indeed it is reviled, but on your part it is glorified.
1PE 4:15 For let none of you suffer as a murderer, or as a thief, or a malefactor, or as a usurper of authority;
1PE 4:16 and if as a Christian, let him not be ashamed, but glorify God in this respect.
1PE 4:17 For the time is come when judgment is to begin at the house of God. And if it begin first with us, what must be the end of them who disregard the glad tidings of God?
1PE 4:18 "If the righteous scarcely escapeth, where shall the ungodly and sinner appear?"
1PE 4:19 Let them therefore who suffer according to the will of God, commit their souls to him in well doing, as to a faithful creator.
1PE 5:1 With regard to the elders among you, being myself a fellow elder, and a witness of the sufferings of the Christ, and a partaker of the glory about to be revealed, I give them this exhortation
1PE 5:2 Tend the flock of God which is among you, watching over it, not by constraint, but willingly; not with a view to sordid gain, but with a ready mind;
1PE 5:3 not as exercising dominion over the lots, but as being examples to the flock.
1PE 5:4 And when the chief shepherd shall appear, ye shall receive an unfading crown of glory.
1PE 5:5 Likewise ye who are young, submit to those more advanced in years. And being all submissive to one another; adorn yourselves with humility; because "God resisteth the proud and granteth favour to the humble;"
1PE 5:6 therefore humble yourselves under the mighty hand of God, that he may in due time exalt you.
1PE 5:7 Having cast all your care upon him, for he careth for you,
1PE 5:8 be sober, be watchful: because your adversary the devil is walking about, like a roaring lion, seeking whom he may devour,
1PE 5:9 him you should resist, standing firm in the faith, knowing that the same kind of sufferings are undergone by your brotherhood in the world.
1PE 5:10 Now may the God of all favour, who hath invited us to his eternal glory by Christ Jesus, when we have suffered a little may he himself fit, support, strengthen and establish you!
1PE 5:11 To him be the glory and the power, for the ages of the ages. Amen.
1PE 5:12 By Sylvanus the faithful brother I have, as I reckon, written briefly to you, exhorting, and testifying that this is the true favour of God for which you stand up.
1PE 5:13 The congregation at Babylon salute you. So doth Marcus my son.
1PE 5:14 Salute one another with a holy kiss. Peace be with you all who are in Christ Jesus. Amen.
2PE 1:1 Simon Peter, a servant and an apostle of Jesus Christ, to them who have obtained a like precious belief with us, in the saving goodness of our God and saviour Jesus Christ,
2PE 1:2 favour be to you, and may peace be multiplied by an acknowledgment of God, and of Jesus our Lord.
2PE 1:3 As his divine power hath freely granted those things conducive to life and godliness, and all are ours by our acknowledging him who hath called us by glory and virtue,
2PE 1:4 through which he hath freely made us very great and precious promises, that by them you may become partakers of a divine nature when you have fled from the corruption which is in the world by lust;
2PE 1:5 therefore, having on your part used all diligence for the very same purpose, add to your faith fortitude; and to fortitude, knowledge;
2PE 1:6 and to knowledge, temperance; and to temperance, perseverance; and to perseverance, piety;
2PE 1:7 and to piety, brotherly affection; and to brotherly affection, universal love;
2PE 1:8 for these being in you, and abounding, dispose you to be neither idle nor unfruitful for the acknowledging of our Lord Jesus Christ:
2PE 1:9 for he who is without these is blind, having closed his eyes, having contracted a forgetfulness of the purification of his past sins.
2PE 1:10 Therefore, brethren, use the more diligence to make your call and election sure; for if you practise these you will never fall;
2PE 1:11 for thus there will further be administered to you, bounteously, the entrance into the everlasting kingdom of our Lord and saviour Jesus Christ.
2PE 1:12 For this purpose I will not neglect to put you always in mind of these things, though you already know them, and are established in the present truth.
2PE 1:13 Indeed I think it right, as long as I am in this tabernacle, to stir you up by admonition;
2PE 1:14 as I know that I must soon lay aside this tabernacle of mine, even as our Lord Jesus Christ hath plainly shewed me;
2PE 1:15 and I will use all diligence that you may be able, every one of you, to recollect these things after my departure.
2PE 1:16 For we indeed did not follow artfully contrived fables when we made known to you the power and the coming of our Lord Jesus Christ; but were ourselves eye witnesses of his majesty.
2PE 1:17 For he was receiving honour and glory from God the Father, when a voice was uttered to him, from the transcendent glory, "This is my Son, the Beloved, in whom I am well pleased."
2PE 1:18 This voice we ourselves actually heard uttered from heaven, when we were with him on the holy mountain.
2PE 1:19 Therefore we have a more complete confirmation of the prophetic word, to which you do well in giving attention, as to a lamp shining in a dark place until the day dawn, and the bringer of light rise in your hearts;
2PE 1:20 knowing this first, that no prophecy of the scripture explaineth itself,
2PE 1:21 for prophecy was not uttered in former days at the will of man; but the holy men of God spoke by an impulse of the holy spirit.
2PE 2:1 Now there were also false prophets among the people, as there will be also among you false teachers, who will introduce destructive sects, denying even the Lord who bought them, bringing on themselves speedy destruction.
2PE 2:2 And many will follow their pernicious courses, on the account of whom the way of the truth will be ill spoken of.
2PE 2:3 Indeed, with insatiable covetousness, they will, with smooth words, make merchandize of you. But the judgment prepared of old for them is not idle, nor is their destruction slumbering.
2PE 2:4 For if God spared not angels who sinned, but confining them in Tartarus, chains of darkness, delivered them up to be kept for judgment
2PE 2:5 and if he spared not the old world, but preserved eight persons, including Noah, the proclaimer of righteousness, when he brought a deluge on the world of ungodly men
2PE 2:6 and when he condemned to destruction the cities of Sodom and Gomorrah, reducing them to ashes, and making them a publick example to future impious men,
2PE 2:7 delivered just Lot, who was troubled at the lascivious conduct of those licentious men,
2PE 2:8 [for at the sight and report, that righteous man who dwelt among them was daily tormented in soul by their unlawful deeds]
2PE 2:9 the Lord knoweth how to deliver the godly from, temptation, and to reserve the wicked to the day of judgment, to be punished;
2PE 2:10 and more especially them who go after flesh, in the lust of uncleanness, and despise authority. Being audacious, and self sufficient they tremble not when they revile glories;
2PE 2:11 whereas angels who are greater in might and power, do not bring against them a railing accusation before the Lord.
2PE 2:12 But these, like irrational brute beasts, made for capture and destruction, railing at what they are ignorant of, shall perish with their own destruction. 13 Receiving wages of iniquity, esteeming riot by day a pleasure; being spots and blemishes; rioting by their deceits; banquetting with you;
2PE 2:14 having eyes full of adultery and unceasing sin; ensnaring unstable souls; having a heart practised in greediness; an execrable race;
2PE 2:15 having forsaken the right road they have gone quite astray, following the way of Balaam son of Bosor, who loved the wages of iniquity,
2PE 2:16 and was convicted of his transgression. [A dumb beast, speaking with a human voice, restrained the madness of the prophet.]
2PE 2:17 They are wells without water; clouds impelled by a whirlwind, for whom is reserved in the bowels of the earth the gloom of everlasting darkness.
2PE 2:18 For uttering, with a solemn tone, swelling words of vanity, they by the lusts of the flesh. by acts of lasciviousness, ensnare them who are indeed flying from those conversant in error;
2PE 2:19 promising them liberty while they themselves are slaves to corruption; for by whatever one is subdued, by that he is enslaved
2PE 2:20 For if alter fleeing from the pollutions of the world by an acknowledgment of the Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ, any are again entangled and overcome by them, the last state of such persons is worse than the first.
2PE 2:21 For it had been better for them not to have known the way of righteousness, than, after knowing it, to turn away from the holy commandment delivered to them.
2PE 2:22 But it hath happened to them according to the true proverb, "The dog is returned to his vomit," and "the washed hog to its wallowing slough."
2PE 3:1 . This, my beloved, is now the second letter which I am writing, with which I stir up your sincere mind by way of remembrance,
2PE 3:2 that you may remember the predictions of the holy prophets, and the injunction of us the apostles of the Lord and Saviour;
2PE 3:3 knowing this first, that in the last day scoffers will come, walking after their own desires,
2PE 3:4 and saying, "Where is the promise of his coming? for since the fathers fell asleep, all things continue as they were from the beginning of the creation."
2PE 3:5 For this they wilfully forget, that by the word of God there were heavens of old, and an earth consisting of water and in water,
2PE 3:6 by which the world that then existed, being deluged, was destroyed;
2PE 3:7 but the heavens and the earth which now exist are, by the same word, treasured up for fire, being kept for the day of judgment, and destruction of these impious men.
2PE 3:8 Now let not this one thing, my beloved, escape you, That with the Lord one day is as a thousand years and a thousand years as one day.
2PE 3:9 The Lord is not slack with regard to his promise, as some reckon slackness. But he is long suffering towards us, not willing that any should perish, but that all should come to a reformation.
2PE 3:10 Now the day of the Lord will come, as a thief at night, when the heavens with a crashing roar shall pass away, and the elements shall be dissolved by fire, and the earth, and all the works thereon, shall be burned up.
2PE 3:11 Therefore as all these things are to be dissolved, what manner of persons ought you to be in holy conversation and godliness,
2PE 3:12 expecting, and eagerly desiring, the coming of the day of God, in which the heavens, all on fire, shall be dissolved, and the elements shall melt with intense heat,
2PE 3:13 and we, according to his promise, expect new heavens, and a new earth in which dwelleth righteousness!
2PE 3:14 As you therefore, beloved, expect these things, use all diligence to be found at peace with him, without spot and without blemish;
2PE 3:15 and reckon the long suffering of our Lord to be salvation; as our beloved brother Paul, according to the wisdom given him, hath also written to you;
2PE 3:16 as he hath also in all his letters, when speaking of these things; in which there are some things hard to be understood; which the unlearned and unstable torture, as they do the other scriptures, to their own destruction.
2PE 3:17 As you therefore, beloved, know these things beforehand, be on your guard, that you may not be hurried away by the error of these lawless men, and fall from your stedfastness;
2PE 3:18 but increase in the favour and knowledge of our Lord and Saviour Jesus Christ. To Him be the glory both now and forever. Amen.
1JO 1:1 What was from the beginning; what we have heard; what we have seen with our eyes; what we have viewed attentively, and our hands have handled [with respect also to the word of the life
1JO 1:2 even the life was manifested, and we have seen, and testify, and announce to you, that eternal life which was with the Father, and hath been clearly manifested to us]
1JO 1:3 that which we have seen and heard, we announce to you, that you also may have communion with us. Now this communion of ours is with the Father, and with his son Jesus Christ.
1JO 1:4 And we write these things to you that your joy may be complete.
1JO 1:5 This indeed is the message which we have heard from him, and announce to you, That God is light and in him there is no darkness at all.
1JO 1:6 If we say that we have communion with him, and walk in darkness, we lie, and do not practise truth.
1JO 1:7 But if we walk in the light as he is in the light, we have communion with one another, and the blood of Jesus Christ his son cleanseth us from all sin.
1JO 1:8 If we say that we have not sin, we deceive ourselves, and the truth is not in us.
1JO 1:9 If we confess our sins, He is faithful, and just to forgive us our sins, and to cleanse us from all unrighteousness.
1JO 1:10 If we say that we have not sinned, we make him a false speaker, and his word is not in us.
1JO 2:1 My children I write these things to you that you may not sin. But if any one sin, we have an advocate with the Father Jesus Christ the righteous,
1JO 2:2 and he is an atonement for our sins, and not for ours only, but for those of the whole world.
1JO 2:3 Now by this we know that we have known him, if we keep his commandments.
1JO 2:4 He who saith I know him, and doth not keep his commandments, is a liar, and the truth is not in him.
1JO 2:5 But whosoever keepeth his word, in him indeed the love of" God is perfected. By this we know that we are in him
1JO 2:6 he who saith he abideth in him, ought to walk as he walked.
1JO 2:7 Brethren, I am not writing to you a new commandment but an old commandment, which you had from the beginning. This old commandment is the word which you heard from the beginning.
1JO 2:8 Again I write to you a new commandment, a thing which is true in him, and in you. Because the darkness is past, and the light, the true light, now shineth,
1JO 2:9 he who saith that he is in the light, and hateth his brother, is still in darkness.
1JO 2:10 He who loveth his brother, abideth in the light, and in it there is no stumbling block.
1JO 2:11 But he who hateth his brother is in the darkness, and walketh in the darkness, and knoweth not whither he is going, because the darkness hath blinded his eyes.
1JO 2:12 I write to you, children, because your sins are forgiven you on account of his name.
1JO 2:13 I write to you, fathers, because you have known him, who is from the beginning. I write to you, young men, because you have overcome the evil one. I write to you, children, because you have known the Father.
1JO 2:14 I have written to you, fathers, because you have known him who is from the beginning. I have written to you, young men, because you are strong, and the word of God abideth in you, and you have overcome the evil one.
1JO 2:15 Love not the world nor the things in the world. If any one loveth the world, the love of the Father is not in him
1JO 2:16 For all that is in the world, the lust of the flesh, and the desire of the eyes, and the pomp of this life are not of the Father, but are of the world.
1JO 2:17 Now the world is passing away, and the desire thereof; but he who doth the will of God shall abide forever.
1JO 2:18 Children, the last period is come: and as you have heard that the Antichrist cometh, there are even now many Antichrists, by which we know that it is the last period.
1JO 2:19 They went out from us; but they were not of us. For if they had been of us, they would have continued with us.
1JO 2:20 But to the end that they might be made manifest [because all are not of us] even you yourselves have an unction from the holy one, and know everyone.
1JO 2:21 I have not written to you because you do not know the truth; but because you know it, and because no kind of falsehood is of the truth.
1JO 2:22 Who is the liar; but he who denieth that Jesus is the Christ? He is the Antichrist who denieth the Father and the Son:
1JO 2:23 whosoever denieth the Son, hath not the Father.
1JO 2:24 As for you, therefore, let that which you have heard from the beginning abide in you. If that which you have heard from the beginning abide in you, then you will abide in the Son, and in the Father.
1JO 2:25 And this is the promise which he hath promised us, even the life which is everlasting.
1JO 2:26 These things I have written to you with a view to them who are seducing you.
1JO 2:27 As for you, the unction which you have received from him abideth in you, and you have no need that any one should teach you. As then this unction itself teacheth you concerning all, and is true, and is not a falsity; abide ye in him as it hath taught you.
1JO 2:28 And now, children, abide in him, that when he shall appear we may have confidence, and not be made ashamed by him at his coming.
1JO 2:29 If you know that he is righteous, you know that every one who practiseth righteousness is born of him.
1JO 3:1 Behold what a love the Father hath shewn us, that we should be called children of God: on this account the world doth not know us, because it did not know him.
1JO 3:2 Beloved, we are now children of God. Though it hath not yet been manifested what we shall be, yet we know that when he shall appear we shall be like him: that we shall see him as he is.
1JO 3:3 Now, everyone who hath this hope in him purifieth himself as he is pure.
1JO 3:4 Whosoever committeth sin, committeth a violation of law; for sin is a violation of law.
1JO 3:5 Now, you know that he was manifested to take away our sins, and there is no sin in him.
1JO 3:6 Whosoever abideth in him doth not sin: whosoever continueth to sin hath not seen him, nor known him.
1JO 3:7 Children, let no one deceive you. He who practiseth righteousness is righteous, as he is righteous.
1JO 3:8 He who practiseth sin is of the devil, because the devil sinneth from the beginning; for this [purpose] the son of God was manifested, that he might destroy the works of the devil.
1JO 3:9 Whosoever is born of God doth not practise sin, because his seed abideth in him, and he cannot sin because he is born of God.
1JO 3:10 By this the children of God are manifest, and the children of the devil. Whosoever doth not practise righteousness is not of God, nor he who doth not love his brother.
1JO 3:11 For this is the message which you have heard from the beginning, that we should love one another,
1JO 3:12 and not be like Cain, who was of the evil one and slew his brother. And why did he slay him? Because his own works were evil, and his brother's righteous.
1JO 3:13 Wonder not, my brethren, if the world hate you.
1JO 3:14 We know that we have passed from death to life, because we love the brethren. He who loveth not his brother abideth in death.
1JO 3:15 Whosoever hateth his brother is a murderer; and you know that no murderer hath everlasting life abiding in him.
1JO 3:16 By this we know the love of God. Because he laid down his life for us, therefore we ought to lay down our lives for the brethren.
1JO 3:17 Whosoever hath worldly substance, and seeth his brother in want, and shutteth up his compassion from him, how dwelleth the love of God in him?
1JO 3:18 My children, let us not love in word, and with the tongue, but in deed, and in truth.
1JO 3:19 When we know by this that we are of the truth, let us in his presence persuade our hearts,
1JO 3:20 in respect to what things soever our heart condemneth us, that God is greater than our hearts, and that he knoweth all things.
1JO 3:21 Beloved, if our heart doth not condemn us, we have confidence towards God,
1JO 3:22 and whatever we ask we obtain from him, because we keep his commandments, and do the things which are pleasing in his sight.
1JO 3:23 Now this is his commandment, that we believe in the name of his son Jesus Christ and love one another, as he hath commanded us.
1JO 3:24 And he who keepeth his commandments will abide in him, and he will abide in that man. And by this we know that he abideth in us, even by the spirit which he hath given us.
1JO 4:1 Beloved, trust not every spirit, but try the spirits whether they be of God; for many false teachers, are gone forth into the world.
1JO 4:2 By this you know the spirit of God; every spirit which acknowledged! Jesus Christ come in flesh, is of God.
1JO 4:3 And every spirit which doth not acknowledge Jesus. Christ come in flesh, is not of God. This indeed is that of Antichrist which you have heard is coming, and is now already in the world:
1JO 4:4 You, children, are of God, and have overcome them, because he who is in you is greater than he who is in the world.
1JO 4:5 They are of the world, therefore they speak suitably to the world, and the world hearkeneth to them.
1JO 4:6 We are of God. He who knoweth God, hearkeneth to us. He who is not of God doth not hearken to us. By this we know the spirit of truth and the spirit of error.
1JO 4:7 Beloved, let us love one another; for love is of God, and every one who loveth is born of God, and knoweth God.
1JO 4:8 He who doth not love hath not known God, for God is love.
1JO 4:9 By this the love of God was manifested among us, because God sent his only begotten son into the world, that we may live by him.
1JO 4:10 In this is the love; not that we loved God, but that he loved us, and sent his son to be an atonement for our sins.
1JO 4:11 Beloved, if God so loved us; we surely ought to love one another.
1JO 4:12 No one hath ever seen God. If we love one another, God abideth in us, and his love is perfected in us.
1JO 4:13 By this we know that we abide in him, and he in us, because he hath given us of his spirit;
1JO 4:14 and we have seen, and do testify, that the Father hath sent the Son to be the Saviour of the world.
1JO 4:15 Whosoever will confess that Jesus is the son of God, God abideth in him, and he in God.
1JO 4:16 Now we have known and believed this love which God hath for us. God is love; and he who abideth in this love abideth in God, and God in him.
1JO 4:17 Love is by this perfected among us that we may have confidence in the day of judgment, because in this world we are as he is.
1JO 4:18 There is no fear in this love. This perfect love excludeth fear. Because fear is accompanied with torment, therefore he who feareth is not perfect in love.
1JO 4:19 As for us we love him because he first loved us.
1JO 4:20 If anyone saith, I love God, and hateth his brother, he is a liar. For how can he who doth not love his brother whom he hath seen, love God, whom he hath not seen?
1JO 4:21 Besides, we have this commandment from him, That he who loveth God, love his brother also:
1JO 5:1 Whosoever believeth that Jesus is the Christ is born of God; and every one who loveth him who begat, loveth him also who is begotten of him;
1JO 5:2 by this we know that we love the children of God. While we love God, we keep his commandments;
1JO 5:3 for this is the love of God that we keep his commandments. Now his commandments are not grievous,
1JO 5:4 because whatever is born of God overcometh the world, and the victory which overcometh the world is our faith.
1JO 5:5 Who is he that overcometh the world, but he who believeth that Jesus is the son of God?
1JO 5:6 This Jesus is the Christ, whose coming was pointed out by water and by blood, not by the water only, but by the water and the blood; and the spirit is testifying this. Because the spirit is the truth,
1JO 5:7 because there are three that bear witness, the Spirit, and the Water, and the Blood, and these three are to one and the same thing,
1JO 5:8 OMITTED
1JO 5:9 if we admit the testimony of men the testimony of God is greater, for this is the testimony of God, which he hath testified concerning his son.
1JO 5:10 He who believeth in the son of God hath this testimony in himself: he who doth not believe God, impeacheth his veracity, because he believeth not the testimony which God hath given concerning his son.
1JO 5:11 Now this is the testimony, that God hath given us everlasting life, and this life is by his son:
1JO 5:12 he who hath the son hath this life: he who hath not the son of God hath not this life.
1JO 5:13 These things I have written to you who believe in the name of the son of God, that you may know that you have everlasting life; and that you may believe in the name of the son of God:
1JO 5:14 this also is the confidence which we have in him, that if we ask any thing according to his will he hearkeneth to us.
1JO 5:15 Now, if we know that he hearkeneth to us in whatever we may ask; we know that we obtain from him the petitions which we have asked.
1JO 5:16 If any one see his brother committing a sin not unto death, let him ask, and he will give him life for them who do not sin unto death: there is a sin unto death, with respect to this I do not say that he should make petition.
1JO 5:17 Every act of unrighteousness is a sin; and there is a sin not unto death,
1JO 5:18 and we know that every one who is born of God doth not sin; he indeed who is born of God guardeth himself and the wicked one doth not cling to him.
1JO 5:19 We know that we are of God and that the whole world is laid prostrate by the wicked one;
1JO 5:20 and we know that the son of God is come, and hath given us understanding that we may know him who is true; and we are in him who is true, and in his son Jesus Christ. He is the true God and the life eternal.
1JO 5:21 Dear children, keep yourselves from the idols. Amen.
2JO 1:1 The elder to Electa Cyria and her children whom in truth I love [and not only I, but all who have known the truth]
2JO 1:2 on account of the truth which abideth in us, and will be with us for ever:
2JO 1:3 with you be favour, mercy, peace from God the Father, and from the Lord Jesus Christ the Son of the Father, in truth and love.
2JO 1:4 I was greatly rejoiced because I found some of thy children walking in truth, as we received a commandment from the Father.
2JO 1:5 And I now intreat thee, Cyria, not as writing to thee a new commandment; but that which we had from the beginning, that we love one another;
2JO 1:6 and this love is that we may walk according to his commandments. This is the commandment, as you have heard from the beginning, that you may walk therein.
2JO 1:7 Because there are many deceivers come into the world, who do not acknowledge that Jesus Christ is come in flesh. [This is the deceiver, and the Antichrist]
2JO 1:8 Look to yourselves, that we may not lose our labour, but that we may receive ample wages.
2JO 1:9 Whosoever transgresseth, and abideth not in the doctrine of the Christ, hath not God. He who abideth in the doctrine of the Christ hath both the Father and the Son.
2JO 1:10 If any one cometh to you, and doth not bring this doctrine, receive him not into your family; nor wish him success;
2JO 1:11 for he who wisheth him success is a partaker with him in his evil works.
2JO 1:12 Having many things to write to you, I determined not to commit them to paper and ink; but I hope to come to you, and deliver them by word of mouth, that our joy may be complete.
2JO 1:13 The children of thy sister Electa salute thee. Amen.
3JO 1:1 The elder to Gaius the beloved, whom in truth I love
3JO 1:2 Beloved, I wish thee health and prosperity in all things, as thy soul prospereth.
3JO 1:3 For I was greatly rejoiced at the coming of the brethren, who bear testimony to thy truth, as thou walkest in truth.
3JO 1:4 I have no greater joy than to hear that my children are walking in truth.
3JO 1:5 Beloved, thou actest as a believer, in what thou dost for the brethren, and for the strangers,
3JO 1:6 who have borne testimony for thy love, in the presence of the congregation whom thou wilt do well to forward on in their journey in a manner worthy of God;
3JO 1:7 for they have gone forth for his name's sake, taking nothing from the Gentiles.
3JO 1:8 We therefore ought to entertain such, that we may be fellow helpers in the truth.
3JO 1:9 I wrote to the congregation, but Diotrephes, who affecteth a preeminence among them, doth not regard us.
3JO 1:10 For this cause, when I come I will take notice of his works which he doth, talking lightly of us with malicious words, and not content with this, he doth not entertain the brethren himself, and them who would, he hindereth, and casteth them out of the congregation.
3JO 1:11 Beloved, do not imitate what is evil, but what is good. He who doth good is of God. But he who doth evil, hath not seen God.
3JO 1:12 Demetrius hath a good testimony from all, and from the truth; and even we ourselves bear testimony for him; and you know that our testimony is true.
3JO 1:13 I had many things to write, but I do not choose to write to thee with ink and pen;
3JO 1:14 but I hope to see thee soon, when we shall speak face to face. Peace be with thee. The friends salute thee. Salute the friends by name.
JUD 1:1 Jude a servant of Jesus Christ, and brother of James; to the called, who are sanctified by God the father, and preserved by Jesus Christ:
JUD 1:2 mercy be to you, and may peace and love be multiplied.
JUD 1:3 Beloved, when I was using all diligence to write to you respecting the common salvation, I found a necessity to write to you, and exhort you to contend earnestly for the belief which was once for all delivered to the saints.
JUD 1:4 For Certain persons have slily crept in among us, who have been of old written of, and for this very crime, wicked men, who are turning the favour of our God into licentiousness, and denying our only sovereign God, and Lord Jesus Christ.
JUD 1:5 Now I desire once for all to remind you of this which you knew, That the Lord, having saved a people out of the land of Egypt, destroyed afterwards them who did not believe:
JUD 1:6 and the angels who did not keep their own government, but left their proper abode, he hath reserved in perpetual bonds, under darkness, for the judgment of the great day.
JUD 1:7 As Sodom and Gomorrah, and the cities around them, which, in like manner with them, abandoned themselves to licentiousness, and went after strange flesh, were made an example of, suffering the vengeance of everlasting fire;
JUD 1:8 so likewise shall these dreamers. They indeed defile the flesh, and despise authority and revile glories,
JUD 1:9 whereas Michael the archangel, when he contended with the devil, and disputed about the body of Moses, did not take the liberty to bring against him a railing accusation, but said "the Lord rebuke thee:"
JUD 1:10 but these rail at what they do not know; and what they do know in a natural way as irrational animals, with these they corrupt themselves.
JUD 1:11 Alas for them! For they have gone in the way of Cain, and rambled in the error of Balaam's reward and perished in the rebellion of Kore.
JUD 1:12 They are hidden rocks in your love feasts. When they feast with you, they feed themselves without restraint. They are clouds without water, impelled by winds; autumnal trees without fruit, twice dead, and to be rooted up;
JUD 1:13 raging waves of the sea, foaming out their own shame; wandering stars, for whom is reserved the gloom of everlasting darkness.
JUD 1:14 Now to such as these Enoch, the seventh from Adam, prophesied, saying, "Behold the Lord is coming with his holy myriads
JUD 1:15 to execute judgment on all, and to convict all the wicked among them of all their impious deeds, which they have impiously committed, and of all the bitter things which impious sinners have uttered against him."
JUD 1:16 They are discontented mumurers, walking after their own lusts. Though their mouth speaketh swelling words, they hold persons in admiration for the sake of gain.
JUD 1:17 But as for you, beloved, remember what the apostles of our Lord Jesus Christ foretold you.
JUD 1:18 For they assured you that in the last time there would be scoffers, walking after their own wicked desires.
JUD 1:19 These are they who separate themselves, being sensual, and not having the spirit.
JUD 1:20 But as for you, beloved, building yourselves up in your most holy faith, praying with a holy spirit,
JUD 1:21 keep yourselves in the love of God, as you expect the mercy of our Lord Jesus Christ for everlasting life;
JUD 1:22 and making a distinction, have compassion on some,
JUD 1:23 and save others by fear, snatching them out of the fire; abhorring even a garment which is stained by flesh.
JUD 1:24 Now to him who is able to keep you from falling, and to present you, without blemish, before his glory with great joy
JUD 1:25 to the only wise God, our Saviour, be glory and majesty, dominion and power, both now and forever. Amen.
REV 1:1 A REVELATION of Jesus Christ, which God gave him, to shew to his servants things which must shortly come to pass, and which he sent by his angel, and signified to his servant John,
REV 1:2 who hath testified the word of God, and the testimony of Jesus Christ, and what he saw.
REV 1:3 Happy he who readeth, and they who hear the words of this prophecy; and keep the things that are written therein! For the time is at hand!
REV 1:4 John to the seven congregations which are in Asia; favour be to you, and peace from him who is, and who was, and who is to come; and from the seven spirits which are before his throne;
REV 1:5 and from Jesus Christ who is the faithful witness, the first born from the dead, and the sovereign of the kings of the earth. To him who hath loved us, and washed us from our sins with his blood,
REV 1:6 and made us kings and priests to God, even his father to him be the glory and dominion for the ages of the ages. Amen.
REV 1:7 Behold he is coming with clouds, and every eye shall see him, even they who pierced him; and for him all the tribes of the earth shall mourn. Yes, be it so.
REV 1:8 "I am the Alpha and the Omega, the beginning and the end," saith the Lord, "who is, and who was, and who is to come, the Almighty."
REV 1:9 I John, who am your brother, and a partaker in this affliction, and in the kingdom and patience of Jesus Christ,  was in the island which is called Patmos, on the account of the word of God and of the testimony of Jesus Christ.
REV 1:10 I was in the spirit on the Lord's day, and I heard behind me a loud voice, like the sound of a trumpet,
REV 1:11 saying, "I am the Alpha and the Omega; the first and the last," and "what thou seest, write in a book, and send it to the seven congregations which are in Asia, to Ephesus and to Smyrna, and to Pergamus, and to Thyatira, and to Sardis, and to Philadelphia, and to Laodicea."
REV 1:12 Whereupon I turned to look towards the voice which spake to me; and upon turning about, I saw seven golden candlesticks,
REV 1:13 and in the midst of the seven golden candlesticks one like a son of man, clothed with a robe down to the feet, and girded about the breast with a golden girdle;
REV 1:14 and as for his head, the hairs like wool were glittering white as snow, and his eyes were like a flame of fire;
REV 1:15 and his feet were like fine brass, as if they were glowing in a furnace; and his voice was like the sound of many waters.
REV 1:16 And he had in his right hand seven stars; and out of his mouth went a sharp two edged sword. And his countenance was like the sun shining in its strength.
REV 1:17 And when I saw him I fell at his feet as one dead. Whereupon he laid his right hand on me, and said to me, "Fear not. I am the first and the last,
REV 1:18 even he who liveth. Though I was dead yet behold I am alive, and live for the ages of the ages, Amen. And I have the keys of the mansion of the dead, and of death.
REV 1:19 Write what thou hast seen, and the things which are, and the things which are about to be hereafter.
REV 1:20 With respect to the hidden meaning of the seven stars which thou sawest in my right hand, and the seven golden candlesticks; the seven stars are the angels of the seven congregations and the seven candlesticks which thou sawest are the seven congregations.

REV 2:2 I know thy works, and thy labour, and thy patience, and that thou canst not bear with them who are evil, and hast tried them who pretend to be apostles, and are not, and hast found them liars,
REV 2:3 and hast borne and dost exercise patience, and hast laboured for my name's sake, and hast not fainted.
REV 2:4 But I have this against thee that thou hast lost thy first love.
REV 2:5 Remember therefore from what thou hast fallen, and reform, and do thy first works; else I will come to thee quickly, and remove thy candlestick out of its place, unless thou reform.
REV 2:6 But thou hast this, that thou hatest the deeds of the Nicolaitans, which I also hate,
REV 2:7 Whosoever hath an ear to hear let him hear what the spirit saith to the congregations. To him who overcometh I will give to eat of the tree of life which is in the midst of the paradise of God."
REV 2:8 "And to the angel of the congregation at Smyrna write, "Thus saith the first and the last, who was dead and is alive,
REV 2:9 "I know thy works, and thine affliction, and thy poverty, [though thou art rich] and the slander of them who say they are Jews, and are not, but are a synagogue of satan.
REV 2:10 Be not terrified at what thou art about to suffer. Behold the devil will soon cast some of you into prison, that you may be tried; and ye will have tribulation ten days. Be thou faithful unto death, and I will give thee the crown of life.
REV 2:11 Let him who hath an ear hear what the spirit saith to the congregations. "He who overcometh shall not be hurt by the second death."
REV 2:12 And to the angel of the congregation at Pergamus write, "Thus saith he who hath the sharp two edged sword,
REV 2:13 "I know thy works, and where thou dwellest, even where the throne of satan is; yet thou holdest fast my name, and hast not denied the belief of me, even in the days in which Antipas was my faithful witness, who was slain among you where satan dwelleth.
REV 2:14 Nevertheless I have a few things against thee, because thou hast there them who hold the doctrine of Balaam, who taught Balak to cast a stumbling block before the children of Israel, to eat things sacrificed to idols, and to commit fornication.
REV 2:15 In like manner thou hast them who hold the doctrine of the Nicolaitans, which I hate.
REV 2:16 Reform. If thou dost not, I am coming to thee quickly, and I will fight against; them with the sword of my mouth.
REV 2:17 Let him who hath an ear hear what the spirit saith to the congregations. To him who overcometh I will grant to eat of the manna which was laid up; and I will give him a white stone, and on that stone a new name written, which no one knoweth but he who receiveth it.
REV 2:18 And to the angel of the congregation at Thyatira write, "Thus saith the son of God, whose eyes are like a flame of fire, and whose feet fire like fine brass;
REV 2:19 "I know thy works, and thy love, and thy service, and thy faith, and thy patience, and that thy last works exceed the first:
REV 2:20 but I have a few things against thee, because thou sufferest that woman Jezabel, who calleth herself a prophetess, to teach and seduce my servants to commit fornication, and to eat things sacrificed to idols.
REV 2:21 Though I gave her time to reform from her fornication, yet she hath not reformed.
REV 2:22 Behold I am about to cast her into a bed, and them who commit adultery with her into great tribulation, unless they reform from their works;
REV 2:23 and I will slay her children with death; and all the congregations shall know, that I am the searcher of reins and hearts, and will give to every one of you according to your works.
REV 2:24 But to you I say, even to the rest at Thyatira, to as many as do not hold this doctrine, and who have not known the depths [as they call them] of satan; on you I will lay no other burthen, besides what you have;
REV 2:25 hold it fast until I come.
REV 2:26 As for him who overcometh, and keepeth my works to the end, to him I will give power over the nations,
REV 2:27 [and he shall rule them with a rod of iron. Like vessels of potter's clay they shall be broken in pieces,]
REV 2:28 as I have received from my Father; and I will give him the morning star.
REV 2:29 Let him who hath an ear, hear what the spirit saith to the congregations.

REV 3:3 Remember therefore how thou hast received, and heard, and keep fast hold, and reform. For if thou wilt not watch, I will come against thee, as a thief, so that thou shall not know at what hour I shall come against thee.
REV 3:4 Thou hast a few names even in Sardis who have not defiled their garments. These shall walk with me in white robes because they are worthy.
REV 3:5 He who overcometh shall be clothed with white raiment, and I will not blot his name out of the book of life, but will acknowledge his name before my Father, and before his angels.
REV 3:6 Let him who hath an ear hem what the spirit saith to the congregations."

REV 3:13 Let him who hath an ear hear what the spirit saith to the congregations.
REV 3:14 "And to the angel of the congregation of the Laodicians write, Thus saith the Amen, the faithful and true witness, the beginning of the creation of God,
REV 3:15 I know thy works, that thou art neither cold nor hot. I wish thou wert cold or hot.
REV 3:16 So then; because thou art lukewarm, and neither cold nor hot, I am about to spit thee out of my mouth,
REV 3:17 because thou sayest, "I am rich and become wealthy, and have need of nothing," and knowest not that thou art wretched, and miserable, and poor, and blind, and naked.
REV 3:18 I advise thee to purchase of me gold tried in the fire that thou mayst be rich, and white raiment that thou mayst be clothed, and that the shame of thy nakedness may not appear; and anoint thine eyes with eye salve, that thou mayst see.
REV 3:19 Whomsoever I love, I rebuke and chastise. Be zealous therefore, and reform.
REV 3:20 Behold I stand at the door and knock. If any one will hearken to my voice and open the door, I will come in to him, and sup with him, and he with me.
REV 3:21 To him who overcometh I will grant to sit with me on my throne, as I have overcome, and sit with my Father on his throne.
REV 3:22 Let him who hath an ear hear what the spirit saith to the congregations."
REV 4:1 After this I looked and behold a door was opened in the heaven, and the voice which I heard at first like that of a trumpet speaking to me said, Come up hither and I will shew thee the things which must hereafter come to pass.
REV 4:2 Thereupon I was immediately enrapt, and behold a throne was set in the heaven, and one was sitting on the throne.
REV 4:3 And he who was sitting was in appearance like a jasper and sardine stone, and there was a rainbow, in appearance like a smaragdine, around the throne.
REV 4:4 And around the throne there were four and twenty thrones; and on the thrones I saw the four and twenty elders sitting, clothed in white raiment and they had on their heads crowns of gold.
REV 4:5 And from the throne proceed lightnings and thunders and voices. And there were seven lamps of fire blazing before the throne: these are the seven spirits of God.
REV 4:6 And before the throne was a glassy sea resembling chrystal. And in the middle of the throne and around the throne were four animate beings full of eyes before and behind.
REV 4:7 And the first animate being was like a lion; and the second animate being was like a calf; and the third animate being had a face like a man; and the fourth animate being was like a flying eagle.
REV 4:8 And the four animate beings had, each of them six wings around and underneath they were full of eyes. And they rest not day and night, saying, Holy, holy, holy, Lord God, the Almighty, who was and who is and who is to come!
REV 4:9 And when the animate beings give glory and honour and thanks to him who is seated on the throne, to him who liveth for the ages of the ages,
REV 4:10 the four and twenty elders are to prostrate themselves before him who is seated on the throne, and to worship him who liveth for the ages of the ages, and to cast their crowns before the throne saying,
REV 4:11 Thou, O Lord, art worthy to receive the glory and the honour and the power, because thou hast created all things, and at thy will they exist and were created.
REV 5:1 And I saw in the right hand of him who was sitting on the throne a volume written within and on the back sealed with seven seals.
REV 5:2 And I saw a mighty angel proclaiming with a loud voice, "Who is worthy to open the volume, even to loosen the seals of it."
REV 5:3 And no one in the heaven, nor on the earth, nor beneath the earth was able to open the volume and look into it.
REV 5:4 And when I was weeping much because no one was found worthy to open and read the volume; even to look into it,
REV 5:5 one of the elders saith to me, "weep not; behold! the lion who is of the tribe of Judah, the root of David, hath prevailed to open the volume and to loose the seven seals thereof."
REV 5:6 Then I looked and behold in the midst of the throne and of the four animate beings and in the midst of the elders stood a lamb as if it had been slaughtered, having seven horns and seven eyes which are the seven spirits of God sent forth into all the earth.
REV 5:7 And he went and took the book out of the right hand of him who was sitting on the throne.
REV 5:8 And when he took the book, the four animate beings and the four and twenty elders fell down before the lamb, having, every of them, kitharas and golden cups full of incense which is the prayers of the saints.
REV 5:9 And they sang a new song, saying, "Worthy art thou to take the book and to open the seals of it, because thou hast been slain and hast purchased us for God with thy blood, out of every tribe and tongue and people and nation;
REV 5:10 and hast made us kings and priests for our God, and we shall reign on the earth."
REV 5:11 And I looked and heard the voice of many angels around the throne and the animate beings and the elders and the number of them was myriads of myriads and thousands of thousands, 12 saying with a loud voice, "Worthy is the lamb that was slain to receive power and riches and wisdom and strength and honour and glory and blessing."
REV 5:13 And I heard every created being which is in the heaven and on the earth and underneath the earth and those which are in the sea, even all in them, saying, "to him who is sitting on the throne and to the lamb, be the blessing and the honour and the glory and the dominion for the ages of the ages."
REV 5:14 And the four animate beings said, Amen. And the four and twenty elders fell down and worshipped him who liveth for the ages of the ages.
REV 6:1 And I looked when the lamb opened the first of the seals and I heard the first of the four animate beings say as with a voice of thunder, "Come and see."
REV 6:2 And I looked and behold! a white horse, and he who was mounted on him had a bow and a crown was given him and he went forth conquering and to conquer.
REV 6:3 And when he opened the second seal, I heard the second animate being say, "Come and see!"
REV 6:4 And there went forth another horse of a fiery colour, and to him mounted thereon it was given to take peace from the earth and that men might slay one another; and a great sword was given him.
REV 6:5 And when he opened the third seal, I heard the third animate being say, "Come and see!" And I looked and behold! a black horse, and he who was mounted upon him had a balance in his hand.
REV 6:6 And I heard a voice in the midst of the four animate beings, saying, A choenix of wheat for a deniar and three choenices of barley for a deniar, but hurt not the oil and the wine."
REV 6:7 And when he opened the fourth seal, I heard the voice of the fourth animate being say, "Come and see."
REV 6:8 And I looked and behold! A pale horse, and one mounted on him, whose name was Pestilence; and the mansion of the dead followed him, and to them power was given to slay on the fourth part of the earth with sword and with famine and with pestilence, and by the wild beasts of the earth.
REV 6:9 And when he opened the fifth seal I saw under the altar the souls of them who had been slain for the word of God and for the testimony which they had borne.
REV 6:10 And they cried with a loud voice, saying, "How long, O sovereign, the holy one and the true, dost thou defer judging and avenging our blood on the inhabitants of the earth?"
REV 6:11 And to every of them were given white robes and they were told that they should rest yet a little while till their fellow servants and their brethren who were about to be slain as well as they were completed.
REV 6:12 And I looked when he opened the sixth seal. And behold there was a great earthquake. And the sun became black as sackcloth made of hair; and the moon was like blood;
REV 6:13 and the stars of heaven fell on the earth as a fig tree sheddeth its unripe figs when it is shaken by a mighty wind;
REV 6:14 and the heaven recoiled like a scroll rolled up; and every mountain and island were moved from their places,
REV 6:15 and the kings of the earth and the nobles and the rich and the chief commanders and the under officers and every bondman and every freeman hid themselves in the caves and among the rocks of the mountains,
REV 6:16 saying to the mountains and the rocks, "Fall upon us, and hide us from the face of him who is sitting on the throne and from the wrath of the Lamb,
REV 6:17 for the great day of His wrath is come and who is able to stand?"

REV 7:3 saying, "Hurt not the earth nor the sea nor the trees until we seal the servants of our God on their foreheads."

REV 7:7 of the tribe of Simeon were sealed twelve thousand; of the tribe of Levi were sealed twelve thousand; of the tribe of Issachar were sealed twelve thousand;
REV 7:8 of the tribe of Zabulon were sealed twelve thousand; of the tribe of Joseph were sealed twelve thousand; of the tribe of Benjamin were sealed twelve thousand.

REV 7:15 For this cause they are before the throne of God and serve him day and night in his temple. And he who sitteth on the throne will spread his tent over them.

REV 8:1 And when he opened the seventh seal, there was a silence in the heaven for about half an hour.
REV 8:2 And I saw the seven angels who were standing in the presence of God, and to them seven trumpets were given.
REV 8:3 And another angel came and stood by the altar, having a golden censer: and to him much incense was given, that he might offer it, for the prayers of all the saints, upon the golden altar which is before the throne.
REV 8:4 And when the smoke of the incense for the prayers of the saints ascended from the hand of the angel before God,
REV 8:5 the angel took the censer and filled it with some of the fire of the altar and threw it on the earth. And there were noises and thunders and lightnings and an earthquake.
REV 8:6 And the seven angels who had the seven trumpets prepared themselves to sound.
REV 8:7 And the first angel sounded; and there was hail and fire mingled with blood which were thrown on the earth and the third part of the trees was burned up, and all the green grass was burned up.
REV 8:8 And the second angel sounded, and something like a great mountain blazing with fire was cast into the sea; and the third part of the sea became blood;
REV 8:9 and the third part of the creatures, which were in the sea and which had life, died; and the third part of the ships was destroyed.
REV 8:10 And the third angel sounded; and there fell from heaven a great star blazing like a torch; and it fell upon the third part of the rivers and on the fountains of the waters.
REV 8:11 [Now the name of the star is called wormwood.] And the third part of the waters became wormwood; and many of the men died of the waters because they were made bitter.
REV 8:12 And the fourth angel sounded; and the third part of the sun, and the third part of the moon, and the third part of the stars were smitten, so that the third part of them was darkened and the day did not shine the third part of it and in like manner the night.
REV 8:13 Then I looked and heard an angel [as he was flying in mid-heaven] saying with a loud voice, Alas! Alas! Alas! for the inhabitants of the earth, because of the remaining sounds of the three trumpets which are about to sound.

And to it was given the key of the pit of the bottomless gulf, 2 and it opened the pit of the bottomless gulf; and a smoke ascended out of the pit like the smoke of a great furnace; and the sun and the air were darkened by the smoke of the pit.
REV 9:3 And out of the smoke there came forth locusts on the earth; and to them a power was given, as the scorpions of the earth have power;
REV 9:4 and a charge was given to them not to hurt the grass of the earth nor any thing green nor any tree, nothing but the men only who have not the seal of God on their foreheads;
REV 9:5 and they were enjoined not to kill these, but to torture them five months. And their torture was like the torture of a scorpion when it stingeth a man.
REV 9:6 And in those days the men will seek death and shall not find it; and they will earnestly desire to die and death will flee from them.
REV 9:7 Now the shapes of these locusts were like horses prepared for battle; and they had on their heads as it were crowns of gold; and their faces were like the faces of men;
REV 9:8 and they had hair like the hair of women, and their teeth were like the teeth of lions;
REV 9:9 and they had breast plates like breast plates of iron; and the sound of their wings was like the sound of chariots with horses rushing to battle,
REV 9:10 and they have tails like scorpions and there were stings in their tails; and their power was to hurt men five months;
REV 9:11 and they have a king over them the angel of the bottomless gulf, whose name in Hebrew is Abaddon, and in Greek he is called Apollyon.
REV 9:12 The first Woe is past and behold after these things there are two yet to come.

REV 9:15 and the four angels who were ready prepared were loosed for an hour, and a day, and a month, and a year, that they might slay the third part of men.

REV 9:19 for their powers are in their mouth and in their tails, for their tails having heads are like serpents and with these they do mischief.
